author: punk6529
body:
Builds on #2516 (the identity mirror, which contains #2512, #2513 and #2515) and contains their commits, so CI runs against main: review those first; this PR's own commits are the ones not in #2516. It uses only #2515's gateway client.

## Issue

- From Wed 25 Nov people change their identity, profile, handle, delegations, REP and NIC on the 6529 chain through this site. The site drafts each operation at the chain gateway (`POST /v1/draft`), the wallet signs its EIP-712 typed data, and the signed operation goes to the chain.
- An identity join (adding a wallet to an identity) needs two signatures over the same operation: the identity's wallet and the joining wallet. Those are often in two browsers or devices, so something must hold the half-signed operation until the second wallet signs.
- The backend has the gateway's service access (higher limits than a browser's), so it should be able to relay.

## Fix

New routes under `/api/chain` (all need a signed-in wallet):

| Route | What |
| --- | --- |
| `POST /chain/submit` | Relays `{ tx_id, signed }` or `{ tx_id, unsigned, signatures: [{ role, key_type, sig }] }` to the gateway's `/v1/submit`. `tx_id` is the draft's txId, the digest every signer signed: without it the answer is 400 and nothing is sent. Success answers the node's answer with `outcome: 'accepted'`. A failure answers `tx_id` and an `outcome`: `refused` (422 `CHAIN_REFUSED`, with the chain's code), `not_taken` (502 `CHAIN_UNAVAILABLE`, safe to send again) or `unknown` (502 `CHAIN_OUTCOME_UNKNOWN`, with `node_tx_id` when the node took another transaction): it may have landed, so ask the chain rather than send it again. |
| `POST /chain/pending` | The identity's wallet (role 0) holds an identity join it has signed: `{ tx_id, op_type, principal, unsigned, typed_data, expires_at, required: [{ role, key_type, signer }], signatures: [...] }` (the draft's `txId`, `unsigned`, `typedData`, `expiresAt` and signer list). Any other wallet gets 403. `typed_data` must hash to `tx_id` (EIP-712); the principal, the window and the signers (role 0, the wallet the header's key id names; role 4, the body's joining wallet) are read from it, and a given `principal`, `expires_at` or `required` that says otherwise is refused. Posting a join again once it was sent answers its state. |
| `GET /chain/pending` | Joins waiting for the signed-in wallet's signature (not expired; one query, at most 50), each with the `unsigned` and `typed_data` the joining wallet checks and signs. |
| `GET /chain/pending/:tx_id` | One operation. |
| `POST /chain/pending/:tx_id/signatures` | The signed-in wallet adds its signature `{ role, key_type, sig }` for its role: the joining wallet signs here. |
| `POST /chain/pending/:tx_id/retry` | Relays a complete operation again after the node surely didn't take it. |
| `DELETE /chain/pending/:tx_id` | A signer or the creator cancels a `PENDING` operation. |

- Only identity joins are held. A new join is held only when its role-0 wallet belongs to the principal now, read through the gateway at the latest finalized height (400 if not; 503 when the chain can't be read or doesn't answer in 5 s).
- Every signature is checked before it is kept: it must recover, over the operation's `tx_id` (the EIP-712 digest), to the wallet named for its role. Only wallet signatures (`key_type` 1) are held. The chain checks everything again on submit.
- No signature is ever returned: `signers[].sig` is always null, and `signed` says who has signed. The relay submits, so no wallet needs another's, and a signature handed out could finish a join its signer had withdrawn.
- Every submit carries the draft's txId, and the gateway client checks that the node's answer is of that transaction.
- A held operation is sent at most once. Once every signer has signed it is claimed under its row lock, moving from `PENDING` to `SUBMITTED` before anything is sent. Every result has an `outcome`: `accepted` (the node's answer, and the chain's `tx` once a read has asked), `unknown` (with `txId`, and `nodeTxId` when the node named another), or `refused` (the node's code, the chain's result name for a join that ran and failed, or `expired`). An unknown outcome stays `SUBMITTED` and is never sent again. Only an answer that the node surely didn't take it puts the operation back to `PENDING` for a retry; a refusal marks it `FAILED`.
- A read of a sent join (`GET /chain/pending/:tx_id`) asks the chain at most every 10 s (the time is kept in `result.checkedAt`) until it is final: held in a block or the pool, `accepted` with the chain's `tx`; run and failed, `FAILED`, with `last_error` worded as the node words a refusal; held nowhere five minutes past its expiry in the chain's time, `FAILED` (`expired`). A read's write applies only while the outcome and `checkedAt` are the ones it read, so a slower read never undoes a faster one.
- A cancel takes the same row lock and moves the operation only from `PENDING`, so a withdrawn join is never sent and a sent one is never shown as withdrawn. It also drops the signatures held, and is tried once more when MySQL rolls it back to break a deadlock.
- Limits for a held join: its unsigned envelope up to 4 KiB and its typed data up to 8 KiB; its window within the chain's `maxValidityMs` (from `GET /v1/ops`, a day when unreadable); at most five pending joins created by one wallet (429 `TOO_MANY_PENDING`, counted under a lock on that wallet's joins; a wallet that has never held a join has no row to lock, so a first burst of posts at once can pass five). A direct submit's unsigned bytes are capped at 128 KiB.
- An answer for an operation: `tx_id, op_type, principal, unsigned, typed_data, created_by, expires_at, status, final, result, last_error, created_at, updated_at, signers: [{ role, key_type, signer, signed, sig }]`. A pending operation past its expiry shows as `EXPIRED`. `final` is true once nothing about it will change (the chain's tx is final, or it is `FAILED`, `CANCELLED` or `EXPIRED`): poll `GET /chain/pending/:tx_id` until it is.

## Changes

- `src/chain-relay/chain-relay.service.ts` (checks, holding, relaying, reading the outcome), `src/chain-relay/chain-pending-operations.db.ts`, `src/chain-relay/identity-join.fixtures.ts` (tests).
- `src/entities/IChainPendingOperation.ts`: `chain_pending_operations`, `chain_pending_operation_signers` (created by the schema sync).
- `src/api-serverless/src/chain/chain.routes.ts`, mounted at `/chain` in `app.ts`.
- `docs/architecture.md`: the routes under the gateway boundary.
- Not in `openapi.yaml` yet: the frontend PR for the chain flows uses these shapes directly; the team may want them added to the spec and generated models when it settles.

## Validation

- `chain-relay-service.test.ts` (47 tests) and `chain.routes.test.ts` (13 tests), pass locally, with real wallet signatures and real EIP-712 typed data: typed data that doesn't hash to `tx_id` refused; only identity joins held, as their typed data says; a join held until the joining wallet signs and then relayed with its txId; relaying at once when all signatures come together; a signature by another wallet refused; expired, malformed and oversized input refused; two first posts of one join at once held as one; the chain unreachable (stays pending, retry relays) and refusing (failed); an unknown outcome never sent again; an answer of another transaction; a cancel, also when MySQL breaks a deadlock, and a join withdrawn while it is being completed never sent; the limits, the identity check and a slow gateway; reads of a sent join (final, failed with its result, only in the pool, held nowhere after its expiry, never undoing a newer read); the direct relay's answers and `tx_id` required; `EXPIRED`, `final` and no signature returned on every route.
- `chain-pending-operations.db.test.ts` (testcontainers, CI): store, waiting list, status moves guarded by the result's outcome and `checkedAt`, a cancel held on the locked row until a claim commits, two first pos

author: rekola
body:
The scrollbar could only be read, not used. This lets the thumb be dragged in every widget that draws it: `Table`, `ChoiceDialog` and `CommandPalette`.

- A press on the thumb grabs it where it was pressed; dragging scrolls the list.
- A press on the bare track jumps the thumb to the pointer and carries on as a drag.
- The thumb stops at the ends however far the pointer goes past them.
- In `ChoiceDialog` and `CommandPalette` the drag scrolls without moving the selection (like the wheel), and the release neither chooses nor cancels. In `Table` the release neither sorts nor selects.
- The shared logic is `ScrollbarDrag` in `Scrollbar.h`; `ChoiceList` gains `beginThumbDrag()`, `dragThumb()` and `endThumbDrag()`.

Tests: added a `ChoiceList` test for the drag; the full ctest suite passes (`cellui_ptyscreen` skipped, no `pyte`). The widgets' mouse handling was not exercised in a real terminal or window.

stocks follows cellui's `main`, so its table gets this on the next cmake run after merge.

`config.json` names the architecture (`LlamaForCausalLM`), not the checkpoint, so a remote stage could only show "Llama".

`_stage_config` now adds one key:

```python
config["exo_model_id"] = model_path.name.replace("--", "/", 1)
```

For example, `mlx-community--Llama-3.2-1B-Instruct-4bit` becomes `mlx-community/Llama-3.2-1B-Instruct-4bit`. Both stage paths get it, because both read their config from `_stage_config`: the configured attach (`attach_configured_remote_stage`) and the proxy node (`hand_layers_to_stage`).

- **exo's own stage server:** unaffected. `ModelArgs.from_dict` drops unknown keys.
- **The iPad stage ([exo-touch](https://github.com/eaglstun/exo-touch)):** shows the ID in its stats panel (exo-touch#4).

**Checked:** Llama-3.2-1B decode through `_stage_config` against the iPad at about 118 tok/s, and the panel showed `Llama-3.2-1B-Instruct-4bit`. ruff check and ruff format are clean.

author: msant262
body:
## What changed Second AI front, separate from SAST. After OpenGrep, candidate grouping, AI TP/FP review and the report, the Portable runner now runs a **business-logic review** over code flows, even when SAST raised nothing. - `portable-business-logic.ts` - `extractBusinessFlows` selects flows deterministically. It follows Graphify `EXTRACTED` call chains from business entry points such as orders, payments, approvals, roles, status and quotas (depth ≤ 3, ≤ 10 steps, ≤ 24 flows). Without a graph it falls back to route and domain files from the snapshot (`code-context`). - `runBusinessLogicPass` sends 4 flows per model session, with their source excerpts. The session can only call `workspace.read` and `results.write`. The prompt asks for these flaws: - authorization or ownership checks - state transitions and workflow bypass - limits, and amounts trusted from the client - idempotency and race conditions - broken invariants It excludes the pattern bugs SAST already covers. - Budget: the pass spends at most 25% of the scan cap, and never more than the part of the cap still left. Each turn is reserved with `reservePortableTurn`. When the pass runs out of budget, the remaining flows are marked `skipped-budget` and the scan still completes. The overall cap is never exceeded. - Reuse: a flow is reused from a prior scan of the same repository (`reviewReuseSources`) only if all of these hold: - the flow key matches - every step range has the same hash - every cited evidence range has the same hash The avoided cost is recorded. - `scanBusinessLogic` re-checks citations on every read. A finding stays confirmed only if every citation resolves to lines in the retained snapshot; otherwise it becomes inconclusive. A flow marked `issues` whose findings are all uncited is shown as inconclusive. - New endpoint `GET /scans/:id/business-logic`, with the `viewerScan` access policy. - The review is on by default for new scans (`businessLogic` in `StartScanRequest` and the worker configuration). Older configurations and existing tests behave as before. - UI: a new "Regras de negócio e fluxos (IA)" panel on the scan Evidence tab, below the AI verdicts. It shows each flow's status and steps, the cited findings, AI cost against the pass budget, and reuse with the cost it avoided. Copy is in pt-BR, en, es, de and fr. ![Business-logic panel](https://app.devin.ai/api/presigned_proxy?token=eyJhbGciOiJIUzI1NiIsInR5cCI6IkpXVCJ9..B5a14AGcEYo_WaNq_wwlKaZVuMGYp0XUEojQ2BcOcHU) ## Validation - [x] `pnpm check:repository` - [x] `pnpm typecheck` (api and web `tsc --noEmit`) - [ ] `pnpm test`: only the touched files were run, all passing: - `portable-business-logic.test.ts`, 7/7: Graphify flows, code-context fallback, citation gating, budget skip, reuse versus changed evidence, invalid artifact - a new runner integration test, plus the existing vault and Graphify runner tests - the worker, scan-start and route-policy tests - [x] `pnpm build` (web) - [x] UI change: desktop and mobile checked; copy in pt-BR, en, es, de and fr - [x] UI change: Playwright e2e for the new panel and the existing reuse panel ## Limitations - So far this has only run against mock sessions. A full scan with a real LLM (Grok OAuth) is being run on this branch in a separate session. Do not merge before it passes. - Flow selection is heuristic and bounded. A flow that was not selected was not reviewed, which does not mean it is safe. - Cost figures are estimates from frozen pricing. ---

author: arran4
body:
## Cause
[Attempt 1](https://github.com/arran4/abc-kohler-report-rss/actions/runs/44931613075/job/136929251192) successfully uploaded an artifact but deploy-pages found zero artifacts immediately afterward. [Attempt 2](https://github.com/arran4/abc-kohler-report-rss/actions/runs/44931613075/job/137058819361) found two artifacts named `github-pages` because reruns share the workflow run ID.

## Fix
Use `github-pages-${{ github.run_attempt }}` consistently in the existing upload and deploy actions. This prevents collisions with previous attempts without introducing polling, sleeps, additional permissions, or extra jobs. The original visibility race remains a possible upstream/transient issue; this PR does not claim to solve it.

## Verification
Verified that the upstream v5 actions support the `name` and `artifact_name` inputs. Live deployment is not verified. After merge, start a fresh workflow dispatch on main and check its result. If deployment still finds zero artifacts, investigate that failure separately rather than introducing speculative retries.

## Upstream findings
- [actions/deploy-pages#451](https://github.com/actions/deploy-pages/issues/451) documents the exact same intermittent zero-artifact failure in a single-job Pages workflow followed by duplicate artifacts on rerun. The reporter observed 62 successful deployments out of 63 and reports that separating build and deploy jobs avoided the issue for them.
- [actions/deploy-pages#338](https://github.com/actions/deploy-pages/issues/338) tracks duplicate artifact discovery on reruns. Both issues remain open as of 2026-11-22.
- The three preceding Pages runs in this repository succeeded; [CI for the simplified change](https://github.com/arran4/abc-kohler-report-rss/actions/runs/44974214155) also passed. CI does not exercise actual Pages deployment.
- Keep the existing single-job layout for now. Consider separate build/deploy jobs only if zero-artifact failures recur; pass the upload job's actual artifact name as a job output to handle deploy-only reruns.

author: andrewgarrison
body:
A spike to test whether UI SDK (`@ui-sdk/react`, beta) can be the behaviour layer for a "Jelly Design" system, with our WebGL2 jelly drawn on top. Try it at `/lab` (not indexed).

## What's here
- **Jelly split into three parts** (`src/components/jelly/`):
  - `body.ts`: the soft-body physics, with no DOM. Now has four edge springs and rounded-rect shapes, so it can do pills and panels.
  - `renderer.ts`: one WebGL2 context for the whole page. Each component draws on its own 2D canvas, and the renderer copies pixels into it, so jelly can still sit behind a component's text.
  - `stage.ts`: one animation loop for every surface. It sleeps bodies that have settled, and skips off-screen surfaces and hidden tabs.
- **The dock now runs on the shared stage.** It looks and behaves as before.
- **Three spike components:**
  - `JellySwitch`: follows UI SDK's `data-checked`. Pressing tugs the thumb toward the other side, and it squashes against the track when it lands.
  - `JellyTabs`: the dock's jelly, following the `--active-tab-*` variables that `TabsIndicator` measures.
  - `JellyPopover`: the surface grows out of the trigger and shrinks back into it. Closing starts a do-nothing Web Animation in the same task, so UI SDK keeps the panel mounted until the shrink finishes.
- Adds `@layer ui-sdk;` to `globals.css`, as UI SDK's docs ask.

## Results
- **Shared context:** six surfaces (three switches, tabs, popover and the dock) all draw through one WebGL context.
- **Bindings:** the components only read UI SDK's state attributes and CSS variables. Mouse, keyboard (Space, arrow keys, Escape) and focus return all still work.
- **Exit timing:** after Escape, the popover stays mounted for the shrink (about 360 ms), then hides, and focus returns to the trigger.
- **Idle cost:** once settled, only the breathing Tabs jelly keeps drawing.
- **Dark mode:** works, including on switches that are asleep.

## Not tested
- Touch devices, Safari and Firefox
- Screen readers. The canvases are `aria-hidden`, and UI SDK's ARIA is untouched.

author: jonruttan
body:
How a bundle publishes, as one shared implementation: a roll script in the kit and a release workflow a bundle calls.

Eight bundles (ash, cc, krn, logo, python, r5rs, r7rs, sweet) each carry a `tools/bundle.sh` and a `release.yml`. No two copies are the same, and all write the old pin form. The library bundles need the same thing, so it moves here.

## What it adds

- **`tools/bundle-kit/roll.sh TAG [OUT]`** writes three files, named for the repository:
  - `REPO-TAG.tar.gz`: `bundle.xon`, `lib/`, and `LICENSE` and `README.md` where the bundle has them, under one directory, with a `version` file holding the tag. The suite, tooling and CI are left out.
  - `REPO-TAG.tar.gz.sha256`
  - `bundle.pin.xon`: `(name ...)`, `(release ...)`, `(bundle "sha256:..." URL)`, `(source ...)`.
- **`.github/workflows/bundle-release.yml`**, reusable: on a pushed `v*` tag it runs the spec gate on the x-lang the bundle declares, rolls with main's `roll.sh`, and creates the GitHub release with the three files. Started by hand with a tag, it rolls, keeps the files as an artifact, and publishes nothing.
- **`make check-bundle-kit-roll`**, in `gates` and `gates-fast`: a fixture repository rolled, the tarball's contents and the pin checked, the same tag rolled twice to the same bytes, and `(Pin install ...)` run on the rolled pin.
- `docs/lang-contract.md`: "Publishing one: the roll".

## Points worth a look

- **The repository is read, never derived.** `roll.sh` takes it from `BUNDLE_REPO`, `GITHUB_REPOSITORY` or the origin remote, so a bundle named `net` at `x-lib-net` needs no rule.
- **The tarball is narrower than the eight copies make it.** They archive the whole repository at the tag.
- **`git archive --add-file` is required** (git 2.38). The copies drop the version stamp on an older git; this refuses.
- **A defect carried over, not fixed here.** The step that clones required bundles is copied from `bundle.yml` and guesses the repository as `jonruttan/x-NAME`. That is wrong for a library at `x-lib-NAME`. No bundle requires a library yet; where a required bundle's repository comes from is still to be decided.

## Verified

- `sh tools/check/bundle-kit-roll.sh` passes locally, 11 cases.
- The pre-push `gates-fast` passed.
- The workflow has not run: it needs a bundle to call it. x-lib-net is the first.

author: onlyonebyte
body:
Fixes #863

## Decision applied
Three-decimal currencies (KWD, BHD, OMR, JOD, TND) are out of scope: VROOM stores every amount as whole cents. This PR changes only the code and the error text. The matching docs sentence goes in with #874 (WS6 owns `docs/**`).

## What changed
- `hasAtMostTwoDecimals` (`backend/src/utils/money.ts`) no longer allows a millionth-of-a-cent slack. A value now passes only if it is within a relative 1e-12 of a whole-cent value. That rejects `1.999999999`, `2.000000001` and `9999999.999`, but still accepts typed amounts (`999999.99`, `10000000.01`) and float-computed ones (`0.1 + 0.2`, `1234.56 - 1000.01`, ten cents added 100 times). This is the one shared check behind expense create/update, splits, reminders, insurance costs and the CSV import.
- The CSV import's decimal error now explains the rule: `Amount "12.345" can have at most 2 decimal places. VROOM stores amounts to the cent`.

## Release note
CSV imports and the API now reject any amount with more than 2 decimal places, including values that only miss by a tiny fraction (for example `1.999999999`), instead of rounding them. Amounts from currencies with 3 minor digits must be rounded to 2 decimals before import.

## Tests
- `input-bounds.test.ts`: the new accept and reject values for `hasAtMostTwoDecimals`, including computed sums, plus an API create with `1.999999999` → 400.
- `import-csv.test.ts`: the new message.
- `bun test` over utils, expenses, insurance, financing, reminders and `src/__tests__` (1404 pass), expenses under `TZ=Pacific/Auckland`, `check:musl`, `type-check`.

Note: #886 (#867) also edits `money.ts`, in the helper just below this one. Whichever lands second gets rebased.

This PR changes docs only; there are no code changes. It adds the report from round D of the live test on the Mac. - **D1 (critical, wrong math):** «Try a Similar One» on cos(2π/3) asks for cos(5π/6), then shows **−0.5** and rejects −√3/2.

- **D5:** The Português answer box holds the whole essay, with its numbered list flattened.
- **D6:** The transcribed question shows Markdown asterisks literally.

_Requested by **Logan** · [project thread](https://claude.ai/code/project/chan_01MbRm8WoR7UvfiANS7K5yLz?thread=cmsg_01MbRm8WoR7UvfiANS7K5yLzGAW51vVaECPutSVQ6kdnt5)_

## Release / coordination evidence

Workstream: Website
Owner authorization: In the project thread on 2026-11-22, the owner approved re-pinning to 1.8.3-beta ("go ahead") and then chose "Build the ranked play page". Neither covers launch. **NO MERGE OR DEPLOY without owner sign-off, NO production D1 migration, NO `graftbound_launch_v1` activation.**
Files/Scope: Builds on the former #133 branch, merged with current `main`.
- **Re-pin** (`src/graftbound-verify/**`, `scripts/graftbound-pin.mjs`): the 47 rules files from the Game Lab manifest at the pinned SHA, plus `lab-source-manifest.json`. The digest is computed exactly the way the Lab computes it.
- **Ranked page** (`games/graftbound.html`, `games/graftbound.js`, `games/graftbound.css`): uses the shared site header, Arcade template and footer. It has controls to start, resume and start over a verified run, a server-verified result panel and the leaderboard. When the launch flag is off, it shows "Ranked not open yet" and the game is still playable as practice. It is **noindex and not linked from the Arcade** until launch.
- **On-site game** (`games/graftbound-play/**`): `src/**`, `assets/**` and `styles.css` are an exact copy of the pinned Game Lab client. Only `index.html` (site canonical, noindex, bridge script) and the new `site-ranked.js` bridge differ. The bridge:
  - loads the server checkpoint into the game;
  - forwards each decision the engine accepted to the parent page;
  - keeps verified runs out of the practice save;
  - hides the Lab's local "Ranked preview".
- **Parent page:** batches decisions into `segment` calls. On any rejection it resyncs from the server, and it shows only server-computed totals.
- `_headers`: `/games/graftbound-play/*` may be framed by the same origin only (same rule as Stackbreaker's play document).
- `functions/api/graftbound.js`: `start` on an open attempt now also returns its accepted `decisions`, so the game can rebuild its replay log. This is read-only, with no schema change.
- **Tests:**
  - PIN test and on-site client parity test: every rules file in `games/graftbound-play` matches the manifest hash.
  - Template test now covers `games/graftbound.html`.
  - New `tests/graftbound-site-browser.test.mjs` with a test-only static and API server in `tests/helpers/graftbound-site-server.mjs`.

Concurrent work: Supersedes #133, which was closed on 2026-11-22 at the owner's request. Game Lab #204/#205 are design-only. When they ship, re-pin and re-copy the client using the steps in `docs/GRAFTBOUND-INTEGRATION.md`.
Test plan: local runs in this session, results below.
- `npm run test:unit`: **512/512 pass**
- `npm run test:workers`: **5/5 pass**
- `npm run test:browser`: **62/62 pass**. This includes the new end-to-end GRAFTBOUND test in headless Chromium against the real API and an in-memory D1. It starts a verified run, submits 20 moves, reloads and resumes from the server checkpoint, sends a tampered move (server rejects it and the game resyncs to move 20, with nothing stored), plays to the end, and checks that the shown result equals the server's stored score and that the player appears on the leaderboard. A second test covers the launch-off state at phone width (390px): no horizontal scroll, header visible, local preview hidden.
- `npm run check`: **248 site checks pass**
- Game Lab `npm test` at the pinned SHA: 719 pass, 1 skipped, 0 fail. The Lab and site engines produced an identical decision log, scoring and totals.
- Not done: signed-in staging on real Cloudflare and D1. The tests use an injected bearer key instead of a real device cookie; cookie auth is covered by the API tests. Workers Builds is red on `main` too (it fails instantly), so it is not caused by this PR.

Rollback: Close this PR. `main` is unaffected. If ever merged, revert the merge commit. The launch flag stays 0.

### Promotion evidence
Lab source SHA: `367c15af26231b0ea707bd5d3e4ca75d78f32bfa`
Rules version: `graftbound-rules-1.8.3-beta` · pool `real-pool-133-v7` · scoring `gb-score-2` · challenge `gb-expedition-01` rev 30 · build `graftbound-1.8.3-beta`
Score/replay validation: rules digest `6ddba82f23c4af1790910ce7ef8647f746e4b9eb0a33145297328095d4ccc51e` matches the Lab manifest. The server replay tests cover tamper rejection, sequencing, identity, resume and leaderboard privacy, and the browser test covers the full page flow.

### Known gaps before any launch
- Signed-in staging on Cloudflare, Workers CPU timing on full replays, and rate-limit tuning.
- The bot loses in Act 1, so no test plays a full three-act expedition.
- At launch: remove the page's noindex, link it from the Arcade, homepage and sitemap, back up D1, run the migration, then turn the flag on. Each step needs owner approval.

### Deployment
- [x] From current main; supersedes older #133
- [ ] All relevant tests, mobile and production security checks passed
- [ ] Human owner authorized this production change
- [ ] Post-merge exact Cloudflare production commit, deployment ID, and smoke test to be recorded

## What this does

Removes the dead code listed in #7:

1) Unused locals: `bpp` (`img/bmp_file.py`), `rows_per_strip` and `strip_offsets_index` (`img/tiff_file.py`), `main_seen` (`vjass/codegen.py`), `adapters` (`vjass/runtime.py`) and the two `brace` names in `vjass/zinc.py`. 2) The outer `nonlocal replaced, failed` in `w3x/optimize.py`, which assigned nothing. The inner `one()`, which does the counting, keeps its own `nonlocal`.
3) The second `from wc3files.w3o import ObjectFile` in `cli/main.py`.
4) `mpq/utils.py`, which nothing in `src/`, `tests/` or `tools/` imports (see the comment on #7). #14 was changed so it no longer touches this file, which avoids a modify/delete conflict.

## What this adds (Paddle **sandbox**, test cards only)

- **Pricing page buttons** now open checkout: *Get the Founding price*, *Get Pro Yearly*, and *or pay $5 monthly*.
- **Sign-in first:** signed-out visitors see the sign-up screen with a note; their plan choice is remembered for an hour, even across email confirmation.
- **Founding Teacher** checks how many of the 100 spots are left; if none, it offers Pro Yearly instead.
- **After payment,** Floatle checks every few seconds until Pro turns on, then says thank you.
- **Settings** shows *Get Floatle Pro* (free) or *Floatle Pro, active through …* (Pro).
- **`supabase/functions/paddle-webhook`** checks that each message really came from Paddle, then updates the teacher's row in `plans`. District pilot end dates are never shortened.
- **`floatle-paddle-payments.sql`** adds the payment columns, stops teachers from editing their own plan from the browser, and adds `founding_spots_left()`.

## Setup needed before testing (see the chat for step-by-step)
1. Run `floatle-paddle-payments.sql` in Supabase.
2. Create the `paddle-webhook` Edge Function from `supabase/functions/paddle-webhook/index.ts`, with JWT verification off.
3. In Paddle (sandbox): add a notification destination pointing to the function, and set the default payment link to `https://floatle.com/`.
4. Add the `PADDLE_WEBHOOK_SECRET` secret in Supabase.

## Tested
- Signature check: accepts real Paddle signatures; rejects changed messages, wrong secrets, old timestamps and missing headers.
- Pro dates: active and renewing, past due (7-day grace), canceled (ends now).
- SQL: runs cleanly twice on a test database, keeps pilot dates, blocks teachers from editing `plans`.
- Browser (with a stand-in for Paddle): signed-in checkout opens with the right price and account id; signed-out visitors get sign-up first.

## Going live later
Change `PADDLE.env` to `"production"` and swap in the live token and live price IDs.

author: isma-l154
body:
Closes #315

## What changed

- The 56 committed difficulty faces are replaced by one lossless atlas, `assets-src/faces.webp`: 176×176 tiles, rows in `FACES` order, columns bare + `HALOS`, and `unrated` on an extra row. `npm run assets` cuts it into the git-ignored `assets/faces/`, with the same names. `faceFile()` and the search filters are unchanged.
- **Download size stays the same:** the original faces were lossy WebP (448 KB in total). The atlas keeps the decoded pixels losslessly as the master, and the generated faces use quality 90 with lossless alpha: 444 KB in total, at least 38 dB PSNR against the atlas. Cutting them losslessly would have tripled the download (1.38 MB).
- Cubes and faces share `cutAtlas()`, which checks the atlas size before touching the output folder. Every catalog prints its summary from `main`, which reads js/config.js and js/components/faces.js once each.
- Output constants are named by catalog (`CUBE_DIR`, `FACE_DIR`, `FLAG_DIR`), and the README and `.gitignore` describe all three generated catalogs.

## Verified

- Before switching to lossy, all 56 losslessly cut faces were **identical in raw RGBA** to the originals. After the switch, they look the same side by side at 48 and 176 px, halos included.
- `npm test`: 936 pass, 1 skipped. `npm run lint` clean. `semgrep p/default --error` clean.
- Mutation check, with the assets regenerated for each mutation: 6/6 killed. Each of these makes a test fail: the atlas-size check, lossy faces, the quality floor, the `unrated` tile, the halo columns, and the cubes' `exact` flag.
- `npm run site` publishes 485 cubes, 56 faces and 249 flags plus the licence, with no `assets-src`, and a stamped `CACHE`.
- Browser: the app's faces load with no broken images.

## Review changes

- I asked Codex to fix the size regression and to deduplicate the cube and face builders into `cutAtlas`.
- I resolved the merge with the flags branch myself and renamed the constants for clarity.

author: cristina1270
body:
## Que cambia

La imagen de ejecución `eclipse-temurin:17-jre-alpine` usa **musl** y no trae el cargador de glibc (`ld-linux-x86-64.so.2`) que pide **snappy-java**, ni `libstdc++`, que piden snappy y **RocksDB**. En contenedor, la topología de KPI abre almacenes RocksDB, que necesitan libstdc++: moría al arrancar con UnsatisfiedLinkError, report-kpi-streams quedaba Empty y /kpis/live nunca tenía datos; su productor interno comprime además con snappy.

Se agrega a la etapa de ejecución:

```dockerfile
RUN apk add --no-cache gcompat libstdc++
```

No cambia ninguna configuración de Kafka: `compression.type=snappy` se mantiene, como indica la guía de tuning del curso. Afecta igual a `infra/apps/compose.yml` y a `infra/deploy/compose.yml` (EC2), que construyen con este Dockerfile.

**Es un bug que ya existe en `develop`**, no introducido por los PR de la EP5. Apareció en la prueba de punta a punta sobre la integración de todos los PR abiertos.

Indicadores 1, 4 y 5 de la rúbrica EP5: sin esto, el sistema no publica ni procesa en contenedor.

## Como probarlo

No hay test unitario posible: el fallo solo existe dentro de la imagen (los tests corren en el host, donde las librerías nativas cargan). **Verificado en contenedor**, antes y después:

- Antes: Streams en PENDING_ERROR con UnsatisfiedLinkError … libstdc++.so.6.
- Después: REBALANCING to RUNNING, report-kpi-streams Stable con 3 miembros y lag 0, y /kpis/live con disponible=true.

```bash
docker compose --env-file infra/apps/.env -f infra/apps/compose.yml build report
docker compose --env-file infra/apps/.env -f infra/apps/compose.yml up -d --no-deps report
```

- [ ] Cierra la casilla `<fase>.<numero>` de `CHECKLIST.md` (no corresponde: corrección de la EP5)
- [x] Sin secretos ni archivos `.env` en el diff
- [x] El proyecto compila y los tests pasan localmente (el Dockerfile construye; los tests no cambian)

author: ppicinic
body:
## What
Q1b of #490, the second of two PRs ([plan](https://github.com/ppicinic/ShinyBotHunter/issues/490#issuecomment-7070737013), steps 8 to 11; [approval](https://github.com/ppicinic/ShinyBotHunter/issues/490#issuecomment-7070744354)). It adds `checkDecisions` and `checkItemsWindow` to `rs-pickup.ts`, adds the scenarios `rs-pickup` (thirty won battles and the items window), `rs-pickup-ruby` (the take set-up and ten wins on RU-Wild) and `rs-pickup-heal` (Complete at Lv 12, HP written low, then the heal trip and training after it), and updates `qa-automation.md`. It also has the #496 review fixes.

## Added
- `ShinyBotHunter.Qa/dashboard/rs-pickup.spec.ts`, `rs-pickup-ruby.spec.ts` and `rs-pickup-heal.spec.ts`. The plan's file list: "the eight `rs-pickup*.spec.ts` files".
- In `rs-pickup.ts`: `checkDecisions`, `Decision` and `checkItemsWindow` (plan step 8). Also `GEN4`, FR-13's Gen 3 to Gen 4 table, which is not exported (plan: "FR-13's ten as a table kept in the module"). `PICKUP_ITEMS` is now built from its keys.
- `pickupRun` takes a `whileIdle` option, a hook that runs between the Cancels (see Deviations).
- No package, project, interface, config key, folder, cheat or save.

## Deleted
- `NO_ITEM` from `rs-pickup.ts`. Nothing used it.
- The `export` keyword on everything in `rs-pickup.ts` that no spec imports: `ZIGZAGOON`, `PICKUP_SAVE`, `BALLS_POCKET`, `readPockets`, `bagCounts`, `Pockets` and `PickupResult`.

## Deviations from the plan
1. **When the items window is checked.** `checkItemsWindow(admin, rom, takes)` runs between the Cancels, through the new `whileIdle` option on `pickupRun`. The plan said after the bot Cancel, before the shutdown. `trainingRun` has no hook there, and `rs-training.ts` may not change beyond what is already listed. Between the Cancels the takes are final and the bot is idle.
2. **How it finds the window.** It takes the admin page, not the Electron app, and finds the Pickup window through `admin.context().pages()`. The frame keeps the app private.
3. **Six minutes per won battle, not three.** In `rs-pickup` and `rs-pickup-ruby` each won battle, and the visit after the last one, may take up to 6 minutes. A heal trip (the walk, the nurse and the walk back) can fall between two wins, and `rs-train-heal` itself allows 6 minutes for the nurse alone. Stops and stale-timeouts still fail at once through `waitPickup`.
4. **PP written full at Complete.** In `rs-pickup-heal` the lead's PP is written full at Complete together with the HP. Run 1's battle uses PP, and the heal line is asserted with damaging PP 70 (Tackle 35, Mud-Slap 10, Water Gun 25), so the trip is taken for the HP alone.
5. **The start-menu Down in `rs-pickup-heal`.** Run 2 is judged with no start-menu Down on any visit. "The first visit of a run" is read as the first visit since launch, because the game keeps the cursor for the session. `checkDecisions` takes this as `firstSinceLaunch`.
6. **The ROM for `rs-pickup-ruby`.** The spec sets the ROM itself: it sets `process.env.QA_RS_ROM = 'RU-Wild'` for its test and puts the shell's value back in a `finally`. `trainingRun` reads `rsRom()` itself, so making `pickupRun` take a ROM would have meant changing `trainingRun`. With this, `npx playwright test rs-pickup-ruby` runs on Ruby with no variable.
7. **Where the logs are cut.** `checkDecisions` is called on the log cut at the trip line the scenario waited for (the HGSS scenario cuts the same way), so a Cancel that lands late cannot leave a half window. The bag and party checks still use the whole log.
8. **More than one cell on the first row** is asserted only when the GET has more than one item.

## Checks run
- `npx playwright test --list` in `ShinyBotHunter.Qa/dashboard`: `Total: 70 tests in 70 files`. `--list` with `rs-pickup.spec`, `rs-pickup-ruby` and `rs-pickup-heal` each lists exactly 1 test.
- `../../PokemonDashboard/node_modules/.bin/tsc --noEmit --strict --target es2023 --lib es2023,dom --module commonjs --moduleResolution node --esModuleInterop --skipLibCheck --typeRoots ../../PokemonDashboard/node_modules/@types --types node rs-*.spec.ts rs-pickup.ts`: no errors. Run before step 8's commit and again on the tip.
- `powershell -ExecutionPolicy Bypass -File Scripts/ci-local.ps1` on the tip: `ci-local: PASS (8/8 steps, 03:04)`. It was not run before the step 8 to 10 commits: those touch only `ShinyBotHunter.Qa/dashboard`, which ci-local does not read, and they had the list and type checks.

## Tests
All of these need the emulator, so each is QA for the orchestrator:
- QA `rs-pickup` (`npx playwright test rs-pickup.spec`), about 15 minutes plus about 3 for a heal trip; timeout 35. Thirty won battles; `checkDecisions` finds 31 windows or more, the first `held 0`, every visit under NFR-1's bound. It fails if any one press kind is retried more than twice. It also checks every take, the items window, the party with nothing held and the bag.
- QA `rs-pickup-ruby` (`npx playwright test rs-pickup-ruby`), about 8 minutes; timeout 20. The take checks on visit 1 on RU-Wild, then ten won battles and `checkDecisions`.
- QA `rs-pickup-heal` (`npx playwright test rs-pickup-heal`), about 10 minutes; timeout 25.
  - Run 1: `nothing to take`, one won battle, Complete at Lv 12.
  - At Complete, with the bot idle: HP written to floor(maxHp/4), PP full.
  - Run 2: the heal line with that HP and damaging PP 70, the plan to the Oldale Center, `checkHome`, one count line after the walk back counting the holders, two wins each followed by a visit, and `checkDecisions` from Run 2.

## Not run
No scenario, emulator, backend or Electron was run (the orchestrator was running emulator QA on this PC). The three new scenarios have never run.

## Noticed, not done
- `rs-training.ts:639`: `REPEL_STEPS =VARS` is missing a space.
- `checkVisit` cannot handle a menu with no ITEM: the `B on a menu` kind is in `KIND` but never in `expectedKinds`. No scenario reaches that path, since mail is skipped before its menu is opened.

## Docs
`docs/specs/qa-automation.md`:
- the three run lines;
- a paragraph for the sixty-fifth to sixty-seventh scenarios (numbered after `hgss-sign-walk`), with `checkDecisions` and `checkItemsWindow`;
- the three scenario rows;
- `rs-pickup-field-move`'s row now says five list Downs;
- the changelog line.

Review fixes from #496: the `rs-pickup-field-move.spec.ts:33` comment now says five Downs (slot 6 is cursor 5), and the missing space at `rs-training.ts:617` is added.

author: otih
body:
Three robustness improvements for layout loading:

- LRU cache (max 20 entries) for fetched layout SVGs: layout switches and re-renders do not re-fetch unchanged files. Cache stays bounded, eviction drops the oldest entry (Map insertion order).
- fetchWithTimeout via AbortController (10 s): a stalled request can no longer leave the card in the loading state indefinitely.
- Same-origin guard: the layout SVG URL is resolved and checked against the serving HA instance before fetching, so a manipulated layout config cannot make the card request SVGs from arbitrary origins.

Note on cache invalidation: the layout URL carries the hacstag / v=
  query parameter from makeURL(), so a new card version changes the URL
  and effectively invalidates cached layouts.

author: hyungunoh321
body:
## 내용
`src/decode/app_tls.py` — `parse_tls()` (DESIGN 7.9)
- **레코드 헤더 5바이트만** 해석: Content Type(20 ChangeCipherSpec, 21 Alert, 22 Handshake, 23 Application Data, 24 Heartbeat), Version(0x0300 SSL 3.0, 0x0301~0x0304 TLS 1.0~1.3), Length. 내용은 해석하지 않음
- 한 세그먼트에 **레코드가 여러 개**면 Length만큼 건너뛰며 레코드마다 한 줄 (첫 레코드가 summary, 둘째부터 lines)
  - 10개가 넘으면 나머지는 개수만 (작은 레코드가 잔뜩 든 세그먼트로 화면이 넘치지 않게. fields에는 전부)
- 마지막 레코드(또는 다음 레코드 헤더 앞부분)가 **다음 세그먼트로 이어지면** `(레코드가 다음 세그먼트로 이어짐: 이 세그먼트에 1310/2426 bytes)`
- **레코드 헤더로 시작하지 않는 세그먼트**(앞 레코드가 이어지는 중)는 None → `[DATA]`
  - 헤더 모양 = Content Type·Version이 위 값이고 Length가 2^14+2048(암호화된 레코드 최대) 이하. 암호문이 우연히 통과할 확률은 100만분의 1보다 작음
- 헤더 모양으로 시작하는데 5바이트가 안 되거나, 첫 레코드 뒤가 헤더 모양이 아니면 `ValueError` (파서 약속) → `decode()`가 잡아 `[DATA]`
- fields: `records`(레코드마다 `content_type`, `type_name`, `version`, `version_name`, `length`, `in_segment`), `continues`

`src/decode/app_select.py` — **TLS 분기**
- `TCP_BY_PORT`에 `"tls"`: `ports["tls"]`(443·465·993·995, `--port`로 바뀐 값) 포트면 `parse_tls()`. 다른 분기처럼 함수 안에서 import
- 평문 HTTP 요청줄·상태줄은 TLS 포트여도 지금처럼 내용으로 HTTP (TLS 레코드는 20~24로 시작해 겹치지 않음)
- `tls`를 `http`보다 앞에 둠: `--port tls=8080`처럼 한 포트가 둘 다에 들면 TLS로 (http가 앞이면 TLS 데이터가 전부 `[HTTP] continuation`으로 찍힘)
- 공개 함수 약속은 바뀌지 않음

## 출력 예 (실행 흐름 점검)
```
#4    20:06:40.004000  OUT  TCP  10.0.2.15:51234 -> 34.223.124.45:443  len=571
  [TLS ] TLS record type=22(Handshake) version=TLS 1.0 len=512
#5    20:06:40.005000  IN   TCP  34.223.124.45:443 -> 10.0.2.15:51234  len=1502
  [TLS ] TLS record type=22(Handshake) version=TLS 1.2 len=122
         TLS record type=20(ChangeCipherSpec) version=TLS 1.2 len=1
         TLS record type=23(Application Data) version=TLS 1.2 len=2426
         (레코드가 다음 세그먼트로 이어짐: 이 세그먼트에 1310/2426 bytes)
#6    20:06:40.006000  IN   TCP  34.223.124.45:443 -> 10.0.2.15:51234  len=1170
  [DATA] 1116 bytes  9e 9f a0 a1 a2 a3 a4 a5 a6 a7 a8 a9 aa ab ac ad ae af b0 b1 b2 b3 b4 b5 b6 b7 b8 b9 ba bb bc bd …
```
ClientHello → 서버 첫 응답(ServerHello + ChangeCipherSpec + 암호화된 Handshake) → 그 레코드가 이어지는 세그먼트

> 참고: 레코드의 Version은 실제로 고른 버전과 다를 수 있습니다 (Wireshark도 같게 보임). ClientHello는 보통 TLS 1.0, TLS 1.3 연결도 레코드에는 TLS 1.2로 나옵니다 (RFC 8446 5.1). 고른 버전은 Handshake 내용(supported_versions)에 있어 레코드 헤더만으로는 모릅니다. 시연·보고서에서 헷갈리지 않게 적어 둡니다.

## 확인한 것
- `tests/test_tls.py` 21개: ClientHello·ServerHello·ChangeCipherSpec·Alert·Heartbeat·Application Data 레코드, Version 5가지, Length 상한, 레코드 여러 개(TLS 1.3 서버 첫 응답, TLS 1.2 ClientKeyExchange + ChangeCipherSpec + Finished), 이어지는 레코드·잘린 다음 헤더, 레코드가 많을 때 줄 수 제한, TLS가 아닌 데이터 → None (이어지는 세그먼트, HTTP, SSH, DTLS, SSLv2 등), 짧거나 깨진 데이터 → `ValueError`, parse_app → decode → format_packet 실제 연결
- `tests/test_app_select.py` 5개: 443·465·993·995 양방향 → TLS 분기, 이어지는 세그먼트 → None, `--port tls=8443` 재지정(`main.parse_args` 결과 그대로), http·tls가 겹치는 포트, 443의 평문 HTTP·UDP(QUIC)
- 전체 137개 통과 (로컬 파이썬 3.12·3.14), CI 단계(문법 검사·모듈 불러오기·`--help`·단위 테스트)도 로컬에서 통과. 3.10은 로컬에 없어 문법만 확인 → CI에서 확인
- 실제 `curl -4 https://example.com` 캡처는 Ubuntu에서 확인 예정

## 확인 부탁 (A)
리뷰 후 merge 부탁합니다. 레코드 헤더로 시작하지 않는 세그먼트는 issue대로 None이라 `[DATA] N bytes`로 찍히는데, HTTP처럼 `[TLS ] continuation N bytes`로 보이는 게 낫다면 알려 주세요. `test_app_select.py`에서 `--port` 확인에 A의 `src.main.parse_args`를 불러 쓰는 것도 괜찮은지 봐 주세요.

Closes #13
Refs #10

author: hondazn
body:
## Bug and impact

`hado repl` は入力の文字列の接尾辞 `->` を継続として剥がすので、行コメントの中の `->`
でも剥がれる。main `b67f323` の実測:

- `0 as x ->` のあと `1 // as x ->` の `x` は `1` に替わり、`0` が印字されない。
- `1 as x -> // keep` のあとの `x` は E100 と E204 で未束縛のまま。
- `1 -> // gone` は E100 になり、次の `2` まで届かない。

## Root cause

`split_step` が文字列の接尾辞 `->` を割り、その前の末尾の単語の直前が文字 `as` か
どうかで束縛を決めていた。行コメントは字句に残らないので、コメントの中の `->` が
継続になり、本当の `->` の後ろのコメントが継続を隠す。

## Fix

継続にするのは入力の最後の字句が `->` のときだけにした。束縛はその直前が `as` と
名前の字句のときだけ（`binding_name`）。本体はその字句より前のソースを字句のスパンから
スカラ単位で切る（`source_before`）。字句が読めない入力は今までどおり剥がさず、本検査の
E100 に任せる。

## Validation

- main `b67f323` の木で上の 3 形を再現。修正後は順に `1` / `0`、`1`、`2` を印字し、
  診断は出ない。
- 単体テスト 5 本はテスト先行コミットで 2 failed / 6 passed（`step.display` と
  `binder == Some("x")`）、修正後 8 passed。
- 結合テスト `cargo test --offline --test command repl::` は 22 passed（新しい
  `repl_does_not_take_a_binding_from_a_comment` を含む）。
- `bash scripts/verify-repl.sh` は main の木で 11/12（検査 12 が赤）、修正後 12/12。
- `bash scripts/run-gates.sh --tier quick` は 38/38、`scripts/lint-docs.sh` は 16/16。
  rustfmt と clippy（`-D warnings`・認知複雑度）は緑。corpus lock は差分なし。

PR #113 は古い base を持っていたので、同じ修正を現行 main で測り直した版である。着地後に
#113 を superseded として閉じる。

ラウンドの記録: `docs/rounds/repl-lexical-continuation.md`

- [x] `cargo test --offline --lib repl::tests::`
- [x] `cargo test --offline --test command repl::`

author: perctrix
body:
The first version of the Discord adapter, for amplimit/Havn#185. It needs the gateway's servers and threads (amplimit/Havn#285, in Havn 0.2.11).

## How it works
- **Discord's side.** The gateway connection uses twilight (`twilight-gateway`, `twilight-http`, `twilight-model`, `twilight-cache-inmemory` for channels, servers and roles). The shard reconnects and resumes on its own. On start, the daemon reads the bot and its Message Content intent from the application's flags, and it asks for that intent only when it has it (`sees_all`).
- **havn's side.** `havn_ws.rs` and `gateway.rs` come from the Telegram adapter: the WebSocket with resume and the kept last delivered reply, and file upload and fetch. An upload in a server names the channel and the server (`group`, `space`).

## Ids
- A person is `discord:<user>`.
- A server is `discord:s<guild>`, a channel `discord:c<channel>`, and a thread `discord:t<thread>`.
- A message is `discord:<channel>:<message>`.
- A server is never a target: the adapter refuses to send to `discord:s…`.

## Server messages
- **Addressed.** A message is addressed when it mentions the bot or its role, or replies to it. Every message in a thread the bot opened is addressed.
- **Lazy threads.**
  - A mention in a channel names a thread `discord:t<message id>`, the id Discord gives a thread opened from that message, named from its first line.
  - The thread is opened when the first reply to it goes, so a channel not let in keeps no empty thread.
  - After a restart, a waiting thread is opened from the message the reply answers, named "conversation".
- **Gateway support.** Server messages and interactions go on only once the gateway's `Commands` frame says `groups`.
- **Files.** The files of a message to the bot are uploaded; those of other messages are named in the text.
- **Typing** shows only in private chats, as with Telegram groups.

## Interactions
- **Slash commands.** The gateway's commands become global slash commands, each with an optional `text`. An invalid name is left out, and at most 100 are set. A command is answered with the command as it was asked, then goes on as typed text.
- **Buttons.** A button's custom id is its data (at most 100 characters). A press updates the message to remove the components and goes on as the data.
- **Questions.** An `ask_choice` becomes a multi-select menu (at most 25 options), remembered by number. A choice goes on as `answer` followed by the chosen numbers.

## Outbound
- **No pings.** Every message is sent with `allowed_mentions` empty, so nothing pings.
- **Splitting.** Text is split under 2000 characters, at paragraphs, lines, words, or anywhere if it must. A code fence cut in two is closed and opened again with its language.
- **Replies.** A reply answers its message only where that message is in the same channel. `fail_if_not_exists` is false.
- **Files.** A file is sent up to 10 MB. Otherwise a line says why it was not.
- **Attachments are downloaded** only from `cdn.discordapp.com` and `media.discordapp.net`, at most 25 MB.

## Tests
There are 23 tests, covering:
- splitting, with long words and code blocks across parts;
- mentions, channels, emoji and timestamps as names;
- thread names;
- ids and targets;
- message ids;
- the slash command rules;
- button rows;
- the question menu and its answer;
- the bounded map;
- typing;
- the config, including that tokens are not shown.

fmt and clippy (pedantic, `-D warnings`) pass, and so do the tests, on Windows and on Linux.

An end-to-end test with a real bot and gateway follows, once the bot is made.

## Summary

- Extract the scheduler polling delay into `waitForSchedulerInterval`, used directly by `main()` and supplied with an injectable timer adapter for deterministic tests.
- Release the transient shutdown listener and pending timer on normal timeout, shutdown abort, an already-aborted signal, an abort during registration, and timer setup failure.
- Exercise the production helper itself; verify listener/timer counts over 100 consecutive poll completions.

## Why this replaces Aikido PR #272

PR #272 remains unmerged and is not being merged as-is. Its proposed runtime change addressed the same listener leak, but its large duplicated test implementation did not invoke the actual scheduler helper and contained placeholder listener-count assertions. This replacement tests the production code path directly and asserts that listeners and timers return to zero after each cycle. See umbrella triage issue #277.

## Validation

- Clean `npm ci`: 178 packages; npm audit reported zero vulnerabilities.
- Focused scheduler tests: 7/7 passed.

- `git diff --cached --check` passed.

## Compatibility and release boundary

No public API, database schema, migration, dependency, lockfile, package version, or SemVer change. Polling interval, scheduling order, and shutdown ownership remain unchanged; the change only releases per-interval resources. Package 0.6.2 remains private/unreleased and production remains NO-GO. author: toranek
body:
### What

Stacked on #25406 and #25407: only the last commit is new.

Four cases where a class callback of the JavaScriptCore C API declines, and `libSceNKWebKit` did something else than JavaScriptCore. Reference: `neonmodder123/PS5-WebKit-11.x@80f77e94`, [`JSCallbackObjectFunctions.h`](https://github.com/neonmodder123/PS5-WebKit-11.x/blob/80f77e94c63ee7202eec3d4b5b1a021dd89011ba/Source/JavaScriptCore/API/JSCallbackObjectFunctions.h).

**1. `convertToType` that returns NULL, or an object.** JavaScriptCore falls back to the ordinary conversion in both cases (L244-L259):

```cpp
            if (result) {
                JSValue jsResult = toJS(globalObject, result);
                if (UNLIKELY(jsResult.isObject()))
                    return JSValue::encode(asObject(jsResult)->ordinaryToPrimitive(globalObject, hint));
                return JSValue::encode(jsResult);
            }
        }
    }
    
    RELEASE_AND_RETURN(scope, JSValue::encode(thisObject->ordinaryToPrimitive(globalObject, hint)));
```

For a class whose `convertToType` returns NULL for strings, `String(obj)` is `"[object Name]"` in JavaScriptCore; the port gave `"undefined"`. When the callback returned an object, the port passed it on and the engine raised a `TypeError`.

**2. `x instanceof obj` for an object of a class without a `hasInstance` callback.** A `JSCallbackObject` always implements `hasInstance`, and `customHasInstance` returns false when no class in the chain has the callback (L503-L528). The port exposed `Symbol.hasInstance` only when a callback existed, so the engine threw a `TypeError`.

**3. A static value whose getter declines.** A static value entry with a NULL `getProperty`, or whose getter returns NULL, is not a property in JavaScriptCore (L185-L193, L646-L677). The port reported it as present without calling the getter: `"x" in obj` and `JSObjectHasProperty` were true while `obj.x` was `undefined`.

**4. A class `callAsFunction` that returns NULL.** The result goes through `toJS(globalObject, NULL)`, which is `null` (L567); the port returned `undefined`. Functions made by `JSObjectMakeFunctionWithCallback` and static functions already return `undefined` on both sides and are unchanged.

Left as it was, in the debt fragment: after an enumeration the name of a declining static value still answers as present, and the `Symbol.hasInstance` of point 2 is an own property a script can see, which JavaScriptCore does not have.

### Tested

Windows 11, MinGW GCC 15.2. Not tested on a console.

- New test `nkwebkit_jscclasscallbacks` (new file `tests/JscClassCallbacks.cpp`): one function per point, by script and through the C API, with the callback declining and answering, and with parent and child classes where only one has the callback.
- With `JscObject.cpp` from #25407 the test fails; with the change it passes, and `nkwebkit_jscclassprototype`, `nkwebkit_jscconstructor` and `nkwebkit_jsc` still pass.
- Negative controls: 11 mutations, each rebuilt and run on its own, all make the test fail: a declining `convertToType` giving `undefined`, an object result passed through, four on the ordinary conversion, `hasInstance` needing a callback again, a static value assumed present or described without a value, the static-value lookup stopped at the current class (the parent's `hasProperty` callback then runs before the parent's static value, which `getStaticValue` does not do), and a NULL call result as `undefined`.
- `python tools/check_conventions.py --base origin/main` and `python core/libs/tests/test_public_headers.py --audit-only` pass. `python tools/debt_fold.py --check` fails for the reason it fails on `main` today (two `libkernel_sys` fragments, #25313 and #25318).

**Not verified.** The expected values come from reading the JavaScriptCore source, not from running a WebKit binary.

**Overlap** (`python tools/pr_overlap.py --branch fix/nkwebkit-js-class-callbacks`):

- The tool reports no overlap with open pull requests, apart from #25406 and #25407, which this one is stacked on.

- [x] Based on current `main`; no other open PR implements the same functions
- [x] One topic per PR; follow-ups go in a new PR
- [x] No comments in code except [technical debt](https://github.com/boykopovar/AnyPS5/blob/main/docs/dev/CONVENTIONS.md) and the licence notice of code adapted from upstream (see AGENTS.md)
- [x] Unimplemented paths throw (`NotImplemented_nid_no_patch`); silent stubs are listed under Silent stubs in their library's [technical debt](https://github.com/boykopovar/AnyPS5/tree/main/docs/dev/debt) file

author: viditnanda
body:
## Two fixes for `cubes` input

**1. Memory.** `build_cubical_sparse` kept two `std::map<std::vector<int64_t>, …>`: one from coordinates to births, one from coordinates to ids. At about 100 bytes per node, that dominated memory and time on large inputs. It never built a dense grid; the cost was entirely the maps.
- Doubled coordinates are now packed into one 64-bit key per cell, with axis 0 most significant. Key order therefore is the lexicographic order of the old builder.
- Each cell type (the set of axes the cell spans) is a sorted array. Faces are found by binary search in the type below.
- The complex and its numbering are identical to the old builder's. The old builder stays as the fallback when the bounding box does not fit in 63 bits.
- `read_cubes` merges repeated cubes by sorting instead of through a map.

**2. Integral output.** The algebraic Morse reduction ran only for `cells` and `sset`. With `--integral`, every other explicit format went straight to dense Smith forms and refused anything large. The reduction now also runs for every explicit format when `--integral`, `--image` or `--torsion` is requested. Barcode-only runs are unchanged.

## Measurements

| input | before | after |
|---|---|---|
| two spheres meeting in a circle, 1.9M top cubes (15.6M cells), Q barcode | 35 s, 4.49 GB | 15 s, 2.12 GB |
| same, `--integral --image 0,1` | refused ("too large for dense Smith forms", 2.0M × 5.9M) | Z, 0, Z³ in 22 s, 3.33 GB (15.6M → 4 cells) |

## Summary

On the web, a loading Skeleton keyed each placeholder by its box. Two elements drawn whole at the same box, such as stacked 40×40 icons, gave two placeholders with one key. React then logged `Encountered two children with the same key, 149,3884,40,40`, and the two overlapping 15% boxes drew one darker spot.

```diff
 measureSkeleton(root)
   walkChildren(root, scene)
-  return scene.found
+  return { ...scene.found, placeholders: onePerBox(scene.found.placeholders) }   # first drawn wins

 <Placeholders>
-  key={keyOf(placeholder)}        # local to skeleton.tsx
```

iOS and Android draw placeholders natively and are untouched.

body:
## What

Auxiliary LLM calls (vision, titles, summaries, compression) and the OpenRouter image/video plugins now send `provider.data_collection` with the profile's configured value (`provider_routing.data_collection`, forced to `deny` by boot on every profile).

- New `hermes_cli/fork_ext/openrouter_data_policy.py`: reads the configured value and returns a copy of the request body with it set in `provider`. The config value wins over a caller's `data_collection`; other caller `provider` keys are kept; a config read failure sends nothing extra and never fails the request.
- `agent/auxiliary_client.py` `_build_call_kwargs`: applied when the destination is OpenRouter (by provider name or `openrouter.ai` host).
- `plugins/image_gen/openrouter`: applied on both the Image API and the chat-image paths, only for `openrouter.ai`.
- `plugins/video_gen/openrouter`: applied before `POST /videos`, only for `openrouter.ai`. No `zdr` (OpenRouter documents that no video endpoint offers it).

## Why

Boot's `deny` reached only the main turn, cron agent, delegation and the auditor judge. These paths build their own bodies and can carry client data, so OpenRouter could route them to providers that train on prompts. Decision of 2026-11-21: the bar for client data is GDPR, with `deny` on every OpenRouter call.

## Reviewer notes

- The main turn is untouched, so the per-conversation prompt cache is not affected.
- A `:free` aux fallback model now fails routing instead of answering (free models train on prompts). Production vision uses `deepseek/deepseek-v4.1-flash`, which already works under `deny` on the main turn.
- On `/images` and `/videos` OpenRouter documents `deny` as "no training", not "no retention".
- Not verified against the live API: whether the video model in use has a provider that accepts `deny`. The image model (`bytedance-seed/seedream-4.5`) is on the ZDR list.
- Needs a deploy to take effect; meant to be batched with the next one.

## Tests

- `tests/hermes_cli/test_openrouter_data_policy_fork.py`: 27 passed; the aux tests fail with the aux hunk reverted (checked).
- `tests/agent/test_provider_parity.py tests/test_provider_data_collection_deny.py tests/plugins/image_gen tests/plugins/video_gen tests/agent/test_auxiliary_client.py`: 604 passed, 1 failed (pre-existing: the local venv lacks the `anthropic` package).
- `ruff check` on the changed files: clean.

## Docs

`CLAUDE.md` privacy section and the `boot_reconcile.py` comment updated to say these paths now send the policy.

body:
🤖 Generated with [Claude Code](https://claude.com/claude-code)

https://claude.ai/code/session_01LBDG2hS6jhyigc59FqqP8s

## Why

An app on the composable runtime (Silk UI's `Runtime.node()`) parses its whole bundle at every launch and keeps the parse heap. The engine has bytecode images for this (`js_bytecode_image`), but the runtime had no way to use one, and an image could only run under the file name it was written with. A desktop app's bundle is named by where the app is installed, which the build does not know.

The compile cache (`NODE_COMPILE_CACHE`) was measured as the alternative and is not it: it turns lazy compilation off, and a 66 MB bundle then holds about 636 MB more heap.

## What

- `Runtime.writeModuleImage(name, source)` compiles an ES module into a bytecode image without running it. `Runtime.evaluateModuleImage(name, source, data, length)` runs it with nothing parsed: each function's code stays in the image's bytes until its first call. `moduleImageLoadable` says whether this build wrote the bytes.
- `js_bytecode_image.loadNamed` gives the decoded script or module another file name: the module's own name, which its imports resolve from, and its functions' file name.
- A function that a deferred read brings later takes the file name and the host values (owning module, `import()` callback, script metadata) of the function that holds it. A lazy reparse now gives its descendants the host values too. Without this, `import.meta` in a function nested in a deferred or lazy function threw "import.meta not supported in this context".
- A module run from an image is reported to the host as a compiled one is (script metadata with the lazy `source`, the source map registry, coverage, the inspector). The source map comment is found in the last bytes of the text, so a text that is part of the program is not paged in.

## Tests

- `js_bytecode_image_named_tests`: an image written as `/built/app.js` runs as `/installed/app.js`, and functions read at their first call report the new name (fails without the reader change).
- The embedding smoke test now runs its module from an image written under another folder, with a different `./lib.mjs` beside that name, and checks `import.meta.url` in a nested function. Both ran here: the smoke program without WebAssembly prints the expected lines and ends with status 3.

## Note

The branch starts from 258e3fb (Silk dev.94) so Silk UI, still on dev.94, can pin its commit. Please merge with a merge commit so the commit stays on main.

author: ajmyers
body:
Phase 3 step 2: rule checks and traces on `CubeService`, plus a small odata addition they need.

## What changed

- **`Tm1Request.postList(path, body, itemType)`:** a POST whose response is a collection, streamed like any other. Actions such as `CheckRules` return `Collection(...)`, which no existing factory could express.
- **`checkRules(cube)`** compiles the saved rules. **`checkRules(cube, rules)`** checks proposed ones without saving them, which matters because TM1 saves rules that don't compile.
- **`traceCellCalculation`** and **`traceFeeders`** explain one cell. **`checkFeeders`** lists the fed and unfed cells under a consolidation. All four need 11.1.0.
- **Result navigation.** The results' `Cube` navigation (`CalculationComponent/Cube`, `FedCellDescriptor/Cube`) is reached with the query's `$expand`, so those two endpoints are declared on the methods that return them.
- **Coverage.** Six endpoints come off the pending list. The gate now reports 71 implemented.
- **Plan.** §16.5 records the two findings below.

## Decisions

- **A cell is a `Map` of dimension name to element name**, in the cube's order, with each element in its dimension's same-named hierarchy. Plan §16.8 lists "tuples built from a `Map<dimension, element>`" among the helpers callers kept rewriting, and taking one here saves every caller from building element paths. Alternate hierarchies aren't covered yet.
- **The query goes on the action itself**, so callers choose what of the result to expand.
- **`postList` isn't retried on a dropped connection**, since a POST isn't idempotent. The replay after a 401 still applies, because TM1 doesn't run a request it answers with 401 (pinned in phase 0).

## Pinned against TM1 (11.8.35)

- A syntax error is reported with its line number, and checking doesn't save.
- A trace names the rule statement and, when expanded, the cell and the cube.
- `$expand` into a complex property needs a path (`FedCells/Tuple`); nested options get 400. `traceFeeders`' Javadoc says so.
- `checkFeeders` over a consolidation reports the fed rule cell once there's a value to feed from. The test writes that value through the raw session, since cell writes are phase 4.

Closes #100

author: mgh3326
body:
## Summary

The held pass (`makeHeldBatches`) and the digest pass (`makeBatchesDue`, digest branch) each scan `lane_inbox` by a predicate that no index matched. The lane-leading hold and digest indexes do not bind `lane`, so each pass read most of the table, at least every 60 s and after every write (about 17 % of hub-schema reads).

- **SQLite** (`openLaneInboxStore`): two partial indexes on `id`, each partial on its pass's own predicate: `lane_inbox_hold_pending` and `lane_inbox_digest_pending`. `EXPLAIN QUERY PLAN` for both statements now searches the new index; on base both were `SCAN lane_inbox`.
- **Postgres**: migration `0038_lane_inbox_pass_indexes.sql`, the same two partial indexes.
- **MySQL**: migration `0031_lane_inbox_pass_indexes.sql`, one `ALTER` adding two composite keys, because MySQL has no partial indexes. `(digest_batch, hold_until)` serves the held pass (seek the unbatched group, range over `hold_until>0`). `(class, digest_batch, digest_at)` serves the digest pass (seek the pending interrupt group, range over `digest_at>0`). `acked_at`, `superseded_at` and `hold_until=0` are checked on the rows the seek returns.
- The two statements move into `laneInboxHeldQuery` and `laneInboxDigestDueQuery`, so the plan test runs the SQL production runs. Their SQL text is unchanged. The escalation variant keeps its text.
- `docs/hub-postgres.md` "Scan cost" gains a bullet naming the indexes.

The migration numbers are the next free ones. The brief's `mysql 0030` and `postgres 0037` were already taken by `spawn_operations.trace_history` (hk 6074).

The migration is additive. An older binary never names these indexes.

## Tests

- `TestLaneInboxPassIndexesHaveAMigrationOnEveryDialect_hk6081`: reads the Postgres and MySQL migration files and requires both index names in each. Like the t5776 check, it needs no database.
- `TestLaneInboxPassQueriesUseTheirPartialIndexes_hk6081`: SQLite `EXPLAIN QUERY PLAN` for both statements must search the new index and must not `SCAN lane_inbox`.
- `TestLaneInboxPassesClaimTheSameRowsOnEveryBackend_hk6081`: a fixture covering pending, acked, superseded, already-batched and not-yet-due rows. It checks that both scans select the expected rows, then runs `makeBatchesDue` and `makeHeldBatches` and checks the claimed rows. It runs on every `laneInboxBackends()` backend, so Postgres and MySQL run it in CI.

Run locally, in the worktree: `gofmt -l .` (clean), `go vet ./...` (clean), `go test -run 'TestLaneInboxPass' .` (SQLite passes; the Postgres and MySQL subtests skip because no database URL is set), and `go test -run 'Migration|LaneInbox|InboxHold|Batch' .` (passes). The Postgres and MySQL DDL and the pass fixture on those backends are unverified until CI runs them.

🔬 Measurements and explain-the-number checks are on the hk task; the SQLite plan change is shown by the test above.

author: djbclark
body:
## Bug

Operator djbclark: "I don't see a tab open for your successor". Verified 2026-11-22: in the `fork-release-alerts` chain `4c3521b9-65c8-4fba-be7f-d44cae5c1d3e` -> `4fd28378-a943-4809-ba35-b052f1553626` -> `96711956-9bf6-44c9-b646-eac2e975ec6d` all three Paseo agents carry the identical name `fork-release-alerts` (handoff records: `identity.title_source = predecessor-name`; `plan_identity`'s chain requested -> predecessor-name -> chain-record -> derived). So the sidebar cannot tell the live lead from retired ones, and a retired predecessor the operator types into (Paseo un-archives on a message) looks exactly like the live lead.

## Design choice and why

1. **Rename the retired predecessor, not the successor.** After `finish` confirms the archive, a predecessor whose current name equals the successor's inherited title is renamed `RETIRED <old name> (-> <successor full id>)` (`agent update PRED --name=...`), then read back with `agent inspect`. The successor keeps the plain name (no generation counter in the lead's own title; the live lead stays the one clean name).
   - **Order (after archive, never before).** Read in getpaseo/paseo a3aa8afaa: `agent update` -> `updateAgentCommand` -> `updateAgentMetadata`; for a non-live (archived) agent it goes through `writeStoredMetadata`, which spreads the stored record and changes only `title`/`labels`/`updatedAt`, keeping `archivedAt`; the live path's `applySnapshot` also preserves `archivedAt`. So a rename does not un-archive. A rename before the archive would call a still-live agent RETIRED through the AGENT_RUNNING retry loop. The readback checks `Archived` is still true anyway: if some Paseo version un-archived on rename it is recorded as `failed: rename-unarchived-predecessor`, never "fixed" with a second archive.
   - Skips: `names-differ` (a `--title`/other name already tells them apart; final), `malformed-identity` (final), `predecessor-not-archived` (retried), `already-retired` (ok, nothing renamed twice). Truncation cuts the old name, never the suffix, to Paseo's 200 UTF-16 units.
   - A `RETIRED ...` name is never inherited as the next successor's title (revived retired agent handing off falls to the chain record).
   - The id in the retired title: the old `plan_identity` rule (no agent id in a lead title, paseo#9668 partial-title archive fallback) protects live leads. This title is on an archived agent, which a title match can only meet as `AGENT_ALREADY_ARCHIVED`; `finish` also refuses to archive when the id is absent from the listing (`LISTING_GAP`). Docstring and docs say so.
2. **Window name: advise, do not rename.** `ade-worker-run rename-lead` resolves the window from the calling lead's own agent record and holds its own lock; the window name is the operator's sidebar. `finish` (run by the successor) reads `paseo workspace ls`, checks the successor's window against `LEAD <repo> (<work>)`, and records `lead_window` (`ok` / `rename-advised` with `command: ade-worker-run rename-lead --lead <successor id>` / `unknown` with reason), also printed on stderr. Read-only.
3. **Visible, never fatal.** `identity.checks.retire_rename` = `ok|skipped|failed`, detail in `identity.retire_rename` (`reason`, `name`, `native_error`). Both steps run after the archive and again on a re-run of an archived record (a failed rename is retried); a failure never fails `finish`.

## Tests

`tests/test_self_session.py`: 402 passed (was 387; 15 new tests incl. 4 parametrized cases, 3 existing assertions updated for the new `retire_rename` check and the predecessor rename). With `tests/test_ade_lead_succession.py` and `tests/test_archived_send_guard.py`: 740 passed. `tests/test_ade_coord_adapter.py::test_reclaim_cannot_publish_legacy_record_over_enrolled_workspace` fails on origin/master too (checked with the change reverted: `CLAIM_RESOURCES_NOT_BOUND`); unrelated to this PR.

Mutation checks (each mutant applied alone, focused `-k`, run under bgrun, original restored and compared byte for byte): 16 of 16 killed: no rename call; no un-archive readback; no name readback; `names-differ` branch removed; `already-retired` branch removed; suffix truncation removed; `SessionError` not caught (rename refusal fatal); no retry on re-run; `predecessor-not-archived` check removed; `malformed-identity` not skipped; revived-RETIRED name inherited; LEAD window never `ok`; window advice always `ok`; window listing error fatal; archived-re-run rename dropped; end-of-finish rename dropped.

Prior art / docs checked: read getpaseo/paseo a3aa8afaa (`lifecycle-command.ts` updateAgentCommand, `agent-manager.ts` updateAgentMetadata/writeStoredMetadata/setTitle, `agent-storage.ts` applySnapshot, `cli agent/update.ts`); firecrawl web and developer search for an upstream issue on renaming archived agents: none found.

Not done: nothing here touched the live Paseo daemon or real agents (all fakes); no live `load-watch ci decide`. The installed Paseo build was not probed for rename-on-archived behavior (the readback records it at the first real finish).

🤖 Generated with [Claude Code](https://claude.com/claude-code)

Adversary verdict (prose, lead 22d935c8-34f4-4e73-9e0b-41ec589553a6): APPROVE on head 1c23c4a5287de956a6314b26b30b1e7ceaa586b6 (HIGH 0, MED 0, LOW 3). The successor id in the RETIRED title is safe: server-side resolution (send/inspect/wait/update) takes only exact id, id prefix or exact title, which a RETIRED title can never equal; the CLI partial-title fallback (paseo#9668) can only hit the retired agent, never the live lead. LOWs to a follow-up PR: (1) docs say a title match can only meet AGENT_ALREADY_ARCHIVED, untrue once revived; (2) rename-lead advice never fires for a successor placed in a new workspace (looks up the predecessor's workspace); (3) LEAD_WINDOW.fullmatch -> match mutant survives. test_ade_coord_adapter failure is pre-existing on base.

## 요약

`docs/feature-guidelines.md`를 추가했어요. 코드 변경은 없어요.

- 슬래시 명령 한도: 디스코드 공식 문서 기준 한도 표, 현재 beta의 글로벌 명령 31개(command piece 37개 중 개발 전용 6개 제외)를 `BOT_MODULES` 모듈별로 센 표, 서브커맨드로 묶을지 판단하는 기준, 모듈별 상한 제안(제안일 뿐 코드로 강제되지 않는다고 명시)
- 새 기능 도입 기준: 코드로 확인되는 규칙만 적었어요 (지표 키, 모듈 소속과 토글, 개인정보 영향, `GuildJobScheduler`의 `kind` 핸들러, 인텐트). 인텐트는 D-13에 따라 새 기능 기준만 적었어요.
- `docs/README.md` 색인, 루트 `README.md`, `README.ko.md` 문서 표에 링크를 추가했어요.
- 명령 개수는 현재 beta 기준이고, `/설정` 통합 PR이 머지되면 3개(`mixer`, `chat-settings`, `chattools`) 줄어 28개가 된다고 문서에 적었어요.
- 호환성: 데이터 마이그레이션, 저장 형식, API 변경 없음.

## 결정 로그

- 모듈별 상한(전체 50, 모듈별 합 42)은 근거가 되는 코드 규칙이 없어서 "제안"으로 표시했어요.
- 코드로 확인하지 못한 규칙(예: 비용 상한 장치)은 "코드에 없음"으로만 적었어요.
- 개인정보 보관 기간 값은 P-13에서 미정이라 숫자를 쓰지 않았어요.

## 검증

- 문서의 모든 파일 경로가 실제 존재하는지 스크립트로 확인했어요 (확장자 있는 경로 중 누락은 파일명만 적은 `emojiEnlarge.ts`, `helpCatalog.test.ts` 두 건이고, 둘 다 같은 문서에 전체 경로가 있어요).
- 명령 개수는 `apps/bot/src/core/pieceInventory.test.ts`의 `EXPECTED_COMMAND_CATEGORIES`와 `packages/utils/src/modules.ts`의 `commands` 배열, 각 command 파일의 `addSubcommand(` 호출 수로 셌어요.
- 한도 수치는 https://docs.discord.com/developers/interactions/application-commands 를 2026-11-22에 읽고 적었어요. 웹 도구가 요약한 결과라 한도에 가까워질 때는 원문 재확인이 필요해요.
- 미검증: `yarn lint`는 워크트리에 `node_modules`가 없어 실행하지 못했어요. 또 `yarn lint`(turbo)는 `src/**/*.ts`만 검사해서 md는 대상이 아니에요. 참고로 prettier를 md에 직접 돌리면 이번에 안 건드린 기존 문서(`docs/architecture.md` 등)도 경고가 나요.
- 미검증: 기존 명령별 8000자 크기 (측정한 적 없음).
- CI는 이 브랜치에서 돌고, 결과는 PR 체크에서 확인해요.
