body: ## Issue Reference No tracking issue. This closes the gap that dependency scanning was not enforced. ## Description Dependabot now opens weekly update pull requests for: - Composer (`composer.lock` at the repo root; package composer.json files have no lockfiles of their own) - npm at `/`, `packages/Webkul/Admin`, `packages/Webkul/Installer`, and `packages/Webkul/WebForm` - GitHub Actions - Docker (`docker/Dockerfile`) and Compose (`compose.yaml`, `compose.prod.yaml`) Minor and patch updates are grouped. Major updates stay as their own pull requests. CI gains a Dependency Audit job. `composer audit --locked` fails on any known advisory (Composer 2.11 needs `--locked` before packages are installed). `npm audit --audit-level=high` runs for every project lockfile and fails on high and critical advisories. Laravel's own lockfile under `vendor/` is excluded. The secret scan still uses Gitleaks on the full history of the commit under test. It no longer scans every other branch that `fetch-depth: 0` downloads. Current findings, and what landed: | Lockfile | Before | After | | --- | --- | --- | | Root `package-lock.json` | 3 high: follow-redirects 1.16.0, source-map-js 1.2.1, vite 6.4.3 (launch-editor and dev-server advisories) | follow-redirects 1.16.3, source-map-js 1.2.4, vite 6.4.6. `npm audit` reports 0. | | `packages/Webkul/Admin/package-lock.json` | 2 high, 3 moderate | 0. follow-redirects 1.16.3, postcss-selector-parser 6.1.6, esbuild 0.25.12, `@vitejs/plugin-vue` 5.2.4, vite 6.4.6. | | Installer and WebForm lockfiles | already clean (Vite 6.4.5) | unchanged | | `composer.lock` | `composer audit --locked` reports no advisories | unchanged | Vite 5 has no patched release for the admin highs (the advisories cover every release through 6.4.3). Admin now uses the same Vite 6 line and Vue plugin the installer and web form already build with (`vite` `^6.4.4`, `@vitejs/plugin-vue` `^5.2.1`). `laravel-vite-plugin` 1.3.0 already accepts Vite 6. That is a major bump of two dev dependencies, and the admin production build still succeeds. CSS and JS bundle sizes stay within about 1 percent of the Vite 5 output. No advisory was left behind, so there is no ignore entry. ## How To Test This? ```bash composer audit --locked npm audit --audit-level=high npm audit --audit-level=high --prefix packages/Webkul/Admin npm audit --audit-level=high --prefix packages/Webkul/Installer npm audit --audit-level=high --prefix packages/Webkul/WebForm npm run build npm run build --prefix packages/Webkul/Admin npm run build --prefix packages/Webkul/Installer npm run build --prefix packages/Webkul/WebForm php artisan test --compact npm run test:js ``` Local results: `composer audit --locked` clean. All four npm audits clean at high (admin is clean at every severity). Root, admin, installer, and web form production builds succeeded. Pest: 657 passed (15135 assertions). JavaScript property tests, Pint, and PHPStan passed. ## Documentation - [ ] My pull request requires an update on the documentation repository. Changelog entry added under v2.2.9. No separate docs change. ## Branch Selection - [x] Target Branch: main ## Tailwind Reordering No Tailwind class changes. Admin assets were rebuilt because Vite moved from 5 to 6. The rebuilt CSS matches the previous rules aside from minifier whitespace.

author: miguelr0drigues
body:
## Why
Schools don't have a "relatório de execução curricular". What they do have is the *cumprimento das planificações* review: teacher → conselho de turma → departamento → conselho pedagógico. A director report only earns trust if it says what it counts and how much of the school it covers. It also can't present lessons delivered as "curriculum achieved".

## What changes (`/school/reports`, behind `class_state_enabled`)
- **Name:** "Balanço do cumprimento das planificações" (en: "Progress against lesson plans").
- **What is counted:** a note under the header. Percentages count the lessons planned to date whose content is not behind, from teachers' records. They are not what students mastered.
- **1. Registos (new):** "Registos confirmados em X de Y turmas com aulas previstas até hoje", plus the list of turmas with no records. These turmas used to drop out of the figures with no sign.
- **2. By department:** "586 de 588 aulas · 99%" instead of a bare percent. The 99% cap from #325 is kept.
- **3. Classes to follow up:** each one shows `Motivo: <newest check-in note>`, read from the existing `/direction/turmas/{id}` endpoint.
- **Dashboard and drawer labels:** "Aulas em dia" instead of "Execução do currículo". The English copy stays market-agnostic.

## Known limit
The reasons cost one detail request per class to follow up, marked `shortcut:` in the code. If schools end up with dozens of late classes, move the note into `/overview`.

## Checks
- vitest `school/direction` (15 tests), eslint and tsc pass on this branch.
- Checked signed in on local data (AE do Vale, 86 turmas): coverage 84/86, two no-records turmas listed, reasons shown.

author: haksungjang
body:
Single-choice button groups were drawn four different ways, and the scans status filter used buttons with role=tab whose selected option was filled navy like the primary button. This adds a value-based wrapper over Primer's SegmentedControl in components/primer and uses it for the scans status filter, the components Table/Graph switch and dependency-type selector, the vulnerabilities Group by selector and the dashboard 7d/30d/90d window. Existing test ids stay on each option button, and each option also carries data-active, so the harness and e2e specs read the selection as before. Keyboard behavior is Primer's (each option is a Tab stop, Enter or Space selects).

The scans table body is now 14px with the secondary columns (started, duration) at 12px muted, and the actions column has 24px right padding to match the first column.

On the vulnerabilities tab the sort option now reads "Priority" (the KEV, severity, EPSS order is in its tooltip). The track used a fixed 1740px floor for every column, so at 1440px with the sidebar open SLA due was cut at the right edge and three more columns sat off screen. The floor is now computed from the visible columns, several columns are narrower, and a fresh user starts without Title, Owner and Discovered (stored column choices are kept). The default set needs 1136px against a 1184px pane. The user guide notes the hidden defaults in EN and KO.

Visual baselines for the scans, dashboard, components and vulnerabilities screens will change and need regenerating in CI.

body:
## 수정

#132가 병합된 main `788e313`에 재배치했습니다. 제품 코드는 `material-context.ts`만 수정했습니다.

- 막·잔여물·찌꺼기·얼룩·부착물·묻음·끈적·슬러지·분진·이물을 공통 잔류 표현으로 묶어 질문 탐지와 명시 부정 처리에 함께 사용합니다. 설명·공정·오염 칸에 긍정 내용이 남으면 추가 정보를 요청합니다.
- `얼룩 없음`, `막·잔여물·이물 없음` 같은 완결된 부정문을 인정합니다. 분진·슬러지의 발생물 분류 검사도 같은 부정 처리를 사용해, 없다고 쓴 내용을 긍정으로 다시 읽지 않습니다.
- 다른 칸의 긍정과 알려진 위험·구조화된 접촉 상태는 기존 우선순위를 유지합니다. 납품·수납·납작과 막대·마지막은 짧은 물질/잔류 단어로 오인하지 않습니다.

## 리드 입력의 수정 전후

아래 수정 전 상태는 리드가 제공한 main 재현이며, 수정 후는 고정셋·네이티브 회귀 및 실제 local 폼 요청에서 확인했습니다. 첫 번째 입력은 자체 기준 실행에서도 같은 추천 누출을 재현했습니다.

| 입력란 | 정확한 입력 | 수정 전 | 수정 후 |
|---|---|---|---|
| 설명 | `합성 구리 스크랩, 끈적한 막` | 조건부 추천 | 추가 정보 필요 |
| 설명 | `구리 스크랩, 잔여물 있음` | 조건부 추천 | 추가 정보 필요 |
| 설명 | `구리판, 얼룩 없음` | 추가 정보 필요 | 조건부 추천 |
| 오염 | `막·잔여물·이물 없음` | 추가 정보 필요 | 조건부 추천 |

## 고정셋과 보존

- 기존 60건의 입력과 기대값을 유지하고 일반 잔류 표현 71건을 추가했습니다. 총 131건이며 입력 원본과 개별 해시를 갱신했습니다.
- 초기 추가 68건은 수정 전 31건만 기대와 일치했고 수정 후 68건 모두 일치했습니다. 추천 → 질문 12건, 불필요한 질문 → 조건부 추천 21건, 필요한 오염 질문 보완 4건입니다. 추가 리드 입력 3건도 통과했습니다.
- 원래 18건: 원본 해시와 전체 판정 18/18 동일, 상태 변화 0건.
- 기존 안전셋 60건: 입력 해시와 **전체 판정 해시 60/60 동일**.
- 확장 안전셋: **131/131 기대 일치**. 조건부 추천 47 / 추가 정보 필요 64 / 검토 필요 20입니다. 노출된 합성 개발 입력의 회귀 결과이며 현장 정확도나 모든 자연어 표현의 안전성 보장은 아닙니다.

기준 실행은 `61b6fab`에서 수행했습니다. #132의 변경은 안내 문구와 관련 테스트이며, `788e313`의 안전 판정 코드는 기준 실행과 같습니다. 최종 검증은 재배치와 리드 입력 추가 후 수행했습니다.

## 검증

- 관련 재질·네이티브 회귀: **204 pass / 0 fail**.
- `bun test --timeout 30000 ./tests`: **1,738 pass / 0 fail**, 78개 파일.
- 타입 검사 2종, 빌드 2종, 스모크 통과. 스모크는 `SCAFFOLD_ONLY`이며 실제 모델 호출이 없습니다.
- 실제 local 서버에서 설명·공정·오염의 질문 전환과 명시 부정을 확인했습니다. 추가 리드 입력 세 건은 정확한 문자열로 제출하고 원본 내보내기 보존까지 확인했습니다.
- 독립 검토: **APPROVE / high confidence**, 차단 지적 없음. 131건의 입력·결과, 원래 18건과 기존 60건의 해시 보존, 최종 테스트 로그를 대조했습니다. 기록: `.omo/evidence/general-residue/gate-review.md`.

재현 명령: `bun scripts/measure-guidance.ts --out /absolute/path/to/new-evidence-directory`

로컬 증거: `.omo/evidence/general-residue/`의 `before/`, `after132/`, `prior60-comparison-132.json`, `focused-132.log`, `full-132.log`, `types-132.log`, `build-smoke-132.log`, `native-http-qa.json`, `native-http-lead-132.json`.

화면 구조·가격·업종·대안 경로를 변경하지 않았습니다. 기존 명시 부정·위험 우선 규칙을 재사용한 작은 어휘 보완입니다.

author: eichann
body:
## 概要（オーナー向け）

段 4b-2：出来事をきっかけに、責任者のパソコンの AI が仕事を動かす「アプリ側」です。

- **変わること**
  - アプリが「出来事の仕事を受け取れます」とサーバーに伝えます。
  - AI が動いている間、アプリは「まだ動いてよいか」をサーバーに確かめ続けます。次のときは AI を止めます。
    - 確かめが3分取れないとき（スリープ中の時間も数えます）
    - サーバーが「だめ」と返したとき
  - 1回の確かめで返事を待つのは30秒です（オーナー決定）。
  - AI を始める直前にもう一度確かめます。断られたとき、または時間が切れていたときは始めません。
  - 前の作業への遅い返事で、今の作業が延びることはありません。
  - 設定 →「定期の仕事」に「AI が動いた回で、確かめが要るもの」を足しました。押せる人にだけ、「もう一度」と「作られていた／作られていなかった」が出ます。
- **時刻の仕事にも、同じ止める決まりが当たります**：通信が悪いと途中で止まる回が増えます。止まった回は、あとで「もう一度」できます。
- **変わらないこと**
  - 「AI の番」の作業とプラグインの手順は今のままです（オーナー決定：別に考える）。
  - 時刻の仕事の引き受けでサーバーに送る中身は、前とまったく同じです。
- **今の利用者が安全な理由**：出来事の仕事は、管理画面（4b-3）ができるまで作れません。古い版のサーバー（4b-0.5）に戻した場合も、出来事の回は渡されず、動いていた実行は止まります。
- **入っていないもの**：止まったつながりの念押しの知らせ。サーバー側の小さな別の PR にします（オーナー決定）。

## Details (English)

Stage 4b-2 (app side of event jobs run by the responsible person's PC AI; server side was #724).

- Turn list asks `kinds=time,event`; only an event claim sends `kinds` and the `source_record` check. A time claim body is byte-identical to before (deepEqual test). Event turns are parsed with strict pairing; harmless time-turn forms (`kind:'time'`, `source:null`) are accepted.
- Fail-closed hold for every job run (`claims.ts`):
  - renew deadline 30 s (`JOB_RENEW_TIMEOUT_MS`), interval 60 s;
  - confirmation counted from the renew's send;
  - age = max(monotonic, wall) elapsed, so sleep or a forward jump counts and a clock set back never extends;
  - watch tick every 15 s; the AI stops past 3 min unconfirmed, or at once on renew 401/403/404/409 and on run-ending token-call refusals;
  - an expired hold is never revived by a late renew (checked before send and before accept);
  - answers count only for the hold that sent them (opaque hold handle).
- Pre-start confirm; refused → nothing starts; unanswered → given back `NOT_CONFIRMED`; cutoff reached during confirm → `TIME_LIMIT`, no start. After the turn is tracked, chat-server re-checks the job's tool ceiling and aborts with `job-ended` if the run was lost while preparing (or timed out).
- D11 screen from `GET /me/job-occurrences`; new IPC `jobs:occurrences` / `jobs:retryOccurrence` / `jobs:reconcileOccurrence`, ids validated before URLs; unknown later-server values keep the entry (generic words) so 「後始末」 is never hidden. A server older than 4b-1 (404) shows nothing.
- `APP_JOB_SCHEMAS` → `[1,2,3]`. Rules updated: `jobs.md`, `ai-turns.md`; IPC inventory regenerated.

Reviews: independent review (2 medium, 5 low — all fixed), Codex 4 passes (2 P2 fixed; final pass "No actionable regressions"). Every new guard mutation-checked; guards not caught alone are named in `jobs.md` with their reason (pairs where either half suffices).

## Decisions for the owner
- Renew deadline 30 s (owner), 3-minute window (recommended, kept).
- The fail-closed stop also applies to time jobs (safe side, D12).
- Record runs (「AI の番」) unchanged for now (owner: consider separately).
- Stopped-chain reminder left to a separate server PR (owner).
- A `NOT_IN_STEP` token refusal also stops the run (cannot be told apart from a failed condition).
- A current responsible person who was not the pinned one does not see those occurrences in the app (their retry would be refused anyway).

Fixes #35

- **Cancelled send releases its reservation:** `send` and `send_within_budget` now share `Tx::enqueue`, which holds a `Release` drop guard. It is disarmed only once the message is in the channel (the writer releases it then); a dropped future (caller `timeout`) or closed channel releases the bytes.

body:
Settings reads and writes are now authorized in the service layer (SDK and API alike).

- Value writes/deletes: ISettingsAuthorizer checks level and scope. System = SuperAdmin.
  Tenant = SuperAdmin or settings.manage.tenant in the current tenant (TenantAdmin via bypass).
  Lower levels via optional ISettingScopeOwnerResolver, else SuperAdmin only.
  Allow-all default when the auth module is not registered.
- Admin writes (levels, groups, definitions): [RequiresRole("SuperAdmin")].
  Listing reads: [RequiresPermission("settings.read")]. Effective-value reads stay open.
- Startup fails if the auth module is registered but the settings services are not
  registered with AddAuthorized.
- Setup wizard keys are writable at System level without a user until setup completes.
- Secrets stay masked for everyone.
- Fix: AuthorizationInterceptor now applies the SuperAdmin/TenantAdmin bypass for
  [RequiresPermission] (affects every AddAuthorized service).
- Permission keys: + settings.manage.tenant; - settings.write, settings.delete (unused).

Tests: unit 1623 / 12 known; integration 357 / 48 known (+17 new); sample 22/22.

author: razisnihaa
body:
## Résumé

Cette PR ajoute le module d'irrigation FARMLINK : quelles parcelles arroser, quand et combien.

- **Moteur dans l'API** (`services/api`)
  - `GET /api/v1/irrigation/crops` : les 39 cultures FAO-56, avec leurs noms en français et en arabe.
  - `POST /api/v1/irrigation/farm` : récupère la météo du jour (Open-Meteo, NASA POWER en secours, choix enregistré), puis appelle le moteur (`run_farm`). Renvoie la décision par parcelle, les priorités et le partage de l'eau, ou 503 si aucune météo n'est disponible.
  - Le moteur est copié sans modification dans `app/irrigation/engine/` depuis `research/irrigation-notebook`. Ce dossier est exclu de ruff et de mypy (copie d'un code externe).
  - CORS réglable avec `CORS_ALLOW_ORIGINS`. Par défaut : localhost:3000 et :8080.
- **Notebook corrigé (v3.1)** dans `research/irrigation-notebook/` : notebook Kaggle, résultats de l'exécution, modèle sauvegardé, paquet du moteur et README simple.
- **Pages HTML** dans `research/irrigation-notebook/html/` :
  - `ferme_3d.html` : la ferme en 3D pour l'agriculteur. Elle appelle l'API quand celle-ci tourne, sinon elle affiche une démo.
  - `banc_essai.html` : le banc d'essai des modules.

Le dossier `research/` n'est pas lu par la CI.

## Tests

- `services/api/tests/unit/test_irrigation.py` : 11 nouveaux tests, avec une météo déterministe (sans réseau). Ils vérifient :
  - la liste des cultures ;
  - la décision par parcelle ;
  - que la réponse de l'API est identique à `run_farm` ;
  - qu'une culture inconnue est signalée et non devinée ;
  - le 503 en cas de panne météo ;
  - le rejet (422) des entrées invalides.
- En local, toutes les étapes de la CI passent : `ruff check`, `ruff format --check` et `mypy app` sans erreur, `pytest` 12 réussis.
- Testé aussi en vrai avec la météo du 22/11/2026 : Open-Meteo, Penman-Monteith, 15 jours de prévision.

## Points d'attention

- Nouvelles dépendances de l'API : `numpy`, `pandas`, `requests`. Le fichier `uv.lock` est mis à jour.
- Avec pandas 3, le moteur affiche un avertissement de dépréciation (`dt.dayofyear`). Les tests passent quand même.
- Le partage de l'eau suit la règle du moteur : protéger, puis remplir. Après avoir protégé les parcelles urgentes, il continue de remplir les autres jusqu'à leur capacité au champ, même celles qui n'ont pas besoin d'être arrosées.
- Les volumes restent indicatifs tant que le type de sol et les capteurs ne sont pas mesurés ou calibrés sur la parcelle.

Descrição:

Cria a página **Julgamento da Avaliação** (`docs/fase-4/julgamento.md`), que aplica aos resultados da Fase 4 os critérios de julgamento definidos na Fase 2 (`niveis-pontuacao.md`), e inclui os dados e cálculos das métricas que faltavam (M1, M2, M10, M15 e M20).

2. **Respostas às questões e hipóteses:** resposta a Q1–Q16 e classificação de H1–H16 (Tabelas 2 a 5).

## Esforço acima de 4 h (I3)

- **Caio Borges (7,2 h):** a maior parte vem de `coleta/inspecao_coleta.py` (535 linhas), que automatizou o primeiro avaliador da inspeção de M1, M2, M10 e M20, mais a conferência manual como segundo avaliador e o fechamento do julgamento.

author: alemenon
body:
TASK-19 — Ajustar mecanismos de controle de saturação

Objetivo

Aprimorar o controle de carga dos servidores Python e C++, com base nos gargalos identificados nos experimentos da TASK-18.

Alterações realizadas

  • Implementação de limite configurável de requisições em processamento ou aguardando (max_inflight).

  • Aprimoramento do controle de admissão e rejeição por saturação.

  • Preservação das requisições já aceitas.

  • Exposição de novos indicadores de admissão e saturação.

  • Implementação de testes automatizados e experimentos comparativos antes/depois.

  • Documentação dos mecanismos e resultados obtidos.

Configurações avaliadas

Parâmetro | Antes | Depois -- | -- | -- Workers | 1 | 2 Capacidade da fila | 2 | 8 Limite de admissão | 3 | 6

Foram utilizados três clientes simultâneos, matriz sintética densa task18_dense_512 e cargas de 45, 90 e 180 requisições, com duas repetições por cenário.

Resultados

C++

A configuração ajustada eliminou as rejeições por saturação em todos os cenários executados. Todas as requisições foram aceitas, e o servidor permaneceu estável.

Python

Houve aumento no número de requisições aceitas nos cenários de 45 e 90 requisições. Entretanto, no cenário de 180 requisições, a quantidade de aceites foi inferior à configuração original, indicando que os ajustes não produzem melhorias uniformes em todas as cargas.

Estabilidade

As 24 execuções retornaram stable=True.

Limitações

author: zby9999
body:
Closes #21

Stacked on #59 (#20); base is `20-pi-rpc-start`. Retarget to `main` after #59 merges.

## Mapping (`packages/agent-host/src/pi-events.ts`)

| Pi RPC record | Timeline entry |
|---|---|
| `message_update` / `text_delta` (assistant) | `agent_message_delta` (a `"\n\n"` delta between text blocks) |
| `message_end` (assistant) | `agent_message` with the final text; `stopReason: "error"` → `error` (origin `agent`), with the `pi auth login` hint on 401/auth failures |
| `auto_retry_start` / `auto_retry_end` | kept as `unknown_agent_event`; a failed attempt's error is held back, so a retry that recovers leaves no error and one that fails leaves exactly one |
| `tool_execution_start` | `tool_call` |
| `tool_execution_end` | `tool_result`; `isError` → also `error` (origin `tool`); successful `write`/`edit` → `file_edit` (project-relative path, `create`/`modify`, Pi's unified `patch` as `diff`) |
| `extension_error`, failed `compaction_end` | `error` (origin `agent`) |
| `extension_ui_request` `notify` with `notifyType: "error"` | `error` (origin `agent`) |
| `extension_ui_request` `setStatus` / `setWidget` / `setTitle` / `set_editor_text` | no entry: terminal UI state. A real Pi with the user's extensions sends many of these, found while checking #23. |
| `agent_settled` with `aborted: true` | kept as `unknown_agent_event` |
| structural: `agent_start/end`, `turn_start/end`, non-aborted `agent_settled`, `tool_execution_update`, `queue_update`, thinking/tool-call argument deltas, non-assistant messages | no entry (their content reaches the Timeline through the events above) |
| anything else (compaction, extension UI requests, future events, records missing tool ids) | `unknown_agent_event` with the raw record |

Extension dialogs (`select`, `confirm`, `input`, `editor`) are answered `cancelled: true`, so a user's extension can't block Pi waiting for a dialog Aha can't show yet. The request is still kept on the Timeline.

## Acceptance criteria

- [x] Each Pi event type maps to a Timeline entry: see the table. Structural events are named explicitly, and everything else is kept.
- [x] Contract tests turn a recorded event stream into the expected Timeline: `test/pi-events.test.ts` replays `test/fixtures/*.rpc.jsonl` through a fake Pi and checks the exact Timeline. The fixtures are written by hand in Pi 1.5.2's wire format. Real recordings replace them in #24.
- [x] Unknown events are kept, not dropped: `unknown_agent_event` with `raw`.

## Known limits

- Files changed by `bash` (rm, mv, redirects) produce no `file_edit`, and `change: "delete"` is never emitted.
- Create vs modify for `write` uses the file's birth time (within 3 s counts as new), because records are read after Pi may already have written the file.

Tests: agent-host 26 (6 new); `pnpm check` green.

body:
Closes innerstacklabs/tachlon-issues#1878

What: this is the part of tl#1878 that `main` does not do yet: `hosted-browser` reads the `book` artifact with `actions/download-artifact` on every run, so a download failure on a self-hosted runner still turns that job red. The `book` job also keeps its build on this machine's disk, in a folder keyed by run id and attempt beside the wasm bindings' folder; `hosted-browser` copies it from there when the folder is on its machine and downloads the artifact when it is not; the deploy job (a GitHub-hosted runner) keeps its downloads.

## Change

- `.github/workflows/ci.yml`: `env` line `BOOK_HANDOFF` beside `WASM_HANDOFF`; a `keep the book on this disk` step in `book` before the upload (an empty key stops it, entries older than a day are removed from the parent folder, a failure only warns); a `book-disk` step in `hosted-browser` that copies the folder to `$RUNNER_TEMP/book` and writes `hit=true`, with `if: steps.book-disk.outputs.hit != 'true'` on the existing download.
- `scripts/lib/wasm-handoff-checks.mjs` (run by `scripts/test-deploy-conditions.mjs` in the `web` job): three new checks and the existing "takes this run key's" check now also runs the `book-disk` shell line against a temporary home.

Budget (`git diff --numstat`, added column): 11 code (`ci.yml`) + 9 tests = 20, stop 34.

## Each new check is red with its key line reverted

Run locally with `node scripts/test-deploy-conditions.mjs` after reverting one line of `ci.yml` at a time:

| reverted | red check |
|---|---|
| `if: steps.book-disk.outputs.hit != 'true'` on the download | `hosted-browser downloads the book artifact only when its disk step found no hit` |
| the keep step's `cp -r book/book` | `the book folder is keyed by run id and attempt, and book writes it before its upload` |
| the run id, or the attempt, or the whole `BOOK_HANDOFF` line | same check |
| the empty-key guard in `book-disk`, or in the keep step | `an empty run key stops the book-disk step and the book keep step ...` |
| `book-disk` copies another run's folder | `the disk steps take this run key's bindings and book, and no other run's` |

On the old workflow (checks only, `ci.yml` unchanged) the four book checks are red; with the change all pass.

## Gates

- `cargo test -p app --test it architecture`: 206 passed. Full `cargo test -p app --test it`: 1432 passed, 7 ignored. `cargo test -p app --lib`: 57 passed.
- `wc -l`: `scripts/lib/wasm-handoff-checks.mjs` 28 (cap 400); `scripts/test-deploy-conditions.mjs` untouched (394).
- Scope check: `scope-check: ok: 2 changed path(s) inside Scope: tachlon`.
- No README keys-table or doc change: no key or flag changed.

## What the local run cannot show

Whether `book` and `hosted-browser` land on one machine (the disk path) or on two (the fallback). Log lines of this PR's own `ci` runs:

One run so far: `ci` push run 44984796902 on head 265bc76, all jobs green (`select`, `wasm`, `rust`, `book`, `hosted-browser`, `hosted`, `smoke`, `ci-summary`; `web` and `deploy` skipped by the tier). `book` ran on runner `thinkpad-gantt` and `hosted-browser` on `thinkpad-gantt2`, one machine (same `$HOME`). The `hosted-browser` log line:

`book read from /home/gh-runnergantt/.cache/tachlon-ci-handoff/book-44984796902-1, no download`

The disk path is the one this run took. No run took the fallback (`book is not on this disk, downloading the artifact`); it is covered by the checks alone (the `if:` check and the shell-line case for a missing folder).

Route: P:o I:s R:A+x. Seats run by the scrum master.

author: jucasoliveira
body:
## Why

The goal is a fully working Oite, held to Node's output. Functions held no properties on any backend (`F.x = 1; F.x` was `undefined`), had no `name`, `length` or `bind`, and `F.prototype` was `undefined`, so `fn.cache = {}`, `this.h = this.h.bind(this)`, `f.bind(null, 1)` and ES5 constructors failed on vm, jit and aot.

Stacked on #198. The new commits are `4210e4b` (failing tests first), `bc1edb4` (the change), `510ed01` (`String`/`Number` prototypes), `c8d8f82`, `dca652c` (docs) and `ac392c4` (perf).

## What changed

- A function keeps its own properties in an object made when the first one is set. VM: `VM::fn_props`, keyed by `functions::FunctionId`, which is what `===` compares. Native: a new `NativeFunction::props` field (32 to 40 bytes, `code` and `env` keep their offsets). Get, set, delete, `in`, `Object.keys`, `for...in`, spread and `console.log` (`[Function: f] { x: 1 }`) all see them.
- `name`, `length` and "has a `prototype`" come from a new `OpCode::FunctionInfo`, placed between the `Jump` over each body and the body, so it never runs. Native code registers it per function at start (`ot_register_function`). Names come from declarations, variables, assignments, properties and methods.
- A plain `function` gets a `prototype` when first read. `new F()` inherits it and `instanceof` checks it (it used to be true for any function).
- `bind`: VM `JsValue::BoundFunction` (`HeapData::Bound`). Native: a function whose code is `ot_bound_function` and whose env is `[target, this, ...args]`, so the inline call paths need no change. `call`/`apply`/`bind` are `Receiver::Function` method values. `new` on a bound function constructs its target.
- `String` and `Number` are functions whose `prototype` holds #198's method values (`String.prototype.trim === "x".trim`). `Number(v)` is new. The VM's `__call__` objects are gone.
- Classes: `C.length`, statics in `console.log`, and `Object.keys(C)` no longer lists `name`, `prototype`, `constructor`.

## Tradeoffs

- A function expression that captures nothing is one value on both backends (as `===` already said), so its properties are shared across evaluations.
- Strings and numbers do not look methods up on `String.prototype`. `"a".shout()` after `String.prototype.shout = ...` still fails.
- Built-ins other than methods have no `name`. Every built-in has `length` 0.
- Each native closure is 8 bytes larger. A loop making 20M closures: max RSS 2.25 GB to 2.41 GB, time within noise.

## Blast Radius

Every property access, `in`, `delete` and `Object.keys` on a function, `new`, `instanceof`, and `console.log` of functions (`log_format.out` now has Node's `[Function: f]`). Shared with the concurrent native Map/Set work: `src/runtime/builtins.rs` (`Receiver` gains `Function`, appended last), `src/runtime/stubs/{calls,globals,inspect,objects,classes}.rs`. For #200: this adds VM heap references that `mark_roots` must trace: `VM::fn_props` (keys hold env and bound-function indices, values are property objects), `JsValue::BoundFunction`, and `HeapData::Bound`'s target, `this` and arguments. VM allocations go through one `functions.rs` `alloc` helper, the one line to switch to `gc_alloc`.

## Verification

- `tests/lang/functions/{properties,name_length,bind,constructors,builtin_prototypes}.ot` on vm, jit and aot, held to Node's output. The first four fail on #198's head.
- `cargo fmt --check`, `cargo build --release`, `cargo test --release` and `scripts/bootstrap_verify.sh` pass. Local clippy 1.90 reports nothing in touched files. `src/types/check/narrow.rs:145` (untouched) already warns on #198.
- Call loops, median of 7 interleaved runs, no change beyond noise on either backend. Numbers in the first comment.

## O que é

O adendo 3 da tarefa do pet que pensa: medir o teto antes da próxima linha. Só papel. O pedido é do Matheus em 2026-11-22, depois da D1b
(#1089, não passa o corte): à pergunta "Qual linha segue o pet que pensa?", ele respondeu "Medir o teto antes".

## Summary

Step 1 of the ACS panel rebuild Devin asked for. The data itself comes in the next PR, with the regenerated calibration and a republished site.

- The data-freshness check's message for a stale panel now points at this workflow.

The workflow has to be on main before it can be triggered, which is why this is its own PR.

## Scope
Review-only change based on the installed protected `77a2c1a` runtime. After worker FD9 and database-heavy FD8, the normal wrapper validates the provider's actual `observed_at` from the same selected resource-evidence file as Python. It opens with `O_NOFOLLOW | O_NONBLOCK` and rejects nonregular files before reading, so a no-writer FIFO cannot hold both locks. Missing, malformed, future, or older-than-210-second evidence returns existing healthy deferral (75 → wrapper exit 0). Fresh evidence runs unchanged `run-once` 250/30 and full Python/SQL guards.

Python worker stays byte-identical to installed `77a2c1a` (SHA-256 `b73bf918fdb9453d26933fafd39078616711462700c6618ac779d7e49187ffd6`). Wrapper SHA-256 `91322fec9f6bb6d3ff3511d979bdc9e8911770498adea41df59e5e5e6ca713be`. Tracked `scripts/vps/runtime_manifest.sha1` now records wrapper SHA-1 `34d3884404e3aedf83d8881f039c4252eab76be9`; manifest SHA-256 `f194aeec3e98231a5b31a8a9bd518be1a6ce58856b6026c0fe0de91054d8641a`. No database limit, source/capture path, lock order, flags, cron, or provider timestamp semantics change. File mtime/fetch time never supplies freshness.

## Exact-head local proof
Commit `598f2f3ef3477457ccdf0b87753b8482cdee0003`: `bash -n`, `git diff --check`, focused isolated tests **12 PASS / 0 FAIL** (log SHA-256 `33e21adb67e4e560aaa80979ffe5e7702b2ab9115d3fdba91d7d1aa5202d49cb`) and `shasum -c scripts/vps/runtime_manifest.sha1` **53 OK / 0 FAIL** (manifest log SHA-256 `322471e22d25e0a26a75c7ce4c2504d6d30be7c38d81ac8a77bc0f765c9ed4e3`). Tests cover fresh and 210-second boundary, stale provider time with new mtime, future/missing/malformed/wrong-shape evidence, no-writer FIFO, symlink, directory and source-priority heavy-lock deferral. Fake worker receives exact 250/30 argv only on admitted cases; timeout cleanup reaps the full isolated test process group. No production DB/provider call.

## Release boundary
This draft targets the protected branch whose wrapper bytes match installed runtime; current main has a different unprotected wrapper. Do not auto-merge or activate during certification. A later deployment needs a new immutable runtime with the updated manifest, exact env path and DB/lock checks, and coordinated truthful future release-label/pin review. Historical runs remain unchanged. See `docs/leaderboard-shadow-provider-time-deferral.md`. Customer reads/backfill stay off; full certification and guard checks remain required.

The viewer went blank for a version file like `project-client's.json`; it now opens it like any other version. ## What changed **Root cause:** `src/editor.js` pasted the version filename raw into `'{{project}}'` string literals inside the viewer's script, so the apostrophe closed the string: `SyntaxError: Unexpected identifier 's' (/p/quoted-demo/:606:33)`, the whole module died, preview blank at `00:00.00`. The CLI reads the file directly, so it was fine. **Fix:** the server now passes the filename, version label and slug once as script-safe JSON (`{{pageData}}`, with `<`, U+2028 and U+2029 escaped), and the page reads them as `PROJECT`, `VERSION_LABEL`, `SLUG`. All previous raw `{{project}}`/`{{slug}}`/`{{version}}` uses inside the script use these constants. The project name and version in the HTML title/header are HTML-escaped. - `test/editor-version.test.js`: opens `project-client's.json` in real Chrome and checks no page errors, the timeline length and the exact title. - `test/stale-tab.test.js`: supplies the `PROJECT` constant its VM harness used to get from the removed inline declaration; no assertions changed. - `docs/viewer.md`, `CHANGELOG.md` (Unreleased → Fixed). ## Measured or checked **Failing test first, then passing:** - On main: `node --test test/editor-version.test.js` → `actual: [ "SyntaxError: Unexpected identifier 's' (/p/demo-amp-team/:606:33)" ], expected: []` - With the fix: `ℹ pass 1 ℹ fail 0` - `npm test`: 84 pass, 0 fail. `motlab doctor`: Ready. **Real viewer run** (Chrome 158, `motlab edit` on a one-scene project with `project-client's.json`), before (main) left, after right: ![Before / after](https://app.devin.ai/api/presigned_proxy?token=eyJhbGciOiJIUzI1NiIsInR5cCI6IkpXVCJ9..VHIXYHyTRL1eqJzuie89HKeFKKO6yTjNfdagLlU45hA) | | Page errors | Timeline | Preview | |---|---|---|---| | main | `SyntaxError: Unexpected identifier 's'` | 00:00.00 | blank | | this PR | none | 00:01.00 | drawn | The example project still loads (00:09.00, no page errors). Only console entries left are 404s for `favicon.ico` and the absent `selection.json`. **Try it:** `node bin/motlab.js edit "path/to/project-client's.json"` **Not tried:** Windows, and exporting the quoted version from the viewer. ## Checklist - [x] `npm test` passes - [x] Docs updated in the same commit: the doc in `docs/` that owns this, README if its claims change, `SKILL.md` if the agent uses it, `CHANGELOG.md` - [x] `ROADMAP.md` updated if this builds or tests something listed there (nothing listed) - [x] No generated output or private files committed ---

### What does this PR do?

In the Inbox layout the sidebar doesn't show drafts. If you click New session, type something, open an existing session and then click New session again, the app makes a brand-new empty draft. The earlier draft keeps its text, but nothing in the UI can open it again.

author: ford442
body:
Closes #258 (except the emsdk bump, which the issue asks for in its own PR — see "Not in this PR").

The primary renderer now has automated runtime coverage at three levels: every pipeline is compiled by Tint + Dawn, the compute passes are compared with their CPU twins on a real (software) GPU, and a headed-browser job boots WebGPU, draws all 16 benches and recovers from a device loss.

## What is in it

| # | Issue item | What landed |
|---|---|---|
| 1 | Dawn in Node | `webgpu` devDependency, `scripts/lib/node-gpu.mjs` (prefers the software adapter, skips with a notice, `REQUIRE_GPU=1` fails), ADR-0020, ESLint bans `webgpu` / `pixelmatch` / `pngjs` under `src/` |
| 2 | `test:pipelines` | Builds the app's own `PipelineLayoutCache` on a Dawn device and calls every `ensure*` with the real shader text: 5 sessions × 2 depth formats × 1× / 4× — 54 pipelines each. Features / limits audit for #171. naga pin 0.19.0 → 30.0.2, all 50 modules pass, no allowlist |
| 3 | `test:gpu-golden` | Six passes, 52 tests (table below) |
| 4 | Headed WebGPU e2e | `playwright.webgpu.config.js`, `e2e/gpu.webgpu.js` (5 specs), CI job `webgpu-e2e`, `window.__gpuErrors` |
| 5 | Image baselines | 6 views × 2 renderers, pixelmatch, report-only, artefact + job summary, `e2e:update-baselines` |
| 6 | One pin file | `config/toolchain.json` + `scripts/toolchain.mjs`; `check:toolchain` fails on a version written elsewhere |
| 7 | Bundle budget | `config/bundle-budget.json` + `check:bundle-budget`, in `validate` and after the CI site build |

`npm run validate` goes from 18 to 22 steps (adds `check:toolchain`, `check:bundle-budget`, `test:pipelines`, `test:gpu-golden`); 91 s wall on 8 cores here. It now prints skip notices for green steps, so a GPU or naga gate that skipped cannot look like a pass.

## GPU goldens

| Pass | Reference | Bound | Measured on Lavapipe |
|---|---|---|---|
| `fdtd-tmz-compute` | `FdtdTmzGrid`, same grid / sources / drive / materials | 1e-4 of peak after 200 steps | 6e-6 |
| `chores-reduce-f32` | `chores_reduce.cpp` (shipped WASM on the same data + native fixture) | 1e-5 rel | exact on the fixture |
| `seg-roller-compute` | `buildAllRollerInstances` | 1e-3 rad per second | 4e-5 rad at 1 s |
| `particle-compute` | invariants, 16 modes × 5 times × plant states | — | all hold |
| `ibl-prefilter-compute` | energy per layer; texel-for-texel vs the CPU bake | 4 %; 1 % of peak | 3.2 %; 8e-4 |
| `overview-cull-compute` | sphere / frustum from camera parameters, in double | exact | exact |

## Where this differs from the issue text

- **`seg-roller-compute` is not compared with the native plant golden.** The pass is closed-form kinematics of (time, ω, layout), not an integrator, so its twin is the CPU instance builder. The bound is 1e-3 rad *per second*: the shader evaluates the jitter seed in f32, so GPU and CPU roller angles drift ~1.7e-4 rad/s (1.2e-3 rad at 7.3 s).
- **IBL energy bound is 4 %, not 2 %.** At the 24–32 taps the rough layers use, the quadrature is off by up to 3.2 % — in the CPU bake too, to the same digits (GPU and CPU agree to 8e-4).
- **`chores-reduce` uses the WASM build of `chores_reduce.cpp`** for arbitrary data (the native binary only has the fixed 5-element fixture, which the GPU reproduces exactly). No C++ change, so `sim_core.wasm` is not stale.
- **Bundle budgets are 152 / 135 / 21 kB gzip** (entry / WebGPU / WebGL2), not 120 / 115. The chunks are 139.8 / 124.3 / 18.8 kB today — they grew with #255–#257 after the issue was written. Each budget is today's size + ~8 %, the same headroom the issue's numbers had.
- **Spec 2 switches benches with `setMode()` in one page** instead of 16 navigations (`?device=` / `particles=0` are not real params). A separate spec covers the `high` tier (shadow / MSAA / TAA / field volume / FDTD pipelines).
- **A `null` pipeline raises no GPU error** — its draw is skipped — so the specs observe draws with a test-side probe on `setPipeline` / `draw*`. Reintroducing `fluxSegmentPipeline = null` for non-SEG benches fails spec 2 with `transformer: fluxSegmentPipeline did not draw` (checked by mutation).
- **Baselines were generated on this dev box**, with the same Playwright Chromium / SwiftShader as CI, not on the CI image. The hosted runner's first run matched them: 0.00–0.08 % of pixels differ across the six WebGPU views (limit 1 %). `Validate` → `update_baselines` regenerates them on the runner if they ever need to come from there.
- **"emsdk version in the source-hash sidecar"**: there is no sidecar file. The emsdk pin is an input of `sim_core_source_hash()` (still hashed under its old path, so moving the pin did not stale the binary — hash unchanged, `8aafa66fa45a42d8`); a binary built before an emsdk bump reads as stale.

## Not in this PR

- **emsdk 3.1.61 → 4.x.** The issue wants it in its own PR. The pin is now a one-line change plus a rebuild; the gates (ABI, goldens, bit-identical snapshots, size) are in `build-wasm.yml`.
- Baselines gating (`BASELINE_GATE=1`) — after two stable weeks.
- Lazy per-bench registration (the optional follow-up in §7).

## Things the new tests showed (not fixed here)

`check:toolchain` found one stale version on its first run (`docs/SNAPSHOTS.md` said emsdk 3.1.64) — fixed.

The WebGPU ↔ WebGL2 parity captures (`e2e/baselines/`, table in docs/WEBGL2.md) differ in 70–79 % of pixels for SEG focus and overview. Looking at the frames:

- WebGPU is much brighter and less saturated than WebGL2 (overview's foreground cylinders are near white).
- SEG rollers lie at assorted tilts on WebGPU and stand upright on WebGL2. The WebGPU instances come from `seg-roller-compute.wgsl`, whose rolling quaternion turns each roller about the orbit tangent.

Both are SwiftShader frames at the `low` tier (no IBL, no SSR); I could not check a hardware GPU from here. Worth a look before the release build.

## Verification

- `npm run validate`: 22 / 22 on 8 cores, Lavapipe.
- `npm run test:e2e:webgpu`: 18 / 18 here (5 runtime specs + 12 captures + report), ~10 min. Run-to-run the captures differ in < 0.1 % of pixels.
- Mutations: a wrong vertex attribute format fails `test:pipelines` in all 10 combinations; the #252 null pipeline fails e2e spec 2.
- On the hosted runner (third commit): `validate` passes with `REQUIRE_GPU=1` (Dawn on Lavapipe), and `webgpu-e2e` passes, 18 / 18 in about 10 minutes. Getting there took two test fixes: the WebGL2 parity capture read back black on the runner (it now reads inside the app's own render call), and spec 3 sampled the lazily built FDTD pass too early (the specs now wait until the expected pipelines have drawn).
- `Playwright (WebGL2)` is red on this PR for a reason that predates it: its second step, the offline PWA test (`e2e/offline.preview.js:42`, `navigator.onLine` stays `true` under `setOffline`), has failed on every run on `main` and on every branch since at least 2026-11-14. The WebGL2 suite itself passed here (101 passed, one `#lab=` tour test flaky).

author: marysa2006
body:
## ¿Qué hace este PR?

En Android, el teclado tapaba los últimos campos de los formularios y no dejaba ver lo que se escribía (en Expo Go y en el APK). Ahora:

- **En el APK** (y en un development build): con `react-native-keyboard-controller`, la pantalla **sube sola el campo que se escribe** por encima del teclado, y sobre el teclado aparece una barra con **Anterior, Siguiente y Listo** para pasar de campo en campo.
- **En Expo Go**, que no trae esa librería: la pantalla deja libre el espacio del teclado (`KeyboardAvoidingView` con `padding`) y se puede desplazar hasta el último campo. El equipo sigue trabajando en Expo Go como siempre.

## Historia de usuario

Corrección transversal, sin issue: lo reportó María al probar los formularios del #251.

## Tipo de cambio

- [x] 🖼️ Pantalla o componente (UI)
- [ ] 🔌 Datos: tipos, mock, hook o llamada a la API
- [x] 🧱 Base compartida: tipos, tema, layouts, dependencias o configuración
- [x] 🐛 Corrección
- [ ] 📝 Documentación

**Base compartida (la aprueba Jorge):**
- **Paquete nuevo, aprobado por María:** `react-native-keyboard-controller` **1.22.7**, la versión que fija Expo para la SDK 58 (`bundledNativeModules.json`), instalado con `npx expo install`. No necesita config plugin y usa `react-native-reanimated`, que ya estaba.
- **Lockfile con npm 10** (`npx -y npm@10 install --package-lock-only`) y verificado con `npx -y npm@10 ci` en un clon limpio: pasa. **Después de fusionar, todos corren `npm ci`.**
- `src/app/_layout.tsx`: `ProveedorTeclado` envuelve la app.

**Por qué pasaba.** Desde la SDK 54, las apps de Expo en Android son edge-to-edge: la ventana ya no se achica con el teclado. `Pantalla` tenía `KeyboardAvoidingView` sin `behavior` en Android, y la guía de Expo dice: *"On Android, Expo apps are edge-to-edge, so the window no longer resizes for the keyboard. A view without a `behavior` stays under the keyboard."* Para formularios recomienda `KeyboardAwareScrollView`, pero *"The Keyboard Controller library is not included in Expo Go."* ([Keyboard handling](https://docs.expo.dev/guides/keyboard-handling/))

### Cambios
- `src/components/ui/Teclado.tsx` (nuevo):
  - `tecladoNativo`: si el módulo nativo `KeyboardController` existe en la app que corre (`TurboModuleRegistry.get`, que devuelve null sin él). No se usa `ExecutionEnvironment`: su `StoreClient` incluye Expo Go y los development builds por igual.
  - La librería **solo se carga con el módulo nativo**: en Expo Go no se ejecuta nada de ella.
  - `ProveedorTeclado` (`KeyboardProvider` con `preload={false}`, sin el parpadeo al abrir), `ScrollViewTeclado` (`KeyboardAwareScrollView`) y `BarraTeclado` (`KeyboardToolbar` con la API compuesta de la 1.22: `Prev`, `Next` y `Done text="Listo"`).
  - La librería trae las etiquetas del lector en inglés ("Previous", "Next", "Done"); un botón propio las pone en español ("Anterior", "Siguiente", "Listo") con su ayuda, y con área de 44×44.
- `src/components/ui/Pantalla.tsx`, con `conTeclado`:
  - **con el módulo nativo:** `KeyboardAwareScrollView` en lugar del `ScrollView` (con `bottomOffset` para no quedar debajo de la barra), sin `KeyboardAvoidingView` para no subir dos veces, y la barra. Se conservan recargar, el botón flotante, el pie y "subir al inicio" (la referencia es la del ScrollView);
  - **sin él (Expo Go):** `KeyboardAvoidingView` con `behavior="padding"` en las dos plataformas y `keyboardVerticalOffset` medido con `measureInWindow` (sirve con encabezado apilado y sin él).
- `src/app/tablets/solicitar.tsx`: usa `conTeclado`, porque tiene los campos de "Tus datos" al final.

**Fuera de este PR:** `npx expo install --check` muestra parches pendientes de la SDK que ya estaban en `develop` (`expo` 58.0.22 → 58.0.26, `expo-router`, `react-native-safe-area-context`, etc.). Van en un `chore/…` aparte.

## Capturas

<!-- María: en el APK, un formulario con el teclado abierto en el último campo y la barra Anterior/Siguiente/Listo; en Expo Go, el mismo campo visible -->

## Cómo probarlo

```bash
git switch fix/teclado-android
npm ci
npx expo start
```

**En Expo Go** (lo de siempre):
1. **Laura Pérez** → Capacitaciones → Solicitar: tocar **Objetivo** (el último campo). El campo y lo que se escribe se ven, y se puede desplazar hasta Enviar.
2. **Carlos Ramírez** → un espacio → un horario libre: **Novedades**. **Laura** → Solicitar tablet: el celular.
3. Registro e inicio de sesión: el último campo. Al cerrar el teclado, sin espacio vacío abajo.

**En un APK de esta rama** (`npx eas-cli@latest build --profile preview --platform android`):
4. Al tocar un campo de abajo, la pantalla lo sube sola por encima del teclado.
5. Sobre el teclado aparece la barra: **Anterior** y **Siguiente** pasan de campo en campo (se deshabilitan en el primero y en el último) y **Listo** cierra el teclado. Con TalkBack se leen en español.
6. Deslizar para recargar y "subir al inicio" (por ejemplo, al cambiar de paso en un formulario por pasos) siguen funcionando.

## Lista de verificación

- [ ] Corrí la app en mi celular o emulador (Expo Go: sí; APK con la librería: pendiente)
- [x] Mi rama está actualizada con `develop` y no tiene conflictos
- [x] Las pantallas usan hooks de `src/hooks`, no llaman a la API directamente
- [x] Hay estados de carga, error y vacío
- [x] No subí claves ni `.env`
- [x] El PR tiene menos de ~400 líneas (si no, explica por qué)

`npm run lint` y `npm run typecheck` pasan sin errores. `npx -y npm@10 ci` pasa en limpio.

body:
## 問題與變更

在推送 PR head 後接著更新 PR 內文時，既有 Windows 完整 CI 監聽 `pull_request.edited`，可能為相同 head 建立另一個 run，並由既有 concurrency 取消先前 run。移除 edited，只保留 opened、synchronize、reopened；main／tag push、merge_group、workflow_dispatch、concurrency、來源預檢及原有測試／發行門檻不變。標題只用於 run 顯示名稱，變更內文或標題不再啟動完整 CI。

變更 PR 的 base 後，如需新的完整驗證，須使用重新開啟 PR 或更新來源等現有觸發事件；來源預檢仍要求 event、公開 PR、base 與 live main 一致。此變更不放寬來源檢查，也不將舊 run 當作新基底證據。

## 真實紅綠與驗證

先在既有 `test/powershell/integration/workflow_semantics_tests.ps1` 加入精確 PR 事件清單斷言，在私人 TEMP 複製基底 workflow 與最終測試後，以 Windows PowerShell 5.1 `powershell.exe -NoProfile -NonInteractive -ExecutionPolicy Bypass -File test/powershell/integration/workflow_semantics_tests.ps1`，實際 exit 1，`PR workflow runs only for open synchronize and reopen` 斷言為 false。私人原始記錄 SHA-256 `9835A4B40166B9BF5090272D93942CAE9B0191161FE90BB186C9768CBFB220DC`，紅燈未提交。移除 edited 後同命令使用固定 actionlint 1.7.12，12 項斷言通過、exit 0；私人 TEMP 將三個事件重新排序後同套測試亦通過，確認事件順序不影響斷言；綠燈記錄 SHA-256 `94160F53A3189AFC5452E26015342878D6CD0398A7C3DB542AB0D17EEFC42B58`。

固定 Go 1.27.3、GOTOOLCHAIN=local、GOWORK/GOPROXY/GOSUMDB=off、vendor 執行 `go test -mod=vendor -count=1 ./script/test/pr_source_preflight` 通過。未手動觸發 workflow；正式 CI 與獨立審查待完成。

author: akingdbets
body:
## 무엇을 / 왜

멀티턴·멀티에이전트 실험으로 넘어가기 전에 필요한 기반을 만든다. 멀티턴 실행기는 이번 PR에 없다.
연구 질문(정확도 유지율 90%에서 입력·총 토큰·실제 비용 기준 최대 절감)에 답하려면 캐시·추론 토큰과 실제 비용을 호출 단위로 남겨야 한다.

## 변경

- **`src/llm.py`**
  - LLMResult에 `cached_tokens`, `cache_write_tokens`, `reasoning_tokens`, `raw_usage`, `reasoning_text`(DeepSeek `reasoning_content`), `created_at`(UTC)을 추가했다. 서버가 주지 않은 값은 None이다(0이 아님).
  - `parse_usage_details`가 제공사별 후보 이름을 차례로 찾는다.
  - `python src/llm.py --cache-probe [answer|judge]`를 추가했다. 약 2,000토큰 프롬프트를 연속 두 번 보내 캐시 필드를 확인한다.
- **`src/cost.py` + `data/pricing.json`**
  - 단가: gpt-6.1-sol Standard 2 / 0.10 / 2.50 / 10, deepseek-flash 피크 단가 고정 0.30 / 0.006 / 출력 1.20.
  - `cost_source`로 계산 근거를 표시한다.
  - `recompute_costs(path)`로 단가를 바꾼 뒤 저장된 궤적의 비용을 다시 계산할 수 있다.
- **`src/multiturn/trajectory.py`**
  - 호출 1번이 JSONL 1줄이다.
  - 대화 기록에는 최종 답변만 넣고 추론은 따로 저장한다(모듈 docstring에 명시).
  - `history_before_turn`은 replay 모드에서 턴 k 직전까지의 대화 기록을 재구성한다.
  - `reasoning_effort`는 명시적으로 고른 값만 받는다(`server_default` 포함).
  - `summarize_steps`는 추론 실행 여부, finish=length, 빈 답변 비율, 실제 지출과 실험상 비용을 집계한다.
- **`src/multiturn/response_cache.py`**
  - LLM을 감싸는 SQLite 응답 캐시다. 캐시 키에 backend, base_url, model, messages, 요청한 샘플링 설정, reasoning_effort, sample_idx가 들어간다.
  - 캐시 적중 시 원래 호출의 토큰 값을 그대로 돌려주고 `cache_hit=True`로 표시한다. `RESPONSE_CACHE=off`로 끌 수 있다.
- **`src/experiment.py`** (최소 수정)
  - trials에 `answer_cached_tokens`, `answer_cache_write_tokens`, `answer_reasoning_tokens`, `answer_raw_usage`를 기록한다.
  - summary에는 `usage` 합계와 `answer_health` 키만 새로 추가했다. 기존 키와 값은 바뀌지 않는다.
- **문서**: `docs/todo_with_keys.md`(키가 필요한 확인 작업), README 진행 현황.

## 리뷰 시 참고

- **캐시 쓰기 필드 이름은 미확인이다**(`--cache-probe`로 확정 필요). 캐시 읽기·추론 필드도 문서 기준이고 실제 응답으로는 아직 확인하지 않았다.
- DeepSeek `prompt_cache_miss_tokens`는 캐시 쓰기로 보지 않았다. 일반 입력 단가로 청구되기 때문이다.
- 응답 캐시 키는 실제 전송값이 아니라 **요청한** 샘플링 값으로 만든다. 서버가 400으로 인자를 거부하면 실제 전송값이 바뀌기 때문이다.
- `answer_reasoning_effort` 기본값 `"none"`은 그대로 두었다. 문서상 논문 주 run들이 `"none"`이었기 때문이다.
- judge 토큰 세부 필드는 넣지 않았다. 채점 비용은 평가 비용이라 주 지표가 아니다.

## 테스트

- 새 테스트 31개는 모두 통과한다(네트워크 없이 가짜 usage dict와 가짜 LLM 사용).
- 전체 228개 중 `test_published_evidence_results` 1건이 실패한다. #59의 코퍼스 파일이 Windows `core.autocrlf=true`에서 CRLF로 체크아웃되어 생기는 기존 문제로, 이번 변경과는 무관하다.
- `--cache-probe`와 싱글턴 3문항 실행은 API 키가 필요해 아직 돌리지 않았다. 명령어는 `docs/todo_with_keys.md`에 있다.

author: pateta51-ops
body:
Row K640 (`docs/plan/K640.md`, `state: done`). Component: `clock` only, plus its entry in `docs/catalog-notes.json` and the generated docs.

## What changed
1. A fractional step: behaviour kept (it counts as the next whole step, in the move and in `overrun`), now said in README rule 4 and pinned by a test.
2. `onSpace`'s guard for a state off the row is pinned (space 0 is true; a state at -1 is false for an unknown space).
3. Every README block is run: the engine-core recipe and both lose-space blocks are `ts` blocks that the tests execute and compile (5 blocks); only the one `<Track .../>` line is left as text. Rules 10 and 11 each have a test that reads the rule and runs what it says. Every call the README names with `(spec` or `(crossings` must be an export.
4. `step` throws for an amount that is not a finite number. On a `wrap` row a step of more than 1000 laps lands where the full step lands and fires as a step of 1000 laps plus the rest, so a step of 1e9 returns at once; the result then carries `cut`, the laps not walked (absent when nothing was cut).
5. `checkClock` also reports: a key that looks like a misspelt one (one letter added, dropped, changed or swapped against a known key of 3 letters or more, or its first 3 or more letters: `end`, `threshold`, `directions`, `dir`, `onec`); other keys a game adds (`name`, `label`, `id` on the spec) pass as on main, `once` that is not a boolean, an `id` or `kind` that is not text, `values` that is not an object of lists.
6. The two README sentences about states off the row are corrected (`reached` with a value between two spaces; `stepsTo` then `step` from a state that is not a space).
7. New by addition: `stepsTo(spec, state, space, 'back')`, the way back round a `wrap` row as a negative amount. Default and `stop` rows: today's answer.

A frozen copy of the part as it was on main (`components/clock/clock.frozen.ts`) stays, with a comparison test: 4 seeds x 1500 random valid specs (1 to 12 spaces, count or ids, up/down, stop/wrap, every threshold kind, whole steps up to four laps): `step` (state, crossings, `overrun`, keys), `stepsTo`, `left`, `ended`, `reached`, `onSpace`, `indexOf`, `spaceOf`, `valueAt` equal on every input, and `checkClock` returns `[]` for every one of those specs.

## Seen failing first
Tests written before the code, run against main's `index.ts` (39 tests, 4 failed):
```
× K640 a huge step on a wrap row returns at once ...            RangeError: Invalid array length
× K640 a step that is not a finite number throws ...            AssertionError: stop NaN: expected [Function] to throw an error
× K640 checkClock reports once that is not a boolean ...        AssertionError: expected [] to deeply equal [ Array(1) ]
× K640 stepsTo back: the way back round a wrap row ...          AssertionError: expected [ 3, 3, 3, 1 ] to deeply equal [ 3, 3, -1, -3 ]
```
The other points pin lines that were already right, so each was checked by breaking its line, one change per run (26 runs, every one failed, then restored):

| Line broken | Test that failed |
|---|---|
| `Math.ceil` removed from `overrun` | K640 a fractional step |
| `onSpace` guard removed; guard `> 0` | K640 onSpace (and the comparison for `> 0`) |
| README: `ended` renamed in the engine-core recipe | K640 README recipe engine-core and track; every call is an export; the examples compile |
| README: `onSpace` swapped for `ended` in the checkpoint check | K640 README lose-space recipe |
| README: reach-or-pass block reversed; its sentence reversed | K640 README lose-space recipe |
| README: rule 10 reversed; rule 11 reversed | K640 README rule 10; rule 11 |
| README: an inline call renamed | K640 every clock call the README names is an export |
| the finite check removed | K640 a step that is not a finite number throws |
| the lap limit raised; lowered to 3 | K640 a huge step; the comparison (for 3) |
| each of the six new `checkClock` lines (before the review round; the near-miss rule and `cut` came after and are pinned by expected values) | K640 checkClock reports ... |
| README: each of the two corrected sentences put back | K640 README on states off the row |
| the `'back'` term removed; its README line changed | K640 stepsTo back |
| wrap arithmetic off by one on one lap | the comparison |
| README: the fractional sentence; the NaN sentence | K640 a fractional step; a step that is not a finite number |

Existing callers: the 25 tests from before pass unchanged except one expected print of the lose-space recipe (the block now prints the checkpoint check too); the comparison test shows the same answers as the frozen copy.

## Departures
Old calls whose result changes:
- `step` with NaN, Infinity, -Infinity, `undefined`, `null`, text (also the text `'2'`, which moved 2) or `true` (which moved 1): now throws `clock: a step must be a finite number`. Before: a silent no-op, a move, `overrun: Infinity` on a `stop` row, or a `RangeError` on a `wrap` row.
- `step` on a `wrap` row with more than 1000 laps (more than 1000 x spaces): same landing space and the same `once` crossings, but a threshold that fires every pass fires for 1000 laps and the rest, not for every lap, and the result says so with `cut`. `breaking:` in the title is for this call only: no other valid old call changes.
- `checkClock` on a broken spec: a key that is a near-miss of a known key, `once` not a boolean, `id` or `kind` not text, `values` not an object of lists: now a problem. A game's own key is reported only if it is such a near-miss (`value`, `kinds`, `date` on a threshold).

Where this leaves the brief:
- "At most a lap or two of work": the walk is as before, capped at 1000 laps plus the rest, not rebuilt to do two laps of work. The limit is high so that no step a rule gives changes (a limit of a few laps would change a step of 10 on a 1-space row); the cost is bounded by 1000 x spaces x thresholds.
- A `pass` threshold on the forward end of a `stop` row (it can never fire) is still not reported: it is not one of the review's 15 kinds and reporting it would turn specs that check clean today into failures.
- The three searches are found through four new tags in the catalogue entry, not through `docs/mechanics.json` (outside this batch's files). Each prints `clock` on its first line; no test holds that.
- The comparison test checks more calls than listed (`indexOf`, `spaceOf`, `valueAt`).

## Checks
GitHub's check on the head commit.

body:
No ticket: the repository tracks none yet.

Two small classes of the Polecat backend were left out of the last slice because each needed a decision first; both are now tested.

- `DescribeColumn` takes a `DbException` where it took a `SqlException`, and its class and file are renamed `DbExceptionExtensions` after the type they extend. The provider's exception cannot be made outside the provider; its base class can, and the method reads the message only.
- `DbExceptionExtensionsTests` (new): what each column the database names is called, and that anything else is a value.
- `PolecatTenantStoresTests` (new): one stream store and one group store per tenant, kept; the tail asked for by the id the store keeps for the tenant; what the wildcard has and is refused; and the name comparer following the database's collation.

## For the reviewer

- **One source change**, the parameter type and the rename above. The two callers pass the `SqlException` they caught, as before.
- **No package added.** I said this test project had no faking library; that was wrong, `Tests.props` gives FakeItEasy to every test project. The document store is faked with it and never called; the two context factories are stand-ins that throw if they are.

## Verified

- `dotnet test` on the server solution, unit tests: 685, 0 failed (672 before).
- Unit line rate of `Dracocephalum.Nightingale.Server.Polecat`: 63.8% to 64.7% (2357 of 3645); both classes at 100%.
- Three behaviours broken on purpose, in one run: five of the new tests failed, each stating that behaviour. Sources restored.
- `dotnet build` 0 warnings, the integration projects included; `dotnet format analyzers --verify-no-changes` exits 0.

author: ramzy-collab
body:
When WorkOS refused a sign-in step with a status below 500, the login page showed WorkOS's own message. Some refusals only happen for emails without an account (`sign_up_not_allowed`, `email_domain_not_deliverable`), so anyone could tell which emails have one. Every sign-in step now shows Formelab's own copy.

**Test plan:** [Sign-in answers the same for every email](/test-plans/2026-11-22-signin-enumeration), 47 browser test cases to hand to Claude Cowork (file: `docs/test-plans/2026-11-22-signin-enumeration.md`). **Not run yet**: skipped for now and listed under the README's "Before a wider launch" checklist.

## What changed (`src/signin.ts`)

- **`toPublicAuthError(res, flow)`**: one helper maps every WorkOS refusal to what a visitor may see. No route shows WorkOS's text on the four sign-in flows. The server log gets the real status, code (read from `code` or `error`, since OAuth-style errors use `error`) and WorkOS request id, never the email.
- **Send code (`magic_auth`)**: every status below 500 except 429 shows the same page as a sent code: "If there's an account for (email), we've sent a code. It works once and expires in 10 minutes." 429: "Too many attempts. Try again in a minute." The `magic_auth` answer (which carries the code) still never reaches the browser; a test now asserts it.
- **Log in with code**: redirects unchanged; every other refusal below 500 reads "That code is invalid or expired."; 429 gets the rate-limit message (it used to read as a wrong code).
- **Log in with password**: generic wrong-password text and all redirects kept. Added `radar_challenge`, `radar_sign_up_challenge` and `radar_sms_sign_in_challenge` to the steps that go to WorkOS's page. 429 and Formelab's own limiter use the new rate-limit message.
- **Forgot password**: unchanged, confirmed: every status below 500 gets the same page.
- **Kept on purpose**: WorkOS's password-strength reason when resetting (needs the emailed link) or setting a password (signed in). Neither reveals whether an account exists.
- Email format is already checked in the browser (`type="email" required`) and on the server (`isEmail`).

## Staging check: not run

`scripts/workos-enum-check.sh` checks WorkOS staging directly (runs on macOS's built-in bash; instructions at its top). It and the Cowork plan answer what code can't: whether unverified and two-factor accounts get their extra step even with a wrong password (that would still reveal those accounts), whether asking for a code creates a WorkOS user for an unknown email, and timing. Tested only against a local stand-in server mimicking WorkOS's documented answers. Both are on the README's "Before a wider launch" list; the spec's open item points there.

## Testing

- `test/login.test.ts`: six new cases mock every WorkOS error shape (`{code, message}` and `{error, error_description}`) for each flow and assert an email with and without an account get the same status, page and cookie; every redirect code in both shapes; the one-time code never in the page or cookies.
- `npm run typecheck` and the full suite (390 tests) pass.

https://claude.ai/code/session_01PNJFXMBJquCDxeYBURoCAA

This is the first step toward real vehicles, starting with the m1l1 truck ride.

- `$v drive $path [speed ...]` moves the vehicle node to node along the path's `target` chain at that speed (MOHAA units/s, scaled). At the end of the path it notifies `drive`, so `waittill drive` returns and the mission continues.
- `modifydrive speed` changes the speed. `stop` and `fullstop` end the drive where the vehicle is.
- `lock`, `unlock` and the attach/detach driver, passenger and turret slot commands are accepted as no-ops until players can ride.
- There is no vehicle model or physics yet, so the vehicle moves from node to node in straight lines rather than following the curve of the path.

Tests: a new `test_vehicle_drive` (ASan/UBSan) runs a three-node chain plus a stopped drive. dod_mohaa_test, the integrate tests, the hlsdk syntax check (`__GAMECUBE__`) and the root `pytest tests` (96) pass.

author: samuelschlesinger
body:
Part of #7210 (part of #3261; extends #3494).

In deterministic synchronous distributed computing, the oral messages protocol (`CslibFrontier.Computability.Distributed.Byzantine.RecursiveOralMessages`) solves `t`-resilient Byzantine agreement for `n > 3t` in `t + 1` rounds by relaying trees of length up to `t + 1`, so its message size grows exponentially with `t`. This PR adds `CslibFrontier/Computability/Distributed/Byzantine/PhaseKing.lean`, landing two polynomial-communication synchronous protocol steps toward #7210 in `Cslib.Distributed.Byzantine`:

1. **Two-round rotating-king protocol step (`phaseKing`, `4 * t < Fintype.card P`, `2 * (t + 1)` rounds, `Msg = V`, after Berman and Garay 1989):**
   Given an injective schedule `kings : Fin (t + 1) ↪ P` of `t + 1` phase kings over any `[DecidableEq V]`, each two-round phase runs a universal broadcast of current estimates (`est : V`) followed by a tie-break broadcast from `kings k`. Because `4 * t < n` implies `n < 2 * (n - 2 * t)`, at most one value achieves multiplicity `n - 2 * t` (and at most one achieves `n - t`, extracted computably via `uniqueAboveOn`). Unanimity among correct processes persists across every phase whenever `2 * t < Fintype.card P` (`phaseKing_persists`, frozen past `2 * (t + 1)` rounds by `phaseKing_state_eq_of_le`), even under an equivocating faulty king; in any phase with a correct king (`kings k ∉ F`), all correct processes converge to the king's proposal whenever `4 * t < Fintype.card P` (`phaseKing_converges_of_notMem`), yielding protocol-correctness and existence steps `phaseKing_solvesByzantineAgreement` and `exists_polyMsg_solvesByzantineAgreement`. Every wire in every round carries a single element of `V` (`2 * (t + 1) * (|P| - |F|) * |P|` honest point-to-point transmissions across the `2 * (t + 1)` active rounds) with a three-field ghost-free local state (`PhaseKingState`). The `4 * t < n` bound is sharp for this 2-round phase structure: on `Fin 4` with `t = 1`, `phaseKing_fails_four_one` refutes agreement for every king schedule and round horizon `R` (contrasting with `om1` and `om`, which succeed on `Fin 4` using relay vectors/trees). Primary-source locator verification against the paywalled LNCS 372 proceedings text of Berman and Garay (1989), results-inventory registration, and the 3-round-per-phase `3 * t < n` extension of Berman, Garay and Perry (1989) remain open under #7210.

2. **Multivalued-to-binary reduction step (`turpinCoan`, `3 * t < Fintype.card P`, `R₀ + 2` rounds, after Turpin and Coan 1984, §§2–3, pp. 74–75):**
   Given any binary protocol `πBool : Protocol P SBool MBool` solving `Protocol.SolvesByzantineAgreement t R₀`, `turpinCoan t default πBool` (over message sum `TurpinCoanMsg` with predicate `TurpinCoanMsg.isVal` and local state `TurpinCoanState`) solves multivalued Byzantine agreement over any `[DecidableEq V]` in `R₀ + 2` rounds for all `3 * t < Fintype.card P` (`turpinCoan_solvesByzantineAgreement`, requiring neither `[Inhabited MBool]` nor `[Inhabited SBool]` and covering `R₀ = 0` as well as `R₀ > 0`). Domain values in `V` are transmitted in round 1 only (`turpinCoanValueMessagesSent`, `turpinCoan_valueMessagesSent_eq`, proving exact count `(Fintype.card P - F.card) * Fintype.card P` across `R + 1` rounds); round 2 broadcasts a 1-bit `perplexed` flag (`2 * count(input) ≤ n + t`), computes `alert` (`n - 2 * t ≤ count(true)`) and `candidate` (`t + 1 ≤ count` among non-perplexed senders), and rounds `3` through `R₀ + 2` execute the binary subprotocol on `alert`. Composing `turpinCoan` with `(phaseKing t kings).toProtocol` gives purely polynomial-message multivalued agreement for `4 * t < n` (`V` in round 1, single bits in rounds `2` through `2t + 4`), while composing with `om` reaches `3 * t < n` resilience in `t + 3` rounds with `V` sent in round 1 only. Verified firsthand against the published IPL scan (`TurpinCoan-ipl84.pdf`, SHA-256 `d2dfb0e2dfe3d367f93df30b6dd9c32b5c35c6b4be42d3f337d57918b86a4836`); results-inventory registration remains open under #7210 pending an outside-author-fleet source check.

### Source-to-Lean mapping and scope notes (`#7210`)

- **`MultivaluedProtocol` and `MultivaluedProtocol.toProtocol`:** `Cslib.Distributed.Byzantine.Protocol` fixes inputs and outputs to `Bool`. `MultivaluedProtocol` (`MultivaluedProtocol.state`, `MultivaluedProtocol.decision`, `MultivaluedProtocol.SolvesByzantineAgreement`, `MultivaluedProtocol.SolvesByzantineAgreement.mono`) generalizes only the input/output value type to `Val` with identical round execution, bridges losslessly to `Protocol` at `Val = Bool` (`MultivaluedProtocol.toProtocol`, `MultivaluedProtocol.toProtocol_state`, `MultivaluedProtocol.toProtocol_decision`, `MultivaluedProtocol.toProtocol_solvesByzantineAgreement_iff`), and inherits the `2 ≤ |P| ≤ 3 * t` impossibility bound for `[Nontrivial V]` (`MultivaluedProtocol.not_solvesByzantineAgreement` via `Protocol.not_solvesByzantineAgreement`, after Fischer, Lynch and Merritt 1985, Theorem 1 and §3.1).
- **Firsthand Turpin–Coan (1984) verification (`manual/sources.md`):** Checked against the MIT CSAIL scan of *Information Processing Letters* 18(2), pp. 73–76, 1984 (`https://groups.csail.mit.edu/tds/papers/Coan/TurpinCoan-ipl84.pdf`, SHA-256 `d2dfb0e2dfe3d367f93df30b6dd9c32b5c35c6b4be42d3f337d57918b86a4836`) and MIT LCS Technical Report `MIT/LCS/TR-315` (`https://groups.csail.mit.edu/tds/papers/Coan/MIT-LCS-TR-315.pdf`, SHA-256 `21766180f09ac93e1e0078ec9d3d8ba02d848c86dfa52aa2e18f320902455785`): §1 (pp. 73–74, synchronous complete unauthenticated network, `P > 3T`), §2 (p. 74, `v`, `p`, `perplexed` at `(P - T) / 2`, `alert` at `P - 2T`, majority vote over `{v(j) | p(j) = false}`), §3 (pp. 74–75, unnumbered validity and agreement proofs via `(P + T) / 2 + (P - T) / 2 = P` and `≥ T + 1` correct content processes when `alert = false`), and §4 (p. 75, `O(P^2)` round-1 `V`-messages; optional 1-round `2T + 5` variant for biased binary algorithms not formalized). `turpinCoan` writes §2's exact rational threshold `count(heard ≠ input) ≥ (P - T) / 2` in integer-multiplied form `2 * count(heard = input) ≤ n + t`, includes self-messages in `MultivaluedProtocol` (`(n - |F|) * n` total round-1 transmissions), and computes `candidate` uniformly via `uniqueAboveOn` (`uniqueAboveOn_eq_some_iff`, `uniqueAboveOn_eq_some_iff_of_lt_two_mul`) on both content and perplexed processes.
- **Step disposition (`policy/statements.md` Rule 2):** Because the paywalled LNCS 372 (Berman and Garay 1989) and IEEE FOCS '89 (Berman, Garay and Perry 1989) proceedings PDFs were not openly accessible, no internal theorem/section locators are claimed for those two papers, `CslibFrontierResults/Entries.lean` is untouched, and #7210 stays open (`Part of #7210`) for primary-source verification, outside-fleet source checks, inventory registration, and the 3-round-per-phase `3 * t < n` Phase-King extension.

`CslibFrontierTests/Computability/Distributed/PhaseKing.lean` checks the module as an ordinary `module` client: `decide`-checked runs of `phaseKing` on `Fin 5, t = 1` (over `Bool` and `Fin 10`) and `Fin 9, t = 2` (two consecutive faulty kings), the `Fin 4, t = 1` failure trace contrasted with `om1`, `V = ℕ` and independent-universe instantiations, and `turpinCoan` runs on `Fin 4, t = 1` (with `om1` and `om`) and `Fin 5, t = 1` (with `(phaseKing 1 kings5).toProtocol`). Existing `Byzantine/*.lean` modules and `CslibFrontierTests/Computability/Distributed/Byzantine.lean` are untouched.

author: realtolufash
body:
## Description
Web sign-in with Apple read a ready-made client secret from `OAUTH_APPLE_WEB_CLIENT_SECRET`, a JWT Apple lets live at most six months, so it would fail for everyone the day it expired. The API now signs it itself.

- `AppleClientSecret` (new, `Integrations/OpenIdConnect`) signs ES256: header `kid` = key id; claims `iss` team id, `sub` `OAUTH_APPLE_WEB_CLIENT_ID`, `aud` `https://appleid.apple.com`, `iat` now, `exp` iat + 300 s. A fresh one per redemption, so none is sent after its `exp`.
- `HttpCodeRedeemer` takes it instead of the fixed secret. A missing or non-P-256 key logs an error (key id only, never key material) and answers `provider.code_not_redeemed` without calling Apple. Google's path is unchanged.
- New variables: `OAUTH_APPLE_WEB_PRIVATE_KEY` (the `.p8` PEM, real newlines or `\n`), `OAUTH_APPLE_WEB_KEY_ID`, `OAUTH_APPLE_TEAM_ID`. `OAUTH_APPLE_WEB_CLIENT_SECRET` is removed from `compose.yaml`, `services/api/.env`, `.env.test` and `services.yaml`.
- `compose.yaml` and `.env` carry a development P-256 key for the local and QA stacks; the `oidc` sandbox accepts any `client_secret`.
- `docs/architecture/sessions.md` production notes updated.

## Risks
- Production must set the three new variables from the Apple developer account before deploy; without them web sign-in with Apple answers `provider.code_not_redeemed` (logged). Google and the app keep working.
- The committed key is a development key only; it is trusted by nothing but the sandbox.

## References
- Story: https://app.shortcut.com/soirely/story/80881 (blocks sc‑555; found by sc‑559)
- Apple, "Creating a client secret" (Sign in with Apple REST API)

## Evidence of work
`tests/Unit/AppleClientSecretTest.php` (9 tests, green locally): header and claims, ES256 signature verifies with the public key; `exp - iat` = 300 ≤ 15,777,000; each redemption gets a new secret; escaped-newline keys read; missing / P-384 / RSA / garbage keys make no secret, log one error and never the key; Apple is sent the signed secret; without a key Apple is not called and `provider.code_not_redeemed` is thrown; Google still redeems with its own secret.

Also run locally on the changed files: `mago analyze`, `mago lint`, `mago guard`, `lint:comments`, prettier. Not run locally: the full API suite and php-cs-fixer (no stack in this worktree); CI covers both.

## Next Steps
- QA: **Continue with Apple** on the web against the sandbox signs in as before; Google web sign-in unchanged; app Sign in with Apple untouched.
- Ops: set `OAUTH_APPLE_WEB_PRIVATE_KEY`, `OAUTH_APPLE_WEB_KEY_ID`, `OAUTH_APPLE_TEAM_ID` in production; drop `OAUTH_APPLE_WEB_CLIENT_SECRET`.

author: guillaumelauzier
body:
## Objective

`/resources` and `/events` now show the same open Spin-Out Lab cohort, drawn from the server's cohort record. A failed list, stats or cohort read now says Unavailable, with Try again, instead of looking empty or showing nothing.

Closes #6992

## Implementation

- **One card.** `LabProgramCard` is now used on both pages.
  - `LabProgramSlot` draws the card's states: loading, the card itself, the programmes' empty line, or Unavailable with Try again.
  - The card is fed by `useCohortRecord`, which each page reads once. The places count comes from the same record through the new `placesFromRecord`, so the cohort brief is not read twice.
  - The card names the cohort as the record does, for example "December 2026". It no longer uses the client-side `openCohortCopy()` number.
  - A blank Starts, Applications close or Places field reads "Not recorded".
- **Read states.**
  - `useLiveList` now returns `{state, items, retry}`, where `state` is `loading`, `loaded`, `empty` or `unavailable`. Its logic lives in the pure helpers `listRead`, `statsRead` and `listState`.
  - The new `useSiteStatsRead` reports failures through `reportError` and returns `{state, stats, retry}`.
  - `useSiteStats` keeps its old shape, because `PublicDirectoryPage.jsx` (not in this PR) still uses it.
- **Separate empty lines.**
  - On Resources, programmes and events each have their own empty line.
  - On `/events`, with no filter set, the empty line now says "No upcoming events are scheduled right now." The "match your filters" wording stays for when a filter is set.
- **Panel order.** Resources puts panels that have rows before panels that don't; an open cohort counts as a row.

### Behaviour change on failure

This PR changes what visitors see when a read fails.

- **Resources lists:** a failed list read used to show that list's empty sentence, such as "No open roles right now." or "Nothing is scheduled right now.". It now shows "Unavailable" and "We could not load this list." with a Try again button that reads the list again.
- **Resources figures:** a failed `/api/public/stats` read used to be swallowed and show nothing. It is now reported, and the header says its figures are unavailable, with Try again.
- **Spin-Out Lab card:** on `/events`, the card used to be drawn from the client-side cohort count even when nothing had been read. On both pages it now shows only a cohort that the server's record returned. A failed cohort read says "Unavailable. We could not load the open cohort." with Try again; it never says "No programme is open."
- **Never 0:** no failed or missing read draws a 0. A blank field reads "Not recorded".
- **Directory page:** `PublicDirectoryPage` is unchanged. It still receives null on failure and draws no figures.

The house `DataState` component shows "Unavailable" as a chip followed by the sentence, so the page does not print "Unavailable. We could not load this list." as one literal sentence.

## Files changed

- `frontend/src/components/site/LabProgramCard.jsx` (new): the card, its slot, `hasOpenCohort`, and the empty and unavailable lines. It is a new file so that the Resources page does not import the events page.
- `frontend/src/pages/events/PublicEventsPage.jsx`: the card moved out; the Programs row now uses `useCohortRecord` and `LabProgramSlot`; adds `eventsEmptyLine()`.
- `frontend/src/pages/site/ResourcesPage.jsx`: Programs and Events sub-sections, Unavailable states for lists and figures, and the panel order.
- `frontend/src/pages/site/network.css`: three small layout rules.
- `frontend/src/lib/siteResources.js`: the read states, `useSiteStatsRead`, and the pure helpers.
- `frontend/src/lib/spinoutLab.js`: adds `placesFromRecord`.
- `frontend/src/components/README.md`: the `site/` row mentions the card.
- `documentation/architecture/decisions/D6992.md`
- Tests:
  - `frontend/test/resources_events_cohort_6992.test.mjs` (new).
  - Updated for the new behaviour: `network_hub_d679`, `network_events_jobs_d679`, `spinout_copy_6990` and `spinout_lab_week_names_6991`.

## Testing

All tests below are in `resources_events_cohort_6992.test.mjs`, which mounts both real pages against a mocked `fetch`.

- **Open cohort, no events:** both pages show the cohort card and the events' own empty line. A further test checks that a closed cohort shows the programmes' own line on both pages.
- **A rejected list read:** shows Unavailable and Try again, not the empty line. One read answers 500 and one rejects, and pressing Try again reads the list again and draws its rows. Further tests cover a failed cohort read and a failed stats read (no 0 drawn), plus the read states themselves.
- **No typed cohort value:** a record with blank fields reads "Not recorded". The test also scans the card, the events page and the Resources page for client-side cohort numbering.
- **Panel order:** panels with rows come before panels without.

Every command below exited 0:
- `npm ci` in the root, `frontend/` and `cloudflare-worker/`.
- `verify-before-push run`: `generated`, `build`, `guards`, `types-frontend`, `lint-undef`, `dark-mode`, `lfs`, and `affected-frontend` (50 files).
- `check-folder-docs`, `check-decision-ids`, `check-unused-imports`.

One earlier `guards` run failed `check-test-clock`, on a `setTimeout(r, 0)` in the new test. That line now uses `setImmediate`, and the check passes.

These tests also pass one by one: `spinout_lab_intro`, `spinout_landing_d385`, `program_presentations_6966`, `public_events_feed`, `event_types_parity`, `honesty_sweep_d332`, `account_phone_d700`, `contact_legal_cookies_d680`, `site_routes_d673` and `landing_home_d674`.

The full frontend parts (`frontend-1-of-2`, `frontend-2-of-2`) were not run locally; CI runs them.

Mutation check: 18 mutations, 18 caught, 0 equivalent.

## Risks

- **Ships to production:** the frontend build only. There is no Worker, migration or `wrangler.toml` change.
- **Visible change:** visitors see "Unavailable" with Try again where a failed read used to show an empty list. The Lab card now appears only when the server returns a cohort.
- **Rollback:** revert the PR.
- **Security:** no secret in the diff, no `dangerouslySetInnerHTML`, and no change to auth.

## Dependencies

#6990, merged via #7029. Not in scope here: the card's redesign (#6979) and the homepage's own copies of the read hooks in `LandingPage.jsx`. Part of #6976.

## Agent

S15 · Claude Code

## Help impact

None: public site copy for failure and empty states only. No Help guide describes these panels.

## Review requested

Session 1, or an agent from another vendor. Please check the wording of the failure states.
