author: erfirst
body:
## Summary

Cleans up the MIDI app so it works properly on the website and works better in general.

### Web / deployment fixes
- Trunk now builds with relative paths (`public_url = "./"`), so `dist/` works from any folder on a site (e.g. `/midi/`), not only the domain root.
- Removed the broken service worker. It tried to cache files that don't exist (`eframe_template.js`). `index.html` now unregisters it for anyone who still has it installed.
- Save on the web previously used `std::fs` and failed. It's now a browser download.
- Added a native browser file picker for opening files (before, the web only supported drag and drop, which doesn't work on phones).

### Playback
- Web playback rewritten: one shared AudioContext unlocked on a real user gesture (needed for Safari), a lookahead scheduler with note envelopes, and Stop that actually silences notes. Before, each Play created a new AudioContext (browsers cap these), leaked timers, and left notes ringing after Stop.
- Native playback prefers a real synth over Linux's "Midi Through" port, uses the right MIDI channels, sends all-notes-off on stop, and tells you when there's no MIDI output device.

### MIDI parsing and export (new `src/midi.rs`)
- Notes are tracked per channel, with a full tempo map and SMPTE timing support.
- Export keeps tempo and channels (it used to always write 120 BPM on channel 0) and orders note-offs before note-ons, so repeated notes aren't cut short.

### Editor
- All 128 keys with a keyboard and a bar ruler (before, every octave was folded into 12 rows).
- Playhead that follows playback; click or drag the ruler to move it.
- Add, delete, move and resize notes with snap; pan and zoom; undo and redo.
- Keyboard shortcuts: Space (play/stop), Home, Ctrl+Z/Y, Ctrl+O/S.
- Toolbar with BPM, snap, default note length and zoom; light/dark theme.

### Housekeeping
- Upgraded to egui/eframe 0.37, which requires Rust 1.95 or newer. Removed unused dependencies (serde, getrandom, persistence).
- CI now runs fmt, clippy (native and wasm), tests and a `trunk build`, and uploads the web build as an artifact.
- README covers usage, controls and how to deploy to a website.

## Testing
- `./check.sh` passes: fmt, clippy `-D warnings` on native and wasm32, 14 unit tests, `trunk build --release`.
- Headless Chromium, with the build served from a subfolder: file picker open, drag-and-drop open, add/move/delete note, undo, play/stop (the AudioContext reached `running`; audio not listened to), download. No console errors.
- The native desktop build compiles and passes the checks above, but I haven't launched it (there's no display in the environment I worked in).

author: gokselozgur5
body:
Closes #391.

`SubFilter::predict_ca` previously carried no acceleration state and executed the same constant-velocity state transition (`x += v * dt`) as `predict_cv`, while `ImmFilter::predict` modeled only positive turn rates and `ImmFilter::step` accepted non-finite or non-positive `dt` values that poisoned subsequent fused states with `NaN`.

Extend `SubFilter` with 3D acceleration state and full 9x9 position-velocity-acceleration covariance blocks (`cov_pa`, `cov_aa`), implement exact quadratic constant-acceleration kinematics (`p += v * dt + 0.5 * a * dt^2`, `v += a * dt`) with continuous white-noise jerk `Q` in `predict_ca`, propagate acceleration updates across `update_axis` and heterogeneous 9-state IMM mode mixing, infer mirrored turn sign from estimated lateral acceleration in `ImmFilter::predict`, and reject non-finite or non-positive `dt` before mutating filter state.

| Commit | File | Diff | Responsibility |
| :--- | :--- | :--- | :--- |
| `cd22adf2` | `tests/imm.rs` | `+50 / -0` | Add failing reproduction tests for `dt` validation, `predict_ca` quadratic kinematics, and mirrored turns |
| `09adb062` | `src/imm.rs` | `+19 / -10` | Add acceleration state and covariance blocks to `SubFilter` |

| `4655c7ab` | `src/imm.rs` | `+14 / -5` | Handle mirrored turn sign in `predict` and validate `dt` in `step` |

body:
Fixes #8741 (and the earlier #7287).

**Review PR against my own fork — not submitted upstream.**

### What
Removes the `name:` and `about:` keys from `.github/ISSUE_TEMPLATE/ci_failure_report.md`.

### Why
The template is automation-only: its `{{ env.GITHUB_WORKFLOW }}` / `GITHUB_SERVER_URL` / `GITHUB_REPOSITORY` / `GITHUB_RUN_ID` placeholders are interpolated by `JasonEtco/create-an-issue`, which four scheduled workflows (`amd-mi200`, `no-torch`, `nv-flash-attn`, `nv-sd`) invoke on failure. Because the file also carried `name:`/`about:` front matter, GitHub listed it in the manual "New issue" chooser, which never expands mustache. Users who picked it filed issues titled literally `{{ env.GITHUB_WORKFLOW }} CI test failure`:

- #8741 (2026-10-04)
- #7287 (2025-05-16) — same artifact, 17 months earlier

This is a **recurring** defect, not a one-off. GitHub only offers a markdown template in the chooser when it has a `name:`; `create-an-issue` reads only `title`, `labels`, `assignees` and the body. Dropping the two keys removes the chooser entry and leaves the automation path byte-identical, so **no workflow file needs editing**.

### Alternative considered
Moving the file out of `.github/ISSUE_TEMPLATE/` also works but requires updating the four `filename:` references. Rejected here: it is a larger diff, and a PAT without `workflow` scope cannot push workflow edits. A patch for that variant is kept locally as a fallback.

### Verification performed
- `pre-commit run --files .github/ISSUE_TEMPLATE/ci_failure_report.md` → exit 0 (`check-yaml`, `codespell`, whitespace/EOF hooks). `check-license` does not apply: it matches only `.py/.c/.cpp/.cu/.cc/.h/.hpp/.cuh/.hip/.tr`.
- Front matter re-parsed with PyYAML: yields exactly `{title, labels, assignees}` — the keys the action consumes — and no `name`/`about`.
- Body unchanged.

### NOT verified
No GitHub Actions runner here and no way to trigger a scheduled run, so **the automated `create-an-issue` path is not verified end-to-end**, and the disappearance of the chooser entry was **not observed empirically** — it follows from GitHub's documented rule that only templates with a `name:` are offered. Suggested post-merge check: the next scheduled failure should open an issue with a real workflow name and run URL, and the template should no longer appear under "New issue".

No DeepSpeed code paths are touched, so no accelerator / ZeRO-stage / precision / parallelism / convergence / throughput / memory results apply.

### AI assistance
AI assistance (Claude Code) was used for the investigation and this change. Per `AGENTS.md`, a human must read every changed line and add the DCO `Signed-off-by` before this goes upstream — **no sign-off has been added.**

author: lubelski
body:
A shell command that timed out or was stopped could leave things running. This change makes sure everything the command started is stopped too.

## What changed

- `ShellCommandTool` starts zsh with `posix_spawn` and `POSIX_SPAWN_SETPGROUP`, so zsh leads a new process group whose ID is its own process ID.
  - `Process` has no documented way to choose the process group, which is why it is replaced here.
  - The child gets `/dev/null` as input, the pipe as output and error, the home folder as its working directory, and every other descriptor closed. Signals start from their defaults and unblocked.
- A timeout or a Stop sends SIGTERM to the whole group, then SIGKILL to the group after a grace period.
  - The grace period is `killGracePeriod`, two seconds by default.
  - A command that finished on its own is never signaled, so a process it put in the background keeps running.
- The output format and the `[exit status N]` line are unchanged. A command ended by a signal still reports the signal number, as `Process` did.

## What I found on this machine

- `Process` on macOS 27 already puts the child in its own process group, and `terminate()` appears to reach the whole group. A plain `kill` of zsh's process ID did leave a grandchild running, but `terminate()` did not.
  - That behavior is undocumented, so the new code no longer relies on it.
- The real gap in the old code was the missing SIGKILL. A command that ignores SIGTERM ran until something else killed it. The new test for that case hung for 97 seconds on the old code until I killed its zsh by hand.

## Tests

- 53 tests pass, 5 of them new.
  - A background process outlives a command that finished on its own.
  - A timeout stops a grandchild that ignores SIGHUP and is not one of zsh's jobs.
  - A command that ignores SIGTERM is killed after the grace period and reports exit status 9.
  - Stopping the task stops the same kind of grandchild.
  - The command leads its own process group, separate from the test runner's.
- The existing `aBackgroundProcessDoesNotHoldTheResult` still passes.

## Limits

- A process that moves itself to another process group or session, such as with `setsid`, is out of reach. That would need a process tree walk.
- The SIGKILL follow-up goes to the group ID after the grace period even if zsh has already exited. Process IDs on macOS are handed out in order, so reuse of that ID within two seconds is very unlikely.

author: arpan404
body:
A bot with Notion connected asked the person about every Notion tool. "See what you can see in my notion" on Auto-review gave three cards in a row, each saying "It doesn't say what it does, so you decide each time." The auto-reviewer never saw any of them, because a tool that declares nothing went straight to the person, and most apps' MCP servers (Notion's included) annotate nothing.

The owner's goal holds: an ordinary read in a connected app doesn't ask, even with the optional model review on. Three rounds of GPT security review followed; this PR now closes every finding (see the three "Security review" sections below).

## What changes

**Ordinary reads in connected apps run.** A connected app's tool with no trusted declaration is read from its own name (`spade_core::effect::named`). The name is folded (NFKC), case-folded and split at camelCase, digits and separators. It counts as a read only when all of these hold:
- it has a read verb (`list`, `get`, `search`, `fetch`, `query`…);
- no word for a change appears anywhere in it: as a whole word, inside a longer word (`searchandupdate`, `getOrCreate`), or in Spanish, French, German, Portuguese or Italian;
- it is plain ASCII;
- its description has no change word;
- its arguments are plain (next point);
- its definition matches the one pinned for its connection.

Such a read runs with no card while nothing untrusted is in view. With untrusted content in view, it goes to the reviewer first, never to the person.

**What a call reaches outranks its name** (`effect::shape`). These make a call unresolved, whatever its name:
- an input naming a destination (`url`, `host`, `endpoint`, `webhook`, `to`, `recipient`, `email`…), nested ones included;
- a name like `fetch_url`;
- an input taking text the app runs (`sql`, `code`, `script`, `expression`);
- a `query` argument, unless the tool searches and the query holds no statement word.

Unresolved calls are reviewed, go to the person under untrusted content, and a package needs `network` declared for them. A trusted server's own read-only annotation still counts as a read.

**Person-only actions are recognised anywhere in a name.** Paying, sending as the person, sharing or changing access or naming a secret, and deleting (in any letters, once folded) always reach the person.

**Everything else goes to the reviewer, in both modes.** Full access no longer runs an unresolved app tool on the classifier's abstain. It's reviewed; if the reviewer is down, the person decides. If the classifier reads a person-only effect as plausible (25% or more), it goes to the person. An effect the classifier raises is checked against the package ceiling.

**The reviewer's prompt is hardened.** It names the app and treats tool descriptions and arguments as untrusted claims.

**Definitions are pinned per connection.** On a connection's first use, Spade pins a digest of every tool it lists (name, description, input schema). A tool that changes, or is listed later (a write renamed to look like a read), loses its read status and any grant until a call of it is approved, then it is re-pinned. Requests carry the definition they showed. An allowed call whose tool changed before it starts doesn't run on that answer.

**Always allow for Notion covers ordinary writes only.** That means one verb of create, update, edit, append, add, set or insert on the app's own content, with plain arguments, and nothing that publishes, shares, sends, pays, deletes, or names access, credentials, a webhook, URL, email, message or comment. The grant is `{kind: "app", app, writes: true, tools: {tool: definition}}`, and each tool is pinned to the definition the person was shown.
- Spade refuses a grant naming anything else, or a tool whose definition changed.
- Tools added later aren't covered until the person sees them.
- It needs the person's stamp. Without standing, the card asks them to confirm it's them.
- It is per bot. Permissions › Apps shows it, and Ask again revokes it.

**Cards say what the gate decided.** Requests now carry the gate's effect:
- **Headings** come from that effect, never the tool's name, and requests of another kind get their own card. For example: "Quill wants to make 3 changes in Notion", "send 2 things in your name with Notion", "use Notion 2 times, in ways it doesn't declare".
- **Each call** shows what it makes, where it goes (nested recipients included) and the gate's reason, with its full arguments behind Details before anything is allowed.
- **Lookup wording** ("list your shared Notion pages") is used only for a gate read, so `list_and_delete` never reads as a read.

All rules live in `spade-core` and read only the call and Spade's own store. A cloud Spade applies them the same way, and nothing depends on a local secret.

**Existing installs** get this at once. Each connection's tools are pinned on its first use after the update, and answers the person kept for a tool before still hold.

Docs: ADR 0202 amendment 5 (revised), the note on ADR 0171, `spade/docs/autonomy.md` and `security.md`, and the Full access sentence in `packages/ui-core/src/spade-chat/security.ts`.

## Security review, round 1: what changed per finding

1. **Name-only reads were spoofable (P1).** Names are now folded and split, change words are vetoed anywhere in a name and in five more languages, and non-ASCII names never read. Definitions are pinned per connection, a changed or late-listed tool loses its read and grants until approved, and allowed calls are rechecked at dispatch. Name-only reads go through the reviewer whenever untrusted content is in view.
2. **Reads with caller-picked destinations or code (P1).** `effect::shape` makes those calls unresolved: reviewer-judged, the person's under taint, and they need `network` under a package. A trusted read-only annotation still counts as a read.
3. **App grants were too broad (P1).** Grants now cover only positively identified ordinary writes, named per tool and pinned to the definition shown. Unclear tools are never covered. Spade refuses anything else.
4. **Full access regression (P2).** Unresolved app tools stay on the review path. A downed reviewer means the person decides, a plausible person-only effect goes to the person, and the ceiling is checked against what the classifier raises.
5. **The batch card hid what it approved (P2).** Headings come from the gate's effect, cards split by effect, and every call shows its target and reason with its full arguments a tap away.

## Security review, round 2: what changed per finding

Round 2 (at 53798362f2) confirmed these hold: the 25% plausible threshold, the reviewer-down path to the person, the ceiling check on raised effects, and pins kept in Spade's SQLite.

1. **Sends weren't bound to what was approved (P1).** Each connected app call the gate lets run or the person allows is bound to the tool's definition digest and the session generation (\`Engine::bind_app\`, by call key). The connector sends it with \`Connectors::call_expecting\`, which checks both on the sending session right before each send. A replaced session or a relisted definition refuses it as not run. A renewal the call makes itself rechecks the definition before its one send. Reviewer verdicts are stored bound to the definition (\`app:<digest>\`), and one reused after a restart holds only for it. A retry after the person reconnects an app is sent only while the tool is unchanged. The ADR now says pins record what a server *claims*, never what it does.
2. **A legacy kept "yes" survived a description change (P1).** Kept answers now live under the tool's whole definition. An answer under the older identity (which left the description out) can only say no (\`effect::kept_answer\`). A changed tool is pinned again only after the reviewer or the person approved it, never on the rules' say alone.
3. **Shape gaps (P2).** A schema or arguments nested deeper than 16 levels are unresolved. A query given as a list or an object is read whole, every str

author: riff-como-technologies[bot]
body:
Refs #929

`just copies BASE HEAD` lists each copy that the lines of `git diff BASE...HEAD` add to the Rust files and the Go files. The fix session and the verify of a pull request run the same command, so they find the same copies (rule 4b of the waves). `BASE` is `origin/main` and `HEAD` is `HEAD` when the command names neither. The work is `xtask copies`, a new module `xtask/src/copies/` with a scan for each language.

The question: none of its own. The change serves the rule of the code against copies: "Functions and repetition" in `docs/src/development/code.md`, and rule 4b of the waves.

### The fix of the verify of b907837

The verify of `b9078373` failed on the reach of a private table of `impl_texts!`, and on rule 4b. This head does the two items of the call of the lead:

- **One owner for the scope of a visibility.** `scope_of` of `rust.rs` gives the scope of each Rust item, also of the table of a macro. `macro_table` of `rust_sets.rs` gives only the texts of the table now, and its `match` of the visibility is gone. `syn` reads the visibility at the start of the macro, and `Reader::value` gives its scope with `scope_of`, as for each other item. So a table of `impl_texts!` with no visibility reaches its module, as `code.md` says.
- **The words of a visibility.** `Keyword::Super` and `Keyword::SelfValue` hold `super` and `self`, and `scope_of` reads them. No line of xtask writes `pub` now, because `syn` reads it.
- **The table of a trait.** `impl_closed_set!` implements the trait `ClosedSet`, so its table reaches the package, as before. `TABLE_MACROS` marks it, and `Reader::value` gives the package to it, as to each function of a trait impl.
- **The Rust extension.** `rust_reach` of `copies/reach.rs` reads `Lang::Rust.extension()` in place of the raw `".rs"`.

The new test `a_table_with_no_visibility_reaches_its_module_and_a_table_of_a_trait_reaches_the_package` has the sample of the verify, and a table of `impl_closed_set!`. A function of `src/b.rs` returns each of the four texts of `src/a.rs`. Only the text of `impl_closed_set!` is a finding. With the `rust.rs` and the `rust_sets.rs` of `b9078373`, the test also gets `src/b.rs:2 [return] "pack-one-x"`, and it fails.

On the commit of #886, the command lists no value of `ConsolePack` on a line of `src/api/mask/tests.rs`. The call of the lead expects no line of that file. Two lines stay, and the output of `b9078373` has them too. Each one holds `profiles`, the value of `ListKind::Profiles`. `ListKind` is `pub` in `pub mod ops`, so the file can name it, and the line 397 is a finding by `code.md`. The line 385 is `json`, a place that is no copy. The three literals of `ConsolePack` are no findings now, so the consts at the lines 31 to 33 of `tests/console_address.rs` name them as "the literal at":

```
$ just copies dbf912d2^ dbf912d2 2>/dev/null | grep '^src/api/mask/tests.rs'
src/api/mask/tests.rs:397 [row] "profiles": profiles is the value of ListKind::Profiles (src/ops/list.rs:47)
src/api/mask/tests.rs:385 [json] "profiles": profiles is the value of ListKind::Profiles (src/ops/list.rs:47)
```

The 9 findings of this branch that the lead accepted stay, and no finding is new. `origin/main` has no new commit since the merge of `b9078373`.

### What the change does

- **The values.** The command reads the tree of `HEAD` with `git archive`, so a commit of another branch needs no work tree. A package tree is the directory of a `Cargo.toml` or of a `go.mod`. The command reads the texts of each closed set: the serde names of a Rust enum, the tables of `impl_closed_set!` and of `impl_texts!`, a `match` that gives a text for each variant (such as `Error::kind` or a `Display`), each Go const of a named string type, and the rows of a Go map table such as `eventKinds`. It also reads each string const, each string of a const array or of a table of tuples, and each route: a text that starts with `/v1/`.
- **The scans.** A Rust file goes through `syn` for its declarations and through `proc-macro2` for its tokens. A Go file goes through a lexer of the Go specification, written in Rust, with the `;` that the compiler adds at the end of a line. Both give one tree of tokens, so one walk gives the class of the place of each literal in the two languages.
- **A finding.** A literal on an added line holds a value that its file can name. A route on an added line is also on another line of the tree. A const that the change adds has the value of another declaration or of a literal of its tree. Each string of a const array is such a const. A function that the change adds has the body of another function of its tree, apart from the names of its arguments. A const or a function is a copy also when neither of the two can name the other.
- **The words.** A value with a mark, a capital letter, or a digit, such as `read-error` or `--pin`, counts at each place of the literal, as a whole word. A value of plain words, such as `drift` or `no answer`, counts only when it is the whole literal, as in `"newer "`. A plain word also counts beside one more value that is no plain word, as in `"drift DriftFound "`.
- **The classes.** The class of a place tells what the literal does there: `compare`, `switch`, `value`, `return`, `call:NAME`, `field:NAME`, `row` or `row:FIELD`, and `other`. The lines of the second kind of finding are `const` and `helper`. These places are no findings, and the command lists them apart: `json` (a JSON or a JS input of a test, or a key of a map literal of a test), `rules` (a YAML file of rules of a test), `script` (a shell script of a test), `case` (an argument of `t.Run`, or a field such as `name` of a row), `label` (an argument of `t.Errorf` or of `panic!`, the message of `assert!`, or an argument for a parameter such as `where`), and `tag` (the tag of a field of a Go struct).
- **The output.** Each line gives the file, the line, the class, the literal, and each declaration that holds the value, with its file and its line. The command exits 1 when it lists a finding, and 0 when it lists none. An error of git or of a parse exits 2, as each command of xtask does.

### Two classes and a rule that the design does not name

- `script` and `tag` are no findings, as `json` is. A script of a test is the code of a stand-in, such as the fake `strata` of the observer, and the scan of #867 put it under "other". A tag holds the JSON name of a field.
- A literal is a copy only where its file can name the declaration of its value. So an unexported Go const of another package, a const of a package that imports the package of the literal, and a const of a test for other code are no copies of a literal. The scan of #867 put such words under "unexported", and the verify of `65332a08` passed with them. This reach is only for a literal. A const or a function that the change adds is a copy at any place of its tree, as the design says.

With these rules, the output of `2e955f30` keeps each raw word of the verify, and the output of `65332a08` has none of them.

### The output on 65332a08

On `65332a08`, the head that passed the verify, the command lists 72 copies, and no raw word of the verify of `2e955f30` is among them. 43 of them are literals and routes. The scan of #867 found these places too, and the body of #898 gives a reason for each one: words of the page (`off`, `lost`, `same`, `none`, `images`) that are also values of a closed set, the type `cluster` of a profile, the folder `testdata/api`, and a few routes and consts of `testkit` that are also in the code. The other 29 are lines `const` and `helper` of kind 2, and 26 of them are new on this head, because kind 2 has no reach limit now. Most are consts of `testkit` with the value of an unexported const of another package, such as `testkit.StateFile` and `check.stateFile`. The others are the copies that the tests of `internal/docs` keep, because `testkit` imports `internal/docs`, such as `docs.decode` and `testkit.Decode`. Problem: any change to src/gate, bin/archangel-gate.mjs or workflows/archangel-gate.yml meant hand-editing ARCHANGEL_GATE_SHA and re-copying the workflow in every watched repo.

- `archangel doctor` (online) warns per repo (id gate_pin:<repo>) when the repo's workflow pins a SHA older than the latest local Archangel commit touching those paths (git log), when the pin is unknown to the local checkout, or when the workflow differs from the canonical template ignoring the pin line.

TEST-007 production regression test for BUG-001 (issue #88): **5/5 scenarios PASS** against the deployed app (`v2-20261122-progress-flush`) and the real Cloudflare Worker/D1 backend. No mocked cloud API in the final run.

UTC window of the final clean run: `2026-11-22T04:21:57Z` → `04:22:08Z` (from the test script's own `results.json` meta). The runner's local clock was `Sat Nov 21 23:35 EST 2026`, which is UTC 2026-11-22 04:35 — so the UTC date is correct; a stale timestamp copied from a draft run was corrected in the report.

- Immediate logout after one reward: 0 → 1 → re-login 1.
- Three rapid rewards then immediate logout: 1 → 4 → re-login 4.
- Refresh + logout/re-login: 4 → 5 → 5 → 5.
- A/B isolation with distinct deltas (A 5→7, B 0→1) through repeated immediate switches: no loss or leakage.
- Real backend evidence: 62 Worker responses = 55 application requests (44 POST + 11 GET, all 200) + 7 OPTIONS preflights (204); paths `/create`, `/login`, `/me`, `/salt`, `/progress`, `/events`. Method/path/status only — no tokens, PINs or auth headers captured.

Only two newly created synthetic accounts (TEST-A / TEST-B aliases); no real accounts or production data altered. Browser-offline probe showed the UI did not falsely report a saved cloud state, and progress recovered after re-login; this is browser-local, not Worker-side failure testing. The deterministic A-in-flight/B-switch race remains explicitly untested. 0 unexpected page/console errors or failed requests (the only 3 failures were the intentional offline probe).

Report: `OPENCODE-TEST-007-REPORT.md`; 6 redacted screenshots in `test-reports/test007/`. All screenshot references verified against the committed tree before PR creation. Leave open for independent review.

Source evidence attached (sanitized): `test-reports/test007/results.sanitized.json` and `test-reports/test007/network.sanitized.json` — method/host/path/status and counts only, no headers, tokens, cookies, bodies, PINs or learner identifiers.

author: hajisensai
body:
拍板台 qiqSbvdxrk（维护者留言：「导入 zip、7z 等加密包或挂载根本上支持吧，这个是导入的工作」）。

## 改了什么

**Rust 胖核心**（`native/fushi_compute/src/archive.rs`，C ABI `ffc_archive_probe` / `ffc_archive_extract`）
- zip：ZipCrypto + WinZip AES-128/192/256（`zip` 9.8，MIT）；7z：AES-256，含加密文件名 `-mhe=on`（`sevenz-rust2` 0.25，Apache-2.0）。纯 Rust，五端交叉编译不需要 C 工具链。
- 探测返回格式 / 加密方式 / 条目数 / 归档指纹（SHA-256(长度 + 头尾各 1 MiB)）。
- 解包：zip-slip / 绝对路径 / 盘符 / NTFS 备用流整包拒绝，符号链接跳过，总字节数与文件数按实际写出量限，可取消；错口令（含 ZipCrypto 漏过校验字节、AES HMAC、7z CRC）统一报 WRONG_PASSWORD。
- RAR 不在 Rust 里解（UnRAR 许可不能链进 GPL 本体），探测只认出来交 7-Zip 命令行。

**统一解包点**（`packages/fushi_engine/lib/utils/archive/archive_unpacker.dart`）
- `ArchiveUnpacker`：zip / 7z 走原生库（探测与解包各一次后台 isolate），RAR 走 7-Zip CLI（口令经 `-p`）。
- 口令流程只写在这里：先试按指纹记住的口令 → 不对就删掉并带提示重问 → 错口令带「上次不对」重问 → 解开后按需记住；用户取消 / 宿主不能交互给稳定原因码。每次尝试解进新的兄弟暂存目录，成功才并入目标目录，错口令不留半截文件。
- `DiscoveryArchiveExtractor`（发现页下载 / torrent 整包 / 控制通道与服务端 `import auto`）和 `MangaSevenZipExtractor`（RAR / CBR / CB7，以及**加密的 CBZ / ZIP**）都改成它的薄包装。删掉了 `package:archive` 的 zip 内置解码回退：zip / 7z 现在五端都由原生库解，Android / iOS 上也能导入 7z。

**App**
- `AppArchivePasswordProvider`：系统安全存储（`flutter_secure_storage`，键 `archive_password_v1_<指纹>`）+ 口令对话框（文件名、错口令 / 记住的已失效提示、显隐切换、「记住密码」；AnimatedSize / AnimatedSwitcher 切提示，错口令重开时口令框抖动，时长走 `fushiMotionDuration`）。启动时装到 `ArchivePasswords.provider`；并发来问的加密包排队一次只开一个对话框。
- 片源库后台扫描用 `StoredOnlyArchivePasswords`：只用记住的口令、不弹窗（避免每次重扫都弹）。
- 发现页阻断码新增 `archivePasswordRequired`（追加在枚举末尾），任务行文案与控制通道文案都接上。
- i18n 只用 `i18n_sync`（en / zh-CN / zh-HK / ja 人工翻译，其余语言回落英文）；原生许可汇编已重生成。

## 覆盖的入口与格式
| 入口 | zip | 7z | rar |
|---|---|---|---|
| 漫画导入对话框 / 文件夹批量 / 控制通道（`importArchive`） | CBZ、ZIP（加密的走解包点） | CB7 | CBR、RAR |
| 片源库扫描（本地 / 远端） | 同上，只用记住的口令 | 同上 | 同上 |
| 发现页下载、torrent 整包（书 / 漫画 / 有声书 / 游戏） | ✓ | ✓ | ✓（需 7-Zip） |
| 无头服务端 `import` / 库扫描 | ✓（加密包报要口令） | ✓ | ✓ |

## 验证
- `cargo test --profile quick --lib archive`：10 passed
- `dart test test/archive_test.dart`（fushi_compute）：6 passed；`dart test test/utils/archive/archive_unpacker_test.dart`（fushi_engine）：14 passed
- `dart tool/heavy.dart --wait-max-min=10 -- flutter test`（口令对话框、发现页执行器、漫画包导入、片源库扫描、原生许可守卫、控制通道路由、下载任务种类、发现页生产装配，8 个文件）：226 tests PASSED
- `packages/fushi_server` `dart test discovery_import_host_test library_scanner_manga_test`：17 passed
- 全量 `dart tool/heavy.dart --wait-max-min=10 -- flutter analyze --no-pub`：No issues found
- 夹具用真 7-Zip 打包（AES-256 zip、ZipCrypto zip、内容加密 7z、加密文件名 7z、未加密 zip / 7z），生成命令见 `packages/fushi_compute/test/fixtures/archive/make_fixture_pages.py`。

## 没做 / 缺口
- 仓库里没有「挂载」概念（只有 UI 挂载），没有可接的地方。
- 书籍导入框 / 拖放不收 `.7z`，也不会把「装着 epub / txt 的 zip」先解包再导：通用「导入一个压缩包」入口目前只有发现页下载、torrent 与控制通道 / 服务端 `import auto`。要不要在书架 / 拖放加这个入口属于行为扩展，待拍板。
- 字体导入（`custom_fonts_page` 选得到 7z / rar，但 `font_download_service` 只解 zip）、词典包没有接入解包点。
- 分卷 7z（`.7z.001`）不支持；RAR 口令经命令行参数传给 7-Zip（进程列表里看得到），RAR 也仍然只有带 7-Zip 的平台能解。
- 没有「清除已记住的压缩包密码」的设置入口（需要的话可以按 `archive_password_v1_` 前缀删）。
- Android / iOS 交叉编译只靠 CI 的 native-compute gate 验证，本机只编过 Windows DLL。

### Release Notes

<details>
<summary>mw00/project-Maya (ghcr.io/joryirving/maya)</summary>

### [`v1.1.73`](https://redirect.github.com/mw00/project-Maya/blob/HEAD/CHANGELOG.md#v1173---2026-11-22)

[Compare Source](https://redirect.github.com/mw00/project-Maya/compare/v1.1.72...v1.1.73)

Inkling 2 Mini runs on far more PCs: NVIDIA cards from 8 GB (the experts that do not fit stay in RAM), V100 and RTX 20
cards, and AMD on Linux (Radeon RDNA 3 / 4 cards and the Strix / Gorgon Halo); it drafts with its official drafter and
earlier text where that is faster, with the same answers. Fixes: `--vram-reserve-mib` is kept on every start and
DeepSeek keeps the reserve for the whole run ([#​1026](https://redirect.github.com/mw00/project-Maya/issues/1026)); Hy4-Flash on two GPUs copies between them only where that is safe
([#​1100](https://redirect.github.com/mw00/project-Maya/issues/1100)) and no longer crashes at the start when a draft step gets invalid numbers ([#​1084](https://redirect.github.com/mw00/project-Maya/issues/1084)).

- **Inkling 2 Mini on cards from 8 GB (NVIDIA, Linux):** where the card does not hold every expert, the most-used experts stay in VRAM (from a profile shipped with Maya) and the others in RAM; for each token, the GPU copies the missing experts in or the CPU computes them beside it, split by rates measured once on the PC and saved (`~/.maya/ik2-offload-calib.txt`). An expert gives the same result wherever it runs, so the answers do not depend on the split. RAM holds only the experts the card does not keep: about 13 GB with an 8 GB card, 9 GB with 12 GB, 5 GB with 16 GB. The setup's verdict says what a PC needs and refuses in one line where RAM and VRAM together cannot hold the model. Where every expert fits, the v1.1.72 path runs unchanged.
- **Inkling 2 Mini on V100 and RTX 20:** their own tensor-core kernels (Volta and Turing); the setup accepts them and refuses only older GPUs, with the reason.
- **Inkling 2 Mini on AMD (Linux):** `maya-ik2` is built in HIP builds for RDNA 3 / 3.5 / 4 and runs where every expert fits: a Radeon with 24 GB or a Halo / APU with that much free memory. Prompts use the matrix cores and hipBLASLt picks measured once and kept beside the model (a read-only folder says so once). Tested on a Radeon 8065S; Radeon RX 7000 / 9000 cards are built but untested - please report.
- **Inkling 2 Mini drafting (`--drafting auto`, the setup's default where it can run):** the official drafter (`mtp.safetensors`, 0.6 GB, downloaded and checked by the setup) and prompt lookup (earlier text of the conversation) propose tokens, and one window checks them with the same math as one token at a time, so drafting on and off give the same answers. The first start measures no drafting, lookup and the drafter once and keeps the fastest for the PC (`--speed-calibration` measures again; `--drafting off|on` by hand). A drafter that would change the context or the pictures is left out with a NOTE (on a 24 GB card it fits up to about 200K positions; the lookup still drafts). Off for now on V100 / RTX 20 and where experts stay in RAM.
- **Inkling 2 Mini: the looped layers' gate step is faster on every card**, with bit-identical results.
- **Inkling 2 Mini: the Monitor** no longer shows a "0% of experts in VRAM" card for it.
- **Fix: `--vram-reserve-mib` on a normal start ([#​1026](https://redirect.github.com/mw00/project-Maya/issues/1026)):** `./maya.sh --vram-reserve-mib N` was only taken by the setup (GLM and DeepSeek); a start now writes it into the config as each engine's own setting, and the MiniMax, Hy4-Flash and Qwen setups take it too.
- **Fix: DeepSeek kept less VRAM free than the reserve ([#​1026](https://redirect.github.com/mw00/project-Maya/issues/1026)):** what the engine allocated after placing the experts came out of the reserve, so on an 8 GB card requests could fail for lack of memory. It now measures that once, keeps it free from then on (`vram-late.txt` beside the pack) and, on the start that measured it, restarts once by itself, so no request runs short.
- **Fix: Hy4-Flash on two GPUs with the IOMMU translating ([#​1100](https://redirect.github.com/mw00/project-Maya/issues/1100)):** the layer split copied between the GPUs directly, which faults on such PCs. Direct copies are now used only where the driver offers them, the IOMMU allows them and a test copy arrives intact; otherwise the hand-offs go through pinned RAM (`HY4_HOST_STAGE=1` forces it, `HY4_PEER=1` tries direct copies anyway). Tensor parallel no longer turns direct access on.
- **Fix: Hy4-Flash crashed at the start on some two-GPU PCs ([#​1084](https://redirect.github.com/mw00/project-Maya/issues/1084)):** a draft step whose numbers were all invalid read far outside the vocabulary; it now ends the draft, and a start whose model gives invalid numbers stops with a clear message.
- **Credits:** Inkling 2 Mini's engine is [@​alesha-pro](https://redirect.github.com/alesha-pro)'s (with [@​mrsirg97-rgb](https://redirect.github.com/mrsirg97-rgb), [@​OscarSheng](https://redirect.github.com/OscarSheng) and [@​cobra91](https://redirect.github.com/cobra91), v1.1.72), and the experts-in-RAM support builds on [@​OscarSheng](https://redirect.github.com/OscarSheng)'s cache code; the rest of this release is by [@​mw00](https://redirect.github.com/mw00) (peasantsmith).

## What and why

Slice 2 of the web presence track (#3861), as accepted in #3865. It puts the track's decision D1 into effect, and carries D1's decision record as a pending file.

The Book's sidebar is now organised by kind first, then by concern. After the front page:

- **Learn Bynk**: the six chapters, unchanged.
- **Concepts**: the 15 explanation pages the concern landing pages already mark **Understand**, grouped under each concern's landing page (decisions A and B), then the two comparison pages from About.
- **Guides**: the 88 how-to pages in twelve groups by task, exactly as in the proposal's table.
- **Reference**, **Specification**, **Troubleshooting**: unchanged. **About** keeps only Versioning & roadmap until slice 13.

No page moves: every guide keeps its URL, and the compiler's documentation links are untouched.

**Generator** (`generate-sidebar.mjs`)

**Decision record:** `design/pending/web-presence-slice-2.md` carries D1's ADR with `level: patch` (decision D), so the stamp assigns a patch version and the ADR number at merge.

Closes #3865

author: alessandropcostabr
body:
## What changed

Word and PowerPoint now share one run-preserving, non-recursive replacement helper. It computes matches from the original text, applies them right-to-left, and never searches inserted replacement text again.

The integration also:

- includes Word runs nested in hyperlinks;
- avoids processing linked headers and merged table cells twice;
- preserves all `w:t` nodes, tabs and breaks while normalizing Word runs/comments;
- respects PowerPoint soft-break boundaries and edits text inside grouped shapes.

## User impact

Previously replacements such as `cat` → `cats` could loop in Word, text inside hyperlinks/groups was skipped, cross-run matches could lose formatting, and linked/merged content could be processed more than once.

## Duplicate search

Searched open and closed issues/PRs for `office_text_replace`, Word hyperlink replacement, linked headers, merged cells, PowerPoint grouped text and soft-break replacement. No matching implementation was found. #158768 is complementary and only covers slide duplication safety.

## Verification

- `scripts/run_tests.sh` over the focused Office helper, DOCX and PowerPoint cases: 15 passed.
- `python scripts/check`: 22 checks passed.
- `git diff --check`: passed.

Tested on Linux with Python 3.14, python-docx 1.2.0 and python-pptx 1.0.2.

author: meta-harness-davecthomas[bot]
body:
## What this change does

The console gets an "Improve with AI" action beside a goal's description. It calls `POST /v1/goals/enrich`. The proposal shows in a panel beside the original text, with what the model added and its open questions. The operator can edit the proposal, then accept or discard it. Nothing changes until Accept.

- New goal form: Accept fills the Description field. Only the form's Save buttons save the goal. The request sends what the form has so far. That is the title, chosen repos, tracker, Jira project and label. It also sends the label's free issues by title and the picked refs, at most 200 in all.
- Goal page: the action shows while the goal is not met or canceled. Accept calls `POST /v1/goals/{id}/enrich/accept` and shows the saved description. If the service refuses the accept, the panel stays open with the reason.
- A failed proposal call shows an alert with the service's message. The description keeps what the operator typed, and the goal can still be saved.

Files:
- `console/src/features/goals/ImproveGoal.tsx` (new): the action and the proposal panel.
- `console/src/features/goals/ImproveGoal.test.tsx` (new): tests for the four checks, plus the goal-page accept path and a refused accept.
- `console/src/features/goals/api.ts`: `enrichGoal` and `acceptEnrichment` calls, and their types.
- `console/src/features/goals/NewGoal.tsx` and `GoalPage.tsx`: mount the component under the description.
- `docs/technical-design.md` (outside the task's paths): one passage in the New goal form section describes the action. AGENTS.md asks that a change to documented console behavior update the design in the same pull request.

Checks:
- `cd console && npm ci && npm run typecheck && npx vitest run`: install and typecheck passed; vitest passed 98 files and 497 tests, 5 of them new.

Decisions:
- The proposal opens inline under the description. A modal would hide the form it edits.
- The button is off while the description is empty, since the endpoint needs a statement.
- An empty proposal cannot be accepted.
- The service retries the model call itself. The console sends the POST once, as its `call` client does for a 502.

author: jaykk99
body:
BrowserBro's privileged `/api` endpoints accept no bearer token when `BROWSERBRO_TOKEN` is unset. A configured `BROWSERBRO_HOST=0.0.0.0` would therefore expose browser sessions, cookies and page evaluation to the network. This change refuses non-loopback binds without a token while preserving unauthenticated loopback use and authenticated remote binds.

Adds `tests/bind-security.test.js` covering loopback IPv4/IPv6 and public bind cases. Existing open PR #2 modifies session profile validation, not this startup guard; merge conflicts may still require a rebase.

Verification: source-level review completed; Node test and live runtime checks pending CI. Do not merge before tests.

author: izzyn0okami
body:
## Summary
- Write manually imported BIOS files to a temporary file and flush it before installation.
- Preserve the current BIOS as a backup before promoting the new file.
- Restore the previous BIOS if promotion fails, and recover a leftover backup if an earlier import was interrupted.
- Keep a backup if post-install cleanup fails, and report the condition in the game log.

## Scope
Only `BiosManager.import()` is changed. This does not add BIOS hash validation or change BIOS readiness rules, RomM firmware downloads, or core behavior.

## Validation
- CI/style/build validation pending.
- Device validation still required for successful import, replacement of an existing BIOS, and recovery after an interrupted/failed replacement.
- No merge or release is authorized by this PR creation.

author: charlieanna
body:
Fixes #4088.

The actual macOS Extension Host closed before the first window because its profile socket path exceeded Darwin's 103-byte limit. Eight stock host fixtures created profiles directly under the inherited temporary directory. They now use the existing private host root helper, including the stock, semantic, Kilo, quota, Requirements, source-recovery and Rustup tests. Existing profile isolation and cleanup assertions still run.

- The quota and Kilo setup regressions fail on master `b06e3d4268` because both fixtures bypass the shared root. All four focused setup and cleanup tests pass on the branch.
- The Node 22 extension build and test suite pass, with 806 passes and 22 explicit skips. Ruff and mypy (999 files) pass.
- On the separate integrated proof-gates checkpoint, the same installed VS Code ran the real first-Go and protected-directory cases after placing the profile below a short fixture root. On this PR’s fixture revision `e69d87bc7`, the actual macOS editor passed first-Go end to end with normal macOS `TMPDIR` and completed owned cleanup. Current head `f0abe0fba` adds that evidence to STATUS only. Required CI is pending.

The reproduction, evidence and current boundaries are in [STATUS.md](issue-review/mac-extension-host-socket-root/STATUS.md).

body: ## Causa / por quê Gap **2.8 (P0) de `docs/GAPS-ENTERPRISE.md`**: "IP allowlist — Inexistente". Empresas que compram plano Enterprise exigem restringir o acesso à organização a faixas de IP conhecidas (VPN, escritório, egress fixo). Sem isso o gap de segurança fica aberto e o pacote SOC 2 / ISO 27001 não fecha. ## O que muda **Migration `20261122220000_ip_allowlist.sql`** - Tabela `public.ip_allowlist` (`organization_id`, `cidr`, `label`, `created_by`) com `UNIQUE (organization_id, cidr)` e `ON DELETE CASCADE`. - `CHECK ip_allowlist_cidr_format` valida IPv4 (`0-255` por octeto, prefixo `0-32`) **e** IPv6 (exige `:` — sem isso a regra antiga aceitava `abc` e `deadbeef` como CIDR válido). - RLS: só `admin` da org via `has_org_role(...)`. GRANT para `authenticated` + `service_role`. - `organizations.ip_allowlist_enabled boolean NOT NULL DEFAULT false` e `organizations.last_known_ip text`. - `ip_in_cidr(_ip, _cidr)` IMMUTABLE — máscara em `bigint`, fallback textual para IPv6. - `is_ip_allowed(_org, _ip)` SECURITY DEFINER STABLE — **fail-open por desenho**: `enabled=false`, lista vazia ou org inexistente ⇒ libera. Nunca tranca ninguém fora por acidente. - `get_my_ip_status()` — jsonb com `{allowed, enabled, ip, rules}` para a UI avisar antes de ligar o bloqueio. - `touch_last_known_ip()` — lê `request.headers` (`x-forwarded-for` / `x-real-ip`) e grava o IP do chamador. **Frontend** - `src/hooks/useIpAllowlist.ts` — `rules`, `status`, `enabled`, `addRule`, `removeRule`, `setEnabled`; grava o IP atual (`touch_last_known_ip`) antes de ler o status. - `src/components/lux/settings/IpAllowlistPanel.tsx` — lista de regras, adicionar/remover CIDR, toggle de bloqueio, banner vermelho se o IP do próprio usuário não passaria. - `Configurações > Segurança` (`SettingsView.tsx`): nova aba `security` com ícone `ShieldCheck`. **Registry multi-tenant** - `ip_allowlist` em `ORG_SCOPED_TABLES` (`withOrg.ts`) + `tablesWithOrganizationId` do fixture. ## Verificado de verdade | Verificação | Resultado | |---|---| | Migration aplicada em Postgres 15 limpo (container efêmero) | OK — tabela, CHECK, RLS, 4 funções, GRANTs | | `ip_in_cidr` — 13 casos (IPv4 exato, /8, /24, /32, /0, octeto inválido, `null`, IPv6 exato/prefixo) | 13/13 corretos | | `is_ip_allowed` — desabilitado, habilitado+match, habilitado+fora, IP nulo, lista vazia, org inexistente | 6/6 corretos (fail-open confirmado) | | `UNIQUE (organization_id, cidr)` | duplicata rejeitada | | `CHECK` de CIDR — 7 válidos aceitos / 6 inválidos rejeitados (`abc`, `256.0.0.1`, `/33`, `1.2.3`, `999.*`, `deadbeef`) | 13/13 | | `tsc --noEmit` | **9 erros = baseline exato** (nenhum novo) | | `vitest run` | **987/987, 89 arquivos** | | `vite build` | exit 0 | | `scripts/check-migrations.sh` | "Migrations válidas (53 avisos de legado)" | | `vitest run src/integrations/supabase/__tests__` | 47/47 | ## Regra 8 Contém **DDL em produção** (nova tabela + 2 colunas em `organizations` + 4 funções) → **fica aberta aguardando o dono**, sem merge. ---

author: chunbin1
body:
### 变更说明

解决 macOS GitHub Actions runner 打包 DMG 时偶发的 `hdiutil: create failed - Resource busy` 导致发布流水线中断的问题：

1. **Makefile 增加重试与防锁机制**：
   - 在执行 `hdiutil create` 前调用 `hdiutil detach -force` 强制卸载可能残留的卷，并执行 `sync` 刷新文件写入缓存。
   - 增加 `create_dmg` 重试逻辑（最多 5 次，每次间隔 3 秒）。
   - 在 DMG 根目录创建 `.metadata_never_index`，防止 Spotlight 后台扫描。
   - 使用 `ln -sf` 确保符号链接幂等。
2. **CI 与 Release 工作流优化**：
   - 在 macOS 构建任务开始前禁用 Spotlight 索引（`sudo mdutil -a -i off`）。

author: aledbf
body:
## Why

A workspace restored from a checkpoint has to run. In #459, a fast (postcopy) load in compat completed (`setup, active, postcopy-device, postcopy-active, completed`) with no RESUME. `Resume` returned nil, and the guest never ran. QEMU's stderr in that attempt said why: `Failed to get "write" lock. Is another process using the image [/dev/fdset/2]?`

There were two faults:

- **QEMU starts a loaded guest only if it can take its disks, and reports a failure only on stderr.** QEMU 11.2.0-rc0 adds a held machine's block nodes inactive. Both run bottom halves (`process_incoming_migration_bh` for a full load, `loadvm_postcopy_handle_run_bh` for a fast one) activate them with `migration_block_activate(NULL)`. On failure they skip `vm_start()` and tell the monitor nothing. The load still completes, and the run state stays `inmigrate`. `Resume` read that as success, in full loads as well as fast ones. A full load onto an overlay that a running machine holds returned nil, leaving the machine `inmigrate` (the new `boot:record` subtest, on real KVM).
- **The boot tests leaked the lock.** `rootDisk` never closed its files. QEMU's image lock is on the open file description it is handed, which the test's `*os.File` shares. So the lock outlived the killed "in full" machine until Go's finalizer closed the file, and the fast load right after it was refused its overlay whenever no collection had run in between. That is why it was intermittent.

## What changes

- `machine.QEMU.Resume` sends `blockdev-set-active` after binding the disks, before `migrate-incoming`. QEMU's refusal becomes the resume's error (`resuming: taking the machine's disks: blockdev-set-active: GenericError: Failed to get "write" lock`), before a byte of the state is read. The run BHs then find every node active and start the guest.
- `rootDisk` in `boot/` closes its files when the test ends, as `extDisk` already did, and so do disklimit's data disks.
- `Disk.Locking` documents the contract: close a bound `Disk`, or its lock outlives the VMM. `spin-machine` already does.
- `boot:record` gains "a disk another machine holds": a resume onto an overlay that a running machine holds must fail with QEMU's reason, before the state is read. A unit test holds the same for a refused activation, and `TestResume` holds the order.

## Verification

- Reproduced on the laptop (KVM, `vm.unprivileged_userfaultfd=1`, QEMU 11.2.0-rc0, v20261122.01's tree) with `GOGC=off`, so the leaked file is never finalized. Main's code missed 10 of 10 fresh-process runs of `TestACheckpointIsWaitedOnByItsEvents`, with #459's exact events and stderr. This branch passed 50 of 50. With GC on, main's code passed 60 of 60 on the laptop, which matches a miss that is rare in CI.
- Bench loop, 100 fresh-process runs of the events test each (`check:record` on throwaway branches `exp-459-loop-before` and `exp-459-loop-after`, not for merge): main's code missed 3 of 100 (lab 44984233276), each with #459's events and the lock error on stderr. This branch missed 0 of 100 (lab 44984233299).
- restore-first on the bench (nested, spin's shape and login, v20261122.01's parts, 30 a side interleaved, `fast=true`, lab 44984162863), fix against main: evicted login −0.3 ms [−2.4, +4.8], `running` +0.2 [−1.6, +4.9], cached login −0.6 [−4.8, +1.7], all within noise. All 30 fast restores on each tree logged in.
- `go tool task lint test mutate` (30 refused, 0 survived). `boot:record`, `boot:cpu-plug` and `boot:rollback` pass on the laptop's KVM.

Closes #459

author: sky-compute
body:
## What

New library module `skyoauth_service::trust` (not wired to any endpoint, no migration, no dependency): `create_source` and `update_source`. They enforce IR-152, which nothing enforced before: a trust source's `discovery_url` (purpose `oidc_discovery`) and `token_review_endpoint` (purpose `token_review`) must exactly match an enabled `egress_allowlist_entry` when written.

- `create_source(tx, public_identity, &NewTrustSource, &SourceAudit)` and `update_source(tx, public_identity, tenant_id, id, expected_revision, &TrustSourceChanges, &SourceAudit)`. The caller owns the transaction and the commit.
- `SourceWriteError` (`#[non_exhaustive]`): `Unauthorized`, `InvalidDestination{member}`, `EgressNotAllowed{member}`, `UnsupportedIsolation`, `Registry(RegistryError)`. Display never contains the URL; 40P01/40001 arrive as `Registry(Retry)`.

## Order and locks

Create: URL syntax (before any statement), savepoint, READ COMMITTED check, `authorize_operator_locked` (TrustAdmin, tenant scope), egress entries `FOR SHARE` (discovery, then token_review), `create_trust_source`, audit append last (tenant `FOR KEY SHARE`, head `FOR UPDATE`).
Update: savepoint, isolation check, operator rows, `trust_source` row `FOR NO KEY UPDATE` (NotFound / StaleRevision before any entry lock), syntax of changed members only, entries `FOR SHARE` for changed members only, the compare-and-set `update_trust_source`, audit last.

`FOR SHARE` on the entry conflicts with a disable's UPDATE, so the check and a concurrent disable serialise. This puts `trust_source` before `egress_allowlist_entry`, against the README's step-1 by-name order; the README documents it, and a future entry writer must not lock `trust_source` after an entry row (and an entry writer that creates an operation must lock no `trust_source` row at all).

**Every update through `update_trust_source` takes `FOR UPDATE` on the source row at the compare-and-set** (it always sets `name`, and `trust_source` has BEFORE UPDATE row triggers, so PostgreSQL takes the lock from the SET list), until commit: `principal_binding` and `consumed_assertion` inserts referencing the source wait, or fail with 55P03 under a `lock_timeout`. Callers must commit promptly. Pinned by `every_source_update_blocks_references_to_the_source_until_commit` (no-op, status-only, URL-only and rename). The audit append must stay after the compare-and-set: before it, an update deadlocks with a consumer (`an_update_waiting_for_a_consumer_holds_no_audit_head`).

## Picks (all provisional until the maintainer ratifies the ADRs; dated 2026-11-21 stay provisional, Gate M0)

(inferred) unless marked:
- The functions take `public_identity: &str` and build the `OperatorRequest` themselves (Tenant scope, TrustAdmin), so a caller cannot ask for another role.
- Each call runs in a savepoint, so the caller's transaction stays usable after a refusal; a failed audit append undoes the registry write.
- Update checks syntax and entries for changed members only; an update that disables a source and changes a URL in one write is still checked.
- Status-only updates use the `trust_source.update` action (the action table's convention would use enable/disable: open).
- Audit event content carries no member names or entry ids (the envelope has no details field).
- Syntax rule: canonical form (lead ruling): the destination must equal `Url::parse(raw).as_str()`, with no raw whitespace, control character or backslash, no escaped unreserved character and no incomplete or non-hex `%` escape, https, a host, no userinfo and no fragment. A path of at least `/` follows from canonical form (not from IR-152), so a TokenReview endpoint is written `https://host:6443/`; the path-less form used by the `registry_trust.rs` fixture (a raw-writer fixture) would be refused if it went through `create_source`.

## Changed existing tests

- Unit test `https_urls_with_a_host_and_a_path_pass` renamed `canonical_https_urls_with_a_host_pass`, accepted list changed; `https://ISSUER.example/X` moved to the refused list (`other_destinations_are_refused_naming_only_the_member`).
- `a_near_miss_of_an_entry_is_refused` split: canonical values are `EgressNotAllowed`, non-canonical ones `InvalidDestination`.
- `only_a_trust_admin_of_the_tenant_may_write` extended (unlisted-URL cases for create and update; cross-tenant update at revisions 1 and 99).
- MALFORMED grew from 11 to 27 entries, which changes `a_malformed_destination_is_refused_before_any_statement` and `an_update_rechecks_only_a_changed_destination`.
- `a_deadlock_is_a_retry` reads the server's `deadlock_timeout` (the test role cannot set it).
- `an_update_waiting_for_its_source_holds_no_entry` and `a_refusal_releases_its_locks` (added in an earlier commit of this PR) were changed in the review rounds.

## Tests and mutants

664/664 locally on the merged head (PG 16.15; CI pins 17.12), 136 lib tests in-process: 24 trust tests (6 unit in `source.rs`, 18 integration in `service/tests/trust_source_egress.rs`). 39 mutants, 38 killed; the survivor is M10d (host check dropped; `url` refuses an empty https host at parse time), equivalent. M12b (update audit appended before the update) is NOT equivalent: it deadlocks with a consumer, and is killed by `an_update_waiting_for_a_consumer_holds_no_audit_head`. M16 and its weaker variant (step-2 lock as `FOR KEY SHARE`) are killed by integration tests; the logic-refusal savepoint mutants (M19a/b) by `a_refusal_releases_its_locks`; the new percent-escape mutants by the corpus unit test. After the last change only the five escape-related mutants were re-run; the others were not.

## Not done

No endpoint, HTTP or startup wiring; no DB trigger; the fetch-time `jwks_uri` match is T11.8; tenant status is not checked; address policy (loopback, link-local, private and metadata addresses, IPv4-mapped IPv6) belongs to the fetcher or the entry writer, not this check. Widening (IR-052) is undecided: the README says not to wire this path before that and T14.1/T14.2. No T00.x is ticked; 0001-0008 untouched.

## Verification

fmt, clippy `-D warnings`, `cargo +1.98.1 check`, doc `-D warnings`, docs-check, prettier on the README, nextest 664/664 on the merged head.

author: hdholm
body:
## Scope

Three desktop changes, all requested directly, plus a follow-up to the first. None changes financial behaviour.

**1. Freezes (79f92e0, af38168).** The desktop froze, and even the window manager's close button couldn't end it. GTK handles every window on one thread, so a stuck main loop answers nothing, and nothing inside the process can ask anything.
- **Watchdog** (`gui/watchdog`, started only by the launcher):
  - **Logging.** The main loop ticks a heartbeat every second, and a thread watches it. After 20 s without a tick, it writes every thread's stack (`faulthandler`) to `hang-<time>.log` under the data folder's `hang-reports`. The log names the main thread, and the latest five are kept.
  - **Prompt.** It then starts `gui/stall_prompt` as a separate process asking **Wait** (the default) or **Quit BreadSched**. The prompt withdraws itself if the heartbeat resumes.
  - **Quit.** Quitting records a hang report and ends the process. Nothing saved is lost: saves are complete SQLite transactions, and a lock whose process is gone is replaced as stale.
  - **On demand.** On Linux and macOS, `kill -USR1 <pid>` writes the stacks to `stacks-on-request.log`. af38168 guards this by `sys.platform` so it also type-checks on Windows, where `faulthandler.register` doesn't exist.
- **Report on restart.** The next start offers **Report Problem…** once. It opens the existing GitHub bug form with the version, what happened, and the start of the log prefilled (`issue_url` gains `what` and `log`). The home directory is masked as `~`, and nothing from the book is included.
- **Hidden dialogs.** A modal dialog behind another window looks like a freeze. When the main window becomes active, the modal dialogs over it come forward. **View → Bring All Windows Forward** presents this application's windows, dialogs last.

**2. Overflow arrows (68db8c6).** The toolbar and the tab row used to scroll under a horizontal scrollbar. As GnuCash's tabs do, `widgets/scrolling_bar.ScrollingBar` now scrolls them with no scrollbar, between a left and a right arrow:
- the arrows appear only while the row is wider than the window, and each is greyed out at its end;
- each click scrolls half the width shown, and the mouse wheel scrolls the row too;
- choosing a tab brings it into view.

**3. Slow work announced to the watchdog (25a06c4).** Opening a book, and above all upgrading a large one (back up, verify, migrate), blocks the loop by design. `watchdog.busy(doing, allow)` announces it: the watchdog waits up to the allowance (180 s by default) before asking, the hang log's first line names the work, and the prompt says "BreadSched has been upgrading your book for N seconds, longer than expected". `open_book_announced` wraps the open as "upgrading your book" or "opening your book". Background work (imports, reports behind progress dialogs) keeps the loop ticking and needs no announcement.

## Verification

- New GTK tests:
  - A freeze logs every thread's stack, and waiting neither quits nor reports.
  - Quitting records a report that the next start offers once, with the log filled in and no home directory.
  - The prompt waits unless told to quit.
  - Announced work gets its longer allowance, then the log and question name it; `busy` is a no-op without a watchdog; the prompt's wording names the work; upgrading a book announces itself before opening.
  - Hidden dialogs come forward, and Bring All Windows Forward presents only this app's windows, dialogs last.
  - A too-wide row shows both arrows: the left starts greyed, the right scrolls to the end and then greys. `reveal` works, a row that fits shows no arrows, and the toolbar and tab row are such bars.
- By hand under Xvfb: with the main thread stuck, the prompt appears in its own process and closes itself on recovery. At 1000 px, Scheduled's toolbar shows the arrows and no scrollbar.
- Full core suite passes. Full GTK suite: passes except the two tests that fail in this container on `main` too (`TestNativePrinting::test_long_tables_repeat_their_headings_on_every_page`, the CSV import dialog's minimum width).
- `make lint format-check typecheck typecheck-extended` and `mypy --platform win32|linux|darwin` over the GUI: clean.
- Not verified locally: running the prompt process on Windows and macOS. If it can't start, the log is still written and nothing is killed.

## Document disposition

- README.md, AGENTS.md, CONTRIBUTING.md: reviewed; no change needed. None describes freezes or toolbar scrolling.
- DESIGN.md (and its parts under docs/design/): `user-interfaces.md` updated with a section on freezes (including `busy`) and the toolbar and tab-row arrows. The index and the other parts are reviewed; no change needed.
- ROADMAP.md: reviewed; no change needed. No item covered these.
- CHANGELOG.md: updated. Two Unreleased entries (the watchdog entry covers the upgrade allowance).
- src/breadsched/USER_GUIDE.md: reviewed; no change needed. Troubleshooting and window layout are described per interface, in the desktop guide.
- src/breadsched/guide/desktop.md: updated. Find your way around (the arrows) and Troubleshooting (the prompt and its longer allowance while a book opens or upgrades, hang log, Report Problem, SIGUSR1, Bring All Windows Forward).
- src/breadsched/guide/web.md, src/breadsched/guide/cli.md: reviewed; no change needed. Those interfaces are unchanged.

## Repository contract

- [x] Every commit has the author's `Signed-off-by:` DCO trailer.
- [x] A tool that wrote a material part of a commit is named in an `Assisted-by:` trailer.
- [x] Financial fixtures are synthetic or deliberately sanitized.
- [x] Every document above has a disposition, and each updated document is accurate for this change.
- [x] A change a user would notice has a `CHANGELOG.md` entry under `Unreleased`.

author: plproduction
body:
## The problem

`prisma migrate deploy` sat directly in the build command, and `DATABASE_URL` is scoped to **all deploy contexts**. So simply opening a pull request applied that branch's migrations to the live database — before review, and regardless of whether the PR ever merged.

This isn't hypothetical. #10's preview build did exactly that an hour ago. That migration was purely additive so nothing broke, but the same code path would run a `DROP COLUMN` just as willingly, against the database real customers are using.

## The fix

Migrations run only when Netlify reports `CONTEXT=production`.

- **Production deploys** still migrate automatically — so a merged migration can't be forgotten, which was the good part of the original setup
- **Deploy previews and branch deploys** no longer touch the schema
- **A failed migration still fails the build.** Deploying code that expects a schema the database doesn't have is worse than not deploying

Previews share the production database, so the schema they need is already there. A preview whose branch adds a migration renders against the pre-migration schema; to exercise new tables in a preview, apply it deliberately with `npm run db:deploy` or point that preview at a Neon branch.

## Verified

| Context | Behavior | Exit |
|---|---|---|
| Local (`CONTEXT` unset) | skips | 0 |
| `deploy-preview` | skips | 0 |
| `branch-deploy` | skips | 0 |
| `production`, no local prisma | fails loudly | 2 |
| `production`, real Prisma 7 | runs migrate, fails build on unreachable DB | 1 |

The last row matters most — it confirms the production path genuinely still migrates and still fails the build when it can't.

## Two side notes

`npx` runs with `--no-install`. Plain `npx prisma` fetches from the registry when it can't resolve locally, and that currently lands an 8.x release candidate which rejects `migrate deploy` on this Prisma 7 project. Caught while testing this.

Also, `npm run build` now works on a machine without a database, which it didn't before.

## Merge order

Worth merging **before** #10, so the contracts migration is the last one that reaches production the old way.

author: nathancall
body:
## Outcome
A Python adopter's server-side cleanup code can revoke a pending invitation with no admin caller. `revoke_invitation_as_system(inv_id)` sets the invitation to `revoked` with `terminal_by = None` and runs no authorization check (ADR 0028 rules 6-10). `revoke_invitation` keeps its owner/admin check unchanged.

- **No caller id:** the method takes none, so a route that forwards a missing caller id can't reach the unchecked path (rule 8).
- **Call-site gate:** the `TenancyStore` docstring states the rule 7 gate: server-side system or automation callers only, never a user-facing or tenant-scoped route.
- **Postgres:** one transaction. The invitation row is read `FOR UPDATE`, then the pending check runs, then the update.

## Check
- `tenancy/revoke-invitation-as-system.json` is vendored byte-identical to spec main (sha256 `b374170db4e62d97ba55b612a8625da13bb38f4beaeb0d37b4268e11a0a03e18`) and wired into `tests/test_conformance.py`. `revoke-invitation-authz.json` still runs unchanged.
- `tests/test_revoke_invitation_as_system.py` covers a revoke with no actor, a non-pending refusal that leaves the invitation unchanged, and an unknown id, on both stores.
- Local run with `TENANCY_POSTGRES_URL` set (Postgres 16): `pytest -q`, 135 passed.

## How a user reaches it
From a job or other server-side code: `store.revoke_invitation_as_system(inv_id)`. It returns an `Invitation` with `status == InvitationStatus.REVOKED` and `terminal_by is None`. An unknown id raises `NotFoundError`; an invitation that isn't pending raises `InvitationNotPendingError`.

## Broken on purpose
Each break made tests fail, and the code was restored after each:
- In-memory, the method raises: 4 failed, including the fixture vector.
- In-memory, it records a non-null `terminal_by`: 2 failed, including the fixture vector.
- Postgres, it writes `expired` instead of `revoked`: 1 failed.

## Checklist
No secrets. Queries are parameterized. No new listener, permission or dependency (`pyproject.toml` is unchanged). No debug routes.

## Surprise
The repo's fixture runner is in-memory only, so the Postgres store is covered by the store tests rather than the fixture.

Not in this PR: the version bump and release notes.

# Description

I3S geometry conversion assigns a shared layer material definition directly to the working glTF material. Color conversion, texture-index remapping, and alpha-mode normalization then modify that shared input. Reusing it for another node converts the already-linear colors again, progressively darkening the generated materials.

Deep-clone the definition before converting it. The existing per-primitive material copies continue to handle primitive-specific alpha modes.

body:
## Summary

This adds a replay test for perf/sample.rs, the next lowest-covered kernel file. It extends `perf_sample_tests.rs` with `perf_wakeup_polls_signals_refreshes_and_traps`. The test makes the perf-wakeup case's calls through `Kernel::handle`, in the guest's order, and compares its lines with the guest's.

- **What it replays:** poll without a buffer and with one, `wakeup_events`, `wakeup_watermark`, the `O_ASYNC` signals of each overflow, `PERF_EVENT_IOC_REFRESH`, and `sigtrap`'s `SIGTRAP`, both handled and blocked.
- **Signals:** when a call returns into the guest's handler (`rip` at the handler), the test reads the siginfo of the frame the kernel built, does what `on_io` or `on_trap` does with it, and returns through `rt_sigreturn`.
- **Left to the differential tests:** the forked child whose event hangs up when it ends. The test stops at the guest's "blocked" line, the 12th of its 14.
- **`Attr`:** it gains `wakeup_events` (offset 48) and `sig_data` (offset 120).
- **Expected lines:** they are the guest's own. I built `tests/guests/processes/perf.c` with `build.sh`'s flags and ran `perf perf-wakeup` under the release build in `mise run linux-dev`. The differential job compares the perf-wakeup case (listed in cases.json) with Linux on every run.

No docs change: quality.md already lists `perf_sample_tests.rs`.

## Verification

- `cargo test -p paludarium-kernel --lib -- perf_sample_tests`: 2 passed, on macOS.
- `mise run lint:all`, including stable clippy, passes.
- Local `cargo llvm-cov` puts perf/sample.rs at 581 → 623 of 803 lines (72.4% → 77.6%). That is macOS, so the coverage job on x86-64 Linux is the evidence.

**Not verified:** the test on x86-64 Linux; CI will run it.

**Still uncovered:** the sample fields that no guest case asks for (ip, time, cpu, read, regs, stack and others), and the throttling. The perf-throttle case changes a sysctl and spins for 20 ms of CPU time.

**Known CI failure:** main currently fails `processes_mounts` ("exe status=-1" native vs "exe status=98" emulated), which this PR does not touch.

author: hn8w7ftp7j-afk
body:
Soccer rankings repeatedly disappeared during automatic Reader renewal: the server revoked the valid head while a 35–40 second replacement was still running, and the client separately received the new receipt before downloading its result.

Stage automatic renewals and atomically publish a fresh, validated replacement. Start renewal 90 seconds before expiry and terminate abandoned owned runs so retries can recover. A conditional current read returns a changed full result with its same-query receipt; the client validates the whole tuple and replaces it in one state update. Unchanged reads remain small. Fallback polling is bounded and rate-aware.

Manual requests, repricing, immutable 180-second deadlines, 45-second receipt freshness, identity/league fencing, model formulas, qualification thresholds, settlement and rebates are unchanged.

Validation:
- Targeted PostgreSQL renewal/race/orphan recovery, API contract tests and 32 provider cases pass, including real-proof ranking continuity and late/manual/repricing counterexamples.
- Final full isolated regression and production build pass. CI Verify 44985832221 passes for 8a6bd2032f132d415557ea82ceb5719c5ec2b18f, including PostgreSQL settlement, full tests, build and Reader packaging.
- Production 11.10.119 verified staged publication and atomic full/receipt transport with six ranked directions. Continuous verification found a remaining scheduler gap: REFRESH_NOT_DUE deletes the queue before the exact due instant and can let quotes expire before the next Reader POST. Ranking continuity is PARTIAL, with a follow-up due-time scheduling fix in progress.

author: imaimai17468
body:
## 何ができるようになるか

- `bun run mutate` で StrykerJS（Vitest ランナー）が走る。対象は coverage の gate が測るファイルと同じで、`vitest.config.mts` の `coverageInclude` / `coverageExclude` を読み込んで共有する。
- `ticket-work` の自己チェックで、変更したモジュールだけを変異させ、生き残った変異と、どの変異も倒していないテストを `reports/mutation/mutation.json` から引く。
- CI の `mutation report` ジョブが PR と main への push で走り、HTML レポートを成果物として残す。スコアや実行の成否ではジョブを落とさない（報告だけ）。

## 速さ（ローカル、12 スレッド）

| 対象 | 設定 | 秒数 |
|---|---|---|
| `src/shared/gateway/`（14 ファイル・353 変異） | そのまま | 72 |
| 同上 | `ignoreStatic` | 37 |
| 同上 | incremental、変更なしの 2 回目 | 7 |
| リポジトリ全体（50 ファイル・5,356 変異） | キャッシュなし | 421 |
| 同上 | incremental、変更なしの 2 回目 | 15 |
| 1 ファイルに絞る（`--mutate`） | incremental | 5 |

- **incremental を既定にした**: コードとそれを通るテストが変わっていない変異は前回の結果を使い回す。CI では結果ファイルを、依存（`bun.lock`）とテスト準備（`vitest.config.mts`、`stryker.config.mjs`、`src/test/**`）のハッシュごとにキャッシュする。これらが変わると結果が変わりうるので、作り直す。
- **`ignoreStatic` は使わない**: 時間は半分になるが、gateway 層の生き残り 63 件のうち 48 件（76%）が静的変異で、見落としの大半を隠す。
- **CI の分割はしない**: キャッシュがあれば PR の実行は差分だけになる。

## 決めたことと、その代わりに選ばなかったもの

- **TypeScript 7 と衝突する前処理**: Stryker は tsconfig を書き換えるときに `ts.parseConfigFileTextToJson` を呼ぶが、Go 実装の TypeScript 7 パッケージにはない。`tsconfigFile: ""` で書き換えを飛ばす。サンドボックスはプロジェクト全体を写すので、書き換える相対パスはそのまま解決する。`inPlace` で書き換えを避ける手もあるが、作業ツリーのソースを直接書き換えるので選ばなかった。
- **変更したファイルを選ぶ自前スクリプトは書かない**: incremental が同じことをする。
- **報告だけのジョブ**: Stryker が完走しなくても、実行ステップの `continue-on-error` でジョブは通る。レポートはその場合も上げる。

## 現状のスコア

全体の 76% の変異を倒している（倒した 4,055、生き残り 1,215、どのテストも通らない 44、エラー 42）。分岐 100% のテストでも生き残る変異が多く、足りないアサーションを探す道具として働いている。生き残りの解消はこの PR の範囲外。

## 確かめていないこと

- GitHub のランナーでキャッシュなしの初回にかかる時間。ローカルの 421 秒に対して、コア数が少ないぶん数倍かかる見込みで、`timeout-minutes: 45` はこの PR の最初の実行を見て直す。

## 確認

`bun run check`、`bun run test`（825 件）、`bun run dead-code`、`bun run dupes`、`actionlint`、`check-ci-gate`、frontmatter の確認が通る。`code-reviewer`（opus / high）の指摘はすべて反映済み（`✘` を削除候補と読む誤り、出力量、worktree ごとの初回、`progress` が端末以外で何も出さない点、`reports/` の無アンカー指定、ほかのファイルを指すコメント、キャッシュの保存条件と鍵）。

author: cldellow
body:
Fixes #116.

## Change

`collect_items_by_timestamp` (`data/collect_items.h`) collects objects at a past date. For each index it calls `reconstruct_items` twice, once for the current and once for the attic file. It passed the end iterators by value, and a block iterator's copy constructor copies its whole block buffer. So every index cost two full buffer copies, whether or not anything there matched.

The three end-iterator parameters of the two `reconstruct_items` overloads are now `const` references. The iterators' `operator==` is already `const`.

One file, three parameters. No change to the database format, the query API or the results. Current-data queries don't use this code.

## Impact

CPU time (user + system), Nova Scotia full-history database (Geofabrik full-history extract, imported with the `better-imports` build of `update_database`; see #2), warm cache, 4-core VM. Alternating runs against `master` (8edf11b): 5 per build for h1–h6, 3 for the rest. Output and peak memory are identical.

| Query | `master` | This PR | Change |
|---|---:|---:|---:|
| R13 (the prompting query) | 18,972 ms | 11,650 ms | **−39%** |
| R10 | 27,361 ms | 21,383 ms | −22% |
| Q | 1,779 ms | 1,361 ms | −24% |
| R9 | 16,146 ms | 13,518 ms | −16% |
| R12 | 19,597 ms | 16,547 ms | −16% |
| S | 14,457 ms | 12,413 ms | −14% |
| R7 | 12,396 ms | 11,022 ms | −11% |
| h1 | 1,237 ms | 1,204 ms | −3% |
| h2 | 6,336 ms | 5,910 ms | −7% |
| h3 | 5,047 ms | 4,994 ms | −1% |
| h4 | 325 ms | 329 ms | +1% |
| h5 | 1,696 ms | 1,640 ms | −3% |
| h6 | 1,948 ms | 1,915 ms | −2% |
| **h1–h6 total** | **16,589 ms** | **15,990 ms** | **−4%** |

The gain grows with the number of indexes a query scans at a past date: wide boxes and member lookups gain most. h3, h5 and h6 are mostly current data, and h4 scans few indexes.

| Query | Text |
|---|---|
| R7 | `[date:"2018-01-01T00:00:00Z"][out:csv(::count)]; node(42,-67.6,47.5,-58); out count;` |
| R9 | `[date:"2018-01-01T00:00:00Z"][out:json]; way[highway]; out geom;` |
| R10 | `[date:"2018-01-01T00:00:00Z"][out:json]; nwr[name]; out center;` |
| R12 | `[date:"2018-01-01T00:00:00Z"][out:csv(::count)]; way(42,-67.6,47.5,-58); out count;` |
| R13 | `[date:"2018-01-01T00:00:00Z"][out:xml]; rel(42,-67.6,47.5,-58); out body;` |
| Q | `[date:"2018-01-01T00:00:00Z"][out:csv(::count)]; rel[route=hiking]; (._;>;); out count;` |
| S | `[date:"2018-01-01T00:00:00Z"][out:csv(::count)]; rel(45.566265,-62.428420,45.586924,-62.388716)->.s0; node(around.s0:0)["footway"]; out count;` |
| h1 | `[date:"2018-01-01T00:00:00Z"][out:csv(::count)]; nwr[amenity](44.60,-63.66,44.70,-63.52); out count;` |
| h2 | `[diff:"2026-11-12T00:00:00Z","2026-11-19T00:00:00Z"]; nwr(44.60,-63.66,44.70,-63.52); out meta;` |
| h3 | `[out:csv(::count)]; nwr(newer:"2026-11-08T00:00:00Z")(43.3,-66.5,47.1,-59.6); out count;` |
| h4 | `[date:"2018-01-01T00:00:00Z"][out:csv(::count)]; way[highway=primary](44.60,-63.66,44.70,-63.52); (._;>;); out count;` |
| h5 | `nwr(uid:{{UID}})(44.60,-63.66,44.70,-63.52); out meta;` |
| h6 | `[out:csv(::count)]; nwr(uid_touched:{{UID}})(44.60,-63.66,44.70,-63.52); out count;` |

`{{UID}}` is the user id with the most current objects in the box. It comes from licensed data, so it isn't given.

## Testing

- **Differential fuzzer** (`bench/fuzz.py`, see #2) against `master`: 1,500 history queries with `history,users,complete` (seed 141) and 500 plain queries (seed 142). **0 differences**; 5 timeouts skipped.
- **Every query above** gives identical output on both builds.

The change only avoids copies, so no mutation test applies.

## Memory

No new allocation. Peak RSS is unchanged within 1% on every query above.

## Limitations

- **Narrow test setup:** one regional extract, warm cache, one VM.
- **Copies elsewhere:** the iterators passed to `collect_items_by_timestamp` itself are still copied, but only once per call.

---
