author: duqaxxx
body:
A person who has lost every device can recover from the app with the recovery key written down at setup.

- The first screen, and the "removed" and "keys missing" screens, offer "Recover with your recovery key". The person gives the key's public part (person id, relay address, relay key), then types the key.
- The app reads the person's devices with the key and asks one question: "Could someone else have one of your devices?" No keeps the other devices; Yes removes every other device. It then offers a new recovery key, shown and typed back before anything is sent.
- The reset is sent by a recovery connection. Once it is placed, this Mac is one of the person's devices again and opens the history with the recovery keys: the one typed to start, and any earlier key the history is sealed to. "I no longer have this key" leaves that part unreadable, after a confirmation naming it.
- The recovery is done when every epoch held is sealed to the current recovery key. The app then names the recovery keys that can be destroyed and deletes every recovery key it held.
- The recovery secret never enters JavaScript and is wiped after use. A stop at any step drops the recovery keys held. A restart resumes at the step stored, and asks for the key again.
- Protocol: the link takes a recovery key (`AppLink.recover`), reports the recovery log and outcome, and can hold earlier recovery keys to open the history; a recovery outcome that retrying cannot change stops the link.

Not in this change, recorded in `docs/limits.md`: the unreadable list names conversations without dates, and once the reset is stored the recovery has no Stop.

author: ewels
body:
## Feature

F-006: Spike S2: vendor the 26.10 nf-lang grammars, generate a TypeScript parser with antlr-ng, parse the corpus and compare with `nextflow lint`, and generate the 26.10 catalogue from the language server.

Spec IDs: ADR-0005

## What changed

- `packages/lang-2610/grammar/`: the four nf-lang grammars at v26.10.7, verbatim, with upstream NOTICE and licence; `port.ts` maps every Java action to TypeScript.
- `pnpm gen:grammar 26.10 [--check]` generates `src/generated/` (committed, strict `tsc`, do-not-edit headers); `parseScript`/`parseConfig` (in `src/parser/parse.ts`, not yet on the pack entry, so the parser stays out of the initial bundle) with a two-stage parse like upstream's; errors carry upstream's messages and code-point columns.
- `pnpm corpus:lint` + `pnpm test:corpus` (CI job `corpus-parse`): 570 of 570 lint-accepted corpus files parse; three fixture differences listed with causes.
- Stage 1 predicts the `sep` and `type` decisions with full LL: sarek warm parse 37.8 s → 1.1 s, cold 51 s → 15.9 s.
- `tools/spec-extract` + `pnpm gen:catalogue 26.10 [--check]` (CI job `catalogue`): `catalogue/script.json` and `config.json` from the language server v26.10.2, deterministic across JVM builds.
- [Report](https://github.com/ewels/nf-builder/blob/feat/F-006/docs/research/2026-11-22-spike-s2-parser.md); [ADR 0020](https://github.com/ewels/nf-builder/blob/feat/F-006/docs/adr/0020-parser-and-catalogue-generation.md); ADR 0005 spike result; `docs/licences.md` rows.

## Definition of done

- [x] The feature's steps pass end to end: `pnpm test:e2e -- --grep F-006`, and every step in `features.json` is verified (no Playwright test; the CI `corpus-parse` and `catalogue` jobs are the end-to-end evidence, Q13)
- [x] `pnpm check` is green
- [x] New behaviour has tests that fail without the change, with requirement IDs in their names
- [x] Spec or ADRs are updated if behaviour or a decision changed: an `Accepted (agent)` ADR for each ADR 0001 trigger
- [x] `features.json` and `progress.md` are updated
- [x] The PR template is complete

## Checks

- [x] CI is green: every job of the CI, Deploy check and Scope guard workflows
- [x] `features.json`: only `passes` set and `notes` appended (the Scope guard job checks this), or the PR has the `scope-change` label and the decision is recorded
- [x] Budgets unchanged, or the raise and its reason are in `scripts/budgets.json` and below
- [x] No tests or visual baselines deleted, skipped or weakened
- [x] Fresh-context review done; findings addressed or answered below

Review: fixed the CI catalogue failure (overload descriptions now picked in signature order, not reflection order), explained every docs gap, removed the parser from the initial bundle (193.5 kB → 71.3 kB gzip), added upstream's "Unexpected input" message under the bail strategy, corrected the report (comment tokens, code-point columns, file counts, the scope of the tree-equality check), and noted the step evidence. Simplifier cuts applied (shared port entries, comparator helper, fewer options); regenerated output is byte-identical.

## Decisions made for the maintainer

- New runtime dependency `antlr4ng` 3.0.16 and dev dependency `antlr-ng` 1.0.10, pinned and grouped; generated parser committed; spec-extract as single-file Java; catalogue from language server v26.10.2 (nf-lang 26.10.4) against 26.10.7 grammars; build-time hosts; `ci.yml` jobs `corpus-parse` and `catalogue`, both blocking: [ADR 0020](https://github.com/ewels/nf-builder/blob/feat/F-006/docs/adr/0020-parser-and-catalogue-generation.md).
- Licensing: upstream NOTICE and licence ship with the grammars; licences.md rows for the generated parser, ported classes, catalogue text and antlr4ng.
- QA-03 cold-start risk handed to F-113 (notes); catalogue overload descriptions noted for F-109.

author: jazztong
body:
## Summary

The owner confirmed the design on 2026-11-22 ("Yes, all suggested"), and this PR builds it. Settings → AI → **AI models** sets which model does each job, per AI connection. Lite, Enterprise and Cloud use the same rows and words.

- **Rows**:
  - **AI agent replies**: live replies, Try it, scheduled tasks and previews. Default: Main model.
  - **Ask Ezy**: normal questions. Default: Fast.
  - **Translate**: default Fast.
  - **Writing help**: Suggest reply, the grey text, Fix English and Edit with AI. Default: Fast.
  - **Background checks**: Safety AI check, the phrase list and Dream lessons. Default: Fast.
- **Choices**: Fast, Main model, or any model the connection lists. Where the model has a level, **Speed and quality: Faster · Balanced · Smarter** sets reasoning to low, medium or high.
  - ChatGPT always takes the level.
  - An OpenAI key takes it only for reasoning models (gpt-5…, o-series; not chat variants or o1-mini). It sends a level only when the admin chose one, so the default stays as before.
  - Claude takes none; Claude thinking is phase 2.
- **Fixed on the main model, with no row**: Ask Ezy setup, the Dream mode merge and customer enrichment.
- **Per connection**: the setting is `ai_task_models[mode][row]`, and a save changes only the current connection. If a saved model is no longer listed, the row runs on Main (agent replies) or Fast and shows a warning.
- **Server**:
  - `ai/task-models.ts` resolves the row for every AI call (`taskCall` in `service.ts`).
  - Providers take `reasoningEffort` on the prompt or call.
  - `GET/PUT /api/ai/task-models`: admins only, 30 saves a minute. Errors are 400 `model_not_listed` and 400 `thinking_not_supported`.
  - Audit `settings.ai_task_model` records before/after choice and level only.
  - Logs add `task` and `thinking`, never text.
- **Upgrade**: a permanent start-up step, `migrateTaskModels`, moves the old "Model for suggestions" into Writing help.
  - `agent` becomes Main for every connection.
  - A model id is kept under the current connection.
  - `upgrade-from-oldest` seeds the old value and checks the result.
  - The old routes `GET /api/ai/reply-suggestions/model` and `PUT /api/ai/reply-suggestions {model}` now read and write Writing help.
- **Web**:
  - New `AiModelsSection` card in en, ms and zh-CN.
  - The Reply suggestions card loses its picker and gets one line pointing to Writing help.
  - The privacy and cost lines for Live translate and Fix English now name the right row.
- **Docs**:
  - The mock now uses the confirmed labels.
  - The confirmation is recorded in `design.md`, `mock-index.json` (latestConfirmed) and the `docs/ai-models.md` decision log.
  - Also updated: `docs/live-translate.md`, `docs/ask-ezy.md`, AGENTS.md, CHANGELOG and LEARNINGS.

## Verification

- `npm test` with coverage: 501 files, 6171 tests green. `coverage:changed`: **100 % (188/188)**.
- `npm run typecheck` and `npm run lint` are clean. A web-client contract test checks the client calls against the real routes.
- `npm run e2e`: 193 passed. The new `e2e/ai-models.spec.ts` failed in the full run because of a test bug (it clicked a hidden radio and relied on another spec's connection). After the fix it passed on its own. `reports.spec` (desktop) failed once in the full run and passed when run alone; this PR does not touch it.
- **Enterprise** on `pack:core` tarballs (`use-local-core`): typecheck clean, lint 0 errors (1 existing warning), 659/659 tests.
- **Screen review**: `e2e/ai-models-screens.mjs` drives the real server (fake WhatsApp, no model). 36 shots at 1280/360, light/dark, en/ms/zh-CN, with 0 page errors and 0 overflow; see `docs/screenshots/ai-models/`. The 30 mock shots were refreshed.
- **Dev Build check** is logged in `docs/dev-build-checks.md`.
- `/code-review` (medium) found 8 issues (3 important). All are fixed, with tests.
- No real AI provider was called. Unit tests check the model and level each call sends, using mock providers and a mocked network.

## Left for the owner

- **Local AI eval** (AGENTS.md rule for AI behaviour changes): before/after scores on the test build with a real model. The defaults keep today's models, except that Translate and Edit with AI now default to Fast.

Security: no new listener, outbound host or secret. Admin-only routes with audit.

- [x] test

author: ironleaf-maintainer
body:
Measured on Sonnet 5.5 over twelve designs (two notes, six kinds): whole
redrafts written against the judge's scores moved them 0-4 points for three
times the tokens. So the effort goes into the first draft and a further turn
only on what the page measured as broken.

- One fix turn at most, and only for words cut off, boxes on top of each
  other, a squeezed column or a block left out; contrast and a page up to
  12% too full are put right without the AI.
- The first draft gets a page plan per kind, a reference design, a spacing
  system (section, heading, group and panel gaps) and the room it has
  (the note's words against what the pages hold).
- Pages are filled with scale, never by spreading sections apart.
- The last fit leaves the footer its room.
- The narrow-column check counts characters a line.
- Scoring the pages is an option for trials, off in the app.

Twelve designs: 20-53k tokens in and 17-91 s each (was 35-116k and
58-138 s), scored 67-76 by the judge.

author: bhu103-data
body:
## Problem identified in actual WebGL
The latest validated main `ca55c38` daytime spawn screenshot still shows the 32-piece ground-floor hotpot masonry nearly black, even though the timber detail is visible. Reading the shader inputs revealed compounded multiplication of the locally generated stone atlas, material color `0xb5b5ae`, and 5 relatively dark per-instance stone colors. This is a local material defect, not an obstacle or missing texture.

## Narrow fix
- Change **only the hotpot plinth's cloned material** from generated `pbr.cutStone` to the **already loaded Poly Haven CC0 photographic concrete `pbr.stone`**, preserving its diffuse/normal/ARM roughness texture chain and using neutral light limestone albedo `0xf3f0e9`.
- Keep 5 subtly varied, neutral stone tints with a lighter continuous cap; avoid white emissive or flat shading, and preserve dark night contrast.
- Preserve **32 stone meshes + 72 timber meshes, 1,248 triangles, 2 instanced draws**. No changes to positions, lighting, collision, interactive hotpot, roof, windows, road, traffic, other maps, network assets or texture memory.
- Regression: assert map/normal/roughness reuse; source material clone isolation; neutral tint brightness/variation; old geometry budget and window/sidewalk clearance.
- Browser QA: capture existing same-camera `00b-spawn-day.png` and record fixed lower-storefront luminance ROI to review against `ca55c38` actual screenshot. Avoid exposure-based hard thresholds that can flake with sunlight.

**Merge gate:** Node tests + Cosmos + real Chromium WebGL and inspect screenshot comparison. Not photogrammetry, not global exposure tuning.

author: troyjlee
body:
Test a linear relation on the translated monomials `(z - ρ)^i`. Its evaluation isolates the coefficient of the `i`-th derivative times `i!`. The jet functionals are therefore linearly independent, and their span has dimension `n`. The inherited `sorryAx` occurs in the definitions of the jet functionals and the ambient entire-function algebra through their existing construction lemmas (#4065 and #4061).

The full `lake build` and `scripts/lint.sh` passed. All 4,764 declaration signatures matched the base revision. The section checked in 6.05 seconds before and 5.92 seconds after the change.

```text
'RiemannMasullo.entireJetSpace_finrank' depends on axioms: [propext, sorryAx, Classical.choice, Quot.sound]
```

Closes #4067

body:
第三批切片 14（规格已由用户批准，对应 C1、C5、C7、C8）。规格：`docs/spec/slice-14.md`。

## 做什么

`orchestrator/cli.py release --repo <owner/name> --version <版本> [--dry-run]`，以及 `release --resume <issue> [--confirm "<原话>"]`：
- **执行**：按流程逐段执行"合并后 → 发布前 → 发布 → 发布后 → 上线后"，合并前段跳过。命令在发布开始时那个提交的一次性克隆里运行，环境里不带令牌，超时 30 分钟。
- **证据**：记录 stdout（sha256 加最后 40 行）、url、file 三种。命令退出码非 0，或缺少声明的证据，就停下（stopped）。
- **等人**：以下步骤会停下等人（waiting），写明要你做什么：
  - `ask:` 步骤，以及 `by` 为 human / external 的步骤；
  - 没写 `auto_when` 的步骤；
  - 发布档位达不到要求的 ai 步骤。
- **跟踪 issue**：机器人开一个 issue，开头有一个机器可读块，之后每一步一条评论。全部完成后写总结、关闭 issue，并在本机 ledger 记一笔。
- **续跑**：
  - 已完成的步骤跳过；
  - 停在等人的步骤必须带你的原话 `--confirm` 才能继续：人做的步骤确认后直接记完成；**ai 步骤确认后才真正执行**；
  - stopped 的步骤修好后不带确认重跑，带了确认会被拒绝；
  - 发布过程中流程文件变了，就停下；
  - 只认机器人发的、没被编辑过的记录。
- **发布档位**：这个切片只读原始值（spec-guard 项目读项目级 `takeover.release`，其他仓库读 `takeover.yml` 的 `release:`）。上限和降档在切片 15 做。

## 验收

代码由 Codex 写（delegate run `20261122120410.11326`）。我验收时发现一个语义问题：续跑确认会把"因发布档位不够而等人"的 ai 步骤直接记为完成，命令却从没执行；比如沙盒模板的 publish 确认后就会被跳过。打回第二轮（`20261122121738.24443`）修正后，ai 步骤确认后执行，原话记进记录；人做的步骤维持"确认即记完成"。
- 全部测试在 Python 3.9 和 3.10 上都通过（新增约 40 个）。
- 没有压制注释。
- 对沙盒真实跑了一次预演：沙盒还没有 `pipeline.yml`，按类别要套 plugin 模板，而这个模板在切片 16 才写，所以停下，退出码 2，符合预期。完整演练放在切片 17。

| S B18, Tap half | `K654 S-B18: "exhaust this card and exhaust a card" with the source the only card in play is not offered under cost = whole` | pinned (passes with the existing knob `cost: 'whole'`; check and play asserted) |

Today pin (default policy only, so it does not hide the defect): `K654 E-B9 today: under the default policy a number above what is held is offered; picked, it pays and gains nothing` |

### Offer-policy case list, corrections from the older engine's inventory
- Case 21: that engine does rule it (full bars partial). Today's behaviour stays pinned by `K579 case 21 (pins today)` in `offer.test.ts`; the other behaviour needs the three-way answer (full / partial / none), a later row and out of scope here. README now says a game can rule it.
- Already tested, nothing added: case 6 (`K579 case 6 (pins today)`), 16 (`K579 case 16`), 25 (`K583 case 25`), 26 (`K583 case 26`), 27 (`K579 case 27 (pins today)`), 31 (`K583 case 31`), 32 (`K579 case 32`).

S B18 (the half where a played card has left the hand: K583 case 31) and the case-list items 6, 16, 21, 25, 26, 27, 31, 32 above.

author: jerbouma
body:
Adds TA-Lib's Hilbert transform indicators and Ehlers' MESA adaptive moving average, in the cycle topic.

| Method | Indicator | Reference implementation |
|---|---|---|
| `get_hilbert_dominant_cycle_period` | the dominant cycle period | TA-Lib HT_DCPERIOD |
| `get_hilbert_dominant_cycle_phase` | the dominant cycle phase, in degrees | TA-Lib HT_DCPHASE |
| `get_hilbert_phasor_components` | the in-phase and quadrature components | TA-Lib HT_PHASOR |
| `get_hilbert_sine_wave` | the sine and lead sine | TA-Lib HT_SINE |
| `get_hilbert_trend_mode` | whether the price trends (1) or cycles (0) | TA-Lib HT_TRENDMODE |
| `get_hilbert_instantaneous_trendline` | the instantaneous trendline | TA-Lib HT_TRENDLINE |
| `get_mesa_adaptive_moving_average(fast_limit=0.5, slow_limit=0.05)` | MAMA and FAMA | TA-Lib MAMA |

All seven run on one Hilbert transform (Ehlers, 2001, Rocket Science for Traders): the smoothed price, the detrender, the in-phase and quadrature components and the homodyne discriminator, computed bar by bar per ticker. They equal TA-Lib bar for bar after its lookback (32 bars for the period, phasor and MAMA, 63 for the others), to a relative difference of 3.5e-11 on the test data and on synthetic cycles, and pandas-ta-classic's port as well. The recursions start on the bars TA-Lib's warm-up starts on, which the exact equality needs. FAMA takes about 80 more bars than MAMA to catch up with the price; on daily data that falls in the year before the start date that the Toolkit also retrieves.

MAMA uses the close, where Ehlers uses the median price; `close_column` selects another. The trend mode is NaN during the lookback, where TA-Lib returns 0.

The indicators fill `collect_cycle_indicators` and `collect_all_indicators`, and the period, phasor, sine wave, trendline and MAMA form a new "cycle" collection of `get_factor_analysis`. The phase (it wraps from 315 to -45 every cycle) and the trend mode (0 or 1) are left out of it, as their ranks say nothing. Through the MCP server the cycle measures are in the momentum tool, next to the seasonality, and MAMA and the trendline in the overlap tool, as TA-Lib files them. Every existing column is unchanged.

author: cazzer
body:
Labels the streets around the focused station and each entrance with the street it opens onto, so a rider can tell which road an exit comes out on. This is step 5 of the street layer and finishes the epic's core ask.

Work items: underground-ost.5 (epic underground-ost). Follow-ups filed: underground-ost.8 (entrance streets as panel text for screen readers), underground-ost.10 (streets under route bundles), underground-ost.11 (frame a bare station's entrances on phones).

## What changed
- **Entrance labels:** each entrance shows its street, side, corner or median, and the cross street, in DOM labels placed per frame in the canvas container (the useLevelLabels pattern, aria-hidden). Examples:
  - "Bedford Av & N 7 St · NE corner · elevator"
  - "Broadway · west side at W 94 St"
  - "Broadway median between W 95 & W 96 St"
  - "7 Av · east side · exit only"
- **Abbreviations:** MTA style, e.g. "N 7 St", "Park Av S", "St Nicholas Av".
- **Street names:** rotated along their streets and kept upright, with hysteresis so they don't flip. Streets an entrance label names come first. Names step aside from the route bundles and the interior outline.
- **Declutter:** greedy and sticky.
  - Entrance ranking: elevators first, then unique text, then one label per head house, then distance from the middle of the free area.
  - On phones, entrance labels go on two lines and take corner-anchored slots.
  - Blocked: the header, the footer, the panel, level labels (MEZZANINE / PLATFORM), entrance marks, and station markers and the focus ring at their drawn size.
  - The layout re-places once after the view settles.
- **Entrance marks:** faint marks for entrances the interior doesn't draw, at renderOrder 7.6, matched to the interior's by position.
- **Draw order is now automatic:** above the veil at about 1.9:1 when an interior shows, otherwise at 0.35 under the route lines. `?streets=under|over` still overrides it (TEMPORARY).
- `streetKey` moved to `src/lib/streetClass.ts`. Script outputs are byte-identical.

## Evidence
![Bedford Av on a phone: the elevator and each head house labelled with its street](https://github.com/cazzer/underground/blob/6865fec8be8a24ab723e48e385cae75598e2c3cf/docs/evidence/ost.5/L08-phone-full.png?raw=true)
![Times Sq on desktop: every exit labelled, street names beside the bundles](https://github.com/cazzer/underground/blob/6865fec8be8a24ab723e48e385cae75598e2c3cf/docs/evidence/ost.5/127-desktop-full.png?raw=true)
![96 St on a phone: Broadway medians and sides with their cross streets](https://github.com/cazzer/underground/blob/6865fec8be8a24ab723e48e385cae75598e2c3cf/docs/evidence/ost.5/120-phone-full.png?raw=true)

Phone perf at 390×844 with 4× CPU throttle, during a 6 s orbit: about 4 ms of script per frame, no long tasks, and about one style recalculation per frame (the label transforms). That was headless with a software GPU, so treat it as main-thread numbers only.

## Decisions taken alone
- **Draw order is automatic** (from the ost.4 UX review). ![auto at L08](https://github.com/cazzer/underground/blob/6865fec8be8a24ab723e48e385cae75598e2c3cf/docs/evidence/ost.5/L08-desktop-full.png?raw=true)
- **On a phone, a dense entrance cluster shows its most important exits at landing zoom.** The rest appear on pinch-zoom: Bedford Av shows 6 of 9 at landing. ![L08 phone DPR 3](https://github.com/cazzer/underground/blob/6865fec8be8a24ab723e48e385cae75598e2c3cf/docs/evidence/ost.5/L08-phone-full-dpr3.png?raw=true)
- **Duplicate entrances get context.** Duplicates within 15 m share one label. Other duplicates get the nearest cross street, then "north of" / "south of" it. This is computed in the client; the street files are unchanged.
- **Entrance labels may sit over route lines and trains.** Only the street names step aside.

## Verify
```
npm run typecheck && npm test && npm run build
```
2865 tests pass. Reviews:
- Code review: 4 rounds, final MUST-FIX 0.
- UX review at phone size: 2 rounds. The elevator must-fix and the marker-blocker must-fix are both resolved.
- Rebased onto main with nav's complex and outage changes. A complex interior covers all of its members.

## Deferred
- underground-ost.8: entrance streets as panel text, since the labels are aria-hidden.
- underground-ost.11: on phones the tall arrivals panel covers bare stations' entrances. This is camera framing, owned by the trains tab.
- underground-ost.10: street lines under route bundles.
- Look-card items for ost.7: label styling and the veiled-street order mid-reveal.

author: scobyseo
body:
Closes #292

T1-4 (Linux stand-alone IME, D3 + candidate gate + packaging) and the T2-1 key-log extension to the IBus frontend.

## What changed

**D3 full stack** — `engine-d3-ibus` drives a real `ibus-daemon` and GTK client through the shared `tests/e2e/run-d3.sh`; expectations come from `hunmin-sim --trace --layer word` (the word-buffered oracle this frontend actually runs). The shared runner gained an `HUNMIN_D3_HOST=ibus` mode; the case loop, X servers, private bus, injector and client harness are unchanged. Candidates use IBus's host lookup table, so the own-window gate does not apply; D2 asserts page size, contents and show/hide.

**Engine fixes found by real use** — the D3 layout seam used to pass a NULL Latin id, making the layer single-language and silently declining 한/영; `NULL` now keeps the existing Latin half and D2 pins it. Both `Hangul` (0xff31) and `Alt_R` (0xffea) are language keys — the physical key reports the latter under XKB `us`. The IBus panel shows a 한/영 property and the engine can emit T2-1's personal key log.

**Packaging** — `libhunmin`, `hunmin-data` and `hunmin-ibus` are separate binary packages; the jammy artefact has no fcitx5 dependency. `nobilus` build profile selects the 22.04 package set. `libibus-1.0-dev` is in Build-Depends and both Linux apt lists, with a CI gate that fails if the IBus lanes are missing, skipped or failed. `deb` and `ibus-jammy` run nightly; `linux` also runs nightly because `deb` needs its fcitx5 artefact. Each packaging step prints its own wall time.

**FE14** — `LICENSE.md` + `meta.json` beside `layouts/` and `compose/`, enforced by `doctor.py#check_terms` in `schema-contract`.

**Real-use evaluation** — `tools/ibus-real-use.sh` (desktop / portable / install) opens a real GTK editor with a private IBus daemon and the built artefacts, plus a live per-key trace and a mode toast; see `tests/manual-checklists/ibus-real-use.md`.

## Verification

- `ctest -j16 -LE slow`: 133/133 green. IBus D1/D2/D3 green; FE11 697/700.

author: kuddy-on
body:
Closes #1389

## Summary

- Add the bounded `internal/nodeswap` contract (`inspect | apply | restore`, SHA-256 revision fencing, and fixed `512 MiB` / `1 GiB` / `2 GiB` memory tiers with no arbitrary sysctl keys, file paths, sizes, or commands).
- Implement the Linux root Agent host swap executor (`internal/agent/swap_host_linux.go`) serialized under `host-swap.lock` with durable recovery state in `/var/lib/vastora/agent/host-swap.json` (`0600`):
  - `512 MiB` and `1 GiB` systemd KVM hosts: `256 MiB` LZ4 `/dev/zram0` (`priority 100`, `/usr/local/sbin/vastora-zram` waiting on `udevadm settle`, `/etc/systemd/system/vastora-zram.service`) + `512 MiB` zero-filled `/swapfile` (`0600`, `priority -2`, marked `/etc/fstab` entry) + `vm.swappiness = 60` (`/etc/sysctl.d/zz-petauron-swap.conf`).
  - `2 GiB` systemd KVM hosts: `512 MiB` zero-filled `/swapfile` (`0600`, `priority -2`, marked `/etc/fstab` entry) + `vm.swappiness = 10`, with no zram device or service.
  - Containers, non-KVM or non-systemd hosts, hosts outside `512 MiB` / `1 GiB` / `2 GiB`, hosts missing kernel `zram` support on zram tiers, hosts with `< 1.5 GiB` root free space, and hosts with pre-existing unmanaged swap/zram remain strictly `read_only`.
  - Detect external edits (`action_required`), check `MemAvailable > zram_logical + swapfile_used + 64 MiB` before `restore`, and block Agent decommission/uninstall until active managed swap is restored.
- Add forward-only Center SQLite migration `134` (`00134_node_swap.sql`), `GET /api/v1/agents/{id}/swap` and `POST /api/v1/agents/{id}/swap` (supporting both standard and `landingOnly` Linux root nodes), task lease/expiry/abandon-only disposition handling, and regenerated `docs/openapi.json`.
- Add confirmation-gated `NodeSwapControls` on the Node Manage sheet, execution abandonment labels in `ExecutionSettings`, and operator documentation in `docs/host-swap.md`.

## Verification

- Repository PR CI (`privacy`, `go-tests`, `go-packages`, `go-quality`, `go-build`, `integration`, `composite-runtime`, `web`, `deployment`, `security`, `CI / gate`) and `CodeQL` checks on exact PR head `e584538f`.
- Subsequent production release and isolated KVM host acceptance are tracked in local operations/task records per `AGENTS.md`.

Teksty: `src/copy/pl.json` w `develop` ma już `method.path`, `method.verdicts`, `method.details` i `nav.on_page`, więc `pnpm sync` nie był potrzebny i go nie uruchamiałem.

## Dowód

Testy napisałem przed kodem. Na `develop` z nowymi testami: 11 czerwonych (scenariusze drogi pytania, spisu treści i braku przebiegu plus lista katalogu, werdykty, zasady). Po zmianie: `pnpm test` 401 zielonych, 0 czerwonych.

- „strona zaczyna od drogi pytania”: `tests/evidence/method-page.test.tsx`, pierwszy h2 to `method.path.title`, 12 kroków `01`…`12` w kolejności `analysis.steps`.
- „spis treści przewija do sekcji”: `tests/routes/how-it-works.test.tsx`, klik „Katalog źródeł” w nawigacji „Na tej stronie” w szynie wywołuje `scrollIntoView({ behavior: 'smooth', block: 'start' })` na `#katalog`; przy „ogranicz ruch” `behavior: 'auto'` (sprawdzone mutacją: bez gałęzi test czerwieni się). Że nagłówek nie chowa się pod belką, pilnuje istniejący test `scroll-padding-top` w `tests/routes/app-bar.test.tsx`.
- „nie ma zakończonego przebiegu ewaluacji”: sekcja mierników pokazuje `method.metrics.no_run`, w jej tekście nie ma żadnej cyfry i nie ma linku.

W przeglądarce (Vite z proxy na API dev, prawdziwy katalog z 64 pozycjami): po kliknięciu „Katalog źródeł” nagłówek stoi 80 px od góry, belka ma 64 px, `scroll-padding-top` 80 px.

Zrzuty ekranu: nie dołączone. Oglądałem stronę w przeglądarce (niżej), ale nie mam jak wgrać obrazów do PR z wiersza poleceń. Do dodania ręcznie.

## Ryzyko scalenia

Drzwi: dwukierunkowe
Zasięg: lokalny, tylko strona /jak-dziala; nowe komponenty shadcn `accordion` i `badge` nie zmieniają innych stron

## Jak sprawdzone

- [ ] Python: nie dotyczy
- [ ] Python: nie dotyczy
- [x] TypeScript: `pnpm check` (Biome, 0 ostrzeżeń), `pnpm build` (`tsc -b` i Vite), `pnpm test` (401/401, w tym `tests/architecture/`), `pnpm knip` (tylko istniejące podpowiedzi konfiguracji), `pnpm depcruise` (0 naruszeń)
- [x] Ręcznie: /jak-dziala przy 1440 px jasny i ciemny, 390 px jasny, 320 px ciemny; brak przewijania w poziomie przy 390 i 320 px; klik w spis treści; rozwinięcie wierszy zasad. Nie oglądałem 390 px w ciemnym ani 320 px w jasnym. API dev nie ma zakończonego przebiegu ewaluacji, więc dużych liczb mierników nie widziałem na żywo, tylko w testach. Nie uruchamiałem `pnpm a11y` (axe).

Skille projektowe z AGENTS.md: wzorzec wizualny był już zatwierdzony w prototypie (`lab/about.tsx`, `lab/PLAN.md`), więc zasady z `frontend-design`, `design-taste-frontend`, `emil-design-eng` i `impeccable` przyjąłem z niego: jedna biała powierzchnia, bez kart i linii, ikona tylko przy nagłówku, podświetlenie wiersza przy najechaniu, kolor zmienia się płynnie dzięki globalnej regule z `index.css`. `animate`: jedyny nowy ruch to płynne przewijanie i rozwijanie Accordion, oba wyłączone przy `prefers-reduced-motion`. Tych skilli nie ładowałem osobno w tej sesji.

Kryteria ze zgłoszenia, których nie domknąłem: zrzuty ekranu w PR. Spis treści na telefonie stoi pod treścią, bo tak układa szynę powłoka z #122 (zgłoszenie dopuszcza „nad treścią albo pod nią”).

author: meszmate
body:
Step-up authorization (SEP-835), now that clients do it: Claude Code re-prompts for more OAuth scope during a tool call (v2.1.288), and Cloudflare's API MCP server shipped step-up on 2026-10-19. Next item 1 from the 2026-11-22 comparison.

**How it works**
1. **The refusal records what's needed (roll-access's evaluator).** When an OAuth connection's own rules refuse an MCP tool call, and adding one rule would let it through, roll records a step-up: the connection and that one rule, exactly as the gate decided it, resource and index included. It's kept for 10 minutes, at most 10 per connection. It's never recorded for:
   - a refusal by the person's role in a project
   - a move between projects, a copy or a link, where another check decided
   - `access`'s own rules over tokens and approvals
   - roll's quiet internal probes
2. **The challenge carries only the id (roll-mcp).** The refusal carries `Bearer error="insufficient_scope", scope="roll:step-up:<id>", resource_metadata=…` in `_meta["mcp/www_authenticate"]`, which ChatGPT reads, beside its usual text and widen link. A single, unbatched call from Claude Code 2.1.288 or later gets HTTP 403 with that `WWW-Authenticate` header.
3. **The consent screen shows roll's record (dashboard and roll-access).** It looks the id up as the signed-in person with `GET /v1/access/oauth/step-ups/{id}`. Anyone else's, an expired one, or an unknown one gets the same "no such step-up". The screen shows:
   - the one rule, said plainly when it reaches far (admin, reveal, every resource)
   - the connection it joins
   - whether the policy has an admin approve it

   The person can add it, deny it, or set up a new connection instead. "Add it" sends only the id.
4. **Adding it changes only the rules.** The rule joins the connection's stored rules in one transaction that rechecks the connection (live, not waiting on an admin) and decides on the merged rules whether an admin must approve. The token policy applies. The step-up is used once, and nothing else about the connection changes. The client's code is for that connection, so its other sessions widen too and nothing new is made. Mail goes out only when something was added.

A client never chooses what's proposed. Scoped tokens (`rlt_`) have no consent to step up. A progress-streamed call keeps the challenge in-band only.

**Two independent security reviews.** The first version let the client list rules in `scope`, and the consent screen ticked them onto the person's connection. The first review found:
- a client could pre-tick any rule
- role refusals would loop
- a resource it couldn't encode became every resource
- a widen reset other settings, or took an expired or the wrong connection

The redesign above came from that. The second review confirmed those were fixed and found more:
- placement refusals could still loop
- the token policy was skipped
- `access` rules were offered in one click
- a concurrent change could be approved unseen

All are fixed here.

**Tests**
- roll-access `step_up_widens_the_connection`:
  - the refusal's step-up shows the exact rule
  - someone else can't see it
  - adding it widens the same connection, and only on that resource, whatever the form sent
  - other settings are kept and nothing new is made
  - it's used once
  - a revoked connection's step-up is no one's
  - an `access` refusal has none
- roll-mcp `a_refused_oauth_call_challenges_for_the_rule`: in-band; 403 and header for Claude Code 2.1.300; in-band for 2.1.200; nothing for `rlt_`.
- Dashboard `consent.test.tsx`: shows and adds by id, warns when a rule reaches far, offers a new connection, and falls back to a plain consent when it isn't the person's. `access-api.test.ts` covers `stepUpId` and `broadRule`.

Gate: `cargo test -p roll-access -p roll-mcp`, clippy, `cargo test -p rolld --test auth` (the new route is classified), and the dashboard's vitest and `tsc --noEmit`.

author: joelmharvey
body:
CI tested the Action only from the working tree (`uses: ./`). Nothing ran the tag people use, and nothing noticed when `v1` sat three months behind `main`.

Two jobs in `ci.yml`, on the existing weekly schedule and on a manual run:

- **published-tag** runs `JoelMHarvey/vibecheck@v1` on this repository (must pass at the default `fail-on: high`) and on the planted sample app (must report at least one critical finding).
- **tag-drift** fails when `v1` does not point at the newest `v1.x.y`, or when `main` has a commit under `vibecheck/`, `action.yml` or `action_entry.py` that `v1` lacks. It prints the commits. Site-only merges do not count.

Neither runs on a push or a pull request, so a merge is never red merely because its release has not been cut yet (`RELEASING.md`). A manual run of this branch is linked in the first comment.

Merging this also deploys the site, with no change to it: the deploy workflow skips only Markdown and `docs/`.

body:

Profile reviews previously put old/new values and raw panel anchors on dense lines with unsupported arrow glyphs. They now show previous values in red `-` lines and new values in green `+` lines, with a legend and separate readable anchor/offset lines. Additions omit a fictitious removed value; restoring a position explicitly shows Default position.

The formatter is shared by Profiles, clipboard imports and shared-profile reviews. Saved receipts retain their reviewed values while theme or language changes redraw the text. The Saved setups guide demonstrates three changes including a moved panel. This follow-up changes presentation; profile storage, commands and application behavior stay compatible.

## Required review

- [x] **Documentation:** affected READMEs, user/developer docs, examples, and release notes are accurate.

Display boundaries use the shared Get/Format API; a bound review display redraws cached values when language changes. All eleven catalogs and aliases remain intact; untranslated messages use English. author: sircypkowskyy
body:
Closes #123

## Co i dlaczego

Strona główna przestaje być pustą rozmową z polem przyklejonym do dołu. Tłumaczy produkt i ma jeden przycisk „Sprawdź informację”, a pole jest na nowej stronie `/sprawdz`.

```
src/routes/index.tsx        -> HomePage (src/components/home-page.tsx)
                               hasło, wstęp, „Sprawdź informację” -> /sprawdz, „Jak działa Meritum”
                               przykład wyniku: ResultCard z examples.json, inert, bez ramki,
                               pierwsze twierdzenie w całości, następne wygaszone maską
                               trzy zasady z `method` z ikonami, legenda pięciu werdyktów
src/routes/sprawdz.tsx      -> NewCheckPage (src/checks/_new-check.tsx)
                               tytuł, wstęp, Composer w treści strony, przykłady, AiNotice
                               Rail -> SessionHistory (CheckHistory z historią karty i konta)
src/checks/_send.tsx        useSend wyjęty z _check-page.tsx, używany przez obie strony
src/components/app-bar.tsx  „Sprawdź” -> /sprawdz (tylko cel linku)
```

Wysłanie z `/sprawdz` i kliknięcie przykładu idą przez istniejące API i przechodzą na `/sprawdzenie/$checkId`. Nagranie i obraz działają przez te same przyciski co dotąd (`useAttachments`).

## Dowód

Testy napisane przed kodem (pierwszy commit), na fałszywym `fetch`:

- `tests/routes/home.test.tsx`: strona główna nie ma pola; przykład jest inert, pierwsze twierdzenie poza wygaszeniem; trzy zasady z ikonami i pięć werdyktów; przycisk otwiera `/sprawdz`.
- `tests/routes/new-check.test.tsx`: `/sprawdz` ma tytuł, pole nieprzyklejone, przykłady i informację o AI; historia w szynie otwiera sprawdzenie; „Sprawdź” i kliknięty przykład przechodzą na `/sprawdzenie/c_01`.

Przed zmianą 8 z 8 nowych testów nie przechodziło, po zmianie `pnpm test` daje 402 zaliczone, 0 niezaliczonych.

Testy rozmowy, historii, prywatności i wyniku, które otwierały `/` po pole albo wątek, otwierają teraz `/sprawdz` albo adres sprawdzenia. Testy belki oczekują `/sprawdz` przy „Sprawdź”.

Zrzutów ekranu nie ma w tym opisie. Stronę oglądałem lokalnie (szczegóły niżej), ale nie wgrałem obrazów do PR.

## Ryzyko scalenia

Drzwi: dwukierunkowe.
Zasięg: lokalny, strona WWW. „Usuń moje sprawdzenia” i sekcja konta zostają na stronie sprawdzenia; na `/sprawdz` ich nie ma.

## Jak sprawdzone

- [ ] Python: nie dotyczy
- [ ] Python: nie dotyczy
- [x] TypeScript: `pnpm check`, `pnpm build` (`tsc -b`), `pnpm test`, `pnpm knip`, `pnpm depcruise` przechodzą lokalnie po rebase na `origin/develop`
- [x] Ręcznie: `/` i `/sprawdz` w przeglądarce przy 1440, 768, 390 i 320 px, w trybie jasnym i ciemnym, bez poziomego przewijania. Nie wysyłałem sprawdzenia na żywym API i nie testowałem czytnikiem ekranu.

Skille projektowe: `frontend-design` i `emil-design-eng` wczytane; trzymałem się prototypu i design systemu, bez nowych kolorów i ruchu. Przykład wyniku nie ma animacji wejścia (`animate-none!`), bo ruch ma odpowiadać na działanie użytkownika. `design-taste-frontend`, `impeccable`, `animate` i `review-animations` nie były wczytane; zmiana nie dodaje ruchu.

## Lista kontrolna

- [x] Zgłoszenie jest podlinkowane i punkty z „Criteria of success” są spełnione albo opisane niżej
- [x] Nowe zachowanie ma testy `node --test`, pisane jako czerwone przed kodem
- [x] Eksporty mają JSDoc z `@feature`
- [x] Reguły architektury: widoki w `src/checks/_*.tsx`, trasy cienkie, pliki do 250 linii, depcruise bez naruszeń
- [x] Zmiany w UI: tokeny, komponenty i teksty z design systemu, werdykty ze słowem; zrzutów w opisie brak (patrz „Dowód”)
- [ ] Samoprzegląd skillem `mattpocock-skills:code-review` nie był uruchomiony; przejrzałem diff sam
- [x] Dokumentacja: bez zmian, `docs/architecture.md` już obejmuje `src/checks/_*.tsx`
- [x] CI bez testów e2e
- [x] Bez podpisów AI w commitach i opisie PR

Czego nie ma albo jest inaczej niż w zgłoszeniu:

- Zrzuty ekranu jasny i ciemny nie są dołączone.
- Na `/sprawdz` nie ma linii „Usuń moje sprawdzenia” ani sekcji konta. Prototyp `NewCheck` ich nie ma, a zostają na stronie sprawdzenia. Do rozstrzygnięcia, czy mają wrócić do szyny.
- Wszystkie potrzebne klucze były w `src/copy/pl.json` z `develop`; `pnpm sync` nie był uruchamiany.

## Odstępstwa od design systemu

- `CheckHistory` w szynie ma swoje linie między wierszami i przerywaną ramkę pustego stanu. Komponent jest użyty tak, jak jest w `develop`; zmieni się z design systemem (#126).
- Przykład wyniku to obecny `ResultCard` bez ramki, tła i animacji wejścia (klasy przez `className`, etykieta ukryta przez `data-reply`), zgodnie z notatką w zgłoszeniu do czasu design-system/007.

## Przegląd

Z decyzji właściciela ten PR jest scalany po zielonym CI, bez pętli recenzentów.

author: ivargrimstad
body:
Fixes #398

## Cause

Open Liberty doesn't expose the RESTEasy SPI to applications. When `RestEasyConfigProvider` registers `KrazoValidationResolver` (a `ContextResolver<GeneralValidator>`), RESTEasy fails with:

```
RESTEASY002145: NoClassDefFoundError: Unable to load builtin provider org.eclipse.krazo.bootstrap.CoreFeature
java.lang.NoClassDefFoundError: org/jboss/resteasy/spi/validation/GeneralValidator
    at org.eclipse.krazo.resteasy.bootstrap.RestEasyConfigProvider.configure(RestEasyConfigProvider.java:34)
```

As a result:

1. Krazo can't stop RESTEasy from validating controller parameters. RESTEasy's `GeneralValidatorImpl` throws on the violations and responds with 400 before the controller is invoked (the `save.person.age: must be greater than or equal to 18` warning in the issue).
2. The error escapes `CoreFeature.configure()`, so the rest of Krazo's initialization is skipped.

Liberty's `restfulWS-4.0` feature exposes no RESTEasy packages to applications (not even as third-party API), so the resolver can't be made to load there. The only standard switch RESTEasy honors is `@ValidateOnExecution` on the controller method or class. Krazo can't add it automatically, because RESTEasy reads it through reflection, not from the CDI annotated type.

## Changes

- **`RestEasyConfigProvider`**: register `KrazoValidationResolver` only if `GeneralValidator` is visible to the application. Otherwise, log a warning that names the problem and the fix: annotate controllers with `@ValidateOnExecution(type = ExecutableType.NONE)`. Krazo still validates the parameters itself and reports violations in `BindingResult`.
- **Documentation**: an Open Liberty note with an example in the quickstart's RESTEasy section.
- **`ValidationIT`** (added in #416): it couldn't pass on any server, which is why it also failed on GlassFish and WildFly:
  - it requested the form from `resources/validation`, which nothing served;
  - all four views were added as `index.jsp`, overwriting each other;
  - the form had no CSRF token, so the POST got 403;
  - it expected the message to contain `"foo"`.

  The form is now served by a controller and includes the CSRF token. `FormDataBean` is a plain object passed to the view through `Models`. As a `@RequestScoped @Named` `@BeanParam`, RESTEasy injects it as a Weld client proxy: Bean Validation then reads the proxy's unused fields, and `ConstraintViolations` can't find the `@MvcBinding` field on the proxy class.
- **New `ValidateOnExecutionFormController`**: tested on all servers. The tests for the plain `FormController` are skipped on Liberty.
- **`testsuite-liberty-managed` profile**: Open Liberty 26.0.0.11 (was `22.0.0.13-beta`), liberty-maven-plugin 3.8.2, and the Jakarta EE 11 platform, matching the TCK module's setup.

## Testing

With Krazo built from this branch:

| Server | `ValidationIT` |
|---|---|
| Open Liberty 26.0.0.11 (`-Ptestsuite-liberty-managed`) | 2 passed, 2 skipped (plain controller) |
| GlassFish 8.0.5 (`-Ptestsuite-glassfish`, bundled Krazo removed) | 4 passed |

Before the change, Liberty logs the `NoClassDefFoundError` above and rejects invalid submissions with RESTEasy's 400. After it, Krazo logs its warning, and the annotated controller renders its error view with the violation in `BindingResult`.

The full GlassFish testsuite has 6 failing classes on both `main` and this branch (`HiddenFormMethodIT`, `RedirectScopeBoundaryIT`, `RedirectScopeBoundaryOnRootIT`, `AnnotationDrivenConverterIT`, `ConverterPriorityIT`, `MixedSetupValidationIT`). At least `HiddenFormMethodIT` fails with `403 Validation of CSRF failed due to missing field`, the same missing CSRF token fixed here in `ValidationIT`. Those are left for a separate change.

author: take-cheeze
body:
## Bug
A resumable method is one whose block may suspend in a Fiber. When one is called from C, it runs its steps in a loop (`bc2cpp_resumable_resume_from_c`), and that loop calls the block itself. If the block raised, the exception left the loop, and the method, without re-entering the step. The step's handler states (its `ensure`, its `rescue`) never saw the exception.

In a self-compiled bc2cpp this left `ScanCache.compute`'s computing count raised (#1474). A later ENV read then died with `ScanCache::Error`.

## Fix (RESUME_FROM_C_HANDLERS)
When the step has handlers, the drive loop now runs the block under `bc2cpp_protect_call`. A raise is delivered back into the step: `raise_pending` is set and the exception becomes the resume value. This is what the Fiber runtime already does (`bc2cpp_method_frame_unwind_into`). The step's handlers run and re-raise whatever they don't handle.

## Check
`ensure_yield_raise_check` reproduces `ScanCache.compute`'s shape as a resumable method: a Fiber suspends in its block, so the method compiles to a step function. It is called from C with:
- a raise;
- a rescue's re-raise;
- a raise from inside `File.open`'s block;
- nested calls;
- `next`;
- a `rescue` in a resumable method.

Before the fix, the compiled counter stayed raised by one per raise (`[1, 1]`, `[2, 2]`, …) while the interpreter returned `[0, 0]`. After it, compiled matches interpreted.

The world pin moves to rpg-maker-clone `3b9b334` (take-cheeze/rpg-maker-clone#3379), which adds the check's policy entry.

**Not covered:** `break` or a block `return` through a resumable method's `ensure`. Those are C++ unwinds (`bc2cpp_block_break`, `bc2cpp_method_return`) that `bc2cpp_protect` passes through. A step's handler states never see them, whether C or a Fiber drives the step. Fixing it needs an `ensure`-only path for C++ unwinds that `rescue` clauses can't catch.

## Validation
- `ensure_yield_raise_check` passes.
- Existing checks pass: the 24 resumable, fiber, step, ensure, call_from_c and yield_c_boundary checks, run with the full-core library, so their behaviour parts ran too.
- A self-compiled rebuild with runner_generation parity is in progress; results will follow here.

body:
Karl applied the v2 help keyword map to production and verified it on 2026-11-22: **version 2, stuck 33, solve_it 20**. This commits that map so the repo matches production. **It makes no route, prompt or server code changes.** The server already reads the map from runtime config, through the same `helpKeywordMapSchema`.

## Migration: `supabase/migrations/20261206000000_lisa_help_keywords_v2.sql`
- **Contents:** a comment header first, then Karl's SQL byte for byte, guard included.
  - The header carries the `LYCEON-MIGRATION-REVIEWED` marker the repo hook requires, the annotation, and the re-run note.
  - The body was checked with `cmp` against the SQL as given.
- **The guard:** it raises unless the row is at version 1.
  - Re-running against production (now at v2) raises. That is intended.
  - A fresh database applies the v1 seed (`20261201000000`) first, so the guard passes there. Every CI pipeline applies migrations once, in filename order, and none re-applies them.
- **Timestamp:** `20261206000000` is later than every migration on every remote branch (the latest elsewhere is `20261205000000`).
- **Checked on local Postgres,** using the real table definition from `genesis-schema.expected.sql`:
  - the v1 seed gives `1 | 24 | 14`;
  - this migration gives `2 | 33 | 20`, matching production;
  - a second run raises `tutor_help_keywords is not at version 1`.

## Contract test: `tests/ci/tutor-help-keywords-v2.contract.test.ts`
The map is built from the two committed migration files, not hand-copied: the v1 `$json$` seed plus the arrays the v2 `UPDATE` appends with `||`. That derivation equals the JSON Postgres produced, compared exactly.

| | Message | Expected |
|---|---|---|
| K1 | (the map itself) | version 2; 33 stuck, 20 solve_it; parses with the server's schema |
| K2 | "dont know", "dont remember", "help me" | `stuck` |
| K2 | "whats the value", "u solve it" | `solve_it` |
| K3 | "I just didnt know how to do it", "how do I solve it" | `null` |
| K4 | "i dont know u solve it" | `stuck` (longest match: "i dont know", 11 characters, beats "u solve it", 10) |

**Plants:** each phrase was removed from the committed migration once. Each anchor occurs exactly once, and I checked it by line number. Each removal fails its own assertion:

| Phrase removed | Fails at |
|---|---|
| `"dont know"` | line 70 |
| `"dont remember"` | line 71 |
| `"help me"` | line 72 |
| `"whats the value"` | line 73 |
| `"u solve it"` | line 74 |
| v1's `"i dont know"` (the longest-match case) | line 85 |

Each removal also fails K1's count. Both files were restored byte for byte afterwards.

## CI gate H3 (`scripts/ci/tutor-help-level-gates.sql`)
H3 asserted **version 1** after the full migration pipeline, so it would have gone red with this migration. It now asserts version 2 with 33 stuck and 20 solve_it phrases, the production state.

Checked: it passes on the v2 database and fails on a v1-only database ("not version 2 with 33 stuck and 20 solve_it phrases").

## Verification
- `pnpm -s run build`: exit 0.
- `pnpm test`: 7,789 passed, 1 failed. The failure is `tests/assemble-batch.apply.test.ts` ("SASL: client password must be a string"). It is environment-only: it fails whenever a local Postgres is running in this container, which I started for the checks above. It does not touch this change.

## Deploy
Nothing to deploy. Production is already at v2. This only records it.

body:
## User-visible improvement

Keep waiting-agent marks crisp in forced colours: selected tabs and Inbox
no longer regain grey halos after the system appearance explicitly clears
shadows. Their marks, words, names and keyboard focus remain. Normal
elevation now paints CSS-authored layers back-to-front, matching Rune Kit;
stored tiers, glow replacement and the four-layer limit are unchanged.

Accessibility/contrast overrides the queued navigation category because the
observed halos violate the existing forced-colour contract. Next category:
alignment/spacing. This is a contained fidelity improvement, not a redesign
or a claim about physical-phone feel.

## Upstream adoption

- Advance `dc8f7f7213cbe43af45212de6998d530d0945187` →
  `52f858284387401dad7f7e12574ce7764f32889f`, after reviewing consumer
  changelog, public API and examples.
- All nine upstream manifest entries and their lock sources agree. The sole
  documented winit exception is `ba5690bf204b3f98bdd116601bca2c9fc588a693`:
  direct descendant of the new base, exactly the unchanged reviewed six-file
  Wayland cursor patch. Owned-fork review: no-phux/rune#4.
- All 23 Rune-source locked packages agree; no registry package, checksum
  or version changed. No new shim, allow or test skip.
- Adopt Kit's corrected CSS shadow order in both OWN adapters; prevent
  normal glow metadata from restoring alpha to forced/transparent roles.
  No new native mobile stand-in replacement is supplied by this range.

## Evidence

Fixture-only baseline `9b396f079` uses the old pin. The before/after review
covers 1,025 real Runtime/GPU pages with matching trees, plus 26 paired
live-server desktop/phone frames on isolated same-source servers. Selected
attention states include closed, keyboard-focused and opened Inbox,
1100×720 / 640×360, light/dark, normal/forced and true 2×. The core gallery
retains phone/small phone, keyboard-open, Settings, resources and Inbox.

Before: soft grey clouds around hard status marks on system-colour grounds.
After: compact hard silhouettes; status text, focus and selection stay intact.
Four actual presented-Pose regressions fail before the production correction
and pass afterward. Attention fixtures route real Focus Sidebar, Shift+Tab
and Space; independent review caught and corrected the non-Apple chord's
missing Shift without weakening any assertion.

Independent original-image review: IMPROVEMENT, no new production visual
regression in 28 viewed matched pairs; all 1,025 matching gallery trees are
identical. Live evidence is scoped precisely: ten core desktop/phone frames,
four actually opened 1100-wide Inbox frames, and twelve extra attached-terminal/
onboarding repeats. The latter eight attention-labelled and four 640-wide
Inbox-labelled captures do **not** prove a selected waiting tab, keyboard flow
or small live Inbox. The complete selected-flow matrix is the actual Runtime
gallery, not those live repeats. No live keyboard or physical-device claim.

Fresh integrated `31129dd46` review personally inspected 17 final originals:
IMPROVEMENT; no new visual regression. All 1,025 final trees match baseline;
all final gallery images match the accepted earlier candidate. Every 1,051
gallery/live PNG also passed CRC and IDAT checks. Source-specific review,
not matching pixels alone, provides visual acceptance. Private device/signing,
installation and hosting evidence are intentionally excluded.

## Native failure evidence

The previous release's single permitted retry failed read-only simulator
health queries. Its first native report could be lost before deletion; an
offline reproduction established that diagnostic-loss race, not the unknown
underlying app/runner failure. Neither failed attempt is qualified; no
further blind retry or tag movement is planned.

Retain strictly allowlisted **UNVALIDATED** original report/tree/input-gate
and scene bytes after owned simulator shutdown, before deletion, including
background evidence the seal handshake would replace. Original host failure
remains primary. Reject unsafe, changing or oversized files; a forensic-only
16 MiB limit uses pre-read size checks and bounded reads, never truncation.
No native acceptance limit, assertion, timing, input or retry policy changes.
Independent review caught and resolved unbounded reads; 19 focused tests
cover late publication, credentials, links, malformed/missing data, growth,

## Summary
Connects the Valley backcountry on foot all the way to the high country and populates Tuolumne Meadows, Tenaya Lake, Wawona, and Crane Flat with living trails, regional boards, outer-hub rescues, and a meaningful SAR progression payoff.

### Backcountry Foot Traverse & Tenaya Lake Content
- **Sunrise Trail (`Little Yosemite Valley` ↔ `Tenaya Lake`)**: Added two-way `RegionDoor` trailheads in `scenes/story/content/little_yosemite_valley.tscn` (`SunriseTrailUp`) and `scenes/story/content/tenaya_lake.tscn` (`SunriseTrailDown`) with `tioga_road` seasonal snow closure so players can walk from Happy Isles → Little Yosemite Valley → Tenaya Lake → Tuolumne Meadows entirely on foot in summer and fall.
- **Tenaya Lake Backcountry Camp & Fishing**: Added a backcountry tent site (`TenayaCamp`) at Sunrise Lakes Trailhead (registered `"tenaya_lake"` in `Backcountry.REGIONS` and generalized `BackcountryCamp.place_name`) and a brook trout deep-water fishing spot (`TenayaLakeBasin`).

### Outer-Hub Travelers, Regional Boards & Rescues
- **Outer-Hub `Travelers`**: Added `traveler_thru_hiker` (PCT/JMT hiker walking Tuolumne Meadows between Arrival, Soda Springs, Tuolumne Lodge, and Cathedral Lakes Trailhead) and `traveler_wawona_walker` (Wawona naturalist walking between Wawona Hotel, History Center, and Mariposa Grove), complete with 32px sprite sheets, portraits, rest-day weather routines, and regenerated `data/park/walks.json`.
- **Regional `BulletinBoard`s & Notes**: Placed working `BulletinBoard`s in `tuolumne_meadows.tscn` (`TuolumneBoard`) and `wawona.tscn` (`WawonaBoard`), and added 4 hub-gated seasonal requests to `BoardRequests.NOTES`.
- **Outer-Hub `Rescues` & Search-and-Rescue Pack Payoff**: Added 4 outer-hub SAR calls (`tenaya_lake_hypothermia`, `cathedral_peak_stranded`, `wawona_grove_lost`, `crane_flat_snowbound`), hub-gated `Rescues.eligible()`, upgraded `Rescues.REWARD`, and added the **Search-and-Rescue Pack** payoff — completing 3 rescues expands `Backcountry.canister_capacity()` from 12 to 20 overnight food items.

### Verification
Added `tests/backcountry_hubs_test.gd` (30/30 checks passing) and verified all 11 related headless suites pass with 0 failures:
- `backcountry_hubs_test`, `travelers_test`, `rescue_test`, `seams_test`, `open_world_test`, `travel_test`, `fishing_test`, `valley_life_test`, `half_dome_test`, `cast_test`, `smoke_test`

body:
## Ticket Specification
<!-- WAVE:2 -->
# T-90-feedback-20261122_011021-4-frontend-table-integration: Live Table Wiring — Throw-In Visibility Gating, Full-Size Cards CSS, Tight Hand Contour, 20%–80% Hand Overlap, Multi-Card Throw-In, Compact Icon Buttons & QA Presets

## Scope & Owned Files
Modify these frontend files to wire all Wave 1 backend & frontend modules end-to-end into the live UI:
- `frontend/src/components/ActionBar.tsx`
- `frontend/src/components/GameTable.tsx`
- `frontend/src/styles/table.css`
- `frontend/src/pages/GamePage.tsx`
- `frontend/src/pages/LobbyPage.tsx`
- `frontend/src/api/client.ts`
- `frontend/src/types.ts` (only if needed for preset/action types)
- `frontend/src/__tests__/GameTable.test.tsx`
- `frontend/src/__tests__/GamePage.test.tsx`
- `frontend/src/__tests__/LobbyPage.test.tsx`

Do NOT touch `README.md`, `ARCHITECTURE.md`, `play-local.sh`, or `backend/`.

## Requirements & Architecture

### 1. Strict Throw-In Outline Visibility Gating (`GameTable.tsx`) (ITEM-1)
- Render `[data-testid="throw-in-outline"]` (and its surrender wrapper `[data-testid="surrender-throw-in-anchor"]` when in `SurrenderThrowIn`) **ONLY** when the active viewing player can legally play a card into it:
  - `view.canThrowIn === true`
  - Viewer is NOT the defender (`myIdx !== view.defenderIdx`)
  - Viewer has NOT already passed (`!view.myHasPassed`)
  - Viewer has at least one legal throw-in card in hand (`(view.throwInCards?.length ?? 0) > 0`)
  - Remaining throw-in capacity > 0 (`(view.throwInCapacity ?? 0) > 0`)
- When ANY of those conditions fail (defender POV, player with no valid throw-in cards, player who has passed, or bout full), `[data-testid="throw-in-outline"]` MUST NOT be rendered in the DOM at all (neither inline nor above/below surrendered cards).
- Preserve the existing surrender placement behavior when visible (below taken cards for opponent surrender, above taken cards for active user surrender — note: when active user is the surrendering defender, the outline will now naturally be hidden for them and visible only to opponents who have legal throw-in cards and haven't passed!).

### 2. Unified Full-Size Cards Matching Outlines (`table.css`, `GameTable.tsx`) (ITEM-2)
- Define and enforce unified CSS custom properties in `table.css`:
  - Desktop (`>= 900px`): `--card-width: 100px; --card-height: 140px; --card-radius: 10px;`
  - Mobile (`< 900px`): `--card-width: 48px; --card-height: 68px; --card-radius: 6px;`
- Apply `width: var(--card-width); height: var(--card-height);` uniformly to:
  - Hand cards in `[data-zone="player-hand"]`
  - Attack & defense cards in `TablePair` inside Row 2 battlefield
  - `[data-testid="throw-in-outline"]` and `[data-testid="redirect-outline"]`
  - Talon deck & bottom trump card in `[data-zone="table-deck"]`
- Audit and remove any stale CSS rules in `table.css` that shrank `.card`, `.hand-card`, or `.table-pair .card` smaller than `--card-width × --card-height`.

### 3. Active Hand 20%–80% Overlap Layout + Tight Non-Rectangular Highlight Contour (`GameTable.tsx`, `table.css`) (ITEM-3 & ITEM-5)
- Replace the old hand card layout and old rectangular hand highlight box inside `[data-zone="player-hand"]` completely (ignoring all past specs for the old highlight box):
- Measure the available width of `[data-zone="player-hand"]` via `ResizeObserver` (with a sensible test/SSR fallback width when `ResizeObserver` returns 0, e.g., `640px` desktop / `300px` mobile).
- Call `computeHandLayout(...)` and `buildHandContourPath(...)` from `frontend/src/utils/handLayout.ts`:
  - Pass the current card count, measured container width, canonical card size (`100×140` desktop / `48×68` mobile), and the set of lifted card indices (playable cards and/or selected cards shifted upward).
  - Position each card cleanly according to the returned layout coordinates inside the hand stage box so all cards overlap between **~20% min and ~80% max** of card width, keeping every card's left-side rank & suit always visible.
  - Even when a player holds **30–52 cards** (verified with `large-hand-stress`), the hand stays 100% inside `[data-zone="player-hand"]` with zero horizontal overflow off-screen and zero overlap onto `[data-zone="table-deck"]`, Row 3 Col 3 controls, or the left/right sidebars!
- Render the tight non-rectangular hand highlight contour as an `<svg data-testid="hand-highlight-contour" data-contour-shape={...}>` containing the `<path d={contour.pathD} />` stacked strictly inside the hand stage using **CSS Grid layer stacking (`grid-area: 1 / 1`)** (following the zero-overlap CSS Grid spatial rules — NEVER using `position: absolute` or `position: fixed` to place seats, hands, bouts, or sidebars!).
  - When playable or selected cards shift upward, the highlight contour immediately distorts non-rectangularly around those exact raised cards and hugs the entire hand tightly at all times.
  - Only show the active highlight glow when the active viewer has legal moves/turn prompt (or consistent with turn-indicator highlighting), keeping it responsive on resize, card play, selection toggle, and POV switch.

### 4. Always-Visible Drag Interaction (`GameTable.tsx`, `table.css`) (ITEM-4)
- Audit `table.css` and `GameTable.tsx` for any `.dragging`, `[data-dragging="true"]`, or drag-state rules that reduce card visibility (`opacity: 0`, `opacity: 0.15`, `visibility: hidden`, etc.) and replace them so dragged cards ALWAYS remain fully visible (`opacity: 1; visibility: visible;`).
- Ensure dragging a card from `[data-zone="player-hand"]` to a target outline, table card, redirect outline, or `[data-testid="throw-in-outline"]` keeps the card clearly visible throughout the entire drag gesture.

### 5. Remove "Throw In" Button & Wire Drag / Double-Click / Multi-Select Batch Throw-In (`ActionBar.tsx`, `GameTable.tsx`, `GamePage.tsx`) (ITEM-6)
- **Remove the `"Throw In"` button completely** from `ActionBar.tsx`, `GameTable.tsx`, and `GamePage.tsx` (no `"Throw In"` button anywhere in the DOM!).
- Wire all three throw-in interactions in `GameTable.tsx` -> `GamePage.tsx`:
  1. **Single-card drag:** Dragging any legal throw-in card onto `[data-testid="throw-in-outline"]` immediately dispatches `ThrowInCards` for that card (or if the dragged card is part of a multi-selection of legal throw-in cards, deploys all selected legal throw-in cards together!).
  2. **Single-card double-click:** Double-clicking a legal throw-in card (when no other throw-in cards are selected) immediately dispatches `ThrowInCards` with `[card]`.
  3. **Multi-card click-select + double-click deploy:**
     - Single-clicking legal throw-in cards toggles their membership in the current selection (`selectedThrowInCards`), enforcing `selected.length <= throwInCapacity` and allowing only cards present in `view.throwInCards`.
     - Selected cards visibly raise upward in the hand (and the tight non-rectangular hand contour from ITEM-3 dynamically wraps around them!).
     - Double-clicking any selected legal throw-in card (or double-clicking a legal throw-in card while others are selected, including it if within capacity) dispatches a single `ThrowInCards` action with ALL selected legal cards at once and clears the selection!
     - Clear stale selections whenever `view.tablePairs`, `view.boutPhase`, `view.myId`, or `view.myHand` changes.

### 6. Compact Theme-Matched Icon-Only Surrender & Pass Buttons (`ActionBar.tsx`, `GameTable.tsx`, `table.css`) (ITEM-7 & ITEM-8)
- Update `ActionBar.tsx` to import and render `SurrenderIcon` and `PassIcon` from `frontend/src/components/icons/` using the compact themed classes from `frontend/src/styles/actionIcons.css`.
- **Surrender button:**
  - Contains ONLY `<SurrenderIcon />` visually — NO visible `"Surrender"` word!
  - Accessible via `aria-label="Surrender"` and `title="Surrender"`, with `data-testid="surrender-button"`.
  - Compact size, styled to match the dark emerald/slate/gold table aesthetic (NO bright red background!).
  - Positioned

## What and why

The e2e job on main has been red since #473: `team.spec.ts` waits for the dialog to close after a failing session check, but it never closes. Since #471 the shell checks the session quietly, and a focus while a check is in flight joins that check. The spec fired the failing check before the released one had answered, so on a busy runner the second focus reused the successful answer. The app behaviour is correct; the spec now waits for the released check's response first, as `shell.spec.ts` and `orders-pipeline.spec.ts` already do.

## How to test

Locally, `pnpm test:e2e` on main failed the same test in the same place as CI (41st test, `team.spec.ts:294`); the file alone passes. With this change the full suite passes: 64 passed.

## Checklist

- [x] I read every line of this diff, including AI-written code, and removed anything this change does not need.
- [ ] `pnpm check` passes locally. Ran the full e2e suite, the web typecheck and eslint on the file.

body:
## What

Hosts can edit an RSVP, or answer for a household that never replied, from the RSVP drawer at `/admin/rsvps`. This must ship before the Dec 12 deadline: after it, guests can't change replies but hosts still can.

- **Edit reply** (or **Answer for them** on a Waiting household) opens an edit form in the same drawer at `?household=<id>&edit=1`. It works without JS; with JS the drawer swaps in place. Esc, Cancel and Back return to the read view, keeping `filter`/`q`.
- Form (Paper Admin 15 / 15b / 16): Yes/No answer, then per seat a tick, the name and the slipper size, then the note. Errors show beside their field. Choosing No collapses the seats to "Nobody is coming". After the deadline, a navy note at the top.
- Each save **appends** a response with `source: "host"` and `edited_by` set to the host's email (`AdminStore.saveRsvp`, D1 + fake). Earlier versions are never touched.
- A household that never replied gets respondent = the host's first name and an empty email, shown as "—".
- Host renames change the seat's current name only (`named_by_kind: host`). Invited names and the guest-lookup keys are untouched.
- Stale saves are refused with "This reply changed while you were editing" and a Reload link. The check uses the `households.updated_at` token, which guest replies and Guest list edits also bump.
- One rule set: `validateSubmission` became `validateSubmissionProblems` (a list of problems). The guest path calls it as before, with unchanged behaviour; the host form uses the same rules.
- Fixes the focus-trap flake `tests/admin-rsvps.spec.ts:118` (lesson L-055).

Criteria: approved by the user and saved locally as `.context/host-rsvp-edit/criteria.md` (A–H, items 1–25).

## Classification

Runtime, **Risky**: writes guest RSVP data in `src/lib/admin/**` and touches `src/lib/rsvp/logic.ts`. Gets the Codex second opinion. No schema change, no migration, no dependency or config change.

## Who built it

- **Codex `gpt-5.6-luna`, effort high** (not medium, because PR #101's r1 at medium came back BLOCKED). r1 built the logic, markup and specs. r2 added the missing e2e coverage, temporary-household specs and the live "was" note. No `sol` rounds.
- **`layout-implementer` (Sonnet 5.5, high)**, one run: CSS to Admin 15/15b/16. It also fixed `<select value>` → `<option selected>`, so prefilled and kept sizes now show.
- **Claude fixes:**
  - A host rename no longer rewrites `name_key`/`surname_key`.
  - The edit-form listener is delegated, so the form re-syncs after a drawer swap.
  - The size select is no longer server-disabled, so no-JS hosts can pick a size; sizes on unticked seats are dropped.
  - Dedicated `hh-rsvp-editor` fixture.
  - Spec races: Esc before the swap; the stale count read on the read view.
  - The JS-only Add button in the temp-household helper.
  - The slipper-chart spec now runs under `withAdminLock`.
  - The seat list keeps Paper's closing rule: an open list on the drawer ground (L-051).

## Local
