body:
## Summary

```text
POST /v1/saves/:slot/versions
  Roda/config.ru
    SessionAuthenticator
      real SessionService#current
    SaveUploadService
      PostgresSaveStore

PostgreSQL migrations
  001_sessions.sql
    -> 002_outbox_retry_state.sql
      -> 20261119_34_cloud_save_versions.sql
        -> 20261120_25_public_profiles.sql

PUT /v1/profile
  ProfileService
    public_profiles + alias reservations

server/bin/outbox_worker.rb
  outbox dispatcher with externally supplied runtime configuration
```

Integra save upload, autenticación, worker de outbox y aliases públicos de perfil. Conserva los cambios HTTPS que ya están en `main` (`a9a6657`, `8500cf1`). Relacionado con #52 y #53; esta rama combina ambos alcances y añade las correcciones y pruebas finales.

La secuencia de migraciones requerida es:

1. `001_sessions.sql`
2. `002_outbox_retry_state.sql`
3. `20261119_34_cloud_save_versions.sql`
4. `20261120_25_public_profiles.sql`

El worker requiere configuración externa (`DATABASE_URL`, credenciales de Resend, URL pública y secretos versionados de verificación) antes del despliegue.

## Evidence

- **Before:** Las pruebas de PostgreSQL no tenían cobertura completa del montaje Rack, autenticación real, worker ni aliases.
  **After:** La suite local terminó con `133 runs, 772 assertions, 0 failures, 0 errors, 18 skips`.
- CI PostgreSQL 16 para `caa4af47da0b4d3b809ad8338041d12a1be55737`: [run 44991009148](https://github.com/JuanciscoPacketTracer/dungeon-critters/actions/runs/44991009148), `success`.

## Merge Danger

**Door:** two-way

La integración conserva los cambios HTTPS actuales de `main`. Antes del despliegue deben aplicarse explícitamente las cuatro migraciones en orden y provisionarse la configuración externa del worker.

**Blast Radius:** server

Afecta autenticación, persistencia PostgreSQL de guardados, perfiles públicos, outbox y sus pruebas; no accede a partidas ni requiere secretos en el repositorio.

author: billsecond
body:
Stacked on #101.

## What it does
Picture from the Camera was at most 640 × 480, because the camera was read the way a recording reads it (the camera sits in a corner of a video, so more only makes the recording bigger). A still is a picture of its own, so now:

- The still asks the camera for its largest picture first (then about 1280 × 720, then whatever it gives fastest, if the camera won't start that way), and keeps it at that size (at most 4096 on a side), at a higher JPEG quality.
- On Windows the camera runs in its helper program as before; the helper is told `full` after the camera's number and hands the full-size pictures over its pipe (the pipe now takes records up to 32 MB).
- Recordings are unchanged: their camera is still read at about 1280 × 720 and kept at most 640 × 480.
- Also: the PR number for the guide formats (#101) in the parity list.

## How to use it
Picture from the Camera (the tray, the Capture page or its shortcut), as before: the picture is now as large as the camera makes.

## What was checked
- `cargo xtask ci` green (fmt, clippy, tests, assets, names, layers, wasm).
- Camera tests: a 1920 × 1080 picture stays 1920 × 1080 as a still and becomes 640 × 360 for a recording; one wider than 4096 is fitted to 4096; a full-size picture comes back whole through the helper's pipe as a still and is refused as a recording's; the helper's arguments with and without `full`, and junk.

## Not done
Not tried on a real camera (tests never use the owner's devices); how large a camera's largest picture is depends on the camera and its driver.

author: mathiasgruber
body:
## Summary

New players learn each system by doing it, and keep a story to follow from Genin to the Chunin Exams.

### Academy Trials (hands-on)
- **The opening plays on Horizon's sector map.** A new player walks over to Lemu and is caught in the chase the story is about: a violet flash, the pup bolting past and the masked hunter, who leaves a smoke double behind. The scene is drawn only for that player, around where they stand, on tiles no scenery covers. Reduced motion shows how it ends, and missing artwork leaves figures out without holding the lesson.
- **Characters speak on the map.** `MapSpeech` shows their lines as bubbles that follow them, stay whole on the map and keep clear of the player, targets, other bubbles and the map's panels. Lines can carry answer controls, so quests and NPCs can use it. The opening's lessons keep only their title and what to do; without a map they show the words themselves.
- **Story figures use the map's own controls.** A `StoryActor` is a figure only this player sees; its `interaction` gives it the map's attack or talk control, so the smoke double is attacked like any other character. Lessons mark figures and tiles with the shared `Spotlight`, which can leave the page lit, and `useQuestFight` starts or retries a quest's fight from any control. Migration 0193 adds an LPC half-mask design, which Lemu wears.
- **The player always makes the move.** No lesson moves the player to another page. `getTutorialWay` works out the next control from wherever they stand (Profile or Travel in the main menu, the village in the location menu, then the building), and steps that end where their control leads complete on arrival. A guided fight ends where it began. Only a running battle and the hospital open by themselves.
- **Each fight teaches one thing:** the smoke double instructs moving and basic attacks, the Academy Dummy (after training and the shop) shows Sonic Slash, the masked courier is coached from its first turn, and the exam is unaided. A lost first fight keeps the student out of the hospital and is retried at full health.
- **Experience and levels by hand, with fading pointers:** first round fully guided; second round points only at *Assign XP*; third and fourth rounds (pup mission, graduation) give no pointers and run on any page.
- **Rewards are claimed by the player.**
- **Combat:** the first two fights instruct their first turn only. After it, and throughout the courier fight, the lesson coaches instead: it states AP, distance and what is in reach, and explains a choice that cannot work (out of reach, too few AP, End Turn left selected). Phones show these facts in the action line.
- **The masked courier (240 HP)** takes several turns, all of them the player's own.
- **The Genin exam's proctor clone (300 HP) must be beaten.** A loss leads to advice and a *Retry battle* button in the lesson, and the advice stays on screen during the rematch.
- **Tutorial fights keep the field and controls clear:** the dock sits beside the battlefield, narrowed to the free space, with Lemu as an avatar in its header. The page never scrolls the AP bar out of view. Elsewhere Lemu scales to the room above the dock and steps back on practice and story cards.
- **Every lesson teaches on its own page.** Shortcut buttons and the skip offer appear only after the lesson's reading time and an idle spell. Any tap or key restarts the wait, including on the globe and inside dialogs. Neither shows over an open dialog or during a trip.
- **Travel is taught on the Global map.** Trips mark the destination with its quest "!" and name it, the action line follows the trip, and on arrival the lesson says to walk to the marker.
- **The page dims around everything the player should press.** That includes controls on the map and in the dock: the Quests tab, then the answer or claim inside it. Words spoken on the map stay readable, and a confirmation dialog stays lit around its marked button.
- **Pressing the highlight goes on.** A highlight that only shows something moves to the next step, as Next does, and a lone answer or Claim takes presses anywhere in its lit box.
- **The Quests tab says what to do there.** Unclaimed rewards come first, finished objectives fold to one line, an awaited answer stays on screen, and long claim labels wrap to fit the dock.
- **Lemu sits inside the lesson card,** mirrored and placed by her hand, which reaches just past the divider on every lesson. She is hidden where the page's own scene already shows her. An edge pill points at a highlight that is scrolled off screen.
- 49 steps; old saved steps are remapped in the migration.

### The Blacksteel Path (chapters 8–17)
- Story chapters narrated at the Academy, with Leads started there.
- Onboarding objectives: bank deposit, Guard Hall, Chakra Storm scouting, element, gear, job, cooking, feeding, tavern hello, sensei and clan requests.
- A story dock that never empties, including *Experience to spend* when unassigned XP covers a level.
- Chapter-complete cards, one-time system intro banners and a guidance setting.
- Full-page village chooser, rank-up and *Tomorrow* screens, and a Dashboard ending with the first streak claim.
- **Express Trials** for returning players: they get the trials' experience, Sonic Slash (equipped) and shuriken, and still assign the experience, level up and take the exam themselves.
- Recruitment chapter funnel, the lapsed-tutorial email, Mission Hall reward previews, and a training push prompt in the native apps.

### Dashboard and quests
- The dashboard drops the locked system rows and folds the Energy queue hint into the Training row.
- Lead quests are routed to the Academy.
- Onboarding objectives are counted only while a story quest or onboarding daily asks for them. They use one sparse quest read and never fail an action that has already been saved.
- The village chooser balances new Genin across villages using a weekly activity count cached in the Runtime Cache; player counts are not shown. A village whose weekly players exceed the quietest village's by 25% and by at least 20 is left out and named below the cards, the two quietest always stay open, and the quietest open village is tagged *Needs shinobi*. The server refuses a dialog answer into a full village, from the quest log and at an overworld NPC, and the chooser then reloads its villages. Cards and art size to the number of villages shown.

### Game fixes
- A learned jutsu, including the Express Trials one, joins the active loadout. An empty active loadout is filled from the equipped jutsu.
- A new fight starts with no action selected. End Turn and a spent Move no longer carry into the next round, and visual-only ground marks are left out of the tile tooltip.
- A marker tap that starts a fight raises no in-battle toast.
- Experience sliders move in whole points, and Simple/Advanced is a labelled control in the form.
- The village chooser opens on its first village, and the tutorial pup is adoptable only after it is handed over.
- The travel map fills the space above the dock.

### Migration `0193`
- New columns: `UserData.guidanceLevel`, `seenIntros`, `playedBefore`; `UserPet.isSanctuaryPup`.
- Remaps saved tutorial steps to the new step list, and leads students on the former arena objective to their jutsu with the experience it owed them.
- Adds the story content as idempotent statements: quests, the courier, smoke double and proctor AIs, and the dailies.

## Validation
- Correctness, UI/UX, performance and simplification review loops ran until they returned no findings, and each finding was validated before it was fixed.
- `make typecheck`, Biome, and `make test` with the SQL suites: 0 failures.
- Played on the dev server from character creation to the Dashboard ending, desktop and 375px phone:
  - guided first turns, then coached turns;
  - all four XP practice rounds;
  - manual claims;
  - a forced proctor loss, hospital, retry and win;
  - Express Trials.
- Measured Lemu's placement o

body: ## Problem Hue's export copy rewrites `url.full`, `http.url`, `http.target`, `url.path` and `url.query`, and HTTP URLs in span names, so userinfo, query strings, fragments and credential path segments never leave the process. Both SDKs ran that sanitizer only for `CLIENT` spans: - Python: `safe_http_span` returned early on `span.kind != SpanKind.CLIENT` (`packages/sdk-python/src/hue_sdk/_http_identity.py`). It runs for finished spans (`snapshots.py`, `_SpanSnapshot`) and for live placeholders (`snapshot_pending_span`). - TypeScript: `redactSpan` scrubbed URI aliases and the span name only when `span.kind === SpanKind.CLIENT` (`packages/sdk-typescript/src/privacy.ts`). An application that gives Hue its existing tracer provider also records its HTTP server spans there. Those server spans, and internal, producer and consumer spans carrying the same attributes, were uploaded with the original request URL, including query secrets such as OAuth callback codes. ## Changes - **Both SDKs:** the URL sanitizer now runs for every span kind. Non-client spans get exactly what client spans already got: URL aliases filtered, `url.query` removed, a URL that cannot be sanitized omitted rather than sent, and URLs in names scrubbed. Python also names the copy by its HTTP method, or `HTTP` when the name holds a URL. Python live placeholders go through the same function. TypeScript placeholders are exported through `redactSpan`. - **Exception for Hue's own tool endpoint evidence:** a `tool()` span carrying `hue.tool.endpoint.source` with `url.full` as its only URI attribute is left as recorded. `toolEndpointAttributes` / `tool_endpoint_attributes` already reduced that URL to the allowlisted query parameters and passed it through the redactor, and the existing `tool-endpoint` tests require those parameters to survive. If such a span also carries another URI alias, it gets the full sanitizer. - **TypeScript only:** the scrub no longer requires an HTTP method or an `http(s):` `url.full` before it acts, and it drops non-string URI values (Python already rejected them). Before this, a server span with only `url.path` + `url.query`, or a list-valued `url.full`, could skip the scrub. - READMEs and `CHANGELOG.md` (both packages, **Wire**, Fixed) describe the new coverage. Reviewers should look first at the tool endpoint exception in `_http_identity.py` and `privacy.ts`. ### Related paths checked - `_records.http_truncated_attributes` (Python) and `httpSpanIdentity` (TypeScript `http-capture.ts`) also check for `CLIENT`. Neither sanitizes URLs: the first handles body-cut markers, and the second matches Hue's outgoing-request capture to client spans. Non-client spans skip both and now reach the generic sanitizer. - Log records have no span kind and never went through `safe_http_span` / the span URI scrub. Only URL-valued `resource.name` is filtered on logs. Log attributes such as `url.full` on a log record are outside this change and are still open. ## Verification Tests that prove the fix: https://github.com/hue-run/hue-sdk/pull/456 (`packages/sdk-python/tests/test_non_client_http_identity.py`, `packages/sdk-typescript/tests/non-client-http-identity.test.ts`). They are not part of this PR. **verify-sdk** (narrowest checks, loopback receivers only): Tests from #456 against unchanged `main`, showing the bug: ``` $ uv run --frozen --all-groups pytest tests/test_non_client_http_identity.py FAILED ...test_borrowed_provider_strips_non_client_url_credentials[True|False-SpanKind.SERVER|INTERNAL|PRODUCER|CONSUMER] (8) FAILED ...test_server_spans_lose_each_url_alias_instrumentation_sets[attributes_in0|1|2] (3) FAILED ...test_unsanitizable_server_url_is_omitted FAILED ...test_server_span_name_does_not_keep_the_request_url FAILED ...test_open_server_span_placeholder_strips_the_request_url E - https://example.test/token/[redacted]/callback E + $ bun test tests/non-client-http-identity.test.ts 0 pass 11 fail ``` Tests from #456 with this fix, run on this branch with the #456 test files copied in temporarily: ``` $ uv run --frozen --all-groups pytest tests/test_non_client_http_identity.py tests/test_tool_endpoint.py tests/test_http_identity.py 94 passed in 18.79s $ bun test tests/non-client-http-identity.test.ts tests/tool-endpoint.test.ts 22 pass 0 fail Ran 22 tests across 2 files. ``` Existing tests on this branch, without the #456 files: ``` $ uv run --frozen --all-groups pytest tests/test_http_identity.py tests/test_tool_endpoint.py tests/test_http_capture.py \ tests/test_http_markers.py tests/test_isolation.py tests/test_live_spans.py tests/test_sdk.py \ --deselect tests/test_live_spans.py::test_placeholder_copies_attributes_consistently_while_the_span_changes 479 passed, 1 deselected $ bun test tests # whole TypeScript suite 2646 pass 12 fail Ran 2659 tests across 69 files. ``` The 12 TypeScript failures are not caused by this change. Nine come from `setup.test.ts` / `setup-application-security.test.ts` (application matrix, real setup HTTP adapter, runtime installer) and fail identically on unchanged `main` in this sandbox. Two are timing flakes in `artifact-settle` / `cli-world` eval verification that also fail on unchanged `main`. `hue world run > stops what the command left running` failed once and passed 3/3 when rerun. Full Python suite (with the stress test below deselected): 1,931 passed, 1 failed. The failure is `test_wheel.py::test_installed_wheel_runs_standalone_stream_tool_error`, whose nested pytest copies `test_live_spans.py` and was killed by the sandbox's memory limit. The deselected `test_placeholder_copies_attributes_consistently_while_the_span_changes` grows past 6 GB at the same rate on unchanged `main` and with this change, so it was not run here; CI covers it. Variants of the same technique, run against the sanitizers directly on server, internal, producer and consumer spans with content capture on and off: `url.full` without a method, `http.target` with a query and no method, a lone `url.query`, a relative `http.url`, an `ftp:` `url.full`, a list-valued `url.full`, a URL only in the span name, and a spoofed `hue.tool.endpoint.source` next to `http.url` or `url.query`. author: smile-minecraft
body:
## Problem
After a Sparkle update or a manual DMG replacement, the privileged Helper can lose its launchd/BTM registration, keep a stale cdhash constraint, or answer an old XPC protocol. The app only looked at `SMAppService.status` and swallowed a synchronous refresh, so it showed a green "Helper running" dot for a Helper that did not work. There was no explanation or recovery action for the user.

## What changed
- **Sparkle handoff** (`UpdaterController`): snapshots Helper enabled/healthy state, app version and cdhash before the bundle is replaced, drops the XPC connection, and clears the snapshot when an update fails or is cancelled.
- **Manual DMG detection** (`HelperClient`): persists the last app/helper pair for which a handshake actually succeeded and synthesises an update handoff when either changes, so drag-and-drop updates are covered too. `needsReregistration` now covers signed as well as ad-hoc builds.
- **Verified liveness** (`HelperHealthMonitor`): probes over XPC on launch, every 60 seconds and immediately on `NSApplication.didBecomeActiveNotification`. Safe failures get one handshake retry and up to two soft repairs before a prompt; lost registrations and stale binaries get a verified reinstall. Failures are logged with a structured `os.Logger`.
- **Clear alerts**: a one-click `HelperRecoveryBanner` at the top of the detail view with `Repair Helper` / `Open Login Items` / `Dismiss`. The sidebar footer, setup sheet and Helper diagnostics now show the verified health state instead of raw registration status. A single deduplicated local notification alerts menu-bar-only users.
- **Pure, testable core** (`Sources/Storage/HelperUpdateHandoff.swift`): state enum, handoff persistence with expiry/consumption, and the recovery decision engine. Placed in `Storage` because no existing SwiftPM test target depends on `HelperProtocol` — `Package.swift` and `project.yml` are untouched.

## Verification
- `make test`: 172 tests in 33 suites passed, including 21 new `HelperUpdateHandoffTests` covering persistence, expiry, cancellation, every planner transition, manual DMG detection, and healthy recovery.
- `make build`: Debug Xcode build succeeded. No new warnings introduced.

## Risks
Recovery is automatic but bounded and non-destructive first; a full reinstall is only used when an in-place refresh cannot spawn the new binary, and it may require the user to re-approve in Login Items. Notifications are only posted when permission was already granted, never requested.

author: fardcrex
body:
Fase 2 del QR "como Yape". **Apila sobre #142**: fusionar #142 primero; al hacerlo, GitHub cambia la base de este PR a `main`.

Con monto libre, el tope por operación (S/ 2,000) no frena a quien tiene el teléfono y el PIN de otra persona, porque le basta con pagar varias veces. El límite diario acota ese daño a un día.

## Regla
- **Monto:** S/ 5,000 o US$ 1,500 al día por titular (`LIMITE_DIARIO_QR` en `app/services/limite_diario.py`).
- **Monedas:** no se suman entre sí.
- **Qué cuenta:** el QR estático y el cobro dinámico, de **todas** las cuentas del titular. Si el tope fuera por cuenta, abrir 5 cuentas lo multiplicaría por 5.
- **El día:** calendario de Lima (UTC-5).
- **Al superarlo:** 400 `QR_DAILY_LIMIT` con `disponible_centimos`, `limite_centimos` y `moneda`.
- **`/validar`** devuelve `disponible_hoy_centimos` para que la app avise antes de pedir el PIN.
- **Envíos y recargas no cuentan** (fuera de alcance de este PR).

## Concurrencia e idempotencia
- **Tabla nueva `qr_consumo_diario` (migración `0004`):** PK `(user_id, moneda, fecha)`. La fila se crea con `INSERT … ON CONFLICT DO NOTHING` y se bloquea con `FOR UPDATE` antes del PIN y del libro mayor. Así, dos pagos simultáneos no pasan juntos del tope.
- **Orden de bloqueos:** una petición toma una sola fila de consumo y la toma antes que las cuentas, así que no se forma un ciclo de bloqueos.
- **Reintentos:** el consumo se suma solo si el libro mayor registró un pago nuevo. Un reintento no suma y no se rechaza por límite, porque ese pago ya ocurrió. La clave se vuelve a consultar con la fila ya bloqueada.
- **Lo que no gasta cupo:** un PIN incorrecto o un cobro que ya pagó otra persona.

## App
`QrFailure.dailyLimit(Money disponible)` muestra "Hoy aún puedes pagar S/ X" o, si ya no queda cupo, "Podrás pagar de nuevo mañana".

## Pruebas
- Backend: 572 passed (antes 564). Incluye `test_qr_limite_diario.py`: tope, estático y dinámico juntos, reintento, `/validar`, PIN incorrecto, cobro ya pagado, cambio de día y día de Lima frente a UTC.
- **No corrió en local:** `test_limite_09` (cuatro pagos simultáneos contra Postgres). Corre en el job *Backend (PostgreSQL 18)*.
- App: 1009 tests y `flutter analyze` sin issues.
- Contrato app ↔ API en local con la migración `0004`: 16/16.

## Al desplegar
- Hay que aplicar la migración `0004`.
- La tabla arranca vacía: el día del despliegue, lo pagado antes no cuenta.

## Docs
`CLAUDE.md`, `despliegue.md`, `modelo-datos.md`, `diccionario-datos.md` y `catalogo-controles.md`. Se agregan DT-14 (PIN siempre en QR) y DT-15 (límite diario); el total pasa a 51 controles, también en `apf2-cumplimiento.md`.

## What
The A2A rail's checkout leg locks the order to Pivota's own reference and an approval ceiling. The ceiling is price × qty, plus a 15% tax allowance rounded up, plus $10 shipping, capped at $200 and at the rail limit. All three are env-tunable. The confirm card is scanned against that ceiling.
- The scan accepts only amounts it can read with certainty. Anything it cannot read, or that adds up past the ceiling, is refused before the confirm.

## What changes

On a view a read-only package ships, a pin, a rename or a set-default writes the whole view into the package's customization pair (`PACKAGE.custom`, ruling record 7058654416 keeps those three). Manage views now:

- marks such a row "customized" (served with the ADR-0146 D2 declaration `overrides` naming the package it is served under);
- offers "Restore factory version" in that row's menu; one confirm says every user of the view sees the factory version again; on confirm the override is removed and the views are read again, showing the package's own view;
- offers no restore, and no mark, on a view without a customization; Delete stays hidden and rename, pin, set default and "View config" stay as the ruling has them.

Pieces:

- `@object-ui/data-objectstack`: `ObjectStackAdapter.restoreFactoryView(objectName, viewName)` reads the served view, refuses (sending nothing) when it is no override of its package, takes the pair from the ensure door for that package (the same home `updateView` writes into), and deletes the view's draft then its row there: the existing door `DELETE /meta/view/NAME?package=PAIR`, the one Studio's "Restore package original" uses. A pair that held no row throws. `listViews()` now carries a record's `overrides` onto the flattened row.
- `@object-ui/plugin-view`: `ViewTabItem.customized`, `ManageViewsDialogProps.onRestoreFactory`, the mark and the menu entry.
- `@object-ui/app-shell`: the `customized` verdict in the title switcher's Manage views items, and `handleRestoreFactoryView` (confirm, restore, re-read, toast; a refusal is said with the door's message).
- `@object-ui/i18n`: 8 keys in every locale pack (zh-Hant regenerated by `gen:zh-hant`); the de quote-pairing pin counts the two new pairs.

No server, protocol or `packages/spec` change.

## Server door, measured (scratch test, not committed)

Real engine, SQL store, protocol, `HttpDispatcher` reads and `RestServer` delete, both topologies, at 446de0ec / f35f7f31:

- After a pin (`PUT /meta/view/NAME?package=APP.custom` with the declaration): `GET /meta/view?object=OBJ` serves the row with `_packageId` = the base and `overrides: { package: BASE, basedOn }`, in the canonical `config` shape (hence the `listViews` change).
- `DELETE ?package=APP.custom&state=draft` 200 `reset:false`; `DELETE ?package=APP.custom` 200 `reset:true`; the list then serves the base's view with no `overrides`.
- Without `manage_metadata`: 403 `FORBIDDEN` ("Resetting a metadata item requires the `manage_metadata` capability"), the same gate as the pin's write; Manage views is the admin's, as for pin.
- After the last override is removed the pair stays: the ensure door answers it again with `created: false`, so it keeps blocking uninstall (ADR-0146 D3). This PR adds no package deletion.

## Tests

New files: `ManageViewsDialog.restoreFactory-36011.test.tsx` (plugin-view), `restoreFactoryView-36011.test.ts` (data-objectstack), `ObjectView.restoreFactoryView-36011.test.tsx` (app-shell: pin then restore under the real English I18nProvider, the confirm text, a cancelled confirm, a refused restore).

</details>

author: maligzar
body:
From the owner's log at the scope, 2026-11-22 at 22:53. After ★ ALIGN, the lock calibrated, centred Saturn from 480 px off on the full frame, overshot to 146 px and was abandoned ("corrections were making it worse").

## Cause: integral windup
During the approach, both corrections sat at the never-reverse limit (az `17.47-16.47`, alt `-7.32+6.32`). Meanwhile the integral summed the large error to its 15 "/s clamp. At 2.4" from centre the corrections were still near full: az −14.21; alt `0.5 × −2.6 + 15` clipped to +6.32. The integral then unwound at about 1 "/s per cycle, so the planet ran past the centre.

## Fix
`core/GuideLaw.h` holds one step of the control law, moved out of `CentroidTracker.cpp` unchanged apart from conditional integration: an axis whose output is pinned at a limit by the error's own sign does not integrate. Near centre, unpinned, the integral works as before, absorbing a stale tracking rate (+9 "/s at 19:47 the same night).

## Tests
`guide_windup` feeds the night's numbers through a model of the mount:
- **The night's start, old law:** overshoots about 24" (about 120 px). The real 146 px also had camera delay, which the model leaves out.
- **The same start, new law:** overshoots 3.7" and settles in 22 s.
- **A short approach:** settles under both laws.
- **A 9 "/s stale rate:** still absorbed.

The min/max macro check passes. `CentroidTracker.cpp` compiles only on Windows; this PR's CI builds it and runs `rate_guide` on the emulator.

**Owes:** a long centring on the sky that settles.

## Docs
- Phase 172 plan, finding 12;
- PHASE-STATUS 172;
- a Help history row;
- version 3.3.47.

Merges only on the owner's word.

body:
The first real trace app run in Router's enclave failed inside the sandbox ("The app stopped the sandbox; it may have run out of memory"). A temporary CI run of the exact pinned sandbox image, under the production container settings and with each setting removed in turn, ran the app correctly every time, so the settings are not the cause. The part CI never saw fail is the worker thread the sandbox started per app.

- The sandbox now runs the app on its own thread. It is a single-use container with no network or keys; an app the engine's limits miss is stopped by the runner's deadline, after which the host removes the container.
- If the engine fails, the sealed error, which only the owner reads, adds the container's and the machine's memory, so a memory shortage can be told from anything else.
- Only the embedded sandbox script changes; the pinned Router image stays. The sandbox's code hash, and so the runners' code hash, change: owners' tools need this checkout to verify runs.
- New CI check (`subhost/dev/sandbox-check.mjs`, in the sub-container host end-to-end job): runs an ordinary app, an endless loop and a network probe in the pinned sandbox image with the host's own create-container body and the embedded script, on the real Docker daemon.

After deploying: rerun the kept throwaway request with the owner tool.

## What Changed

- Added `ServiceRadarCoreElx.CameraRecording.ArchiveBlockJob` on the `:nvr_archive` Oban queue (unique per `catalog_entry_id` across `[:available, :scheduled, :retryable]`) to check catalog eligibility, archive settings/policy (`:not_required` when disabled or `:local_only`), and upload holds, delegate upload and readback to `NVRArchive.archive_block/5`, and atomically record `NVRArchiveReceipt` and transition `RecordingCatalogEntry` to `:verified` in a single `Repo.transaction/1` with `FOR UPDATE` locking.
- Implemented archive job outcome and error handling: snoozing `archive_busy` and held states without consuming attempts, retrying transient errors with jittered exponential backoff (30 s to 30 min), refusing an identical retained receipt on Transition 8 re-archive by returning the entry to `:missing`, and marking 422, 409 `archive_receipt_conflict`, and Core `NVRArchiveReceipt` conflict rollbacks (`%Ash.Error.Changes.InvalidArgument{}` and wrapped error containers) as `:failed_terminal` with job discard.
- Added `NVRTargetConfig.resolve_by_storage_id/2`, configured the `:nvr_archive` Oban queue in `elixir/serviceradar_core_elx/config/runtime.exs` (`OBAN_QUEUE_NVR_ARCHIVE`, default `2`), wired best-effort `ArchiveBlockJob.enqueue_for_entry/1` into `NVRWorker` after registering `:pending` entries, and added unit/integration tests alongside NVR doc and OpenSpec task updates.

✅ Low: The CI fix moves receipt-conflict detection to the commit-result boundary in persist_verified/4. There it matches the exact errors the real code produces: a bare InvalidArgument (field :receipt_bytes, "conflicts with retained record") from verify_idempotent_or_refuse/2, and the same error wrapped in an Ash error class or changeset. Other errors still take the retryable path. The earlier review decisions (narrow terminal classes, indefinite snooze backoff, policy-read error retryable, queue only on core-elx) are all present in the current code, so the change is well-bounded.

author: brun-after
body:
## Por quê

Na troca de região, a tela parava por segundos. O perfil de CPU de uma troca (Chromium com GPU Intel UHD, Direct3D 11) mostrou que a maior parte do tempo ia para **compilar shaders WebGL**. Cada cena criava um `Application` do Pixi e um `PalcoVivo` do three.js novos, cada um com seu contexto WebGL, e a primeira imagem de cada um recompilava tudo. Depois vinham o envio de texturas e a pintura do chão no fio da página: ~36 ms por bloco, um bloco por quadro.

## O que muda

- **Pixi guardado** (`render/stage.ts`): a cena que sai devolve o `Application` (palco vazio, canvas fora da página), e a próxima o reaproveita. Ficam no máximo dois, porque na troca a cena velha e a nova coexistem. O que uma cena esquecer de soltar sai da placa pelo `GCSystem` do Pixi 8 (1 min sem uso).
- **Palco 3D compartilhado** (`render/vivos/palco-compartilhado.ts`): o `PalcoVivo` passa de cena em cena. Se o mesmo id aparece com outro modelo, o ator é trocado; quem não é pedido sai em 30 quadros.
- **three.js sem `checkShaderErrors`** fora do desenvolvimento.
- **Chão no Web Worker** (`render/solo/assar-trabalhador.ts`, `assador-remoto.ts`): o `AssadorDeSolo` pinta num `OffscreenCanvas` e devolve um `ImageBitmap`. Sem Worker ou OffscreenCanvas, a página pinta como antes. A guarda de assados fecha o bitmap com `close()`.
- **Medida:** `?bench=mundo&regiao=<id>&troca=<id>[,<id>...]` encadeia trocas e grava as medidas em `window.__trocas`.

## Medidas (build de produção, rota de 5 trocas, 2 rodadas)

| Troca | Antes | Depois |
|---|---|---|
| Média por troca | ~13,9 s | ~7,7 s |
| Vila do Centro | 6,1 a 6,9 s | 2,8 a 3,3 s |
| Encosta do Leste | 12,8 a 14,2 s | 4,7 a 5,1 s |
| Quadros depois do 1º (JS) | 100 a 250 ms, picos de ~2,2 s | 35 a 80 ms |

Na medida, as duas cenas desenham ao mesmo tempo, então os tempos absolutos ficam maiores que no jogo. O chão pintado no trabalhador saiu idêntico ao de antes: fotografei a mesma cena nos dois builds.

## O que falta

- As **Ruínas do Norte** quase não melhoraram: o primeiro quadro delas ainda leva ~4 s de JS. Fica para investigar a seguir.
- A primeira troca depois de entrar no Mundo ainda cria um `Application`, porque a guarda começa vazia.
- Não foi medido num celular nem numa troca real com servidor.

## Testes

- Typecheck e lint dos arquivos alterados passaram. O teste novo em `assados-guardados.test.ts` confere que o `ImageBitmap` é fechado com `close()`.
- `npm test`: 2150 testes passaram e 3 estouraram o tempo de 60 s com a máquina carregada (loopback, determinismo, passagens). Rodando sozinhos, os três passam. O build passou.

author: thkt
body:
Closes #235

## Changes and rationale

壊し方の記録ファイル（`.feedback-loop-mutants.json`）だけの変更では、依存記録の状態によらず、テストを実行しないようにした。`selectQuality`（`src/selection.ts`）は、次の 2 つが成り立つときに、`source.reach` の照会と `fullRunReason` を使う前に、記録ファイルだけの変更として返す。

- 変更が記録ファイル 1 件だけで、そのファイルが宣言として扱われる
- Vitest では、`--repo` の外の変更も無い

宣言として扱うのは、記録ファイルが `dependencies`・quality のテスト・`globalChanges`・lockfile のどれにも当たらないときだけである。そのため、`dependencies` に記録ファイルを書いた repo では、今と同じく対応するテストを選ぶ。Bun は、記録ファイルだけの変更として返ると依存記録を保存しないので、依存記録を捨てない。Vitest は、外の変更から import でテストに届くので、外の変更があるときは今の選び方のままにした。Bun は外の変更を選択に使わないので、外の変更があってもテストを実行しない（f7d005f）。

改善の手順（`references/improve-tests.md`）と契約（`references/contract.md`）の文を、実際の動きに合わせた。

- npm と pnpm の呼び方に `-s` を付けた。付けないと、npm 11 と pnpm 10 は script の見出しを標準出力に書き、JSON として読めない
- `--key` の鍵を単一引用符で囲み、鍵の `'` を `'\''` に置き換えると書いた。pnpm 10.2.0 より前の版は、引数を二重引用符で包み直すので、鍵の `$` と `` ` `` を展開する。その版では、その鍵の壊し方を埋めていない壊し方として控えると書いた（f7d005f）
- 手順の始める前の確認に、`mutation` script があることを足した。`-s` を付けた呼び方は、script が無くても診断を表示しない（f7d005f）
- `--check-changes` の比べる先を、`.feedback-loop.json` の `base` か既定の比較元と書いた
- package manager の決め方に、`apply` と同じ祖先の lockfile の規則を足した
- `apply` を再実行する文では、`--feedback-command` だけを今の `check:feedback` の値にし、ほかは導入時と同じ引数を渡すと書いた
- 契約の 89 行目と選択の表に、`ignoredChanges` だけの変更と assurance のテストファイルだけの変更でも、依存記録の無い quality を実行することを書いた。Bun で依存記録を使えないときは、全 quality を実行する。記録ファイルの行には、記録ファイルに import や依存記録で届く quality も選ばないことと、走らせたいときは `dependencies` に書くことを書いた

## Requirements coverage

Issue の受け入れ条件 10 個に合う。

1. npm の呼び方は、手順の表と契約の例の両方で `npm run -s mutation -- <引数>` である。契約は、`-s` で見出しが標準出力に出ないことを書く
2. `--key` の鍵は単一引用符で囲み、`'` を `'\''` に置き換える
3. pnpm の呼び方は `pnpm -s mutation <引数>` である。pnpm 10.2.0 より前の版が鍵の `$` と `` ` `` を展開することを、手順と契約に書いた。その版での扱いを手順に書いた
4. 手順の始める前の確認に、`mutation` script があることを足した
5. `--check-changes` の比べる先は、`base` か既定の比較元である（`src/changes.ts` の `comparisonBase` と合う）
6. package manager の決め方は、`src/inspect.ts` の `hintSource` と `src/lockfiles.ts` の `ancestorLockfiles` と合う
7. `apply` の再実行の文は、`--feedback-command` に今の `check:feedback` の値を渡す。ほかの引数は導入時のまま渡す
8. 記録ファイルだけの変更では、依存記録の状態によらず、Bun と Vitest のどちらでもテストを実行しない。Vitest では外の変更が無いときに限る。Bun では依存記録を捨てない
9. `dependencies` に記録ファイルを書いた repo では、対応するテストを選ぶ。形の崩れた記録ファイルの非ゼロ終了は変わらない
10. 契約の 89 行目と選択の表は、`ignoredChanges` だけの変更と assurance のテストファイルだけの変更の今の動きと合う。Vitest の行と Bun の 2 行は、記録ファイルだけの変更を除く

版は上げていない。Issue の方針の表が、版を上げない変更と決めている。

## Verification and unverified items

Target commit: f7d005f0784a0ba6481aef093ddde1eb380ea0a8

Workflow: 8341a65 で、host の `bun run check` が通り、独立したレビューが 2 回目で accepted だった。f7d005f では、`bun run check:feedback` と `bun run check` がローカルで通った（565 件、失敗 0）。

足したテストと直したテストは次のとおりで、どれも quality である。

- `tests/recovery.test.ts`：Bun で依存記録が無いまま記録ファイルだけを変えると、テストを実行せず、依存記録も作らずに終了 0 で終わる。直す前の `src/selection.ts` で落ちることを確かめた
- `tests/recovery.test.ts`：`dependencies` に記録ファイルを書いた repo では、対応する quality だけを実行する。直す前の実装でも通り、宣言の判定を見ずに早く返す実装を防ぐ
- `tests/vitest-selection.test.ts`：Vitest で依存記録の無い quality があっても、記録ファイルだけの変更ならテストを実行しない。直す前の `src/selection.ts` で落ちることを確かめた
- `tests/subdirectory.test.ts`：Git のルートより下の Bun の package で、外の変更と記録ファイルだけの中の変更があり、依存記録が無くても、テストを実行しない。直す前の `src/selection.ts` と 8341a65 の両方で落ちることを確かめた（f7d005f）
- `tests/standalone.test.ts`：改善の手順の `--key` の鍵が、単一引用符で囲まれていることを確かめる。正本の鍵の引用符を外すと落ちることを確かめた。テストの名前にこの条件を足した（f7d005f）

文書の文のうち、次の外部の動きは、19007bd で実行して確かめた。

- npm 11.20.0 は、`-s` が無いと見出しを標準出力に書く
- pnpm 10.0.0 と 10.34.9 は、`-s` が無いと見出しを標準出力に書く。pnpm 12.21.0 は書かない。どの版も、`-s` を付けると書かない
- pnpm 8.15.0・9.0.0・9.15.0・10.0.0・10.1.0 は、鍵の `$` と `` ` `` を展開する。10.2.0 以降の 10 系と 12.21.0、npm 11.20.0 の `-s`、`bun run` は、単一引用符で囲んだ鍵をそのまま渡す

確かめていないことは次のとおりである。

- 書き直した文書の文が、実際の動きと合うこと。`check` はこの文を読まない。Issue のとおり、thkt が PR のレビューで確かめる
- zsh と bash で、引用符なしの鍵が止まるか切れること。見直しのレビューが 19007bd で確かめ、この PR では実行していない
- 記録ファイルを import する quality を、記録ファイルだけの変更で選ばないこと。テストは無い。契約の前提（記録ファイルを読むのは `mutation` だけとみなす）に沿った動きである

## Findings and responses

- 独立したレビュー（defect、直した）：契約の記録ファイルの行が、記録ファイルを `ignoredChanges` と同じに扱うと書いていた。記録ファイルに届く quality を選ばない動きと食い違うので、8341a65 で、選ばないことと `dependencies` に書く方法を書いた
- 独立したレビュー（concern、直した）：`apply` を再実行する文が、`--repo` と `--check-command` の渡し方を書いていなかった。8341a65 で、`--feedback-command` だけを今の値にし、ほかは導入時と同じ引数を渡すと書いた
- 独立したレビュー（concern）と `/code-review`（important）：Bun は外の変更を選択に使わないのに、外の変更があると記録ファイルだけの変更として扱わず、依存記録が無ければ全 quality を実行した。f7d005f で、外の変更を見るのを Vitest だけにした
- `/code-review`（important）：pnpm 10.2.0 より前の版は、単一引用符で囲んでも鍵の `$` と `` ` `` を展開する。f7d005f で、手順と契約にこの版の扱いを書いた。Issue にも受け入れ条件として足した
- `/code-review`（pre_existing）：pnpm 10 は、`-s` が無いと見出しを標準出力に書く。f7d005f で、pnpm の呼び方を `pnpm -s mutation <引数>` にした

author: evensol
body:
Adds `neqsim-meg-loop` (flow-assurance), stacked on #85.

**What it does**, for one gas or gas-condensate well stream with condensed and formation water:
- Lean MEG injection rate: bisection on the NeqSim SRK-CPA hydrate temperature of the whole inhibited stream at the design pressure, so it sits at the coldest temperature minus the margin.
- Rich MEG at arrival and MEG lost to gas and condensate, from a multiphase flash. Includes a Hammerschmidt cross-check.
- Regeneration: water boiled off, reboiler temperature (CPA bubble point of lean MEG) and duty (NeqSim enthalpy balance).
- Salt balance: salt in, steady-state salt for a reclaimer slipstream, the minimum slipstream and the days to reach the limit without reclaiming.
- Lean-concentration alternatives and findings.

**Example** (8 MSm3/d, 20 m3/d of 60 g/L formation water, 150 bara and 4 C with a 3 C margin):
- 2774 kg/h of 90 wt % lean MEG.
- Rich MEG 49.2 wt %, against 50.4 wt % from Hammerschmidt.
- Reboiler at 143.7 C, 1705 kW.
- The reclaimer needs at least a 36 % slipstream; 30 % was given, so the result is a high finding.

**Tests:** 27 pass (logic without Java plus NeqSim integration). Hooks and manifest validation pass.

The skill is still an orphan until the agents PR wires it in (to follow on equinor/neqsim-community-agents).

author: dhimno
body:
## Deskripsi PR

Implementasi tugas D-06 (Registrasi Perangkat + Notifikasi Masuk) untuk Tahap 6 (Notifikasi).

### Cakupan Implementasi

1. **Service Notifikasi (`src/services/notifications.ts`)**:
   - `getNotifPermission` & `requestNotifPermission`: Pengecekan dan permintaan izin notifikasi dengan penjelasan singkat (`Alert.alert`) sebelum memicu dialog sistem jika status `undetermined` (FR-50, SRS 4.3).
   - `getDeviceToken`: Mengambil Expo Push Token untuk perangkat dengan project ID EAS, serta membuat Android notification channel (`default`) dengan prioritas `MAX`.
   - `hashToken`: Fungsi hash deterministik 16-karakter heksadesimal untuk menghasilkan `deviceId` unik dari token, sehingga token yang sama tidak menduplikasi dokumen di Firestore.
   - `saveDeviceToken`: Menyimpan `{ token, platform, updatedAt }` di `users/{uid}/devices/{deviceId}`.
   - `removeDeviceToken`: Menghapus dokumen token di `users/{uid}/devices/{deviceId}` saat logout (FR-50) atau saat token ditolak (FR-54).
   - `extractNotifPayload`: Parsing payload aman dari data notifikasi FCM/Expo push.
   - `getNotifTargetRoute`: Menentukan rute target sesuai peran dan jenis notifikasi (N1 → `/praktikan/presensi`, N2/N4 → detail sesi, N3 → detail izin).
   - `addNotificationListeners`: Mendaftarkan listener foreground banner dan respons tap notifikasi, serta menangani cold-start tap via `getLastNotificationResponseAsync`.

2. **Store (`src/store/appStore.ts`)**:
   - `notifPermission`: Status izin notifikasi terkelola di store dengan selector `useNotifPermission()`.
   - `registerDevice`: Dipanggil otomatis setelah login, register, dan saat sesi tersimpan dipulihkan (`initAuth`).
   - `logout`: Menghapus token perangkat (`removeDeviceToken`) sebelum `authLogout` dijalankan agar otentikasi Firestore masih valid saat menghapus dokumen.
   - Mengeskpor hook `useNotificationHandler` dan helper terkait agar `_layout.tsx` tidak mengimpor `services/` secara langsung (menjaga arsitektur layer).

3. **Root Layout (`src/app/_layout.tsx`)**:
   - Mengatur penanganan foreground notification banner via `setNotificationHandler` (tetap tampil saat aplikasi dibuka).
   - Mengatur listener interaksi tap notifikasi.
   - Menangani pembukaan layar tunda jika pengguna mengetuk notifikasi sebelum login (`pendingNotifPayloadRef`), sehingga setelah login langsung diarahkan ke layar tujuan yang sesuai.

4. **Firestore Security Rules (`firestore.rules`)**:
   - Menambahkan rules untuk subkoleksi `users/{id}/devices/{deviceId}`:
     - Baca: Pemilik (`uid() == id`) dan Asisten (`isAsisten()`).
     - Create & Update: Hanya pemilik (`uid() == id`) dengan validasi `hasOnly` + `hasAll` `['token', 'platform', 'updatedAt']`, `token is string && token.size() > 0`, `platform is string && platform.size() > 0`, dan `updatedAt is timestamp`.
     - Delete: Pemilik (`uid() == id`) dan Asisten (`isAsisten()`).

5. **Kontrak & Integritas**:
   - Tanda tangan kontrak D-02 tidak berubah.
   - File `types/` dan lockfile tidak diubah.

### Verifikasi

- `npm run typecheck`: 0 error
- `npm run lint`: 0 error (12 warning bawaan, tidak ada penambahan warning)
- Logika hash, ekstraksi payload notifikasi, dan penentuan rute target telah diverifikasi.

body:
## Summary

Handles the remaining items from the flow/link audit. Five commits, no production data changes.

| # | Item | Commit |
|---|---|---|
| 1 | CI never ran the tests; dead Firebase/auth/style files | `chore(ci)` |
| 2 | Six divergent money formatters; copy-pasted order workflow | `refactor` |
| 3 | Three Supabase 404s and ~850 ms block on every page load | `perf(catalog)` |
| 4 | Six help pages published bracketed placeholder copy | `fix(help)` |
| 5 | Duplicate migration version; missing rate-limit baseline | `fix(db)` |

## 1. CI and dead files

`.github/workflows/phase1-ci.yml`

- Added `npm test` before `npm run build`.
- Switched `npm install` → `npm ci` (lockfile is committed).
- Added `main` to the push trigger, so the suite also guards the deployed branch.
- Dropped the `functions-install` job, since `functions/` is deleted.

Removed verified-dead files (zero references):

```
functions/                 Firebase stub, never provisioned
src/auth/OwnerAuth.jsx     unused second auth implementation
src/demo-products.js
src/lib/useSupport.js
src/standard.css           288 lines, never imported
```

Also removed the unused `OwnerAuthProvider` / `useOwnerAuth` / `OwnerRoute` / `OwnerSignIn` re-export aliases from `StaffAuth.jsx`, and un-ignored `.env.example` (it was caught by `.env.*`).

## 2. One money formatter, one order workflow

New `src/lib/money.js`:

| Helper | Missing value | Kobo |
|---|---|---|
| `formatNaira` | `Price on request` | no |
| `formatNairaDash` | `—` | no |
| `formatKobo` | `₦0` | divides by 100 |
| `formatKoboDash` | `—` | divides by 100 |

The null behaviour is now explicit per audience instead of accidental. `store.jsx` keeps exporting `naira` for existing call sites, and `checkout.js` re-exports the shared `formatKobo` so its tests and imports are unchanged.

New `src/lib/orders.js` owns `ORDER_TRANSITIONS` and `orderStatusOptions`; `Admin.jsx` and `admin/OrdersManager.jsx` both import them. This removes the byte-identical copy that could silently diverge.

While consolidating, fixed `PaymentsManager` helping history: it used `p.amount_kobo || p.amount` and always divided by 100, so a naira fallback was shown 100× too small.

## 3. Catalogue load no longer blocks on missing tables

`useCatalog` used `Promise.all` over `products` plus three metadata tables that do not exist in production. Every visit waited ~850 ms and logged three 404s before products painted.

- Products load and render first.
- Metadata enrichment runs afterwards.
- The migration is detected from `products.category_id` / `products.product_type_id` (shipped in the same migration), so a populated catalogue skips the metadata queries entirely when they cannot exist.
- A failed probe is remembered for six hours, then retried, so the app self-heals after the migration is applied.

## 4. Help pages no longer publish placeholder text

`src/data.js` now holds `helpContent`. Pages with `null` copy render “This page is being finalised and is not published yet”, with an Instagram route. The contact page uses the real Instagram channel.

An unknown `/help/<topic>` now shows a not-found page with valid topics instead of silently rendering the first policy at the wrong URL.

## 5. Migration ledger

- Renamed `20261113140000_admin_confirm_bank_transfer_service_role.sql` → `...140001...`, resolving the duplicate version.
- Added `supabase/baseline/20261115060245_raw_hairs_admin_rate_limit_repair.reconstructed.sql`, a clearly labelled reconstruction kept out of `supabase/migrations/` so it cannot add a second production ledger entry.
- `supabase/baseline/README.md` records why full `db push` readiness still requires mapping the remaining drift from the reconciliation audit.

## Verification

```
npm test   61 passed (7 files; was 54)
npm run build  clean
```

New tests cover the shared formatters and order workflow, including the null semantics and kobo division.

## Not in this PR

- Applying `20261114182000_catalog_flexibility.sql` to production. The code now tolerates its absence efficiently, but the feature remains unavailable until the migration is applied.
- Fully aligning the migration ledger for `supabase db push` (needs production-ledger mapping, documented in `docs/database/`).
- Merging the Admin Orders tab UI into `OrdersManager`. The duplicate workflow constant is gone, but the two screens still render orders differently.

body:
## Description

The default suite no longer waits on wall-clock timers for events, and a new sleep must now justify itself.

- **Event waits synchronize on a signal** instead of polling the clock: the `notify` watch tests, the `opener` late-request watcher test, and the `session` reaper/attach tests. The reaper drives its client reattach off the second session-status poll, and the attach test waits for the *folded* sample, so both interleavings are deterministic rather than timed.
- **The genuine dwells keep a marked `time.Sleep`**: two negative assertions (`opener` forward, `channel` proxy, `session` pressure), an OS-port-release poll, the spinner's frame cadence, and two child-PTY output polls in `test/harness`.
- **The ambient gate gains a `time.Sleep` category**, so a new unmarked sleep fails `make test`. Folded into `specs/testing/test-isolation.md`.

```diff
 ambientCallKind
   net.*  os.*  syscall.Kill
+  time.Sleep   # a clock wait; mark it if it is a genuine dwell
```

This is surface 5 of the hermetic suite design (`plans/2026-11-07-hermetic-test-suite-design.md`), implemented by `plans/2026-11-22-hermetic-wall-clock.md`. The companion cadence plan (`plans/2026-11-22-hermetic-cadence.md`) is carried here as documentation only — not implemented.

## (Optional) Ramifications

- No production behavior change: every edit is in `_test.go` files or the brain.
- A **two-way door**: reverting restores the sleeps. The one lasting effect is the gate category, which constrains future tests to mark a wall-clock wait with a reason.

author: jdavini23
body:
## Summary

Every waitlist signup now sends you an alert email through Resend:

> **Cache waitlist #7: parent@example.com**
> Form: hero · Campaign: threads / carousel-1 · Total signups: 7

How it works:
- **Database trigger (new migration).** An after-insert trigger on `waitlist` posts the new row through `pg_net` to `POST /api/webhooks/waitlist-signup`. The endpoint URL and shared secret are read from **Supabase Vault**, so no secret is in this repo. If either Vault secret is missing the trigger does nothing. Any pg_net error is downgraded to a warning, so an alert can never block or roll back a signup.
- **Endpoint (`server.ts`).** It checks the `x-waitlist-alert-secret` header with a constant-time comparison and validates the email. It looks up the running total; if that lookup fails, the alert still goes out without the count. It then sends a plain-text email through the Resend API, using an idempotency key per email. If Resend fails, the error goes to Sentry and the endpoint returns 502. If the env vars aren't set, it returns 503.
- `.env.example` documents `RESEND_API_KEY`, `WAITLIST_ALERT_TO`, `WAITLIST_ALERT_FROM` and `WAITLIST_ALERT_SECRET`.

## Configuration dependencies

1. **Vercel, Production env:** `RESEND_API_KEY`, `WAITLIST_ALERT_TO` and `WAITLIST_ALERT_SECRET`. `WAITLIST_ALERT_FROM` is optional and defaults to `Cache <onboarding@resend.dev>`. That default sender only delivers to the Resend account owner's own address, which is fine for founder alerts.
2. **Supabase:** run the migration, then create two Vault secrets, `waitlist_alert_url` and `waitlist_alert_secret`. The second must match `WAITLIST_ALERT_SECRET`.

These can be done in any order. Until both sides are configured, signups work exactly as before and no alert is sent.

## Validation

- `npm run lint`: passes
- `npm test`: 66/66 pass, with 6 new endpoint tests:
  - returns 503 when not configured
  - returns 401 for a missing or wrong secret
  - returns 400 for a payload with no email
  - sends the full email, including attribution and total
  - still sends when the count lookup fails
  - returns 502 when Resend rejects the email
- `npm run build`: passes
- Migration: applied in a local Postgres 16 on top of every earlier waitlist migration, with stubbed `vault` and `net` schemas, then tested by inserting as the `anon` role:
  - no secrets: no request is made
  - secrets present: one request with the correct URL, payload and secret header
  - `net.http_post` throwing: the signup still saves, with a warning logged

author: justin13888
body:
## Summary
UniFFI's builtin `Timestamp` keeps the sign on the whole seconds and the fraction as unsigned nanoseconds, so an instant strictly between -1 s and 0 s from the Unix epoch crosses the boundary as its mirror image after the epoch (1969-12-31T23:59:59.25Z arrives as 1970-01-01T00:00:00.75Z). This PR documents that window and pins it with a test. The FFI surface does not change.

- `crates/geocoordinates-ffi/README.md`: a new `## Timestamps` section. It describes the window and lists every timestamp-typed field and argument it affects, notes that the TypeScript wrapper rejects every pre-epoch `Date` (so the window cannot occur there), and says the caveat stays until a UniFFI release keeps the sign.
- `crates/geocoordinates-ffi/src/fix.rs`: the caveat on `Fix.timestamp`, pointing to the README section.
- `crates/geocoordinates-ffi/src/geotag.rs`: the caveat on `GeotagReference.photo_time` and on `Track.locate`'s `at`. Within the window the track is searched at the mirror instant.
- `crates/geocoordinates-ffi/src/cluster.rs`: the same caveat on `Visit.arrival` / `Visit.departure` and `Trip.start` / `Trip.end`. These are the remaining `SystemTime` fields in the FFI crate.
- `swift/Sources/GeoCoordinates/geocoordinates_ffi.swift`: regenerated (`mise run bindings-swift` and the copy the `ffi.yml` staleness check names), so the committed Swift source carries the new doc comments and the changed `track_locate` checksum.
- `crates/geocoordinates-ffi/web/README.md`: the line saying the Python, Kotlin/Java and Swift bindings accept pre-epoch instants now names the one-second exception and links the `## Timestamps` section.
- `crates/geocoordinates-ffi/tests/smoke_geotag.py`: pins the current behaviour.
  - A fix at -0.75 s reads back at +0.75 s.
  - `Track.locate` at -0.75 s, between fixes at -1.75 s and +0.25 s, returns `None`, while the query at -1.75 s is covered.
  - `estimate_offset_ms` with a `photo_time` of -0.75 s gives -500 ms (the true offset would be +1000 ms). A control at -1.25 s gives its true +1500 ms.

## Validation
- `mise run bindings-python`, then `cp target/release/libgeocoordinates_ffi.so bindings/python/ && python3 crates/geocoordinates-ffi/tests/smoke.py`: `python smoke OK`
- `mise run bindings-build && mise run bindings-swift`, then the copy into `swift/Sources/GeoCoordinates/`: the committed Swift source matches the generated one
- `mise run fmt-check`: pass
- `mise run ffi-check`: pass
- `mise run ffi-test`: pass
- `RUSTDOCFLAGS="-D warnings" cargo doc --no-deps -p geocoordinates-ffi`: pass (the new intra-doc links resolve)
- `mise run file-length-check`: pass
- Pre-push hook (`mise run test`): pass
- Not run locally, deferred to CI: the core-crate feature, coverage, mutants, msrv and public-api gates. This PR changes no core-crate code.

## Risks and rollout
- Documentation and test only.
- Coverage gap: the window is pinned only through the Python bindings, which cover both the Rust-side and the Python-side converters. The Kotlin and Swift converters are not pinned. The README states the behaviour for every binding based on the issue's analysis of the shared wire format.
- The upstream UniFFI report is filed separately by the run, so this diff does not link it.

## Decisions taken
Issue 342 - FFI timestamps in the second before the Unix epoch cross with their sign flipped

1. **Document the window rather than change the wire type.** Option taken: the operator's answer on #342, a README caveat plus docs on `Fix.timestamp`, `GeotagReference.photo_time` and `Track.locate`'s `at`, and a test pinning the current behaviour. Rejected: a custom signed-epoch-nanoseconds type, because the operator chose to keep the FFI surface unchanged. Reverse: revert this PR.
2. **Extend the caveat to `Visit` and `Trip`.** These four `SystemTime` fields in `cluster.rs` cross the same builtin `Timestamp`, so they share the window. Option taken: one doc line each, plus a mention in the README list. Rejected: leaving them undocumented, which would make the README's "every timestamp-typed field" claim false. Reverse: drop the four doc paragraphs in `crates/geocoordinates-ffi/src/cluster.rs` and the `Visit` / `Trip` names from the README section.
3. **Pin the window in the Python smoke test, not a Rust test.** A Rust test that calls the exports directly never goes through the wire converters, so it cannot observe the window. The Python smoke test, which CI runs in `python-smoke`, goes through both the Rust and the Python converters. Reverse: delete the appended block in `crates/geocoordinates-ffi/tests/smoke_geotag.py`.
4. **Qualify the web README's statement about the other bindings.** It said they accept pre-epoch instants, which this PR's own caveat contradicts for the last second before the epoch. Option taken: name the exception and link the FFI README section. Rejected: leaving it, which would leave two READMEs disagreeing. Reverse: restore the sentence's last clause in `crates/geocoordinates-ffi/web/README.md`.

## Issue
Closes #342

author: sahlberg
body:
Replaces the hand-written DCE/RPC layer behind the `srvsvc`, `wkssvc`, `lsarpc` and `samr` named pipes (`smb_dcerpc.h` framing plus ndrzcc-generated NDR) with [libdcerpc](https://github.com/sahlberg/libsmb2/tree/master/libdcerpc), the DCE/RPC library from libsmb2. Only its coders and server runtime are built; the libsmb2 transport is not.

A review of the old layer found 32 problems. Several of them were reachable by any client that can open a pipe on IPC$. For example, an ~80-byte `LookupNames` claiming 0x7fffffff names made the server allocate and zero 32 GB, and it was OOM-killed. The full list is in the first commit's message under **"NDR is hard"**.

## ⚠️ Wire behaviour change: NDR64 and big-endian

The old layer spoke **NDR32 little-endian only**:
- it dropped any PDU whose data representation was not little-endian
- it rejected NDR64 presentation contexts
- it rejected bind-time feature negotiation

libdcerpc serves **NDR32 and NDR64, in either byte order**. When a client offers both, as Windows does, it **accepts NDR64**, so Windows clients now talk NDR64 to these pipes. Bind-time feature negotiation is answered with `negotiate_ack`.

## Other behaviour changes

- Replies are fragmented to the client's `max_recv_frag`. Before, anything over 4280 bytes could not reach a Windows client.
- Fragmented requests are reassembled, and a PDU may span SMB2 WRITEs.
- A READ shorter than the current fragment returns what fits with `STATUS_BUFFER_OVERFLOW`. `FSCTL_PIPE_TRANSCEIVE` truncates to `MaxOutputResponse` the same way, and the client READs the rest.
- A WRITE completes a READ already parked waiting on the pipe.
- Context handles belong to the pipe and are freed when it closes. LSA and SAMR handles are typed, so neither service accepts the other's.
- Stream data that is not DCE/RPC fails the WRITE with `STATUS_INVALID_PARAMETER` instead of `STATUS_INTERNAL_ERROR`.

## Service fixes

- `LsarGetUserName` returns the session's user instead of a hard-coded `"myuser"`.
- `LsarQueryInformationPolicy(2)` answers levels 3, 5, 6, 12, 13 and 14 each with its own arm, and other levels with `STATUS_INVALID_PARAMETER`. The account domain is the server identity, matching what SAMR reports.
- `LookupSids`/`LookupSids2` resolve well-known SIDs and groups. `LookupNames` accepts `DOMAIN\account` for the server's own domains.
- `NetrShareEnum` serves levels 0/1/2/501/502. `NetrShareGetInfo` also serves 1005. `NetrServerGetInfo` serves 100/101/102. `NetrShareCheck` is added: smbtorture's NetShareEnumAll test reaches it now that level 2 works.
- `SamrConnect2` is served at its real opnum, 57 (it was registered as 21).

## Structure

- libdcerpc comes in as the `ext/libsmb2` submodule, pinned at upstream's current tip. `ext/libdcerpc.cmake` builds it as a static library linked into `chimera_smb`.
- Its coders are generated from the IDL at build time, so the build needs **python3**, which is now listed explicitly in the Ubuntu CI images.
- The ndrzcc submodule was used only here and is removed.
- The DCE/RPC side (`smb_rpc.c`, `smb_srvsvc.c`, `smb_wkssvc.c`, `smb_lsarpc.c`, `smb_samr.c`) includes only libdcerpc and `smb_rpc_host.h`. The SMB side (`smb_rpc_host.c`) includes only chimera's headers. This keeps `<windows.h>` and libdcerpc's MS-DTYP types (`ACL`, `SECURITY_DESCRIPTOR`, `ACCESS_MASK`, …) out of the same translation unit, so neither set has to be renamed.

## Debug logging (second commit)

With `-d`, libdcerpc logs every call: the request and reply NDR stubs as hex dumps, followed by their YAML transcoding. Example output is in the second commit's message.

## Known gaps

- **Windows (MSVC):** chimera's side is ready, but libdcerpc itself does not build with MSVC yet. It needs small portability fixes upstream in libsmb2: `container_of` uses `typeof` and a statement expression, two `__attribute__((format))`, POSIX I/O and `ssize_t` in `dcerpc_read_yaml_file()`, and statically initialized flexible-array pretty-printer tables, mostly emitted by `idlcomp.py`. The Windows build will fail until those land and the submodule is bumped.
- Still open from the review: there is no access check on `OpenPolicy`/`Connect`; DCE/RPC signing and sealing are unsupported; the interface minor version must match exactly; LSA level 3 still carries the machine SID; share enumeration ignores the resume handle and preferred maximum length.

author: pradeepgudipati
body:
The 'Apply dev scale policy' step runs .github/scripts/set-dev-scale.sh, but the deploy job starts with an empty workspace, so every deploy failed with exit 127 (No such file or directory) — e.g. run 44997859686.

An earlier sparse-checkout fix (az-aca-scale-policy) never reached dev, which is why the same failure kept recurring after PR #58 merged.

This change:
- Checks out the full repository tree as the deploy job's first step, so the script and the workflow always come from the same tree and cannot drift apart.
- Fails the scale step with an explicit error if the script is ever missing, instead of a bare exit 127.

author: teamleaderleo
body: Carries #48376 forward at the same head (432beeb9). The original branch is outside lane/, so this lane could not rerun its CI. That head's only reds were the four cmux-tui artifacts jobs, killed when their runner shut down (exit 143). The daemon-test reds from the older head did not recur at 432beeb9. Related: #48376 (close it when this merges) ## Changelog - None (carries #48376) --- Original #48376 body: Leo, 2026-11-21 ~02:00Z, on `Waiting for the agent service (1:07) Restart agent service` under a chat composer in his NIGHTLY: > this still happens and it's really bad 1. the time is not aligned with the rest of the s*** 2. the "restart agent service" isn't aligned either 3. this shouldnt evne happen. at all. why does it take any time at all to "connect". that's a thing that needs to be fixed This PR is point 3: the wait itself. The alignment (points 1 and 2) is a separate PR. Chat-hold: strict fix ## What made the wait "Agent service" is this app's acpmux daemon. Every chat's handshake runs a lookup that asks it `_acpmux/status` before the pane can open its WebSocket. On Leo's Mac three things stacked: 1. **The daemon ran below its CPU tier.** All 98 of its threads ran at priority 20 (`ps -M`), while the app ran at 31 to 47 and the machine's load average was 80 to 170. `nightly-update` is a launchd job with `ProcessType` `Standard`. Its `acpmux daemon restart` passed that job's utility QoS clamp down to the daemon, and every update's `--take-over` successor (`daemon/exe_swap.rs`) inherited it again. macOS can't lift a clamp from inside the process, and `qos::enter_daemon` sets nothing, so the daemon stayed lowered for good. The `_acpmux/status` that every connect waits on took **0.16 to 51.5 s** (20 probes over 40 s, p50 about 1.7 s). 2. **The lookup's retries started over.** Each status call ended at its 5, 10 or 20 s limit and a fresh call began, so a daemon that answered in about 10 s cost 5 + 10 + 20 + 10 s. The app log shows it: `status unanswered after 5s / 10s / 20s`, then 46 s from the lookup to `transport open`. 3. **Every chat paid the whole lookup again.** Only the launch prewarm kept its endpoint, for one handshake. Every new chat, tab and reload ran the lookup again on the same daemon. ## What changes - **acpmux (Rust):** a `daemon run` that starts below the daemon's CPU tier (`qos::lowered_priority`, read from `proc_pidinfo`) starts again as the login-session launchd job, which launchd runs at `Interactive`, and exits. A `daemon start` or `restart` from a lowered process goes to that job too (`login_placement::placement_lowered`). A daemon that launchd runs as a job (`XPC_SERVICE_NAME`: this home's job, or the `acpmux daemon service` LaunchAgent) never moves, and that LaunchAgent now sets `ProcessType` `Interactive`. Starts that carry a descriptor (the app's `--ready-fd`/`--person-key-fd`) are placed by their starter and stay put. Leo's running daemon gets fixed at the next update swap: its successor inherits the clamp, sees it and moves. - **App host (Swift):** `AcpmuxHost` keeps the endpoint a lookup found for as long as the daemon that took this launch's person key is still the one in `daemon.pid` and still running. That check is one small file read plus `kill(pid, 0)`, with no round trip. A new chat, tab or reload connects straight away. One lookup that may not start a daemon runs in the background after each kept handshake and keeps the endpoint current. If that lookup fails, the kept endpoint is dropped. A restart or reconnect drops it too. - **App host (Swift):** the lookup's status calls now run side by side on separate connections, started 0, 5, 15 and 35 s in (at most four), and the first answer wins. A call made just before a restart is still overtaken (the 2026-11-06 case), and a slow daemon no longer pays for each limit it missed. Every new wait has a stop condition: the hedged calls are a fixed list ended by the first answer, the background check is one at a time, and the lowered take-over's wait is capped at the swap's own 15 s. ## Numbers One harness (`probe.py`: connect, `initialize`, `_acpmux/status` on a fresh unix-socket connection, the lookup's call) against the NIGHTLY's own acpmux binary on a Mac at load 130 to 145. Each run is a `--memory` daemon in a temporary home, 60 calls, three alternating rounds: | daemon started | p50 | p90 | max | |---|---|---|---| | under the utility clamp (what Leo's daemon ran at) | 8.2 / 11.0 / 17.3 ms | 29.5 / 52.6 / 55.8 ms | 65.8 to 284 ms | | at the default tier (what the launchd job gives) | 0.8 / 0.9 / 1.0 ms | 0.9 / 2.5 / 2.9 ms | 1.6 to 23.6 ms | A launchd job of `ProcessType` `Interactive` bootstrapped from a clamped process reads QoS 0x15 (default); a `Standard` job reads 0x11 (utility), which is how Leo's daemon got lowered. - **Floor:** about 0 for a local daemon: no round trip before the composer can send. - **Paid now (Leo's NIGHTLY, 2026-11-21 01:57Z):** 46 s from lookup to transport on one handshake. The line he screenshotted read 1:07. The live daemon's `_acpmux/status` measured 0.16 to 51.5 s. - **After:** a handshake on a daemon that already took the key costs the kept-endpoint check, **0.04 ms p50** (2.2 ms p99, same machine; that's the read plus `kill(pid, 0)`). The first lookup after launch, or after a daemon restart, runs on a daemon at the default tier (memory-daemon p50 about 1 ms, 10 to 20x below the clamped one), and a slow answer costs only its own time, not 5 + 10 + 20 s on top. ## Tests - `AcpmuxPrewarmedEndpointTests`: kept while its daemon serves, gone when the daemon changes or on a reconnect, background check keeps it current. The launch-prewarm cases still pass unchanged. - `AcpmuxLookupStatusHedgeTests`: a slow first call still answers, a hung one gets overtaken, a prompt answer makes one call. - `login_placement`: `placement_lowered` cases. - Known limit, recoverable: right after a dashboard token rotation, one handshake can still get the kept endpoint's old token. Its connect fails, the reconnect drops the kept endpoint and looks up again. - CI runs these. Compile checks went through `cmux-ci` (no builds on agent Macs). ## Changelog - Fixed: a chat no longer waits on "Waiting for the agent service" when the agent service was started below normal priority (by an updater or a background job). It now restarts itself at normal priority. - Fixed: new chats, tabs and reloads connect to the running agent service right away instead of asking it again first. - Fixed: a slow agent service no longer adds 5, 10 and 20 s of retries on top of its own answer time. --- Open in [code]smith · Need help on this PR? Tag @codesmith-bot with what you need. 🤖 Generated with [Claude Code](https://claude.com/claude-code) Agent session: [agent session](https://cmux.com/deeplink/agent?id=aid-c7410c1f5df308c87f22&model=claude-opus-5-5)

author: ahmedashrafaa413-hub
body:
## Why

Ahmed's Snapchat Ads Manager for today (22 Nov, GMT+3) showed **14 purchases, $1,007.88, ROAS 3.65** on $276.17 of spend. `get_snapchat_insights` returned the same spend and impressions (193,871) but **11 purchases, $716.85, ROAS 2.60**, at account, campaign and ad squad level alike.

The MCP asked Snapchat for `action_report_time=impression`, which puts each purchase on the day of the ad impression it is attributed to. Ads Manager here reports at conversion time, so purchases made today from impressions on earlier days are counted today. Spend and impressions do not depend on this setting, which is why only purchases and revenue differed.

## What changes

- `get_snapchat_insights` takes `action_report_time` (`conversion` | `impression`), default **conversion**. The response's `attribution.action_report_time` names the one used.
- `fetchEntityStats` takes `actionReportTime` and falls back to the existing default for a missing or unknown value. It is threaded through `fetchSnapchatLiveInsights` (also part of its cache key).
- The synced cache holds impression-time numbers, so it is only used as a fallback when `impression` is asked for.
- The dashboard and sync keep `ACTION_REPORT_TIME = "impression"`; this PR only changes the MCP default.

## Test plan

- [x] `npm test`: 101/101, including 3 new tests in `test/snapchat-report-time.test.mjs` (URL carries the requested value, default for missing/unknown, MCP schema and default).
- [ ] After deploy: today's account total with the default should match Ads Manager's purchases and value for the same moment.

author: 4mtrade
body:
## Problem

A fully watched video shows no progress bar on its card. It looks unwatched.

`VideoStateController.resetPositionIfNeeded()` runs in `onNewVideo()`, also for the embed (preview) player. For a short (< 6 min) or ended video it calls `resetPosition()`, which removes the saved state. So when the user moves over a watched card, the preview removes the progress of this video.

Device log before the fix:

```
reset video=S9bCLPwzSC0 short=true ended=true embed=true
```

## Fix

- The embed player starts such a video from 0, but does not remove the state and does not save its own position.
- When the user opens the video in the fullscreen player, the skipped reset is done, so the fullscreen behaviour does not change (the video starts from 0).
- The fully watched state is persisted with `persistNow()`. The normal delayed write (10 sec) is lost when the system kills the app in this time. This happens often on low RAM devices.

## Test

Mi TV Stick (Android 9):

1. Watch a short video to the end. The card shows 100%.
2. Move over the card, so the preview plays.
3. Leave the card and restart the app. The card still shows 100% (before: no bar).
4. Open the video from the preview in full screen. It starts from 0, as before.

author: vmoroz
body:
## Description

### Type of Change
- New feature (non-breaking change which adds functionality)
- This change requires a documentation update

### Why
PR and CI build react-native-windows for ARM64, but nothing ever runs those builds: the ARM64 jobs cross-compile on x64 agents and skip every test. v8-jsi and hermes-windows already build and test on two shared VM images, a Windows x64 image and a Windows ARM64 image defined in [microsoft/v8-jsi `.ado/image`](https://github.com/microsoft/v8-jsi/tree/main/.ado/image). This PR moves RNW onto the same two images and runs the ARM64 tests natively on ARM64 agents.

### What
- **Same images as v8-jsi.** x64/x86 jobs demand the `windows-2025-1espt` image. ARM64 jobs use the `windows-2025-1espt-arm64` image and declare `os: windows` and `hostArchitecture: arm64`, as v8-jsi does. CI uses the shared pools. PR keeps its own public pools (`rnw-pool-4`/`rnw-pool-8` plus a new `rnw-pool-8-arm64`), so fork code stays off the internal pools. RNW's own image recipes stay in `.ado/image` for the stable branches.
- **Universal ARM64 tests run natively.** The Universal ARM64 Debug/Release jobs build and run `Microsoft.ReactNative.Cxx.UnitTests`, `Microsoft.ReactNative.IntegrationTests`, and `Mso.UnitTests` on ARM64 agents. These three projects gain ARM64 configurations, and the solution now builds them.
- **Desktop ARM64EC tests run natively.** The Desktop ARM64EC jobs build their unit and integration test DLLs, which the solution used to skip, and run them on ARM64 agents with the same filters as x64.
- **ARM64 E2E.** A new `Arm64Hermes` cell deploys the Fabric test app on an ARM64 agent and runs the Jest/WinAppDriver suite. Hang dumps use ProcDump's ARM64 binary.
- **No silent passes.** Before tests run, a check confirms the binaries are really ARM64 or ARM64EC, so an emulated run can't pass. Each Universal suite must run at least one test.
- **ARM64 agent setup.** ARM64 agents ship without the agent's bundled `node10`, so a step copied from v8-jsi points it at the image's Node before the mandatory post-job tasks run.

## Screenshots
Not applicable.

## Testing
Draft until the new pools are available and PR and CI runs show the ARM64 suites executing natively. So far: YAML, project, and solution checks, plus the architecture check against real ARM64, ARM64EC, and x64 binaries.

## Changelog
Should this change be included in the release notes: no

Run ARM64 unit, integration, and E2E tests natively on ARM64 build agents.
