author: arbelonson-source
body:
## **User description** **What a person saw before.** With the phone full, a word fixed in History waits for room and the fix dialog closes as done (since #712 on Android, already so on the iPhone). History then re-read the conversation from its file, so the line kept its old words until there was room, a newer version of the conversation waiting for room did not show at all, and the person could fix the same word again. Separately, when the conversation's newer version waiting for room no longer had the line (a replay took it off the screen before the conversation closed), a History fix of that line was written to the file and reported saved, then the waiting version was written over the file without the line, and the fix was gone. **What they see now.** History shows each conversation as it will be saved: the newer version waiting for room, or else the file, with the line changes still waiting put in. Both phones read it the same way, through the history writer (`loadNow`), in order with the saves already queued. A History fix of a line the waiting version no longer has is refused: nothing is written and the dialog says the fix was not saved (History no longer shows such a line anyway). **Tests.** Three new OzenKit `TranscriptHistoryWriterTests` and three new Android `TranscriptHistoryWriterTest` cases, using a read-only folder as the full phone. Run with History reading the file as before, they failed: - a fix waiting for room: shown as `[I saw Cohen today, ...]` where `[I saw Avi Cohen today, ...]` was expected; - the waiting newer version: end time `nil` where `200` was expected, and the older lines shown; - the fix of a line the waiting version lost: reported as saved (`Expected value to be false`). They pass now, with the rest of the writer tests (34 Swift, 37 Android writer, 55 ConversationSaverTest) and all portable checks. The iPhone screen change (HistoryDetailView reading through the view model) is only built on CI. **Stars follow what History shows.** With History showing the version waiting for room, a star tapped there used to flip the file's own star: where the waiting version had a star the file lacked, "Remove the star" kept it (and the file took the star). The tap now gives the line the opposite of the star History shows (the waiting version's when it has the line, else the file's), the file takes that state, and the waiting version keeps the same one, so writing it once there is room doesn't undo the tap. **One test expectation changed, by the orchestrator's decision:** "a star tapped in History follows the conversation as History shows it..." (both phones) used to expect the file's star flipped (starred), because History showed the file. Its principle stays (the tap follows what History shows); its expected source is now the version History shows, so the tap takes the waiting version's star off (false, and false in the file once the waiting version is written). Its title says "the version waiting for room" instead of "the file on disk", and it also checks first that History shows the star. Nothing else in it changed. **The starred lines list asks for no star outright.** It shows the stars of the saved files, and its Remove the star went through the same tap, which now follows the version waiting for room: where that version had no star on a line the file had starred (room back, nothing saved yet), Remove the star put the star back on. It now asks for the line to have no star, and the writers set that state on the file and the waiting version (new tests on both phones, plus one through Android's ConversationSaver; they failed before with the line still starred on disk and in what History shows). A line still on the caption screen follows the screen's own star, as before. **Last round (from CodeRabbit on #722).** A line still on the caption screen now takes the state the starred lines list asks for too: a star taken off there while the phone was full stayed in the file, and the list's Remove the star toggled it back on while saying it was removed. A star from History on a line only the version waiting for room has is refused unless that version reaches the disk first (it was called saved while nothing was written). History's view of a waiting version now carries the name, source, language and time zone its save will keep from the file, through the store's own step (`keepingSavedDetails`, now shared with `save`). New tests on both phones failed before; the iPhone app test ran alone on `both-phones-history-shows-a-fix-waiting-for-room-red`. **A refused fix still catches up.** On both phones a History fix refused because the waiting version lost the line still writes what was waiting for room once there is room, and takes the saving warning away when nothing is left waiting (new test on each phone; they failed before: the file kept the older words / the warning stayed). ## Summary by CodeRabbit * **Bug Fixes** * History now displays the latest saved or pending conversation, including word fixes waiting to be written. * Edits to lines no longer present in the latest conversation are rejected, preventing stale changes from being saved. * **Tests** * Added coverage for pending saves, updated conversations, and rejected edits. ___ ## **CodeAnt-AI Description** **Show pending transcript changes in History and align word fixes across phones** ### What Changed - History now shows the newest conversation version and word fixes waiting to be saved, rather than stale text from the file. Fixes are refused when the line is no longer in that version, with a clear explanation. - Word selection for corrections is consistent across iPhone and Android: punctuation is left out, Hebrew name endings are kept, and phrases only join across plain spaces. iPhone word buttons are easier to tap. - Removing a star from the starred-lines list now removes it even when the saved version and the transcript on screen differ. - Long conversations update with less slowdown as new words arrive. ### Impact `✅ Fewer repeated word fixes in History` `✅ Clearer correction refusal messages` `✅ Reliable star removal during save delays` `✅ Smoother captions in long conversations`

author: jonborchardt
body:
# Ticket 0053: PR chip on the board refreshes PR status

Factory job `job-79ed11b0` on `factory/job-79ed11b0-ticket-0053-pr-chip-on-the-board-refresh` → `main`. Spec, build notes, and reviews are in the
job's artifact directory.

## Summary

On the board, the PR phase chip (for example "ready to merge") is now a button on rows where the
server allows Refresh PR. Clicking it, or pressing Enter, runs the same `refresh-pr` action as the
detail page and reloads the board, without opening the job. Each board row carries a new
`pr.refreshable` flag, set in `board()` from the existing `cannotRefreshPr` rule, so the client
derives no workflow rule. On every other row, and on the detail page, the chip stays a label. A
refused refresh shows the server's message under the chip.

## Acceptance criteria

- [x] AC1 — `board()` rows carry `pr.refreshable`, true exactly when `cannotRefreshPr(job)` is null: `tests/server.test.ts` "board refresh flag (ticket 0053)".
- [x] AC2 — a row with the flag renders the phase chip as a focusable button; a row without it stays a label: `web/src/App.test.tsx`.
- [x] AC3 — click or Enter posts `refresh-pr` (`force: true` on a finished job, no force on `needs-human`) and the board is fetched again: `web/src/App.test.tsx`.
- [x] AC4 — the click does not navigate (`window.location.hash` unchanged): `web/src/App.test.tsx`.
- [x] AC5 — a refused request shows its error on the board and the chip can be clicked again: `web/src/App.test.tsx`.
- [x] AC6 — existing assertions hold, including the "ready to merge" chip test.
- [x] AC7 — `npm run check` and `npm run build` pass: verification run 166.
- [ ] Needs human verification: click a real "ready to merge" chip in `orch ui` against a real GitHub PR.

## Validation

Verification run 166 at 8dfc49ac0259b5be520d0fa06a80d26cfc185658: passed; checks `check` passed, `build` passed. Runs 164 and
165 at the same commit failed only on `tests/runner-lock.test.ts`, a file this branch does not
change; `orch` classified it as a flake and the test passes alone. The Playwright suite was also run
once at this commit for the reviewers: 25 passed.

## Review

Round 1 of 3: security PASS, correctness PASS, code-quality PASS, ui-design PASS, ux PASS,
accessibility PASS, web-platform PASS; BLOCKING: 0. Approver: APPROVE. The UI reviews were made
from the diff and logs, not a rendered page.

## Sensitive changes

- `tests/server.test.ts` — one test case added for the board flag; nothing removed or weakened.
- `web/src/App.test.tsx` — two board tests added and fixtures gained `refreshable`; nothing removed or weakened.
- `web/src/Tickets.test.tsx` — fixtures gained `refreshable: false` only.

The verification baseline (`factory.json`) did not change and no policy needed human acceptance.

## Known limitations

- While a refresh is pending the chip is disabled, so keyboard focus can drop from it (MINOR, accessibility).
- A successful refresh gives no feedback beyond the board reload, and a refusal message stays until the next click (MINOR, accessibility).
- The refusal message may sit beside the chip rather than under it in a wide cell (MINOR, ui-design).

author: wagnerflo
body:
Closes #960

Makes `snapshotting.prefix` optional for `cron` snapshotting, so snapshot names can consist of the timestamp only, e.g. `2026-11-22_1504` with `timestamp_format: "2006-01-02_1504"`. Use case and background are in #960 and #121.

**Changes**

- `config.SnapshottingCron.Prefix` is now optional. No other code changes are needed: the cron snapshotter uses the prefix only to build the name, and `snapname.New` already validates the resulting name.
- Docs (`docs/configuration/snapshotting.rst`): naming section, the note on snapshot ownership, and the `cron` example.
- Tests: `TestSnapshotting` now covers `cron` without a prefix (accepted) and `periodic` without a prefix (rejected). The new `TestNewWithoutPrefix` checks that all built-in timestamp formats and a custom one produce valid snapshot names without a prefix.

author: joei4cm
body:
## ELI5

When a follow-up was assigned to a terminal Orca does not own, `worker-stop` correctly avoided closing that terminal but left the follow-up open and blocking reuse. It now cancels the assignment while leaving the external terminal alone.

## What Changed

After the normal stop fence is committed, the local stop path recognizes an external terminal resource and settles the worker as `abandoned` with stage `assignment_settled`. This fails the open dispatch and clears its terminal claim without claiming the agent process exited, closing the terminal, or releasing its resource. The receipt reports `processAction: 'none'` and warns that the external terminal was not closed.

Only Expected B from #46424 is implemented. Expected A (sending new work to a finished dispatch) is unchanged.

## Why

External ownership means Orca has no authority to close the process. Leaving the dispatch in `stop_unknown` strands `terminal_busy`; marking it `stopped` would incorrectly claim process exit. Settling the assignment as abandoned accurately cancels the follow-up while preserving the terminal and its process.

## Linked Issue

Fixes #46424

## Visual Proof

N/A — backend orchestration lifecycle behavior; no visual or interaction change.

## Testing

- [ ] I manually tested these changes locally — no app/manual UI test was performed.
- [x] Added one SQLite-backed state-machine invariant test in `worker-dispatch-stop-state.test.ts`; it asserts assignment settlement without process-exit or terminal-release claims, with hardcoded expectations and no mocks.
- [x] The added test fails if the non-process-exit settlement behavior is removed and avoids the repository's test anti-patterns.
- `corepack pnpm test src/main/runtime/orchestration/db/worker-dispatch/worker-dispatch-stop-state.test.ts --maxWorkers=2` — 1/1 passed.
- `corepack pnpm check:changed` after rebasing on current `origin/main` — 27/27 checks passed (format, lint, typecheck, importing tests, and selected ratchets).
- Platform: Linux. No platform-specific behavior or UI was changed.

## Performance

None. The external path reuses the existing stop transaction and avoids terminal inspection and close work; it adds no polling or recurring work.

## Risk

**Level:** Low

The external agent process may still be running after its assignment is cancelled. The worker is recorded as `abandoned` / `assignment_settled`, the receipt explicitly warns that the terminal was not closed, and the terminal resource remains external. Other ownership states and the federated stop path are unchanged. There is no schema or wire-format change; a plain revert restores the previous `stop_unknown` behavior and its stuck terminal claim.

## AI Disclosure

Implemented with Claude Code (Anthropic), model Opus 5.5. The human selected Expected B only and reviewed the scope; the model authored the implementation and invariant test.

## Review

Self-reviewed the stop fence, lifecycle settlement, and external-resource handling. Maintainer review is pending.

- [x] Not applicable; this change copies or mechanically translates no upstream skill-installer source, tests, fixtures, registry entries, path tables, comments, or documentation.

## Notes

- Security: no new input or IPC surface; existing worker-stop authorization is unchanged.
- Cross-platform: no platform-specific APIs or paths changed.
- Remote SSH: external ownership stays with its existing host; the federated stop path is unchanged.
- Mobile: no mobile UI or behavior changed.
- Backwards compatibility: receipt fields and database schema are unchanged.
- Scope: Expected A is deliberately not implemented.

## Summary Fixes two findings from the installed logging smoke rerun. **PL-1293:** `vox status` and `vox daemon status` wrote nothing to the durable log, whether voxd was up or down. Each call now writes exactly one INFO record with fixed codes. The record never includes the status payload, the endpoint, or exception text: ``` [INFO] client.cli.punt_vox.cli_daemon: vox status: outcome=not_running reason=unreachable [INFO] client.cli.punt_vox.cli_daemon: vox daemon status: outcome=running reason=reachable ``` The top-level `status_cmd` now calls the new `DaemonCli.probe_status(client)`. `__main__.py` already imported `cli_daemon`, so this adds no coupling. CLI output and exit codes are unchanged. **PL-1294:** `LuxScenePublisher` logged `scene unchanged; nothing pushed` at INFO on every identical refresh. A `NoPush` summary now logs at DEBUG. Real pushes and failures keep their current levels. **Verification:** I installed the wheel into a fresh venv with an isolated HOME. I ran both status commands with voxd down and then up: each call wrote exactly one record, with no endpoint or payload. I drove the installed publisher six times with the same scene against a counting Lux fake: one show record, zero updates, no INFO no-ops. author: lyingtree
body:
## Why

The previous parser required a recognized bibliography heading. It indexed the supplied Hocke note, but not the Runge note with counted Chinese headings. A number-only index also cannot distinguish main reference 1 from supplementary reference 1, and label-only hover caches can return the wrong source.

## What changes

- Identify reference blocks directly from actual `^ref-N` / `^sref-N` anchors. Headings are unrestricted and optional. Also support `ref1` / `sref1` and named sets such as `ref-appendix-N`.
- Keep anchor namespaces independent and expand numeric ranges only within the namespace selected by exact link targets. Index the exact reference block, including compact lists and multiline entries, without including following prose or metadata.
- Preserve reference identity in preview caching, metadata refresh, and Reading-view DOM matching. Share same-note path validation between source parsing and rendered links.
- Report ambiguous plain numeric citations instead of mixing reference sets; leave invalid targets and groups spanning different namespaces to native link behavior.
- Set manifest, package, lockfile, and compatibility metadata to **1.2.0**. Preserve `citation-range-preview` and minimum Obsidian version `1.15.1`.

## Validation

- `npm run check`: production build passed; **171 tests passed across 8 files**; ESLint reported no errors and one existing deprecated-settings-display warning in unchanged `src/settings.ts`.
- `npm run package`: installation archive verified to contain the matching `main.js`, `manifest.json`, and `styles.css` under `citation-range-preview/`.
- Supplied Hocke note: **31 reference blocks, 45 citation groups**.
- Supplied Runge note: **96 reference blocks (66 main + 30 supplementary), 108 citation groups**, with every expanded reference resolved.
- Both complete notes produced identical results after all Markdown headings were removed, all headings were renamed, and newlines were converted to CRLF.
- Reading/editor host integration covers distinct same-label previews, edited reference text, moved entries, removed/renamed anchors, and figure/equation link isolation. The user's desktop Obsidian installation was not exercised.

The supplied full notes are not committed; regression fixtures use fictional references.

## Compatibility

Per the requested anchor-based behavior, an unanchored numbered list no longer establishes references, regardless of its heading. Plain in-text citations still work when existing supported block IDs identify a unique reference set. Existing notes with `ref` / `sref` anchors need no content changes.

author: claudioed
body:
CodeQL `go/log-injection` on the `request failed` record in `writeError` (`internal/adapters/inbound/http/response.go:72`): it logged the raw `err`, and an internal error's text can carry request data, so a CR/LF in it could forge a log line.

- Test first: `response_log_test.go` (copied from amr-fleet-control b771a8c) installs a recording slog handler and asserts that no attribute of the record holds CR or LF. It failed before the fix.
- Fix: the record now logs `"error", logReplacer.Replace(err.Error())`, the same fix as amr-fleet-control 672aecd. Where the repo's sanitizer wraps a package-level replacer, the fix calls `logReplacer.Replace` at the sink, because CodeQL does not reliably see through that wrapper.

Part of the fleet log-injection fix wave (already fixed in amr-fleet-control and material-flow-control). This PR includes no release or deploy.

body:
## 解决的问题与行为变化

开启加密历史跨账号选路后，原账号在首次发送时返回明确的额度耗尽 429，现有完整历史保护仍会直接结束请求，即使池内有合格账号且尚无输出。本修改让这一类明确拒绝进入既有有界换号流程，保留完整历史、工具结果、权限与账号资格检查。保留服务端会话指针、密文拒绝、未知交付和已经输出的限制。

普通 OpenAI OAuth 账号遇到短暂 5xx、明确包装为 401 的并发过载或可重试的出字前断流时，优先在原账号有限重试。重试用尽后结束该次请求并保留绑定，避免对暂时性故障连续切号。实际额度耗尽与凭证故障继续使用原有账号处理。生图工具未执行而生成的本地 502 保留原有直接换号行为。

## 关联记录与来源

Refs #805、#807。复用现有账号选择、退避、错误分类与交付回执。上游基础提交为 `8dedf05db37c870265e04327defb9e96e7787603`。先在固定 v2.22.0 上复现同一业务回归，再将修改合并到当前 production 源码。

## 管理员新功能提示

提示 ID、展示位置、关闭行为、重新公告及 A→B→C 提示回归均不适用，本次没有 UI、菜单或新增配置。

## 复现与验收

使用隔离真实 Redis 和 localhost HTTP 上游，首次请求生成完整代理历史。下一请求向原账号发送同一历史和已完成工具结果，上游返回 `usage_limit_reached`，另一合格账号返回完整结果。随后由独立网关实例读取共享记录并继续同一任务。

新增回归覆盖 OAuth/API Key、JSON/SSE，检查第二次发送的完整输入、唯一完成事件、原归属记录以及后继请求。另覆盖外部会话指针、普通限流、截断或重复字段 JSON、回执并发修改。已有密文拒绝、取消及交付保护回归保留。

## 实际验证

| 检查 | 结果 | 范围 |
| --- | --- | --- |
| v2.22.0 原源码加同一新增 handler 回归 | 已复现 | 4 个 OAuth/API Key × JSON/SSE 场景均预期 200、实际 429 |
| v2.22.0 候选的完整历史换号及后继请求 | 通过 | 相同 4 个场景，真实 localhost HTTP 和共享 Redis |
| 相关 Issue805、Issue842、额度回执与临时故障定向回归 | 已执行 | service 通过，handler 旧 520 立即换号断言已按本次语义扩展为 OAuth 保绑定及 API Key 原行为，最终定向复验全部通过，之后的生图相邻回归及受影响路径复验也通过 |
| gofmt、git diff --check | 通过 | 本次差异 |
| 当前 PR head 9962b7f 的 CI | 等待维护者批准运行 | GitHub 将来自新 fork 的检查标为 action_required，未执行，不计为通过 |
| 生产切换 | 待执行 | 独立发布流程处理 |

首次基线运行中的额外 service 测试编译被隔离容器内存限制终止，handler 的四个业务失败已实际执行。随后以限制 Go GC 内存的隔离环境完成 service 定向测试。上述测试使用合成提供方，不宣称通用跨账号密文兼容。

## 兼容性与运行影响

没有数据库迁移或新的配置。明确额度拒绝后的换号仍受现有管理员选择、原请求权限、池内资格和重试预算约束。首次工具发现结果在明确拒绝时只撤回该次任务预留的回执，使用原值比较，其他任务的新记录不会被覆盖。正常计量和已输出后的行为沿用原路径。

## 文档与用户可见变化

用户可观察到额度拒绝后同一请求有机会由备用账号完成，临时 OAuth 故障先在原账号重试。本 PR 尚处于验证阶段，合并与发布分别核验。

## Agent 使用声明

Codex 主线程负责分析、额度修复、回归与发布准备，模型为 `gpt-6-astra`，推理强度未由环境提供。原子线程负责旧补丁历史核查及临时重试移植，独立线程负责业务范围与代码审查，均继承父配置，未覆盖模型或推理设置。

## 提交前自查

- [x] 目标为本仓库 production，差异只含相关后端与回归。
- [x] 公开内容检查未发现生产凭据、内部账号、主机或业务原文。
- [x] 已执行、失败、待验证与生产状态分别列出。
- [x] 沿用现有配置、权限、计量与共享记录合同。
- [x] 管理员提示项不适用，未引入 UI。
- [x] 已披露 Agent 参与范围及已知模型信息。

author: sniezka1927
body:
## Linked issue

Closes #14465

## Type of change

- [x] Bug fix
- [ ] Small improvement or alignment, with no change to how a feature works
- [ ] New provider, MCP app, or connector
- [ ] Translation or documentation
- [ ] New feature or change to existing behavior (needs an approved issue)

## What changed

On a joined server, an agent chat now opens without a long wait while the pictures of another chat download. Before, the next agent showed "Loading" for 2 to 3.5 s.

**Cause.** Each Team data channel in the WebRTC page (`src/renderer/src/features/team/team-webrtc.ts`) could queue up to 4 MiB before the sender waited. When a chat with large pictures opened, the host put several MB of file chunks into SCTP at once. The host's UDP socket discarded packets (`packetsDiscardedOnSend` 355 in one run). SCTP then sent nothing on any channel until its retransmission timer ran. During that time the host's `files` queue stayed at 1,731,763 bytes and its `rpc` queue at 32,357 bytes for 1.75 s, and the client got no RPC answer. The RPC answers of the next agent waited behind that stall.

**Change.**
- The four Team data channels (`rpc`, `events`, `files`, `desktop`) now queue at most 256 KiB and refill below 64 KiB. The browser egress channel keeps its 4 MiB limit.
- A send that waits for `bufferedamountlow` checks `bufferedAmount` again after the event. Before, all waiters on one channel woke together, so the queue could go past its limit by one frame per waiter.

The wire format does not change. Only the sender's local queue changes.

**Surfaces.** The WebRTC page of the desktop app, which is both the host side and the desktop client side of a joined server. The web client and mobile receive with no change. A server must also be on the new version, because it is the sender of the pictures. The changelog says so.

**Not in this change.** Web and mobile senders (`packages/team-client/src/remote-peer.ts`) and the browser egress channel keep their 4 MiB limit. They can cause the same stall during a large upload or egress traffic, but I did not measure them.

**Smallest useful change.** I first tried a send window based on the receiver's `file-ack` frames, as in PairDrop. It did not help: the next chat still waited 1.8 to 2.6 s, because two transfers could still put about 4 MB into SCTP. The stall comes from how much is queued at once, so the fix limits the queue, as js-libp2p does (2 MiB per channel).

Model and harness: Claude Opus 5.5 in Claude Code.

## Verification

- [x] Narrow checks for what changed: `biome check` on the changed file, `bun run typecheck:renderer`, and `bun run test:changed` (no test file imports this file). The pre-commit hook ran `typecheck:renderer`, `typecheck:storybook` and the UI check.
- [x] Surfaces touched are named under "What changed"
- [x] A feature for agents, chats, channels, routines or server settings also works on a joined server: the fix is for a joined server, and the smoke test runs on one
- [x] Relevant manual smoke test completed
- [x] No credentials, private data, generated output, or real user files are included

Before and after, measured with the same probes: `dev:test-client` over WebRTC, `OPENBOT_DEV_RTT_MS=150`, 12 agents of 500 messages, two 8.5 MB pictures. Open the chat with the pictures, then open the next agent.

| | Before | After |
| --- | --- | --- |
| Next agent opens | 3.2 s | 0.39 s, 0.76 s, 1.16 s |
| Longest request wait during the download | 3.1 s | 0.23 s, 0.58 s, 0.99 s |
| Picture download | 3.5 s | 0.8 to 1.5 s |
| Host packets discarded on send | 355 | 82, 186 |

Smoke test on the final head (desktop test client on a joined server, WebRTC, 150 ms added delay):

| # | Feature | Result | Evidence |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| 1 | Open the next agent while pictures download | pass | Scale 2 rows in 388 ms; longest request wait 225 ms; picture downloads 791 and 835 ms, outcome `ok` |
| 2 | Picture download is complete | pass | The 4 pictures in view are `complete`, 2400x1600, from `openbot-remote-attachment` |
| 3 | Upload from the desktop to the server (`files`, other direction) | pass | 3,158,073-byte draft uploaded in 268 ms, then discarded |
| 4 | Reopen chats | pass | Scale 2 in 285 ms, Scale 3 in 334 ms; no renderer errors |

Not checked locally:
- Throughput on a real high-latency link. `bufferedAmount` counts bytes that are not yet sent, so a smaller queue should not cap throughput. I could not add network delay on this computer.
- A TURN relay path.
- Web and mobile clients against the new server.

## Risk and security impact

The change is limited to the send queue of the WebRTC data channels. It does not touch permissions, IPC, the filesystem, persistence or the trust boundary. Risk: slower large transfers on a link with a high bandwidth-delay product, if Chromium counted in-flight bytes in `bufferedAmount`. This is not confirmed.

body:
Fixes #3

Tests added
- Order history sorts the sample dates in newest-first calendar order.
- February date filtering excludes January and March orders.
- A string settlement amount updates Meera’s `totalSettled` numerically to 1,700 and balance to ₹732.01.

Cause
Order dates and date-picker values were compared as `DD/MM/YYYY` strings, so both sorting and date-range filtering used day-first lexical order. Settlement handling added the browser’s string amount directly to the numeric `totalSettled`, concatenating the values.

Fix
Compare order dates using normalized `YYYY-MM-DD` keys for sorting and filtering. Convert settlement amount to a number once before validation, ledger arithmetic, and storing the settlement entry.

Test result
`node --test` — 3 tests passed. The temporary app reproduced the reported bad values before the fix.

author: anthonylim24
body:
Follow-up to #621: closes the known gaps that PR listed.

## What changes

**Near-duplicate venues** (`server/src/trips/sameVenue.ts`)
- "Leeum Museum" and "Leeum Museum of Art" are now one venue. Names are compared word by word, in order, ignoring case, accents, punctuation, spacing and filler words. A longer name matches when it only adds words for the kind of place ("museum", "market", "palace", …). Bracketed names count as other names for the same venue ("Gyeongbokgung Palace (경복궁)").
- Words that name a different place keep venues apart, as do different numbers: "Lotte World" vs "Lotte World Tower", "Seoul Tower" vs "Seoul Station", "Myeongdong" vs "Myeongdong Kyoja", "Stop 1-2" vs "Stop 2-1".
- When both stops have pins, the pins must agree: within 1 km for the same name, 400 m for a near name. So two branches of a chain far apart are two stops.
- One rule for every path: the review's accepted adds, the wishlist list the model sees, matching a plain add to a saved idea, `/apply` (now for every add, not only wishlist adds), and the draft's cross-day dedup.

**Private details stay out of prompts** (`server/src/trips/privateText.ts`)
- What the traveller wrote is redacted before the review, the draft or the concierge sees it. That covers the description, stop notes, day theme, callouts, journal, wishlist notes, open to-dos and addresses.
- Booking codes, emails, and phone, card and passport numbers become `[code]`, `[email]` or `[number]`. Flight and train numbers, dates, times, prices and street numbers stay.
- Model text that repeats a placeholder is never saved (`fromModel`), so a note the model echoes back can't overwrite the real code. This covers wishlist adds, edits, plain adds, draft stops and concierge adds.
- On the real Korea seed: 3 of 283 texts change (the flight confirmation code twice and one booking email), with no false positives. The confirmation code is absent from the built review prompt.
- **Behaviour change:** the concierge can no longer quote a booking code or phone number from a stop's notes, because it now sees the placeholder.

**A scheduled wishlist idea stays scheduled** (`tripMerge.ts`, `editorMachine.ts`, `PATCH /api/trips/:id`)
- A stop is on a day or on the wishlist, never both. The scenario: you press Stop, edit a wishlist idea, and the review finishes on the server and schedules that idea. Before, the client merge let your edit beat the delete, and the idea came back next to its stop.
- Now the stop stays on its day and your edits to the idea move onto it (`scheduledOnce`).
- Undo and Redo (`replayPlan`, which merges the wishlist outside `mergeTrip`) follow the same rule.
- The server's save drops any idea whose id is already on a day (`withoutScheduledIdeas`), so an older client can't bring one back either.
- The new merge and editor tests fail without the fix and pass with it.

## Gaps from #621

| Gap | Status | Evidence |
|---|---|---|
| Near-duplicate venue names | Fixed | `sameVenue.test.ts`, review tests; a real review on a Seoul trip added nothing twice |
| Trip description (with the Korea confirmation code) reaches the model | Fixed | `privateText.test.ts`; review prompt test; Korea seed check |
| An edit after Stop brings a scheduled idea back | Fixed | `tripMerge.test.ts`, `editorMachine.test.ts` (conflict, external change, Undo / Redo), route test |
| `trip_review_enqueue`'s jsonb through PostgREST untested | Verified | Live test below: 202 with the run, 409 with the live run, no row for the rejected id |
| Restart recovery tested only by unit and SQL tests | Verified | Live test below: `kill -9` and SIGTERM both recover, trip written once |

## Testing
- `bun run typecheck:server`; `bun test --parallel --bail server/src`: 808 pass, 4 skip, 0 fail
- `frontend`: typecheck, lint (0 errors), `test:run` (2569 pass), build
- Real review: in-memory store, real Gemini 4 Neon, `api-review` launch config. A Seoul trip whose notes, wishlist and description held a booking ref, a confirmation number, a phone number, a PNR and an email.
  - Completed in 110 s on attempt 1.
  - Every code survived in the traveller's text, and no placeholder was saved.
  - Both wishlist ideas were scheduled and left the wishlist; no venue appears twice.
- **Live queue test** against a real local stack: Postgres 15.8 and PostgREST 12.2.3 in Docker, `supabase/schema.sql` plus the queue migration (re-applying it is a no-op). The real server ran with an env file that held only local Supabase values and the Gemini key; before each start, a check printed the Supabase host as `127.0.0.1`.
  - **Enqueue:** `POST /enhance` returned 202 in 22 ms with `queue` read back from the database. PostgREST returned the jsonb `{inserted, doc}` as a bare object. A second POST while the run was live returned 409 with the live run.
  - **Grants:** anon calling `trip_review_claim` was refused (42501), service_role was allowed, and the revoked helper `trip_review_held` returned 403.
  - **`kill -9` 20 s into attempt 1:** after a restart, the lease lapsed and a sweep reclaimed the run 6 s later (attempt 2/3, 76 s after the kill). It heartbeat every 30 s and completed with 11 stops added. The trip was written once, and the killed process wrote nothing.
  - **SIGTERM 20 s in:** the process exited within 0.5 s, inside PM2's window. The claim was released with no attempt spent (`queued`, attempts 0, no `trip_review_fail`). After a restart, the boot sweep claimed it as attempt 1/3 and it completed.
  - **What clients read:** `GET /enhancements` and `GET /enhancements/:id` return the runs with `queue {state: "done", attempt}`. The rejected run never appears.
- The live test showed that a SIGTERM drain logged "The AI took too long to answer". It now logs the worker's reason (`review stopped: drain`).

No screenshots: nothing visible changes. `tripMerge.ts` and `editorMachine.ts` are merge logic only.

## Summary
Add a GitHub Actions workflow lockfile (`.github/workflows/actions.lock`).

## Why
Workflow lockfiles became generally available on 2026-10-28. With a lockfile, each action runs the commit SHA recorded in it, even if the tag is moved later. This protects CI and release workflows from supply-chain attacks through retagged actions.

## What
- Generate `.github/workflows/actions.lock` with `gh actions-lock`. It covers `ci.yml` and `tagpr.yml`.
- `gh actions-lock` also pinned the `uses` refs to exact patch versions (e.g. `actions/checkout@v4` → `@v4.4.0`).

## Notes for reviewers
- The lockfile is machine-generated. Do not edit it by hand; run `gh actions-lock` to update it after changing actions.
- `gh actions-lock --verify` passes locally.
- No CI verification job is added in this PR.

## References
- https://github.blog/changelog/2026-10-28-github-actions-workflow-lockfiles-are-generally-available
- https://docs.github.com/en/actions/concepts/security/workflow-dependency-lockfiles

author: haaris-usman-saeed
reaperhulk
body:
This PR is independent of the other ARM deduplication PRs (#6114–#6118 and #6128). It shares no files with them.

## What was duplicated

`r2Squares` is the step of the R² mod m computation that comes after the doublings. It runs six Montgomery squarings, taking `2^(65 w)` to `R² mod m`. Until now it inlined its square six times everywhere R² mod m is computed on ARMv7:

- RSA's private and public precomputations
- FFDH's domain and private-key checks
- RSA key generation's candidate
- DSA's probable-prime test

That covers both the base and `_umaal` variants of each. Each inlined square is about 135–345 lines.

## Lean change

- `Impl/Bignum/Arm/R2.lean`: `r2Squares` now keeps its count in header byte 208, the same word `doubleLoop` counts its doublings in, which the doublings leave at zero. It sets the count with `r2SquareCount` (`mov r1, #6; str r1, [r0, #208]`), then loops over one squaring followed by `doubleCount` (`r2SquareStep`).
- `Proof/Bignum/Arm/R2.lean`: `SqC` is the squarings' state with that count, and holds its value only under `P`. The new lemmas are `sqC_square_ok`, `sqC_step_ok`, `r2SquareCount_ok`, `sqC_loop_ok` (by `WP.loop`) and `sqC_squares_ok`. `r2Squares_ok` now follows from `sqC_squares_ok` with its statement unchanged.
- `Proof/Bignum/Arm/R2CT.lean`: `sqC_squares_ct` proves constant time (by `RelCT.loop`, as `doubleLoop_ct` does). `r2Squares_ct` now follows from it with its statement unchanged.
- `Proof/Bignum/Arm/PrimeR2From{,CT}.lean`: the fold's `foldSquares6_ok` and `foldSquares6_ct` (`FoldSq`) now go through the same lemmas, with `P` the fold's condition. The six-step proofs and `foldSquare_ok`/`foldSquare_ct` are removed.
- `Proof/RsaKeyGen/Arm/Search/Verified.lean`: `r2SquareStep` is added to a `simp` list.

No changes to `TCB/` or `Spec/`. All the changes are ARMv7-only Bignum code; no other target changes.

## Assembly

The arm crate's `assembly/` goes from 1,353,736 to 1,294,608 lines, a drop of 59,128. The biggest changes:

| function | before | after |
|---|--:|--:|
| `vg_rsa_private_precompute` | 15,607 | 7,017 |
| `vg_rsa_public_precompute` | 2,777 | 1,059 |
| `vg_ffdh_check_domain` | 10,985 | 5,831 |
| `vg_ffdh_check_private` | 9,540 | 7,822 |

author: oscarhkli
body:
## Why

The 14 routes were hand-written handlers that serialized engine values directly, so nothing checked a response against the OpenAPI spec at compile time. Story 05 also cannot delete the engine's hand-written JSON code while server tests still encode and decode engine models.

## What

- `server/api_server.go`: `Handler` implements the generated `api.StrictServerInterface`, one typed method per route. Mappers turn engine values into the generated wire types, so the compiler checks every success response against the spec. `server/http_handlers.go` is deleted and `server/routes.go` registers the generated routes.
- Same checks in the same order as before (body, token, team, room). Same URLs, status codes, error texts and `Location` header.
- `engine.Archetype.PresetSkills.Names()` is new (the skill names, Jump before Fly, never nil).
- Every server test now goes through the full mux with wire types, so no server test touches an engine model's JSON code.
- `.golangci.yml` allows the generated response interfaces in `ireturn`. `docs/design.md` describes the mapped wire types.

Behaviour changes, for callers other than the browser's own requests:

- Response bytes change (the fields and values do not): alphabetical keys, a trailing newline, `<`, `>` and `&` escaped, because the generated writers use `encoding/json` v1.
- `allowed-tiles?unitId=1&unitId=2` answers `400 Invalid unitId parameter` (the first value used to win). `unitId=%2B16` answers `200` for unit 16 (it used to be `400`).
- `units`, `bombs` and `softBlocks` in `GET /state` come in ID order, not map order.
- Server logs: one `Warn` per error response (method, route pattern, status) replaces the per-route messages.
- A marshal failure answers `500 internal error`. The old handler wrote `200` and then `Failed to encode response`.
- Exported API: `Names` on `engine.Archetype.PresetSkills`, and the 14 route methods on `server.Handler` (the generated interface requires them to be exported).

## Scope

In: the 14 routes, the mappers, the tests, the lint entry, the design note. Out: the spec, the web client, `docs/frontend/`, deleting the engine's JSON code (story 05).

## Tradeoffs

- `runtime.SetJSONCodec` (the process-wide request decoder, set to `encoding/json/v2` so key case, duplicate keys and trailing data stay rejected) is called once at package init, through `var _ = installStrictCodec()` in `server/routes.go`. The setter is an unsynchronised write, so calling it from `RegisterRoutes` would race when two goroutines register routes. A package-level `sync.Once` trips `gochecknoglobals`, `init()` trips `gochecknoinits`, and the plan allows no `nolint`.
- Errors stay on `http.Error`, never the generated `...TextResponse` types (wrong headers). The validator rig checks error statuses, not the compiler.

## Verification

- `make lint`: 0 issues, no `nolint`. `make pre-push` (gen-check, lint, test, web-lint, web-test): pass. `make gen-check`: pass, spec untouched. `make test`: pass. `go test ./server ./engine ./room ./cmd/srpg-web -race -count=1`: pass.
- `TestRegisterRoutesConcurrent` calls `RegisterRoutes` from two goroutines: it reports a data race under `-race` when the codec is set inside `RegisterRoutes`, and passes with the init-time install.
- `make web-e2e`: 33 passed. `make image-smoke`: `smoke-ok`.
- Greps: `grep -c 'operationId:' server/api/openapi.yaml` prints `14`; `grep -c 'm.HandleFunc' server/api/api.gen.go` prints `14`; `grep -c 'mux.HandleFunc' server/routes.go` prints `0`. The old-code grep (`handleError|writeJSON|requireToken|requireRoom|testMux|h\.handle` over `server/`) prints nothing and exits 1; `server/http_handlers.go` is gone. Both engine-model greps over `server/*_test.go` print nothing. `Test Contract` appears 12 times over 4 files.
- Tests first: the decoding, check-order, query and error-shape tests were written and passed on the old handlers before the switch, so they prove the new server keeps the old behaviour.
- Equivalence run (scratch, not committed): states, configs, the catalog and the events of each resolve from 4 played matches (Plain and Divided, with and without sudden death; moves, bombs, explosions, soft blocks, deaths, a match end) match the engine marshaller after sorting entity arrays by `id`. 40 state and event comparisons, 30 repeats, no difference.
- Mutation proofs, each reverted: nil `units` fails the validator rig (not nullable). Dropping `affectedPositions` fails the byte table and the equivalence run, and the rig passes, as the spec does not require it. Removing the `SetJSONCodec` call fails the new decoding tables (5 cases of `TestSurrenderRequestDecoding` flip). Removing the turn-command `unitId` range check fails its table. Removing the query guard fails the allowed-tiles table. Swapping `x` and `y` in the coordinate mapper fails the byte table and the equivalence run.
- Not run: nothing skipped.

## For the human: `AGENTS.md` replacement

`AGENTS.md` is gitignored, so this PR does not touch it. Replace the "Empty Slices vs nil" section with:

> Every array field in a response is always present and never `null`: the client calls array methods unguarded. Hand-written Go imports `encoding/json/v2` only, which writes a nil slice as `[]`. Never put `omitempty` or `omitzero` on a slice or map field, use `*[]T`, or pass `json.FormatNilSliceAsNull`. A generated file may use v1 only while the raw-bytes response check passes.

## What changed

- `tools/gen_routes.py` writes `Data/Routes.lua` (facts only: skill ranges, spell ids, alt flag, faction) for six crafting professions. Enchanting and Engineering pages don't parse yet, so they have no route.
- Planner rule 9: where the guide covers a skill level, the planner chooses only among the guide's recipes for that level (main pick plus alternatives, faction-filtered). Prices, stock, p90 sizing and earmarks still decide between them. Uncovered or greyed levels fall back to the old optimizer and are marked "Off guide: <reason>". User swaps and exclusions still win. A guide main pick's pattern is bought regardless; an alternative's pattern must save more than it costs.
- Faction rows count only when the player's side is known. `/skillup cost` applies the same faction filter as the planner.
- The card shows Guide / guide alt / Off guide. `selftest.route` reports `skillLines` and `rows`. `/skillup guide on|off` (slash only).

luacheck 0 warnings, busted 717/0, stylua clean (run with `-Remote parogdev@parogdev-pc`), python 56 OK. body: ## Request Take "Give Mesh Tools" out: mesh tools shouldn't be something any chat can be given. Meta should have them natively. ## Changes ### Session menu: no Give Mesh Tools (desktop and phone) | Before | After | |---|---| | | | | | | **Shown:** a host chat's right-click menu on Baude (top) and its long-press menu on the phone (bottom): Rename…, Make Bot…, Move to Group, Archive, Move to Trash…. **Before:** both menus had Give Mesh Tools (Remove Mesh Tools once given) on every chat that could be a Bot. The `mesh_tools` op, its reply, the Session listing's `mesh_tools` field and the two copy keys are gone. A host gives the mesh's tools to a Bot's agent and to a head's Meta (a chat started with the head's own tools), and to no other chat. The phone as a host gives them to its Bots only; before, every chat on the phone had them. A chat given them before this keeps them until its agent next starts, then runs without them. ### Meta has the mesh's tools (desktop and phone) | Before | After | |---|---| | | | | | | **Shown:** Meta's page with a reply whose calls listed the mesh's hosts and started a subagent on workshop (new parity scene `panel-meta-mesh`): the cards read Hosts and Start subagent, on Baude and on the phone. **Before:** Meta had no mesh tools; a card for one would have read "Mcp mesh hosts". Baude's and Record's Meta run `baude_headless.py mesh-tools` beside their own relay (Claude Code, pi and Codex; not Apple's on-device models, whose small window they'd crowd and which name tools by server). The phone's Meta gets them from the host it runs on. They are never asked about, as a Bot's aren't, and Meta's prompt says what they do and that they have no undo. Desktop Meta's server runs with `--as-meta` and `--socket` (this user's host process, computed in the app, so Codex's cleared environment still finds it). What it sends is from a chat named Meta, as the phone's Meta's is from its chat "Meta": `input`, `start` and `relay` take `as_meta`, and the host labels the message with Meta's sender. A subagent Meta starts is held to Auto at most, as a Bot's and the phone Meta's are. ### Spec - `schema/ui/README.md`: a `removed` field, `{name, apps, why, decided}`, for parts taken out on purpose. - `SessionRowMenu.menu.json`: the Mesh tools item is gone and listed under `removed` for `baude` and `phone`. - `Meta.panel.json`: Meta's mesh tools and how their cards are titled. - `schema/types`: MeshTools.request and MeshToolsSet.reply deleted; `Session.mesh_tools` removed. `schema/copy/sidebar.json`: `give_mesh_tools` and `remove_mesh_tools` removed. ## Verification The phone's screenshot rig gains `09c-home-session-menu` (a chat's long-press menu); `tap` takes `long = true`, and `layOut()` lays out every window so a menu opened with nothing else changing gets placed and drawn. author: fastsnowy
body:
## 概要
`pnpm audit` で検出された脆弱性17件（Critical 2 / High 2 / Moderate 12 / Low 1）を依存更新で解消し、あわせてコード側のセキュリティ対策を行いました。詳細は `docs/security-review.md` の 2026-11-22 節に記載しています。

## 依存関係
- Next.js 16.4.0 → **16.4.6**（画像最適化API・`use cache` のRCE、Server ActionsのDoS ほか）
- React / React DOM 19.3.1、eslint-config-next 16.4.6、Radix UI・Supabase JS・Tailwind ほかを互換範囲内で更新
- Zod 3 → **4.6.7**（メモリ枯渇の脆弱性）。使っていたのは `vote-input.ts` だけ
- 開発依存経由の `minimatch` と間接依存の `zod` は overrides で修正版に固定
- 未使用の依存を削除：Hono、`@conform-to/*`、`uuid`、`@types/uuid`、`react-number-format`、`supazod`
- Biome・Supabase CLI・`@types/canvas-confetti` を devDependencies へ移動
- `pnpm-workspace.yaml` を追加
  - pnpm 12 は `package.json` の `pnpm.overrides` を読まないため、overrides をこちらへ移動
  - `allowBuilds`：インストールスクリプトを実行するのは esbuild だけ
  - `minimumReleaseAge: 1440`：公開から1日未満のバージョンは使わない（サプライチェーン対策）

## コード
- **未使用の公開API `/api/[[...route]]`（Hono）を削除**：認証なしで呼べるのに、サーバーの `ANNICT_TOKEN` を使って Annict に問い合わせていた。アプリからは参照されていない
- **外部URLの検証**：Annict の公式サイト・画像URLは http(s) のみ許可、X のユーザー名は形式を検証、CSS の `url()` には引用符を付けて埋め込む（`src/lib/safe-url.ts`、`src/lib/annict-works.ts`）
- **Annict 取得処理をまとめた**：重複していた処理を `server-only` の1か所に集約し、トークン未設定の検知・タイムアウト・リダイレクト禁止・レスポンス形式の検証を追加
- **認証リダイレクト**：`/auth/callback` と `/auth/confirm` のリダイレクト先を、リクエストの Host ではなく `APP_URL` から組み立てる。`/auth/confirm` では `next` と OTP 種別も検証する。プロバイダーのエラー文言はURLに載せず、固定のエラーコードだけを渡す
- **投票削除**：`created_id` をUUIDとして検証。取得時も `user_id` で絞り込み、ログに出すのはエラーコードだけにした
- 結果ページ：Annict に問い合わせる作品IDの重複を除き、不要なマッピング処理を削除

## プライバシーポリシーと pnpm（追加コミット）
- **プライバシーポリシーを改訂**：実装と照らし合わせて書き直した。取得項目、Vercel Web Analytics、共有URLで公開される情報、ローカルストレージ、国外サーバーでの処理、第三者提供、退会時のデータの扱いを明記。最終更新日は 2026年11月22日
- **Annict プロフィールの最小化**：Annict の `/v1/me` はメールアドレスや記録数・通知数も返すが、`/api/annict-userinfo` はそれを全部 Supabase に渡していた。ID・ユーザー名・表示名・アバター・メールアドレスだけを渡すように変更
- **pnpm を 12.22.0 に固定**：`packageManager` と `.mise.toml` で指定。pnpm 10 から実行しても 12.22.0 に自動で切り替わることを確認
- Next.js は最新の安定版 16.4.6（16.5 はまだ canary）

## 確認したこと
- [x] `pnpm test`：11件すべて成功（URL検証・Annictデータの整形・UUID検証の回帰テストを追加）
- [x] `pnpm typecheck`
- [x] `pnpm build`
- [x] `pnpm audit`：脆弱性 0件
- [x] pnpm 10 でも `--frozen-lockfile` でインストールできる
- [ ] 全体の lint：既存のエラー8件が残っている。今回変更したファイルにエラーはない

## 注意点
- `/api/annict/:season` と `/api/server/misskey` は廃止しました。外部から使っている場合は知らせてください

body:
Refs #325. Stacked on #675 (per-drive scan timeout), which is stacked on #647.

## What was wrong

The drive card's settings offered four "prescan" overrides. After #675 the ripper reads one of them, the scan timeout. The other three were never read by anything in the backend or ripper:

- **Pre-scan Cache** (`prescan_cache_mb`): the scan hard-codes `--cache=1`;
- **Pre-scan Retries** (`prescan_retries`): the scan's not-ready retry count is fixed;
- **Enum Timeout** (`disc_enum_timeout`): v3 opens the drive as `dev:<path>` and never enumerates `disc:9999`, so there's nothing for it to limit.

Their "global defaults" (1 / 3 / 60) came from `arm_config.PRESCAN_*` keys that don't exist. Whatever an operator saved changed nothing.

These came over from the neu fork, where they drove its MakeMKV prescan loop. A check against hifi's scan logs and the fork's history found nothing to support wiring them up in v3.

## Change

- **API:** the three fields leave `DriveView` and `DriveUpdateRequest`. A PATCH that sends one now gets 422 (`extra="forbid"`), the same as any unknown field.
- **Drive card:** only the scan timeout is left in the settings panel. The "N custom" chip now counts only that override.
- **Database:** the columns stay on the model, marked unused, until a migration drops them. No migration is in this PR.
- **API files:** the OpenAPI snapshot and `api.gen.ts` are regenerated.

Not in this PR:
- `uhd_capable` and `rip_speed` are also unread. `rip_speed` gets wired up (it's useful per drive, but needs hardware testing).
- `uhd_capable` is left for a decision.

## Testing

- Backend: the drive view no longer carries the three fields, and a PATCH with any of them is refused.
- UI: the settings panel shows only the scan timeout and none of the removed inputs. The override chip counts the timeout. The existing per-field tests (bounds, save on blur, sync while closed, typed text kept) now cover the timeout.
- ruff, mypy, backend + ripper pytest (coverage 99%), UI format / lint / lint:styles / svelte-check / vitest: clean.

author: thecruzcontroll
body:
## Why

Every CI run started 28 jobs, and about 20 run at once across all pull requests. Docs-only pull requests and every merge to `main` ran the full set, so runs queued behind each other and the post-deploy check waited in the same queue.

## What changes

A first job, `Scope of the run`, runs `scripts/ci-scope.ts` and answers `light` or `full`.

A run is light when:

- every changed path is docs, the plan, agent tooling, root Markdown or `.env.example`, or
- the push to `main` is a merge onto the previous tip whose tree equals the merged pull request head's tree. That pull request's run already tested the same tree.

A light run skips the integration tests, the 20 e2e legs and both Lighthouse jobs: 24 of 28 jobs. Lint and type-check, unit tests (which hold the docs guards) and the build always run.

## Required checks stay honest

The three aggregate checks pass a skipped job only when the scope job succeeded and answered `light` explicitly. A failed, cancelled or silent scope job fails them. The script answers `full` whenever it cannot tell, and never fails. `scripts/ci-workflow.test.ts` checks every combination of results and scopes.

## Review

Reviewer verdict: approve. Fixed from the review: the milestone verifier and `pnpm e2e:timings` looked for e2e results in `main`'s runs, which are light now, so both point at the pull request head's run. A light merge must also have the previous tip as its first parent.

## Proof

This pull request changes the workflow, so its own run is full and exercises the full path. The light path is first exercised by the next docs-only pull request and by this pull request's merge to `main`.

author: cafxx
body:
## Summary

MySQL 8.4/9.7 exposes a context-specific result type for grouped integer expressions: signed TINYINT/SMALLINT/MEDIUMINT ADD and MOD keys such as `s % 2`, `ti % 2`, `mi % 2`, and `s + s` are reported as INT (`MYSQL_TYPE_LONG`), while the same expressions in a plain projection are BIGINT (`MYSQL_TYPE_LONGLONG`). Storing BIGINT made the materialized reader's result metadata differ from the original grouped query.

- Add a deliberately narrow inference rule only when the selected expression AST exactly matches a GROUP BY expression, for the measured signed narrow-integer ADD/MOD shapes and MySQL 8.4/9.7.
- Keep MariaDB's separate display-length inference unchanged. Unsigned, multiplication, casts, other versions, and unknown shapes retain the existing conservative inference.
- Remove the strict expected-failure markers for the four native group-key regressions.
- Add offline plan guards for MySQL 8.4/9.7 and wider-type controls, plus a native MySQL test comparing full scans with forced generated-column-index scans to check metadata/value stability across access paths.
- Update the corresponding TODO item.

## Validation

- The local container cannot resolve GitHub and has no configured MySQL server, so local Python/native test execution was not possible.
- Exact-head GitHub Actions CI is the validation gate; results will be checked and any failures corrected.

Not merged; no auto-merge enabled.

author: ashtonian
body:
Batch #274 of #283: patch policy, validators and the affected-path list now judge what an operation writes, and the apply engine, value validation, path set and relation renderer each have one owner. One commit per unit, in the issue's order, then #284, then a merge of main and a one-line lint cleanup.

Closes #274. Closes #284. Lands #209's patch half.

| Unit | Commit |
|---|---|
| 1 | Policy, validators and `AffectedPaths` read an operation's writes: a whole value writes everything below it, a merge the members it names, a remove null whatever value it carries, a move its source. The eight trigger rows and an operation × ancestor/exact/descendant table pin it. |
| 2 | `NewPatchPolicyConstraints(ForbidPaths, ConstrainValues, ValidateWith)` checks every pattern and regexp at construction; the token matcher moves into `patch`, `**` is zero or more tokens anywhere, specificity counts tokens. `PolicySubject` moves too. |
| 3 | `patch.Applier[T]` owns the Go-value apply engine; parsers mark the `ParsedPatch` they produce, and `Applier`, `BuildPatchSQL` and policy refuse one without the mark (`ErrUnparsed`) instead of panicking. `JSONEqual` moves to `core`. Go-apply vs SQLite differential in `patch`. |
| 4 | `typedParser` folds into `Resource`; `WithPaths` copies the resource and swaps two schemas. |
| 5 | One `checkValue` step for both wire formats, error texts pinned by tests added first; `Validator` / `ConstraintError` move to `patch`; a nil schema is an error. |
| 6 | `NewPatchSchema` owns a versioned, immutable path set; `AddPath`, `Path`, `Paths`; `ValidPatchOps` becomes `IsValidOp` / `Ops`. |
| 7 | `MaxRelationValues` (1,000) with E2119 at parse, keys deduplicated; one delete and one insert builder binding owners and values as one array each. Executed cases on SQLite and PostgreSQL, including 4 owners × 1,000 keys. |
| 8 | `EstimatedCost`, the schema-not-found alias and the unreachable merge fold are gone; a catalog test provokes every `patch.Codes()` entry. |
| 9 | Relation values are decided at parse: null key E2118, merge null is the clear, add/remove need a key, nullable key types refused. TS validator and the shared corpus agree. |
| #284 | A writable relation's keys take the target key's wire form. |
| 10 | Object merge into a PostgreSQL `json` column. |
| 11 | Deterministic first failure of a typed struct merge. |
| 12 | `json.RawMessage` member of a declared document merges. |
| 13 | `checkJSONMembers` checks the codec's encoding; `omitempty` differential. |

Decisions and departures from the issue text:

- Unit 9 takes the issue's default: a merge-patch null on a relation (and a JSON Patch `replace` with null) is the clear. The schema document's `nullable: true` for relation paths is therefore correct and unchanged.
- The `Codes()` catalog test, listed under unit 7's acceptance, lands in unit 8's commit: the one code nothing could provoke was the alias unit 8 deletes, so unit 7's commit would not have passed.
- Without a target table, PostgreSQL cannot type `unnest($n)` in an `INSERT … SELECT`, and casting by the key's Go type breaks a `string` key of a `uuid` column. That insert reads its rows as the pair table's row type, `jsonb_populate_recordset(NULL::<pair table>, $n)`; record members use the column name folded to lower case, as unquoted identifiers are. #278's quoting changes that fold to the exact name. Deletes and the target-table insert use `= ANY($n)`, typed by the column.
- `patch.NewApplier` takes the generator and parser config, not the schemas: nothing in it reads them yet. #279's refusal of another resource's patch can add them.
- The TypeScript validator does not check `max_relation_values` client-side; that would touch `types.ts`, which #277 owns. The server enforces it.
- Unit 13's `omitempty` differential found no disagreement: in Go 1.27 `reflect.Value.IsZero` treats `-0` as zero, as encoding/json does.
- E2117 is reachable only through a hand-built schema that allows other operations on a relation path; the catalog test provokes it that way.
- Outside the batch's Owns line, by necessity: the `JSONEqual` lines in `filter/README.md` and `docs/queries.md`; root tests that used `AllowedPaths` or the old policy literal; `client_conformance_test.go` classifying the new corpus cases; the schema-document fixture gaining a quoted-key writable relation; `registry.go` serving `max_relation_values`.

Breaking changes, for the release entry:

- `ParsedPatch.PolicyConstraints` and `EstimatedCost` are gone; `AuditInfo` has no `estimated_cost`; `PatchOperation.Value` is nil for remove, move and copy; `AffectedPaths` omits test paths and includes move sources.
- `PatchPolicyConstraints` is opaque, built with `NewPatchPolicyConstraints`; `NewValueConstraint` is gone; `PatchPolicyFromWritableFields` returns an error.
- `core.MatchWildcard`, `core.PolicySubject` (now `patch.PolicySubject`), `core.Validator`, `core.ConstraintError`, `core.NewConstraintError` (now in `patch`) and `filter.JSONEqual` (now `core.JSONEqual`) moved or were removed; a trailing `**` matches its parent.
- `patch.ValidateTransferValue`, `ServerFieldName`, `PathSchema.ClearedValue`, `ValidPatchOps`, `ECodePatchSchemaNotFound` and `PatchSchema.AllowedPaths` are gone; build schemas with `NewPatchSchema`. A hand-built `ParsedPatch` is `ErrUnparsed`.
- `RenderRelationOp` takes a `patch.SQLDialect` and binds sets as arrays; `RelationPath` takes the keys' wire and returns an error.
- A relation operation naming more than 1,000 distinct keys is E2119; a relation add/remove with no keys, or a null key, is E2118 at parse; quoted target keys travel as JSON strings.

Test plan, run locally:

- `go test -race -tags=unit ./parse/...`
- `go test -race -tags=integration ./parse/...` against PostgreSQL/PostGIS (`make parse-postgres-up`, `PARSE_REQUIRE_PG=1`)
- `go vet` and staticcheck v0.8.2 on `parse` with both tags
- `make test-parse-sdk` with the pinned pnpm 12.18.0: typecheck, compat, lint, 317 tests including the new relation corpus cases, build
- Checked failing without the fix: unit 1's tests at `c6b2466` (a worktree of the base), unit 7's argument growth on the old renderer, unit 10's SQLSTATE 42883 with the cast removed, and the determinism tests with the specificity sort removed

author: lauppv
body:
## Why

A scraper has been visiting every 1-2 minutes since 2026-11-21: a real Chrome, a new home IP (Comcast, Verizon, Virgin Media...) for each page, a Mac or Windows user agent, no referrer. It passes the bot check and Cloudflare, and it made today's chart show 342 visits. It only loads pages: no press, no key, no scroll by hand.

## What

A guest now counts with the people only once they do something. The rest are counted apart.

- **Browser** (`useGuestSteps`): once a page, the first trusted `pointerdown`, `keydown`, `wheel` or `touchstart` queues `active`. It goes with the steps or the next page report. `scroll` doesn't count, since a script can scroll, and a lesson scrolls in its panel, not the window. Events made by scripts (`isTrusted` false) are ignored.
- **API**: `guest_visits.active`. A report with `active: true` sets it, and so does a `click` step, for an app still cached from before. `POST /api/visits/steps` now also takes `{ steps: [], active: true }`, but never an empty report.
- **Counts** (`totalsFrom`): a visitor counts with the people when they were signed in at some point that day, or their guest visit is active. The join with `guest_visits` happens before the roll-up blanks the hash. Everything else, meaning visitors, views, pages, sources, guests/signed in and languages, comes from people only. The rest roll up as the new dimension `idle`.
- **Guest list, top clicks, placement funnel**: active visits only. The list says how many it left out.
- **Admin page**: a third chart, "Without interaction a day", under new accounts, with a line that explains it. It follows the same point picked as the other two.
- **Migration** `20261122120000_add_guest_visit_active`: the column, plus a backfill. Existing visits become active when they have a click, a scroll or more than one page. Today's numbers are still live, so they come out clean right away. Days already rolled up stay as they were.

## Edge cases covered

- A guest who looks around, signs up and goes on signed in counts as a person (same hash, `bool_or(signed_in)`).
- A signed-in student counts without doing anything.
- A guest becomes a person from their first action, and then all their pages that day count, the earlier ones too.
- The active report reaches the server after the page report: by timer at 10s, on hide, or with the next page. So the visit already exists when it arrives.
- A scraper that scrolls by script (window and lesson panel) stays idle. Checked in Chromium.
- Signed-in reports with `active` mark the guest visit they had before sign-up.
- A guest with no visit today: the active report is dropped, nothing breaks.
- An app still cached from before: clicks still mark the visit active. A guest who only reads on an old app counts as idle until it reloads.

## Checked

- Unit tests: 4199 passed (UI + API + packages), including the new ones for the hook (trusted vs untrusted events, once a page, sending), the schema, the service, the repository, the chart and the list.
- Integration (`test:integration`, visits): scrapers kept out of every number and the list but counted as `idle`; a guest becoming a person; a student and a guest who signs up; the roll-up writing `idle` before the hashes go.
- The migration's backfill run on sample rows (click / scroll / two pages / one page), then rolled back.
- Browser (Playwright, local API on the test DB): a scraper that loads a lesson and scrolls by script stays `active = f`; a reader who uses the wheel and a visitor who presses Tab and moves on become `active = t`. The admin page shows 2 visitors, 2 without interaction, and the list says 2 are not listed.
- Lint, typecheck, format check.
- Not run locally: the full coverage suite and e2e (CI).

## Not changed

- Locally, `keeps a guest's pages ... from its first page's time` fails the same way on `main`: the local Postgres puts `started_at` in Romania's time zone. It is not related to this change.

author: nickradford
body:
Closes #2.

## Why
The app knew which app came forward and whether modifiers were held, but not which key was pressed, and it forgot everything between events. Exact hit detection (#3) and later coaching features need both.

## What changed
- `CoachCore/KeyPress.swift`: a HID usage → Carbon keycode table, and `classifyKey(keyCode:held:bindings:)` → `.bound(Binding)`, `.unbound`, `.commandTab`, or nil to drop. A key is dropped unless the held modifiers are exactly some binding's, so typing never gets past this function. Command-Tab and Command-Shift-Tab count as the app switcher.
- `HyperKeyListener`: same IOHIDManager. A non-hyper key-down is classified and kept as `lastPress` with its HID timestamp; dropped keys are never stored.
- `CoachCore/History.swift`: `SwitchRecord { bundleID, outcome: hit/miss/unbound, method: hotkey/commandTab/other, at }`, capped at 30 days and 5,000 records (about 0.5 MB).
- `switchOutcome` / `switchMethod` share one definition of "a user switch" with `missedBinding`. Quit/hide activations are not recorded.
- `HistoryFile`: JSON at `~/Library/Application Support/<bundle id>/history.json`, loaded at launch (missing or corrupt starts empty), written atomically after each switch.
- README Permission section and the onboarding Input Monitoring step say what is read and stored, and what is not.

## Scope
No visible change: `missedBinding`, the flash and the guide behave as before.

## Tradeoffs
- ISO-only keys are not in the table, so they are dropped.
- For a non-hyper binding, modifiers are read when the key's callback runs; a near-simultaneous modifier and letter could read without the modifier (not measured).

Kafka events are external input to this context (CloudEvents published by other contexts): their ids, types, subjects, keys, payload fields and the decode / validation / use-case errors raised while handling them can carry CR/LF and forge log lines (CodeQL `go/log-injection` class). Every slog attribute whose value can carry event-derived text now passes through the package CR/LF sanitizer (errors as their sanitized text). author: maf38
body:
## What this is

The bench that the definition of done needs: the grid of the 21 cases, and the means to play a case again and again without anyone.

- **`docs/CASE-GRID.md`**: the status of each case of `docs/USE-CASES.md` (what the table does today, what is planted, whether a replayable scenario exists), what "ticked" means, and what the grid shows about the structure (only pull-request rows are actionable; the repair policy is narrower than the cases; the table keeps its reading for five minutes).
- **`lab/sandbox.sh`**: `status`, `mark-seed`, `reset`, `plant`. A reset restores the seed tree of a test-bed repository **through a pull request** that passes its checks (the repository rules are never touched), and leaves a bot's pull requests alone.
- **`lab/e2e/run-scenario.cjs` + `lab/scenarios/CASE-01.json`**: plays a case the way the maintainer does (reset, plant, sign in, fresh reading of the table, tick, validate, follow the missions) and reads the final state on the forge. Exit code 0 only when every expectation holds.

## Demo

CASE-01 ticked for real, by the runner alone: reset, plant a lodash patch bump on the test-bed `shop-api`, validate in the interface, staging, controller, merge on the forge, release; then reset again. Log of the last run: "the chain went from staging to the release (released ...)", "shop-api lab/case-01-lodash is MERGED", "CASE-01: ticked". **Grid: 1 of 21 ticked.**

## What the first replays found

The table keeps what it read for five minutes, so after a reset it still offered pull requests already closed, and the merge was refused on them (405, 409). The runner now asks for a fresh reading and waits for exactly the planted pull requests. No product code changed.

## Choices to confirm

- A scenario names its pull request by what it planted (version, number), never by "the first row matching a package": the bot reopens its own pull requests after a reset.
- No change to the repository rules of the test bed; no secret or address in the repository (organisation, account and token come from the environment).

## What else is in this pull request, and why

Replaying CASE-01 found two defects of the product, fixed here because the case could not be ticked reliably without them: the controller was given the whole problem in every world and sometimes asked the Git world for the health of the release (the conductor now tells each world its own part, and the controller's prompt says a world is judged on its own objective); and the pull request's own title (text of the forge) reached the sentence the controller reads as the control plane's own (now only what the control plane parsed from it, and checked to be plain text, does). Both are documented in ADR 0032 (amendment) and ADR 0045.

Launch contract files are touched (`CLAUDE.md`, `.gitleaksignore`, `src/Orchestrarr.Core/Missions/`): the maintainer merges this pull request.

## Review

Ten passes of the five agents, on ten heads. Each pass found something real and small; the last head has no blocker, critical or high finding.

| Level | What | Answer |
|---|---|---|
| Fixed | token in a file or on a command line; a `set -e` lost in the reset (each repository now runs in a process of its own); the merge pinned to the head that passed and the required check awaited; `git apply` with a relative path; a failed run leaving the sandbox dirty; validating after a wrong selection; the table's reading; npm with an empty environment and checked names; planting only where a seed is pinned (`lab/seeds.json`); the injection through the title; the objective of the release world; a regex that let a trailing newline through | commits of this branch |
| Fixed | documentation: README, TESTING, CLAUDE.md, USE-CASES, SPEC (D-99), ADR 0045, ADR 0032 amendment, the grid | commits of this branch |
| Declined (minor or medium) | selectors by exact label, extraction of the runner into more functions, a unit test of the jq verdict and of the refusals (the scripts are exercised by the replays; a shell test lane is a separate decision), a lock between two runs (documented: runs are serial), the schema of the scenario file, fixed polling sleeps | a development tool run by hand; the cost is more code, each addition gives the agents a new hold |
| Declined (medium) | the parsed change is three tokens cut from the title | limited to plain characters, no space, and the facts win over the objective in the controller's rules; a structured change instead of a string goes with lot 1 |
| For the maintainer (major) | a problem that is not a pull request now gets an objective without a description ("Solve the problem of kind X of repo") | no such row can be started today (they are `NoAction`); the description with its provenance is built by lot 1, which makes them actionable |
| Process | a `.gitleaksignore` line for the commit that first held `lab/seeds.json` (gitleaks read a public commit hash as an API key) | exact fingerprint, a hash that opens nothing; the file now uses a form the rule does not read as a key |

body: ## Summary - Importing the package no longer loads `react-native-nitro-modules`. Nitro is now required on first use only (`src/nitro.ts`). - `getPaymentHandler()` creates the native handler on first use. A missing native module fails with an `Error` that names the fix (rebuild, Expo Go, web, Jest mock), with the original error as `cause`. `HybridPaymentHandler` already delegated per call, so it is lazy too: its Promise methods reject with the error, the others throw it. - `ApplePayButton` and `GooglePayButton` render `null` on the wrong platform (including web) without loading Nitro, and create their host component on first render. - `expo` is marked optional in `peerDependenciesMeta`, so bare React Native apps don't get it installed or hit ERESOLVE. - Docs: lazy handler and its error (README, HybridPaymentHandler page), troubleshooting for the error, web and a Jest mock, and optional Expo (compatibility, installation, README). Refs #24 ## Test plan - [x] `cd package && bun run typecheck`: passes - [x] `cd package && bun run lint`: passes - [x] `cd package && bun run test:ci`: 252/252 pass. author: chiragagg5k
body:
Part of #5517, after the `ssh2_auth_*` functions (#5569, #5570, #5571).

## What moves

`ssh2_forward_listen` and `ssh2_forward_accept` move to `crates/ssh2/src/php.rs`, in C's order:

- **`ssh2_forward_listen`:**
  1. The arguments in `zend_parse_parameters` order (`rl|sl`).
  2. The session, with `Connection not authenticated` when it isn't.
  3. `libssh2_channel_forward_listen_ex`, with the host as a C string or null, and the port and queue size passed to libssh2's `int`s as C passed them. The queue defaults to `PHP_SSH2_LISTEN_MAX_QUEUED` (128).
  4. On failure, `Failure listening on remote port` and false.
- **`ssh2_forward_accept`:**
  1. The listener resource, with Zend's `TypeError` for another kind.
  2. `libssh2_channel_forward_accept`. False, without a warning, when nothing is accepted.

Both libssh2 calls are retried through the coroutine hook on the session, as `php_swoole_ssh2_hook.h` did for them. The listener and the accepted channel are typed non-null handles. `Answer`'s retry-while-null-with-`EAGAIN` now covers any `Option` handle, not only `Text`.

## What stays C

Four helpers in `ssh2.cc`, under the `allocator` reason from `docs/zend.md`:

- `swr_ssh2_listener_open`: the `SSH2 Listener` resource. Its data is emalloc'd and freed by the destructor, and it holds a reference to the session resource.
- `swr_ssh2_listener` and `swr_ssh2_listener_session`: what a listener resource holds.
- `swr_ssh2_accepted_stream`: the channel stream over an accepted connection. It is built on ssh2's channel stream ops, with C's `Failure allocating stream` warning when no stream can be made.

The resource destructors are unchanged.

## Checks

The `swoole_ssh2` PHPT family ran locally against the sshd fixture, each case in its own process. Outcomes match the parent: 14 passed, plus `ssh2_sftp_001`, which the runner marks unsupported on both. The family has no forwarding case.

A probe script compared this build with the parent inside a coroutine:

- listening on an unauthenticated session;
- after authenticating:
  - listening on all addresses;
  - listening on `127.0.0.1` with a queue size;
  - listening on a port already bound;
- accepting a real forwarded connection, opened inside the fixture container to the forwarded port, then reading `hello` from the stream and writing `world` back (the container received it);
- wrong argument counts and types for both functions, and each resource kind passed to the other function.

The output was identical, warnings and exceptions included.

author: doncoin1999
body:
An operator-only page, **control.incentium.org**, to see every SN0 miner and switch single miners off during the launch period.

## What it does
- Lists every miner registered on SN0 per network (testnet, mainnet): UID, hotkey, tier, ICT balance, and the last epoch as measured by the validator on this server (answered tasks, tokens, spot checks, weight).
- **Switch off / Switch on** per miner. A switched-off miner gets no tasks and no weight from the validator from its next epoch, so it earns nothing through it.
- The switch works for **90 days** from each network's first block (or from a start date given at install). The window is written to disk once and never moved later; after it closes the validator ignores the switch and the page is read-only.
- Only admin accounts get in: Caddy asks `auth.incentium.org/verify-admin`. The board itself listens on 127.0.0.1 only.

## Changes
- `neuron/incentium_neuron/control.py`: the switch file (`validator-<net>-blocked.json` next to the validator's state file) and the window.
- `validator.py`: skips switched-off miners; writes `validator-<net>-stats.json` each epoch for the board.
- `auth/auth_service.py`: `/verify-admin`; the admin page links to the board.
- `scripts/mining_control.py`, `scripts/install-mining-control.sh`.
- Tests: neuron (switch inside/after the window), board (window, switch, origin check), auth (verify-admin).

## Deploy
1. DNS at Njalla: `control` A → 85.190.108.120.
2. Server B (auth): update the checkout and `sudo systemctl restart incentium-auth`.
3. Server A (validators): update `~/incentium-chain` to main, then `bash scripts/install-mining-control.sh` (optionally `TESTNET_START=YYYY-MM-DD`).

Limits: the switch acts through the validators on this server. While they are the only SN0 validators (launch period) that means no rewards; it does not deregister the miner on chain, and the chat gateway does not read it yet.

author: mostlyobvious
body:
## Endless method calls can leave no line delta

- Ruby can increment method coverage without incrementing line coverage for a short endless method call. `track_tests` then omits the calling spec from its line-based context map, so affected-test consumers such as Mutant can skip the spec.
- `track_tests` now credits the endless method's source line when its method counter increases during a test.

## Method counters remain private tracking evidence

```text
                        raw Coverage result
                               │
                ┌──────────────┴──────────────┐
                ▼                             ▼
        method call counters          configured criteria
                │                             │
                ▼                             ▼
     line-based test context map      Result and resultset
```

- Test tracking starts method counters internally when the runtime supports them. Only same-line methods contribute evidence, which avoids assigning partially executed multi-line methods to every body line.
- Method counts are grouped by source location because Ruby can rebuild the receiver and method-name keys before final coverage collection.
- `enable_coverage :method` remains the only configuration that stores or reports method coverage. Internal counters reach `TestTracker` before SimpleCov removes them from the result.

## Mutant selects the calling spec

- An end-to-end fixture confirmed that Mutant selects the spec calling an endless method and kills the resulting mutations.
- The full RSpec suite, Standard, Steep, and changed-subject mutation testing pass.

author: tharindarodrigo
body:
Pull request 3 of [spec 037](https://github.com/Elwids-tech/iot-os/blob/main/specs/037-alert-limits-on-charts/spec.md) (tasks T026 to T047 and T049). This is the one that turns the feature on.

## What people see

- A time series panel draws the value at which a running automation raises an alert on the reading it shows, labelled with the automation, the comparison and how the reading is treated, for example "Pump safety > 25 °C · 10 s average · for 5 min". Nothing is typed into the panel.
- Under the chart, **Alert limits · current rules** lists every limit: the automation (a link for people with `Workflow.view`), the devices it covers, the comparison and the treatment.
- A limit outside the readings is listed as above or below the chart; the value axis is not stretched. At most 8 lines are drawn.
- A suspended automation ("suspended, not checking") and a limit in another unit are listed, not drawn.
- An open dashboard follows an activation or deactivation within a minute, and at once on **Refresh**.
- If the limits cannot be loaded (a request and one retry), no limit line is shown as current and the panel says "Alert limits are unavailable". Readings are unaffected.
- **Show alert limits** in the panel editor's Display section turns them off for one panel.

## How

- `timeSeriesOption` takes `limits` and `EChart` reports the value axis range. The line is in the foreground colour with its own dash pattern, heavier than a panel threshold and labelled at the start of the line where a threshold is labelled at the end.
- `alertLimits.ts` holds the pure parts: which devices to ask for, merging limits that differ only by device, the wording, which 8 to draw, and why a limit has no line.
- `useAlertLimits` asks per device through a batcher, so the devices of every panel go out in one request. A person without `Device.view` is not asked for.
- `config.alert_limits: false` on a time series panel; shown is the absent key, so saved dashboards are not rewritten. The import parser accepts it; no other panel type does.

## Changed from the plan

- The plan had the dashboard workspace collect devices and pass limits down through context. A batcher behind per-device queries does the same with no wiring through the workspace, and covers the editor preview. The spec documents are updated.
- The line was planned in the warning colour. On the running portal it vanished on a shaded alert period, which is when the limit matters, so it is the foreground colour.
- **Refresh** now also reloads alert limits.
