author: danielhanchen
body:
Until now, DiT block swap in Studio diffusion LoRA training only took a bf16 base. Asking for `block_swap` with `base_precision="fp8"` or int8 gave an error, so a model whose 8-bit base still does not fit the card had to train on nf4. Qwen-Image (40.9 GB in bf16, about 20 GB as int8 codes) on a 24 GB L4 is one example. This PR lets block swap stream a frozen fp8 or int8 W8A8 base.

## Change

The frozen fp8 and W8A8 linears keep their codes and scales as buffers. zoo's `BlockSwap` streams only frozen parameters, and `_place_rest` moves every buffer to the card. If only the gate were lifted, the swapped weights would quietly stay on the GPU. This change is all on the Studio side, so `unsloth_zoo` needs no change or release.

`core/training/diffusion_block_swap.py`:
- **Gate:** block swap now accepts `fp8`, and `int8` when it is the frozen W8A8 base (`UNSLOTH_DIFFUSION_INT8_TRAIN=w8a8`).
  - The torchao weight-only int8 base is still refused, since its tensor subclass cannot stream.
  - nf4, mxfp8 and the fp16 fallback are refused as before.
  - `UNSLOTH_DIT_BLOCK_SWAP_LOWP=0` restores the bf16-only gate.
- **Plan sizing:** `_frozen_bytes` and the new `_model_bytes` count a target Linear as its converted size: 1-byte codes in the block, plus the fp32 per-row scale, which stays resident. So both the auto plan and the fit check use the converted bytes, not bf16.
- **Conversion inside `install_dit_block_swap`, before anything is placed:**
  - Resident target Linears are quantized on the card one at a time, as before.
  - Swapped ones are quantized on the card too, so the codes come from the same kernels and are bit-identical. `host_lowp_weight` then moves each layer's codes (and bias) back to host RAM as an `nn.Parameter(requires_grad=False)`, which the swapper streams. The scale buffer goes to the card with the rest.
  - The bf16 base is never whole on the card.

`core/training/diffusion_frozen_fp8.py`: `Fp8BackwardWeights.get` is keyed by `q.data_ptr()`, but a swapped weight lives in a ring slot that other blocks of the same shape reuse.
- **The bug:** block A, now resident in slot 1, would hand its cached column-major copy to block C running from A's old slot 0. That gives a silently wrong dX.
- **The fix:** a swapped layer is marked, and its backward takes a second custom op that builds the same tiled column-major copy without caching it. Resident layers keep the cache.

`core/training/diffusion_dit_trainer.py`:
- With swap requested, the frozen fp8 / W8A8 base is converted inside the install, after the same GEMM probe the resident path runs. A probe failure refuses the run instead of falling back.
- The later `_apply_fp8_training` / `_apply_int8_w8a8` steps are skipped, so nothing moves the host codes back.
- A swap request on the fp16 path is refused up front.

## Measurements

Every arm runs in a fresh process. Z-Image runs at 512 px, rank 16 LoRA.

**Bit-identity:** eager, `torch.use_deterministic_algorithms(True)`, 3 steps, warmup 2. The loss tensor and all 476 LoRA grads are compared with `torch.equal` at every step.

| GPU | pair | loss equal (3 steps) | LoRA grads equal per step |
|---|---|---|---|
| L4 | fp8, 8 of 34 blocks swapped vs 0 | 3 / 3 | 476 / 476, 476 / 476, 476 / 476 |
| L4 | fp8, 0 swapped, A/A | 3 / 3 | all |
| L4 | fp8, 0 swapped, this branch vs main | 3 / 3 | all |
| L4 | W8A8, 8 swapped vs 0 | 3 / 3 | all |
| A100 40 GB | W8A8, 8 swapped vs 0 | 3 / 3 | all |
| A100 40 GB | W8A8, 0 swapped, A/A | 3 / 3 | all |

**Speed and memory:** L4, compiled, 20 steps. s/step is the median of steps 6-20, two arms each, run off / 8 / 8 / off.

| base | swapped | s/step | step-2 peak GiB | loop peak GiB | graph breaks / recompiles |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| fp8 | 0 of 34 | 0.5186 / 0.5356 | 12.22 | 17.18 | 0 / 0 |
| fp8 | 8 of 34 | 0.6005 / 0.6043 | 9.86 | 13.74 | 0 / 0 |
| W8A8 | 0 of 34 | 0.5853 / 0.5894 | 11.63 | 11.63 | 0 / 0 |
| W8A8 | 8 of 34 | 0.6508 / 0.6519 | 9.51 | 9.51 | 0 / 0 |

Read-out:
- **Speed:** forcing 8 blocks to swap costs about 14% (fp8) and 11% (W8A8) per step on a model that fits anyway.
- **Memory:** it saves 2.4 GiB (fp8) and 2.1 GiB (W8A8) at step 2. The fp8 loop peak is higher than step 2 because the fp8 backward cache fills whatever room is left after step 1. That is by design, and swapped layers stay out of it.
- **Compile:** a swapped block holds its codes as a parameter instead of a buffer, which adds one compiled graph (6 instead of 5). No recompiles.

**Capacity:** Qwen-Image (40.9 GB bf16) on L4 (22 GiB usable, 53 GB host RAM), compiled where the base allows, 12 steps, same seed. The last three arms ran on one exclusive VM.

| arm | blocks streamed | s/step | loop peak GiB | mean loss, 12 steps |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| W8A8, no swap | - | out of memory while the base is converted onto the card | - | - |
| W8A8 + `block_swap="auto"` (this PR) | 32 of 60, 16.9 GiB pinned | 2.897 | 19.05 | 0.10405 |
| bf16 + `block_swap="auto"` | 37 of 60, 23.4 GiB host (18.4 pinned) | 5.541 | 19.42 | 0.10398 |
| nf4 (what Qwen-Image trains on today on this card), eager | - | 1.472 | 19.22 | 0.18589 |

Read-out:
- **Against bf16 + swap:** W8A8 + swap is 1.91x faster and streams 6.5 GiB less host RAM. Its per-step loss tracks the bf16 run closely (mean 0.07% apart).
- **Against nf4:** W8A8 + swap is not faster; nf4 is 1.97x quicker per step. The nf4 per-step losses are far from bf16's, but this run does not check that nf4 draws the same timesteps, so the loss column only shows the gap. The case for W8A8 + swap here is accuracy, not speed.

**Fallbacks and gates:**
- **T4 (sm75, fp16 path):** W8A8 without swap still trains, and `block_swap=8` is refused up front with a clear message.
- **Kill switch:** `UNSLOTH_DIT_BLOCK_SWAP_LOWP=0` with fp8 + swap is refused before the load.

## Tests

`tests/test_diffusion_block_swap_lowp.py`, 12 CPU tests, covering:
- the gate and the kill switch;
- byte counting of codes vs bf16;
- an auto plan sized from converted bytes, which swaps fewer blocks than bf16 sizing at the same free VRAM;
- placement: swapped codes stay on the host as frozen parameters that the swapper walks, while scales, resident codes and everything else go to the card;
- swapped vs resident fp8 and W8A8 layers giving bit-identical forward and backward;
- the ring-slot pattern above. Without the bypass, the cached path returns the wrong dX; with it, dX is exact and nothing is cached.

Other results:
- `test_gating` in `test_diffusion_block_swap.py` no longer expects fp8 to be refused.
- `test_differential`: 13 new tests fail on main (missing names) and pass here. All other block swap, fp8 cache and int8 tests are unchanged.
- **Wider sweep:** `tests/test_diffusion_{block_swap,frozen,gc_budget,fp8_prequant,dit_}*.py` gives 455 passed. The 9 red tests are red on main as well, with the same IDs: `test_diffusion_dit_trainer_ltx25` (4), `test_diffusion_dit_trainer_qwen_image_21` (3) and `test_diffusion_gc_budget_trainers` (2), all failing on this host's diffusers / huggingface_hub import. `test_diffusion_dit_trainer_moss_image` fails at collection for the same reason. One flow-shift sampling test failed once in the combined run, then passed on both trees alone.

## Not proven here

- **The wrong hit was not seen on a GPU:** the same fp8 8-swapped arm with the bypass removed still matched the resident run on L4. In that run the slot assignment did not shift between steps. The hazard is shown on CPU with the zoo slot pattern.
- **No compiled bit-identity:** grad equality was only checked eager and deterministic. The compiled timing arms are not deterministic: A/A first-step losses already differ in the 4th decimal.
- **Not run:** FLUX.2-dev, multi-GPU with swap, Windows and ROCm. The swap s/step was measured on L4 only.
- **One seed, 12 steps:** the Qwen-Image arms are short runs on a single seed.
- **Untouched paths:** Auto still never picks fp8 or int8 together with a swap, and the fp16 path still refuses swap.

body:
Closes #284

## Co i dlaczego

Link do YouTube kończył się twierdzeniami ze stopki serwisu, link do X niósł odpowiedzi innych osób, a Facebook i TikTok dawały `url_unavailable`. Dla tych domen transport pod fetcherem z core oddaje teraz tytuł i opis, które serwis publikuje do podglądu linków (Open Graph). Dalej potok traktuje to jak tekst strony, a `fetch_url` dopisuje ograniczenie, że czytaliśmy tylko tytuł i opis.

```
build_check_deps
└─ pages = build_link_fetcher()                 (nowe)
   └─ build_page_fetcher(transport=LinkPreviewTransport)   SSRF, limity: core
      └─ host z PREVIEW_DOMAINS + text/html → preview_text(html) jako text/plain
fetch_url
└─ is_preview_host(url.host) → ograniczenie PREVIEW_ONLY_NOTE
```

Zamiast oEmbed jest Open Graph: oEmbed X jest zabroniony w `robots.txt`, oEmbed TikToka zwraca samą ramkę odtwarzacza, a Meta wymaga tokenu aplikacji. Napisów YouTube nie pobieramy (`robots.txt` zabrania `/api/`, `timedtext` odpowiada 429).

## Dowód

Testy `tests/checks/test_link_previews.py` na nagranych stronach YouTube, X, Facebooka i TikToka oraz dwa scenariusze behave. Przed zmianą nie przechodziły, bo `build_link_fetcher` nie istniał.

Lokalnie, na prawdziwych adresach, ten sam fetcher:

| Adres | Przed | Po |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `youtube.com/watch`, `youtu.be`, `shorts` | stopka YouTube | tytuł i cały opis filmu |
| `x.com/jack/status/20` | wpis z odpowiedziami innych | autor i treść wpisu |
| `facebook.com/zuck/posts/…` | `javascript_required` | autor i początek wpisu |
| `instagram.com/p/…` | nie sprawdzano | autor i opis |

body: ## Summary **Dev and every branch have been red on Backend Tests Pass since 2026-11-22T08:26:23Z.** This is a dev-wide break, not a finding against any PR. Six tests in `tracer/tests/test_derived_metric_retention_clickhouse.py` (metrics shards 5, 8 and 15) fail with `psycopg.errors.InvalidParameterValue: invalid value for parameter "lock_timeout": "2148063609ms"`. Examples: #4306 run 45001867282 and #4289 run 45004304123. Dev's last green Backend CI (ae0bf483, 02:01Z) ran before that time. **Cause:** - The lifecycle lock budget (`deletion_protocol._budgeted_row_lock`) sets `lock_timeout` from the lease's remaining time with no upper bound. - PostgreSQL rejects values above INT_MAX ms (2147483647, about 24.8 days). - The retention fixtures pin their lease clock to 2026-10-28T12:00Z, while `ProjectLease.renew()` renews on the real clock. The remaining time therefore grows with wall time and passed INT_MAX at 08:26:23Z. **Fix:** bound the value to INT_MAX ms with a small helper, `bounded_lock_timeout_ms`. - The 1 ms floor stays. - Real leases, which last at most 5 minutes, are unchanged. - `renew()` is untouched. Its clock mismatch is tracked separately as TH-10627. ## Linked issues Linear: TH-10627 (follow-up: lease clock consistency) ## AI use AI use: written with Claude Code at the maintainer's direction. ## Type of change - [x] 🐛 Bug fix (dev-wide CI break) ## Testing - New `tracer/tests/test_derived_metric_lock_timeout_bound.py`, exact integer arithmetic with no clock: - INT_MAX → INT_MAX, INT_MAX + 1 → INT_MAX, INT_MAX − 1 → unchanged, 10¹² → INT_MAX; - 300 000 (a 5-minute lease) → unchanged; - 1 → 1; 0 and −5 → 1. - GCP VM proof at f3bfba2b against the CI ClickHouse sidecar (`docker-compose.test.yml`, Backend CI's shard environment), run on 22 Nov: ``` $ uv run pytest tracer/tests/test_derived_metric_lock_timeout_bound.py tracer/tests/test_derived_metric_retention_clickhouse.py 43 passed, 3 xfailed in 1227.55s ``` - All six tests that failed on dev pass here. - The 3 xfails are the existing TH-8975 markers (`test_expired_active_conversation_is_not_reanchored_after_source_retention[False/True]` and `test_retired_and_new_spans_with_identical_surviving_rows_require_admission_proof[True]`), not among the six. - Broader regression over the 28 other tracer test modules that import `deletion_protocol`, on the same VM and containers: - one session over the first 11 modules stopped at its 55-minute limit (about 49% of the tests) with no failures; - a second session over the remaining 19 modules gave **380 passed, 2 failed**: `test_derived_metric_refresh.py::test_crash_resumes_frozen_payload_not_new_sources` and `::test_native_refresh_rejects_needs_rebuild_before_expiry_or_attempts`. Both are row-count assertions. - That module run on its own passes **27/27** at this head, 27/27 with `dev`'s `deletion_protocol.py`, and 27/27 at this head again. - The two failures appeared only late in the long session, after 18 other modules, while unrelated suites were also loading the VM. They are order- or environment-dependent and not reproduced by this change; their exact cause is not established here. - This change alters behaviour only when a lease would exceed INT_MAX ms. - CI on f3bfba2b: Backend Tests Pass, E2E Tests Pass and Python Lint Pass are all green. Mypy (advisory) is at dev's level, 230 new. ## E2E coverage E2E: none (backend lock budget only) ## Docs Docs: none needed (internal bound) 🤖 Generated with [Claude Code](https://claude.com/claude-code) --- Open in [code]smith · Need help on this PR? Tag @codesmith-bot with what you need.

author: ersushilthalor
body:
## Summary
- Adds a persisted **Special Photo** toggle to Photo mode.
- Captures the 1x main and 0.5x ultra-wide JPEGs from one shutter action, using 4:3 sensor output sizes (portrait 3:4 after JPEG orientation).
- Uses one still-capture request for logical multi-camera devices; independent concurrent camera devices receive back-to-back requests on the shared camera handler.
- Stores both original images and their sensor timestamp skew, but presents the pair as one item in VCamera's in-app gallery.
- Adds an **Expand** viewer that layers the 1x center over the ultra-wide frame.

## Important limitations
- Android Camera2 cannot guarantee exactly 0 ms between independent camera sensors. The app records the actual skew when both timestamp clocks are comparable; otherwise it marks the skew unavailable.
- This repository currently has no active on-device generative-AI image model/runtime (the Firebase AI and ML Kit dependencies are commented out). The Expand implementation is a local feathered geometric composite, **not generative AI**; it preserves both originals and does not claim AI-quality alignment or scene reconstruction.
- Actual simultaneous capture depends on the handset's Camera2 concurrent/physical-camera stream support. Unsupported output combinations fail safely instead of manufacturing a paired image.

## Validation
The repository's Build Android APK workflow runs on pull requests to main.

author: miguel-heygen
body:
## What

Two changes to the edit accuracy check, both for a shard whose results never reach the gate:

- **The retry plan re-runs it.** `List the shards marked for a re-run` in `.github/workflows/ci.yml` now also lists every shard number from 1 to `EDIT_ACCURACY_SHARDS` that has no `edit-accuracy-shard-<n>` artifact at all, next to the shards that marked themselves `retry`. The retry job runs those again on a fresh runner, as it already does for slow or cancelled shards.
- **The gate never counts it as a drop.** In `packages/studio/tests/e2e/edit-accuracy/ratchet.mjs`, when fewer shards reported than `--shards` expects, the base branch's passing count is taken over the cases that ran, for the full grid too. A missing shard then gives "Edit accuracy did not run: N of M shards reported results" (exit 2), and a case that ran and fell still gives "Edit accuracy fell" (exit 1), as the PR grid already did.

The shard count is now one workflow-level `EDIT_ACCURACY_SHARDS` (30 in the merge queue, 15 on pull requests), read by the retry plan, the retry job and the gate, where each used to repeat the expression. The shard job's matrix still lists its shards, since a job's `strategy` cannot read `env`. A new test in `scripts/edit-accuracy-retry.test.mjs` fails if the matrix lists and the count disagree.

## Why

A merge-group run lost one shard's results to the artifact upload (`Failed to FinalizeArtifact: Unable to make request: ECONNRESET`). That shard had marked nothing, since its bench had finished, so the retry plan did not re-run it. The gate then read 29 of 30 shards and failed with "the passing count fell from 747 to 722": the 25 missing cases, counted as failures because the full grid compared against every case in the base baseline. The pull request left the merge queue for a network error.

## Test plan

fails without the fix: `packages/studio/tests/e2e/edit-accuracy/ratchet.test.mjs` ("says a full grid with a shard missing did not run, not that the missing cases fell"). On main's `ratchet.mjs` it exits 1 with "Edit accuracy fell"; with the fix it exits 2 with "1 of 2 shards reported results".

fails without the fix: `scripts/edit-accuracy-retry.test.mjs` ("the retry plan also re-runs a shard whose evidence never uploaded"). On main's `ci.yml` the plan lists only shard 2; with the fix it lists 2, 3 and 5.

- I ran both files against main's `ratchet.mjs` and `ci.yml` on the devbox: each new test failed and every other test passed. With the fix, both files pass 3 runs in a row (22 and 6 tests).
- "the shard matrix runs exactly the shards the count names" passes, and fails with the count changed to 31.
- The existing "still says accuracy fell when a case that ran regressed, even with a shard missing" test still passes, so a real drop is not hidden behind a missing shard.

## What I did NOT exercise

- A real merge-group run with a failed upload. The retry job itself is unchanged; only the list it receives grows.

body:
Fixes #240 (on `main`; the owner closes it by hand).

## What changed

- `kaizen.rule_metrics` has a new `shadow` count: the distinct spans of INFO `fired` events from a rule whose
  status is `shadow`. That's how often the rule would have fired. It never goes into `fires` or a rate.
- `kaizen report` has a `shad` column straight after `fires`, and the legend explains it. A rule with no shadow
  fires prints `0`.
- `kaizen report --share` exports `shadow` with the other counts.
- An INFO fire on a live rule (a hit inside a quote, or one an allow marker keeps) doesn't count as shadow.
- `fires`, `docs`, `last_fired` and every rate are as before. Calibrate reads none of the new key.

## Why

A shadow rule's row showed `0` fires next to yesterday's date, which reads like a counting bug, and the one number
that matters for a shadow rule wasn't in the report or the export.

## How I tested it

- I wrote the tests first and watched them fail: shadow INFO fires count in `shadow` and not in `fires` (a new draft
  of the same span counts once), a live rule's INFO doesn't count, the table gains `shad` and stays fixed width, and
  the share export carries the key.
- Full suite: 3427 tests, OK (4 skipped). Leak guard: 0 hits.

## Not done

`docs` still counts only BLOCK and WARN spans, as the issue asked, so a shadow-only rule shows `0` docs. A
`shadow_docs` count would be a small follow-up if that's wanted.

author: izderadicka
body:
## Summary

Fixes #211. The announcer only raises `protocol_max`, so a node rolled back keeps its newer build's record, and the leader's raise check counts it in.

```diff
-follower::behind_the_group(state_machine)
-  group > PROTOCOL_MAX → Protocol { group, at }
+follower::needs_an_upgrade(state_machine, me)
+  group > PROTOCOL_MAX               → Protocol { group, at }
+  own record.protocol_max > PROTOCOL_MAX → SpokeNewer { protocol, at }   // "spoke_newer"
```

Called where `behind_the_group` was: `starts_as_core` (no seat), `upgrade_required_from_storage` (flag set from the first moment), and after each fetch in the follow loop. Local, not in the fold. `node.status`, the CLI warning and the UI banner say the new reason.

A voter already seated is checked at its next start (P5-72): its own record can change under it only from storage older than its own announcement, and a rollback is a restart.

## Evidence

- **Before:** #211's test passed: restarted on the older build, the founder took its seat with `upgrade_required() == None` and proposed a raise to `PROTOCOL_MAX + 1`, which committed.
  **After:** `a_voter_a_newer_build_ran_before_takes_no_seat_on_restart`: `upgrade_required() == SpokeNewer { protocol: PROTOCOL_MAX + 1 }` at once, no Raft. `a_follower_whose_record_says_a_newer_protocol_stops`. The wire shape is pinned in `upgrade_required_reads_as_a_reason_and_where_the_node_stopped`; the CLI and Shell tests cover the text.
- 5d-7's `each_node_says_which_protocols_it_speaks_once_and_then_the_group_can_be_raised` faked "speaks 2" on this build, which is what 5g-3 stops: its follower now stops at its own record, and the raise is watched on the founder.
- Hand mutations, all killed: own record ignored; `>=` instead of `>`; `starts_as_core` skips the check; flag not set from storage; the CLI arm; the UI branch.
- `cargo test-all` 800 passed; `cargo test-fast` 633 passed; clippy `-D warnings` clean; Vitest and svelte-check clean.

## Merge Danger

**Door:** two-way

No rollback past a protocol a node has announced: such a node waits for an upgrade instead of voting.

**Blast Radius:** consensus

A node whose record exceeds its build stops following and takes no seat; custody keeps every copy while it waits (5d-8).

author: szchan-bot
body:
<!-- dsh-anyplugin-agent -->

Closes #166.

## What changed

`npm run guard:install` composed from the checkout it ran in and wrote the
ticket worktrees that existed at that moment. The maintainer's audit ran it
from `.agents/worktrees/dsh-1a4cc244-446c`, so the block named that worktree's
`packages/dsh-anyplugin-guard/src/index.ts` and 25 literal
`/tmp/anyplugin-wt/ticket-*` paths — a source that disappears when the review
worktree is removed, and a list that refuses the next ticket worktree.

This PR:

- resolves the composition root from the repository's main checkout. When
  `git rev-parse --path-format=absolute --git-dir` and `--git-common-dir` are
  the same path (an ordinary checkout, a submodule, a `--separate-git-dir`
  main checkout), the root is `--show-toplevel`; when they differ the path is
  a linked worktree, and if the common dir is `<main>/.git` its parent is the
  root. A linked worktree of a submodule or `--separate-git-dir` repo has no
  main working tree git can name, so a real install from it is refused and a
  dry run composes from the invocation checkout. The derivation is the mod
  host's (`packages/dsh-anyplugin-mod-host/src/bridge.ts:1328-1336`) and needs
  git ≥ 2.31 for `--path-format=absolute` (already required by the hook and
  audit scripts);
- writes **one pattern** derived from the discovered ticket worktrees — same
  parent, shared basename stem cut after its last `-` — instead of a snapshot
  (`deriveWorktreeGlob()`); `chooseWorktree` maps a prompt path through the
  pattern to the concrete directory it matched, and confinement uses that
  concrete root, never the glob string;
- refuses to write an ambiguous entry: a literal `*` anywhere in a ticket
  worktree path makes install fail closed, because the block grammar reserves
  `*` for the one wildcard after a stem ending in `-`; status reads a legacy
  exact entry whose path really ends in `*` as that literal path;
- keeps the exact list as the fallback when the discovered paths do not share a
  parent and a stem;
- makes `guard:status` separate `not-installed` from
  `installed-with-stale-paths`, naming every literal path in the block that no
  longer exists (`readWorktrees()` reads the installed block, so status
  composes with the pattern it finds rather than re-deriving a new one), and
  prints desired and installed worktree lists separately;
- protects the resolved git directory by identity, not by the name `.git`:
  the common dir goes into `protectedRoots` when it differs from the main
  working tree, and into `gitDirectories` always. A pattern derived from a
  `--separate-git-dir` layout (`sep-*`) also matches the custom git dir
  `sep-gitdir`, so without this a worker could overwrite the pre-push hook
  the install had just written; a root write there remains allowed;
- adds the acceptance tests, an `apply()`-level glob test, submodule and
  `--separate-git-dir` tests, and a runnable mutation audit
  (`packages/dsh-anyplugin-guard/test/mutations.mjs`).

### Why option (a) (glob), not `guard:refresh`

The master creates worktrees continuously and hands out paths; a `guard:refresh`
step is a second install that gets forgotten, which is the failure mode the
issue is about. The operator installs once (audit F2), and the pattern derives
from the live `git worktree list`. Deriving `<parent>/ticket-*` from the
discovered paths also keeps the issue's broader `/tmp/anyplugin-wt/*` out of the
policy: review/merge/verify worktrees stay non-confinable, and the pattern is
one directory name wide.

The pattern is a **namespace matcher, not a git-worktree attestation**: a
directory under the shared stem is confinable even if git never registered it
as a worktree. That is the intended strength and the residual: it bounds writes
to the namespace the ticket convention reserves, not to paths git attests.

## Acceptance mapping

| Acceptance (issue #166) | Where |
| --- | --- |
| Dry run from a linked worktree names the main checkout's `packages/dsh-anyplugin-guard/src/index.ts`, never the linked copy | `mainCheckout()` + root selection in `scripts/guard-install.mjs`; test `a dry run from a linked worktree composes from the main checkout, not from itself` |
| The static list stops being a snapshot; a worktree created after install can write without reinstall, and the pattern still refuses a write outside it | `deriveWorktreeGlob()` + pattern branch of `composeGuard()`; `matchWorktree()` in `policy.ts`; test `a worktree created after install writes without a reinstall, and a sibling outside the pattern is refused` (creates `ticket/1999` after install, allows a write inside it, denies the `ticket-2000` sibling, status stays `current`); `apply()`-level test `a glob config admits the worktree the prompt named and refuses a sibling at the tool seam` |
| `guard:status` distinguishes `not-installed` from `installed-with-stale-paths` and names the stale path | `scripts/guard-status.mjs` status hierarchy + `stalePaths`; test `guard:status separates not-installed from a block that lists a worktree which is gone` |
| Literal `*` in a checkout path cannot widen the policy | `isWorktreeGlob()` (one trailing `*` only) + `assertRepresentableWorktrees()`; test `a literal "*" in a worktree path is refused, not widened into a pattern` (dry-run exits 1, `starX` is not matched, status reports `refused` then the stale literal) |
| Submodule and `--separate-git-dir` roots resolve to the working tree | `mainCheckout()` + `readGitWorktrees()` normalisation; tests `a submodule checkout installs and reports from its own root` and `a --separate-git-dir checkout installs a ticket pattern and refuses worker writes to the git dir` |
| A worker cannot overwrite the installed hook through a pattern that matches a custom git dir | `insideGitDirectory(target, policy)` + `gitDirectories`/`protectedRoots`; the two layout tests deny a worker write to `<gitdir>/hooks/pre-push` and `<gitdir>/config` and allow the root write | `a --separate-git-dir checkout installs a ticket pattern and refuses worker writes to the git dir`; `a submodule checkout installs and reports from its own root` |
| Docs: architecture and ticket setup | `docs/ARCHITECTURE.md` §8 guard subsection, `docs/WORKFLOW.md` "Isolation: one worktree per ticket". The guard text lives in §8 in this revision; §10 is the verification plan and has no guard-install entry, so §8 is the section that has to move with the code |
| No `DECISIONS.md` edit | unchanged; proposed D67 text below for ratification |

### Reproduction (before → after)

Before, from the audit worktree (`/tmp/repro-166.log`):

```
guard: root /home/szchan/Projects/dsh-anyplugin/.agents/worktrees/dsh-1a4cc244-446c
guard: worktrees 25 ticket worktree(s); protected root /home/szchan/Projects/dsh-anyplugin
name: ".../.agents/worktrees/dsh-1a4cc244-446c/packages/dsh-anyplugin-guard/src/index.ts"
    worktrees:
        - "/tmp/anyplugin-wt/ticket-80"
        ... (25 snapshot entries)
```

After, the same command from the same audit worktree (fixed tree,
`/tmp/dryrun-audit-fixed.log`):

```
guard: root /home/szchan/Projects/dsh-anyplugin
guard: worktrees 25 ticket worktree(s); policy pattern /tmp/anyplugin-wt/ticket-*; protected root /home/szchan/Projects/dsh-anyplugin
name: "/home/szchan/Projects/dsh-anyplugin/packages/dsh-anyplugin-guard/src/index.ts"
        worktrees:
          - "/tmp/anyplugin-wt/ticket-*"
guard: 109/109 payloads match
```

A real install from an ordinary linked worktree was already refused before it
writes; a linked worktree of a submodule or a `--separate-git-dir` repo is now
refused too (round 4). `--uninstall` from a linked worktree is refused as well,
with the main checkout as the remedy.

## Reviewer follow-up (commit `c876040`)

| Finding | Fix | Test that reddens on revert |
| --- | --- | --- |
| MUST: literal `*` in a checkout path became a policy wildcard (`star*` → `starX`) | `isWorktreeGlob()` accepts exactly one trailing `*`; `assertRepresentableWorktrees()

body:
Backport of the conflict mode change from main to 3.x (TYPO3 13.4).

`WriteFile` and `MoveFile` passed their conflict mode strings to `addFile()` / `moveFile()`. TYPO3 13 only knows `rename`, `replace` and `cancel` and falls back to `cancel`, so `changeName`, `renameNewFile` and `overrideExistingFile` behaved like `cancel`. The modes are now mapped to the `DuplicationBehavior` enum.

- Only the conflict mode mapping and its tests are ported, not the TYPO3 14 API changes (`StorageRepository`, the `getRealPath()` check)
- Added a test for the mapping in `MoveFileTest` (main has none)
- Added `CHANGELOG.md` with an `Unreleased` section that describes the behaviour change; the version in `ext_emconf.php` is unchanged (planned as 3.3.0)

Closes #124

author: mdenhartog
body:
## What

Unit 12 of `label-structure` (INT-008, ADR-0058) with the unit that keeps the edge from refusing it, one commit group per unit, built test-first.

- **U-label-structure-12** the api: `POST /api/categories/upload` parses the file with the category policy (unit 04) and stores only a preview row bound to the session, the file hash and the list version (valid for 15 minutes); `POST /api/categories/upload/{preview_id}/confirm` writes one list version through the repository (ids stay stable for names that match, audit record and change notice as a normal save) and answers 409 on any binding mismatch (another session, a changed hash, an expired or used preview, a changed list), a double confirm makes one version; `POST /api/categories/restore-previous` makes a new version equal to the previous one (the body names the version the user sees, so a double click cannot toggle). The routes need the session, the CSRF token and the Origin, share the hourly limit of a list save, are on the route allow-list and the upload route has its own 320 KiB body limit. Raw body only (`application/yaml`, `text/yaml`, `text/plain`; else 415), no multipart dependency. OpenAPI document and reference regenerated.
- **U-label-structure-35** the Helm ingress: a dedicated IngressRoute for `POST /api/categories/upload` with `ingress.uploadBodyLimitBytes` (default 393 216, schema bounds 16 384 to 1 048 576); confirm and restore keep the generic 8 192. Without it the edge refused an upload above 8 KiB with a 413.

## Tests

Locally: the service, route inventory, body limit, OpenAPI and export tests, the chart tests (`tests/infra`) and `helm lint --strict`, plus `ruff`, `pyright`, `bandit`, `vulture`, `xenon`, `deptry` and `export_openapi --check` are green. **Not verified locally**: the 22 database tests of `test_category_upload_api.py` (the development machine's Docker resets every database connection); the CI runs them on a clean machine.

Refs: INT-008
Unit: U-label-structure-12

body:
## A living world: rumours, your good name and town hours

All the logic is in the new `game/rumours.js` (global `RUMOURS`). Other files only get small hooks.

### Rumours that turn into real things on the map
- In the inn you can pay a few coins and ask "What's the word?". In the streets you can chat with the locals for free.
- Each rumour puts an ember "?" on the map for about 36 in-game hours, at most 3 at once. There are five kinds: bandits on a road, a lost shipment, lights in a ruin, someone needing rescue, and a big beast.
- At the spot, a card on the Travel tab lets you see it through.
  - Shipments give loot.
  - The others are a fight with a named, somewhat tougher foe (health ×1.25, normal damage). A simulation of low-level fights won 24 of 24.
- Some rumours are just talk: about 1 in 4 from the inn and 2 in 5 from the street. Speechcraft lowers those odds.

### Towns react to what you've done
- Guards, townsfolk and shopkeepers bring up what you've done: dragons, cleared places, guild ranks, quest lines, crimes. These lines hook into `IMM.bark` and the NPC greeting.
- The Journal (Misc) gets a "Word around Skyrim" page. It lists your current leads and a line for each of the 9 holds saying what that hold knows about you and how much they like you.
- Friends of a hold get 3% off in its shops and heroes get 6%. Crimes and bounty drag your name down.

### Day and night
- The Town tab shows a line for the time of day.
- The inn shows a little crowd picture that is busiest in the evening (ink and pixel versions).
- At night a closed shop shows a sign with a "Knock anyway?" button. If you knock, they serve you until 08:00 at 15% more to buy and 10% less when you sell. This is halved for heroes. Shopping is never blocked.

### Perks
Three new perks, with real effects in `perkfx.js`. All existing perk ids are kept.
- **Good Ear** (Speechcraft 25): half as many false rumours, and leads last longer.
- **Local Hero** (Etiquette 35): your name grows faster, and your hero discount is doubled.
- **Night Owl** (Streetwise 25): no night mark-up when you knock.

### Hooks
- **engine.js:** buy and sell price multipliers, and a knock check in buy/sell.
- **ui.js:** town panel HTML, the lead card, the Journal page, `canShop`, and the map data.
- **map.js:** the lead mark.
- **immerse.js / npcart.js:** lines about your deeds.
- **index.html:** the script tag and `.rw-*` CSS.

The patch notes entry is `b82`, a placeholder to renumber at merge.

### Tests
- `tests/test_rumours.js`: new, 158 checks pass.
- `tests/rumours_ui.py`: new Playwright test on a phone viewport, ink and pixel. All 16 checks pass with no page errors. I looked at the screenshots: inn crowd, closed shop and knock, map mark, lead card, fight result, Journal page.
- `test_perks2` now also scans `rumours.js` and passes.
- `node --check` passes on every touched file.
- Full quick node suite (without test_bal_sim and test_qscale): the only failures are 5 that already fail on main (test_ai2, test_tactics, test_foeperks, test_followers2, test_partyplay). Everything else passes, including test_map11.

## Assumptions & Trade-offs

- No phone was available to pair. The manual check ran against the real `setu-daemon` v1.1.0 and real ADB, but the live card was supplied through the app's own `session-hub` bridge; Disconnect called the real Rust command and returned `no_session` (silent, as specified). Card removal was verified with a `session_down` message through the same bridge.
- In Solo, audit is off by default, so `Transport: Path unknown` is the expected display until a `path_up`; no transport was invented. Audit `session_start` has an empty top-level `session`, so it is parsed before the empty-session rule; only `device_id`, `tunnel_id` and `transport` cross, never `user` or `token_id`.

author: sithglan
body:
## Problem

Aurora Debian (Debian testing; images from the new debian-aurora repository) builds its images with `images/finalize-image` and boots them with `aurora-firstboot`. Neither knows Debian yet:

- `finalize-image` accepts only the Fedora and Arch profiles.
- `aurora-firstboot` rebuilds the initrd for the owner's console keymap only when it finds dracut's default name, `initramfs-<kernel>.img`. Debian's dracut integration names it `/boot/initrd.img-<kernel>`, so a Debian install keeps the image's keymap.

## Change

- `finalize-image` accepts `debian-kde`, `debian-gnome` and `debian-minimal`. A Debian image is finalized like an Arch-flavoured one (dracut; GRUB in `/boot/grub` with the arm64-efi modules in `/usr/lib/grub`), except:
  - the initrd is `/boot/initrd.img-<kernel>`;
  - the first-boot preset check runs in enable-only mode, which is what Debian's first boot applies. Debian's maintainer scripts enable units without presets, and the image supplies the catch-all disable preset that Debian's systemd doesn't ship;
  - `packages.txt` lists the installed packages from `dpkg-query` (state `ii`; removed packages whose configuration files remain are left out);
  - the image record names the `debian-btrfs-v1` layout.
- SELinux labelling and the initial-setup units stay Fedora-only.
- A Debian image must also have no unit enabled or disabled against its preset in `systemctl list-unit-files`. Enable-only mode never reports a unit a maintainer script enabled against the `disable *` catch-all. A full preset pass would, but it also drops `/etc/systemd/system/default.target`, which the first boot keeps.
- A Debian image must have a `wheel` group, which `aurora-firstboot` adds the owner to. Debian has the group only because the image creates it.
- `aurora-firstboot` checks both initrd names.
- `harden-grub` replaces GRUB's core image only when its bytes change (`grub-mkimage` is reproducible), with a rename. Aurora Debian's `aurora-boot` reapplies the hardening after every `update-grub`, which Debian runs on each kernel installation. This applies to every Arch-layout core, including NixOS's `--grub-mkimage` path.
- The profile, GRUB, dracut and package-list steps are marked in `finalize-image`, and the tests run them with `chroot` and `python3` stubbed.

Fedora and Arch images take the same `finalize-image` paths as before.

## Testing

body: _Requested by **Ashik** · [project thread](https://claude.ai/code/project/chan_01GC1TF4ydPa4SP34zEz77C6?thread=cmsg_01GC1TF4ydPa4SP34zEz77C6RZS3iwFkqwJsKw1RExP6V1)_ Follow-up to #10. This replaces the plain select on the Keyless card's "GitHub repository" field. ## What changes - **Searchable combobox** (`web/src/components/RepoCombobox.tsx`, built from cmdk in a radix popover): - Fuzzy search: by prefix, by substring, or by letters in order (`tfw` finds `tiny-firewall`). Full keyboard navigation. - With an empty query, a **"Suggested for this app"** group comes first, then all repos A–Z. - Repos that already publish another app are shown but disabled, labelled "publishes X". Before this PR they were hidden. - Private repos get a lock icon. - **The best match is pre-selected** and tagged "Best match", so most of the time you just press Connect. It is only pre-selected when the match is confident and clearly ahead of the runner-up. Once you pick something yourself, it stays. - **Scoring** (`web/src/lib/repoMatch.ts`). Each repo name is scored against the app's slug and the tail of each package id (`io.nesin.feedbackbee` → `feedbackbee`). The score combines: - TF-IDF cosine over word tokens, with IDF computed over your repo list. A rare shared word counts for a lot; `android`, `app` and reverse-DNS noise count for nothing. - Character-trigram Dice similarity, so `gold-view` matches `goldview` and small typos still match. - Bonuses when the names match exactly after stripping separators, or when one contains the other. Results on a sample list of repos: | app | picked | runner-up | |---|---|---| | feedbackbee | feedbackbee (3.10) | feedback-widget (0.36) | | tinyfirewall | tiny-firewall (2.62) | tinyfirewall-landing (1.45) | | goldview | goldview-android (1.59) | gold (0.84) | | groot | groot (3.10) | groot-mobile-app (1.43) | | myapp (no match) | nothing pre-selected | | ## Testing - `pnpm --dir web typecheck` and `go test ./srv` pass. - Checked in the built UI with mocked GitHub responses: the best match is pre-selected, the suggested group shows, and searching `tfw` lists both tiny-firewall repos. --- _Generated by [Claude Code](https://claude.ai/code)_ --- ## Summary by cubic Replaces the plain select on the Keyless card's GitHub repository field with a searchable combobox that pre-selects the most likely repo, so connecting is usually one click. - Fuzzy search matches by prefix, substring, or letters in order (`tfw` finds `tiny-firewall`), with full keyboard navigation. - An empty query shows a "Suggested for this app" group first, then all repos A–Z. Repos that already publish another app now appear disabled instead of hidden, and private repos get a lock icon. - The best match is pre-selected and tagged "Best match" only when the scoring is confident and clearly ahead of the runner-up. Once you pick a repo yourself, the pre-selection stops. - Repo matching (`web/src/lib/repoMatch.ts`) scores each repo name against the app's slug and package-id tails using TF-IDF cosine over word tokens (IDF computed over the repo list), character-trigram Dice similarity, and bonuses for exact or contained matches. Rewrites the README's setup section so anyone can install and run TorFinder on macOS or Windows, says where to get every `.env` value, and corrects the demo-account table. Also adds `.gitattributes`, without which the Docker stack can't start from a Windows checkout.

Closes #

## Type of change

- **README, Getting started:** four steps (install tools → clone and create `.env` → fill in `.env` → start), each with macOS and Windows (PowerShell) commands, including how to generate `SESSION_SECRET` on both; a troubleshooting list (port in use, short secret, CRLF on Windows); running without Docker, including the TLS-only Docker database.

body:
**Problem:** if `ORIGIN_AUTH` were ever dropped from `greatread-secrets`, the origin check turned itself off, even with `ORIGIN_AUTH_MODE=enforce`. The `run.app` URL would then accept direct calls and skip the WAF, with nothing to show for it.

**Fix:** in enforce mode, a missing secret now stops the server at startup. A new revision without the secret fails its startup check, so Cloud Run keeps traffic on the last good revision. A deploy that loses the secret becomes a visible failed revision instead of a silently open origin. Local development, where `ORIGIN_AUTH_MODE` is unset, is unchanged.

Checked locally against `server/utils/originAuth.js`:

| Case | Result |
|---|---|
| enforce, no secret | throws at load |
| enforce, right header | passes |
| enforce, wrong header | 403 |
| enforce, no header | 403 |
| dev mode, no secret | passes |

Production has both values today: `greatread-secrets` holds a non-empty `ORIGIN_AUTH` (I checked key names only), and the service env has `ORIGIN_AUTH_MODE=enforce`. So the deploy this merge starts will come up normally.

**Deploys:** this touches `server/**`, so merging starts the Cloud Build backend deploy. After it, I'll check that `api.greatread.himaiz.com` answers and the `run.app` URL still returns 403.

## Summary

When Zed updated from this fork's GitHub releases, connecting to a remote SSH/Docker/WSL host without a preinstalled matching `~/.zed_server` binary failed to install the remote server automatically because:

1. `fork_release.yml` built `zed-remote-server-{macos,linux,windows}-{x86_64,aarch64}.{gz,zip}` in every bundle job, but did not upload or publish them in the GitHub release or `release.json`.

- `crates/auto_update/src/auto_update.rs`: Resolve remote server download URLs and local cache downloads from `belizariogr/zed` GitHub releases (`fork-v{major}.{minor}.{patch}/release.json`, falling back to `releases/latest/download/release.json` for custom `fork-v*` tags of the same version), handle both `.gz` and `.zip` in cache naming/cleanup, and add unit tests.
- `AGENTS.md`: Update the fork personalization table to record remote server publishing and resolution.

author: ovler-young
body:
After the account is logged out and the QR code is scanned again, loading
the new session (contact list, message handlers) can take half a minute.
Until now, "Successfully logged in." was shown as soon as the QR code was
scanned, and messages sent in that window still went through the expired
session and failed with a misleading "session might be expired" error,
which suggested restarting EWS.

Changes:
- Outgoing messages and message recalls wait for the new session to be
  ready (up to 120 seconds). If it is not ready in time they fail with
  "WeChat is re-logging in, please retry later." instead of the
  session-expired error.
- Two notices instead of one: "Scanned successfully, loading contacts…"
  when the QR code is confirmed, and "Switch complete, you can send and
  receive messages now." once the new session is in use.
- If logging in again fails, the error is sent to the master channel
  (not only to the log) and waiting messages are released.
- The first login at startup is unchanged: nothing waits and no extra
  notice is sent.

New strings are not yet in the translation catalogs.

Tests: tests/test_reauth.py covers waiting for the new session, the
timeout error, the notice order, failure reporting and the first login.

## Ownership claim

- Machine ID: `martbot-mbp-m5-max-128`
- Computer: `MacBook Pro`
- Agent/session ID: `claude-22-speed`
- Task: chokepoint site bonus kept per site
- Claimed paths: `src/ai/advanced/chokepoints.rs`, `src/world.rs`
- Coordinated with: none
- Related issue/request: operator /loop 2026-11-22 (self-play games well under 10 s end to end)

## What changed

`chokepoint_site_bonus` (gene `chokepoint-siting`) prices a candidate city site from the turn's chokepoint readings of the 37 tiles in its three rings and each ring tile's owning city. A settle scan prices every candidate, and every settler and every replan frame scans again, so the same site was priced over and over: `narrows_at` was 1.4–2.4% of a gene-screen game when a seat drew the gene.

The bonus is now kept per site in the turn's `NarrowsAtlas`, valid while the map is **the very tile allocation it was priced on** (`TileGrid::shares_tiles_with`, a pointer comparison; the map is copied on its first write, so a shared allocation means no tile has changed). Any write starts the kept bonuses afresh, and a new turn clears them with the readings they were built from. The readings themselves are untouched: a site priced from memory read them, through the same turn cache, when it was first priced.

A first version kept the untouched rings across a write by comparing the two maps tile by tile (`TileGrid::differing_positions`); it played the same games and cost **+8.3%** instructions on one seed, because the map is rewritten far more often than a site is asked twice.

## Evidence

Paired `gene_screen` runs (one game each, release profile less LTO with 16 codegen units, both arms from this branch's merge-base, launched together):

| seed | instructions | cycles | rows |
| --- | ---: | ---: | --- |
| 20261009638634 | −3.09% | −2.3% | identical |
| 20261009638635 | −0.00% | −0.2% | identical |
| 20261009638636 | −0.80% | −0.6% | identical |

(The saving follows the gene: an opt-in screened at the draw probability, so games without it are unchanged.)

2026-11-22 に決めた方針（ゲストに Firebase の匿名認証を使う、同期の途絶えた席は30分で片付ける）のサーバー側です。#63・#72・#76 に対応します。アプリ側は #82 です。

## 変更内容

- Firebase の匿名ユーザーのトークンを受け付けます。匿名ユーザーにもサインイン中のユーザーと同じ「1人1席、座り直すと前の席を解放」を適用します (#63, #76)
- 匿名のトークンで作られた席には `ownerAnonymous: true` を記録します。トークンなしのゲストの席と同じく、セッション ID を持つ呼び出し元なら離席・同期できます。ゲストが着席中に Google でサインインしても離席できるようにするためです
- 学習履歴の API は匿名ユーザーを 403 で拒否します
- 同期のない席を片付けるまでの時間を24時間から30分に縮め、掃除のジョブを毎時から10分ごとにします (#72, #76)
- Identity Platform の匿名ログインを有効にします（`terraform/identity.tf`）
- トークンを送らない古いアプリ（1.2.1 以前）は今までどおり使えます

## 確認

- `go vet`・`go test` が通りました。codex-reviewer のレビューは承認でした
- terraform の plan は dev・本番とも「既存の変更3件（匿名ログイン、掃除のジョブ、API のイメージ）、追加・削除0件」でした。dev には適用済みです（API v19）
- dev で次を確かめました
  - 新しいアプリのゲストの席に、匿名ユーザーの UID と `ownerAnonymous: true` が記録される
  - 着席の応答前にアプリを落として残った席が、同じゲストが別の席に座ると消える (#76)
  - ゲストで座ったまま Google でサインインしても離席できる
  - 着席中のサインアウトで席が解放される (#72)
- 画面を消して端末を強制的にアイドル状態（Doze）にしても、学習中の通知が出ていれば同期は5分ごとに続きました（16分間で3回）。通知を拒否した端末では試していません

## 残すこと

author: axl47
body:
Every T3 thread shared three emulators, so agents stomped on each other: one thread would open or modify the emulator another was using mid-test. Now each ward has an emulator of its own. It starts on the first adb command that needs a device, only that ward can reach it, it stops when idle or when the ward stops, and the next use gets a fresh one.

## How it works

- A ward's device is a read-only instance of one base AVD that Ward builds and keeps, run on the host as a transient unit. It boots from a snapshot in about 5 s (about 45 s the first time, while the base image is built) and leaves nothing behind when it stops.
- Each ward runs a stock adb server of its own. Port 5037 is no longer forwarded from the host, and the ward's broker relays only that ward's device ports, so the ward's server can find exactly one device. Nothing parses or filters adb to decide access: the network namespace does. `adb reverse`, `adb forward`, Gradle, Expo and React Native work unchanged.
- `wardd` reads only the first request of each adb connection, to decide whether to boot the device, then copies bytes.
- A device stops after 15 minutes without use (`WARD_DEVICE_IDLE`), with its ward, or with `ward device stop`. At most 8 run at once (`WARD_DEVICE_MAX`).
- `ward device` and `ward devices --json` are the contract T3 uses to open a ward's device in its Device panel and keep other threads off it.
- Your own AVDs are hidden inside wards, and emulator ports can't be forwarded into them.

Also fixes transfers through ward relays running up to twenty times slower than on the host (`TCP_NODELAY`).

## Upgrade

Wards already running keep the old behavior (the host's adb server, no device of their own) until they are stopped and started; `ward device` exits 3 for them. `units/` is unchanged, so `systemctl --user restart wardd` is enough.

## Verified

In a second Ward instance beside the installed one:

- Two agents doing ordinary Android work in two wards at once (install, launch, screenshot, logcat, tunnels on the same port numbers, 300 MB push and pull): each saw only its own serial; the other ward's device, the shared emulators and a phone were "not found".
- Gradle `installDebug` booted the device by itself and installed, and again after the device was stopped under a living Gradle daemon, after `adb disconnect` and after `adb kill-server`.
- Idle stop; a fresh device after the emulator was killed from the host; the cap; a ward stop taking the device, also mid-boot; devices taken up again across `wardd` restarts; a stray adb server evicted from a ward's port 5037.
- With Annex: T3's Device panel opened and streamed a ward's device, refused other wards' devices to the thread, and got a fresh one after a stop.

Not run: a snapshot that fails to load, an emulator that survives its unit's stop, `wardd` starting the host's adb server, and a ward started before this change answering `ward device` (checked on the installed Ward after the upgrade).

`pnpm typecheck` passes; tests: 47 pass, 1 skipped.

Reviewed in four rounds by GPT-6.2 Sol and by Claude Opus 5.5 (against the design, on the goal alone, and a final ship review); design advice from Claude Fable 5.2. Details and limits: `docs/DESIGN.md`, "Devices".

author: lord007tn
body:
## What

Fixes #202 and #203, and sweeps placeholder data as a class (the maintainer's follow-up from #187).

### #202: overview drill-downs select exactly what their widgets show

- **One definition for "Recent problems".** The contract now exports `RECENT_PROBLEM_OUTCOMES` (`failure`, `denied`) and `RECENT_PROBLEM_SEVERITY` (`critical`). The server's list (`packages/clickhouse/src/queries.ts`) and the console's "View all" link (`(outcome:failure OR outcome:denied OR severity:critical)`) are both built from them.
  - On the demo project, View all used to open 696 events, leaving out critical successes and including `unknown` outcomes. It now opens 870, the group the list draws from.
- **The chart's Other band** opens `-outcome:success -outcome:partial -outcome:denied -outcome:failure`: `unknown` and every custom outcome, which is what the band counts. It used to open only `outcome:unknown`. The chart's folding and the link share `NAMED_OUTCOMES` (`lib/overview-queries.ts`).
- **Tests** (`overview-queries.test.ts`): for every band, the outcomes the chart counts in it are exactly the ones its link selects. The set covers the contract outcomes, custom ones and a differently-cased "Success". Field matching is exact, as in the query compiler.

### #203: shared ranges must name a window

- `isValidRange` accepts only:
  - `all`;
  - a positive relative duration whose start can be represented (from 1970 to 9999);
  - two representable instants, in order.
- **Rejected:** `0d`, `0h` and `0m`; `99999999999d`; reversed, equal or malformed absolute ranges; years outside 1970–9999. `resolveRange` uses the same rule, so an invalid value falls back to the default instead of throwing in the top bar.
- **Tests** cover zero, huge, reversed, equal, extra-`..`, pre-1970 and year-275760 ranges.

### Placeholder data is never current (as a class)

Project queries keep the previous answer while a new key loads (`keepPreviousInProject`). That answer belongs to another range, search, entity or page.

- **One helper:** `lib/api/current.ts`.
  - `current(query)` returns the data only when it answers the current key.
  - `awaiting(query)` is true for a first load or a placeholder.
- **Consumers swept:**
  - **Overview.** Switching ranges showed the old range's KPIs, chart and lists under the new label: 2,735 "events" under "Last 7 days" while the 7-day answer loaded. It now shows skeletons.
  - **Fields** page: coverage.
  - **Workspace activity:** rows and the count line.
  - **Support-agent page:** the agent's name came from another agent's own-account facet; the activity chart.
  - **Entity directory:** while a new search loads, the previous rows stay dimmed with `aria-busy`, and the "No matches" state and type chips only describe the current answer.
- **Moved onto the helper:** Explorer, entity profile, support split and the retention preview.
- **One rule, one test pattern.** Components never read `query.data` of a placeholder-enabled project query.
  - They read `current(query)`, or `shownDimmed(query)` where the old answer is shown on purpose. Only the entity directory does that, dimmed with `aria-busy`.
  - `lib/api/current.test.tsx` has a real `QueryClient` render test: the previous range's answer is never shown under the new range.
  - A guard finds every query with `placeholderData` in `lib/api/queries.ts` and every result built from one (directly or through an options variable), and flags any direct `x.data` read.
  - The guard uses no heuristics, and new queries and consumers are covered automatically. Its fixtures cover:
    - a second, unguarded query in a file that already uses the helpers;
    - an options variable;
    - reads after a mention, a negated mention, an `if` either way, or a comment;
    - reads through the helpers.
- **Header range picker on entity pages.** With no range chosen, an entity page's History shows everything, while its summary (stats, support split, activity chart) follows the range. The picker now says what it scopes: "Summary: Last 24 hours" (`useRange().wholeHistory`). History names its own all-time scope. Picking a range narrows History too.

**Contract change (additive):** `RECENT_PROBLEM_OUTCOMES` and `RECENT_PROBLEM_SEVERITY`. The server SQL is unchanged in effect.

## How verified

Real services (the demo workspace on the shared Postgres and ClickHouse):

- **View all:** the URL gets `(outcome:failure OR outcome:denied OR severity:critical)`, showing "870 events · Last 7 days". On master it was `-outcome:success -outcome:partial` with 696.
- **Invalid ranges:** `range=0d`, `99999999999d` and a reversed absolute range each fall back to "Last 24 hours" without errors.
- **Slow switch:** with the overview response held for 3 s, switching 24h → 7d shows skeletons. On master it showed the 24h numbers under "Last 7 days".
- **Entity header:** a tenant page with no range chosen shows "Summary: Last 24 hours".
- **Checks:**
  - app tests: 466 pass (new: overview-queries, current, range validation);
  - contracts tests: 6 pass;
  - `tsc` passes (app, contracts, clickhouse);
  - `biome check` is clean;
  - `pnpm --filter @logbird/app build` passes;
  - CI runs the full gate.

### Screenshots

`marketing/captures/2026-11-22-overview-drilldowns/` (Git LFS):

- `overview-range-switch-loading-before.png` and `-after.png`;
- `recent-problems-view-all-before.png` and `-after.png`;
- `entity-header-summary-label-after.png`.

### Review round 2

- **The guard.** Rounds 2–4 tried branch heuristics, and each left an edge. It now forbids every direct `.data` read, and reads go through `current()` or `shownDimmed()`. Along the way it found real reads, now fixed:
  - the Explorer's ms timing and zoom bounds;
  - the Explorer's last-good bookkeeping and the facet sidebar, now on `current()`;
  - the directory's rows, now explicitly `shownDimmed`.
- **No allow-list.** Autocomplete reads the current range's field coverage and samples, and shows loading while they arrive.
- **Ranges.**
  - `?range=0` or `?range=true` (decoded as a number or boolean) is dropped at the project route boundary. The Explorer and workspace activity then open their defaults (24h and 90d), checked in the browser.
  - Absolute endpoints must be real dates (no Feb 30, no 24:00) and within ClickHouse's DateTime64 calendar (up to 2299).
  - A stored or shared invalid range is labelled as the default it opens: a saved view with `0d` reads "Last 24 hours", not "Last 0 days".
- **Exact links.** The overview's Top actions and Recent problems rows use `formatExactTerm`, so `billing*` is not a prefix search.
- **Membership tests.** Every outcome lands in exactly one band, and only that band's link selects it. Recent problems is compared event by event with the server predicate, including a critical success and an ordinary `unknown`.
- **Entity and support-agent Other bands** use the same `outcomeBandQuery`.
- **Quality:** the Biome findings are fixed, and `pnpm check` passes locally.

Follow-up (guard hardening from the final review): #224.

## Release notes

- **Fix:** the overview's "View all" and chart bands open exactly the events they show.
- **Fix:** shared links with impossible ranges fall back to the default instead of breaking the page.
- **Fix:** pages no longer show the previous range's or search's numbers while the new ones load.
- **Fix:** on entity pages, the range picker says it scopes the summary while History shows everything.
- **Self-hosters:** nothing to do.

Closes #202
Closes #203

author: lcian
body:
Review guides could only be written by Codex or Claude. Picking Antigravity fell back to one of them, or failed when neither was set up.

Antigravity now investigates the checkout read-only, the way Codex does in its sandbox:

- Each guide runs `agy acp --sandbox` with a throwaway profile: `toolPermission: "proceed-in-sandbox"` and `enableTerminalSandbox`, so commands run in agy's terminal sandbox (no writes, no network) without prompting. The profile links the instance's saved sign-in, so a token agy refreshes during the run lands in the real file.
- Permission rules go in `config/config.json` under `userSettings.globalPermissionGrants`: agy 1.5 loads them from there over ACP and ignores `permissions` in `settings.json`. They allow reading the checkout (and the common git dir of a linked worktree) and deny writes, MCP and URL reads. There are no command allow rules, because those let a call that leaves the sandbox run unprompted.
-  agy runs `.agents/hooks.json` hooks from its working directory outside the sandbox, even in an untrusted workspace, and no flag or setting turns them off, so the agent starts in an empty working directory and is told to run `git -C <checkout>`.
- T3 refuses every approval request (an approval only comes when a command tries to leave the sandbox), and fails the guide if a subagent or any non-read tool completes.

Antigravity instances with hooks or MCP servers stay excluded from text generation, as before. Where the terminal sandbox is unavailable, the guide fails instead of running unsandboxed.

Checked end to end with agy 1.5.14 on macOS against a real commit, with gemini-3.8-flash and claude-sonnet-5-5: the guide came back, a canary hook in the checkout never ran, and the checkout was unchanged.

Written by Claude Fable 5.2 in Claude Code, running in T3 Code.

author: th0rgal
body:
## Fix

Remote Core observers stamped up to eight 256 KiB log pages with a time captured before the first fetch. A busy stream could therefore display events minutes before a worker actually finished its command. The observer now samples the ingestion time for each line and updates the checkpoint and settlement times after their respective reads. Tool execution timestamps remain in the event payload.

For every appended event, the old sequence allocator scanned the entire mission inside its write transaction. Two indexed maxima preserve mixed native and imported sequences and avoid that scan. Both append and startup recovery use the same query.

## Verification

The new Core integration test opens an old database with a legacy event table, runs the normal migration, and adds native-format events. A loopback node delivers delayed ACP pages and a final line without a newline. The test checks stream order, contiguous numbering, fresh ingestion times, and the original tool timestamps. It runs in the native CI test job.

A matched pair of x86 Core binaries replayed the same 1,796 events after a 24,001-row imported/mixed history (three isolated runs per binary). Sequence numbers were 24,002 through 25,797 each time. The old build backdated the later events in all three runs. The corrected build retained every fragment and its order, stamped the delayed pages on arrival, and preserved the supplied tool execution times in all three runs.

| Elapsed from first log fetch through persisted final answer | Three runs | Median |
| --- | --- | --- |
| Baseline | 12.564, 12.803, 12.116 s | 12.564 s |
| Corrected | 3.406, 3.802, 3.714 s | 3.714 s |

These times include the same two 1.1-second worker delays. The SQL sequence query alone fell from 3.495 ms to 0.0014 ms in a warmed SQLite fixture of the same size, with EXPLAIN confirming both covering indexes.

body:
`mvt-android check-androidqf -m MODULE` filtered only the top-level AndroidQF modules. When the archive holds `bugreport.zip`, `backup.ab` or an `intrusion_logs` folder, `check-androidqf` runs the corresponding nested command — built without `module_name` — so every nested module ran regardless of the filter.

Pass `self.module_name` to all three nested commands: a filter naming an AndroidQF module now runs exactly that module (the nested commands find no module of that name and run none, as `_selected_modules` already defines), and a filter naming a nested module selects it from the nested command.

Verified manually: `check-androidqf -m AQFGetProp` over an archive containing `bugreport.zip` runs AQFGetProp alone (previously AQFGetProp plus every bugreport module); `-m DumpsysPackages` selects it from the nested bugreport command.

author: ttmarkka
body:
## Problem

`Capability` did two jobs in one class:

- it held a ready-made tool, chain, or skill: `Capability(label=..., value=stop)`;
- it was the contract that subclasses implement by overriding `build()`.

Its `build()` switched between the two on whether a value had been given. Nothing in the signature said which job an instance had, every subclass carried a `value` that was always `None`, and a capability with neither a value nor a `build()` was constructed without error and failed only when the agent was built.

## Change

There is now one way to make a capability: subclass `Capability` and return the tools or skills from `build()`.

- `Capability` is an abstract base class (`abc.ABC`). `build()` is abstract and `value` is gone. `required_attributes` and the routing of built values are unchanged.
- `roboz.shed.capabilities.Stop()` provides the `stop` tool. The orchestrator uses it in place of `Capability(label=ToolLabel("stop"), value=stop)`.
- `roboz tool init` and `roboz skill init` create a subclass.

## Tests

- Shed tests use `Stop()`.
- The three core files that test the deployment machinery with many combinations (`tests/unit/test_deployment.py`, `test_capability_selection.py`, `test_deployment_dependencies.py`) and one core end-to-end test use a small local test class whose `build()` returns the value it was given.
- New: `Capability` and a subclass without `build()` cannot be constructed (`tests/unit/test_deployment.py`), and pyright rejects constructing `Capability` (`tests/type_tests/cases/expected_failures/test_capability_without_build.py`).
- The distribution test builds the generated capabilities and no longer reads `.value`.

## Breaking

Replace each `Capability(label=..., value=...)` with a subclass whose `build()` returns the value in a tuple. Subclasses that already implement `build()` need no change. There is no alias for the old form.

Packages made earlier with `roboz tool init` or `roboz skill init` contain the old form and need that edit.

## Stack

Stack #210, in merge order: #205, this one, #209, then the release #208.

## Checks

Run locally with uv 0.12.10 on Python 3.13:

- `uv run pytest`: 2147 passed, 30 skipped
- the distribution job as CI runs it: `uv build`, `twine check`, `check-wheel-contents`, `pytest tests/distributions --dist <dir>`: 13 passed
- `uv run python -m roboz.examples.simple`
- `uv run ruff check`
- `uv run pyright`
- `bash scripts/run_type_tests.sh`
- `git diff --check`

author: deandromi
body:
The layer above `fuzz_msc`: the phase machine and the enumeration state.

**`tests/usb/fuzz_mode`** walks the real `disk_mode.c` with a fixed seed — random control requests, CBWs of the wrong length, data when no command expects it, stray completions, resets and disconnects — and after every event checks that state and phase stay in range, that the window never moves, and that a read-only mode never reaches `write()`. Then a liveness check: after any walk, a bus reset, a fresh `SET_CONFIGURATION` and a valid INQUIRY must still be answered within a bounded number of completions. Plus the 100 connect/disconnect cycles from T-115, on the mock.

**What it found:** after the medium was released, the mode still ran commands. A host that had not noticed the eject could send one more `WRITE(10)` and it went straight at the block device — the volume the rest of the firmware believes it owns. `handle_cbw()` now refuses anything unless the state is `ENUMERATED`, counts the packet and stays idle. `test_disk_mode` pins it and asserts the fake disk records no write.

**Sizes:** Disk Mode image 40,524 B; bootloader image 108,296 B, sha256 `de9b67e3…`; DFU 116,432 B, `e27d3b38…`; `_moveend` 20,736 B inside `MOVE_AREA`. Normal firmware unchanged at 80,008 B. Full host matrix green, both fuzzers clean under ASan/UBSan. No device run.

La recherche du menu Démarrer montrait le groupe « PuTTY (64-bit) » du menu comme un dossier, avec le sous-titre `~/AppData/Roaming/Microsoft/Windows/Start Menu/Programs` et le même chemin dans l'infobulle. C'est contraire à la règle qui interdit toute marque Microsoft à l'écran.

## Correction

- Les sous-dossiers de `Start Menu/Programs` ne sont plus des résultats. Ce sont les groupes du menu, et leurs applications sont déjà listées. Leurs raccourcis étaient déjà exclus depuis #992.
- `file_place()` nomme le dossier d'un fichier trouvé. Ailleurs, `~/…` s'affiche comme avant. Sous AppData, le sous-titre devient « Menu Démarrer » ou « Données des programmes › PuTTY », sans chemin interne, en quatre langues. L'infobulle suit le même libellé.

## Ce qui est vérifié

- `scripts/test-start-search-appdata.py` sous Xvfb (CI et test-all) : la recherche « putty » ne montre pas le groupe, montre `putty.exe` sous « Données des programmes › PuTTY », et aucun texte ni infobulle de la fenêtre ne contient « Microsoft » ou « AppData ». Sur master, ce test échoue (résultat « PuTTY (64-bit) »).
- `scripts/campagne.d/2905-recherche-appdata.py`.
- `test-start-search.py` et `test-no-microsoft-branding.py` passent.

## Lot

Ce correctif touche `winlux-start-menu.py`, comme #2860 et #2903 : il ne doit pas aller dans le même lot qu'eux.

## Relais

Patch relayé par le fil auteur (sha256 e9c82232…, base 563f4b1a, arbre fcaafc7c vérifié après `git am`), auteur conservé, puis master 7a1d89f6 fusionné. fmt, clippy 1.100 et tests unitaires passent ; seul `msi::tests::dossiers_du_profil_sous_users_compte` échoue dans le conteneur, de même sur master nu (TempFolder du conteneur). Les tests Python sous Xvfb ne peuvent pas tourner dans le conteneur (module gi cassé) : la CI les joue.

## Provenance

Code Winlux seulement. Défaut vu dans une VM installée depuis l'ISO v0.2.21 pendant un tournage (relayé dans le projet le 22 novembre) ; la cause a été lue dans le code et n'a pas été observée dans la VM.

author: jortega0033
body:
## What changed

- `/next-ticket` is sub-issue aware: only leaf tickets are work. A ticket labelled `tracking` or `epic`, or one with open sub-issues, is a container and is never picked. A parent whose sub-issues are all closed is closed with a comment, and the pull request of the last open sub-issue also says `Closes #<parent>`.
- The review gate hook (`.claude/hooks/role_gate.py`) is updated so it works when a ticket runs in a separate worktree.
- Code Reviewer and Reality Checker have no shell, so the driver writes the diff, the diff stat and each check output to `.claude/state/review/` before the gates and names those files in the request. Steps that need a person are done as far as an agent can, and the rest goes under "Owner checks" in the pull request.
- CI is awaited without polling: the pull request is bound to the session where the app offers it, the turn ends with "Draft pull request #N is waiting for CI", and CI is read once on wake-up.
- `.claude/settings.json` adds ask rules at any depth for agent, skill, hook, settings and agency-agent files, so a ticket never changes agent configuration. `CLAUDE.md` and the two agent definitions are updated to match.

## Why

The large-file-browser-editor pilot run showed that a ticket breakdown with parent and sub-issue levels was picked wrong (a container could be taken as work), that the reviewer roles could not see the diff, that the gate hook did not cope with worktrees, and that polling for CI wasted turns and tokens. The ticket breakdown now uses parents with leaf sub-issues, and the driver and playbook follow it.

## Self-test

```
$ python .claude/hooks/role_gate.py --self-test
role_gate self-test passed (gate roles: Code Reviewer, Reality Checker)
```

No runtime code or product tests changed.

Hardening change: merged by the orchestrator after CI.

## 🧪 Find performance regressions (PERFORMANCE-20261122-1D29)

Generated by **TestForge** in its `performance` workflow (find performance regressions). Strategy approved by a reviewer (revision 1). Please review it like any other change.

### Summary

Commit 72802a9 ("Show each line's product name on an order") added a third sequential store round trip (productNames) to GET /orders/:id, raising the `detail` scenario's p95 from 22 ms to 31 ms (+44.3%, 32 ms on rerun). Guard it with a scenario-tagged p95 threshold in perf/orders.js at the baseline plus 20% headroom (existing thresholds, checks and scenarios kept unchanged), record the defect and file it for a person to fix.

### Acceptance criteria coverage

| AC | Criterion | Test cases |
|---|---|---|
| AC1* | The detail scenario's p95 http_req_duration stays within 20% of the last good runs' baseline (22 ms), i.e. below 26.4 ms | TC1 |

\* Derived from the description: the ticket had no explicit criterion.

### Test cases

| ID | Title | Level | Framework | Type | Priority | Covers | File |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| TC1 | http_req_duration{scenario:detail}: p(95)<26.4 | performance | k6 | performance | high | AC1 | `perf/orders.js` |

_Case titles corrected by the agent after approval (the approved ones are in the strategy file (`.testforge/PERFORMANCE-20261122-1D29/strategy.md`)); check each still tests what was approved:_

- TC1: approved “detail scenario keeps p95 latency under 26.4 ms”, tested as “http_req_duration{scenario:detail}: p(95)<26.4”

### Slowdowns and their outcomes

Each scenario metric that got worse than the last good runs past the threshold, and again on a rerun: whether its k6 script now has a threshold that fails on it, its issue, and the commit it first slowed at.

| Scenario | Script | Metric | Threshold | Issue | First slow commit |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| detail | `perf/orders.js` | p95 latency: 22 ms → 31 ms | Yes | Recorded; its issue is still to be filed | `72802a9fba0d` Show each line's product name on an order |

### Results

| Framework | Passed | Failed | Skipped | Status |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| k6 | 2 | 0 | 0 | ✅ |

Self-heal rounds: 1.

### ⚠️ Suspected product defects

These tests are marked expected-to-fail because the application appears not to meet the acceptance criteria. Please triage.

- **Order detail p95 latency up 44% since product names were added (extra store round trip)** (TC1) in `perf/orders.js`: perf/orders.js › detail (GET /orders/:id): p95 latency 22 ms (median of 5 good runs, range 21–24 ms) → 31 ms (+44.3%), 32 ms on rerun. Bisect: first slow at 72802a9fba0d "Show each line's product name on an order". The diff adds `await productNames(...)` in src/app.js's order route after findOrder and orderLines; productNames (src/store.js) does its own roundTrip() (~6–9 ms). The request now makes 3 sequential store queries instead of 2. The commit message says the names come "in one query with the lines", but they're fetched in a separate query. Fix: return each line's product name from orderLines' existing query (it already joins products for priceCents), or run the lookup in parallel. The threshold 'http_req_duration{scenario:detail}': p(95)<26.4 (baseline + 20%) guards it.
  > k6 run perf/orders.js on 35eaba9: ✗ 'p(95)<26.4' p(95)=31.38ms for {scenario:detail}; "thresholds on metrics 'http_req_duration{scenario:detail}' have been crossed", exit 99.

### Notes from the agent

Guards the confirmed slowdown in perf/orders.js › detail. Its p95 went from 22 ms to 31 ms (+44.3%, 32 ms on rerun), first slow at 72802a9 "Show each line's product name on an order". That commit adds a third sequential store round trip, `productNames()`, in addition to findOrder and orderLines on GET /orders/:id (~6–9 ms per round trip in src/store.js).

- Added threshold `'http_req_duration{scenario:detail}': ['p(95)<26.4']` (22 ms baseline + 20%). The existing thresholds, checks and scenarios are unchanged. The full load run now fails on it as intended (p95 = 31.38 ms on 35eaba9, exit 99) until the application is fixed.
- Added a `default` export that calls `list()` and `detail()` once. Smoke runs (`--vus 1 --iterations 1`) override the scenarios and need a default function; without it k6 refused the script ("function 'default' not found in exports"). The named scenarios don't use it.
- Not guarded, because the work item rates them as noise: detail p99 (+36.5%, cv 5.3%), search p95 (−72.8%, cv 40.9%) and search p99 (−18.4%). perf/search.js is untouched.

### Suggested follow-ups

- Remove the extra round trip on GET /orders/:id (return product names from orderLines' query); perf/orders.js's detail p95 threshold fails until then
- Run perf/*.js under load (k6 run, with the app started on BASE_URL) in CI so the thresholds gate merges

### Assumptions & open questions

- Assumption: Threshold derived from the baseline median p95 22 ms with the run's 20% headroom: p(95)<26.4
- Assumption: The app runs for real at BASE_URL (default http://localhost:4310); nothing is faked
- Assumption: run_tests runs k6 with --no-thresholds in smoke mode, so the counted run proves the script runs, not that the threshold passes; under real load it is expected to fail until the app is fast again
- Assumption: The existing script is only extended: its scenarios, checks and global thresholds stay as they are
