author: amirenuradil
body:
As the team asked, this replaces the previous Afterimage files with a new ArtTech entry built from the brief in `docs/ARTTECH-BRIEF-RU.txt`. Earlier work stays in git history; nothing on `main` was rewritten.

## What it is

**Тон дня** is a static, browser-only diary in Russian. The author writes about a day and adds 1–6 photos and a song, as a file or a described link. Explicit rules then turn the day into an animated 4:5 page that plays with the song, and save a folder named after the day.

- **Text** (`src/text.js`) gives tone (light/dark), pace (quiet/lively), nostalgia, and a 3–7 word folder title. Example: «Ночь в офисе перед сдачей».
- **Photos** (`src/photo.js`) give the palette (k-means), light and warmth.
- **Music** (`src/music.js`) is analysed in the browser for tempo, energy and major/minor key. Noise and a steady hum correctly report no beat and no key.
- **Rules** (`src/system.js`) pick one of five techniques from where the day sits on the tone × pace axes:
  - Monet-style brushstrokes: bright and quiet.
  - Seurat-style dots: bright and lively.
  - Kandinsky-style geometry: dark and lively.
  - Japanese ink and empty space: dark and quiet.
  - Old amateur film: strong nostalgia or an old song.

  The song counts for 65% of pace, so on a borderline day the song alone can change the technique. Every visual decision records its reason, shown under «Почему этот день выглядит так».
- **Day folder:** entry, photos, song or link, `memory.webm` video, poster, voice script, a standalone `memory.html` player and `day.json`. Chromium saves a real folder; other browsers get a ZIP.
- **For the demo:**
  - The diary mood map.
  - Replaying the same day with another song as a temporary preview. The archive and the folder keep the saved version.
  - A live reading panel in the editor.
  - A voice-over whose speed and pitch follow the rules.

## How to check

```bash
git fetch origin claude/zen-noether-t6r64k
git checkout claude/zen-noether-t6r64k
npm ci
npm test
npm run build
npm run preview
```

Open http://localhost:4173. With a global Playwright installed, `node scripts/check-browser.mjs` runs the end-to-end check while the preview server is up.

## Verification

- `npm test`: 25 pass, 0 fail. `npm run build`: OK, about 1.9 MB `dist/`. `npm audit`: 0 vulnerabilities. All three were checked from a clean clone.
- `scripts/check-browser.mjs` passes in Chromium. It covers:
  - All six samples get their expected technique and folder name.
  - The live editor reading.
  - Days created from a file and from a link.
  - Playback and mute.
  - A saved folder with a video, whose `memory.html` plays.
  - A song preview that moves the office day from Kandinsky to ink, while a folder saved during that preview still holds the saved song and design.
  - Reload and search.
  - The phone layout at 390 px with no horizontal scroll.
- Further checks, run with throwaway scripts kept outside the repository:
  - Edge inputs: fake or broken files, http links, 6 mixed photos including 4000×3000, a 3000-character entry, an emoji-only entry, noise, silence.
  - Keyboard and Escape, reduced motion, delete.
  - Offline from a nested subfolder: zero external requests.
  - 60 fps playback for every technique.

## Not verified here

- The voice-over: the test browser has no speech voices.
- Saving a real folder in Chrome: tests force the ZIP fallback.
- Playback and recording on the team's own machines.

Limits are listed in `SUBMISSION.md`: mood comes from a Russian/English word list, linked songs use the author's description, and the voice is not recorded into the video.

Sample media are fictional: ImageGen illustrations and scores synthesized by `scripts/compose-demo-audio.py`. The beach score was regenerated at 118 BPM.

## Preview consistency and dependency — issue #293 (2026-11-22)

The same one-file release notes have been updated on this work branch to place `stable_tag: v0.1.4` and `promotion_pr: 289` in a **strict leading HTML comment**. This hides the unwanted YAML-table preview in GitHub while keeping exact source authority and the existing user-friendly narrative intact. This revision is **commit `df81cdaafb723c7bcfc18ce5232fbce8ffe25f55`** and makes the prior `donibawono` approval of `2162729e9f9bb3d56e1e2510788cc6cda946d47b` **stale**.

**Explicit dependency: [parser/legacy notes PR #295](https://github.com/OXY7O/kaori-website/pull/295) under [#293](https://github.com/OXY7O/kaori-website/issues/293) MUST be independently reviewed, merged to staging, and postmerge Full Admission 4/4 PASS before this PR can merge.** Current staging parser at prior source SHA recognizes YAML frontmatter only. The new parser supports both HTML-comment metadata and historical YAML, with release contract tests guarding exact tag/PR. Do not bypass this dependency or use stale approval. Revalidate current head and obtain fresh independent review.

## Summary

Prepare **human-reviewable** public release notes for Website `v0.1.4`, linked to official [draft staging→main promotion PR #289](https://github.com/OXY7O/kaori-website/pull/289). This is a one-file, docs-only source PR; it neither publishes a stable release nor changes the running Website.

## Why

The existing explicit production release workflow strictly requires `docs/releases/v0.1.4.md` with `stable_tag: v0.1.4` and `promotion_pr: 289`. The notes must be independently reviewed, contain an honest user-friendly summary, and avoid representing a signed release candidate as already stable. The file was absent on admitted staging, blocking the stable production release even after accepted UAT.

## What Changed

- Added **only** `docs/releases/v0.1.4.md` (canonical frontmatter and ordered Highlights, Improvements, Fixes, Known Limitations).
- Summarizes accepted Website release-status footer normalization, verified committed receipts, minimal Docker build context, non-root/zero-capability runtime and regression/recovery checks.

author: hoang0211
body:
Milestone 5b: rulebooks are parsed by a vision model that writes each page as Markdown. Four evals compared it with Docling on the same 7 rulebooks; the LLM parser won, so Docling and the reranker are removed.

- **LLM provider** (`app/llm/`): an `LLMProvider` protocol with an OpenAI implementation (Responses API) and a fake that scripts replies for tests. `complete()` returns text; `complete_structured()` returns a Pydantic object through OpenAI's structured outputs. `just test-live` runs the few tests that call the real API.
- **Page parser:** each page is rendered as an image and sent to `gpt-6.1-terra`, which writes it as Markdown under a fixed contract (verbatim text, real heading levels, captions and box titles in bold, tables as tables, text in pictures written out, icons as `[term]`, no page numbers or hidden copies). The Markdown is stored on the rulebook (`rulebooks.markdown`), so a reindex reuses it with no model call; `--reparse` reads the pages again. The OpenAI provider is created on the first parse that calls the model, so the app starts without an API key.
- **Markdown reader:** turns the Markdown into the elements the chunker already takes. Heading paths come from the levels, a page with no heading continues the previous section, and a bold line is a caption that moves into the chunk of the table below it. It doesn't rely on the model's formatting habits: a code fence around a whole reply is removed, table rows split from the lines around them even with no blank line between, and only text starting with a lowercase letter or a digit joins the page before, so a bold "Example" title or a sidebar starts a new block. Credits sections are dropped with their subsections, while a publisher's name used as a heading drops only its own section.
- **Evals:** `just eval-text` measures how much of each page's text layer the Markdown kept and what it added (word recall and precision); `just eval-answers` answers each golden question from its top 5 chunks and has `gpt-6.1-sol` grade the answer as correct, partial or wrong. During the comparison each parser had its own eval database and `just eval --compare` put them side by side; those reports stay committed.
- **Removed:** Docling (the layout parser, the child process that guarded against its native crashes, the OCR and retry settings, the `docling` and `torchvision` dependencies, `ocr_pages` in the parse report and the API) and the reranker (the cross-encoder, its model download, the `search()` wrapper and the reranked half of the retrieval eval). Search is hybrid search alone.

## Results

| Measure | Docling | LLM parser |
| --- | --: | --: |
| Answers found in the top 5 (hybrid search) | 28 / 30 | 29 / 30 |
| MRR (hybrid search) | 0.87 | 0.88 |
| Answered correctly | 24 / 30 | 24 / 30 |
| Text-layer words kept | copies the text layer | 88–100% per rulebook, none invented |

The decision rule was set before the answer check ran: the LLM parser stays unless it answers 2 or more fewer questions correctly and its chunks are the cause, and a tie goes to it. Of the six questions whose verdicts differ, its three losses were a table chunk just outside the top 5, a sentence Docling happened to merge into a neighbouring chunk, and an answer's wording; its gains include the dice odds, which only exist in its Markdown. The reranker beat hybrid search on neither parser's chunks and cost about 5 s per search.

Parsing costs about $0.006 a page, once per rulebook; an answer check about $0.10.

## Tests

The parser contract on scripted fake replies, the Markdown reader and the caption rule, storing and reusing the Markdown, `--reparse`, the provider created on first use, ingestion end to end with scripted page Markdown, the text-overlap and answer reports, the judge's structured reply in both providers, hybrid search's limit, and three live tests behind `just test-live`.

Each fix from the review has a regression test that fails without it.

author: kha
body:
The `adaptation-pr-create` action checks that the upstream PR's merge base coincides with a ref that has green downstream CI, but only while the adaptation branch does not exist yet. Once it exists, every later push is accepted: the action bumps the toolchain of the adaptation branch to the new head, whatever that head is based on.

This happened on leanprover/lean4#16633: after its adaptation PR (leanprover/downstream-lean4#267) had gone green, the PR was rebased from `downstream-green` onto `master`, 45 commits ahead. The action followed, and the adaptation branch was built against upstream changes it had not been adapted to. The resulting failures (batteries, reference-manual) had nothing to do with the PR but were reported on it like any other adaptation result.

Skipping the check for existing branches was needed while the merge base had to coincide with the tip of a single branch, which moves on. Since any ref with green downstream CI is accepted now, the check can run on every update, so a PR rebased onto a commit that is not known to be green gets the usual "merge base does not coincide" message. The force label still bypasses it.

Only `actions/adaptation-pr-create` changes; `dist/index.js` is rebuilt with `pnpm build`.

Third slice of the shared UI building blocks (audit item 6). The Stats card grid becomes an instance of `EditableList`, and the Library gets edit mode on the same list. That means Stats, Today, Habits, Areas and Library all edit the same way.

## Stats cards
- **`EditableList` grid axis**: `axis="grid"` drops a card on the nearest cell. A small cell takes the drop on its left or right; a full-width cell takes it above or below. The logic is a new pure `gridDrop()` in `list.ts`, with tests. Arrow keys on the handle move a card in all four directions. A new `itemClass` prop sets each cell's size class.
- **CardGrid**: renders `<EditableList axis="grid" layout="block">`. In edit mode each card's bar holds the ⠿ handle, its size, Edit and Remove; the bar wraps in small cells. The new order shows at once and is saved with one call.
- **StatCardView**: the ↑/↓ buttons, the footer and the size CSS are gone, since the list owns them now. The ⋯ menu hides in edit mode.
- **Stats pages**: the Customize button is now the shared `EditButton`, and Escape leaves edit mode. The label stays "Customize" because the habit stats page already has an Edit link.
- **API**: `card.order { where, ids }` replaces `card.move`. Cards not listed keep their order after the listed ones.

## Library
- An **Edit** chip sits beside Select, and only one of the two modes can be on at a time. In edit mode you tap a Task's name to rename it, and each row has Archive or Unarchive. Both changes show at once and come with Undo.

No migration.

body:
## Summary

Closes #9
Closes #11
Closes #14

One schema covers all four facility types from the start (per #14): restroom records carry the full CR attribute set from #9 (audience, PWD-accessible, bidet, flush, pail+dipper, water, cleanliness 1-5, last-verified, checker); computer lab carries units total/free; clinic carries a wait estimate; canteen carries a crowd level. Same record shape throughout: building + floor/room location, typed attributes, `verifiedAt`, `verifiedBy`, optional one-line note.

**Seed data awaits #10/#15 field collection.** `data/facility-status.json` ships empty on purpose — no fabricated records. Every surface renders a graceful empty state until verified rows land.

### What shipped

- `src/lib/facility-status.ts`: record types, JSON validation (bad rows dropped, ids deduped), per-type freshness windows — restrooms stay fresh for months, lab/clinic/canteen reports go stale within days (#14 perishability) — plus label/chip/grouping helpers.
- `data/facility-status.json`: the dataset, content-in-git per org convention (same pattern as `data/acad-orgs.json`).
- Building inspector (`BuildingResult.svelte`): collapsed **Facility status** section grouped by floor — attribute chips with pass/fail marks, cleanliness, "Verified/Reported X ago", aggressive staleness ("may be outdated" + outdated count in the summary), checker name, and a report link.
- Search: "CR", "restroom", "comfort room", "computer lab", "clinic", "canteen", "facility" queries return the buildings that have reports, ranked by the index (freshness, then attribute quality). Attribute keywords narrow matches ("pwd cr" only surfaces CRs reporting PWD access). Room labels like "IC LAB" also hit. Suggestions carry a stat secondary line ("F3 · CR FB cleanliness 4/5").
- Reporting: new `facility_status` GitHub issue form + CONTRIBUTING section — the lightweight issue-form path #9 allows, same flow as gate coordinates. Maintainers merge verified reports into the JSON.

### Design notes

- No DB migration or new synced table: records are static repo data read client-side, so they work offline and need no proposal plumbing. The in-app suggest-edit flow is entity-scoped (buildings/rooms); facility records are not DB entities, so reporting goes through the issue form rather than `edit_proposals`.
- Building matching is by `building_name` (the campus-wide key), case-insensitive; search only emits suggestions for buildings that exist in app data.
- Failed attributes render distinctly from unreported ones — unknown is never shown as a failure.

## Test plan

- [x] `bun test src/lib/facility-status.test.ts src/lib/search-suggestions.test.ts` — 24 tests: validation/sanitization, freshness windows, keyword matching (incl. "accreditation" not matching "cr"), attribute narrowing, floor grouping, ranking

- [x] `bunx biome ci .` — clean on changed files (repo has pre-existing format drift in untouched files)
- [x] `bun run check:undefined-names`, `bun run check:readme` — pass
- [x] `bun run build` — passes (astro build, server + static)
- [ ] Component tests: 71 failures are environmental (Node 26 `localStorage` unavailable in this environment; CI runs Node 24) — none in touched files
- [ ] Manual: open a building → Facility status section shows empty state + report link; search "cr"/"restroom" with seed data once #10/#15 land

body:
[SID:4993] P3b-1 — 같은 망 직접 · 서버: 호스트가 «직접 길이 몇 번 쓰였나»를 숫자로만 알리는 칸(Q4 «개수만 보고 · 내용 無»). AC1 «중계 행 0»은 PO가 SQL로 재고, 이 칸은 그 짝인 «직접 N개»를 서버가 가질 자리. 앞 칸 = web 5886(서버 길, 병합) · mobile 924 · 928 · 930 · 931 · 934. 호스트가 실제로 보고하는 쪽(3b-2)은 이 PR 병합 뒤 mobile에서(옛 서버 404도 견디게).

**무엇**
- `PUT /api/v2/desktop/relay/direct-count` (기기 토큰) 본문 `{epoch, commands, doors}` — `epoch`은 호스트가 시작할 때마다 만드는 임의 이름(8~64자 `[A-Za-z0-9_-]`) · 두 숫자는 그 실행 동안의 **누적**(엄격한 정수 — 글자 «1»이나 true는 거절 · 0~10억).
- 새 표 `desktop_direct_counts`(마이그레이션 0496 — **표 하나만 더함**: 옛 판이 같이 살아도 그 표를 안 부르니 안 깨짐) 기본키(기기, epoch) · 숫자만(명령 · 폰 · 주소 · 시각 하나하나 없음).
- 같은 보고가 다시 와도 · 늦게 온 낮은 숫자가 와도 안 변함(**더 큰 것 유지** `GREATEST`) · 한 기기당 최근 20번 실행만 · 마지막 보고 뒤 30일이면 분 단위 청소가 지움(`direct_counts_purged`) · 기기 행이 지워지면 같이 사라짐(CASCADE).
- 한 기기의 보고는 한 번에 하나(`pg_advisory_xact_lock` — 새 실행 보고 여럿이 함께 와도 20개 안 넘김; codex 1판 지적).

author: bennyz
body:
`Machine::attach` (through `build_client`) retried a refused connection every 100 ms. Firecracker binds its API socket a couple of milliseconds after it starts, so a caller that attaches right after spawning it lost the race almost every time and waited the full 100 ms: measured in qarax, 101 ms of a 460 ms sandbox fork.

It now retries every millisecond against the same 5 s deadline, and logs once a second while it waits.

The new test binds the socket 10 ms late and expects attach to return within 50 ms; before the change it returned after 101 ms.

author: pasidu-mihiranga
body:
## What & why

Completes issue #23: delivery reports for dispatchers and admins, built from Kafka events, and an AI delivery
assistant that answers "Where is my parcel?" and "How much to send 2 kg to Kandy?" by calling SwiftDrop's own
APIs, also exposed as MCP tools. Includes M10's platform share (release pipeline, Playwright E2E harness, test
report collection) and the M10 design documentation.

This branch brings together the earlier M10 branches (`feat/m10-reporting`, `feat/m10-ai-assistant`,
`feat/m10-release`, `feat/m10-diagrams`) on top of current `main`, plus the remaining work below.

Requirements covered:
- Admin: view basic reports (deliveries per day, success/failure rate)
- Bonus: AI Delivery Assistant, with the capabilities exposed as MCP tools
- Design: architecture proposal diagram, AI assistant / MCP sequences, design and safety section
- Testing: measurable coverage with results included (`doc/test-reports/SUMMARY.md`)

## Member & area

- Member: M10
- Service(s) / app: `reporting-service`, `ai-assistant-service`, `apps/web` (reports dashboard, chat widget), `tests/e2e`, `.github/workflows/release.yml`

## Highlights

**reporting-service**
- Projections `parcel_fact`, `status_transition`, `daily_delivery_stats`, `courier_daily_stats`; idempotent consumers for ParcelCreated, ParcelStatusChanged and ParcelAssigned. Rollups are recomputed from facts, so duplicates and out-of-order events count once.
- `GET /api/v1/reports/{daily,success-rate,zones,couriers}` for DISPATCHER and ADMIN.
- `POST /api/v1/reports/rebuild` (ADMIN): empties the read model and replays the topics; safe while events keep arriving.

**ai-assistant-service**
- Five tools (`track_parcel`, `estimate_delivery_fee`, `list_my_parcels`, `get_parcel_details`, `list_service_zones`), shared by the chat agent and the MCP server at `/mcp`.
- One OpenAI-compatible agent loop for OpenAI, Gemini, and Gemini on Vertex AI with a service account (`LLM_PROVIDER=vertex`).
- SSE chat (`token`, `tool`, `done`); Redis conversation memory; the user's JWT is relayed so tools see only what the user may; guests get the public tools only.
- Guardrails: scope gate, grounding rules, rate limit per user or client address, tool-round cap, PII pseudonymised before the model (encrypted vault), masked for MCP clients, graceful 503 when no model is configured.
- Town to district resolution for quotes (Nugegoda to Colombo, Peradeniya to Kandy) against pricing-service's live zones.

**Web**
- `/admin/reports`: KPI row, trend chart with previous-period comparison, table view and CSV export, zone and courier breakdowns, insights, filters in the URL.
- Chat widget on every page: streaming answers, lookup chips, stop and new chat; through the BFF, so no token reaches the browser. The BFF now forwards `x-forwarded-for` so the guest rate limit counts each visitor.

**Platform**
- `release.yml` builds, Trivy-scans and pushes every image to GHCR.
- Grafana dashboard `reporting-assistant.json`; Helm values and kind deploy wiring for both services (fixes the assistant looking for Redis on localhost in a cluster).
- Playwright demo suite in `tests/e2e` (`pnpm e2e`); `pnpm test:reports` collects coverage and E2E results into `doc/test-reports/`.

## Test results

| Area | Tests | Lines |
|---|---|---|
| reporting-service | 44 unit + 8 Testcontainers (Postgres, Kafka) | 98.94% |
| ai-assistant-service | 86 | 98.65% |
| web (M10 tests) | 74 | 99.63% for the web app |
| E2E against the full compose stack, live Vertex AI model | 20 passed, 0 failed | |

All Java, Node and Python suites in the repository were re-run for `SUMMARY.md`. The 5 skipped E2E steps
need services from other milestones that are not on `main` yet (dispatch M5, courier status M4, tracking M6,
notifications M9, webhooks M8); the suite names each one and will run them once those land.

Demo acceptance checks, verified on the running stack:
1. Admin opens Reports: the dashboard matches the report API for the seeded demo data (E2E 04).
2. A guest asks the price of 2 kg to Kandy: the assistant calls `estimate_delivery_fee` and answers with the real quote (E2E 02).
3. A signed-in customer asks "Where is my parcel?": the assistant lists their own parcels; other users' parcels are not reachable (E2E 02, 03, 05).
4. An external MCP client lists and calls the tools (E2E 03).
5. Release workflow publishes to GHCR on `main`; the Playwright suite passes.

## Checklist (Definition of Done)

- [x] Unit + integration tests added; coverage gate (70%) passes locally
- [x] Authorization rules tested (customers, couriers and merchants get 403 on reports; dispatchers cannot rebuild; anonymous chat and MCP cannot list parcels)
- [x] API change reflected in `contracts/openapi/*`
- [x] No secrets, no personal data in logs or error messages (the Vertex key lives in the git- and docker-ignored `secrets/`)
- [x] No emojis in code, docs, commit messages or this description
- [x] Config via environment variables; `.env.example` updated
- [x] Dockerfile / compose / Helm values updated
- [ ] Screenshots for UI changes (to be attached in a comment)

## Notes for reviewers

- `apps/web/src/app/admin/page.tsx` and `globals.css` had merge conflicts with M2's pricing work; both sides are kept.
- The production web build stops on a Next.js 16.4.3 security advisory unrelated to this change; Dependabot PR #74 upgrades Next.
- The student ID in the M10 contribution row is still to be filled in.

Closes #23

# ✨ What changes for people?

A participant who selected both clients can prepare the complete Desktop connector and method library before signing in to Code. Pressing Enter at the Code login prompt continues into an explicitly partial Desktop journey, preserving the selected workspace, brain, carrier and full Code profile for later resumption.

Fixes #638.

## 🎯 Outcome at a glance

| Before | After | Why it matters |
| --- | --- | --- |
| Deferring Code login stopped preparation for both clients. | Desktop preparation completes while Code remains pending. | Participants can start with Desktop and resume Code through its original qualification flow. |

```text
both clients selected
  defer Code login
    review and prepare complete Desktop connector + methods
    record: desktop_prepared_code_pending
  explicitly resume Code
    original genuine native qualifier
    preserve compatible Desktop artifacts and observations
```

## 🧩 What is in this PR

### Delivered

- [x] **Independent preparation** — strict schema 3 records distinguish the original both-client selection from the prepared Desktop view. An authenticated preparation capability check rejects incompatible readers before publication.
- [x] **Participant journey** — Mac and PowerShell launchers defer before any Code/authentication invocation, route explicit resumption from fresh canonical status, and retain the existing update flow.
- [x] **Truthful status** — Desktop-scoped diagnostics offer the Desktop journey while keeping Code packets, registration, native hooks and specialists pending. MCP startup and complete live methods work through the canonical partial record.
- [x] **Publication safety** — current source, exact selection, record-digest and existing installation guards are rechecked; the record is published last. Interrupted preparation can be recovered through the original materializer.

### Deliberate choices

CIPP separates preparation from selection. Schemas 1/2 and legacy capability JSON stay unchanged; a new compatible kit is required. Explicit Code resumption and authenticated update retain the genuine native producer and its full enforcement requirement. A Desktop-only observation grants no Code authority.

## 🗺️ Review route

1. Read **CIPP** in `docs/decisions/decision-log.md` and the preparation contracts in Specs 020 and 063.
2. Inspect `internal/installer/client_preparation.go`, the client record reader and continuity guard, then `adapters/mcp/setup/client_preparation.go` and manager dispatch.
3. Follow the Mac/PowerShell deferral and resumption paths, scoped diagnostics, and `TestBothClientsDesktopPreparationExperimentalConsumer`.

## 🧪 Evidence, not optimism

| Evidence | Result | Scope |
| --- | --- | --- |
| Final composed signed-synthetic consumer | **PASS — 80.32s** | Actual package preparation and MCP SDK startup; context/method plans; interruption/retry; confirmation/replay; brain preservation; no Code invocation or downgrade publication. Synthetic authority, no model or host UI. |
| Owning core, manager, wrapper and checker regressions | **PASS** | Strict wire/selection contracts, guarded native dispatch, legacy-method refusal, fresh status routing, Bash 3.2 behavior and report preservation. |
| Canonical wiki reconcile / validate / verify | **PASS** | Original compiler; managed atlas current. |
| Security / specification / interoperability / standards reviews | **APPROVED** | Four independent source reviews of the final composed implementation. |
| Normal unfiltered maintenance package | **PASS — 411.342s** | Unfiltered package, original default10m timeout, no skipped tests. |
| `go run ./dev/harness validate --full` | **PASS** | Original full gate, exit0; contracts, wiki, gofmt, offline vet and complete offline unit phase5m05.777s. |
| Hosted CI, including native Windows | **PASS — 14/14 checks** | Exact final source; native Windows artifact verified against tree751a7a0e, ordinary nonadmin account,9owners/215outcomes/6DarwinMCP PASS. |
| Installed Code / Desktop host acceptance | **PENDING** | The synthetic consumer does not establish installation, loading or functional acceptance in either real client. |

**Before / after:** owning regressions exposed a saved full-Code selection being downgraded, a legacy record entering the Desktop no-op path without complete methods, and YES routing initial/complete carriers into resumption. The final guards and shipped-wrapper routing tests pass for those cases. The initial schema regression was run against the old source after implementation; this PR makes no test-first claim for that test.

## 🛡️ Contracts, privacy and portability

- **Decision:** CIPP. **Specs:** `specs/020-release-distribution.md`, `specs/063-product-native-plugin.md`.
- [x] Test material is synthetic; no client documents, real memory or credentials ship.
- [x] Managed product, owner brain and workspace remain separate.
- [x] Original selection and source authority remain fixed; failed or canceled Code completion preserves a valid prepared Desktop phase.
- [x] Pending Code supplies no current plugin, registration, enforcing hooks or native specialist evidence.

| Runtime | What this PR establishes |
| --- | --- |
| Claude Desktop | Complete artifact preparation, canonical MCP consumer behavior and scoped test guidance. Actual extension/method installation, reconnection and functional use remain host checks. |
| Claude Code | Explicit pending state and preservation of the original qualification/publication owner. A real genuine qualifier and subsequent client observations remain required. |
| Codex | No new host qualification or native parity claim. |

## Merge Danger

**Door:** Two-way for source and newly built kits. Keep compatible readers for any emitted schema-3 record; older readers deliberately refuse it. Existing signed kits are unchanged.

**Blast Radius:** Installer. The change affects both-client preparation, management dispatch, MCP admission for canonical partial records, participant launchers and diagnostics. Existing native qualification and authenticated source/update boundaries remain mandatory.

## 🚫 Explicitly not included

Production signing or rollout; rebuilding or changing existing signed 0.1.83/0.1.84 installations; real-client/cohort acceptance; moving or archiving brain pages. These remain separate from completion of the preparation feature.

## ➡️ Follow-up

Actual Desktop participant acceptance remains tracked in #616 and the guided-test work in #629. Complete this PR’s local and hosted gates before merge; prepare a new compatible experimental kit for host testing afterward.

## Summary

- retain and await the active Web Lock request during browser database teardown
- await coordinator release from vault sessions and coordinated databases
- cover replacement-document lock handoff and map the lifecycle contract in the specification

Production offline reload could make the replacement document proxy through a page whose database owner was already exiting. Waiting for the lock-request promise to settle ensures ownership is relinquished before navigation teardown completes.

## Problem
Burger button style changes (colour, background, padding, border, rounded corners) showed in the editor but not on the live site.

## Cause
The settings are output correctly (checked the generated CSS), but on the live page the theme and Elementor's site settings style every `<button>`: `.elementor-kit-N button` (0,1,1) and `[type=button]:hover` beat the single-class `.kbroo-nav__toggle` rules. The editor canvas loads neither, so it looked right there. Reproduced in Chromium with Elementor kit style button rules: before the fix the toggle took the kit's beige text colour with no background, padding or border (matching the live screenshot); after, it uses the widget's settings.

## Change
- `.kbroo-nav .kbroo-nav__toggle` and `.kbroo-nav .kbroo-nav__close` (two classes), with the same declarations repeated for `:hover`, `:focus` and `:active` so theme hover/focus rules can't leak in.
- Resets margin, min sizes, box-shadow, letter-spacing, text-transform, text-shadow that themes commonly set on buttons.
- `display: none` stays in its own rule so the fold-at-tablet/phone and open-panel rules still win.

Checked: hidden on desktop with "tablet and smaller", shown at tablet width, hover colours apply, close button shows when a side panel opens.

## Description
This pull request introduces automated release management and changelog generation using Google's `release-please`, verifies Conventional Commits on pull request titles, and documents the complete maintainer workflow in `docs/RELEASES.md`. This eliminates manual changelog editing in individual pull requests.

Fixes #351

## Type of change
- [x] New feature (non-breaking change which adds functionality)
- [x] This change requires a documentation update

## What's Changed
- **Release Please Action & Workflow (`.github/workflows/release.yml`)**:
  - Leverages `googleapis/release-please-action@v4` on push to `main` and via `workflow_dispatch`.
  - Automatically manages Release PRs titled `chore(main): release X.Y.Z` containing generated changelog updates and version bumps.
  - Automatically tags commits and publishes GitHub Releases upon merging Release PRs.
- **Release Please Config & Manifest (`.github/release-please-config.json`, `.release-please-manifest.json`)**:
  - Tracks versioning at `0.1.0`.
  - Configures categorized changelog sections (*Features*, *Bug Fixes*, *Performance Improvements*, *Documentation*, *Refactoring*, *Tests*, *CI/CD*, *Chores*).
  - Synchronizes version numbers in `frontend/package.json` and `backend/pyproject.toml`.
- **PR Title Validation Workflow (`.github/workflows/pr-title.yml`)**:
  - Validates PR titles against Conventional Commits (`type(scope): summary`), ensuring commits on `main` provide valid semantic signals for `release-please`.
- **Maintainer & Contributor Documentation (`docs/RELEASES.md`, `CONTRIBUTING.md`)**:
  - Documents release flow, SemVer mapping rules, and fork testing instructions in `docs/RELEASES.md`.
  - Replaces manual changelog instructions in `CONTRIBUTING.md` with the automated Conventional Commits workflow.
  - Updated references across `GOVERNANCE.md`, `README.md`, `README.hi.md`, and `ARCHITECTURE.md`.

- [x] My PR title follows Conventional Commits format (`type(scope): summary`)
- [x] Release automation workflow tested and validated (`.github/workflows/release.yml`)

author: koxudaxi
body:
Second part of section 1 of the `heki recommend` design (4.2): where heki is silent, so no count of reports applies. It reads the blind-spot facts of #159 from the discovery run, which now builds its index with `Facts::Recommend`, and adds two trials. Stacked on #183.

- **Library names without a catalog entry**, by package and name as an `[[tool.heki.ecosystem]]` entry needs them, with calls, awaited, on an event loop, and in loops.
- **Hypothetical-catalog run (run 3):** the configuration plus one entry with `effects = ["blocking_net", "db_query"]` for each of the 64 names with the most reach, and `EFF101`, `EFF111`, `EFF103`, `EFF113` run as `heki check` would (suppressions, `per-file-ignores`). Each report counts for the name at the end of its chain; a report naming several counts for the first by name, and a note says so. The counts print as "if it waits" / "if it sends a query", stay out of the block and out of every count of reports (owner decision 4: a plain list, no template).
- **Names the catalog lacks in packages it covers** (owner decision 15): listed only when run 3 reports through them, with the issue-tracker URL (owner decision 14).
- **Calls heki does not resolve**, by function and reason, with the methods called.
- **Source-root trial (run 4):** a directory below which the dotted path of an import that names no project module is a file becomes a `src` candidate. The trial computes the module names `src` would give (no re-parse and no index: module names do not change the IR) and takes the directory into the block only when its imports resolve, no two files of one kind share a module, every import that names a project module still does, and no contract of the configuration or baseline entry names a module whose name changes. At most 8 are tried, each with the ones taken. An import below several directories is the one of the directory holding the importing file, or no candidate's. Calls of names of those files are left out of the library names.
- **A1 hazards:** the functions with one, and those too large to model.
- **Code:** `crates/heki_rules/src/recommend/blind_spots.rs`; `Project::set_config` swaps the configuration and rebuilds its catalog for a trial; `ProjectEnv::catalog` is the one place a configuration's catalog is built; `heki dump-recommend-facts` builds its index through `Indexed::build`.
- **Bounds:** shapes in `e2e_analysis_bounds.rs` for thousands of library names without an entry (64 tried, lists of 50) and thousands of source-root candidates (8 tried). Peak heap of the memory gate on this branch (macOS, count-alloc build): `recommend` 70.19 MiB, `recommend-owners` 70.57 MiB (budget 100); `check`, `watch`, `owners` byte-identical to main.
- **Tests:** `e2e_recommend.rs` covers each list, the trial counts against `heki check` with such an entry, the round trip of `src` (the block makes the import resolve and the report appear), each reason a source root stays out (baseline, contract, an import that would stop resolving, two files with one module, a directory above a source root), the ambiguous import, the cap lines, and the schema. Unit tests cover the name matching and the text helpers.
- **Not done:** `callers_bind` (the classes every caller binds to an unannotated parameter) needs a fact the index does not keep (argument classes per call site); `--section` is left for a later PR.

  * JSON output now includes blind-spot details and analysis run information.

author: matheusgdqueiroz-del
body:
This places the NPCs of 1,168 maps exactly where the official server shows them: cell, facing and presence.

**Evidence.** I walked the world with a packet capture of the live official server running (2026-11-17 to 11-21: Incarnam, Astrub, Amakna, Bonta, Brâkmar, Sufokia and the roads between them). Each map's contents lists every NPC on it, with its cell and facing. That is a direct measurement, not a guide and not a guess.

I compared the captures with the current `main` (f780d73) on 1,089 maps. The other 79 maps come from captures without timestamps and are unchanged from the same generator.

| | NPCs |
|---|---|
| shown by the official server, missing from that map in Jondo | 403 (258 placed nowhere, the rest on another map) |
| on a different cell | 283 (210 of them from the derived layer) |
| placed by Jondo where the official server shows no such NPC | 247 |
| maps the official server shows with **no** NPC at all | 601 |

Examples:
- `153879813` [2,-5]: Xelore Menda (2882) is on cell 287, not 370.
- `154010370` [-1,-2]: Mercedes Tripadora (2941) on cell 356, facing 1; she was missing.
- The tower concierges added yesterday with inferred cells: Bonta (4056, map 213910026) is on cell **330**, not 218, and Brâkmar (4055, map 215744780) is on cell **283**, not 297.

**What a character cannot see is kept.** The capturing character may not see an NPC that is gated by a quest. On a listed map, an NPC Jondo places there is kept with a criterion when Jondo's own quest data sends the player to it on that map. This covers 255 rows, each with a `kept` note saying which quest. Without this, the official layer would erase quest NPCs.

**Change.**
- `content/npcs/official.json`: per map, the full NPC list as shown, with `npc`, `cell`, `orientation` and an optional `criterion`. An empty list means the map has no NPC.
- `NpcSpawnContent.Load` takes the file as an optional last layer (`ReadOfficial`). On a listed map it erases the rows it does not hold and sets the listed ones exactly. Maps that are not listed are untouched.
- `ContentStore.Override`: sets a row whatever was there, erasures included. Only the authored layer may call it.
- `Npcs` passes the file in.

**Tests.** `NpcSpawnOfficialTests` covers:
- a listed map holds exactly the official rows (the derived guess and the hand-placed cell are gone, the gated row keeps its criterion);
- an empty list empties the map;
- an unlisted map is untouched;
- only the authored layer can override;
- the shipped file puts both concierges on their measured cells.

The actor passages tied to two NPCs that moved (the Astrub mercenary at the old chapel 188745735, and NPC 4355 on 192416776) follow them to their measured cells, and `AstrubBankTests` expects the bankers on their measured cells (259 and 302). The full `Jondo.Unity.Tests` suite passes locally: 5458 passed, 0 failed.

author: hogathos
body:
Dev-only 2D swarm map at /map on the dev panel, loopback only. One node per Run, one node per destination, one edge per Run that called that destination. Time runs left to right, one lane per node, so no two nodes share a place. Clicking a Run node opens its page; clicking a destination node opens the run list filtered to it.

- devpanel/map.py: build_map (pure function of the journal rows) + to_svg (one inline SVG, zero JavaScript). Nodes are Runs, never invented agent names. Edge colors: green allowed, red blocked or failed, amber rate-limited or retry. Edge label is call count + summed seconds.
- Route GET /map in the Pause-button shape (read-only, no proxy state needed). Index page links to it.
- The run list dest filter now reads every row, not only the latest row, so a Run that called a destination on any row shows under that filter. That is what the dest node link needs.

Review risks: a control row with a new method name outside the CONTROL_METHODS set would count as a call (the set is the closed list of control methods today). Latency sums are rounded to 3 decimals for the label. The route loads one query per Run, the same shape the index already uses.

Local: unittest 198 OK, pytest 198 passed + 40 subtests, Ruff 0, flake8 0, Pyright 0.

author: justchr
body:
Follow-up to #363. Home Assistant 2026.10 also logs every tool call that returns a plain dict ("return a ToolResult instead", breaks in 2027.11). `llm.ToolResult` only exists from 2026.10.0 (checked against core's tags), so the floor moves to 2026.10 and the tools return it directly.

**What goes with the old floor**
- `service_target.device_owner` (fallback to `primary_config_entry` / `config_entries`): the service context reads `config_entry_id`.
- The card's `_deviceEntry` / `_isVehicleDevice`: `config_entry_id` only. Card test fixtures now use that shape; the card snapshots are unchanged.
- `frontend.py`: `resource_mode` only (the `mode` fallback was dead since 2026.2).
- `tests_ha/test_setup.py`: `async_get_device_by_identifier` (in 2026.10.0).

**What stays, on purpose**

author: jonasborchelt
body:
### Description of Changes

This series makes Unikraft run multi-process, multi-threaded Linux
applications on several vCPUs. It was developed and tested on x86_64
KVM (QEMU, native platform code) with nginx (several workers, reload)
and PostgreSQL 17 (relational workload, hard stop and crash recovery)
as reference applications, against Linux as reference.

The series has 211 commits on top of `staging` 7a2cdc15. It is ordered
by dependencies. Each commit builds on its own; the series was build
checked with an SMP and a non-SMP profile.

Overview by area:

- **SMP start and per-CPU state** (`plat/kvm`, `plat/native/x86`,
  `lib/uklcpu`, `lib/ukpcpuvar`):
  - secondary CPU bring-up
  - per-CPU IDT and exception stacks
  - nested exception accounting
- **Scheduling and locking** (`lib/uksched`, `lib/ukschedcoop`,
  `lib/uklock`, `lib/ukmpi`):
  - per-CPU run queues and cross-CPU wakeups
  - mutex wait on the marked state after contention
- **Paging and address spaces** (`lib/ukpaging`, `lib/ukvmem`, `lib/ukpt`):
  - serialized page table updates
  - TLB shootdown with deferred frame reuse
  - private address spaces per process with copy-on-write
  - VAS lifetime bound to the scheduler
- **Processes** (`lib/posix-process`, `lib/ukbinfmt`, `lib/ukboot`):
  - fork, vfork, exec and wait4/waitid with correct siginfo
  - process groups and sessions
  - PID reservation until release
  - signal delivery to threads blocked in the kernel
  - interruption of epoll_wait/nanosleep by signal handlers
  - default largest TID raised from 31 to 1023
- **POSIX interfaces**:
  - `lib/posix-futex`: bitset waits, shared keys across address spaces, requeue
  - `lib/posix-mmap`, `lib/posix-fdio`: private anonymous COW mappings, shared file mappings and msync
  - `lib/posix-poll`: EPOLLEXCLUSIVE
  - `lib/posix-unixsocket`: socketpair, SCM_RIGHTS
  - `lib/posix-fdio`: F_SETOWN/SIGIO
  - `lib/posix-sysinfo`: online CPUs
  - `lib/posix-time`: shared timer deadlines
- **File systems and drivers** (`lib/ukfs-virtiofs`, `lib/ukfs-ramfs`,
  `drivers/virtio*`, `drivers/ukbus`): virtio-pci modern transport and
  VirtioFS fixes, needed for the application images. A virtio-fs
  completion wakes only the thread that submitted the request.
- **Console** (`lib/ukconsole`, `lib/nolibc`): console text is written
  together with its line ending.

Public interface changes:
- New Kconfig options for SMP and COW-backed anonymous memory.
- `lib/ukvmem` and `lib/ukpaging` gain batch/deferred-release APIs.
- `lib/ukfile` gains pinned backing ownership for shared mappings.
- Existing interfaces keep their behaviour when SMP is disabled.

Bugs fixed in existing upstream code. Each one was reproduced or
traced to the code path on unmodified `staging`:

| Fix in this series | Problem | Introduced by |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `lib/posix-poll: Keep the epoll file pointer in epoll_autodel` | `epoll_autodel()` reads the entry after removing it | 7b2e3817171a ("lib/posix-poll: Autoremove closed files from epoll") |
| `lib/ukfs-virtiofs: Continue directory reads at the FUSE entry offset` | directory reads restart at the wrong offset and repeat or skip entries | d13f61a29f44 ("lib/ukfs-virtiofs: Introduce VirtioFS driver") |
| `lib/nolibc: Serialize console text with its line ending` | text and its line ending are written separately and interleave between CPUs | 1ea33e7be32d ("lib/*: Turn `\n` into `\r\n`") |
| `lib/ukpaging: Step to the level boundary when skipping a PTE` | unmap/set_attr skip page table entries when a range starts inside an empty higher-level entry; pages stay mapped after munmap() and their frames leak | page table walk in `lib/ukpaging` |
| `lib/ukboot: Start the application with no blocked signals` | the application inherits the fully blocked signal mask of the init thread | init path in `lib/ukboot` |
| `lib/posix-process: Interrupt epoll_wait and nanosleep for signal handlers` | a signal with a handler does not wake a thread in `epoll_wait()` or `nanosleep()` | signal wakeup in `lib/posix-process` |

Testing (x86_64, QEMU/KVM, native platform):
- functional matrix at 1, 2, 3, 4 and 8 vCPUs
- fork/COW/exec with private ELF loading at 1–4 and 8 vCPUs
- thread stack reuse after munmap at 1, 2, 4, 8 and 14 vCPUs
- nginx with 1/2/4/8 workers including reload
- PostgreSQL 17 workload at 1/2/4 vCPUs with hard stop and restart
- network endurance: 500 boots each with INTx and MSI-X
- prime95 correctness

arm64 was build checked only.

### Related Work

This PR depends on:
- unikraft/app-elfloader#107 (process start, fork/exec support in the ELF loader)
- unikraft/lib-lwip#85 (SMP-safe lwIP glue, SO_REUSEPORT, socket readiness)

The applications listed above need all three.

### PR Checklist

 - [x] Read the [contribution guidelines](https://unikraft.org/docs/contributing/) regarding submitting new changes to the project;
 - [x] Tested your changes against relevant architectures and platforms; (x86_64 KVM; arm64 build only)
 - [x] Ran the [`checkpatch.uk`](https://github.com/unikraft/unikraft/blob/staging/support/scripts/checkpatch.uk) on your commit series before opening this PR; (0 errors, remaining warnings mostly description length and existing formatting)
 - [ ] Updated relevant documentation.

author: shihabal3amri
body:
Refs #463

**Tested on one car, with one launcher only.** FangJInGuang tested the first two attributes in #463 on a Destroyer 05 (DiLink 3.0) with the Dudu launcher (嘟嘟桌面) and "Keep CarPlay in the launcher card (experimental)" on: opening DiPlay settings from the CarPlay quick menu no longer moved CarPlay out of the card. Nobody has tested it in the DiYou desktop card. The `CarPlayVideoActivity` attribute comes from reading the code and has not been tested on a car.

## Why

A launcher card is a private virtual display that the launcher owns. The DiYou card in an earlier #463 report was `10:dy-d-r-display 1232x930 flags=12` (PRIVATE + PRESENTATION). Android checks every start onto such a display in `isCallerAllowedToLaunchOnDisplay`. Android 10 applies the check to a virtual display that another app owns, and Android 11 and later to any untrusted display. The started activity must declare `android:allowEmbedded="true"`. If it does not and it starts in a task that is already on that display, Android picks a stack on another display and moves the **whole task** there.

In 0.2.22 only `AdbClusterActivity` declares the attribute. With the same-task setting on, CarPlay runs as `SameTaskCarPlayHostActivity` in DiPlay's task inside the card. Quick menu → More → DiPlay settings (`showDiPlayHome`) starts `DiPlayActivity` from that screen, so Android moved the task, CarPlay included, to the main display.

## What changes

`android:allowEmbedded="true"` on three activities in `common/src/main/AndroidManifest.xml`. Each of them runs in DiPlay's own task:

- **`DiPlayActivity`**: settings and the start page. Confirmed on the car.
- **`SameTaskCarPlayHostActivity`**: CarPlay in DiPlay's task. Confirmed on the car.
- **`CarPlayVideoActivity`** (iOS 27 video in the car, only while parked): `CarPlayVideo.show()` starts it from the application context with `FLAG_ACTIVITY_NEW_TASK` and the default affinity. So it goes into DiPlay's task whenever Android finds that task.
  - On Android 12 (DiLink 4/5), a start without a source activity uses the display of the app's top activity, which is the card while CarPlay runs there. The video then joins the card's task. Without the attribute, Android would move that task to the main display, and CarPlay would stay there after the video closes. With the attribute, the video opens in the card.
  - On Android 10 (DiLink 3), as far as I can tell from AOSP, the start goes to the main display, and Android ignores a task that matches only by affinity on another display. The video then opens full screen in a new task with or without the attribute, and the card is not affected.

Not changed:

- **`CarPlayHostActivity`** keeps its own `.carplay` task and no attribute. With the setting off, CarPlay still opens outside cards, as it has since 0.2.12.
- **`ImageCropActivity`**: it opens only after the image picker returns (`GetContent` / `OpenDocument`). The picker is another app's activity in DiPlay's task and does not allow embedding, so it has already moved the task to the main display. The crop screen then opens there, and the attribute would change nothing on that path. If a head unit's picker turns out to stay in the card, the crop screen will need the attribute too.
- **`MainActivity`** (MFi self-check) is not opened by the app.
- **System dialogs** (runtime permissions, the VPN `ConfirmDialog` during a USB connection) still move the task out, as the reporter noted. They are system activities, and DiPlay cannot change them. They normally appear only once.

## Security note: `DiPlayActivity` is exported

`DiPlayActivity` is the `LAUNCHER` activity, so it is exported. With `allowEmbedded`, any installed app can do what Dudu does, without any permission:
1. Create its own private virtual display.
2. Put one of its own activities on it.
3. Start `DiPlayActivity` there.
4. Read the pixels from the display's `Surface`.

AOSP's comment on the check gives this reason: such contents "can be read from Surface by apps that created them".

What such an app gets:

- **The settings screen as drawn**: connection status, the iPhone's name, the car hotspot's network name and setting values. It gets nothing beyond what the screen shows: no files, preferences or MFi data. Passwords appear only in a dialog that the driver opens, in a masked field. Without `INJECT_EVENTS`, the app cannot send touches to DiPlay, so it cannot open that dialog or move around in Settings.
- **With "Keep CarPlay in the launcher card" on and a session running, also the CarPlay picture.** `DiPlayActivity`'s launcher path opens `SameTaskCarPlayHostActivity` in the same task, on that app's display. That picture is the iPhone's projected screen: maps, and messages and caller names as CarPlay shows them. Starting `DiPlayActivity` on another display can also move DiPlay's open task there, which takes CarPlay off the car's screen. With the setting off, the CarPlay screen does not allow embedding and opens on the main display.

Precedent: `AdbClusterActivity` is already exported with `allowEmbedded` and shows the CarPlay cluster map.

**My judgment: low risk.** The settings screen shows nothing that is not already visible on the head unit's screen. The CarPlay case needs a malicious app installed on the head unit and an opt-in experimental setting. A launcher card cannot work without the attribute, because Dudu is an ordinary third-party app that embeds DiPlay in exactly this way. Limiting embedding to the default home app would need a hidden API (the display's owner), so this PR does not do that.

## Tests

New `CarPlayScreenTest.screensInDiPlaysTaskMayOpenInALauncherCard` (Robolectric, SDK 29). It checks that the three activities have DiPlay's task affinity and `FLAG_ALLOW_EMBEDDED`, and that `CarPlayHostActivity` does not. I checked that it fails (`CarPlayVideoActivity must allow embedding`) when the attribute is removed.

Full CI command from `AGENTS.md`: passed. That is 3,539 unit tests (shared 1,798 with 1 skipped, common 1,730, home 11) and `lintDebug` and `assembleDebug` for mobile, home and maphost. `python3 scripts/check_public_tree.py` passed. The machine was under heavy load from other builds (load average 38 to 60), so I ran the command three times:
1. Another process stopped the Gradle daemon. Before that, `AirPlayEventPeerTest` hit its known loopback "Connection reset by peer" flake.
2. The wall-clock assertion in `SessionLogFileLatencyTest.theCallThatCrossesTheSizeLimit…` failed (5.3 ms against a 4 ms limit).
3. Everything passed. The `:shared` tests were up to date from run 2, on the same tree.

The change touches neither networking nor session logging.

## Release check

The release `verify-apk.py` compares only manifest components (kind, name, exported), so it does not detect this change. The next release compares against 0.2.22, which already ships `SameTaskCarPlayHostActivity`. Its "one added activity" assertion therefore becomes "no added components". It can also assert that exactly `AdbClusterActivity`, `DiPlayActivity`, `SameTaskCarPlayHostActivity` and `CarPlayVideoActivity` allow embedding. No permission or component changes.

author: lennoxp90
body:
MapVariants 1.2.0 is out ([release](https://github.com/LennoxP90/SPT-MapVariants/releases/tag/v1.2.0)) and lets several mods each offer a version of one map. It adds `Maps.SelectedId`, which says whose version a raid loaded as `owner:variant`, for example `com.manimal.lighthouse:manimal`, with `spt:shipped` for the map SPT ships.

This keys a map version by the variant word from `SelectedId` instead of `CurrentVariant`. `CurrentVariant` reads `backport` for every mod's backport, so FumsCustoms and CustomsClassic both ended up as `bigmap~backport`, and a version that keeps the game's scenes could not be told apart at all.

Keys become `Interchange~manimal`, `bigmap~fums`, `bigmap~classic`, `factory4_day~halloween2026`. The game's own map stays unsuffixed. With an older MapVariants there is no `SelectedId`, and the key is exactly as before.

Captures that recorded their scenes still resolve, since the server matches on scenes first. A capture made before scenes were kept, under `~backport`, would be taken again.

The new API is covered in [API.md](https://github.com/LennoxP90/SPT-MapVariants/blob/main/API.md) and [UPGRADING.md](https://github.com/LennoxP90/SPT-MapVariants/blob/main/UPGRADING.md). It builds clean against SPT 4.1.

author: jizhi-de-jichi
body:
This PR adds the algebraic setting of linear patching over a square of rings: README §6.1 "Exact squares of rings and glueing data over them (Kedlaya-Liu 1.3.7)" of the [RelativeFarguesFontaine roadmap](https://github.com/TauCetiProject/TauCetiRoadmap/blob/main/RelativeFarguesFontaine/README.md#61-exact-squares-of-rings-and-glueing-data-over-them-kedlaya-liu-137), the first step of its Layer 6 milestone "linear patching and modifications". It defines `TauCeti.ExactSquare` (exactness of `0 → R → R₁ × R₂ → L → 0`) and `TauCeti.PatchingData` (two modules and one overlap identification `L ⊗[R₁] M₁ ≃ L ⊗[R₂] M₂`) with the names and two-module presentation of the roadmap's `Suggested.lean` signatures. After this PR, §6.1 still needs tensor products and duals of finite projective data, base change along maps of squares, and the comparison with AdicSpacesPartIII's topological glueing squares. Its consumers are §6.2 (`exactSquare_finiteProjective`, `exactSquare_hom`, `UniversalPatching`, all stated over `ExactSquare` and `PatchingData`), §6.4 ("a glueing pair is an exact square") and §6.5 (`beauvilleLaszlo_sections`, `beauvilleLaszlo_recovery` and `beauvilleLaszlo_flat_exact`, stated with `PatchingData`, `patchingDiagonal` and `patchingDifference`).

Roadmap: RelativeFarguesFontaine

`TauCeti/RingTheory/Patching/ExactSquare.lean` (266 lines) defines the predicate and proves two non-degenerate witnesses: the identity square (`exactSquare_self`) and the Zariski square of coprime `f, g` for arbitrary `IsLocalization.Away` algebras (`exactSquare_of_isCoprime`), whose three fields are main's coprime Mayer–Vietoris lemmas `IsLocalization.Away.mayerVietoris_injective/exact/surjective`. It defines the patching maps `patchingDiagonal` (`m ↦ (1 ⊗ m, 1 ⊗ m)`) and `patchingDifference`, and proves that the patching sequence of any module is exact on the right and in the middle (`ExactSquare.exact_patchingDiagonal_patchingDifference`), by right exactness of tensor products (`rTensor_exact`). For a flat module the diagonal is also injective (`ExactSquare.injective_patchingDiagonal`), via `Module.Flat.rTensor_preserves_injective_linearMap`. When the overlap `L` is flat, as for the Zariski square, the diagonal of every module is injective (`ExactSquare.injective_patchingDiagonal_of_flat_overlap`), via `LinearMap.lTensor_injective_of_exact_of_flat`; this is the form of main's Laurent-cover `moduleAugmentation_injective`.

`TauCeti/RingTheory/Patching/Data.lean` (514 lines) defines the sections of a datum as the compatible-pairs module `ker (F.coprod (-G))`. This is the convention of `TauCeti.Algebra.Module.LocalizedModule.Pullback`. The file also defines the comparison maps `compareLeft` and `compareRight`, the morphisms (`PatchingData.Hom`, compatibility tested on `1 ⊗ x`) with a `Category` instance, the functor `sectionsFunctor`, and the canonical datum `can N` with its functor `canFunctor`. `canAdjunction : canFunctor ⊣ sectionsFunctor` is the README's `Hom_R(N, sections D) = Hom(Can N, D)`, with unit `n ↦ (1 ⊗ n, 1 ⊗ n)`. Over an exact square a module whose patching diagonal is injective (a flat module, or any module when `L` is flat) is recovered as the sections of its canonical datum (`ExactSquare.bijective_canUnit`). For such `N`, morphisms `Can M ⟶ Can N` are exactly the `R`-linear maps `M → N` (`ExactSquare.canHomEquiv`, built from `LinearEquiv.congrRight`, inverse `canMap`, with `canHomEquiv_canMap` and the forward forms `left_eq_baseChange_canHomEquiv`/`right_eq_baseChange_canHomEquiv`). The public constructor `canHom` builds `Can N ⟶ D` from maps compatible on `1 ⊗ n`. The comparison morphism `compareHom D : Can (sections D) ⟶ D`, with components `compareLeft` and `compareRight`, is the counit (`canAdjunction_counit_app`). It comes with its overlap compatibility `transition_comp_baseChange_compareLeft` and its naturality `canMap_sectionsMap_comp_compareHom`. This is the full faithfulness that README §6.2 derives from flat recovery. Two functors are `@[expose]`d so that their objects unfold in the adjunction's statements; every other body stays hidden behind `(rfl)` lemmas. The identification of `can N`'s sections with the kernel of `patchingDifference` (`mem_sections_can_iff`) reuses main's `TensorProduct.AlgebraTensorModule.cancelBaseChange_tmul_eq_smul_rTensor` (`TauCeti/LinearAlgebra/TensorProduct/Tower.lean`). The PR no longer changes that file.

Overlap disclosure: open PR #41693 (AdicSpacesPartIII R3.2) adds `TauCeti.Huber.GlueingDatum`, the three-module `(ψ₁, ψ₂)` datum of complete Tate glueing squares. It also has its canonical datum `ofModule` and the flat recovery `bijective_toSectionsOfModule_of_flat`. Both PRs prove flat recovery by the same flat-tensor argument, on different structures in different namespaces. RelativeFarguesFontaine §6.1 owns the algebraic interface and states that "every glueing square of complete Tate rings (AdicSpacesPartIII, R3.2/glueing-square) is an exact square, its finite glueing data are glueing data here". Whichever PR lands second can route its flat step through `ExactSquare.exact_patchingDiagonal_patchingDifference`.

Mathematical sources: K. S. Kedlaya and R. Liu, *Relative p-adic Hodge theory: foundations*, Astérisque 371 (2015), Definition 1.3.7, and the Stacks Project, Section 15.92 (Tag 0BNI), category of glueing data. Both are cited in the module docstrings. No Mathlib material is vendored.

Quality pass:
- Q1 Mathlib duplicates: checked — no exact-square or patching-datum notion exists in Mathlib. Mathlib's `IsLocalization.existsUnique_algebraMap_eq_of_span_eq_top` and `algebraMap_injective_of_span_eq_top` give the sheaf condition only for concrete `Localization.Away` products with `awayToAwayLeft/Right`, not for arbitrary `IsLocalization.Away` algebras over a square; the Zariski square therefore reuses Tau Ceti's `IsLocalization.Away.mayerVietoris_injective/exact/surjective` (see Q2). Middle exactness (now for every module, no flatness) reuses Mathlib's right exactness `rTensor_exact`, and left injectivity reuses `Module.Flat.rTensor_preserves_injective_linearMap`; the Hom bijection reuses `LinearMap.liftBaseChange`, and `can` reuses `AlgebraTensorModule.cancelBaseChange`. `ExactSquare.injective_patchingDiagonal_of_flat_overlap` reuses `LinearMap.lTensor_injective_of_exact_of_flat` and `LinearMap.lTensor_inj_iff_rTensor_inj`. The earlier helper `cancelBaseChange_one_tmul` was dropped: main now has the more general `TensorProduct.AlgebraTensorModule.cancelBaseChange_tmul_eq_smul_rTensor`, which the proof of `mem_sections_can_iff` now uses. Re-run for the latest commit: `canHomEquiv` now reuses Mathlib's `LinearEquiv.congrRight` instead of an inline post-composition equivalence; `compareHom`, `canAdjunction_counit_app`, `transition_comp_baseChange_compareLeft`, `canMap_sectionsMap_comp_compareHom`, `canHomEquiv_canMap` and `left/right_eq_baseChange_canHomEquiv` concern Tau Ceti's own `PatchingData` and have no Mathlib counterpart.
- Q2 Tau Ceti duplicates, on main and in open PRs: checked — I searched main and open PRs for `ExactSquare`, `PatchingData`, `GlueingPair`, `UniversalPatching`, "glueing datum", "exact square" and Beauville–Laszlo. I also looked for `ker (f.coprod (-g))` compatible-pairs code. Nothing on main defines these; `sections` follows main's compatible-pairs convention. `exactSquare_of_isCoprime` is now a term proof from main's `IsLocalization.Away.mayerVietoris_injective/exact/surjective` (`TauCeti/RingTheory/Localization/Away/MayerVietoris.lean`); the earlier private helpers re-proving them were deleted. author: evilclanker9000
body:
<!-- claude-projects-attribution: {"github_login":"Vonsek"} -->
_Requested by **Lucas** · [project thread](https://claude.ai/code/project/chan_01BXgfudnVap9eKr5fwwRwuh?thread=cmsg_01BXgfudnVap9eKr5fwwRwuhTRQwDRpr9EcBTn4WVaGcjh)_

Claimed in the coordination issue as: EGEN-SDWA-DIFF ([claim](https://github.com/ItsNotRexed/Leonida/issues/1902#issuecomment-7081389271))

### What and why

None of the repo's fuzzers generate `_sdwa` forms, although the selects were silently ignored until 2026-11-20 and #2005 fixes another SDWA bug found by a scratch version of this tool. `tools/sdwa_diff.py` is that tool made into a repo tool, in the style of `tools/salu_diff.py` (stdlib only, `python -I`, `--programs/--seed/--max-ops/--ops/--list-ops/--self-test`, shrinking on mismatch, skips counted with reasons, exit 0/1/2/77):

- A separate reference for 92 VOP1/VOP2/VOPC `_sdwa` opcodes in two families. Integer: the 32-bit VOP2 ops, `v_cndmask_b32`, integer VOP1 ops, `v_cvt_f32_{u32,i32,ubyteN}`, the 32- and 16-bit integer compares. f16: `v_add/sub/subrev/mul/min/max_f16`, the rounding ops and `v_fract_f16`, f16 <-> 16-bit integer and f16 -> f32 conversions, the f16 compares and `v_cmp_class_f16`.
- Every selector on both sources and the destination, `sext()`, `dst_unused` PAD/SEXT/PRESERVE, VGPR, SGPR (seeded, so known constants to the translator), integer and float inline-constant sources, `clamp`, f16 neg/abs. Programs chain up to `--max-ops` instructions through v1..v7 and VCC on one lane.
- `--oracle hw` runs the same programs through `tools/hw_oracle` on an RDNA1/RDNA2 GPU (GFX11+ has no SDWA, so it exits 77 there).
- The docstring lists what is modelled, what is skipped and the known divergences. Those divergent forms are left out by default (like `salu_diff`'s lane-mask ops), so a default run shows only new problems. `--known` puts them back, and a hardware-only run always includes them.

`tests/test_sdwa_diff.py` (20 tests, about 6 s): hand-worked reference values (selects, `sext()`, the three `dst_unused` modes, clamp, f16 neg/abs, float constants, the DWORD rule, `v_fract_f16(-0)`, the 16-bit compares, the #2005 shift case), the translator on a fixed list of hand cases, a short seeded run, generator coverage (every op appears; known divergences only with `--known`), canaries (a faked wrong translation is caught, shrinking keeps the guilty instruction) and the exit codes, including 77 with no tools or a GPU without SDWA. `docs/shader_validation.md` gets a short paragraph next to `salu_diff`'s.

This doesn't depend on #2005. The constant-shift form it fixes is one of the known divergences, so the default run and the tests pass on main as it is.

Two new translator divergences came out of this, both posted as findings with minimal repros and not fixed here:
- [16-bit result with `dst_sel:DWORD`](https://github.com/ItsNotRexed/Leonida/issues/1902#issuecomment-7081723191): RDNA2 zeroes the high half for any `dst_unused`. The translator keeps it, following the non-SDWA rule.
- [float inline constant with a `src_sel` in an f16 op](https://github.com/ItsNotRexed/Leonida/issues/1902#issuecomment-7081723579): RDNA2 narrows the f16 value. The translator skips the select (`src_h`).

### Tested

Windows 11, Python 3, CPU unless noted.

- `python -I tools/sdwa_diff.py --programs 1000 --max-ops 4 --seed 1..8`: 8000 programs, 7541 pass, **0 mismatch**, 459 skipped. The skips are 3 kinds: `v_cmp_class_f16` is not supported by the translator in any encoding, the translator has no `clamp` on `v_cvt_f16_{u16,i16}`, and NaN operands the reference does not model.
- `--known --programs 1000 --seed 1`: 52 mismatches. These are the three known divergences (#2005 is not on main yet, plus the two findings).
- Hardware, `--oracle hw` on the AMD Radeon RDNA2 iGPU (Ryzen 9 9950X3D, gfx1036, driver 26.10.1, HIP oracle): `--programs 600 --seed 1` 585 pass, 0 mismatch, 15 skipped (NaN operands). Earlier runs while building the model: 500 mixed programs (seed 21), 600 single-instruction f16 programs and 300 on the conversions, `v_fract_f16` and `v_cmp_class_f16`. Those runs are where the DWORD rule, the f16-constant rule, `fract(-0) = +0` and the class mask read as an f16 constant were measured. The final model matches all of them. The NVIDIA RTX 5080 has no part here (CPU tool, and the hardware oracle needs AMD).
- Every generated instruction form assembles with `llvm-mc` for gfx1013 and gfx1030 (about 30,000 distinct lines each, 0 errors). That check removed `sext()` on `v_cndmask_b32_sdwa`, the nonexistent `v_cmp_f/t_{i16,u16}` and a constant-bus overflow.
- Negative control: sabotaging `sdwa_src` (sext ignored), `sdwa_dst` (UNUSED_SEXT as PAD) or UNUSED_PRESERVE (insert into 0) in `tools/rdna2spirv.py` fails `test_hand_cases_match_the_translator` (2, 2 and 4 failing subtests). The UNUSED_SEXT sabotage also gives 11 mismatches in a 300-program run. All reverted.
- `python -I tests/test_sdwa_diff.py` OK, `python -m compileall -q tools tests` OK, `python -I tests/test_docs_links.py` OK.

### Checklist

- [x] No game data, keys or decryption (CONTRIBUTING.md), including in logs or reports quoted here.
- [x] A new translator rule is in the contract table of `docs/design.md`, with how it was confirmed. (No translator change.)

AI-assisted.

author: lambsouls
body:
Removes the access-check note from `lambsouls/dsh-ssh-ops`, because the issue it describes is **fixed and verified**.

You were right about it. The disclosure pointed at something real, and it was worse than "no DSH access check" — the profile page was reachable by plain top-level navigation:

```
curl 'http://127.0.0.1:<port>/api/ssh-ops/servers/<id>/profile?fence=1'
→ 200, 11693 bytes of profile
```

Top-level navigation sends no `Origin` header, so the Host/Origin allowlist let it through. The `?fence=1` fallback existed because `EventSource` cannot set custom headers — but it had been widened to cover that HTML page too.

## Fix

The page is gone rather than guarded. It had no real purpose left:

- Profiles are rendered in an in-panel drawer from the `/servers/:id` JSON — the drawer shipped a while back.
- The standalone page only existed for `window.open`, and `window.open` is silently dropped in Electron (no `setWindowOpenHandler` on the host, and a refused `window.open` does not throw). That was the "button does nothing" bug I fixed earlier — same root, same dead end.

So: route deleted, `lib/profile-html.js` and its test deleted, and the `?fence=1` fallback narrowed to **`console/stream` only** (the one channel a browser genuinely cannot decorate with headers).

## Verified

| | before | after |
|---|---|---|
| `curl .../profile?fence=1` | 200 + full profile | **403 FORBIDDEN** |
| `GET /servers` with the fence header | 200 | 200 |

A regression test now asserts that `?fence=1` is bound to `console/stream`, and that the page renderer stays deleted — so the widening cannot come back by accident.

## Suggested description

Dropping the trailing sentence leaves what the plugin actually does. The full disclosure remains visible in the repository's `MAINTAINING.md` §3.3.1, including why the page existed and why it was the wrong shape.

Thanks for catching it — a disclosure on the storefront is exactly what made this worth re-auditing.

author: tomerfi
body:
## What

The release workflow fails at the `Set new project version` step when the `bump` input is `auto`:

```
error: the argument '--bump <BUMP[=VALUE]>' cannot be used with '[VALUE]'
```

`uv version` treats the positional `[VALUE]` (explicit version) and `--bump` as mutually exclusive, but the `auto` branch passed both `--bump stable` and the version computed by `version-bumper-action`.

## Fix

In the `auto` branch, set the computed version directly:

```bash
jq_output=$(uv version --output-format json "$NEXT_VERSION")
```

Verified locally: `uv version --output-format json --dry-run 2.5.5` against `2.5.5.dev1` resolves to `2.5.5`. The `patch`/`major`/`minor` branches use `--bump` alone and are unaffected.

### A. Greške unesene u v100
- Plaćena narudžba više ne nudi „Podaci za uplatu”; oznaka se briše ako servis javi da narudžba opet čeka uplatu.
- Torba iz starije vlastite narudžbe nije „rezervirana za drugog kupca” (i obrnuto: nakon raskida ili isteka roka više nije „vaša”).
- Obavijest za prestare preglednike bez tajmera i animacije: druga mala ugrađena skripta postavlja `html.js-fail` kad glavna ne proradi.
- Maska brojeva: crna lista riječi samo na početku riječi („Hrvatskih branitelja 123/4, 10000 Zagreb” ostaje).
- Filtar poveznica: imena s crticom i rečenice „pohvale. Top” prolaze.
- Rok uplate u e-mailu vlasnici čita se iz spremljene narudžbe.

### B. Sigurnost
- Ulica, mjesto i telefon ne smiju sadržavati poveznicu (400 s poljem); u e-mailu kupcu adresa, napomena i napomena uz artikl prolaze kroz filtar, a bez potvrde linkom i kroz masku brojeva.
- `sj_unlink` uklanja samo prave poveznice; ostalo „riječ.riječ” razdvaja razmakom, ne briše.
- Ćirilični nastavci domena, točka U+FF61, slova-modifikatori kao razdjelnik znamenki.
- Ključ narudžbe bez `crypto.randomUUID` iz `getRandomValues`.
- Pun dnevnik izjava: vlasnica dobiva najviše jedan e-mail dnevno.

### C. Kupac i raskid
- Stari linkovi nakon raskida kažu „Izjava o raskidu je zaprimljena”, ne „stornirana”.
- Ploča za uplatu nosi poveznicu na obrazac za raskid s brojem narudžbe (`raskidLink`).
- Ploča na zaslonu prati promjenu stanja (raskid, uplata, izjava bez poveznice) bez osvježavanja.
- Prazna košarica dok narudžba čeka potvrdu to i kaže; 429 razlikuje granicu po primatelju.
- Bez slobodnih unikata gumbi vode na Stalnu kolekciju.

### D. Tekst i dizajn
- Jednoslovna riječ ostaje uz `span.nw`; e-adresa u okviru je `inline-block`.
- Množina i red riječi u porukama o rezervaciji; sitni lektorski ispravci; navodnici ”.
- Admin ne ovisi o `:has`; `-webkit-backdrop-filter`.

### E. Robusnost i testovi
- Stari dnevnik izjava briše se samo kad ga je provjera pročitala do kraja i bez ostatka.
- `tests/compat.js` stroži (vanjska skripta, `randomUUID`, `@media` raspon, ugniježđeni CSS, `@layer`, boje bez rezervne vrijednosti).
- `tests/serve.sh` staje ako je port zauzet.

## Provjera
Svih 11 skupina testova prolazi: compat 13, run.php 98, admin.php 124, paket.py 18, api 131, confirm 42, e2e 252, smtp 10, gas 22, proba 7, pdf417 10.

## Ne mijenja se
Jasminine odluke (glas ja/mi, boja za Ostalo, blokada nakon storna, Uvjeti t. 6), njezini tekstovi i zakonski obrazac za raskid.

body:
MapVariants 1.2.0 ([release](https://github.com/LennoxP90/SPT-MapVariants/releases/tag/v1.2.0)) and CustomsClassic 1.1.0 ([release](https://github.com/LennoxP90/SPT-CustomsClassic/releases/tag/v1.1.0)) are out, with your work in both. Classic is now a source beside a backport, so FumsCustoms no longer has to stand down. This updates FumsCustoms to match.

## What changes

- **Shares Customs with CustomsClassic.** With MapVariants 1.2.0 and CustomsClassic 1.1.0, FumsCustoms stays on and the map screen offers Vanilla, Fums and Classic. Against an older MapVariants or CustomsClassic it stands down exactly as before (client `StandDown`, server `ClassicCoexist.FumsOff`).
- **Public API instead of internals.** On 1.2.0 the Customs entry goes through the new public `Maps.RegisterBackport`, with this plugin's own tiles, so `maps.json` and MapVariants' tiles folder are not written and no restart is needed. The `maps.json` route, including the reflection into `ClientMaps.Add`, is kept only for older MapVariants.
- **Your mismatch check, switched on.** The server declares `com.fums.customs` with `Providers.DeclarePlugin`, so a client with another mod's Customs backport falls back to Vanilla on the map screen instead of loading its scenes over this mod's data.

## Tested

On SPT 4.1.6 with FumsCustoms 1.0.0 and these two DLLs, MapVariants 1.2.0 and CustomsClassic 1.1.0: Customs offered Vanilla, Fums and Classic, and raids on each loaded the right version (Fums: the backport served and `SelectedId` `com.fums.customs:fums`; Classic: the source served, FumsCustoms' patches suspended; Vanilla: both stood down). The server logged the declaration and nothing stood down. Both halves build clean.

[UPGRADING.md](https://github.com/LennoxP90/SPT-MapVariants/blob/main/UPGRADING.md) covers the rest of 1.2.0 for mod authors.

author: scottyfncodes
body:
## What this is

The first playable slice of MONEY LINE: a railroad, mining and terrain-engineering game on an 1890 frontier. One seeded valley, and the whole mining-to-market loop running through connected systems.

## What a player can do

1. Start in Prosperity with $18,000, one tank engine, four hoppers and a gold claim across the river.
2. Inspect terrain and the claim (reserve estimate with survey confidence).
3. Borrow against a credit line that grows with assets; interest is charged daily.
4. Reshape the ground: excavate, fill, grade, blast, clear, each priced by material and distance.
5. Lay a railroad: a surveyor proposes a route, the player moves waypoints, the engineer designs a grade line within 3.5% and prices cuts, embankments, trestles and tunnels. Crews build it day by day.
6. Open a mine, build a loading platform, and let the engine run the service.
7. Sell every shipment at the city market at the day's price.
8. Raise a stamp mill and ship concentrate instead of raw ore.
9. Buy improvements, more hoppers, or a heavier locomotive. Prospect for the second deposit.

## Structure

- `src/sim/` deterministic simulation (no DOM, no three.js), fixed tick, one command entry point
- `src/render/` three.js view: chunked terrain, instanced forest, track, procedural models, smoke, camera, picking
- `src/ui/` React HUD and panels in the chosen "Pay Streak" design; Zustand for interface state
- Saves in IndexedDB with a versioned schema

## Tests

- `npm test`: 174 Vitest tests (terrain costs and persistence, affordability, credit, rail connectivity, routing, cargo conservation, depletion, processing yields, sales, interest, save/load, exploits, and the full loop with money and ore audited on every tick)
- `npm run test:e2e`: Playwright drives the real interface through all twelve steps of the loop, then saves and reloads

## Not in this slice

Fog of war, contract and passenger freight, junction signalling beyond whole-route reservation, day/night, multiple save slots, sandbox settings.

body:
## What changed

Replaces the Dashboard's top navigation row with a side navigation, grouped like the Planner's information architecture. Paths do not change, so every existing link keeps working. Web only; no CLI or Snapshot change.

- **Navigation model** (`src/lib/view/routes.ts`, pure): `NAV_GROUPS` in order (Home, Net worth; Plan: Overview, FI date, Compare; Tax; Records: Ledger, Health), with a flat `ROUTES` derived from it and `routeAt(path)`. Pinned by `routes.test.ts`.
- **Side navigation** (`src/components/shell/`): fixed at `lg` and up (15rem). On narrow screens a menu button in the top bar opens it as a drawer; it closes on Escape, on a link click and on the backdrop. `<nav aria-label="Pages">`, group headings, `aria-current="page"` on the current page. Icons are Lucide SVG elements (ISC licence, noted in `nav-icons.ts`), generated from the Lucide repository, drawn as SVG elements, never `{@html}`.
- **Plan switcher** at the foot of the side navigation: a labelled select ("Scenario", matching the existing pickers and the `scenario` query parameter) of the Snapshot's Scenario names, from the pure `scenarioNames` in `src/lib/view/plan.ts`. It sets `scenario` with `setQueryParam`; Projection and Tax already follow it. Hidden while the Snapshot loads or names no Scenario. Links keep the whole query string, so `scenario` and `demo` persist across pages.
- **Top bar**: the current page's label, the Snapshot status, and a "Display options" button that opens a right-side modal `<dialog>` holding the Hide amounts and Dark theme switches (`PreferenceControls`, same `preferences` module). Escape, the close button and the backdrop close it.
- Route file titles follow the labels: `/` is "Home · Dashboard", `/projection/` is "Overview · Dashboard" (the route-title test requires the label).

## How it was checked
