body:
## What / why
Fixes a flaky device-sync test (Immich album link-only import): a photo told of by another device was adopted whenever any collection this device takes wanted it, Immich albums included.

## Root cause
When device b's record of an album photo (full quality, original) reached device a before a's own link-only Immich import, a listed it as b's photo, so it never became link-only. Ghosts are now adopted only for the depth wanted from peers (`depth_from_peers`, Immich albums excluded); the Immich import brings the photo in and the record then applies to it. The test also waits for a's own listing of the album's members, which are never told between devices.

  - 発行:名前を入れ、再認証の後に発行し、token を同じ Dialog で1回だけ見せる。token はラベルを付けた読み取り専用の欄(textarea)に等幅で出し、focus したら全体を選ぶ。コピーのボタン(Clipboard API)と、コピーできなかったときの知らせ。再認証を取り消したら発行しない。
  - 取り消し:トークンの名前を出した確認の Dialog の後に送る(再認証は求めない。server の決まり)。
  - 結果は Toast(発行は、token の Dialog を閉じたとき)。失敗は Dialog の中の `Notice`。訳は en・ja・zh-Hans。
- token は Dialog の state にだけ置き、TanStack Query(query と送信の cache)に入れない。閉じた後に、画面・URL・query client のどこからも token を読めないことを、画面のテストで確かめる(送信の結果に token を入れるとテストが落ちることも確かめた)。
- 名前は、再認証の前に contract と同じスキーマで確かめる。そのため contract から `deployTokenName` を export した(server の振る舞いは変えていない)。
- 作り物の server(`src/testing/fake-routes/create-deploy-token-routes.ts`)と、画面の story(`screens/DeployTokens`。状態ごと)と、token の値を出す部品(`features/deploy-tokens/ui/token-value.tsx`)の story を足した。
- 決めたことと割り切ったことは `apps/admin/src/features/deploy-tokens/DECISIONS.md`。

## 確かめたこと

- `bun run check`(server のテストを含む全部)
- Storybook(手元の別のポート)で light・dark と状態ごとに描き、行の文字の塊とボタンの縦の中心(差 0px)、右端のそろい、token の欄の左右の余白(13px ずつ)と上下の余白(字面から 10.5px ずつ)、ラベルと欄の間(6px。入力欄と同じ)を測った。幅 375px でもはみ出さない。
- ブラウザで、コピーできなかった後に Shift+Tab で token の欄に移ると、全体(66文字)が選ばれることを確かめた。
- ブラウザで、発行の直後に「コピー」を押すと Dialog が閉じて token を失う不具合を見つけて直した(下の「ほかに決めたこと」)。

- screenshot(light と dark、状態ごと)を見て、見た目を確かめる。
- コピーの成功は、作業に使った内蔵ブラウザがクリップボードを許さないため、テスト(作り物の Clipboard)と、Clipboard を差し替えた Storybook でしか確かめていない。手元の Chrome で一度コピーを試す。
- token を見せている Dialog も、Escape・外側の押下・「閉じる」で、確かめずに閉じる(パスキーの Dialog と同じ。「割り切ったこと」に書いた)。外側の押下では閉じないようにするか、閉じる前に確かめるか。
- 一覧の読み込みに失敗したときは、知らせを出すだけで「再試行」は無い(パスキーの欄と同じ)。足すか。
- 行ごとの「取り消す」は、名前を含まない同じ名前のボタン(パスキーの「削除」と同じ)。スクリーンリーダー向けに名前を含めるかを、パスキーの欄と一緒に決める。同じ名前のトークンを見分ける手段(ID の一部を出すなど)も、名前の重複の扱いと一緒に決める。

author: zhangmq
body:
Fixes the Final Fight Revenge character-select corruption: the background was covered in blue vertical stripes (NBG3 sampled `0x60000`, the NBG0 name table, instead of the real art at `0x62000+`).

## Root cause

`getEatClock()` charged every SH-2 DMA word written into VDP2 RAM **82 cycles**, so a 2048-word ROM->VRAM tilemap copy stays in flight for hundreds of SH-2 time slices (the probe measured ~340 `DMAExec` slices, about six words each).

FFR builds its NBG3 name table exactly that way: it starts the DMA and then, in the same instruction stream, runs an in-place read-modify-write over the same plane that adds the character base `0x100` to every entry. While the copy was still running the CPU read half-filled entries, the DMA then overwrote most of them with un-based values, and the final plane held `0x00XX` where it should hold `0x01XX`.

## Change

`yabause/src/sh2core.c`, `getEatClock()`: the `default(source) -> VDP2 RAM` entry is now **2** cycles (one bus read plus one bus write) instead of 82. A transfer of that size finishes inside a single slice, so the CPU sees the completed plane.

Nothing else is touched; other source/destination combinations keep their current values.

## Verification (H700 device, coin at 17.0 s / START at 18.0 s injection run)

| | before | after |
|---|---|---|
| NBG3 name table at character select | `n01=1777 n00=2319`, 0x100 below the reference | `n01=2352 n00=0`, hash `9B40F920` - byte-identical to yabause 2.5.1 |
| blue-stripe pixels in a 720x480 capture | 18701 (5.41 %) | **0 (0.00 %)** |
| FFR run | fps 59-60, skip=0 | fps 59-60, skip=0 |

Also: the write ordering now matches the reference core (the DMA fills the whole plane, then the CPU adds the base); `gaxeduel` and `astrass` boot and render for 35 s with no errors; the `libretro` and `standalone` builds both succeed.

## Risk

The value paces every ROM/WRAM -> VDP2 DMA. Two facts keep the risk low: this fork already completes a DMA as soon as the CPU reads CHCR (`DmaPollDrive()`), and the reference core prices these DMA words at effectively zero cycles (`DMATransferCycles()` there calls the `*Nocache()` wrappers, which drop the cycle pointer). "The DMA finishes inside a slice" is therefore already an accepted behaviour here; this change makes the common case match it with a defensible per-word cost.

author: matthewlacerda2
body:
## What changed
`dev::memory::decoded_gpu_tests` — the direction check that a texture load from its compressed cache holds no more memory beside its GPU copies than the same textures decoded from PNG — now fails only when the cached figure exceeds the decoded one by more than `SLACK = STAGING_BUDGET` (16 MiB). It compares and prints both figures in bytes, not rounded megabytes. Renamed to `gpu_cached_textures_peak_at_most_a_staging_budget_past_the_same_decoded`, since "no higher" is no longer what it holds.

`.config/nextest.toml`: the test joins the list whose output prints on a pass, so every CI log carries each adapter's figures (`docs/testing.md`, *Which adapters a GPU tolerance holds on*).

## Why
The scheduled run on `68a85bda1` went red on macOS only: "cached peaked 16 MB … decoded 16 MB". The assert was `cached <= decoded` with no slack, and both figures rounded to 16 MB, so it failed by less than a megabyte of allocator noise. The file's header already says this is a direction check only: the unbounded-staging case is caught by `textures_gpu_tests`' four-times test, so a cached load a few megabytes past a decoded one is not the failure this test is for.

## Decisions
- **Slack = one staging budget.** A cached upload legitimately has one staging buffer (up to `STAGING_BUDGET`) in flight that a decoded load does not need on top of its own decode. What the test guards against is much bigger: a kept CPU copy of 32 compressed textures is ~171 MB, and an unbounded staging is the same order. So 16 MiB is small beside it and still catches both.
- The direction is kept. The test is not deleted or ignored.

## Measured (both from dispatched CI run [45057595529](https://github.com/MatthewLacerda2/rusty/actions/runs/45057595529), completed `success` on `250533a1`)
| Adapter | cached beside GPU | decoded beside GPU | GPU (cached / decoded) |
|---|---|---|---|
| Linux, lavapipe (`build-test (dev, 2/2)`) | 34 291 712 B | 293 834 752 B | 178 962 432 / 715 857 920 B |
| macOS-26, Metal (`build-test-cross (macos-26, 2/2)`) | 17 350 720 B | 34 177 088 B | 179 306 496 / 716 177 408 B |
| macOS, the red run on `68a85bda1` (old print, MB) | 16 MB | 16 MB | 171 / 683 MB |
| this container, lavapipe | 37 621 760 B | 288 194 560 B | 178 962 432 / 715 857 920 B |

On Metal the margin between the two figures swings from ~0 to ~17 MB from run to run, which is why a strict `<=` flaked there.

## Gates
`make quick-gates`, `make clippy`, `make doc fuzz-check deny`, `make test` (6604 + 8051 passed) green locally on `6738ca9a`. CI proof run 45057595529 green on `250533a1` (every job, the macOS legs included). The head `3e5dc844` adds only a doc comment with these figures: `make quick-gates` and `cargo fmt --check` green on it. The branch holds the latest `main`.

## For a human
- [ ] `make test-gpu ADAPTER=<gpu> on the head` on a desktop GPU (the cloud has none). The file's sibling header says these memory tests can't fail on a discrete GPU, so this is expected to pass trivially.

Mutation: none needed — test-only change.

Closes #2614

author: ryun1
body:
Stacked on #1008 (M15b): merge that first; GitHub then retargets this PR to `feature/mobile-wallet`.

## Summary

M15d: Mobile parity P4 (custom RPC endpoint) and P5 (Starknet names) on iOS and Android, over wallet-core `v0.6.0`. **Stacked on #1007 (M15a).** Merge that first, then retarget this to `feature/mobile-wallet`.

- **Endpoints from the wallet.** Every RPC read and send gets its `NetworkInfo` from one place, `endpointNetwork` (`NetworkEndpoints.swift` / `.kt`), which is `wallet.networks()`: the override first, the bundled endpoints behind it as failover. `WalletStore.networkInfo` is the only caller. It is computed at each use, so nothing captured while locked carries over. Before a wallet exists or while it's locked, the core has no readable override and the bundled list is used; onboarding has nothing to honour then. The per-endpoint chain-id check is unchanged.
- **RPC endpoint setting.** On the Network screen beside the relay setting, for the selected network (`rpcOverride` / `setRpcOverride`: trimmed; empty clears). The core's refusal is shown under the field and as a toast. A save for the network on screen re-enters the portfolio's scope, so no read goes to the old endpoints after the save. The extension puts the field one screen deeper (Advanced endpoints → Endpoints).
- **Redaction.** `redactEndpoints` covers the core-supplied text the apps can show (`describe`'s pass-through and the token add/scan lines). Transport errors already collapse to fixed copy on both platforms and are never logged, and no `NetworkInfo` is logged.
- **Starknet names (P5)** in the send recipient step:
  1. `starkNameNormalize` decides whether the input is a name.
  2. For each endpoint, the chain id is proven first (`rpcVerifyChainId`), then `starkNameAddressRequest` is sent and judged with `starkNameJudgeAddress`.
  3. `tryNextEndpoint` fails over.
  4. If no endpoint is on the right chain, or every one fails, the lookup fails closed.
  5. A result is dropped if the field was edited or the network changed while it was in flight.

  The review shows the full resolved address with "Resolved from Starknet ID" and leads with "New recipient. Check the full address before you send." when the address isn't in the person's lists. All wording is the extension's.
- **Behaviour change on Continue:** typed text naming exactly one contact or account now picks that row, as the extension's `commitTyped` does. Before, it only showed the invalid-address error.

## Roadmap & release

- **Roadmap issue:** n/a (wallet-core `docs/PLAN.md`, Next PRs: M15; refs #990)
- **Target release:** `feature/mobile-wallet`, not a release branch
- **Acceptance criterion satisfied:** Mobile parity P4 and P5 on mobile
- [x] This change is **in scope** for the target release.

## Checks

- [ ] `bun run check`: not run in full. `tests/conformance/mobile-*` passes (253 pass, 1 skip).
- [ ] `bun run test:e2e`: not run (no extension change)
- [x] Tests are included for the behavior changed:
  - iOS `RpcOverrideTests`: override first with bundled failover, clearing, locked/no wallet, refusals, redaction.
  - iOS `StarkNameLookupTests`: chain proven first, wrong chain never asked, stale answers dropped (edit and network change), each failure line, fails closed, a listed row wins, review facts.
  - Android JVM: `NetworkEndpointsTest`, `ErrorTextTest`, `StarkNameLookupTest`, `RecipientBookTest`, `ReviewFactsTest`.
  - Android instrumented: `CoreBridgeTest.rpcOverrideFirstAndRedacted` and `StarkNameFlowTest`.
  - Not covered by a test: the portfolio reload after a save. The store's portfolio has no injectable transport, so a store-level test would make live reads.
- [x] No lint or type suppressions added
- [x] All changed files stay under the 500-line cap

Run locally before restacking onto #1007:
- iOS `BrambleTests`: 121 tests, 2 skipped, 0 failures.
- Android JVM tests pass.
- Instrumented `StarkNameFlowTest` and `CoreBridgeTest` passed on an API 35 emulator, but that was before the final review commit.
- `lint.sh all` is clean.

## Dependencies

none

author: revealuistudio
body: ## Closes Supersedes #3092. ## Summary - Required judges run from the base commit. The pull request tree is what they scan. That covers the expensive-suite classifier, the result-job decision, the security gate, the quality validators, the backflow guard, the leak scanner, and the archive check. - Where the workflow file is still taken from the pull request, Trusted gate judge checks out only the base commit, reads head files through the API, and compares the locked result jobs and classifier to the base. It uses the GitHub token with contents read and pull request read, and it does not execute head code. - A change to a locked judge path clears through the owner's signed request label plus an SSHSIG on the exact head, the same path the Security review gate uses. With no valid signed request, the locked change fails. A review-controller receipt comes later. - #3092 drafted the script-side fix against an older `test` tip. This branch is cut from current `test` and replaces that draft. No required check name was renamed, added or removed. The judge job stays `Trusted gate judge`. ## Type of Change - [ ] Bug fix - [ ] New feature - [ ] Breaking change - [ ] Refactor - [ ] Documentation - [x] CI/CD or tooling ## Checklist - [x] `pnpm gate --phase=1 --changed` passed (lint and the phase-1 validators) - [x] Tests added and passing (judge suites under `scripts/ci/__tests__` and `scripts/validate/__tests__/security-review-gate.test.ts`) - [x] No `any` types or `console.*` added in production code - [x] Any future-tense claims cite a tracker `pnpm install --frozen-lockfile` stayed clean. ## Owner follow-ups - Locked judge paths are the locked `ci.yml` result jobs, `scripts/ci/expensive-suite.mjs`, `scripts/ci/required-check-result.mjs`, and the other files the judge locks. Those changes clear only with the owner request label and an unexpired owner SSHSIG bound to the exact head. The verifier is the Security review gate's existing owner-record check. An expired signature, a signature for a different head, or a request label without a signature fails. - A review-controller receipt comes later. - This pull request uses its own result script and quality runner when those files are absent from the base commit. After merge, later pull requests run the base copies. - The archive manifest and the leak scanner patterns are the base copies. A newly archived path or a new scanner pattern takes effect after it is on the base commit. - This pull request does not change rulesets, secrets, or variables. ## Test plan - [ ] Confirm a locked-path edit with no signed request fails Trusted gate judge after this workflow is on `test`. - [ ] Confirm the same edit with the request label and an unexpired exact-head SSHSIG passes.

body:
Maintenance patch for the 1.x line, targeting the new `release/1.x` branch cut from v1.8.1.

ZeroAlloc.StateMachine 1.8.1 ships a generator built against Roslyn 5.9, so SDK 10.0.1xx through 10.0.3xx skip it with CS9057. ZeroAlloc.Resilience 3.x still depends on StateMachine 1.x, so its consumers on those SDKs lose the StateMachine generator.

- The generator now reference Microsoft.CodeAnalysis.CSharp 5.0.0, as on main in #243.
- The sdk10-consumer and roslyn-floor CI jobs from #243 are added here too.
- release-please.yml runs on pushes to `release/**` and passes `target-branch: github.ref_name`, so this branch gets its own release PR from its own manifest. CI and baseline-checks run on PRs to `release/**`.

Part of ZeroAlloc-Net/.github#77.

author: slopgobblercobbler
body:
### What and why

Add comprehensive semantic tests and reference mathematical oracle for RDNA2 untyped buffer memory atomic subtraction (`buffer_atomic_sub`) in `tests/semantic/test_buffer_atomic_sub.py`.

The 8-commit suite covers:
1. Reference mathematical oracle and architectural model for `buffer_atomic_sub` (`memory[addr] = (memory[addr] - vdata) mod 2^32`) with 128-bit Buffer Resource Descriptor (V#), hardware bounds checking against `num_records`, and `glc` pre-operation return value.
2. Symbolic AST opcode definitions and typed expressions (`Register`, `BufferAtomicModifiers`, `Opcode.BUFFER_ATOMIC_SUB`, `Instruction`, `Program`).
3. Deterministic scalar instruction interpreter with register file, memory state, and program chain execution.
4. SIMD multi-lane divergence and 32/64-bit `EXEC` masking across Wave32 and Wave64 execution with concurrent atomic accumulation and ticket issuing.
5. Register aliasing and in-place operand preservation (`vdata == vaddr`, SGPR descriptor preservation, and unrelated VGPR isolation).
6. Condition codes, status flags (`zero`, `negative`, `positive`, `borrow_wrapped`, `in_bounds`, `oob_fault`), and scalar `VCC` isolation.
7. IEEE 754 boundary extremes (subnormals, infinities, NaNs, +/-0.0) confirming exact 32-bit bitwise two's complement integer subtraction and boundary dword alignment.
8. Negative controls, syntax rejection (out-of-range registers, invalid immediate offsets, invalid wave sizes), and mutation detection.

### Tested

  - `python -I tests/semantic/test_buffer_atomic_sub.py` (40/40 tests passing)

This PR contains the following updates:

| Package | Type | Update | Change |

| [truvity/ci-actions](https://redirect.github.com/truvity/ci-actions) | action | minor | `v3.14.2` → `v3.15.0` |

---

### Release Notes

<details>
<summary>truvity/ci-actions (truvity/ci-actions)</summary>

### [`v3.15.0`](https://redirect.github.com/truvity/ci-actions/blob/HEAD/CHANGELOG.md#v3150)

[Compare Source](https://redirect.github.com/truvity/ci-actions/compare/v3.14.2...v3.15.0)

##### Added

- **`ssm-secrets` reads a job's secrets from AWS SSM Parameter Store, as the job.** It replaces `openbao-secrets` for a job whose secrets live in SSM; `openbao-secrets` is unchanged. The action takes `issuer`, `account`, `role`, `region` and `path` (all required), `keys` (the leaves to take, whitespace- or comma-separated; empty takes every parameter directly under the path) and `sluisctl` (`auto` or `direct`, as in `openbao-secrets`), and the job needs `permissions: { id-token: write }`. `ci-actions ssm-secrets` (`internal/ssmsecrets`) runs `sluisctl token --audience aws:<account>:<role>` to exchange the job's GitHub identity token at the sluis issuer, presents that token as the web identity of an STS `AssumeRoleWithWebIdentity` call for the role, and makes one `GetParametersByPath` (decrypted, not recursive) under `path`. The temporary credentials stay in the action's process: no AWS profile, config or credentials file is written and nothing is exported to later steps, and the environment's own AWS credentials are never used for the call. The outputs are the `openbao-secrets` ones: `env-file`, the path of a mode-0600 file of `NAME='value'` lines under `RUNNER_TEMP` (the leaf of each parameter, upper-cased with `-` turned into `_`; a leaf that is no environment variable name, or two leaves that become the same name, fail the step), and `value`, set when exactly one parameter is taken. Every value is masked, line by line, as soon as it is read, and so are the exchanged token and the temporary credentials; the step fails when a named key is missing or the path holds no parameters, and a failed run leaves no env file. Tests: a faked SSM client covers the env naming, the keys filter, paging, masking (nothing is printed outside `::add-mask::`), the env-file quoting and every refusal; a fake STS and SSM endpoint checks that the role's ARN and the exchanged token reach `AssumeRoleWithWebIdentity` and that the credentials it returns, not the environment's, sign the read; `hack/tagged-pins-wrapper-cases.sh` covers the wrapper. **Upgrade:** none; an adopter replaces the `openbao-secrets` step with `ssm-secrets` and the OpenBAO inputs (`address`, `namespace`, `mount`, `auth-mount`, `ca-cert`) with `account`, `role` and `region`.

## Summary

This PR merges `dev` into `main` (package version remains `0.1.0`), combining:
1. **Visualization engine hardening** — automated layout anti-collision & visual regression testing, dark-theme & vector/GIF export fidelity, responsive/large-system Interactive 3D Studio polish with 1:1 Python snippet parity, and modularization of the 4 largest render/plot modules.
2. **Commercial-safe code defaults with classic `xkcd Script` gallery** — SIL OFL 1.1 `Patrick Hand` is the default font in library code and the 3D Studio, while front-facing showcase figures in `book/_static/gallery/` keep the classic `xkcd Script` opt-in look (`xm.use_xkcd_script()`).
3. **Targeted scientific hygiene, parser/HTML security & release CI** — analytical validation benchmarks across 9 domains, core numerical edge-case fixes, parser resource ceilings, HTML XSS escaping, and wheel-tested CI/release gates.

---

## Key Changes

### 1. Visualization Engine Hardening
- **Anti-Collision, Layout Auditor & Visual Regression (`style/layout.py`, top-level `xm.*` exports):**
  - Added `resolve_1d_label_positions()`, pixel-bbox `avoid_text_overlaps()`, `audit_figure_layout()` (`LayoutAuditReport` checking text overlaps, figure clipping, dark outer-border leaks, and WCAG 2.1 contrast), and deterministic SSIM-like `figure_visual_fingerprint()` / `visual_similarity()`.
  - Wired automated label separation into `thermo.py`, `reactions.py`, `crystalfield.py`, `charts.py`, and dense spectral peaks (`_spectroscopy_peaks.py`).
  - Added `tests/test_visual_regression.py` (68 tests covering 19 plotters across `classic`, `dark_chalk`, and `blueprint`, plus stress tests for 20 clustered peaks, long formulas, extreme aspect ratios, and crowded subplot grids).
- **Dark-Theme Parity & Vector/GIF Export Fidelity (`layout/export.py`, `style/theme.py`, `plots/{animations,electrochem,ptable,graphs,trajectory,structure}.py`):**
  - Upgraded `save_figure(..., svg_fonttype="path", pdf_fonttype=42, metadata=None)` for crisp font embedding in PowerPoint, Keynote, and Inkscape, and un-sketched canvas patches to eliminate dark-theme border leaks in PNG/PDF/SVG/GIF exports.
  - Audited and fixed WCAG text/pill/tile/legend/colorbar contrast across `dark_chalk`, `talk_dark`, and `blueprint` (`tests/test_dark_and_export_fidelity.py`).
- **Interactive 3D Studio Hardening (`render/interactive.py`, `data/templates/viewer.html`):**
  - Added a responsive collapsible controls drawer (`#xm-sidebar-toggle`, auto-collapsing at `<= 780px` with `ResizeObserver`) so narrow notebook/book iframes never clip controls.
  - Added O(N) spatial-grid bond inference, typed-array depth sorting, and automatic interactive drag LOD for `500–5,000+` atom supercells (snapping to full pen-and-ink detail on pointer release, plus an **Always full detail** toggle).
  - Achieved 1:1 parity between live browser controls (camera, preset, scales, H-bonds, labels, trajectory frame, and live 3D isosurface level/shading/opacity/colors) and **Copy Python** via `xm.generate_python_snippet()` (`tests/test_interactive_studio_hardening.py`).
- **Modularized Oversized Render/Plot Modules:**
  - Split `render/structure3d.py` (1,243 lines), `plots/materials.py` (1,494 lines), `plots/spectroscopy.py` (1,367 lines), and `plots/electronic.py` (1,222 lines) into 19 cohesive modules (`63–519` lines each) with 100% backwards-compatible facade re-exports (`tests/test_module_reexports.py`).

### 2. Commercial-Safe Code Defaults & Classic `xkcd Script` Showcase Gallery
- Switched the library default font across all 9 `ThemePreset`s and `interactive_studio.html` to commercial-safe **SIL OFL 1.1 `Patrick Hand`** (with `Comic Neue` also bundled).

### 3. Scientific Validation, Core Fixes & Scope Transparency
- Added `tests/test_scientific_validation.py` (**30 analytical benchmarks across 9 domains**), `scripts/benchmark_scalability.py`, and a dedicated `scientific-validation` CI job.
- Added `BandGapResult` / `BandStructure.analyze_band_gap()`, LLL cell reduction + exact `BrillouinZone` volume validation & optional `seekpath` backend, Birch–Murnaghan covariance uncertainties (`EOSFitResult`), lossless LAMMPS `xu/yu/zu` & `ix/iy/iz` unwrapping + same-species RDF normalization, and CODATA 2022 unit helpers (`core/units.py`).

### 4. Security, Parser Ceilings & Release/CI Hardening

body:
## Resumen

Cierra el hito **H0 (línea base)** de G-Calls Core 1.0. Incluye dos partes:

1. **`1ff6145` — Trabajo local del 22/11** (autor: Deivid): login real contra PHP en React, CSRF en logout (R-01), correcciones H-01/H-02 en `contactos.php`, `create_admin.php` con contraseña oculta, `seed_servicios.php`.
2. **5 commits de `fix/h0-cierre`**:
   - `fix(auth)`: `session.gc_maxlifetime = 7200` (antes el hosting podía borrar la sesión a los 24 min) y la cookie se expira cuando la sesión caduca por inactividad (M-07). `destroy_session()` centraliza el cierre.
   - `fix(cors)`: dominio real `gcallssas.com` (+ www) en lugar de `gcalls.com.co`; se retira `localhost:3000`; se anuncian PATCH/DELETE para H1/H2.
   - `fix(admin)`: si la sesión expira, `/admin/contactos` avisa y redirige al login.
   - `chore`: se retira el backend Node/Express legado (`server.js`, `express`, `nodemailer`, `cors`, `dotenv`).
   - `chore`: `.gitattributes` (LF) y `.editorconfig` (UTF-8 sin BOM); se quita el BOM de 5 TSX y se corrige texto corrupto.

**Fuera de alcance:** `schema.sql`, base de datos, datos QA, endpoints de negocio.

## Verificación (ejecutada, no "por diseño")

Entorno: MariaDB con `schema.sql` + `seed_servicios.php`, PHP 8.3 (`php -S`), Vite dev con proxy, Chromium (Playwright). Usuarios de prueba admin/editor/viewer.

| Verificación | Resultado |
|---|---|
| `php -l` (todos los PHP) | ✅ sin errores |
| `npx tsc --noEmit` | ✅ |
| `npm run build` | ✅ (sin `admin123` en el bundle) |
| `eslint` | ✅ 0 errores, 8 advertencias preexistentes de shadcn |
| BOM / texto corrupto | ✅ ninguno |
| `git diff --check` | ✅ |
| **Pruebas HTTP (40)** | ✅ **40/40** |
| **Pruebas E2E en navegador (10)** | ✅ **10/10** |

<details>
<summary>Detalle de las 40 pruebas HTTP</summary>

- **Formulario (T01–T11):** alta válida 200; texto guardado íntegro con `<b>`, `&`, comillas y ñ (H-02); servicio válido se persiste; servicio inexistente → NULL; email inválido, tipo inválido, JSON inválido y JSON array → 400; GET → 405; SQLi guardada como texto y tabla `usuarios` intacta.
- **Autenticación (T12–T23):** admin/contactos sin sesión 401; clave incorrecta 401; mismo mensaje para usuario inexistente; SQLi en email 400; login 200 sin `password_hash`; cookie `GCALLS_SESSID` HttpOnly + SameSite=Lax; admin 200, editor 200, viewer 403; POST → 405.
- **Logout y CSRF (T24–T29):** sin token 403 y la sesión sigue viva; token falso 403; token válido 200; después `me.php` 401 y admin/contactos 401.
- **Inactividad (T30, T33–T35):** >2 h → 401; **la cookie se expira**; el archivo de sesión se borra; `gc_maxlifetime` efectivo = 7200.
- **CORS (T36–T40):** `gcallssas.com` permitido; `gcalls.com.co` y `localhost:3000` rechazados; preflight con PATCH/DELETE; OPTIONS → 204.
- **Errores de BD (T31–T32):** error SQL → 500 (no 503) sin detalles SQL (H-01).
</details>

<details>
<summary>Detalle de las 10 pruebas E2E</summary>

E01 ruta protegida sin sesión → login · E02 clave incorrecta muestra "Credenciales inválidas" sin texto corrupto · E03 login real → /admin · E04 navbar con nombre y rol reales · E05 listado con filas reales de MySQL · E06 sesión expirada + "Refrescar" → login · E07 aviso "Tu sesión expiró" · E08 logout desde la UI · E09 tras logout `me.php` 401 · E10 sin errores JS en consola.
</details>

## ⚠️ Antes de fusionar

**Fusionar este PR en `main` despliega a producción** (workflow FTP). Consecuencias:

- ✅ Sale de producción el login simulado (`admin@gcalls.com` / `admin123` en el bundle actual).
- El panel en producción necesitará la API real: `.env` fuera de `public_html`, base de datos MySQL en el hosting y un usuario admin creado con `create_admin.php`. Sin eso, el login responderá 503, que es un estado seguro, pero el panel no funcionará.

Después de bajar la rama en Windows, si `git status` muestra archivos modificados sin haberlos tocado, se resuelve con `git add --renormalize .` (efecto de `.gitattributes`).

Closes: #33170

## Summary

Adding a live data source now looks like its settings page, the picker lists only what you can connect, and the copy across the add flow is plainer. Stacked on #33169, which built the settings page these rows come from.

### Picker

- **Only connectable integrations**: the coming-soon cards are gone. LinkedIn Ads and Salesforce show only when the instance has their app, and Google sources only when Google sign-in is set up.
- **Request a live source**: the last card of the grid. The name is asked for in a popover, tracked as before, and confirmed with a toast.
- **Caption**: "Query the tools you use live, right alongside your warehouse".

### Add dialogs

- **Same rows as settings**: every add dialog (token integrations, PostHog, Google, LinkedIn Ads, Salesforce) lays out as cards of rows, with a label and short caption on the left and the control on the right.
- **Scopes**: integrations whose key needs scopes (GitHub, HubSpot, Meta Ads, PostHog with a key) open with a **Scopes** card, each scope a chip that copies on click.
- **Access**: the account field, then the token with **Test** on the same row. The test result replaces the caption as one green or red line. Salesforce's environment is a "Use a sandbox" switch, production by default.
- **Details**: Name, then the explore prefix (it follows the name, says it can't be changed later, and when it's taken offers a free one to click). LinkedIn Ads and Salesforce get the prefix in #33174.
- **No intro paragraph and no AI hint**: the title and cards carry it, and the hint stays optional on the settings page.
- **Logos**: every add dialog's title starts with the integration's logo, and GitHub's logo follows dark mode.
- **Add only**: these dialogs were only ever opened to add a source, so their edit mode is gone.

### Copy

- Captions, errors and card descriptions are short single sentences with no full stops, for example "From Project settings" instead of "The number after /project/ in your PostHog URL".
- Validation reads "Give it a name" and "Paste the access token" instead of "… is required".

### Shared pieces

- `LIVE_INTEGRATION_CATALOG` holds each integration's `defaultName` and `scopes`, so dialogs, settings and onboarding read one place.
- `LiveSourceSettingsRows`: the settings rows, cards and test outcome line, shared by the settings page and the add dialogs.

## Regression analysis

- **Catalog requests**: the one-click Request on coming-soon cards (`integration: <id>` events) is gone. Custom-name requests remain.

- **PostHog sign-in**: unchanged, it still redirects to PostHog. The Scopes card shows only in API key mode.
- **Onboarding**: the PostHog step on the onboarding page is unchanged.
- **Google, LinkedIn Ads and Salesforce**: they still redirect to sign in. Reconnecting from settings doesn't go through these dialogs.

body:
## Summary
**S0: render every diagram**
- `renderDiagramQueue` renders the document's diagrams one at a time through a second, private `useRenderer` instance. `PresentationDialog` and version comparison already use this pattern.
- Every diagram takes the preview's exact path: engine, theme, safety check, sanitising, cache and timeout. `use-renderer` and the worker are unchanged.
- The active diagram's current preview is reused when its source matches.
- Progress is reported as "n of N", and an `AbortSignal` cancels the queue.
- A diagram that fails becomes an error entry, and the rest of the queue carries on.

**S2: whole-document snapshot**
- With more than one diagram, File → Export → Snapshot (HTML) opens a dialog: "Whole document (N diagrams)" (the default) or "This diagram", with a progress bar and Cancel. With a single diagram it exports directly, as before.
- The page has a contents list, which becomes a `<details>` menu below 640px. Each diagram gets its own section with its own pan and zoom, and failed diagrams show an error box.
- The header shows a combined source SHA-256, the diagram count and the version label.
- **Links between diagrams:**
  - Engine `<a href>` targets that match another diagram's title, id or `diagram-<n>` become `#diagram-<n>`. The match ignores case, a leading `#` and a `.puml`/`.pumlu` suffix. Ambiguous titles are left alone.
  - Project links (`represents`, `implements`, `relates`) show as a "Linked diagrams" line on each section.
- SVG element ids are prefixed per diagram, so gradients and markers can't collide.
- The S1 CSP and safety rules are unchanged, and there is still exactly one hash-pinned inline script.

**Measured** (Chromium, dev server, click to download): 10 mixed diagrams in about 3.0 s, and a 200-task Gantt plus a small active diagram in about 2.3 s. About 0.7 s of each is booting the engine when the dialog opens.

**Known limits**
- Diagrams other than the active one are not decorated with live Jira markers, which exist only for the active diagram.
- Project links appear as a list line, not as anchors inside the SVG.
- The snapshot styles were appended to `14-ai-assistant.css` (chunk order unchanged).

## Test plan
- Unit tests:
  - `render-queue.test.ts` (7): order, reuse, cancel, failure isolation.
  - `snapshot-document.test.ts`: contents, anchors, link rewriting, error entries, one inline script, escaping.
  - `SnapshotDialog.test.tsx`.
  - 184/184 across `app`, `render`, `features/snapshot` and the menus.
- `snapshot-export.spec.ts` on chromium, firefox and webkit. A 3-diagram document is exported and opened over `file://`. It checks the contents and the three sections, zoom per diagram, and that a link between diagrams jumps to the right section. It also checks the external link attributes, that there are no network requests or page errors, and the phone menu with no horizontal scroll at 375px.
- `editor.spec.ts` (Export menu) and `export-options.spec.ts` still pass.

body:
## Summary

This PR introduces a shared content media management module for **Activities and Announcements**, allowing authorised staff to upload, manage, and serve images, videos, and PDF documents through a centralised implementation.

## Changes Made

### 1. Shared Content Media Module
- Added the `apps.content_media` application.
- Introduced the `ContentMedia` model with UUID-based identifiers.
- Supports three media categories:
  - Images: JPEG, PNG, WebP
  - Videos: MP4, WebM
  - Documents: PDF
- Added configurable file-size limits and content validation.
- Stores original filenames, MIME types, file sizes, uploader information, and timestamps.
- Enforces that each media record belongs to exactly one Activity or Announcement.

### 2. Media Management API
- Added endpoints for listing and uploading media associated with Activities and Announcements.
- Added a dedicated media deletion endpoint.
- Implemented file-serving endpoints with access control.
- Publicly published content media can be accessed publicly.
- Draft and archived content media require authentication and an authorised Pastor or Administrator role.

### 3. Activity and Announcement Integration
- Integrated media references into Activity and Announcement serializers.
- Updated public selectors to retrieve associated media efficiently.
- Updated URL configurations and central API routing.
- Ensured public responses expose safe media metadata without revealing internal storage paths or uploader details.

### 4. Security and Data Integrity
- Enforced role-based permissions on media management operations.
- Restricted media uploads and deletion to eligible draft content.
- Added file-type, content-signature, image-dimension, and file-size validation.
- Added database constraints and indexes.
- Integrated media operations with audit logging and transactional service logic.

### 5. Storage and Documentation
- Added configurable Django storage backend settings.
- Added the default local filesystem storage configuration.
- Added `docs/media_storage_and_backup.md` covering storage configuration, access control, backup, restoration, and operational considerations.
- Added migration `0012_contentmedia.py`.

### 6. Testing
- Added tests for media validators, service operations, API permissions, uploads, downloads, deletion, and Activity/Announcement integration.
- Verified the targeted media test suite: **57 tests passed**.
- Django system check completed successfully.
- Earlier full test suite: **448 tests passed**.
- Black and Flake8 are enforced through pre-commit hooks.

## Security Considerations
- Internal storage paths are not exposed through public API responses.
- Draft and archived media remain protected.
- Published media is intentionally publicly accessible.
- Backend permissions are enforced independently of frontend visibility.

## Notes
Production deployment still requires a decision on persistent media storage, backup automation, malware scanning, and retention policies.

## Checklist
- [x] Shared media model and migration added
- [x] Media validation implemented
- [x] Upload, listing, deletion, and file-serving APIs added
- [x] Activity and Announcement integration completed
- [x] Permission and access-control tests added
- [x] Storage and backup documentation added
- [x] Targeted media tests passed
- [ ] Pre-commit formatting changes staged and commit completed
- [ ] Changes pushed and PR reviewed

author: davecthomas
body:
## What was wrong

A run that changed no file failed its task with "pi changed nothing". That is right when the agent could not do the work. It is wrong when the base branch already has the work, because another task or a person merged it first. The task then went round its retries, and its issue stayed open, for work that was done.

## What changes

- **Another model decides which it is.** When a task's run changes nothing, a reviewer pair gets one run on the base branch (`prompts/already-done-v1.txt`). It is told what the first run said, as a claim to test, reads the code, runs the checks, and ends with `submit_review`.
- **Work that is there closes the task.** Verdict clean ends the workflow with outcome `already_done`. The task is closed, and its reason says where the work is.
- **Work that is not there fails as before**, with the missing parts in the reason. So does a run with no verdict, or a deployment with no other model to ask. When the check cannot tell, the answer is "not done".
- **The issue is closed with the reason.** The planner comments "Already done: …" on the issue and closes it, on every tracker. No pull request exists to do that.
- A task that asked for no review gets no check.

## Deploy safety

The new run is behind `workflow.patched("nothing-changed-check")`. A history of the new path is recorded (`patched-nothing-changed-already-done.json`), and every earlier history still replays.

## Why files outside one area change

`planner/tracker_progress.py` changes because closing the issue is the planner's write, and it now writes this one case to trackers it otherwise tells nothing (GitHub).

## Checks

Three cases in `tests/run_service/test_review_loop.py`, the prompt's test, the replay test, and a case in `tests/planner/test_goal_tracker.py`.

author: tuomashatakka
body:
## what the frame gained

The far coast covers both flanks of the `default` frame, and it read as radial brush strokes. Now it reads as rounded fells behind a coast. Zeroing the cloud, mist, fog, lens, glare and indirect light left the strokes where they were, so the cause was the ground itself. Past the ridge, the height was the bearing's crest times a share, so every summit got extruded a kilometre inland as a spoke. The gullies also ran unbroken down every bearing.

## how

- `skyline.ts`: past the ridge, the bearing's crest hands over to `plateauAt`, a 460 m world-space field at 42–74 % of `farShore.rise`. The fells inland now have no bearing.
- Gullies are cut only where a 150 m catchment field says water gathers (`GATHER_SCALE`), and only on the seaward face.
- Inland, the massif's 38 m octave fades to its mean (`RIDGED_MEAN`), because it aliased at the ~60 m ring spacing there. The stands' noise is now 180/120 m instead of 90/31.
- Bare rock on the spurs of the fells, as well as on the steep face.
- Panel: the *the tide* and *running water* rows are gone. `tide.range` and `beck.flow` are now config leaves, with unchanged defaults.

## cost

None. Same mesh and same triangle count, built once. Mobile tour census is unchanged (default 134 draws, near 85, far 113, noon 134, night and winter 138; 1.02M / 0.94M / 1.45M tris; 0 errors).

## verification

- `bun run gate --full` is green.
- Studio pixel diff vs main on the phone tier: default 18.0 % of pixels moved, noon 18.2 %, winter 2.3 %, night 1.8 %, near and far 0.00 %.
- New tests in `skyline.test.ts`: the rim's height no longer follows the crest (|r| < 0.5), and the plateau stays in its band and is deterministic.

## follow-ups

- The far shore's colour is per-vertex, 35–60 m apart. A far-field term in the ground material could add grain finer than that.
- Cloud shadows stay on the sea at `atmosphere.cloudCover=0`, because the front drives them.

## Pourquoi
Sur Xbox, le jeu plante en plein combat dans la Foire de Givrecloche (−5), même en Fluide et après un redémarrage de la console.

Ce que j'ai mesuré :
- le combat ne dessine pas la 3D ;
- en revanche, l'écran de combat pèse lourd : 98 couches de composition, environ 15 Mpx, dont cinq en plein écran.

Hypothèse : Edge reprend le contexte WebGL, puis le rechargement de la page ne retrouve pas de carte graphique, et l'écran « manque de mémoire graphique » s'affiche.

## Ce qui change
- **Contexte perdu :** la page n'est plus rechargée tout de suite.

- **Xbox :** le canevas 3D passe en `visibility:hidden` pendant un combat, pour retirer une couche plein écran. L'écran de combat est opaque, donc rien ne change à l'image.

author: manemone
body:
## 背景

dotfiles は、Windows の再起動のあとサインイン無しで WSL を起こす起動時タスク（S4U。ADR DOC-2611151248 の方式 A）を持っています。2026-11-21 の再起動でこのタスクが WSL を起こしましたが、その WSL の中からは、Windows を経由した NAS のアクセス（drvfs のマウント、WSL から呼ぶ Windows のプログラム）が全部失敗しました。ADR §4 は「S4U ではネットワーク資格情報が使えない」と書きながら、起動後に確かめる対象へ NAS を入れていませんでした。

## このプルリクエストの目的

原因を確かめ、影響を受ける処理を洗い出し、直し方の案を比べて人間に選んでもらったうえで、選ばれた案と「起動後に NAS を確認する手段」を `rebootctl` に入れます。傘ブランチ `reboot-network-creds` の孫1（#243）をマージ済みで、この PR はそれを `master` へ入れる最終 PR です。

## 実装内容

- 原因（読み取りだけで確認）: 起動時タスクで起きた WSL から呼ぶ Windows のプログラムは、S4U のログオンのまま動き、人間が後からサインインしても切り替わりません。そのログオンには Kerberos チケットも `net use` の接続も無く、NAS の UNC に届きません
- 選んだ案: S4U のまま、Windows のプログラムには UNC でなく WSL の中の cifs マウントを `wslpath -w` のパスで渡します。NAS の資格情報は WSL の中（root 600 のファイル）だけに置かれ、S4U を選んだ理由（秘密をマシンの外にも中にも置かない）と衝突しません。比べた他の案と見送った理由は ADR §7 に書きました
- `rebootctl status`（`--json` も）に NAS の確認を3つ追加: WSL の中のマウント／Windows から UNC／Windows から WSL のマウント経由。確認先は環境変数 `REBOOTCTL_NAS_MOUNT` / `REBOOTCTL_NAS_UNC` から読み、未設定の確認は飛ばします。道具が使えない・Windows 側が読めないときは「届かない」でなく「確認できなかった」（JSON は null）にします
- ADR DOC-2611151248 に §7（経過・原因・影響の洗い出し・案の比較と選択・未確認）を追記。`setup` の表示コメントと `bin/README.md` も合わせました
- テスト: `bin/tests/test_rebootctl.py` に、未設定・UNC 不可で WSL 経由可・Windows 側が読めない、の3状況を1つの scenario で固定するテストを1本足しました
- 傘の計画書 DOC-2611230305（孫2〜孫5 の追加、進行記録、全孫のマージ済みの更新を含む）も含みます

変更ファイル: `bin/rebootctl`、`bin/tests/test_rebootctl.py`、`bin/README.md`、ADR DOC-2611151248、計画書 DOC-2611230305

## この傘の他リポの孫 PR

UNC 前提だった別リポの処理を、孫1 で選んだ案（WSL の cifs マウントを `wslpath -w` のパスで渡す）に合わせる孫です。どれも非公開リポの PR のため、役割名で並べます。マージは各リポの人間が行い、すべてマージ済みです。

| 孫 | 対象 | PR |
|---|---|---|
| 2 | 学習ツール（NAS への転送と登録ツールの呼び出し） | 学習ツール #608 |
| 3 | 画像生成ツール（Windows 版 CLI 経路の設定の書き方の文書とテスト） | 画像生成ツール #468 |
| 4 | 画像生成ツール（保管庫の読み書き前にマウント先がマウントされているかを確認） | 画像生成ツール #472 |
| 5 | 登録ツール（保管庫・目録・作例の置き場を WSL のマウント経由のパスで受けても動くようにする） | 登録ツール #152 |

この PR（dotfiles）には、これらの孫の追加と進行を残した傘の計画書 DOC-2611230305 の更新が含まれます。

## レビューで見てほしいところ

- 影響を受ける別リポの処理（学習ツールの転送と Windows 版の登録ツールの呼び出し、画像生成ツールの Windows 版 CLI 経路）は UNC 前提のコードを持ちます。案に合わせる直しは別リポの作業で、この PR では行いません
- 実機で確かめた範囲: 原因（ログオンの種類・資格情報の有無）、WSL の cifs を Windows 側のパスで `Test-Path` と一覧取得できること、`status` の3項目が想定どおり出ること。確かめていない範囲: その経路での robocopy.exe / ruby.exe の書き込み・大容量転送、サインインしない本物の再起動後の確認、Interactive の一時タスク案の細部
- NAS の確認先を環境変数にしたのは、ホスト名などが環境ごとに違いリポに書けないためです。設定ファイルのほうがよいか見てください

## テスト結果

`bin/tests/lint.sh`・`python3 -m unittest discover -s bin/tests`・`./tools/doc-id/doc-id verify` が通っています。

## 今後の予定

マージ後に人間が行います。
1. `deploy-all.sh` で配る
2. シェルの環境変数 `REBOOTCTL_NAS_MOUNT`（WSL の cifs のマウント先）と `REBOOTCTL_NAS_UNC`（Windows から見た共有フォルダ）を設定する（登録済みタスクの再登録は不要）
3. サインインしないまま再起動し、`rebootctl status` の NAS の3項目が「WSL の中のマウントは届く・UNC は届かない・WSL 経由は届く」になることを確かめる

別リポ側の UNC 前提の直しは、上の孫2〜孫5 で済んでいます。

author: pipiche38
body:
## Summary

A model flagged `MainPoweredDevice` that announced itself as a reduced-function device now stays an **End Device**. Only its power source is corrected: MAC capability `0x80` becomes `0x84`, no longer `0x8e`.

## Why

No-neutral switches (Sonoff ZBMINI-L / ZBMINI-L2 / ZBMINIL2, Livolo TI0001, Tuya TS0011…) take their power through the load. They announce MAC capability `0x80` (RFD, power-source bit clear) and are real end devices. For example, the ZBMINIL2 raw node descriptor `1286040004002c000080524002` has MAC capability `80` and logical type 2 (End Device).

`ReArrangeMacCapaBasedOnModel()` rewrote every `MainPoweredDevice` model to `MacCapa = "8e"`, `DeviceType = "FFD"`, `LogicalType = "Router"`. That fixes the power source but also makes the device a router for everything that reads those fields:

- `NetworkMap.is_a_router()`: `MacCapa == "8e"` → the topology scan queries an end device (only the hard-coded TI0001/TS0011/TS0013/TS0601 models are excluded by name)
- `NetworkEnergy.isRouter()`: same test
- `tools_files.how_many_devices()`: counted as a router
- WebUI: `/zdevice-name` decodes `8e` to `["FFD", "RxonIdle", "MainPower"]` and the device list shows a router

It showed up with z4d-certified-devices adding `MainPoweredDevice` to the Sonoff ZBMINI no-neutral models (`fix/sonoff-zbmini-no-neutral-mains`): the battery icon went away, but the ZBMINIL2 was then shown as a router.

## Scope

- `Modules/tools_mac_capa.py`: `ReArrangeMacCapaBasedOnModel()`, main-powered branch only
- Affects models with `MainPoweredDevice` in their DeviceConf (certified: TS0011, lumi.switch.l0agl1, TICMeter, and the Sonoff ZBMINI-L* once that certified PR is merged) and the hard-coded TI0001 / TS0011 / TS0013 / TS0601-switch / TS0601-2Gangs-switch
- All radios; branch `stable9`. No persistent-format change, no REST or UI change

## Details

The announced MAC capability is rebuilt from `Capability`, the list decoded once from the device announcement and never rewritten per model. A device paired before `Capability` was kept has none; its node descriptor's `macapa` (also never rewritten) is used instead. `MacCapa` is not used for this: it may already hold an earlier `8e`.

- Announced **reduced-function**: set only the mains-powered bit (`0x80` → `0x84`, `0x88` → `0x8c`), with `LogicalType = "End Device"`, `DeviceType = "RFD"`, `PowerSource = "Main"`. On an existing install already rewritten to `8e`, this is fixed on the next heartbeat (the function runs on every heartbeat). No re-pair.
- Announced **full-function**, or neither `Capability` nor `macapa` recorded: unchanged, `8e` / FFD / Router as before.

`mainPoweredDevice()` already accepts `84`, and the flag makes it return True anyway, so health and ping behaviour is unchanged. `batterieManagement` treats `84` as mains. This also ends the flip-flop where `ReArrangeMacCapaBasedOnModel()` set these models to Router and `mainPoweredDevice()` set them back to End Device on the same heartbeat. zigpy is not affected: its node descriptor comes from `_rawNodeDescriptor` / `Capability` (#2110).

One `MacCapa == "8e"` test no longer matches these devices: `lumi.py`'s `0000/ff01` `sOnOff2` handling. The only Lumi model with the flag is `lumi.switch.l0agl1`, a single-channel switch, so a second on/off state does not apply to it.

## Validation

- `pytest .`: 3875 passed, 4 skipped (Python 3.12, zigpy 0.241 venv)
- `flake8 . --builtins=Devices,Parameters,Connection --select=E9,F63,F7,F82`: 0
- Not verified on a device: role and power icon in the WebUI and the topology scan with a ZBMINIL2 after a heartbeat

## Unit Test Added

`tests/Modules/Tools/test_tools_mac_capa_rearrange.py` (8 tests): an announced `0x80` becomes `0x84` End Device/RFD and stays main powered; an install already rewritten to `8e`/Router is repaired from `Capability`; without `Capability`, from the node descriptor's `macapa`; RxOnWhenIdle is kept (`0x88` → `0x8c`); the hard-coded TS0011 gets the same; an announced FFD stays a Router; with neither, the previous rewrite is kept; a device without the flag is untouched.

## Summary

Gives the Astro `Site/` folders of Diald and Deadwax Club one structure, so a new app's site is a copy-and-rebrand job. Companion PR: https://github.com/kylescudder/dialdclub/pull/92. Merge them together.

Follows kylescudder/deadwaxclub#119 ("Adopt the shared iOS app conventions"), now merged; this branch is rebased onto `main` (`9883e2d`).

## What changes

- **One layout.** Every page uses the shared `src/layouts/BaseLayout.astro` (document head, the app's `Header`, the page, the app's `Footer`, `src/styles/global.css`). Privacy, terms and support use the shared `LegalArticle`. `DocumentHead` reads `Site/app.json` and now sets `og:url` on every canonical page (without a trailing slash, matching the app's links).
- **App hooks.** `Site/app.json` holds the app's site values: name, deploy-core token, repository, origin, theme colour, icon, contact, support link, pages and expected content, Caddy-only routes and universal-link app IDs. `Site/app.caddy` holds app-only Caddy headers and rewrites. `scripts/write-config.mjs` stays an optional hook for pages that call the API.
- **Shared manifest.** `Scripts/shared-site.sha256` + `Scripts/check-shared-site.sh` (same pattern as `check-shared-ios-core.sh`) cover 23 files. These are the house tooling, `Dockerfile`, `Caddyfile`, `compose.yaml`, Astro/TS/Playwright config, `BaseLayout`, `DocumentHead`, `LegalArticle`, `check-site.mjs`, `e2e/site.spec.ts`, `ci-site.yml`, `release-site.yml`, `e2e.yml` and the doc and script themselves. Only `Caddyfile` and `compose.yaml` are normalised, for the app `token` and `repository`. Site CI runs the check.
- **Identical workflows.** `ci-site.yml` and `release-site.yml` are byte-identical in both apps with no tokens to normalise. The image is `ghcr.io/${{ github.repository }}-site` and the hook is `https://$DEPLOY_HOST/hooks/${{ github.event.repository.name }}`. The deploy-core header names (`X-<token>-Signature`, `x-<token>-deploy-hook`, `x-<token>-revision`) are derived from `Site/app.json` and match the old hard-coded values. CI now smoke-tests the image under `compose.yaml` for every page and route in `app.json` (with and without a trailing slash), the revision and cache headers, 404s, and the AASA content type when present.
- **Data-driven checks.** `check-site.mjs` and `e2e/site.spec.ts` read `app.json`. They check page content, `og:url`, assets, contact links, the list-viewer config and the Apple association when the app has them, and no horizontal overflow on any page.
- **Docs.** New `Scripts/SHARED_SITE.md` documents the layout and app hooks. `SHARED_IOS_CORE.md` (and its manifest), `AGENTS.md`, `README.md` and `Site/README.md` (now the same sections in both apps) are updated. The `ios-app-setup` skill (local) now covers the fifth manifest, the site hooks and `DEPLOY_HOST`.
- `Dockerfile` build arg `<APP>_REVISION` is now `SOURCE_REVISION` (as in the backend), and the image env is `SITE_REVISION`. The public `X-<App>-Revision` header is unchanged.

## Deadwax Club-specific

- **Layouts → one `BaseLayout`.** `SiteLayout`/`LandingLayout` are gone. The home page is split into `HomeHero`, `HomeHighlights`, `HomeFeatures`, `HomeSupport`. The two headers and footers live in `Header.astro`/`Footer.astro`, chosen by page (home / list viewer / legal).
- **`styles.css` + `landing.css` → `src/styles/global.css`.** Dead rules left over from an old landing page were dropped (814 + 687 lines → 1140) (`.hero-landing`, `.sleeve*`, `.vinyl-stack`, `.support-card`, …). Every home-page selector is scoped under `.landing-page`, the list viewer's buttons under `.list-page`, and the bare `footer` selector became `.site-footer`, so neither stylesheet's rules reach the other's pages.
- **List viewer kept as is.** `/l/<token>` (`src/pages/l/index.astro` + `public/js/list.js`), `config.example.js`, `scripts/write-config.mjs`, `compose.yaml` and the AASA all stay. The `/l/*` rewrite and the `/assets/*` immutable header moved to `Site/app.caddy`. The AASA `application/json` header is in the shared Caddyfile. `/l/` passes `canonical={false}`, so it has no `og:url`, as before.
- **New e2e coverage:** `e2e/list.spec.ts` drives the list viewer with a mocked API: records, owner, count, the `deadwaxclub://list/<token>` button and the token sent to both endpoints, plus the "unavailable" state.
- **Visible changes, all on the legal pages:** the shared `LegalArticle` adds a cyan "DEADWAX CLUB" eyebrow above the title, styled like the list viewer's kicker (pages are 31px taller). The terms footer now lists Support · Privacy · Terms like privacy does. The two identical `theme-color` metas became one. Home and list viewer are pixel-identical.
- `package.json` scripts reordered to match Diald (same scripts and dependencies).

## Before merging

- [ ] Merge this PR and its companion together.

Note: Renovate PRs that bump a shared site file (the Bun or Caddy digest in `Site/Dockerfile`, action pins in the site workflows) now need the same bump in the other app plus `sh Scripts/check-shared-site.sh --write`, as for the other manifests. The open `renovate/caddy-2.x` and `renovate/bun-1.x` branches will fail the site check until then.

## Validation

Before: `41354b2` (the conventions branch; `Site/` and the site workflows are unchanged from it to `main` `9883e2d`). After: `4f5181a`, clean tree, then rebased onto `main` as `998126d` with `Site/` and the site workflows byte-identical, and all five shared checks rerun and passing.

author: mavrick-f
body:
## Summary

**This adds a check every pull request must pass.** A new CI job, **Limits only go down**, fails a pull request that raises or removes a limit in `xtask/row-uses.txt` or `xtask/memory-limits.txt`. A deliberate raise needs a maintainer's say: a maintainer comments on the pull request (or reviews it) with a line the failure prints for that change, such as `<!-- ratchet-raise-approved: xtask/row-uses.txt count=790 -->`, then the job is run again. The line names the file, the limit and the value, so a later push that raises it further needs a new approval. The failure message says so and prints each line to copy.

`AGENTS.md` says both files only go down, but only review enforced it: `cargo xtask rows` and `cargo xtask memory` pass when the code is under the limit, so a pull request could edit the limit up to make them pass. The job compares each file with the base commit (the pull request's base branch tip, or the queue entry's parent in the merge queue) and fails when:

- `count` in `row-uses.txt` is higher, or a limit in `memory-limits.txt` is higher;
- a limit is removed, or commented out, or a file is deleted.

A new line (a new memory scenario) is fine, and lowering a limit is what the files are for. It reads the first line of a name, as the xtask readers do, so a later duplicate can't move a limit.

Modelled on `review-deferrals.py` (#2661): `.github/scripts/ratchet-limits.py`, its unit tests, a job on pull requests and in the merge queue (the queue's run sees an approval posted after the last push), and an entry in `tests_pass`. The override follows the deferral one: only a message from the repository's owner, a member or a collaborator counts, a bot's doesn't, and the author may be that maintainer. The line must be on a line of its own, so a message that quotes or mentions it doesn't approve. Each raise, removed limit (a dropped memory scenario needs one too) or deleted file needs its own line. A symbolic link at a limit path, or a head file that doesn't parse, fails with nothing to approve; a base file that doesn't parse needs an approval for that head (the line carries a digest of the head file), since nothing can be compared. `row-uses.txt` is read as `cargo xtask rows` reads it (only `count`, lines without an `=` ignored), `memory-limits.txt` as `cargo xtask memory` does. Lines are read as the xtask readers read them (LF or CRLF endings only, Rust's whitespace rules, the first line of a name counts). Comments are read only when a limit rose.

The job has a read-only token and no secrets, like the others.

**Not covered:** the code that reads the limits (`xtask/src/rows.rs`, `xtask/src/memory.rs`) isn't compared, and the script runs from the pull request's own checkout like `review-deferrals.py`, so loosening those is still for review to catch. Running the check from the base commit, or a CODEOWNERS entry for `xtask/src`, would close that; it is a maintainers' call.

**Left out on purpose:** the number of `Silent` cases in `never_silent_reading.rs`, the ids in `hostile_skips()` and the `exempt` list in `cancellation.rs`. `AGENTS.md` doesn't say those only go down, and each grows for a good reason (a new reader with a known gap, a new command that writes files or reaches the network). Counting them would make those pull requests need the override, so it is a call for the maintainers. The script's docstring says the same.

Updated the `cargo xtask memory` / `cargo xtask rows` lines in `AGENTS.md` and added a paragraph to `docs/contributing.md` next to the deferral override.

## Testing

- `python3 -m unittest discover -s .github/scripts -p 'test_*.py'`: the 20 new tests in `test_ratchet_limits.py` pass: raised, equal and lowered counts; each memory limit held to its own value; a removed, commented-out or deleted limit; a new scenario; duplicate lines; line endings; symbolic links; unreadable files; who may approve and which value an approval names; the queue branch naming the pull request; the whole `main` flow with the base, the files and the comments stubbed. The approval and line-ending tests were seen failing by making `approved()` ignore the named limit (4 tests fail) and by going back to `splitlines()` or Python's `strip()` (1 fails each).
- Seen failing, with the real script in a scratch git repository holding copies of both files as the base commit: raising `count = 782` to `783`, `join = 2.10` to `2.20` and deleting the `save` line printed `::error::xtask/row-uses.txt: \`count\` rose from 782 to 783`, `::error::xtask/memory-limits.txt: \`join\` rose from 2.10 to 2.20`, `::error::xtask/memory-limits.txt: the limit \`save\` (2.50) was removed` and the explanation of the override, and exited 1. With a stubbed `gh` returning a maintainer's message with the line `<!-- ratchet-raise-approved: xtask/row-uses.txt count=783 -->` the row count passed with a notice and the removed `save` limit still failed, printing the line that would approve it; with a message from someone with no association everything failed. Unchanged files passed.
- The `gh api --paginate --jq` calls were run against #2661 to check the fields the script reads (`author_association`, `user.type`, `body`) for comments and reviews.
- GitHub gives `merge_group.base_sha` as the queue entry's parent; the queue branch names in recent runs (`pr-2710-<sha of the previous entry>`) show it is the entry before it, so a raise approved on an earlier pull request in the queue isn't counted again on the next one.
- Fork CI (full gate) passed on `df7138cae`. The new job's step runs only on pull requests and in the merge queue, so the fork's manual run doesn't exercise it: its first real run is this pull request's (it passed on the first head, where nothing was raised).

## UI evidence

No visible UI change.

## Related issue

Part of the guardrail follow-ups after #2661.

The shape holds for max(1000, (n−1)·crawl + 100) ms, then fades out over 400 ms. No dot. There is one accessible node, labelled `strokeOrder.shape(a11yRomanization(rom))`.
  - **Untaught, reduced motion** (also used when the motion query fails): a still with no badges and no arrows. Its label is `close(shape(...))`.
  - **Taught:** unchanged.
- **Screens:** while the hint is up on an untaught letter, the ghost steps aside. "Shape guide" takes the place of the **idle line only**: the miss, pass and keep-going lines always win.
  - In Trace Word block mode this is the whole unit. In letter mode it is the one letter, which gets its own romanization from the new `trace-word/letter-romanization.ts`.
- **Presenter** `StrokePanel`: no numbered dots when untaught.
  - On the stroke build or R, the panel's letter hides while the reveal plays, then comes back, and the hint unmounts.

- **Strings:**

- The TI-2 tip tests (`trace-idle-states.test.tsx`) now play letters as taught, with the gate mocked, so the open-stroke tip and Next path stays covered for after SO-3.
- The spec row SO-1 is marked built.

## Tests (spec §6)
| # | Where |
|---|---|
| 1–6 | `apps/mobile/src/logic/__tests__/stroke-order-taught.test.ts`, using the real `scoreTrace`. Covers: ㅗ bar first gives clean; taught, it gives order. ㅌ in 4 strokes, ㅈ in 3, ㅊ and ㅎ with a horizontal top stroke give clean. ㅎ with a clockwise ring gives loop. ㅁ as one loop gives clean. ㅇ and final ㅇ clockwise give loop. Strict mode passes. Plus `loopNudgeFor` unit cases. |
| 7 | `trace-word/__tests__/evaluate.test.ts` (호 with ㅗ bar first: neither the letter line nor the block line is the order line; a partly taught unit is untaught) and `trace-shape-guide.test.tsx` (shape label, no `orderLabel`) |
| 8 | `screens/minigames/__tests__/stroke-hint-shape.test.tsx` (one group and one shared value, no dot, timing, still with no numerals or arrows, labels, no caption) and `trace-shape-guide.test.tsx` (the strip caption, idle line only; miss, pass, keep-going and retry lines win; ghost steps aside; strict mode on screen) |
| 9 | `screens/presenter/__tests__/letter-slide-shape.test.tsx` |

Results on the final commit:
- `apps/mobile` `TZ=UTC pnpm test`: **1059 files, 19006 tests passed**.
- `pnpm typecheck` (apps/mobile): clean.
- `packages/i18n` vitest: **11757 passed**.
- `node scripts/check-i18n.mjs`: ok.

Not run here: the e2e and Playwright suites. No e2e spec asserts the order or the open-stroke lines.

## Start bundle
`CI=1 pnpm build:web` measured **4,578,889 B raw / 1,259,828 B gzip**. The ceiling is 4,579,300 B, so this is 411 B under it and the budget line is **not raised**. The margin is now thin, so the next row will likely need a raise.

## Review (two independent reviewer agents, each given the spec, the design and the diff)
- **Lens A: spec and design conformance, and code truth.** No blocker and no major.
  - `reviewedStrokeIds` and the stroke data are confirmed untouched.
  - The worklet callbacks only use shared values, constants and `runOnJS`; the hold is computed on the JS side.
  - **Fixed, minor:** the presenter hint, with its a11y node, stayed mounted after the reveal. It now unmounts.
  - **Fixed, minor:** the test helper drifted from the screen's strict rule. It now matches, and a screen-level strict test was added.
  - **Fixed, minor:** there was no screen test for a partly taught unit, or for the Trace Word retry line winning over the caption. Both added.
  - **Fixed, nit:** the bezier now comes from the shared `cubicBezierPoints`.
  - **Fixed, nit:** a missing space in `trace-copy.ts`.
  - **Fixed, nit:** an unneeded mock.
  - **Not done, minor:** the reviewer asked that the ledger review evidence be recorded. It is the review below.
- **Lens B: anti-shame, accessibility and i18n.** Approve. **The es and ko strings are approved** (consistent with "Guía del orden de trazos" and "획순 안내"), so the ledger re-sign is justified, and the SHAs were verified.
  - No danger colour; Hoya's pose does not change with the hint; miss lines are kept; no new way to fail.
  - **Fixed, minor:** under reduced motion the presenter panel had no shape label. The panel now carries it.
  - **Left as designed, minor:** the strip is a polite live region, so "Shape guide" is announced on Android and web when Show me starts (wireframe §8).
  - **Left, pre-existing:** `a11yRomanization` joins with the English word "or" inside es and ko labels ("silent or ng, 모양 안내."). This needs a locale-aware joiner in its own row.

author: dr-dolapo
body:
## What this adds

Broadcasts during a live event (PRD §9.6).

| Story | What works |
|---|---|
| QR038 | Approvers and Admins send a short message (up to 280 characters) to **everyone on the event**, from the event page. This only works while the event is live. |
| QR039 | …or to **chosen people** only. |
| QR040 | Recipients get an **alert on their event page straight away**, with no reload. Phones vibrate and the tab title shows "(1) New message". **Guests never receive broadcasts.** |
| QR041 | Recipients reply **Acknowledge**, **Snooze 3 min** or **Done**. A snoozed alert **comes back after 3 minutes**. |
| QR042 | The sender sees counts (✓ / snoozed / waiting) update live, plus **who replied** and when. |

The composer is deliberately on the event page, not the command centre, so messages don't appear on the HDMI screen.

### How it works
The live room (the `LiveEvent` Durable Object) tags each screen's connection with its user, so an alert goes only to its recipients. The room also tells Admins' screens to refresh replies. The room's single alarm is now set for whichever comes first: the next live hand-over, the end time, or the next snooze due back.

### Push notifications
Per the PRD, broadcasts were to go out as push notifications. Push needs the mobile app, which is on hold, so for now they're **in-app alerts on the web app**. The PRD notes this.

## Checked

- 137 API tests pass (11 new): live-only, Admin-only, everyone versus chosen people, guests excluded and rejected, replies, who can reply, snooze timing and re-alerting with the original message, and replies closing when the event ends.
- I ran it against **`wrangler dev` with the real Durable Object** in three browser sessions, with 15 checks passing. Ada sends to everyone, and Chi and Dayo get it instantly. Chi acknowledges, Dayo snoozes, and Ada's view updates. A message to Chi only doesn't reach Dayo. **Dayo's snoozed alert came back at exactly 180 seconds**, and Done cleared it.

author: earthlingdavey
body:
## What changes, and why

motel hides an app's `env_file` values when the app prints them, because a failed deploy's answer lands in a CI log and a status is read by people. Until now it did that by filtering every finished answer as text, after `json.Marshal`. Of the 182 fields motel sends, 6 can hold bytes an app wrote; the filter searched all 182, and so replaced motel's own words, versions, keys, times and numbers whenever an env value happened to equal a piece of them, renamed JSON keys, and withheld whole answers. The response-filter spike (`research_notes/response-filter-spike/NOTES.md`) measured this and the options; the owner chose "filter at the doors" (option 3), alone.

After this change:

- **No filter runs over a finished answer.** Every answer is marshalled from its typed struct and sent (`RespondJSON` takes no filter).
- **The app's text is filtered once, where it enters** an answer or a stored record, by that app's filter, with the same layers as before: a failed deploy's journal tail, its probe's body and `Location` (`failureDetail`), a line of the app's journal at the logs read (`door.logLine`), and every error string that becomes a field (the **error net**, `errText`: the deploy's outcome whatever failed, an interrupted deploy's record, the watchdog's failed probe and refused relaunch, a recovery that gave up, `log_tail_error`, a push that could not be staged). The net reads and carries an error's text as the logs door reads a line: at most 4 KiB sent, with "…" where it was cut, so what an app makes Go's client quote (an answer that is megabytes of no HTTP) costs moteld no more than a logs line. A failed deploy's tail is filtered a line at a time, and a private key printed over lines, from its BEGIN line to its END line, becomes one line with its marker, as main's whole-tail pass made it.
- **Types say which text passed.** `wire.AppText` (the app's text) is made only in `redact.go`; `wire.ErrText` (an error's text, and every refusal's: `wire.Error.Error` is one now) only by the net or by `wire.OwnText`, whose callers are listed in a test. A string variable in such a field does not compile. A conversion anywhere else in liveswap, the box webhook or notify fails `TestAppTextOnlyFromTheDoor` / `TestErrTextMakers` / `TestBoxErrTextMakers`, in the forms a walk of the source sees: the type named under any import name, in parentheses, through a declared type or an alias, or instantiating a generic function. A decode (`json.Unmarshal` into such a field) makes one with nothing written, and only review sees it (`servedRecord`'s decode of an older record's detail is the one, and passes the door again).
- **Every string field of every wire type is classed**: by its type, or by a `text:"moteld"` / `text:"passes"` tag. `TestEveryStringFieldIsClassed` fails for a field nobody classed, and for a field whose type it cannot class (an interface, another package's type but `time`'s, a named type that is no struct). Nothing filters by default, so a new field cannot ship unclassed. Outside the test, because they are not `wire` types: the box webhook's answers, `box.result` (`box/results.go`) and the `map[string]string` bodies of `box/push.go` (`{"id": …}`, `{"phase": "admitted"}`: the push's id and a constant). Of `box.result`'s text: `id`, `phase`, `commit`, `path`, `signer`, `box_webhook`, `apps`, `named` and the `secrets_*` lists are the box's names, ids and paths; `diff` is filtered where it is made (`box/diff.go`); `error` is the applier's catalogue sentence, with the validate child's line filtered with the box's values and the heuristics where it is read (`box/validate.go`), and a refusal names paths and names, never a value (`box/secrets.go`).
- **motel's probe sentence leaves motel's own URL out** (`health check got no answer: <why>`), so the net does not meet `DB_HOST=localhost` in motel's words.
- **The logs door** filters each line once where it enters the answer, reading exactly as much of a long line as the logs read always has (4 KiB and a margin: 8 KiB, or the longest form of a value it knows if that is longer), and sending what it always sent of a cut line. No pass runs over the body.
- **Records** are the deploy's result as marshalled, marked `filtered_at_entry`, and served as written. A record an older moteld wrote has no mark, and its error and detail are filtered again when read.
- **motel's own data is never changed**: names, versions, figures, times, states, keys. `redacted_env` lists a key's name through the known values, as main did, so a name that is another key's value is that value's marker.
- **moteld's journal says every error as it came**, as main's did; beside a withheld one, the env_file's own read error.

Docs: DESIGN-threat-model.md (the promise, plainly, and "What is no longer searched"), liveswap/DESIGN-liveswap.md (rows), liveswap/README.md, docs/people.md, liveswap/access/DESIGN-access.md, box/DESIGN-box.md, notify's two docs.

Out of this PR, each a later one: the heuristic layers' cut to the quiet shape rules; the version in a summary liveswap tells (`tell` is unchanged in what it does); #651's matching of escaped spellings; markers.

## The brief's premise about old records was wrong

The brief said a record already on a box "may hold text nothing filtered". It does not: every record since records exist (#104, `b1e531fa`, 2026-09-14, `liveswap/deploys.go` `recordDeploy` → `recordRedactor` → `redactJSON`) was filtered whole when written, with the values remembered and the env_file read at write time, and filtered again at each read. What main's read pass added is only the values learnt after the record was written. See "For the owner to confirm".

## Measured, beside the spike's numbers

Run on a scratch branch that is not pushed (this branch, the spike's test files and tools ported from `spike/response-filter-logs-errnet`; the only changes to them: their seams call this code's names, the attack's "heuristics off" is a scratch switch, and option (b) is gone). The instruments were not changed.

| Instrument | The spike measured (option 3 with the error net) | This branch (head `249c0427`) | After the independent review's fixes (head `026c2eeb`) |
|---|---|---|---|
| Client test (`TestSpikeE2E_Client`), outputs | 19,890 | 19,890 | 19,890 |
| · the truth, byte for byte | 19,506 | **19,506** | **19,506** |
| · fails where the truth exits 0 / thinner / false | 0 / 0 / 0 | **0 / 0 / 0** | **0 / 0 / 0** |
| · same exit, a marker where a value stood | 384 | **384** | **384** |
| · a secret readable when the app prints everything / the canary | 0 / 0 | **0 / 0** | **0 / 0** |
| · rows whose verdict differs from the spike's run | — | **0 of 19,890** (102 rows differ in text, all the record's new key `filtered_at_entry` in `motel deploys <app> <version> --json`) | **0 of 19,890**, and every output and every told or held record the same bytes as at `249c0427` (once each run's random temp directory is set aside) |
| Logs test (`TestSpikeLogsE2E_Client`), outputs | 2,588 | 2,588, **every one the same bytes as the spike's option 3 tree** | 2,588, **every one the same bytes as at `249c0427`** |
| · ordinary lines as written / changed by an env value / by the heuristics, of 4,032 | 3,011 / 224 / 797 | **3,011 / 224 / 797** | **3,011 / 224 / 797** |
| · env_file unreadable: the logs reader's commands that fail, of 153 / lines sent as the sentence | 0 / 3,993 | **0 / 3,993** | **0 / 3,993** |
| · loud app: credential lines readable, of 431 / split across two lines, of 44 / nested JSON, of 44 / every other form, of 343 / canary, of 17 | 33 / 30 / 3 / 0 / 0 | **33 / 30 / 3 / 0 / 0** | **33 / 30 / 3 / 0 / 0** |
| · restart gap: credential lines, of 431 / canary, of 17 | 153 / 17 | **153 / 17** (the gap is #657's, unchanged here) | **153 / 17** |
| One logs read of sixteen 48 KiB lines (the checker's `TestSpikeLogsCheck_LongLines`, three alternating rounds, median) | main 113 ms, prototype 341 ms | **main 108 ms, this branch 104 ms**

body: **Draft: not ready to merge.** The third review found 9 important issues that are still open (listed below). ### Linked issue No linked issue. Phase 3 of 4 of `docs/refactors/2026-11-22-mobile-browser-live-view.md`, stacked on #170, which is stacked on #168. ### Type of change - [x] New feature - [x] Docs ### Reasoning When an agent hits a login wall in a Paseo browser tab, you had to walk to the desktop. This lets you sign in from the phone: take control of the tab, tap, type with your password manager's autofill, hand back. Still behind the off-by-default **Browser live view (experimental)** host setting. ### Goals - **Watching is read-only.** An explicit **Take control** locks the tab. While it's locked, agent browser commands on that tab are refused, reads included. **Hand back** clears secret fields and leaves the agent a note without waking it. - **Typing is bound to what you saw.** The phone shows the origin from Electron's committed URL. Text is refused if the origin or the focused field changed. Taps carry the document of the frame on screen and are refused if stale. - **Secrets** are typed through a native field with autofill hints and are never logged. - **Disconnect:** control survives backgrounding. After 5 minutes away it is released and unsubmitted input is discarded. - **Never accept a dialog for the user, never clear on a guess.** Uncertain input is reported as "check the page before sending again". - Typing uses `webFrame.insertText` in the existing sandboxed guest preload, because `contents.insertText` crashed the renderer 3 of 3 times with a cross-origin iframe focused. No webPreferences change. - Protocol is additive, gated on `browserLiveViewInput`. Live view strings are translated. ### Non-goals - Phase 4 (login request tool, notification deep link) and passkeys. - What a per-tab lock can't cover: shared cookies, other same-origin tabs, scripts planted before take-over, copies the page made, a person at the desktop. Listed in the spec. ### CI status (bad75ec11) - **Desktop e2e on Linux:** the new live-input test assumed a wide pane. Fixed in bad75ec11: it sets its own viewport, and the transformed-iframe taps now pass on Linux. It still fails at the next step because of a product bug (below). - **Product bug found by that run:** a tap on a field in the page itself, not in an iframe, focuses nothing when the tab isn't the one shown on the desktop. Chromium leaves `contents.focusedFrame` null. Reproduced on Linux and on macOS whenever the tab isn't on screen. That is the away-from-the-Mac case, so phone sign-in on ordinary login pages likely doesn't work yet. Falling back to the main frame let the next checks pass, but the dialog check then timed out on Linux. It also fails on #178, which doesn't touch the timeline; it passes locally on all bases; and this PR's timeline change doesn't fire in that spec. Likely flaky. ### Open issues from the third review of dc470f2f4 Found by reading the code; not reproduced. Affect secrets or the lock: - [ ] On an `about:blank` document, a refused discard counts as success, so control or release can proceed with the agent's script or the typed input still there. - [ ] A code the page spreads over several boxes isn't fully cleared on hand-back, so the agent can read it. - [ ] After a debugger detach, auto-release can't discard a page that guards unload, so the tab stays locked. Real-Electron regression 4/4 on fresh desktops. Capture harness 26 pass. - A sentinel search for the typed values was clean across daemon, desktop, Metro and both devices' logs and storage. - Targeted tests: protocol 101, server 330, desktop 243, app 501.
