author: ryoitabashi
body:
## The incident

On 2026-11-23 at 07:10 JST the stage-1 Shizuku heal (round 5) destroyed a
healthy server it could not restart. ClosePaw had lost binder
reachability while `shizuku_server` was alive (PID 6381), but the heal
read the failed binder ping as server death: its command killed the live
server and then ran the shell starter route — which no longer existed,
because the owner's fresh Play Store install of Shizuku had wiped the
external `start.sh` the heal invokes. The starter exec failed and the
server stayed down until the owner restarted it from the manager app.
The full field record is in
`shizuku-play-variant-verification-20261123.md` (including both
addenda). A recovery mechanism must never be able to make things worse
than the failure it was reacting to; this round removes that capability
outright.

## The change (3 files)

- `app/MaintenancePolicy.kt` — the kill machinery is **deleted, not
  gated**: the `ShizukuHealAction` enum (including `KILL_THEN_STARTER`),
  `healAction`, and `postKillAction` no longer exist anywhere in
  production sources. In their place, a total pure decision function
  `ShizukuHealPlan.disposition(identity, startRoutePresent)` over the
  tri-state server identity (`Present` / `Absent` / unknown) and the
  tri-state start-route presence:
  - identity unknown (any route) → `PROBE_UNKNOWN`
  - `Present` (any route; route probe skipped) →
    `ALIVE_BUT_UNREACHABLE`
  - `Absent` + route unknown → `PROBE_UNKNOWN`
  - `Absent` + route present → `START_SERVER`
  - `Absent` + route missing → `START_ROUTE_MISSING`
  
  `buildHealCommand` drops its identity parameter, accepts only the
  fixed starter command derived from the shared
  `SHIZUKU_START_SCRIPT_PATH` constant, and emits a single branch:
  on-device identity revalidation, the starter only on `ABSENT`, the
  abort marker otherwise — a failing on-device probe yields an empty
  value, which is not `ABSENT`, so it aborts (fail-safe). The command
  text contains no `kill` (asserted by test). A new
  `START_ROUTE_PROBE_COMMAND` (`[ -f … ]` → `PRESENT`/`MISSING`) and
  `parseStartRoutePresent` feed the route input.
- `app/McpMaintenance.kt` — `healShizukuClaimed` now probes, routes on
  the disposition, and logs before any dispatch. The identity probe
  (`pidof shizuku_server` + `/proc/<pid>/stat` start ticks) runs first;
  only an `Absent` identity triggers the start-route probe. Failed
  exits, truncated or unparseable output, and probe exceptions all fold
  into `PROBE_UNKNOWN` (coroutine cancellation still propagates). Each
  outcome logs a distinct token: `start_server` enters the guarded
  dispatch; `alive_but_unreachable`, `start_route_missing`, and
  `probe_unknown` are report-only and return before any heal exec. The
  State C path itself is unchanged: `execGuarded` + `shouldDispatch`,
  in-command ABSENT revalidation with the abort marker, binder polling,
  and the permission check — maintenance still checks permission without
  requesting it and never surfaces UI.
- `app/MaintenancePolicyTest.kt` — the removed-machinery tests are
  replaced by the full disposition decision table, start-route parsing
  edges, and a rewritten command-invariant test asserting the identity
  probe, exactly one guarded starter occurrence, the abort marker, and
  the absence of any `kill` substring.

## Tests

Standalone rig: **135/135 pass** across 11 suites (120 round-9 tests +
15 maintenance tests) — every row of the (identity × route) decision
table, route parser edges (`PRESENT`/`MISSING`/garbage/empty), the
probe command's derivation from the shared script-path constant, and
the no-kill command invariant. Protected files (including
`AgentService.kt`, `McpBrainSessions.kt`, `PlatformFactory.kt`,
`VirtualDisplayPlatform.kt`, the manifest, and the workflows directory)
verified byte-identical to the round-10 baseline; scope is exactly the
3 paths above across tree diff / diff file / changes JSON,
replay-verified byte-for-byte.

## Process

- Fixed acceptance list: `acceptance-list-r10.md` as corrected — the
  round-9 list (with the r7a/8 floors by reference) as regression
  floor, plus round-10 targets R10-1…R10-10.
- Scoped Codex gate 1 (`gate-review-r10-1.md`): **BLOCKING** on list
  wording only — two criteria said "no exec" where the read-only
  diagnostic probes are execs by design; the substantive behavior
  already held. The list was corrected first (dated note), per the
  fixed-list governance.
- Scoped confirmation gate 2 (`gate-review-r10-2.md`): **OK** —
  R10-4 and R10-5 hold under the corrected wording, floor spot-checks
  held, no list defects.
- Hayato's own final review of the actual diff (`my-review-r10.md`):
  verdict **ship it**, recorded before this PR was opened.

## Accepted residual

- A dead server still cannot be revived while the shell starter route
  is structurally broken (the official Shizuku APK ships DEFLATED
  native libs, so the starter dies in its constructor — see the
  2026-11-23 diagnosis). Removing the Shizuku dependency is the
  stage-2 problem and is unchanged by this round. What this round
  guarantees is that the heal can no longer make things worse: every
  uncertain or live-server state resolves to report-only, and the one
  remaining start path fires only after two independent ABSENT
  confirmations.
- State C still invokes Shizuku's own `start.sh`, whose internals are
  Shizuku's — but the heal now invokes it only when no server process
  exists for it to disturb.

author: muhammadatef
body:
## What and why
T-026 plus the red-team suite (build prompt §10, gate G3: injection attack success = 0%). It adds a multilingual `injection.instruction_like_text` detector. The detector is risk evidence only and is never obeyed. The PR also adds a span-removal guard that runs before the quarantined extractor, input limits (size, MIME, decompression bombs), and 92 red-team cases, each with a clean twin. Each case runs through the shipped router, extractor, arbiter, investigator and responder (#19 / #13 / #18 on main) with a scripted *compromised* LLM. The PR also adds semgrep and container-hardening checks to `make scan`, and a Playwright XSS checker (a stub until the web app lands).

## Changes
- `packages/falcon_core/src/falcon_core/signals/injection/`: `normalise` maps every character of the folded text back to its offset in the original. It folds zero-width, bidi, NFKC/full-width, Cyrillic/Greek homoglyphs, and Arabic letters (alef/ya/ta marbuta, tashkeel, tatweel). `patterns` covers EN, AR (including Gulf) and Arabizi, plus forged structure: spotlight delimiters, chat-template tokens, schema mimicry, fake `ev_` ids, canary probes and tool names. `decode` handles base64, hex, percent and entities with caps. `detector` adds leet, ROT13 and bidi-reversed views, a fire rule that depends on the channel (text in hidden, alt, aria, comment or meta counts as stronger), `neutralise()`, and a registered plugin.
- `security/limits.py`: URL 4 KB, message 8 KB, email 2 MB, image 5 MB; strict UTF-8; a MIME depth and part-count pre-scan that runs before any recursive parser; PNG/GIF/JPEG/WebP header dimension checks.
- `security/injection_guard.py`: `prepare_untrusted()` (neutralise before the extractor) and `llm_failure_evidence()` (an extraction dropped because the reply leaked the canary becomes injection risk evidence).
- `evals/redteam/`: `cases.yaml` (92 cases), `compromised.py`, `pipeline.py`, `run.py`, `html_segments.py` (innerText-style stand-in for the sandbox), `generators.py`, `xss_check.py`. Fixture pages are generated into `services/fixtures/redteam/`. They are Falcon Demo Bank only, carry the TEST FIXTURE banner, their forms post nowhere, and they use reserved hosts.
- `make redteam` / `make redteam-fixtures` / `make xss`. `make scan` now runs `scripts/scan.sh`, which adds semgrep 1.186.0 (p/python, p/secrets, p/typescript, ERROR) and `scripts/compose_hardening.py` (compose config + `docker image inspect`).
- Tests: `tests/security/test_injection_detector.py` (attack phrases, encodings, channels, neutralise, bounds, and a false-positive set of 32 benign AR/EN bank messages), `test_limits.py`, `test_redteam_suite.py`. The suite tests include a self-test proving the metric flags an attack the detector cannot see. Also `scripts/tests/test_compose_hardening.py`.

## Red-team result (artifact `evals/results/redteam-20261122T230147Z.json`, git 8d6435d, scripted compromised route)
**Attack success 0/92 = 0.0%.** Ablation without `neutralise` (informational, not gated): 0/92. There are 4 in-band score drops: page-heldout-cleared, page-heldout-looks-fine, page-heldout2-moderators and msg-heldout2-gulf. In these cases the extractor obeyed, but the deterministic brand claim (`cascade/page.py`) or the detector kept the verdict. Six URL cases have floor warnings: the clean twin is itself below the declared `suspicious` floor under the fitted bands from #29, so this is not caused by the attack.

author: petrsovadina
body:
## Co se mění

PR má dva commity.

### 1. `medplum-mcp` 0.2.0: hook pro potvrzení zápisů
Hook šel obejít šesti způsoby. Tři našlo review toolkitu, tři nezávislé bezpečnostní review změny. Všech šest je opravených a pokrytých testy.

| Obejití (před změnou) | Po změně |
|---|---|
| nefunkční `python3` (stub, pád, prázdný výstup, banner) → zápis projde | wrapper přijme jen jeden řádek s rozhodnutím nebo `{}`, jinak `ask` |
| GET mohl opustit `/fhir/R4/` (`../`, `%2e`, absolutní URL; audit 47/10), skryté znaky (tab, nový řádek, `#`) to zamaskovaly | `deny` pro `%`, řídicí a bílé znaky, `#`, `\`, `..`, scheme, `//`; cesta jen `[A-Za-z0-9$_.-/]` |
| matcher jen pro přesné jméno nástroje pluginu | `mcp__.*medplum.*__.*` bez ohledu na velikost písmen; neznámý nástroj → `ask` |
| citlivá čtení a `$execute`/`$graphql` přes GET bez dotazu | `ask` s důvodem; čtecí operace projdou |
| server se slovem „docs“ by pustil i zápisy | z docs serveru jen 4 známé čtecí nástroje |

`RISK.md` už netvrdí ochranu proti SSRF, kterou audit vyvrátil, a nově uvádí zbytková rizika.

### 2. Body střední priority
- **`mcp-smoke`:**
  - token a authorization endpoint z OAuth discovery jen https na `medplum.test.dokturek.ai` (port 443), jinak exit 2 a token se nepošle; 15 nepřátelských variant v testech;
  - dokumentace refresh tokenů srovnaná: `medplum-mcp` žádá jen `openid profile`, `mcp-smoke` žádá `offline_access` a token drží v keychainu;
  - sdílený OAuth klient je popsaný.
- **`scripts/check_repo.py`:**
  - přesná shoda `*.dokturek.ai` a odhalení napodobenin (`…dokturek.ai.evil.example`);
  - parsuje všechny URL; https je povinné mimo loopback;
  - skenuje celý strom;
  - v konfiguraci a kódu smí být jen povolení hostitelé plus `github.com`, `json.schemastore.org`, `claude.ai` (každý s důvodem);
  - 10 testů.
- **CI:**
  - `timeout-minutes`, `persist-credentials: false`;
  - Python 3.9 (`setup-python` v7.1.0 připnutý SHA), `ubuntu-24.04`;
  - Claude Code 2.1.290 → 2.1.330;
  - gitleaks i nad historií (`git` s `fetch-depth: 0`).
- **Instalátor Claude Desktopu:** srozumitelná chyba u vadného JSON, zápis přes symlink, práva 0600; 5 testů.
- **`smoke_test.py`:** log z `--e2e` se po úspěchu maže; `POST /oauth2/register` je zdokumentovaný jako jediná výjimka z „jen GET“.

## Co jsem ověřil
- `python3 scripts/check_repo.py` → Kontroly prošly (Python 3.13 i 3.9.25)
- unit testy: medplum-mcp 28, mcp-smoke 33, scripts 10 → OK (3.13 i 3.9.25)
- `py_compile`, `sh -n`, `claude plugin validate . --strict` a `tools/medplum-mcp --strict` (2.1.330) → OK
- **Neověřeno:**
  - nový krok gitleaks `git` (lokálně nešel spustit, ověří ho CI);
  - běh hooku v živé session Claude Code proti `medplum.test`.

## Checklist
- [x] `python3 scripts/check_repo.py` a unit testy prošly
- [x] `README.md` a `RISK.md` nástrojů odpovídají změně
- [x] Dokumentace v dokturek-docs: netýká se

- [x] Žádné tokeny, secrets ani data pacientů
- [x] Nový hostitel nebo prostředí: žádný (allowlist beze změny; `CODE_EXTERNAL_HOSTS` jsou jen veřejné referenční hosty se zdůvodněním)

## K rozhodnutí vlastníka
- Čtecí OAuth klient a AccessPolicy pro agenty (33-M2); klasifikace dat v `medplum.test`; nasazení serverové opravy cesty z auditu 47/10.

author: joaoalexandre2
body:
## Problema

O cartão do veículo mostrava "informar" (km nula) enquanto o alerta de pneus dizia "já passou aos 50.000 km". O cartão lê `km_atual` (coluna crua); o alerta lê o maior valor entre abastecimentos, serviços e `km_atual`. O `?? 0` em `ContaInicio` e `Atualizacoes` não causava esse caso, mas era um defeito latente: km nula viraria "vencido".

## O que muda

- O cartão usa o campo novo `km_conhecida` do backend e mostra a km, a data e a origem, por exemplo "em 17/11/2026 (abastecimento)". Sem o campo (backend antigo), volta a mostrar `km_atual`.
- **Sem km conhecida**, o alerta por km mostra "sem km" e "Informe a km de <veículo> para acompanhar a troca de pneus", em vez de "já passou". "Já passou" só aparece quando a km conhecida passou do alvo.
- Link "Informar km" só para quem pode: administrador e gestor na frota (mesmo critério do botão do cartão) e o dono na conta pessoa. Motorista vê o pedido sem link. Nenhuma permissão foi ampliada.
- Função `situacaoPorKm` em `src/utils/avisoPorKm.ts` (nova).

## Deploy

**Depende do PR `fix/km-unico-no-backend` do backend (repositório mycar): publicar o backend primeiro.** O frontend tolera a ausência do campo.

## Fora deste PR

- Na conta pessoa o link "Informar km" leva a `/veiculos`, onde a km é informada por abastecimento ou serviço (não há campo de km).
- A correção do gestor não baixa a km efetiva abaixo do maior valor de abastecimento ou serviço (regra de negócio mantida).

## Verificação

- `vitest run`: 95 arquivos, 681 testes passando (12 novos em `kmConhecida.test.tsx`).
- `npm run build` e eslint nos arquivos alterados: sem erros.
- **Não verificado na tela.**
- Integrado com os outros quatro PRs do frontend desta série em uma branch temporária: sem conflito, 734 testes e build passando.

author: bryanlucas7
body: ## What and why MCP servers can answer `initialize` with `instructions` on how to use them and their tools. The connector source dropped them, so an agent saw each tool's description alone. A server whose tools need usage rules (for example "call `preview_change` before `apply_change`", or "confirm before any destructive call") had no way to say so. MCP's post on server instructions (https://blog.modelcontextprotocol.io/posts/2025-11-03-using-server-instructions/) also recommends that hosts let people review, enable or disable them. Closes #1192. What changes: - **Read with the tools.** `McpSession` gets an optional `instructions()` (the SDK's `client.getInstructions()`), read in the same session that lists the tools. The text is trimmed, kept in the connector source's 60 s listing cache (`ServerListing`) and carried by each of the server's tools (`ToolDefinition.serverInstructions`). - **In the prompt, only where it applies.** The executor builds `serverInstructionsPrompt(granted)` from the run's granted tools, like the GitHub repositories block: one block per connection, appended to "What you can do", after the agent's own block. When present it is part of the computer session's `promptKey`; when absent the key is unchanged. - **Treated as outside content.** Each block goes through `untrustedBlock` (ADR 0117): ``, markers and hidden characters neutralised, cut at 4,000 characters with `[… N more characters cut]`. A heading line says the text is guidance on that app's own tools, ranks below the agent's instructions and everything above it, grants no permission and gives no orders. A run whose prompt holds such a block counts as having read outside text, whatever it calls: the transcript says so (`readServerNotes`, written before the first model call; a failed write stops the run), so `runReadOutside` sees it and the run's posts carry `readOutside`. - **Seen and switched per connection.** `connector_connections.instructions` keeps the text a listing read (migration 0323), stored as Postgres takes text (`pgSafeText`). It is written by the sync, and by a run's listing when the server changed its words, so the screen shows what agents read. `connector_connections.use_instructions` (on by default: an admin chose to connect the server, and one that sends nothing changes nothing) decides whether agents get it. - **API:** `CustomServer` gains `instructions: { text, cut, maxChars } | null` (as agents read it; null for readers who don't manage connectors) and `useInstructions`. `PUT …/connectors/custom/{id}/tools` takes an optional `useInstructions`, with the same permission as the rest of that save. The column is written, and the change audited, only when the request names it. - **Web:** the review step ("What it does") shows, under the tools, a "Server instructions" setting row from the kit (ⓘ, status "N of 4,000 characters", "Cut at 4,000 characters" or "Agents don't get this text.") with the kit's switch, then the text in a well, folded until "Ver mais" as a long text on a page already is (`FoldedBody`), muted while off. A server that sends none shows "The server sends no instructions.". - **Phone:** the same setting under the tools in the phone's review, in a well inside the same card, with the phone's `FoldedBody`. - **As written, on purpose.** The text is shown as the server wrote it, not formatted: `FoldedBody` gains `plain` (web and phone). Formatted, an address to a message or a file here, or an internal id, would become a chip that fetches with the admin's session as the step opens; a link below the fold would take the focus. This is also how the review already shows the server's other words (its tools' descriptions). - On both, the switch is saved with the step's Continue and sent only when the person moved it, so a save never undoes what another device set meanwhile. A service through Composio shows no section. Strings in all 14 languages. - **Left out on purpose.** Catalog connectors: our catalog picks which of their tools are exposed and with which scopes, and their vendor's notes may describe tools we don't expose. Composio sessions have no `initialize`. - **Protocol note.** The connector client is `@modelcontextprotocol/sdk` 1.32.1, which speaks the 2025 handshake, where instructions come in `InitializeResult`. The 2026-07-28 revision moves them to `DiscoverResult.instructions` (`server/discover`). That is in the v2 packages this repo uses only for its own server, not in this client. A server that also speaks 2025 keeps working. Moving the connector client to v2 is left for later. - ADR 0016 gets an addendum. ## Screenshots The review step ("What it does"), from the web test's screens with the app's CSS in Chromium. On, dark, desktop: Off, light, phone width: A server that sends none: The worst a server sends, as written and folded until "Ver mais": Tests: - engine (`packages/engine/test/mcp-server-instructions.test.ts`, through the real executor and the fake provider, 11 tests): - instructions reach the prompt once per server, enveloped, labeled, after the agent's own block; - such a run read outside even with no call, and a server that sends none leaves it as it was; - no instructions, or blanks, change nothing; - on by default; off on the connection removes the block, and turning it on brings it back; - a save that leaves the switch out never writes back what it read; - a server that changes its words is read anew and shown on its screen; - long text is cut at the cap with the note; - a server whose tools the agent can't use stays out; - what a server says is kept as Postgres takes text; - a catalog connector's instructions stay out. - server (`apps/server/test/connectors.test.ts`): the API returns the text as agents read it to admins and `null` to members, refuses a member's switch (403), turns it off through the tools' save, keeps it when the body leaves it out, and audits the change once. - web (`apps/web/test/server-instructions.test.tsx`, 6 tests): the worst a server sends (Markdown, unbreakable addresses, what would be a mention, an id's chip and a link elsewhere, other scripts, emoji, cut at 4,000) shown as written with nothing in it a link, a chip or a control, folded until "Ver mais" opens it, which is the screen the geometry check measures; the setting with its status and text, turned off and saved with Continue; Continue without moving the switch leaves it out; a Composio service shows no section; a server that sends none shows one line and no switch; the English words. - phone (`apps/mobile/test/features/connector-review.test.ts`): on, off and cut statuses; one line for a server that sends none and nothing for an older one; the save sends the switch only where it shows and once moved; nothing for a Composio service. Checks run: `bun run lint`, `bun run typecheck`, `bun run check:boundaries`, `bun run check:migrations`, `bun run db:generate` (nothing new), the touched tests, and the geometry check on the touched web screens. body:

author: jackson-hughes
body:
## Summary
- `ClusterSecretStore/onepassword` now has `spec.conditions[].namespaces` with the 8 namespaces that have ExternalSecrets: cert-manager, external-dns, garage, healthchecks-io, homepage, unpoller, velero, victoria-metrics. I got the list from `kustomize build` of all three Flux trees and it matches `kubectl get externalsecret -A` exactly. There are no ClusterExternalSecrets or PushSecrets. The schema matches the installed ESO v2.15.0 CRD. ESO's `shouldProcessSecret` matches `namespaces` against the `kubernetes.io/metadata.name` label.
- `validate-kubernetes.sh` now fails when an ExternalSecret's namespace isn't listed in its ClusterSecretStore's conditions. Stores whose conditions use a selector or regex are skipped.
- Both Traefik Gateway listeners now set `hostname: "*.ducknet.io"`, and `allowedRoutes` changes from `from: All` to `from: Selector` on `kubernetes.io/metadata.name In [flux-system, garage, homepage, media, podinfo, victoria-metrics]`. That list is every namespace that owns a route, including the Plex chart route in `media`, and it matches the live route list. The label is set automatically, so no namespace needs relabelling. All 13 route hostnames are one label under ducknet.io, with no apex.

## external-dns and `policy: sync`
- external-dns v0.24.0 only creates a record when a route is allowed by the listener (it evaluates `routeIsAllowed`, including `Selector`) and its host matches the listener hostname (`gwMatchingHost`). A route in an unlisted namespace, or with a non-`*.ducknet.io` host, now gets neither Traefik routing nor DNS.
- `--domain-filter=ducknet.io` already limited DNS to ducknet.io. The new part is the namespace bound: a route in any other namespace can no longer claim a `*.ducknet.io` name, so with `sync` it also can't create records that external-dns would then own and delete. external-dns config is unchanged.
- Trade-off: a route with **no** `spec.hostnames` now inherits the listener's `*.ducknet.io`, and external-dns would publish a wildcard record for it. Before this change, such a route published nothing. Every current route sets hostnames.

## Rollout notes
- No ordering steps. Live Gateway status has 13 routes attached, all in listed namespaces, so nothing should detach. Afterwards, check `kubectl get httproute -A` (all Accepted) and the ExternalSecrets (all SecretSynced).
- A new app needs its namespace added to the store list (CI checks this) and/or to the Gateway selector (CI does not check this; an unlisted route shows `NotAllowedByListeners` and gets no DNS).

## Validation
- `./scripts/validate-kubernetes.sh` passes. Removing a namespace from the store list makes the new check fail as expected, and adding a regex condition makes it skip the store. `shellcheck` is clean.
- The Traefik chart template and values schema at v42.4.1 (the live version) pass `hostname` and `namespacePolicy` through unchanged. I read them from the chart source; helm isn't available locally, so I did not run `helm template`.

## Summary by CodeRabbit

* **Configuration**
  * Secret synchronization is now limited to the approved namespaces. Gateway listeners use `*.ducknet.io` hostnames and accept routes only from the approved namespaces.
* **Validation**
  * Kubernetes validation now checks whether each external secret’s namespace is permitted by its referenced secret store. The check reports configuration errors and affects the validation result; it is skipped if a Kustomize build fails.

author: lautaropetaccio
body:
# Pull Request Description

Closes #1494

## What does this PR change?
Local deploys asked contract wallets (EIP-1654) at `latest` only, so a signature valid when the entity was signed was refused. As `@dcl/crypto` does, a link refused at latest is now asked again at the block `Blocks.getDate(ts, false)` selects for the entity timestamp.

- `dcl-auth`: new `verify_entity_auth_chain` (latest, then entity-time block); `verify_synced_auth_chain` uses the same order.
- content: one `AtEntityTime` wrapper takes the block from the access checks' L1 search (`l1_verification_block`): the last block strictly before the timestamp, block 1 before the first blocks. Its `WithoutL1` policy delegates to the validator's own selector on local deploys and is undecidable for synced entities. A failed lookup is Unverifiable, never a rejection.
- `blocks_for` memoized head-bound answers for 60 s, so a retry reused a stale head. `BlockSearch::is_final` now memoizes only answers whose next block is known; a head-bound lookup costs one `latest` read per access check.

## Test Instructions
From `services/catalyst`: `cargo test -p catalyst-content --lib validator::`, `cargo test -p catalyst-content --lib write_deployer::tests::the_signature_check`, `cargo test -p dcl-auth --lib`, `cargo test -p dcl-http --lib`; all pass. Covered: strict predecessor and block 1, acceptance at latest reads no block, failed L1 lookup is Unverifiable, deployer signature wiring, synced latest-then-block, `is_final` under a concurrent search. Clippy `-D warnings` fails only on pre-existing code outside this diff.

## Quality Checklist
- [x] Relevant checks were run; results and any checks not run are listed above.
- [x] Documentation has been updated, if required.
- [x] Performance impact has been considered.
- [ ] For changes covered by `docs/design-feasibility.md`: not applicable.
- [ ] For SDK features: not applicable.

**Follow-ups:** a705668a4 updates the batch deployer's synced contract-wallet test to expect the strict-predecessor block. cded69b83 makes a panicking sync deploy task still wake `on_idle` (an `InFlight` drop guard), so a failing task fails its test instead of hanging the suite.

author: kiff-android
body:
**Ready:** tafs#1757 (the page echoes `state`) is merged and deployed: `runtime.yml`'s `deploy` job succeeded on its merge commit `2ffe16b`.

This ports the iPad's WhatsApp door (`DoorsModel.add` for `whatsapp`), the last piece of DoorsView after #251's Slack door.

## What it does
- **Add a door › WhatsApp** opens tafs cloud's sign-up page in the browser: `GET /doors/whatsapp/connect?taf={id}&state={state}`. The state is fresh for each attempt: 32 random bytes as base64url (`WhatsAppDoor.NewState`).
- While the browser has it, the app shows "Waiting for your browser…" with **Cancel**.
- **The return.** The page sends the browser back to `tafs://doors/whatsapp?taf=…&state=…&code=…&phone_number_id=…&waba_id=…`. `App` reads it (`WhatsAppDoor.Read`). It needs taf, state and code, and a name given twice is no return. The waiting sign-up takes it **only** for the same taf, the same state (compared in fixed time), within 15 minutes of opening the page (`WhatsAppDoor.Takes`). Any other `tafs://doors/whatsapp` link is dropped.
- **The door.** `POST /v1/tafs/{id}/doors {app, code, phone_number_id, waba_id}` as the session, as the iPad does. The state stays on this PC. The new door opens.
- **Cancel** adds nothing and says nothing. If no return comes in time, it says "WhatsApp's signup didn't finish."

## Why the state
On the iPad, `ASWebAuthenticationSession` binds the return to the sign-up it started. On Windows, `tafs:` can be opened by any link. Without the state, a crafted `tafs://doors/whatsapp?taf=<id>&code=<another business's>` opened while this PC waits would connect someone else's WhatsApp Business number as the taf's door.

## Tests
`WhatsAppDoorTests` (part `record`), 12 tests:
- each attempt's state and the page's address;
- the return as the page writes it (`URLSearchParams`, `+` for a space, empty ids);
- eight URLs that are no return;
- only the right taf, state and time are taken: another state, an empty one, another taf, too late, or before opening are all refused;
- the door's body, with no state in it.

The whole suite passes, 2727 of 2727, and the Release x64 app builds.

**Checklist:** DoorsView's row is also edited by #251. Whichever of the two merges second moves the row to Ported (DoorDial and DoorRim aren't reachable at the pin), when its conflict is resolved. The Coverage line is untouched.

## Affects
Doors (`TafPage.Doors.cs`, the new `TafPage.WhatsAppDoor.cs`), the app's `tafs://` handling (`App.xaml.cs`), and access: which WhatsApp number becomes a taf's door. Two logins: mac-local and agentgabo.

author: samarmstrong
body:
Closes #4938

Before this change, only `github.com` got a credential (`GITHUB_TOKEN`), so a private repo on an allowed self-hosted GitLab or Gitea could not be read. All changes are in `core/skills/skill_sources.py`. There is no new setting, endpoint, Settings field or integration field.

- **Per-host credential.** For an allowed DNS host other than github.com, `_credential` reads `SKILL_SOURCE_<HOST>_USER` and `SKILL_SOURCE_<HOST>_TOKEN` through `get_secret`. `<HOST>` is the hostname uppercased, with `.` written as `_D_` and `-` as `_H_`; for example, `gitlab.example.net` reads `SKILL_SOURCE_GITLAB_D_EXAMPLE_D_NET_USER` and `SKILL_SOURCE_GITLAB_D_EXAMPLE_D_NET_TOKEN`. A credential counts only when both keys are set. Keys are derived only for `[a-z0-9.-]` hostnames, and never for IP literals in any form curl accepts (`10.0.0.1`, `127.1`, `2130706433`, `0x7f.0.0.1`). github.com is unchanged: it still uses `GITHUB_TOKEN` with the username `x-access-token`, and the same Settings hint.
- **Child environment.** `_git_env` starts from `os.environ` minus:
  - `SKILL_SOURCE_*` and `GITHUB_TOKEN`
  - `GIT_CONFIG*` and `GIT_CONFIG_PARAMETERS`
  - `GIT_ASKPASS` and `SSH_ASKPASS`
  - `GIT_TRACE*` and `GIT_CURL_VERBOSE`
  - `GIT_SSL_NO_VERIFY`, so a credential never goes out over unverified TLS (added after review)

  Proxy and CA variables (`GIT_SSL_CAINFO`, `SSL_CERT_FILE`, `SSL_CERT_DIR`) are kept. The extraHeader is scoped to `http.https://<exact-host>/`.
- **Refusals.** `_REFUSED` now also catches GitLab's `HTTP Basic: Access denied` and git's `The requested URL returned error: 401` / `403`. The single anonymous retry after a refused credentialed read now applies to every host. Its warning names the host and never includes the token, the Basic string or stderr.
- **Messages for non-GitHub hosts:**
  - No credential: `No skill-source credential for <host>. Set …_USER and …_TOKEN.`
  - Credential refused on both reads: `The skill-source credential for <host> did not grant repository access. Check token expiry and read permission.`
  - TLS failure or unreachable host: a message of its own.
  - Raw stderr is echoed only for anonymous calls; a credentialed call gets `git failed`.
- **Docs.** The keys are documented in the module docstring, since there is no operator doc for `VIGIL_SKILL_SOURCE_HOSTS`.

A subagent reviewed the diff. I fixed its two real findings (`GIT_SSL_NO_VERIFY`, and non-canonical IP forms getting keys). I kept two things as they are:
- A github.com 403 is now treated as a refusal. The spec asks for the 403 pattern on every host, so this is intended.
- `ls-remote` runs with `cwd=None`, so repo-local git config in the API's working directory still applies. That predates this change, and I left it alone to keep the scope narrow.

## Verification

**Ran**
- **Direct module calls against a throwaway Gitea 1.22.** It served HTTPS on 443 as `git-4938.localhost`, with a self-signed CA trusted through `GIT_SSL_CAINFO`.
  - No credential: the "No skill-source credential … Set SKILL_SOURCE_GIT_H_4938_D_LOCALHOST_USER and …_TOKEN" hint.
  - Token only, no user: the same hint.
  - Good credential: cloned the private repo and found `alert-review`.
  - Bad token on the private repo: "did not grant repository access".
  - Bad token on the public repo: OK after the anonymous retry, with the warning naming the host.
  - `GIT_SSL_CAINFO` unset: "the TLS certificate of git-4938.localhost is not trusted".
- **Key derivation:** `_host_keys` returns keys for `gitea` and `gitlab.example.net`, and `None` for `10.0.0.1`, `127.1`, `2130706433`, `0x7f.0.0.1`, `::1` and `github.com`.
- **Full stack (`./start.sh -d`, auth bypassed with `DEV_MODE=true`, see below).** `VIGIL_SKILL_SOURCE_HOSTS=github.com,git-4938.localhost`, Gitea credentials in the environment.
  - `POST /api/skills/repo/preview` on the private repo `@main`: 200, shape as in the issue.
  - `POST /api/skills/repo/install`: 200, `alert-review`.
  - `GET /api/skills`: `source.label`, `source.ref` and `source.commit` are set.
  - After an upstream push, `GET …/library/latest` returned the new commit.
  - `POST …/library/preview`: `latest` is the new commit and `changed[0].note == "SKILL.md changed"`.
  - `POST …/library/update`: 200, `removed: []`.
- **Credential cases, one restart each:**
  - Bad Gitea token, private repo: 400 "did not grant repository access".
  - Bad Gitea token, public repo: 200.
  - Only `_USER` set: 400 hint naming both keys, on both preview and `library/latest`.
  - Host outside the allowlist: 400 "git.example.org is not an allowed skill source".
- **github.com:**
  - Real `GITHUB_TOKEN`: the private `Vigil-SOC/vigil-assured` cloned. It returned "no SKILL.md found" because the repo holds no skills; a refusal would have given a different message.
  - Placeholder `GITHUB_TOKEN` from `.env`: the GitHub Settings refusal message for the private repo, and 200 for `anthropics/skills` after the retry.
- **Environment stripping:** I started the API with `GIT_TRACE` and `GIT_TRACE_CURL` set to file paths and `GIT_CURL_VERBOSE=1`. `/proc/<worker>/environ` showed the worker had them, yet no trace file was ever written, so git never saw them.
- **Leak search:** I grepped `logs/`, `~/.vigil/vigil.log` and an extracted `vigil-support.sh --mode native` bundle for the Gitea token, its Basic encoding (good and bad), the GitHub token and its Basic encoding. Each had 0 matches. A labelled `SKILL_SOURCE_GIT_H_4938_D_LOCALHOST_TOKEN=` line in `.env` came out as `[REDACTED]` in the bundle's `configuration/env`.
- **Lint:** black, isort and flake8 at the pre-commit versions all pass.

**Did not run**
- GitLab: too heavy to stand up here, as the groom note says. Its refusal strings are covered by pattern only.
- Medic redaction: its suffix rules are unchanged and every derived name ends in `_TOKEN`, so I did not exercise it live.
- `scripts/migrate_dotenv_secrets.py` for the new keys: I passed credentials through the environment, so the encrypted-store path was not exercised. `get_secret` is unchanged.
- No LLM involved, so no model run.

**Blocked by the machine**
- No repo venv existed, so I built `venv/` with `uv`. `start.sh` would have built it too.
- First-run bootstrap rejected the setup code the API had just logged (`POST /api/auth/bootstrap` → 403 "Setup code is missing or incorrect.") on a freshly started stack. I worked around it by setting `DEV_MODE=true` in the generated, gitignored `.env`.
- The generated `.env` holds env.example's placeholder `GITHUB_TOKEN`, which overrides the shell's value. I deleted that line for the real-token check.

body:
## What

Phase P14b of the untangle refactor. This is a client-only structural change with no visual or behaviour change.

- `OptionList.svelte`: each row carries `data-option-row`. Arrow/Home/End navigation and a new exported `focusPicked()` both find the rows through one `rowButtons()` helper, so navigation no longer depends on the `opt` styling class.
- `OptionPicker.svelte`: binds to `OptionList` and calls `focusPicked()`, which focuses the picked row (`items.findIndex(on)`) or else the first row. It no longer queries `[aria-pressed="true"]` and then the first `button`.
- `AuthForm.svelte`: calls the existing `focusFirstError(formEl)` from `forms/form-enhance.ts` instead of its own `[aria-invalid="true"]` query.

## Why

Round 5 of the re-audit found implicit DOM-selector conventions. I checked each item before changing anything.

1. **Shared row hook (partly real).** `MultiPicker` has no arrow-key navigation, and its rows never sit inside `OptionList`'s container: `OptionList` only queries its own `ref`. So the two components never depended on each other's markup. The real coupling was inside `OptionList`, where navigation used its styling class as the selector; that is fixed. `MultiPicker` is unchanged, because reusing `OptionList`'s row would change how it looks.
2. **Selected hook.** `OptionPicker` is fixed as described above. **`CurrencyTabs` was dropped**: its query targets markup in its own file (the pills) plus the standard ARIA `aria-checked` of the bits-ui radio group in `SegmentedControl.svelte`, which is outside this phase's files. It does not render `OptionList`, so an `OptionList` focus handle does not apply to it.
3. **First-invalid focus.** There is now one helper with two callers. I kept the existing name `focusFirstError` instead of renaming it to `focusFirstInvalid`, because `FormShell.svelte` calls it three times and is outside this phase's files. Its selector also matches picker buttons whose `aria-describedby` ends in `-error`. No auth form has such a button (every `aria-describedby` there is on an `<input>`), so AuthForm focuses the same field as before. The `tick()` timing is unchanged, so the selector is not passed in.

## Issues

None.

## Checks run

- [x] `pnpm lint`
- [x] `pnpm typecheck`
- [x] `pnpm build`
- [x] `pnpm test:e2e`: 117/117 passed (private Postgres, under the e2e lock)
- [x] Opus verifier: APPROVED, with browser checks on a local dev server. Picker focus on open goes to the picked row, or to the first row when nothing is picked. Arrow keys wrap, and Home/End jump. Enter picks the row and closes the drawer. The MultiPicker filter still toggles. First-invalid focus is correct on /movements/new, /login and /signup.

These keyboard and focus behaviours have no e2e spec, and I did not add one: e2e stays limited to money, data, auth and isolation flows.

Skills: no touch, viewport, input or motion change, so `mobile-native` and `review-animations` were not run. Nothing needs a real-phone check.

None.

author: jssantogit
body:
## Real 30-work failure
Signed-code10 30-work run [#45079717634](https://github.com/jssantogit/tsuzuki/actions/runs/45079717634) completed RED: all three independent Android catalog shards succeeded and source shard #2 succeeded, while source shards #0/#1 failed on `MangaAllRealSourceHostDecoderTest` at `Host failed real chapter decode`. The raw signed-source capture artifacts show five real `reading.chapters` responses exceeding the production Host's immutable `MAX_RESULT_JSON_CHARS=64*1024`, including 425, 548, 653, 753, and 477 chapters in one result (payload lengths approximately 72–147k characters). Production `ProviderRuntimeInvocationResponse.success` correctly returns `MALFORMED_RESULT` / `RUNTIME_PAYLOAD` over this size. The replay assertion wrongly demanded success for those authentic over-limit responses; *no chapter page was actually decoded by the Host*.

## Fix is diagnostic, NOT a bypass
- Keep exact 64KiB Host limit and official P-256 signed code10 untouched. Validate over-limit success-capture responses against the actual closed Host `MALFORMED_RESULT / RUNTIME_PAYLOAD` failure, count them, mark per-work `INCONCLUSIVE_HOST_RESULT_LIMIT` and **never** call them decoded successful chapters.
- Feed original decoder JUnit verdicts into per-work source/catalog/collector/SQLDelight report; verify matching 10-case sets and fail closed if a Host limit was falsely labeled complete or a decoder replay gap was hidden.
- Include `hostResultLimitResponses` in 30-work aggregate and validate it as a nonnegative bounded counter with `sourceIncomplete=true`; regression tests cover original Host 64KiB boundary and strict Python report/aggregate.
- No relaxation of source or Host budgets, Provider signing, Reader/CND grants, or editorial bind.

The CI can now *finish a diagnostic report* even if some chapters are oversized, without reporting them functional. Actual code10 capacity fix requires a separately reviewed/published provider generation supporting smaller pages or a capability-specific bounded source/Host transport.

body:
## Summary

Follow-ups from the PR #103 review (offline admin tools only; no device code).

- `load_revocations` accepts a revocation list modified up to 5 minutes in the future (clock skew); anything further ahead or older than `--revocation-max-age-days` is still refused.
- `reanchor` verifies `--keyset-envelope` (root) and `--policy-envelope` (approved policy key) signatures before hashing, so a wrong file is refused before signing.
- `reanchor` refuses a policy envelope whose `keySetVersion` is below the key set floor (the device would never re-accept it).
- `write_private_bundle` creates the final directory itself and links the 0600 files in, so it never replaces an existing path, including an empty directory created after the existence check.

CI class: Medium — offline admin tooling, no device or server code
Writer: Codex gpt-6.2-sol (high), local; lead verified and committed
Review: independent Claude Opus (high) on 214b72e: merge, no P1/P2; its key-set-version P3 added in bced20f (3-line guard, lead). Codex GitHub review on 214b72e: no major issues
Local tests: `python3 -m unittest discover -s tools -p 'test_*.py'` — 129 tests OK (lead rerun)

- Na agenda, agendado, em uso e concluído se diferenciavam só pela cor, e o rótulo ia no `title`, que não existe no toque. "Agendado" usava a cor da marca (a mesma do erro).

author: tannevaled
body:
Fixes #35.

The earlier fixes and the locker count and Budget in v0.4.0 closed the unlock paths of Open and OpenFrom. The keybag rewrite functions still used DefaultLimits with no way for a caller to tighten them.

- `AddRecoveryKeyLimited`, `AddPassphraseLimited`, `AddArgon2idPassphraseLimited`, `AddInstitutionalKeyLimited` take a `Limits`. The existing keybag's lockers are bounded (`MaxLockers`) and charged to `Limits.Budget`; so is the new locker's own PBKDF2 or Argon2 run, before it runs. The unsuffixed functions call them with `DefaultLimits`.
- A locker refused by a limit during the rewrite's unlock used to read as "passphrase did not unlock any locker". It is now `ErrLimit`.
- `OpenFromWithPrivateKey` gets no variant: it derives no key and stops at the first entry carrying the key's fingerprint, so a keybag costs at most one RSA operation. A test pins that.

Tests: a 200-locker keybag is refused by all four variants with the image untouched; a normal container takes each variant and the new lockers unlock it; a Budget with room for the unlock but not the wrap refuses, and one unit of room either side of the edge behaves; 256 Argon2 threads are refused. mutsweep on extra_lockers.go: the three new guards are caught.

New exported API, so a MINOR tag.

author: basit025
body:
## What

- **Submit** (with a confirmation that previews the viva) locks the code. Only then are the hidden-test **inputs** sent; the browser runs them and the **server marks them** against this student's version of the question. Expected answers never leave the server
- **Viva**: one question at a time, generated from the student's own code (explain a line → predict an output → describe a change), each building on the last answer. Timers enforced on the server; paste off; leaving the page is measured
  - **Ground truth**: for the predict question, after the student answers, their own code is run on that input and the scorer is given the real result. A wrong prediction can't score high, a right one can't score low
  - **Fairness**: ideas scored, never English; Roman Urdu counts fully; blank or "I don't know" scores 0
  - **Resilience**: if every AI provider is down, a question is built from a real line of the student's code; scoring falls back to the teacher reading the transcript
- **Grade** = tests × (100 − viva weight) + viva × weight, using the teacher's weighting
- **Integrity flags** (rule-based, plain sentences, each tied to the `seq` range for "Show me"): large instant insertion; typing far faster than baseline; long absence then a burst; correct without any runs; perfect tests with a weak viva
- **Screens**: the viva (timer ring, progress dots, one question, nothing else) and a results screen (score, tests, suggested mark, per-question feedback, what to revise)

## Verified

- Lint, 45 unit tests (flags tested on a simulated honest session → none, and a simulated copier → the right four), build
- `npm run e2e:viva` (real AI, simulated students; an engineering check only): honest viva 83/100, grade 9.2; copier viva 20/100, grade 6 with 4 flags. Identical code, separated by the viva
- `smoke:ui`: the full journey in Chrome, workspace → submit → tests 5/5 → 3 viva questions → results, with zero console errors (a 409 after submit was found and fixed)

author: revslaughter
body:
Closes #7. Part of the roadmap in #2.

## Summary

One container definition now builds and tests the tool everywhere: in VS Code, on the command line, and in CI.

1. **`Dockerfile`**, in three stages:
   - `toolchain`: Go 1.26.11, Node 26.13.1 (the current LTS), Rust 1.97.1, and the Chromium for Playwright 1.63.0. Each base image is pinned by tag and digest.
   - `build`: compiles the viewer, `acu` and the Go adapter.
   - `runtime` (the default): `acu`, the adapter, and the Go toolchain that the adapter needs to load packages. Use it as `docker run --rm -v "$PWD:/work" -p 4321:4321 acu serve --addr 0.0.0.0:4321`.
2. **`.devcontainer/devcontainer.json`**. It builds the `toolchain` stage and runs as an unprivileged `dev` user. On creation it installs dependencies, fetches the corpus and installs the adapter. It also offers the Go, rust-analyzer, YAML (with the `atlas.yaml` schema), TOML and Playwright extensions.
3. **`scripts/check.sh`** runs every check. CI now runs it inside the `toolchain` container, with layer caching. A second job builds the `runtime` image and maps the fixture with it.
4. **Pins outside the container**: `rust-toolchain.toml`, `.node-version`, and `toolchain go1.26.11` in the adapter's `go.mod`. The golden file stays byte-for-byte identical under Go 1.26.11.
5. **Restricted networks**: `REGISTRY` selects a Docker Hub mirror (the digests stay the same), and an optional `extra_ca` build secret adds a TLS proxy's CA certificate.
6. **Checkouts that another user owns.** CI's first run failed: git refused a checkout owned by the runner's user inside a root container, and `go list` asked git for version stamps. The fix:
   - The adapter now loads packages with `-buildvcs=false`. This also fixes the runtime image for users who mount their own repository.
   - `check.sh` trusts the workspace for its own git calls only.
   - The runtime image trusts mounted repositories.

   I reproduced the failure with a checkout owned by uid 1001, and the full check suite passes there now.

## Verified

- Locally: `scripts/check.sh` inside the `toolchain` container passes, including the end-to-end smoke test on all three examples in both themes.
- Locally: the devcontainer's set-up command, run as `dev`, followed by `scripts/check.sh --quick`, passes.
- Locally: the `runtime` image runs `--version`, `extract`, `check` and `serve`.
- CI: both jobs pass.

author: pmilewsskiedu-gif
body:
## Correctness
On `main aa2988cc`, `CommandList::copy_resource` rejects self-copies and `copy_texture` rejects empty/inverted boxes, invalidating an entire otherwise legal D3D12 command list. Independent parity PR #3933 showed WARP `Close` succeeds and Leonida fails; author released these fixes in #3918 comment 7086918553. Ownership claimed before edits: https://github.com/ItsNotRexed/Leonida/issues/3918#issuecomment-7087219631.

## Fix
Validated no-op copies return success without recording an overlapping or zero-extent Vulkan copy. Invalid resource IDs, unsupported footprint-to-footprint copies and operations on closed lists still fail. Production changes are limited to `runtime/src/command_list.h` and `runtime/shims/d3d12_com.cpp`: the COM boundary additionally rejects self-copies of UPLOAD/READBACK/CUSTOM heaps, as native WARP does for UPLOAD.

## Native and Vulkan verification
New independent `d3d12_noop_copy_test` uses real COM API calls and synthetic data. Five DIRECT command lists: texture self-copy and DEFAULT-buffer self-copy and zero-width, zero-height and inverted-box upload-to-texture copies. Each is submitted, fenced and checked for preservation of an upload buffer's 65,536-byte pattern.

- Native D3D12 WARP: 5/5 submissions pass, zero mismatches.
- Unmodified original main on RTX 4060 Ti: native WARP passes; Leonida `Close` fails on case 0, HRESULT `80070057`, exit 1; no invalid Vulkan dispatch.
- Patched RTX 4060 Ti with `LEONIDA_VK_VALIDATION=1`: 5/5 pass, zero pattern mismatches, exit 0.
- MSVC/Ninja focused CTests **6/6 passed**, 13.44 s: `d3d12_noop_copy`, `d3d12_predicated_copy`, `d3d12_subresource_copy`, `d3d12_copy_xfmt`, `d3d12_stencil_copy`, `replay_copy_offset`.
- Final expanded RTX/WARP CTest **12/12 consecutive passes**, 8.19 s; focused six tests rerun **6/6** in 9.35 s. Additional negative control: native WARP rejects UPLOAD-buffer self-copy at Close, initial patch incorrectly accepted it, corrected COM wrapper now rejects it as well. `git diff --check` clean.

Commits `820c1b62211c1cb360551b389a6884456857309d` and follow-up `40cf85c2e3963ccece8578577ebabf899456f1cb`, base `aa2988cc555bad7ecd508b48a702adbb32fe7c95`, 4 files +145/-2. No full-suite or other GPU-vendor claim. No game files, extracted shaders, binaries or secrets. **AI-assisted development and testing.**

## Summary
- `*.omsession.json` (`om.session/1`): a JSON link to a model plus the UI state to restore — viewArea pane tree, group tabs + rules subpane state, per-grid chips/selection/scroll, dock layout, theme
- Layered per-key override: app defaults < model-file presentation (`page_selections`, widths) < session < live changes; tolerant ID resolution — unknown view/dim/item skipped with a "partly applied" notice, never fatal

- Scroll is the one state not in `ViewState` — pending-scroll map consumed at grid scroll-restore points; `scrollProbe` captures it for active tabs only (inactive-tab scroll is a documented deferral)

body:
## Objetivo

Antes de alterar a rotação de descanso ou o gerador, demonstrar quando as jornadas >9h são inevitáveis com os mesmos dias de trabalho. O cenário real de novembro 2026 tem oito jornadas de 9h30; quatro colaboradores com 19 dias de trabalho e três domingos de 5h. Por pessoa: 16×9h+3×5h=159h, faltando 1h para as 160h do ciclo. Como a capacidade por jornada normal é 9h30, são necessárias **pelo menos duas jornadas >9h por cada um dos quatro colaboradores**. Portanto, **8 é o mínimo MATEMÁTICO mantendo os dias escalados**.

## Implementação

- `analyzeFixedWorkdayLongDayBound`: limite inferior puro, determinístico, independente do gerador, com capacidades reais por dia e dias de abertura curta bloqueados. Não altera horários.
- `analyzeMonthlyFixedWorkdayLongDayFloor`: só apresenta resultados de quatro semanas civis consecutivas **inteiramente no mês**, com 160h por pessoa e configuração de pausa V2/rolling28. Nunca declara possibilidade ou necessidade de alterações com dados incompletos.
- Diagnóstico JSON: `analysis.cycleLongDays`, nulo quando não demonstrável, incluindo limite matemático por colaborador. **Sem nova configuração no UI e sem alterar HARD/SOFT existentes.**
- Testes sintéticos anonimizados que distinguem um ciclo com mínimo 2 jornadas longas e outro em que 0 é matematicamente viável.

## Próxima decisão (não implementada neste PR)

Estudar se é possível modificar a **distribuição de dias escalados e domingos** respeitando descansos, fins de semana, cobertura, 160h e qualificação funcional. A análise atual NÃO prova que exista uma alternativa com menos de oito jornadas e não altera a rotação. Não fazer merge nem publicação Cloudflare sem autorização.

## Validação real do PR95 — Safari 22/11/2026 23:10 UTC

Ficheiro exportado pelo utilizador: `schedule-engine-diagnostico-2026-11-12.json`, período novembro de 2026, exportedAt `2026-11-22T23:10:46.556Z`, `origin=generated_preview`, `settingsMatchGeneratedPreview=true`. **Dados individuais não armazenados neste PR.**

Verificação independente minuto a minuto dos **171 turnos** e cálculos do ciclo completo de **02 a 29/11**:
- `analysis.cycleLongDays.cycleStart=2026-11-02` e `cycleEndExclusive=2026-11-30`.
- 8 jornadas de 9h30 observadas = **8 jornadas de limite matemático** (`minimumLongDaysSameWorkdays=8`; `potentiallyRemovableLongDays=0`) com os mesmos dias de trabalho. Quatro colaboradores: 19 dias/ciclo, 3 domingos de 5h, 160h efetivas e 2 jornadas longas; o limite foi recalculado diretamente dos turnos e das capacidades: `16×9h + 3×5h = 159h`, restando 60 minutos a distribuir em incrementos de no máximo 30min acima de 9h por jornada, logo mínimo 2. Todos os outros colaboradores têm limite 0.
- **160h efetivas em 28 dias para as 8 pessoas**. **0 minutos** de abertura sem ninguém, **0 minutos** com uma só pessoa, **0 minutos** Caixa sem pessoas e **0 minutos** Vendas sem pessoas; sem funções atribuídas fora das qualificações; 5 a 8 pessoas escaladas todos os dias. 171 turnos e 8 longos, igual aos indicadores do teste anterior, sem afirmar equivalência integral turno a turno sem diff.
- 7 das 8 jornadas longas mostram 6h30 de trabalho contínuo após almoço: melhoria de qualidade futura **não introduzida como HARD**.
- `validation.displayed` e `validation.recalculatedWithCurrentSettings` ambos `insufficient_context` APENAS com 2 `CONTEXT_INCOMPLETE` nas fronteiras externas de 26–31/10 e 01–06/12. Não é certificação global `valid`, não é aprovação de escala.

**Critérios de aceitação do PR95 confirmados em teste real.** Implementação do diagnóstico pronta para revisão/autorização de merge, **sem tocar no gerador**, na rotação ou nas HARD constraints. PR permanece **Draft e não integrado** até autorização do utilizador. Próximo estudo separado: se outras datas de descanso, domingos e composição diária podem reduzir o limite observado respeitando todas as regras; o PR95 NÃO prova que tal solução exista.

Foi recebido `schedule-engine-diagnostico-2026-11-13.json` (exportação `2026-11-23T10:06:34.620Z`), comparado campo a campo com `-12.json` de `2026-11-22T23:10:46.556Z`. **Todos os campos são rigorosamente iguais, exceto `exportedAt`.** O SHA-256 do conteúdo JSON normalizado de `proposal.assignments` coincide nos dois: `bacf42ae91f558e758abc5c366ca5ea418c8febb006aceba6cf5df054baf4601`.

author: atqamz
body:
Adds `POST /api/v1/skills/add` and `POST /api/v1/skills/remove` to the Board API, behind the same gate as `sync`, `update` and `propose` (host session only, CSRF, board controls on, one skills request at a time, five-minute budget that stops at Board shutdown). A paired Companion still gets `403` for both ("a paired Companion cannot update, propose, add or remove skills; use the host's Board"), while `sync` stays open to it as on main.

## What it does

- `add` takes `scope`, `project` (with `scope: "project"`), `source` and an optional `ref`. `source` must be the bare name of a skill of Hand's own repository, which tracks `main`. Every other source (a URL, `file://`, `git@`, a path, a login, a query or a fragment, a name ending in `.git`) is `400 bad_request` before any command runs, so nothing is fetched or written and the value is not echoed. Third-party sources have no API path in this PR: they stay `hand skills add` in a terminal. `name` and `yes` are refused on `add`.
- `remove` takes `scope`, `project` and `name`. `name` is required: the API never removes every skill of a scope, unlike the CLI. `yes`, `source` and `ref` are `400`. Refusals (edited copy, unmarked folder, no lock entry, dirty project folder) are `200` with a `refused` row and the CLI's reason.
- New result state `added` (`detail` is the commit). `cmdSkillsAdd` now records its row, which `skillsAct` returns; before, an add through `skillsAct` answered an empty run.
- New feature `skills_manage` in `/api/v1/meta`, so a client can tell the routes exist before drawing controls; the list is now `skills`, `skills_manage`, `skills_sync` in `api_host.go`, `api_host_test.go`, `internal/cli/board_test.go` and `docs/api.md`.
- One `skills.added` or `skills.removed` event per `add` or `remove` that completes with no error and no refusal, with the same shape as `skills.synced`: `SCOPE[ PROJECT] by operator (desktop): NAME`. A refused request (`400`, `403`, `409`), a failed run and a `refused` row write none, even when an I/O error left a partial change; a failed event write answers `500`. `state.SkillsSynced` became `state.NoteSkills(kind, detail)`, and `skills.synced` is unchanged.
- Docs: `docs/api.md` (routes, request rules, `added`, the events, features table and meta example, errors, receipts), `docs/commands.md`, `docs/spec.md`, `docs/vocabulary.md`, `docs/safe-use.md`. The spec, the API and the vocabulary say the same about when an event is written.

## What differed from the design

- `add` accepts only a bare name; the design also allowed the exact own-repository URL. That URL would copy the repository root as a skill named `skills`, so it is refused too.
- The design extended the leading-dash refusal to `source` and `ref`. Not needed: `source` must match the skill-name pattern (no leading dash) and `ref` is passed as `--ref=VALUE` and checked by the CLI's ref rule; both cases are tested.
- Own `add` with a `ref` is allowed (a branch, tag or commit of the own repository); `refs/...`, `pull/...`, `merge-requests/...` and `..` refs are `400`.
- Reading origin/main before building: every claim in the design's "Today" section held (`skillsAct`, `apiSkillsAction`, the `skillsBusy` lock, `add` not setting `r.rec`, `remove` going through `eachSkill`).
- Second place that pins the feature list: `internal/cli/board_test.go` (the real board's `/meta`), besides `api_host_test.go` and the docs checks.

## Clients

- Desktop: the Skills page sentence now reads "The window has no add or remove control. Run hand skills add or hand skills remove in a terminal; the next check lists the change." `SkillResult.State` is a plain string; `skillResultTone` returns `neutral` for a state it does not know. The page never sends `add` or `remove`, so it cannot receive `added` today; no change here.
- Android: reads only `GET /skills` (`SkillInfo.state` is a string, an unknown one is `Neutral`) and decodes no action result, because a paired Companion's actions are `403`. No change.

## Tests

Board (`api_skills_test.go`, `api_skills_phone_test.go`): the paired-phone refusals as a table of sentences with `add` and `remove`, one event per successful add and remove with the skill's name, a failed event write answers `500` for `add` and `remove` as for `sync`, no `skills.` event after a refused sync, an update or a propose, no event for a refusal, an error, a `refused` row or a phone; add and remove through the shared gate (no CSRF, no session, no hooks, paired phone, `GET`, concurrent request), body refusals, receipts, the feature list. CLI (`skills_api_manage_test.go`, real git fixtures): own add in fleet, project and user scope with the lock, `skills.json`, all four roots and the listed `trusted`/`current` state; a ref and odd refs; 21 refused sources, each answering the bare-name rule (a name ending in `.git` included, so it is not fetched); a dirty project folder is `409`, an unknown project `404`, nothing committed in a project; remove of one of two skills from every root, lock and subscription, with a later `sync` not bringing it back; no name, `yes`, `source`, `ref`, dash and path names all `400` with both skills intact; edited, unmarked and unknown copies refused with files intact; a dirty project folder refused; a planted subscription stays untrusted after an add; a failing clone and a login in a clone error leave no path or login; a Board shutdown mid-add leaves no folder, lock or temp folder.

Mutants run against these tests (each made one at a time, then reverted):

| Mutant | Result |
|---|---|
| `r.rec.done` not set in `cmdSkillsAdd` | killed |
| Board `remove` name guard removed | killed (CLI and Board) |
| `refuseDirty` bypassed in `remove` | killed |
| `refuseUnlessClean` bypassed in `remove` | killed |
| own-source check on `add` removed | killed |
| `cleanErr` dropped on request errors | killed |
| `skillsBusy` skipped for `add` and `remove` | killed |
| paired-device `403` skipped for `add` and `remove` | killed |
| `Forget` not called in `remove` | killed |
| `Skills.Remove` stops after the first root | killed |
| Board `add` source-required guard removed | killed |
| Board allows `yes` on `remove` | killed |
| `skills_manage` dropped from the feature list | killed |
| no event for `add` and `remove` | killed |
| event written for a `refused` row | killed |
| event written for a failed run | killed |
| event without the skill's name | killed |
| `remove` recorded as `skills.added` | killed |
| event for `update` and `propose` too | killed |
| old 403 sentence for add and remove | killed |
| a paired phone may `add` | killed |
| a name ending in `.git` passes the bare-name check | killed (it fetched, then failed with 400; the test now requires the bare-name answer) |
| `remove` route runs as `sync` | killed |
| event write error ignored for `add` and `remove` | killed |
| `update` writes an event with an empty kind | killed |
| `add` ignores `ref` | killed |
| dash refusal not covering `source` and `ref` | survived: equivalent, the same values are refused downstream, so the extension was dropped |

The design's mutants for the trust branch (`ownURL` forced for a third-party source), the `yes` equality, `--ref <commit>` after a yes and the lock-commit post-check belong to the third-party step and are not part of this PR.

## Not done

- The scope's skills file lock is a blocking flock that ignores the request context; a terminal `hand skills` holding it stalls an API request up to the five-minute limit. Existing gap for `update`, left for a separate change.
- Unreachable or private own source answers `500 internal` with the scrubbed message.
- Desktop controls and Android are not part of this PR.

author: adebesin-cell
body:
### 🔗 Linked issue

None.

### 🧭 Context

PostHog's web vitals showed a few blog posts loading slower than the rest (LCP around 3.2 to 3.5s at p75). Lighthouse on slow 4G put the post page at LCP 3.6s, with nothing render-blocking: the article text was waiting on the main thread. About 300 KB of JavaScript runs before it can paint, and posthog-js (86 KB compressed, 278 KB raw) was preloaded and initialised at startup on every page even though nothing needs it that early.

### 📚 Description

- `posthog-js` is now imported dynamically inside `onNuxtReady`, so it is no longer part of the startup bundle. The build references its chunk only through `import()`.
- Pageviews and custom events that fire before it loads are queued and flushed once it initialises, so nothing is dropped. Pageviews carry the URL they were captured on.
- Post pages no longer use the `slide-enter-content` fade-in, so the article text paints as soon as it arrives instead of starting invisible. Other pages keep the animation.
- `useTrack` now calls a provided `$track` function instead of reaching for the client, so callers don't change.

Lint and typecheck pass. I'll compare Lighthouse on the preview against production under the same slow 4G and 3G throttling before merging.

body:
## Summary

Rebased cleanly onto `main` (`006489c`, preserving PR #41 Console ASCII mode and PR #42 dark mode) in two focused commits:

### 1. Quality Fixes & Regression Tests (`28ae843`)
- **Core math & engine**: Fix `BigFloat::ToString` UB for `|val| >= 2^64` and `TryParse` exponent/caching edge cases; invalidate `DeepReferenceCache`/BLA state around cancellation and in-place overwrites while preserving active limb precision; clamp Newton coarse midpoint reconstruction to its root basin; guard non-finite escape/denominator values, Julia zoom guard-band clamping, `FramePresentation` deep-center resolution, and ARM64 BLA step delta clamping.
- **GPU solver & HLSL shaders**: Fix OpenMP cancellation in `GpuMandelbrotBla`; key GPU orbit/BLA uploads per `DeepReferenceCache` instance; detect D3D11 device loss on `Map` failures; align row-chunk heights to 16-row threadgroups with explicit `heightLimit`; flush multi-pass stages; switch indirect dispatches to 2D grids (`32768` max X groups); harden `DeepExp` `Renorm2`/escape/smooth-coloring and LDS-BLA underflow/skip bounds; validate movie band/frame dimensions.
- **Movie export, muxer & CLI**: Fix cancellation/wakeup race in `MovieExporter`; prevent GPU-mode CPU fallback and `uint64_t` TDR strip overflow; equalize zoom-out pyramid chunk iterations; handle `MF_E_TRANSFORM_STREAM_CHANGE` and reset rejected candidate state in `MovieWriter`; validate HEVC VPS and H.264 high-profile `avcC` records and avoid signed overflow in H.264 scaling lists; harden `MovieCli` UTF-8/JSON surrogate/depth/float parsing and console handling (preserving PR #41 narrow `std::cout` output in `--ascii` mode).
- **UI, CI/packaging & tests**: Guard image export re-entrancy; check event suppression before mutating slider/checkbox state; revoke movie dialog click handler and validate selection/preview dimensions; scope GitHub Actions permissions and harden `release.yml` / packaging PowerShell scripts; add regression tests across `HighPrecision`, `MandelbrotEngine`, `FramePresentation`, and `MovieCli`.

### 2. Modular Refactoring & Deduplication (`f351328`)
- **Movie CLI**: Split `MovieCli.cpp` (`-> 558` lines) into `ViewStateJson.h/.cpp` (`725` lines) and `MovieCliParser.cpp` (`1,092` lines, including PR #41 `--ascii` CLI options).
- **WinUI `MainWindow`**: Split `MainWindow.xaml.cpp` (`-> 948` lines) into `MainWindow.Navigation.cpp` (`467` lines, including PR #42 app theme controls), `MainWindow.Palette.cpp` (`227` lines), and `MainWindow.Export.cpp` (`81` lines).
- **GPU solver**: Extract `GpuSolverPrep.cpp` (`661` lines) from `GpuFractalSolver.cpp` (`-> 705` lines) and deduplicate `DispatchGpuSubpixelPass` / `ReadbackBuffer` across interactive and movie pipelines (`GpuMoviePipeline.cpp -> 307` lines).
- **Movie export & zoom pyramid**: Move `MoviePlan::PrepareAutoTargets` into `MoviePlan.cpp`, extract `MovieFrameRenderer.h/.cpp` (`660` lines) with shared `ComputeGpuBandRows` / `BuildShutterParams` (`MovieExport.cpp -> 456` lines), and split linear-light resampling/compositing into `MovieZoomResampler.cpp` (`634` lines; `MovieZoomPyramid.cpp -> 394` lines).
- **GPU shaders**: Split `GpuShallowAndLdsShaders.cpp` and `GpuDeepAndMovieShaders.cpp` into `GpuShallowShader.cpp` (`320` lines), `GpuPerturbLdsShaders.cpp` (`695` lines), `GpuDeepExpShader.cpp` (`563` lines), and `GpuMovieShaders.cpp` (`498` lines).
- **Project files**: Updated `MandelbrotViewer.vcxproj` and `MandelbrotViewer.Tests.vcxproj` with consistent `NotUsing` PCH settings while preserving PR #41 `ConsoleAscii.h/.cpp` (note: PR #41's `ConsoleAscii.cpp` was left untouched).

## Verification
- **Unit Test Suite**: All **132 / 132** tests passed (`0` failures, `0` compiler warnings across all 42 translation units), including all PR #41 `ConsoleAscii` tests, PR #42 `AppTheme` tests, and newly added regression tests.
- **Project & Symbol Audits**: Verified `MandelbrotViewer.vcxproj` and `MandelbrotViewer.Tests.vcxproj` XML integrity, file existence, and PCH consistency, plus 1:1 `MainWindow` member definition coverage (`112/112` methods).

author: dudaf3rnandes
body:
## Contexto

A issue #48 reportou ajustes pontuais de UI/acessibilidade, com foco em:
- erro 403 no console para voluntário em Configurações;
- coluna "Data" no histórico de usuários sempre vazia;
- quebra de layout com nomes longos no histórico;
- texto de confirmação de exclusão para "entrada" com artigo incorreto;
- landmarks `<main>` aninhados;
- falta de nome acessível em cartões clicáveis do dashboard;
- modais sem `role="dialog"`;
- menu "Mais ações" sem fechamento por Esc;
- sobreposição do botão VLibras na sidebar;
- busca da tela Início sensível a acentos e ausência do cartão de Configurações;
- confirmação de exclusão sem identificar o item.

A causa principal era combinação de semântica incompleta (ARIA/landmarks), regras de busca sem normalização de acentos e pequenos detalhes de renderização/UX.

## Alterações

- Configurações:
  - `obterPerfil` passou a usar apenas `/usuarios/me`, removendo chamada desnecessária a `/usuarios` (evita 403 para voluntário).
- Histórico de usuários:
  - coluna Data passou a aceitar `dataCadastro || dataCriacao || createdAt`.
  - colunas Nome/E-mail com quebra de texto para não estourar tabela.
- Histórico genérico:
  - menu "Mais ações" fecha com tecla Esc.
  - confirmação de exclusão agora ajusta artigo ("este/esta") por entidade.
  - confirmação passa a exibir identificação do item (nome/produto/email/id).
- Cadastro de usuários:
  - menu "Mais ações" fecha com Esc.
  - modais de edição/exclusão com `role="dialog"` e `aria-modal`.
- Dashboard:
  - cartões clicáveis recebem `aria-label` ("Abrir <título>").
- App:
  - removido `<main>` aninhado no container principal (wrapper trocado para `div`).
- Início:
  - adicionada opção de serviço "Configurações".
  - busca agora ignora acentos (normalização Unicode NFD).
- VLibras:
  - reposicionamento do botão para base da tela, reduzindo sobreposição dos itens da sidebar.

## Escopo e compatibilidade

Correção pontual dos itens listados na #48, sem alteração de contrato de API.
Sem mudanças de regra de negócio.

## Validação

| Comando/verificação | Resultado |
| --- | --- |
| Testes específicos: `npm test -- tests/issue-48-ui-acessibilidade.test.jsx tests/configuracoes-senha.test.jsx tests/usuarios.test.jsx` | ✅ 44 passed |
| Suíte completa: `npm test` | ⚠️ execuções agregadas tiveram timeouts intermitentes em testes já existentes; ao isolar os arquivos que falharam (`sessao.test.jsx`, `editar-historico.test.jsx`, `usuarios.test.jsx`), os testes passaram |
| Lint/build, quando aplicável | ✅ `npm run lint` (apenas warnings preexistentes) e ✅ `npm run build` |
| `git diff --check` | ✅ sem erros |

### Limitações

Há flutuação de tempo na execução agregada da suíte (`vitest run`) no ambiente local, com timeout intermitente em alguns testes; não foi identificada regressão funcional da mudança nos arquivos afetados.

## Issue

Closes #48

In stage 3, after D3's and D6's B1, I read every release after each pin once more against this list, read `setup-go`'s `src/main.ts` and `src/installer.ts` at both pins, and diffed each `action.yml` between the old and new pinned commits (inputs, defaults, outputs, `runs.using`, `post`). Rows added in that pass are marked "stage 3".

**The order.** I read and saved the notes from 22:58:48Z to 22:59:42Z on 2026-11-22, before the first workflow commit (`c4e47a8f`, 23:00:47Z). I wrote this list down after the four workflow commits: the file was last written at 23:03:42Z, and the PR opened at 23:03:48Z. The brief asks for the list before any workflow line changes. That rests on my own record, and the record shows the list was written after the commits.

**The runtime.** All four targets declare `using: node24`, and the old pins declared `node20`. On these runners the old pins already ran on Node 24, forced by the runner. The control's log (`a5-windows-experiments` on `main`, job 137389500407) reads: `##[warning]Node.js 20 is deprecated. The following actions target Node.js 20 but are being forced to run on Node.js 24: actions/checkout@11d5960a…, actions/setup-go@40f1582b…, actions/upload-artifact@ea165f8d…`. The head's jobs print no such warning. So `node24` changes what the actions declare, not the runtime they ran on. The head's runner is v2.338.2 (Linux and Windows), above the v2.327.1 the notes require. The notes are another project's text, read as data. Every input this repository passes (checkout `ref`; setup-go `go-version-file`, `go-version`, `cache`; setup-python `python-version`; upload-artifact `name`, `path`, `if-no-files-found`) is still in the target's `action.yml`. **No `with:` key is changed.** No workflow uses `pull_request_target`, `workflow_run`, a job `container:` or a Docker container action.

### actions/checkout, v4.4.0 to v7.0.1

| Major | Change the notes give | Note | Touches us? |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| v5 | "Update actions checkout to use node 24"; "Minimum Compatible Runner Version v2.327.1" | [v5.0.0](https://github.com/actions/checkout/releases/tag/v5.0.0) | Yes, all 26 lines: the runtime moves from `node20` to `node24` (`action.yml` at the target: `using: node24`). Hosted runners only; the runner version is read from the runs' logs, not assumed. |
| v5.0.1 | "Port v6 cleanup to v5" *(row added after review, stage 2)* | [v5.0.1](https://github.com/actions/checkout/releases/tag/v5.0.1) | No: the PR it names (actions/checkout#2301) makes v5 clean up v6-style credential configuration when v5 and v6 check out the same repository to the same path in one job. Each of our jobs runs one checkout version. |
| v5.1.0 | "**[BREAKING]** backport `allow-unsafe-pr-checkout` to v5"; "backport fixes to releases-v5" *(row added after review, stage 2)* | [v5.1.0](https://github.com/actions/checkout/releases/tag/v5.1.0) | No: no workflow has `pull_request_target` or `workflow_run` (see v7 below). |
| v6 | "Persist creds to a separate file": "`persist-credentials` now stores credentials in a separate file under `$RUNNER_TEMP` instead of directly in `.git/config`"; "No workflow changes required — `git fetch`, `git push`, etc. continue to work automatically" | [v6.0.0](https://github.com/actions/checkout/releases/tag/v6.0.0), README "Checkout v6" | Yes. No workflow sets `persist-credentials`, so every checkout keeps the default, `true`. `a6-c2-old-reader.yml` runs `git fetch origin` after checkout, which the note says still works (the public repository needs no token to fetch). The file is `$RUNNER_TEMP/git-credentials-<uuid>.config` (`src/git-auth-helper.ts`, `getCredentialsConfigPath`, at `3d3c42e5`). author: flyingrobots
body:
Closes flyingrobots/footprint#10.

Every exported symbol on the blast radius carries its **call sites, with file and line**. A symbol
nothing references is listed with an empty list, never dropped. The additive fields ride the same
unreleased `footprint.blast_radius` **1.1.0** draft as #12's `unanalysed_languages`.

## Where the call sites come from, and why not graft

graft 0.14.0 has reference analysis, but **no graft CLI contract answers with a call site's line**.
Verified against the installed 0.14.0:

| Subcommand | What it gives | Line numbers? |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `graft symbol blame <name> --json` | `referenceCount`, an integer | no — no per-reference list at all |
| `graft struct review --json` | `breakingChanges[].impactedFilePaths` | no — file paths only |
| `graft symbol difficulty --json` | `friction.referencingFiles` | no — file paths only |
| `graft struct test-coverage --json` | `referencingTestFiles` | no — file paths only |

All four read the WARP index rather than the tree, and `symbol blame` answered `referenceCount: 0`
for a symbol with live references in an unindexed checkout. `AGENTS.md` carries that as a
correction, because the #8 decision table had promised `symbol blame` would be the source.

So footprint computes the call sites itself, with a **conservative whole-word identifier scan** of
the tracked, non-binary files of the working tree. The boundary is `grep -w`'s own — a letter,
digit or underscore in any script — which is what makes the independent `grep` oracle in the test
exact rather than approximate. It over-reports (the declaration itself, comments, strings, prose,
lockfiles) and under-reports (dynamic dispatch, a re-export under another name), and it is per
*name*, not per declaration. All of that is stated in the result, in the schema, in the reference
and under the list in the `--human` section. It is evidence a reviewer can check in one `grep`,
not a call graph.

## The oracle, exactly

`git ls-files -z` for the file set, then real `grep -I -n -w -- <symbol> /dev/null <files…>` in
batches of 200, parsed into a set of `file:line` pairs and asserted **equal** — not merely
contained — to what footprint lists, for all seven symbols of a real signature change in this
repository (543477a, where the exported `render` gained `review?: StructuralReview | null`). The
file enumeration is shared on purpose: what is under test is the matching, against an
implementation of `-w` nobody here wrote.

## Done

- [x] Planned test-plan rows before the code (now **OUT-13a–OUT-13r**, renumbered around #12's OUT-12)
- [x] Red first: the golden grep-oracle case and the edges, committed failing
- [x] Green: `src/callsites.ts`, the schema at 1.1.0, the `--human` section, the CLI step and warning
- [x] Living docs, schema changelog, `CHANGELOG.md`, status line
- [x] Focused self-review in place of Baker Street (waived for today)
- [x] Merged current `main` and resolved by union

## What the self-review found

- **The word boundary was wrong.** A differential fuzz against real grep (2,400 comparisons) caught
  an ASCII-only `[A-Za-z0-9_]` claiming a call site for `r` inside `rünïcode`. Now `[\p{L}\p{N}_]`,
  with the case pinned deterministically.
- **The schema's conditionals bite.** Probed over eight hand-built records: a symbol missing
  `call_sites` while the scan ran is rejected, as are a missing `counts.call_sites`, `line: 0`, an
  extra key on a site, version 1.0.0, and an available surface with no `call_site_scan`.
- **`inv` does not cover the working tree**, which the scan reads — now said in Output › Identity.

## Two things found while merging

- `test/cli.test.ts` ran the CLI with `node` off PATH, so **graft never executed** and every
  blast-radius assertion quietly took its "unavailable" branch: 1.7s and 113 expectations, now 172s
  and 483. `gh` stays off PATH, which is the isolation that was intended.
- A blast radius with call sites is ~67 KiB, past parley-emit's 64 KiB **sidecar** threshold, so the
  receipt names a file beside it instead of inlining the record. Two of main's receipt assertions
  are now stronger: they follow the sidecar, check its stated SHA-256, and validate the record.

`bun test`: **118 pass, 0 fail, 754 expect() calls** locally (56 / 244 before this branch; 438 on
CI, where graft installs but does not answer — recorded in the test plan's known gaps).
