_Requested by **Panos** · [project thread](https://claude.ai/code/project/chan_017rj9aZs7ZdFkL59tCXc6wp?thread=cmsg_017rj9aZs7ZdFkL59tCXc6wpVcPMseRPboJuTSjiTzyjBp)_

## What it does

Panos asked: "A user can add a personal notifications on item when is crossed on the list. For example if on the list is a shampoo and i put the notification on the item, as soon as someone crossed the item of the list a notification will pop up to you".

- The item sheet has a new action, **"Tell me when it's checked"** ("Πες μου όταν τσεκαριστεί"). Tap it again ("Stop telling me when it's checked") to turn it off.
- When someone else checks that item, you get a push notification right away, not in the 30-minute digest. It reads like the digest line: "🛒 Supermarket: Maria checked Shampoo".
- A small bell on the row shows you which items you asked about. Nobody else sees your bell.
- Turning it on asks for the Android 13+ notification permission if it hasn't been asked yet, the same way a due date already does.

## How

- `watchedBy[]` on the item holds the members who asked (`ListItem.watchedBy`, `ItemRepository.setWatched`).
- `notifyListChange` still writes the digest note first, then sends the watchers' notification (`watchers()` in `notify.js`: watchers who are still members, minus whoever checked it). It reuses the existing `push_item_checked` string, so no new notification strings are needed. No new Cloud Function: only `notifyListChange` changes.
- Firestore rules: a member may add or remove only their own id in `watchedBy`, never on a new item, at most 100. The mute rule now shares the same helper.

## Calls Claude made that Panos didn't name
- A quiet list does not block it, because you asked for this one item yourself.
- The watch stays after the check, so if the item is unchecked and checked again you hear again.
- The bell only shows on unchecked items.

## Checks
- `./gradlew :app:assembleDebug testDebugUnitTest :app:lintDebug`: passed.
- Functions tests (`node --test notify.test.js`): 10 of 10 passed, one of them new.
- Firestore rules tests on the emulator (`npm test` in `firebase/`): 29 of 29 passed, one of them new.
- Screens drawn with sample data (not a run on a phone): `design/notify-when-checked/before-and-after.png` in the project files.
- **Not tried on a phone**: the real push needs the deployed function and two accounts.

## After merging
1. In the `firebase` folder: `firebase deploy --only firestore:rules,functions`. Until the rules are published, turning the bell on fails silently. Console fallback for the rules: https://console.firebase.google.com/project/list-anything-12208/firestore/rules
2. The push only works once the functions deploy succeeds (the last known deploy of functions failed).

body:
Claimed in the coordination issue as: https://github.com/ItsNotRexed/Leonida/issues/3918#issuecomment-7087282323 (new TEST item)

### What and why

On Windows, `os.readlink` returns an absolute link target with the `\\?\` prefix: a plain `os.symlink(r"C:\...\t.txt", link)` reads back as `\\?\C:\...\t.txt`. `test_destination_symlinks_update_the_target_and_remain_links` in `tests/test_saves.py` compares `os.readlink(link)` with the spelling it created the link with, so its two absolute subcases (`relative=False`) fail on every Windows machine that can create symlinks (Developer Mode or an elevated shell). #2688, which added the test, noted it still needed a run on a symlink-capable system; it had only been skipped there. `tools/saves.py` itself keeps the link as it was.

The comparison now drops a leading `\\?\` (`removeprefix`, a no-op elsewhere and for relative links). One line plus a comment; the tool is not touched.

### Tested

Windows 11 Pro with Developer Mode (symlinks allowed), Python 3.12.10. No game data, no GPU.

- `python -I tests/test_saves.py` on `main`: `FAILED (failures=2, skipped=1)`, `AssertionError: '\\?\C:\Users\...\target-False-False\save.jsav' != 'C:\Users\...\target-False-False\save.jsav'` (and the same for `False-True`).
- On this branch: `Ran 56 tests ... OK (skipped=1)`.
- A bare `os.symlink(abs_target, link); os.readlink(link)` outside the test shows the same `\\?\` prefix, so it is Python's reading of the link, not something `saves.pack` writes.

AI-assisted (Claude Code); the runs above were done on this branch.

### Checklist

- [x] No game data, keys or decryption (CONTRIBUTING.md), including in logs or reports quoted here.
- [x] A new translator rule is in the contract table of `docs/design.md`, with how it was confirmed. (Not applicable: no translator change.)

Fixes widget drafts that flash during theme changes and ignore the host's background and text tokens.

## User Impact

<!--
"User impact: <what users, operators, or developers can now do or expect>."
Lead with the concrete outcome in plain language, usually one sentence.
For internal-only changes, say there is no user-visible change; do not invent a benefit.
Keep important risks, breaking changes, migrations, and required user actions visible here.

The Alcove client can supply full theme snapshots, keep a loaded draft visible until its replacement loads, and size drafts through the same 120–1200 pixel clamp as finished widgets.

This change needs a protected server/runtime release and client vendoring. It does not deploy either service. `src/canvas/wrap.ts` and stored widget HTML remain unchanged.

Fixed authored white backgrounds cannot safely receive automatic recoloring. A client can offer explicit light appearance through `setTheme("light", completeLightTokens)` for those widgets.

## Why This Change Was Made

<!--
Briefly explain how the change addresses the problem without repeating the impact.
Keep the body short. Leave file lists, internal acronyms, and root-cause walkthroughs
in the diff or optional <details>; include technical detail only when it explains
behavior or a material tradeoff. Do not hide risks or required actions in <details>.
-->

The package accepts initial theme tokens, replaces complete snapshots on updates, and exposes `setHeight(rawHeight)`. The existing `onReady` callback remains bound to the matching resource notification.

The protected shell injects allowed token CSS into script-free drafts and buffers theme replacements until their load event. Superseded buffers cannot publish readiness. The visible double-frame sandbox retains its opaque origins and permissions.

The protected app blocks inline styles in `srcdoc`. A separate empty `/api/protected/v1/widget-measurement` document supplies the exact draft base CSS and a restrictive response policy. The client must populate only sanitized markup in a hidden, inert, script-disabled measurement frame. Scripts, external resources, child frames, and forms remain blocked. The client removes navigation tags and attributes. No ports or credentials enter either draft.

## Evidence

<!--

validation easy to understand, not to restate the diff.
Summarize what was checked and the result; note meaningful gaps. Link long output
or put it in optional <details>, keeping the useful evidence summary visible.
-->

The regression failed with the original shell: the draft's background was transparent instead of the supplied `oklch()` token.

`pnpm exec tsx --test grogu/protected/widget-styles.test.ts grogu/protected/widget-measurement.test.ts` passed all three tests (latest wall time 4.00s). Chromium and WebKit preserve the measurement response CSP after `document.open/write`; hostile markup caused zero server requests and no parent DOM mutation. The widget boundary covers draft/final tokens, omitted-token fallback, rapid theme buffering, matching readiness, sizing, and explicit light appearance.

`node --import ./scripts/tsx.mjs --test --test-name-pattern='^Family HTTP isolates chats, relays device authorization, and durably revokes sessions$' grogu/protected/http.test.ts` passed under native outbound-network isolation and fresh state (47.99s wall).

`node scripts/run-tsgo.mjs --project "$PROOF/widget-host-tsconfig.json"` passed. The temporary config includes only changed TypeScript entry points, their imports, and existing ambient declarations.

`OPENCLAW_OXLINT_SKIP_PREPARE=1 node scripts/run-oxlint.mjs --tsconfig "$PROOF/widget-host-tsconfig.json" packages/widget-host/src/protected-host.ts src/agents/sandbox-host.ts grogu/protected/widget-measurement.ts grogu/protected/widget-measurement.test.ts grogu/protected/widget-styles.test.ts` passed, reusing declarations already generated by the previous lint gate. The initial run including `grogu/protected/http.ts` and `grogu/protected/http.test.ts` failed on baseline diagnostics outside the diff: unbound methods, catalog type resolution, and existing header spreads. Those expressions were verified unchanged against HEAD; unrelated repairs are excluded.

`node_modules/.bin/oxfmt --check packages/widget-host/src/protected-host.ts src/agents/sandbox-host.ts grogu/protected/http.ts grogu/protected/http.test.ts grogu/protected/widget-measurement.ts grogu/protected/widget-measurement.test.ts grogu/protected/widget-styles.test.ts packages/widget-host/README.md` and `git diff --check` passed. No whole-repository checks ran. CI seconds were not measured; these focused browser checks use Node's test runner, not `pnpm test`/Vitest.

One independent read-only Copilot review reported no significant issues within the requested P0/P1 scope. This is a narrative Copilot review, not an isolated helper certification. The coordinator also passed its paired Chromium/WebKit desktop/phone light/dark client matrix, including the explicit fixed-white fallback, under the deployed app CSP. No service was deployed by this work.

author: nitsuah
body:
- Mutating and compute-heavy routes (attack runs and job output, RAG reindex, ad-hoc decrypt, all vault routes) require `KRYPTOS_API_TOKEN` via `Authorization: Bearer` or `X-Kryptos-Token`.
- Routes are closed with no token configured. `KRYPTOS_API_AUTH=off` is a local-dev opt-out honoured only for direct loopback requests outside production (Render/`KRYPTOS_ENV=production`).
- The token is checked before any limiter. Separate buckets: anonymous callers on public routes (`KRYPTOS_RATE_LIMIT_PER_MIN`, 60), failed token checks per client (`KRYPTOS_FAILED_AUTH_LIMIT_PER_MIN`, 10, answered 429 once spent), valid callers (`KRYPTOS_AUTH_RATE_LIMIT_PER_MIN`, 300). Anonymous junk cannot use up an operator's allowance.
- Concurrent attack jobs are capped (`KRYPTOS_MAX_ATTACK_JOBS`, default 3).
- Client identity: with `KRYPTOS_TRUST_PROXY=1` (set in `render.yaml`) the limiter reads `X-Forwarded-For` from the right (`KRYPTOS_TRUSTED_PROXY_HOPS`, default 1). Render's proxy appends the connecting address, so the right-most entry is the real client and anything a client forges sits to its left.
- Left public on purpose (read-only demo data, rate limited): `/api/status`, `/api/runs`, `/api/candidates`, `/api/attack-vectors`, ledger, frontier list, pivot status, world-clock diagnostic, RAG status and search.
- Dashboard sends the token saved in `localStorage["kryptos.apiToken"]`.

Deploy note: the Render blueprint must be re-synced for `generateValue` to create `KRYPTOS_API_TOKEN` (and for `KRYPTOS_TRUST_PROXY`); until then the protected routes answer 503.

Tests: `tests/functional/test_api_security.py` (auth, buckets, `client_key` with `X-Forwarded-For`) plus API, vault, log, job and CLI suites in Docker (python:3.12-slim).

body:
<!-- claude-projects-attribution: {"github_login":"tuannm3812"} -->
_Requested by **Mike** · [project thread](https://claude.ai/code/project/chan_01RWe5FEHmDbruVcBUq5tac3?thread=cmsg_01RWe5FEHmDbruVcBUq5tac3XUZzWrgrS8DQnE717pvCh7)_

## Summary

This PR builds user accounts as designed in `docs/superpowers/specs/2026-11-22-user-accounts-design.md`, which Mike approved on 2026-11-23 (DEC-43). It is one commit per slice. Production does not change until the `ACCOUNTS_ENABLED` variable is set after the one-time setup in `docs/6_deployment.md` §5.

1. **Sign-in tokens on the API.** Every protected route accepts `Authorization: Bearer <Firebase ID token>` when `FIREBASE_PROJECT_ID` is set. `google-auth` checks the token against cached Google certificates. A valid token is the `accounts` principal with the token's uid.
   - The body `user_id` is replaced by the uid, and another user's history path gets 403.
   - Feedback must reference the same user's own plan. Testing showed that, without this rule, one account could rate another's meal.
   - Sending both a key and a token is refused. No API key may use the reserved `accounts` client_id. The rate limit counts each user separately.
2. **Firestore storage.** `STORAGE_BACKEND=firestore` is a new repository behind the DEC-4 protocols, in the optional `firestore` extra.
   - Every id is escaped, and each record is stored as JSON.
   - The contract suite runs on JSON, SQLite and Firestore. CI starts the Firestore emulator.
3. **Account routes and hosted history.**
   - New routes: `GET`/`PUT /me/profile` (bounded React profile fields) and `DELETE /me` (removes the account's plans, feedback and profile).
   - A hosted deployment on Firestore keeps history, and `/health` reports `history_enabled`. Hosted SQLite still refuses history (DEC-10).
4. **React sign-in.** Accounts are on only when the build has the `VITE_FIREBASE_*` config. Without it, nothing changes.
   - **Visitors:** a visitor is signed in anonymously at the first API call, so a first visit still makes no network call before planning.
   - **Google sign-in:** from the Profile page or the top bar. It links the anonymous account, and the device and account profiles sync.
   - **Sign out and delete:** Sign out, and "Delete my account and data" behind a confirmation.
   - **Size:** `firebase` 13.2.0 adds about 35 kB gzipped.
5. **Deploy.** `deploy.yml` sets Firestore, `FIREBASE_PROJECT_ID` and the `web.app` CORS origin when `ACCOUNTS_ENABLED=true`. A new `hosting` job publishes React, `firestore.rules` and `firestore.indexes.json`.
   - The rules refuse every browser read and write.
   - `live_check.sh` checks the shared-storage path.
   - `docs/6_deployment.md` §5 has the setup and a by-hand check.

## Verification
- `uv run pytest` with the Firestore emulator: 774 passed, coverage 97%. Without the emulator, the Firestore cases skip.
- `ruff check` and `ruff format --check` pass.
- Frontend: `vitest run` 257 passed, `eslint` is clean, and `vite build` works with and without the Firebase config.
- **Not yet run against the real project.** That needs the one-time setup in `docs/6_deployment.md` §5.

author: jancona
body:
After an RF transmission on another CAN, MMDVM-Host misses the header of the next transmission on its own CAN. It only picks that transmission up from the LICH, about 240 ms in, and reports it as `late_entry`. The cause is a late-entry search that an EOT doesn't end; this fixes it.

<details>
<summary>Claude Opus 5.5</summary>

### Cause

- The header of a transmission on another CAN is ignored, as it should be. Its stream frames then move the RF state from listening to `LATE_ENTRY`, and every LICH it rebuilds fails the CAN check too.
- An EOT ended `DATA` and `REJECTED`, but not `LATE_ENTRY`, and the modem sends no "lost" after an EOT. So the state stayed in `LATE_ENTRY`.
- A header was only accepted while listening. So the next transmission's link setup frame was dropped, and the transmission was only found once a full LSF had been collected from the LICH.

The same happens after any transmission that's never accepted and ends with an EOT.

### Changes (`M17Control.cpp`)

- An EOT in `LATE_ENTRY` returns to listening. It resets only the RF LSFs, not `writeEndRF()`, because that also clears the callsigns shared with the network side and can reset the network, and network traffic is allowed during a late-entry search.
- A header is accepted in `LATE_ENTRY` as well as while listening. No RF transmission is in progress in that state, and it also covers an EOT the modem missed.

### Testing

Harness tests (M17Control fed with modem frames generated by libm17): a stream on CAN 7, then one on CAN 0, with and without the first stream's EOT.

Before:
```
M17, received RF late entry voice transmission from N1ADJ to ALL
M17, received RF end of transmission from N1ADJ to ALL, 0.2 seconds, BER: 0.0%
```
After, in both cases:
```
M17, received RF voice transmission from N1ADJ to ALL
M17, link setup frame: errs: 0/368 (0.0%)
M17, received RF end of transmission from N1ADJ to ALL, 0.4 seconds, BER: 0.0%
```

The existing scenarios (voice, lost, self-only reject, SMS, duplex) give the same output as before.

Over RF on a Pi 3B+ running Pi-Star OS, with a Repeater-Builder STM32 DVM board on M17-Project MMDVM firmware 63c7db2: a call on CAN 3, then one on CAN 0. The second was received from its header (that build also had #31, #32 and #33):

```
M17, received RF voice transmission from N1ADJ 8 to ECHO
{"M17":{"action":"start","can":0,"dst_callsign":"ECHO","source":"rf","src_callsign":"N1ADJ 8",...,"traffic_type":"audio"}}
M17, received RF end of transmission from N1ADJ 8 to ECHO, 3.5 seconds, BER: 0.7%, RSSI: -43/-43/-43 dBm
```

</details>

## Summary
<!-- A human-written summary of the content of the code. This is required. -->

Sometimes wired connection gets stuck, for example when enabling wired mode while the client was already streaming wirelessly. This happens to be because cloned socket handles are not marked to not be inherited by child processes, and so the cloned handle gets inherited by ADB. This is a longstanding bug in the Rust stdlib. The workaround is to share the same handle using an Arc. This also should fix the case when SteamVR spawns any child processes while the stream is running.

Also disable creating the UDP socket when wired (client is in loopback), and some renaming in log in connection.rs

Linear: CORE-303 (C9.2)

## What

When a pharn-oss release's `pharn-install.json` declares a `dest` that fails `isPharnOwnedPath`, `fetchRepo` still refuses the whole release (containment guard; `OWNED_SEGMENT_RE`, `MANIFEST_PATH_RE` and `isPharnOwnedPath` are unchanged). Only the message changes. It now:

- names the offending `dest` (escaped with `escapeUnsafe`) and its `files[i]` entry;
- says it is a problem in the pharn-oss release and nothing in the project was changed;
- names what works today: an existing install keeps working, report it at https://github.com/pharn-dev/pharn-oss/issues, once upstream has fixed `main`, move to it with `pharn update --ref main` (`pharn init --ref main` for a new install; `add` and `status` take no `--ref`).

One helper, `disallowedDestMessage` (`src/lib/upstream-manifest.ts`), reached by `init`, `add`, `update` and `status` through `fetchRepo`. No new option.

New text, for `pharn/floor/.eslintrc.json`:

> pharn-oss's pharn-install.json files[N] would write pharn/floor/.eslintrc.json, outside the paths pharn installs; refusing this release. This is a problem in the pharn-oss release, not in your project: nothing in your project was changed, and an existing install keeps working as it is. Report it at https://github.com/pharn-dev/pharn-oss/issues, then move to main once pharn-oss has fixed it: `pharn update --ref main` (`pharn init --ref main` for a new install).

`OWNED_SEGMENT_RE` and `MANIFEST_PATH_RE` now carry a comment saying pharn-oss's generator (`assertPlainRelative` in `.dev/floor/install-manifest-core.mjs`) mirrors them and must change with them (sibling PR in pharn-oss: CORE-302).

## Tests

- `tests/commands/update.test.ts`: a release whose manifest holds `pharn/floor/.eslintrc.json` → `pharn update --yes` exits 1, prints the message (path, "nothing in your project was changed"), config and records byte-identical, whole-tree snapshot unchanged, no clone left.

`src/lib/install-surfaces.ts` changes a comment only (the mirror note on `OWNED_SEGMENT_RE`), so no test imports it for this change; the allowlist's behaviour is unchanged and stays covered by the existing outer-bound tests.

body:
## Summary

- Pause automated translation by default on pull requests, pushes, and releases. The repository variable and Boolean dispatch input restore the translation commands, artifact checks, native coverage gate, and full acceptance evaluation.
- Keep the independent JavaScript and Rust checks, grammar generation, package validation, offline consumer tests, and downstream workloads required. With the pause active, the aggregate still fails on any applicable independent check failure.
- Permit manual ports with shared behavior fixtures and native checks. The case study maps all seven issue requirements to implementation and verification, with the baseline CI evidence and alternatives considered. [Issue #248 case study](https://github.com/link-foundation/meta-language/blob/issue-248-3afae7c35b4a/docs/case-studies/issue-248/README.md)

## Reproduction and verification

The baseline run failed automated translation on relative-array provenance, report sizing, and generated package validation. The pause preserves those test commands in the opt-in path. The workflow regressions exercise the default and opt-in conditions, failed prerequisites, retained strict commands, exact native test filters, and rejection of stale rollout observations. [Baseline CI](https://github.com/link-foundation/meta-language/actions/runs/45059254685)

```sh
node --test --test-concurrency=1 js/tests/issue-195-evidence-automated-translation-{pause,rollout}.test.js
```

On `d460599c7`, all six JavaScript translation shards reported the pause. The JavaScript matrix, bulk grammar pipeline, all 15 package jobs, and delivery candidates passed. This includes all 11 raw schema and consumer tests. The protected-scope check verified 474 requirements and 495 fixture identities against the default branch. [Prior CI](https://github.com/link-foundation/meta-language/actions/runs/45112972070), [JavaScript aggregate](https://github.com/link-foundation/meta-language/actions/runs/45112972070/job/137536464969), [raw schema and consumer tests](https://github.com/link-foundation/meta-language/actions/runs/45112972070/job/137507809375)

The same run packed and uploaded both packages at log lines 535 and 589. GitHub skipped the independent consumer jobs because a translation report was a skipped ancestor. The current workflow explicitly admits clean consumers, Relative Meta Logic workloads, and Formal AI partitions after successful delivery candidates. Cargo Check reported missing observation calls and unsupported SHA-256 hexadecimal formatting at log lines 1149–2388. Rust lint reported an inline test, two oversized files, and 199 Clippy diagnostics at lines 1138–1140, 4425–4426, and 4305. The batch restores the observation helper, fixes formatting, moves the test bodies with their assertions, and replays reviewed corrections through the generators. The native lint policy remains in effect. The focused checks passed all 39 JavaScript tests for the affected generators, historical inputs, stale-edit rejection, and binary paths. Naming conformance passed 81 active tests, including the restored historical owners, and the bulk grammar pipeline passed its 67-language matrix. Four jobs found the relocated ownership metadata test missing from the dependency inventory. A fifth found stale naming fixture digests in the generated acceptance manifest. The package contracts partition reproduced both errors and passed the full naming check at log line 685. The separate raw schema and consumer partition passed all 11 tests with zero skips. [CI](https://github.com/link-foundation/meta-language/actions/runs/45144165350), [naming conformance](https://github.com/link-foundation/meta-language/actions/runs/45144165350/job/137589212564), [grammar matrix](https://github.com/link-foundation/meta-language/actions/runs/45144165350/job/137589213975), [dependency inventory failure](https://github.com/link-foundation/meta-language/actions/runs/45144165350/job/137589211407), [manifest failure](https://github.com/link-foundation/meta-language/actions/runs/45144165350/job/137589212106), [package contracts](https://github.com/link-foundation/meta-language/actions/runs/45144165350/job/137639287457), [raw schema and consumer tests](https://github.com/link-foundation/meta-language/actions/runs/45144165350/job/137639287454)

author: codewizard0909
body:
fixes #136

While adding tests for the dnssd package (it had none), I found three bugs in txt.go:

1. **`rs` slashes were never stripped.** `decodeTxtScanner` strips the leading and trailing `/` from `rs` into a local variable, then assigns the original `value` to `uriPath`. So `rs=/eSCL/` stayed `/eSCL/` instead of `eSCL`.

2. **A2 paper sizes were never detected.** `txtPaperMax` lowercases the value, but the cases for A2 were written as `"isoC-a2"` and `">isoC-a2"`, with a capital C. `papermax=isoC-A2` always came back as `PaperUnknown`.

3. **The duplicate key check never ran.** The `found` map was checked but never written to, so a key that appeared twice was decoded twice and the last value won. I now record each key and compare keys in lowercase. RFC 6763 section 6.4 says keys are case-insensitive and only the first occurrence counts. This also stops a bad duplicate (like a second `priority=bad`) from failing the whole record.

One small side effect: the key in error messages is now lowercase (for example, `priority: ...` instead of `Priority: ...`).

**Tests:** I added `discovery/dnssd/txt_test.go`. It covers the TXT helpers (`txtParse`, `txToLower`, `txtKeywords`, `txtOption`, `txtAuth`, `txtPaperMax`, `txtMediaKind`, `txtColors`, `txtInputs`) and `decodeTxtPrinter`/`decodeTxtScanner`, including defaults, errors and duplicates. The new tests fail on the current code and pass with the fix.

```
go test ./discovery/...
ok  github.com/OpenPrinting/go-mfp/discovery
ok  github.com/OpenPrinting/go-mfp/discovery/dnssd
ok  github.com/OpenPrinting/go-mfp/discovery/wsdd
```

I haven't tested this against a real printer or scanner.

I used an AI coding assistant (Claude) to help write this change. I've reviewed and tested it myself.
